scope.note: All 22 office categories in this reviewed research collection; completeness does not claim every community service was discovered.

types.label: Crisis and Detox
types.definition: Crisis stabilization or specifically supported withdrawal management; facts distinguish medical detox from nonmedical support.

types.label: Outpatient Treatment
types.definition: Direct outpatient substance-use assessment or treatment, including IOP/PHP and integrated clinical care.

types.label: Medication Treatment
types.definition: Direct medication treatment for substance-use disorders, not medication referral or psychiatric medicines alone.

types.label: Residential Treatment
types.definition: A supported residential clinical substance-use treatment programme.

types.label: Recovery Housing
types.definition: Housing specifically organized around recovery or treatment participation; clinical treatment is not implied.

types.label: Peer and Family Support
types.definition: Dedicated mutual aid, nonclinical recovery coaching or support for family members affected by addiction.

types.label: Harm Reduction
types.definition: Overdose-prevention supplies or training, safer-use outreach and related direct support.

types.label: Prevention and Education
types.definition: Structured substance-use prevention or education with public, school or community access.

types.label: Court Programs
types.definition: Specific diversion, DUI, probation or custody-linked treatment or education.

types.label: Treatment Navigation
types.definition: Individualized routing or referral to appropriate treatment, beyond routine clinic admissions.

types.label: Practical Recovery Support
types.definition: Recovery-targeted employment, documents, education or other stability support.

types.label: Maternal & Child Health
types.definition: Maternal, infant and child health care, including prenatal care, vaccination, lactation and specialist clinical access; nonclinical education is not medical treatment.

types.label: Parenting & Home Visiting
types.definition: Parenting instruction, home visits, parent-child activities and practical family developmental consultation.

types.label: Child Care & Early Education
types.definition: Child-care payment or access help, preschool and Head Start; funding does not guarantee a placement.

types.label: Development & Disability Support
types.definition: Child developmental screening, early intervention, disability-system navigation and specialized developmental support.

types.label: Family Supplies
types.definition: Diapers, baby equipment, childrens clothing and other practical family goods.

types.label: Food & Nutrition
types.definition: Child or family food benefits, feeding support and nutrition services.

types.label: Health Coverage
types.definition: Health-insurance eligibility, enrolment and specific covered-benefit access for children or pregnancy.

types.label: Family Safety & Shelter
types.definition: Emergency child shelter, family or maternity housing and the Safe Haven route; admission and household limits remain distinct.

types.label: Family Mental Health & Grief
types.definition: Family or maternal clinical counselling and clearly distinguished peer, adjustment or bereavement support.

types.label: Family Advocacy & Navigation
types.definition: Family-system advocacy, kinship assistance, visitation and substantial coordinated family-resource navigation.

types.label: Respite
types.definition: A defined programme providing a short break for family caregivers.

types.label: Child safety and protection
types.definition: Child injury-prevention support such as car seats and safe sleep, and specific abuse/neglect reporting or child-protection pathways. Records distinguish safety equipment, education, confidential support and official reporting that can trigger an investigation.

types.label: Financial Help
types.definition: Family-targeted cash or cost assistance; general-population benefits need a distinct family pathway to belong here.

types.label: Everyday Clothing
types.definition: Ordinary clothing and shoes, including specialized-client closets; age and size limits remain in the resource.

types.label: Work & Interview Clothing
types.definition: Professional clothing, uniforms or job-required footwear; excludes generic clothing with no stated employment service.

types.label: School & Formal Wear
types.definition: School uniforms, back-to-school clothing or formal-event attire; excludes school supplies alone.

types.label: Baby & Toddler Supplies
types.definition: Diapers, infant/toddler essentials or safe-sleep equipment; distinguishes these from ordinary child clothing.

types.label: Beds & Furniture
types.definition: Beds or other home furniture, including referral/conditional funding; excludes ordinary housewares and unconfirmed free thrift furniture.

types.label: Household Essentials
types.definition: Bedding, kitchen items, cleaning supplies or move-in kits; not a blanket tag for all assistance.

types.label: Personal Care Supplies
types.definition: Toiletries and personal hygiene items; diaper-only programs use Baby & Toddler Supplies.

types.label: Laundry & Showers
types.definition: A service for washing clothing or bathing, not clothing donation availability.

types.label: Medical Equipment & Recovery Garments
types.definition: Loaned medical aids or condition-specific recovery garments; coordinate with Disability/Medical categories.

types.label: Appliance Repair & Replacement
types.definition: Conditional household-appliance repair or replacement programs; preserve service-area restrictions.

types.label: Benefits and Coverage
types.definition: Disability-related cash, health coverage, financial support, savings and application or work-incentive pathways.

types.label: Help at home and respite
types.definition: Disability-related help with daily living at home, including personal assistance, practical household support, home-delivered meals, habilitation and defined caregiver respite. A meal-delivery programme does not itself provide nursing or attendant care.

types.label: Day Programs
types.definition: Structured adult or youth day supports; participation has program-specific age, funding and supervision rules.

types.label: Housing and living support
types.definition: Disability-targeted residential housing and community-living support, including accessible independent apartments, developmental homes and supported living. Each entry distinguishes the actual care level; this is not general emergency shelter.

types.label: Work and Transition
types.definition: Job preparation, supported employment, vocational rehabilitation and school-to-work planning.

types.label: Equipment and service animals
types.definition: Disability-related equipment assessment, trials, lending, adapted devices and financing, and trained service-animal or therapeutic-companion-animal programmes. Each record distinguishes equipment from animal training and states eligibility; ordinary pet supplies or boarding do not qualify.

types.label: Vision, Hearing and Communication
types.definition: Specialized skills, accessible information and communication supports for sensory or print-access disabilities.

types.label: Child and School Services
types.definition: Child development, early intervention, special education and student accommodation pathways.

types.label: Rights and Advocacy
types.definition: Disability-rights protection, self-advocacy and formal complaint or dispute-resolution routes.

types.label: Adaptive Recreation
types.definition: Adaptive sports, inclusive recreation, camps and community participation programs; ordinary day-program activities alone do not establish this type.

types.label: Home Accessibility
types.definition: Home modifications and repairs that address disability-related access or safety.

types.label: Transportation Access
types.definition: Accessible rides, member transport and travel-navigation programs with distinct eligibility and trip boundaries.

types.label: Therapy and Medical Access
types.definition: Specialty assessments, rehabilitation, therapy and medical-service coordination; each record distinguishes clinical care from access guidance.

types.label: Navigation and Peer Support
types.definition: Disability-specific information, coordination, family guidance, mentoring and peer support.

types.label: Safety Planning and Advocacy
types.definition: Survivor-focused support, safety planning, helplines and continuing advocacy; direct shelter and legal-service conditions remain separate.

types.label: Emergency Shelter
types.definition: Short-term emergency shelter or screened overflow housing for survivors; child-only and ordinary homelessness alternatives must retain their restrictions.

types.label: Transitional and Recovery Housing
types.definition: Longer-term transitional, supportive or recovery housing after immediate danger; duration, fees and program rules vary.

types.label: Counseling and Recovery Support
types.definition: Survivor counseling, trauma therapy, support groups or structured emotional recovery services; coaching and clinical treatment are distinguished in the record.

types.label: Legal Information and Representation
types.definition: Legal information, consultations, document help or representation for survivor-related civil, immigration or victims-rights issues; each provider states the actual level offered.

types.label: Protective Orders and Court Support
types.definition: Protective-order preparation/filing, lay court advocacy or support with specific court processes. This does not by itself imply attorney representation.

types.label: Victim Case Services
types.definition: Case-linked victim-rights information, notifications, restitution guidance or institutional response through police, prosecution, probation, military or campus systems.

types.label: Medical Forensic Care
types.definition: Specialist medical-forensic examinations and centers that coordinate access after violence; not routine medical treatment or generic referrals.

types.label: Practical and Financial Help
types.definition: Survivor-related escape assistance, emergency costs, crime-loss compensation or public crisis assistance; funding and referral requirements apply.

types.label: Pet Safety
types.definition: Specific pet accommodation or temporary animal care that supports a survivor’s safe move.

types.label: Abuse Reporting and Protection
types.definition: Official child or vulnerable-adult protection reporting and coordinated child-protection response, distinct from confidential survivor advocacy.

types.label: Resource Navigation
types.definition: Public survivor-service directories, official program information or safety-related administrative support such as Address Confidentiality Program enrollment.

types.label: Adult Basic Education and High School Completion
types.definition: Literacy, adult basic education, GED/HSE preparation, testing and diploma completion; eligibility and pathway distinctions remain in the text.

types.label: English and Citizenship Learning
types.definition: English-language instruction, conversation practice and citizenship-test learning; not immigration representation.

types.label: Career and Technical Training
types.definition: Instruction leading toward occupational skills, a trade, professional credential or technical degree.

types.label: Education access and student support
types.definition: Navigation to adult, vocational or college learning opportunities, enrollment planning, advising and continuing academic support. K–12 access has its separate school-access Type.

types.label: Education Costs
types.definition: Scholarships, grants, approved training funding, matched savings and practical student financial-aid guidance. Includes early-education scholarships and childcare-cost assistance with an explicit school or training eligibility route; a place or award is never implied.

types.label: Tutoring and Study Help
types.definition: Individual or group academic tutoring, writing support, test preparation and study help outside a full diploma program.

types.label: Digital Skills
types.definition: Computer, internet and technology literacy instruction and learning tools.

types.label: Parent and Family Learning
types.definition: Classes or coaching helping parents support a child’s learning and development.

types.label: Accessible Learning
types.definition: Education accommodations and specialized learning or transition services for disabled learners.

types.label: Small Business Learning
types.definition: Business-startup education and technical assistance for self-employment.

types.label: Apprenticeships and Internships
types.definition: Structured learning combined with paid work, apprenticeship or internship access; placement remains conditional.

types.label: Career Readiness
types.definition: Workplace skills, career exploration and preparation linked to employment rather than a specific academic credential.

types.label: Early learning and school access
types.definition: Early-childhood and school enrollment, preschool learning, culturally focused K–12 support and educational access when housing or other barriers disrupt learning. Childcare alone does not establish an instructional programme.

types.label: Job search and readiness
types.definition: Career planning, general job-readiness or professional-skills learning, resumes, interviews, job-search tools, employer referrals or help retaining a job. Occupational-training-only and document-only services have separate Types.

types.label: Staffing and Shifts
types.definition: Staffing-agency placement or an app that directly lists short-term work assignments; ordinary job-search advice is a different type.

types.label: Career Training
types.definition: Structured occupational instruction, a career certificate or job-specific training beyond general job-search coaching.

types.label: Apprenticeships
types.definition: Registered or employer-sponsored apprenticeship access, approved pre-apprenticeships, or navigation to an apprenticeship sponsor.

types.label: Paid Work Experience
types.definition: Paid internships, subsidized work or a defined transitional-work placement; does not imply ordinary training provides a wage.

types.label: Supported Employment
types.definition: Individualized disability- or mental-health-recovery-related job development, on-the-job coaching, transitional employment, or group/individual supported work. Provider membership or authorization may apply; no placement or wage is promised.

types.label: Work Essentials
types.definition: Help with a practical requirement for starting or keeping work, such as authorized child care, work clothing, equipment or work-related transportation.

types.label: Training Costs
types.definition: A defined scholarship, training grant or other program that may reduce an eligible participant's education or occupational-training costs; tuition-free instruction alone stays Career Training.

types.label: Benefits and Work
types.definition: Guidance or a defined program connecting employment with disability benefits, public-assistance obligations, unemployment requirements or employer hiring incentives.

types.label: Employment with Housing
types.definition: Employment help accessed through a particular shelter, transitional home or residential program; housing admission or program enrollment is a prerequisite.

types.label: Adult Learning
types.definition: Basic education, English, high-school-equivalency or supported academic learning that can prepare an adult for work or further training.

types.label: Income and payment claims
types.definition: Public cash income, survivor payments, child support and claims for money owed to the applicant; excludes ordinary expense-specific grants.

types.label: Rent and move-in costs
types.definition: Help paying rent, mortgage, deposits or other housing-stability costs, including referral to an actual housing-assistance program.

types.label: Utility bills
types.definition: Payment help, account arrangements or qualifying discounts on household energy, water, phone or internet bills.

types.label: Medical costs
types.definition: Help with eligible medical bills, treatment costs, medication charges, insurance premiums or health-cost discounts.

types.label: Money management
types.definition: Budgeting, credit or debt counseling, financial coaching and access to safer banking accounts.

types.label: Tax help
types.definition: Tax-return preparation, tax credits, taxpayer disputes or property-tax relief.

types.label: Benefits access and appeals
types.definition: Screening, application assistance, required eligibility or continuing-benefit steps, advocacy and appeals involving public or veteran benefits. Not every direct benefit merely because it has an application form; a required assessment does not itself award payments or resolve all claim questions.

types.label: Education and savings
types.definition: Scholarships, education-cost assistance or matched savings toward education or business goals.

types.label: Child care and respite costs
types.definition: Subsidies or financial help for child care, in-home care or caregiver respite.

types.label: Funeral costs
types.definition: Help with burial, cremation, funeral or final-disposition expenses.

types.label: Home repairs
types.definition: Financial help for essential home repairs, accessibility changes or weatherization.

types.label: Transportation costs
types.definition: Financial help or discounts for transit, qualifying vehicle expenses or essential travel; program-specific exclusions still apply.

types.label: Food costs
types.definition: Food-purchasing benefits or financial assistance with groceries; ordinary food distribution is assessed in Food.

types.label: Hardship funds
types.definition: Discretionary assistance addressing unforeseen personal or family emergencies; eligibility and covered expenses vary and no response speed is implied.

types.label: Reentry planning and mentoring
types.definition: Individual transition planning, coaching, peer navigation or mentoring across practical needs.

types.label: Employment and training
types.definition: Job placement support, job readiness, education or vocational training connected to reentry.

types.label: Housing
types.definition: Actual housing, residential programs or defined housing-navigation and funding pathways; distinguish placements from referrals.

types.label: Treatment and recovery
types.definition: Mental-health, substance-use or specialized behavioral treatment and clinical or peer recovery support.

types.label: Legal rights and record relief
types.definition: Help with criminal-record remedies and legal barriers after justice involvement, including fair-chance rights and related self-help information. Court supervision and general employment coaching remain separate Types.

types.label: Court and supervision support
types.definition: A defined criminal court, probation or parole pathway and help meeting its obligations.

types.label: Family connection
types.definition: Parent-child relationships, family counseling, parenting or family reunification support connected to incarceration.

types.label: Documents and benefits
types.definition: Help obtaining identity documents, public benefits or coverage needed after release.

types.label: Transportation and essentials
types.definition: Practical transport, clothing, food or similar immediate reentry needs; no inference from provider name.

types.label: Health-care transition
types.definition: Continuity of physical or behavioral health care across release through a defined transition pathway.

types.label: Financial assistance
types.definition: Direct financial support, vouchers or relief for qualifying reentry expenses; excludes ordinary financial-literacy teaching.

types.label: Groceries and food pantries
types.definition: Food boxes, choice pantries, groceries and recurring food distributions; eligibility remains in each record.

types.label: Community meals
types.definition: Ready-to-eat meals available through community meal services; distinguish a public meal from resident-only meals.

types.label: Home food delivery
types.definition: Actual home-delivered meals or groceries, or a defined intake pathway for those deliveries.

types.label: Food benefits and grocery aid
types.definition: Public food-purchasing benefits, food-specific vouchers or grants, and application help for them. Includes SNAP, WIC and qualifying grocery assistance; ordinary pantry distribution is a separate Type.

types.label: Senior nutrition
types.definition: Age-targeted meals, food packages and senior nutrition access; preserve each age and income rule.

types.label: Infant and young-child nutrition
types.definition: WIC and targeted infant/young-child food or formula assistance.

types.label: School and student nutrition
types.definition: School meals, school-mediated food bags and college student food access; public campus distributions retain their broader eligibility.

types.label: Produce and grocery savings
types.definition: Produce-match incentives, farmers-market nutrition benefits and low-cost produce purchasing.

types.label: Find food and referrals
types.definition: Practical public lookup or navigation to an appropriate pantry, meal or food program.

types.label: Meals for enrolled clients
types.definition: Meals or food limited to shelter residents, enrolled service clients or a similarly defined program population.

types.label: Dietary options
types.definition: Explicit kosher, medically adapted or individually tailored food options; availability and accommodations must be confirmed.

types.label: Primary and walk-in care
types.definition: Ongoing or episodic general medical care, including family and pediatric clinics; site and payer rules remain in the record.

types.label: Dental treatment
types.definition: General, restorative, emergency or special-care dentistry, including donated treatment pathways.

types.label: Dental hygiene and prevention
types.definition: Cleanings, sealants, preventive teaching clinics and oral-health outreach; not a promise of restorative treatment.

types.label: Eye exams and medical eye care
types.definition: Optometry, ophthalmology, disease evaluation and eye treatment or surgery pathways.

types.label: Glasses and low-vision support
types.definition: Eyeglass assistance, low-vision rehabilitation, adaptive devices and vision-loss living skills.

types.label: Specialty care and rehabilitation
types.definition: Condition-focused specialist treatment, physical/occupational/pulmonary rehabilitation, medical respite and medical-forensic examination after violence. Exam coordination alone is navigation, not direct examination.

types.label: Prescriptions and medication costs
types.definition: Pharmacy access, prescription discounts and disease-specific medicine assistance.

types.label: Health coverage and medical bills
types.definition: Insurance enrollment and help paying eligible medical or dental charges; not direct cash aid.

types.label: Vaccines and health prevention
types.definition: Immunizations, communicable-disease and public-health screening, structured fall-prevention or chronic-disease self-management education, and preventive nutrition or harm-reduction supplies and guidance. Education is not clinical treatment; general recreation alone does not establish this Type.

types.label: Sexual, reproductive and pregnancy health
types.definition: STI/HIV testing or care, reproductive healthcare, prenatal and postpartum care, lactation or pregnancy-exposure guidance, and related screening. The record distinguishes information or testing-only services from ongoing clinical care.

types.label: Medical equipment
types.definition: Loans or access to mobility, bathing and other durable medical equipment.

types.label: Mobile and home-based care
types.definition: Clinical outreach at homes, facilities, schools or changing community sites.

types.label: Healthcare navigation and transportation
types.definition: Practical appointment, referral, health-system or medical-transport assistance.

types.label: Diagnostic testing
types.definition: Dedicated laboratory or imaging access; specific exam and location must be confirmed.

types.label: Emergency shelter
types.definition: Short-term overnight shelter or direct shelter-admission routes; screening and capacity remain explicit.

types.label: Transitional and supported housing
types.definition: Time-limited or supportive housing with programme-specific eligibility and case management.

types.label: Housing assessment and navigation
types.definition: Coordinated-entry assessment, shelter linkage and practical housing-system navigation.

types.label: Street outreach
types.definition: Teams that engage people outside conventional offices and connect them with support.

types.label: Cooling and daytime rest
types.definition: Day centres, seasonal cooling or respite spaces and specifically designated access routes such as heat-relief transportation. A transport-only entry does not itself offer a resting space; none of these services alone implies an overnight bed.

types.label: Meals and basic supplies
types.definition: Food, clothing and personal supplies for people experiencing homelessness.

types.label: Showers and laundry
types.definition: Practical access to bathing or clean clothes.

types.label: Documents, mail and storage
types.definition: ID assistance, mailing access and secure belongings support.

types.label: Health care and respite
types.definition: Medical or mental-health care, care navigation, healthcare outreach and recuperative respite tailored to people experiencing homelessness. Records distinguish nonclinical connections from clinical treatment and residential recovery.

types.label: Housing stability support
types.definition: Prevention, benefits or income-linked help to sustain or regain housing.

types.label: Court and legal support
types.definition: Specialized case-management or legal routes addressing barriers associated with homelessness.

types.label: Pet support
types.definition: Pet supplies, healthcare or accommodation relevant to people experiencing homelessness.

types.label: Housing navigation
types.definition: Help finding housing, assessment, application support or outreach connecting people to housing; not a promise of a unit.

types.label: Rent and deposit help
types.definition: Rental subsidies, homelessness prevention, rapid rehousing or move-in/deposit assistance with programme-specific eligibility.

types.label: Affordable rentals
types.definition: Income-restricted apartments, vouchers and rental application/waitlist programmes.

types.label: Emergency shelter
types.definition: Short-term crisis shelter and direct coordinated shelter-entry routes.

types.label: Transitional housing
types.definition: Time-limited housing with a plan toward longer-term stability.

types.label: Recovery housing
types.definition: Sober living or residential recovery programmes; treatment and house requirements are stated separately.

types.label: Supported living and foster homes
types.definition: Residential or in-home daily-living support for disability or behavioral-health needs, and staffed foster/residential-care placements for children in care. Records state the actual care model and placement authority; ordinary rental apartments, emergency shelter and clinical inpatient admission have separate Types.

types.label: Supportive housing
types.definition: Longer-term housing paired with ongoing support services.

types.label: Home repairs and accessibility
types.definition: Repairs, accessibility modifications and essential home-system improvements that keep a residence safe or habitable, including approved weatherization and temporary cooling-equipment loans. Ownership, landlord permission and repair versus loan rules belong to the particular programme; ordinary bill discounts are not repairs.

types.label: Homeownership help
types.definition: Housing counseling and assistance with buying or keeping an owned home.

types.label: Medical respite
types.definition: Temporary residential recovery for people who cannot safely recover on the street or in ordinary shelter.

types.label: Pet housing support
types.definition: Temporary animal care and assistance that remove pet-related barriers to housing or shelter.

types.label: State identification
types.definition: Arizona state ID, driver-license or replacement-credential issuance and direct assistance obtaining them.

types.label: Birth and civil records
types.definition: Birth, death, marriage and other certified civil records, including help obtaining them.

types.label: Social Security cards
types.definition: Replacement Social Security cards and assistance assembling the required evidence.

types.label: Application and fee help
types.definition: Hands-on document navigation, applications, appointments, transport or fee assistance; specific limits remain in Information.

types.label: Immigration and consular documents
types.definition: Immigration, citizenship, passport, tax-identification or foreign-consular documents and their supporting procedures.

types.label: Tribal records
types.definition: Tribe-specific enrollment, identification and membership records.

types.label: Name changes and corrections
types.definition: Legal name changes or correction of identity records and help updating documents afterward.

types.label: Mail and document storage
types.definition: A reliable mailing address or secure storage for important identity documents.

types.label: Supporting records
types.definition: Education, military, benefit and occupational records used to establish a history, credential or eligibility; these are not necessarily accepted photo identification.

types.label: Identity protection
types.definition: Identity-theft recovery or identity/address protection for endangered people.

types.label: Immigration applications
types.definition: Help with immigration forms, documents, consultations or official application procedures.

types.label: Citizenship preparation
types.definition: Naturalization application support, civics, interview practice and citizenship-test preparation.

types.label: Asylum and removal defense
types.definition: Legal representation or specialized help with asylum and removal proceedings.

types.label: Detention and court access
types.definition: Detention-focused assistance, advocates, hearings, check-ins and court administration.

types.label: Rights and protection
types.definition: Rights education, community protection, consular assistance and complaints about misconduct or fraud.

types.label: Refugee settlement
types.definition: Resettlement, integration and ongoing casework specifically for refugees or other eligible newcomers.

types.label: English and education
types.definition: English learning, school/college access and other newcomer education.

types.label: Work and household support
types.definition: Newcomer-focused employment, housing navigation, household essentials and community connection.

types.label: Health and benefits
types.definition: Newcomer health care, medical screening, public benefits and coverage access.

types.label: Child and survivor support
types.definition: Specialized services for immigrant children or survivors of violence, torture or trafficking.

types.label: Advice and referrals
types.definition: Brief legal consultations, triage and help finding an appropriate legal-service provider.

types.label: Forms and case procedures
types.definition: Self-help legal forms, filing directions, court or administrative-review procedures and case administration. A form or instructions tool does not provide representation.

types.label: Housing and tenant rights
types.definition: Eviction, landlord-tenant disputes, housing discrimination and manufactured-home rights.

types.label: Family law
types.definition: Divorce, parenting, child support, child protection and related family-court matters.

types.label: Protection and victims’ rights
types.definition: Protective orders, survivor advocacy and enforcement of crime victims’ rights.

types.label: Immigration law
types.definition: Immigration applications, representation, detention issues and immigration-related legal support.

types.label: Criminal cases and record relief
types.definition: Criminal defense, specialty criminal courts, wrongful convictions and record-related remedies.

types.label: Civil and disability rights
types.definition: Disability, education and other civil-rights claims, advocacy and complaint routes.

types.label: Workplace rights
types.definition: Wages, employment discrimination, workplace protections and employment-related legal disputes.

types.label: Benefits and insurance
types.definition: Public benefits, veterans benefits, health coverage and insurance disputes.

types.label: Debt, tax and consumer problems
types.definition: Debt, bankruptcy, tax debts and taxpayer disputes, consumer fraud, contracts and other consumer-law disputes. Tax-return preparation alone is not legal dispute assistance.

types.label: Wills and probate
types.definition: Estate planning, probate, adult guardianship and related legal procedures.

types.label: Mediation
types.definition: Neutral mediation or referrals to help parties resolve a dispute without assuming either side has a lawyer.

types.label: Crisis help
types.definition: Immediate crisis counseling, clinical stabilization or mobile crisis response.

types.label: Counseling
types.definition: Individual, group or family psychotherapy.

types.label: Psychiatry and medication
types.definition: Psychiatric care and medication management.

types.label: Intensive treatment and support
types.definition: Inpatient psychiatric treatment, psychiatric partial-hospitalization or intensive-outpatient programmes, ACT, specialized SMI health-home care and clinically supported residential mental-health care. Ordinary weekly therapy, generic case management or substance-use treatment without an established mental-health component alone does not establish this level of support.

types.label: Peer and recovery support
types.definition: Nonclinical peer support, recovery groups and community participation.

types.label: Family and parent support
types.definition: Family peer navigation, caregiver advocacy and support with children’s mental-health systems.

types.label: Early psychosis
types.definition: Specialist intervention for a first episode of psychosis.

types.label: Pregnancy and postpartum
types.definition: Perinatal mental-health counseling, support and care navigation.

types.label: Trauma and survivor care
types.definition: Targeted care for trauma, abuse or violence survivors.

types.label: Access and rights
types.definition: Service eligibility, coverage, clinical escalation, advocacy and court-linked access.

types.label: School and college support
types.definition: Mental-health care or navigation through a school or student service.

types.label: Prevention and wellness
types.definition: Mental-health education, suicide prevention, resilience and early supportive connection.

types.label: Psychological evaluation
types.definition: Specialized psychological or developmental assessment beyond routine treatment intake.

types.label: Arts and learning
types.definition: Creative classes and non-credit learning for community participation.

types.label: Recreation and wellness
types.definition: Fitness, movement and recreational participation.

types.label: Social connection
types.definition: Peer activities, supportive networks and inclusive community participation.

types.label: Mentoring and volunteering
types.definition: Opportunities to mentor, contribute cultural knowledge or volunteer.

types.label: Practical navigation
types.definition: Help finding services or overcoming barriers to joining community life.

types.label: Pet support
types.definition: Help preserving the human-animal relationship during hardship.

types.label: Benefits and money
types.definition: Help with benefits applications, bills, taxes and affordability.

types.label: Meals and food
types.definition: Congregate or delivered meals, food packages and food benefits.

types.label: Help at home
types.definition: Personal care, household tasks and practical support for living at home.

types.label: Rides
types.definition: Rides or concrete assistance arranging appropriate transportation.

types.label: Caregiver support and respite
types.definition: Education, support and relief for unpaid caregivers, including adult day care.

types.label: Dementia care and support
types.definition: Assessment, care, education and support specifically related to dementia or memory loss.

types.label: Legal rights and protection
types.definition: Civil legal help, advance planning, exploitation reporting and resident advocacy.

types.label: Housing and home safety
types.definition: Housing arrangements, repairs, accessibility and home-safety improvements.

types.label: Social connection and learning
types.definition: Activities, community connection, arts, learning and digital skills.

types.label: Disability access
types.definition: Vision, hearing, mobility and assistive-technology supports.

types.label: Health coverage and care navigation
types.definition: Older-adult health-insurance counseling, long-term-care enrollment, clinical access and navigation for health, safety or care-planning needs. A referral service does not itself provide treatment or personal care.

types.label: Work and volunteering
types.definition: Employment training and structured opportunities to contribute as a volunteer.

types.label: Public transit
types.definition: Scheduled bus, rail, circulator and public microtransit services.

types.label: Accessible rides
types.definition: Disability-related paratransit and accessible on-demand ride options.

types.label: Medical rides
types.definition: Ground transportation to health appointments or clinical care.

types.label: Volunteer rides
types.definition: Trips supplied by volunteer-driver and neighbor-help programs.

types.label: Fares and fuel
types.definition: Passes, fare reductions, fuel grants and medical-travel reimbursement.

types.label: Vehicles and repairs
types.definition: Vehicle repair, maintenance, ownership or vehicle-placement assistance.

types.label: Bicycles
types.definition: Bicycles, bicycle repair and bicycle safety equipment or education.

types.label: Driving documents and holds
types.definition: Driver licenses, driving-related fee waivers and court or registration holds.

types.label: Work commutes
types.definition: Carpool, vanpool and employment-related commuting assistance.

types.label: Program-linked rides
types.definition: Transport limited to enrolled disability, education, shelter or other program participants.

types.label: Planning and travel skills
types.definition: Help finding ride options, planning trips or learning to use transit.

types.label: Medical flights
types.definition: Charitable flights for medically necessary long-distance travel.

types.label: Roadside help
types.definition: Limited roadside safety and stranded-motorist assistance.

types.label: Utility bill help
types.definition: Grants or direct assistance for utility bills, deposits or related financial crises.

types.label: Bill discounts
types.definition: Recurring or seasonal reductions to utility charges or rates.

types.label: Payment plans
types.definition: Installments, extensions, budget billing or repayable account advances.

types.label: Phone plans
types.definition: Discounted telephone or mobile service and Lifeline provider options.

types.label: Home internet
types.definition: Affordable or subsidized internet plans and take-home connectivity.

types.label: Devices
types.definition: Computers, hotspots and other general digital equipment to purchase, receive or borrow.

types.label: Public internet
types.definition: Internet access or public computers at shared community locations.

types.label: Technology help
types.definition: Digital skills, practical technology support and finding suitable connectivity resources.

types.label: Accessible communication
types.definition: Relay calling or equipment/training for disability-related communication needs.

types.label: Home energy savings
types.definition: Weatherization, efficient equipment, shade or water conservation that reduce future use.

types.label: Cooling and repairs
types.definition: Cooling equipment or repairs to essential home systems.

types.label: Application and advocacy
types.definition: Help choosing programmes, applying for benefits or resolving utility-related complaints.

types.label: Alerts and outage support
types.definition: Account notifications, outage planning and priority restoration, including support for qualifying medical needs.

types.label: Benefits help
types.definition: Help applying for or managing military and VA benefits.

types.label: Legal help
types.definition: Legal advice, representation, discharge reviews or court programmes.

types.label: Jobs and careers
types.definition: Job search, career preparation and employment support.

types.label: Education and training
types.definition: College access, education benefits or occupational training.

types.label: Financial help
types.definition: Payments, bill assistance, pensions or tax relief.

types.label: Housing and homelessness
types.definition: Shelter, housing access and housing stability.

types.label: Medical and dental care
types.definition: Clinical health, nursing, dental or vision services.

types.label: Mental health and recovery
types.definition: Counselling, crisis response, treatment and recovery support.

types.label: Peer and family support
types.definition: Social connection, family support and military-community navigation.

types.label: Transportation
types.definition: Rides or reimbursement for eligible travel.

types.label: Home repairs and accessibility
types.definition: Home modification, repairs and disability-related adaptations.

types.label: Household and pet needs
types.definition: Furnishings, basic items and keeping pets during instability.

types.label: Business support
types.definition: Counselling and training for military entrepreneurs.

types.label: Military records
types.definition: Obtaining, safeguarding or correcting military-service documentation.

types.label: Housing legal help
types.definition: Legal advice, representation or court help for eviction, landlord-tenant problems, housing discrimination and related housing rights; general housing search is a separate Type.

types.label: Workplace rights
types.definition: Help with wage claims, employment discrimination, workplace accommodations and related employment-law disputes. A rights provider does not necessarily supply job placement or represent every case.

types.label: Child passenger safety
types.definition: Child car-seat or booster education, installation checks, inspections and specialized safe-travel consultations. A class or inspection does not guarantee a free seat or a ride.

types.label: Youth mentoring and skills
types.definition: Structured youth mentoring, social-development or practical independent-living skills programmes. Mentoring is distinct from clinical treatment, ordinary recreation and agency-only case management.

types.label: Life skills and wellbeing
types.definition: Structured nonclinical learning in everyday decisions, personal safety, recovery skills, resilience or independent living. Includes defined prevention curricula and arts, nature, cultural or community lifelong-learning courses; general counseling, peer support or leisure events alone do not establish a course.

types.label: Self-employment
types.definition: Practical business-startup or self-employment learning, mentoring, counseling and navigation. A loan, grant, business approval or resulting income is not implied.

types.label: Document and filing fees
types.definition: Payment or waiver of identity-document, court-document or immigration/application filing charges. Does not imply the underlying application is approved or that legal representation, medical charges or tuition are covered.

forGroups.label: Caregivers
forGroups.definition: Support for unpaid caregivers of older adults, people with disabilities or people with substantial health needs. Includes caregiver-specific respite, education or support; ordinary parenting alone does not qualify.

forGroups.label: Domestic violence survivors
forGroups.definition: A dedicated domestic/intimate-partner abuse safety, shelter, advocacy, legal or recovery pathway. Other uses of the word survivor do not qualify.

forGroups.label: Families
forGroups.definition: A service designed for a household, parent-child unit, kinship family or family supporters. A family-law case alone does not establish a family-service program.

forGroups.label: Foster & kinship families
forGroups.definition: A specific foster-care, adoptive-family or relative/kinship-caregiver service or eligibility route. General parenting and a vague child-welfare reference do not automatically qualify.

forGroups.label: Homeless
forGroups.definition: A program specifically addressing homelessness, unsheltered living or imminent housing loss. Poverty, food need or ordinary rental assistance alone does not establish this pathway.

forGroups.label: Immigrants
forGroups.definition: An immigration, refugee, asylee or newcomer-specific eligibility, legal or settlement pathway. Language use alone does not establish immigration status.

forGroups.label: LGBTQ+
forGroups.definition: A dedicated LGBTQ+ program, coordinator or explicitly documented population-specific access pathway. General nondiscrimination alone does not qualify.

forGroups.label: Low-income households
forGroups.definition: An explicit financial-eligibility, means-tested or dedicated low-income assistance pathway. Being free, nonprofit or generally available does not by itself qualify.

forGroups.label: Medically vulnerable
forGroups.definition: A dedicated condition, recovery, medical-equipment or clinically vulnerable access pathway such as cancer rides, NICU support or medical respite. General patients or all Medicaid members do not automatically qualify.

forGroups.label: Men
forGroups.definition: A dedicated men’s program, men’s housing or father-specific pathway. A general service admitting adults does not qualify solely because men may participate.

forGroups.label: Native American
forGroups.definition: A tribal-member-specific or explicitly Native/urban-Indian culturally focused program. Tribal-land benefit geography alone does not establish identity-based eligibility; culturally focused programs may also welcome other clients.

forGroups.label: People with disabilities
forGroups.definition: A disability-targeted program, eligibility route or documented disability accommodation. Diagnosis or participation in health care alone does not qualify. Includes the more specific vision and hearing groups.

forGroups.label: Pet owners
forGroups.definition: A documented pet-accommodation, pet-supply or pet-related access pathway. This does not promise that every animal or shelter placement is accepted.

forGroups.label: Pregnant/postpartum
forGroups.definition: A pregnancy, birth, lactation, postpartum or perinatal-loss pathway. General women’s health alone does not qualify.

forGroups.label: Re-entry
forGroups.definition: A service explicitly targeted to people preparing for release, returning from custody, under justice supervision or addressing a criminal-record barrier. Prior incarceration is not required for every included program.

forGroups.label: Seniors
forGroups.definition: A dedicated older-adult program, age-based benefit or specific older-adult access pathway. A general service available across all ages does not qualify solely because it mentions older adults.

forGroups.label: Spanish
forGroups.definition: Explicit Spanish-language service, interpretation, staff or program access. This describes language access and does not imply ethnicity or immigration status.

forGroups.label: Students
forGroups.definition: A service tied to school or college enrollment, a school partnership or student-specific eligibility. General adult education open to the public does not automatically qualify.

forGroups.label: Uninsured/underinsured
forGroups.definition: Explicit care, fee assistance or enrollment access for people lacking adequate health coverage. Merely accepting insurance does not qualify.

forGroups.label: Veterans
forGroups.definition: A dedicated military-service, veteran or eligible military-household pathway. Service, discharge and program rules differ.

forGroups.label: Women
forGroups.definition: A dedicated women’s program or women-specific health, housing or support pathway. A name or a condition affecting all genders does not establish this group.

forGroups.label: Youth
forGroups.definition: A child, adolescent or explicitly youth-targeted young-adult pathway. Program ages vary; a general adult service is not tagged merely because some young adults could use it.

forGroups.label: Blind & low vision
forGroups.definition: A specifically documented blind/low-vision service, eligibility or vision-access accommodation; includes the broader People with disabilities group. Training people to produce braille does not imply trainees are blind.

forGroups.label: Deaf & hard of hearing
forGroups.definition: A dedicated deaf, hard-of-hearing or DeafBlind pathway, including explicitly offered interpreting or communication access; includes People with disabilities.

forGroups.label: Abuse survivors
forGroups.definition: Dedicated response to sexual assault/abuse, trafficking, exploitation or other interpersonal abuse. Domestic violence has its own retained group. Generic crime-victim, bereavement or trauma language alone does not establish this pathway.

resources.name: Valleywise Health - Prenatal, Postpartum, OB/GYN and Teen Pregnancy Care
resources.description: Valleywise Health provides prenatal, postpartum, newborn, lactation and teen pregnancy care through its safety-net maternity system, including a Mesa community health center and teen-specific support with prenatal education, classes, counseling and community resources.
resources.address: Valleywise Community Health Center - Mesa, 950 E. Main St., Mesa, AZ 85203
resources.hours: Valleywise Community Health Center - Mesa is listed Monday-Friday 7:00 AM-6:00 PM. Teen program classes with same-day prenatal care are described at Phoenix Medical Center on Tuesdays and Maryvale on Thursdays, so call to confirm Mesa components.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Valleywise maternity services include prenatal care, postpartum care, newborn care and lactation support. The Teen Pregnancy Program adds teen-focused pregnancy support, full medical care, counseling, community connection, pregnancy classes, nutrition, fetal development, labor and delivery education, postpartum care, career planning, healthy relationships, breastfeeding and baby care.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are for pregnant and postpartum patients, newborns and pregnant teens needing maternity care through Valleywise Health. Coverage, financial assistance and clinic/hospital requirements depend on the patient's situation and appointment type. Ask about income-based financial assistance and uninsured discounts; the applicable schedule depends on the service and eligibility.

**Population Served**
Pregnant and postpartum patients, newborns, families and pregnant teens in Maricopa County, including Mesa patients served through Valleywise Community Health Center - Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 1-833-855-9973 to schedule maternity care. The Mesa clinic phone is 602-655-6200 at 950 E. Main St., Mesa, AZ 85203. Use MyChart or the request-a-callback option if already connected to Valleywise. Request free Spanish interpretation when scheduling or checking in.

**Important Information to Know**
Labor and delivery are not provided at the Mesa community clinic. The teen page lists Mesa as a Teen Pregnancy Program location, but same-day prenatal care with classes is specifically described at the Phoenix Medical Center and Maryvale. Call before referral to confirm which teen-specific services are delivered in Mesa and which require travel to another Valleywise site.

resources.name: Circle Road Foundation — Live Better recovery-housing scholarships
resources.description: Short-term recovery-housing scholarships and support for people rebuilding after incarceration, detoxification or residential addiction treatment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Short-term recovery-housing scholarships and support for people rebuilding after incarceration, detoxification or residential addiction treatment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The programme focuses on people leaving those settings who face homelessness or housing instability and substance-use or mental-health challenges. Staff must confirm application requirements.

**Population Served**
People transitioning from incarceration, detox or residential treatment who need recovery-housing support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-558-8742 to ask about the Live Better programme, its application process and current funding. Review the programme website before arranging a placement.

**Important Information to Know**
A scholarship, particular residence or immediate opening is not guaranteed. This foundation is separate from Circle the City.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Corrections, Rehabilitation & Reentry — Maricopa Reentry Center
resources.description: ADCRR therapeutic reentry center in Maricopa County for eligible people on community supervision addressing substance abuse or transitioning back into community life.
resources.address: 24601 N 29th Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85027
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A structured therapeutic reentry setting for eligible adults under ADCRR supervision, including substance-use education, treatment opportunities and transition support. ADCRR materials also describe assessments and community-clinic linkage for medical, mental-health and substance-use continuity.

**Eligibility Requirements**
This is not a general public treatment program. It serves people under ADCRR community supervision, including technical violators or people needing structured support to complete community supervision. Placement is controlled by ADCRR/community supervision processes.

**Population Served**
Justice-involved adults in Maricopa County under Arizona community supervision who need reentry support related to substance abuse or community transition.

**How to Best Connect**
Eligible clients should ask their community supervision officer or ADCRR contact about Maricopa Reentry Center placement. ADCRR's public contact number is 602-542-5497.

**Important Information to Know**
Placement is controlled through ADCRR/community supervision. This is not a public walk-in rehabilitation clinic or open shelter. Work through the assigned officer or case contact to establish the appropriate placement and current services.

resources.name: Diverse Ability Incorporated - Peer Navigation Services
resources.description: Diverse Ability Incorporated offers peer navigation services for young people with disabilities, connecting them with resources for self-advocacy, education, employment, independent living and transition-to-adulthood needs.
resources.address: Post Office Box 46316, Phoenix, AZ 85063
resources.hours: Use the request form; response time and meeting format may vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Peer-led resource navigation by trained Arizona young adult leaders with similar lived experience. Navigation examples include self-advocacy, IEP meeting preparation, communication practice, work-readiness resources, postsecondary education resources, college disability supports, Vocational Rehabilitation and job-search preparation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For young people with disabilities seeking help exploring community resources and supports. DAI says peer navigation is no cost to most young people, but each request is reviewed individually.

**Population Served**
Arizona youth and young adults with disabilities, including transition-aged students and young adults in Mesa and Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the official Peer Navigation Services request form or the contact/request-involvement link on the DAI website. Include the young person's goals and what resources are needed.

**Important Information to Know**
DAI states this is not long-term case management, mentoring or buddy matching. It is short-term, peer-led resource navigation tailored to the request.

resources.name: Southwest Family Advocacy Center - Victim Advocacy and Family Advocacy Center Services
resources.description: Southwest Family Advocacy Center is a multidisciplinary West Valley family advocacy center where law enforcement, child protection, prosecution, medical, mental-health and victim-advocacy professionals coordinate on child abuse, sexual assault, domestic violence and elder abuse cases.
resources.address: 2333 N. Pebble Creek Parkway, Suite A-200, Goodyear, AZ 85395
resources.hours: Call main number before visiting. Public site lists main contact but not walk-in intake hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Southwest Family Advocacy Center coordinates victim advocacy, forensic interviews, medical exams, therapy and multidisciplinary response for child abuse, sexual assault, domestic violence and elder abuse investigations.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Best fit appears to be victims and families connected to participating West Valley jurisdictions or investigations. It is not a residential shelter, and eligibility for a Mesa case may depend on law-enforcement jurisdiction or referral.

**Population Served**
Victims and families in Goodyear, Avondale, Buckeye and western Maricopa County service areas, including domestic-violence, sexual-assault, child-abuse and elder-abuse cases.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 623-333-7900 before visiting. Ask whether the case can be served directly, whether an investigating agency referral is needed, and whether advocacy or therapy services are available. Ask about Spanish advocacy or interpretation for the case.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a family advocacy center, not a shelter or countywide hotline. It is a useful reserve for western Maricopa or West Valley cases but should not be used as the primary Mesa shelter route.

resources.name: Arizona Brainfood - Weekend Food Bags
resources.description: Arizona Brainfood provides weekend food bags to students through participating schools, reporting 110 participating schools and about 3,000 students served each weekend.
resources.address: 325 E McKellips Rd, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: School-year program through participating schools; families should ask the school social worker, counselor or front office about access.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Arizona Brainfood provides backpacks or bags of food for students to take home for weekends during the school year through participating schools.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Access appears to run through participating schools and is intended for students experiencing food insecurity. The public page does not provide a household self-application form.

**Population Served**
School children at participating Arizona Brainfood schools, including Mesa and East Valley schools when participating.

**How to Best Connect**
Families should ask the child's school social worker, counselor, family resource staff or front office whether the school participates and how to be added. Organizations can contact Arizona Brainfood through its website.

**Important Information to Know**
This is discreet school-based food support, not a walk-up pantry. The current public page reports 110 participating schools and about 3,000 students per weekend, but the exact current Mesa school list should be confirmed through the child's school.

resources.name: Arizona Achieve — Self-Advocacy and Peer Mentorship
resources.description: A statewide cross-disability self-advocacy coalition with peer mentorship, leadership learning, resources and opportunities to participate in community policy discussions.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

A statewide cross-disability self-advocacy coalition with peer mentorship, leadership learning, resources and opportunities to participate in community policy discussions.

**Eligibility Requirements**

For people with disabilities interested in self-advocacy and participation. Ask about the current mentorship or training process and any event requirements.

**Population Served**

Arizona self-advocates, including people with intellectual or developmental disabilities.

**How to Best Connect**

Email becky@tempearc.org or use the website’s current meeting and participation information. Coalition meetings are generally virtual; confirm the next date and access details.

**Important Information to Know**

This is peer and leadership support, not ongoing case management or legal representation. Arizona Achieve is a project of The Arc of Tempe.

resources.name: AZCEND - Gilbert Utility Discount Program and Rent/Utility Assistance
resources.description: AZCEND provides Gilbert residents with CAP rent, utility, and mortgage assistance plus a Gilbert utility discount for income-eligible Town of Gilbert water customers.
resources.address: Gilbert Heritage Center, 132 W Bruce Ave, Gilbert, AZ 85233
resources.hours: CAP Gilbert: Monday 7:30 AM-6:00 PM, Tuesday-Thursday 7:30 AM-5:00 PM, Friday 8:30 AM-noon. Utility discount questions: Monday-Friday 7:30 AM-4:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Rent, utility, and mortgage assistance for Gilbert residents through AZCEND's Community Action Program. The Gilbert Utility Discount Program can provide a monthly $30 water-bill discount for qualifying Gilbert residents.

**Eligibility Requirements**
CAP rent, utility or mortgage assistance is for Gilbert residents and requires income/hardship documentation and any applicable landlord or vendor paperwork. The water discount requires a Gilbert home, a Town water bill in the applicant’s name and income within the posted limit (listed as 120% AMI). A tenant whose landlord pays all utilities is not eligible for that discount.

**Population Served**
Gilbert households experiencing financial hardship, including income-qualified Town of Gilbert water customers.

**How to Best Connect**
For rent and utility CAP assistance, call 480-892-5331 ext. 200 or email cap@azcend.org. For the Gilbert Utility Discount Program, use the virtual or physical application links on AZCEND's page or call 480-963-1423 ext. 200. The Gilbert Heritage Center is at 132 W. Bruce Ave., Gilbert.

**Important Information to Know**
Both routes are limited to Gilbert. The $30 monthly water discount is not immediate payment of a past-due balance. Complete discount applications are reviewed in 3–5 business days; credits may take 7–10 business days after approval to appear. Renew annually and report address changes. Ask separately about emergency CAP help.

resources.name: City of Glendale - Glendale OnBoard Microtransit and Paratransit ADA
resources.description: Glendale OnBoard provides shared microtransit within Glendale and ADA paratransit for eligible trips, with app or phone booking and published fares.
resources.address: 6210 W Myrtle Ave Building S, Glendale, AZ 85301
resources.hours: Microtransit operates Monday-Friday 7:00 AM-6:00 PM and weekends/observed holidays 7:00 AM-5:00 PM. Ride line hours: Monday-Friday 7:00 AM-5:30 PM; Saturday 7:00 AM-4:00 PM. ADA reservations have separate phone hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Glendale OnBoard offers shared microtransit within Glendale and ADA paratransit. Microtransit is curb-to-curb demand service; ADA paratransit provides door-to-door service for ADA-eligible riders within the qualifying fixed-route buffer.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Microtransit trips must start and end in Glendale. Reduced fares apply to qualifying juniors, seniors and disabled riders. ADA paratransit requires Valley Metro ADA eligibility.

**Population Served**
Glendale riders, including seniors and people with disabilities. Regional ADA trips outside Glendale are handled through Valley Metro Paratransit.

**How to Best Connect**
Book microtransit through the Glendale OnBoard app or call 623-930-3500. ADA paratransit reservations are made at 623-930-3515. For general questions call 623-930-2940.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a Mesa service. Same-day microtransit is weekday-focused; weekend and holiday trips require advance reservation. Cash fares require exact change unless paying by card through the app.

resources.name: NOAH - Cholla Health Center Family and Child Medical Care
resources.description: Scottsdale community health center offering family medical care, well-child visits, immunizations, sick visits and related clinical services near the East Valley.
resources.address: 8705 E. McDowell Rd., Scottsdale, AZ 85257
resources.hours: Cholla medical listing: Monday-Friday 7 AM-6 PM; Saturday 8 AM-1 PM. Confirm the particular service and clinician schedule.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Family medical care including well-child and well-woman exams, immunizations, sick visits, chronic-condition care, prescriptions, laboratory services and referrals. Telehealth is available for many services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Call to discuss the patient's age, clinical need, insurance or self-pay arrangements and appointment availability. Individual services and clinicians may have different schedules.

**Population Served**
Children, adults and families able to reach the Scottsdale Cholla clinic, including Mesa residents seeking a regional alternative.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-882-4545 or request an appointment online. Cholla is at 8705 E. McDowell Rd., Scottsdale; its medical listing shows weekday and Saturday hours.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm which services are provided at Cholla before travel. The current medical page supports family and child care but does not establish a currently open prenatal panel; ask directly rather than assuming maternity care or delivery is included.

resources.name: Arizona Board of Regents — Arizona Promise Program
resources.description: Last-dollar scholarship covering qualifying students’ in-state tuition and required program and mandatory fees at ASU, NAU or the University of Arizona after other aid. Up to eight academic semesters may be covered.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Last-dollar scholarship covering qualifying students’ in-state tuition and required program and mandatory fees at ASU, NAU or the University of Arizona after other aid. Up to eight academic semesters may be covered.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Arizona residency, graduation from an Arizona high school with at least a 2.5 GPA, Pell Grant eligibility, and first-time, full-time, on-campus degree enrollment in the fall immediately after high school. Universities can review permitted enrollment gaps. Admission, FAFSA and verification deadlines apply.

**Population Served**

Eligible recent Arizona high-school graduates entering an Arizona public university.

**How to Best Connect**

Apply for university admission and complete FAFSA and requested verification. There is no separate Promise application. Contact the university’s financial-aid office; current guidance emphasizes April 1, so ask about the applicable entering-year deadline.

**Important Information to Know**

Housing, meals, parking and books are not covered. This is separate from Mesa College Promise and Maricopa Promise. It is not a general scholarship for returning adult or transfer students.

resources.name: SMART Recovery - Mesa Meetings and Family & Friends Meeting Finder
resources.description: SMART Recovery's meeting finder helps people locate Mesa, online and national mutual-aid meetings, including Family & Friends support for people affected by a loved one's addictive behavior.
resources.hours: Meeting schedules change; check the SMART Recovery meeting finder before attending.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Meeting-finder access to SMART Recovery mutual-aid meetings for people seeking addiction recovery support and Family & Friends meetings for people affected by a loved one's addictive behavior. Options may include local in-person and online meetings.

**Eligibility Requirements**
SMART meetings are mutual-aid supports, not clinical treatment. Meeting eligibility, format, facilitator and any registration requirement vary by meeting listing.

**Population Served**
People in Mesa and online seeking self-management addiction recovery support, and family/friends affected by another person's addictive behavior.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the official SMART Recovery meeting finder and search Mesa, Arizona, then confirm the meeting time, address, format and any registration step before attending.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an access point and directory for meetings, but it directly assists clients in finding support meetings. It is not detox, MAT, outpatient treatment or a crisis service.

resources.name: Fountain of Life Christian Fellowship - Mission Kitchen 153 Emergency Food Boxes
resources.description: Mission Kitchen 153 at Fountain of Life Christian Fellowship offers emergency food box signup with twice-weekly pickup beginning at 5:00 PM.
resources.address: 6625 E Main St, Mesa, AZ 85205
resources.hours: Pickup begins at 5:00 PM on two weekly service days; exact days should be confirmed on the signup form or with the church.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Mission Kitchen 153 provides emergency food boxes. The official page says the program serves twice a week and allows people to choose the day that works best through the food box signup form.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The page is for people needing an emergency food box and does not list income, ID or residency requirements. Registration through the form appears required.

**Population Served**
East Valley and Mesa households needing emergency food boxes.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Mission Kitchen 153 food box signup form on the official page. Pickup begins at 5:00 PM. Email info@fountainoflife.tv if the form or schedule needs confirmation.

**Important Information to Know**
The official page confirms twice-weekly service but does not expose exact weekly days in the text. Confirm the selected pickup day through the form before travel.

resources.name: APS — Payment arrangements
resources.description: Offers payment arrangements for past-due APS electric bills.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Offers payment arrangements for past-due APS electric bills.

**Eligibility Requirements**
APS customers with an outstanding balance of at least $75 typically qualify, subject to account review and any required upfront payment. Budget Billing customers are not eligible.

**Population Served**
APS customers needing more time to pay an outstanding electric bill.

**How to Best Connect**
Request an arrangement through the APS account portal or call to discuss the available term. Monthly installments are at least $25; a 12-month arrangement requires a past-due balance exceeding $300.

**Important Information to Know**
Pay current charges as well as the installment. This is not debt forgiveness. Contact APS promptly if an agreed payment cannot be made; a broken arrangement can lead to disconnection.

resources.name: Society of St. Vincent de Paul Phoenix - Ozanam Manor Transitional Housing
resources.description: Ozanam Manor is a Phoenix transitional-housing community helping eligible adults experiencing homelessness move toward stable, independent housing.
resources.address: 320 W Watkins Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.hours: Call 602-850-6900 between 8:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. for eligibility screening.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Transitional housing with community support, group activities, life courses and individual case management to help residents work toward permanent housing. Ozanam Manor has select beds for veterans; that pathway uses VA referral.

**Eligibility Requirements**
SVdP lists transitional-housing eligibility for adults age 55+, adults age 18+ living with a disability, adults age 18+ working or looking for work, and select veteran beds at Ozanam Manor. Veterans should work through the VA for Ozanam Manor veteran-bed placement.

**Population Served**
Eligible adults experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County, including older adults, adults with disabilities, adults working or seeking work and selected veterans.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-850-6900 between 8:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. for eligibility screening. Veterans should also contact the Phoenix VA CRRC/homeless-veteran care team for the veteran-bed referral route.

**Important Information to Know**
There is no cost if a resident has no income; otherwise SVdP states the cost is 30% of income. A screening call and face-to-face interview are required, and placement depends on eligibility and bed availability.

resources.name: Maricopa County Civil Mental Health Court / Court-Ordered Evaluation and Treatment
resources.description: Maricopa County’s civil mental-health court administers court-ordered evaluation and treatment proceedings under Arizona Title 36, with clinical evaluation, court review and representation rights.
resources.hours: Court and treatment access depend on the Title 36/court-ordered mental-health case; use crisis services immediately for an active crisis.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Civil court proceedings for court-ordered mental-health evaluation and treatment under Arizona Title 36. Hearing arrangements, including virtual participation where offered, depend on the court and treatment setting.

**Eligibility Requirements**
This is not routine voluntary counseling. It applies when a person may need involuntary evaluation or treatment because a behavioral-health crisis places the person at risk of self-harm, harm to others, or inability to function safely. Petitions, court review, clinical evaluation, due-process rights, and provider decisions apply.

**Population Served**
People involved in Arizona’s civil court process for court-ordered mental-health evaluation or treatment, and those assisting them.

**How to Best Connect**
For immediate crisis help, call or text 988 or call the Central Arizona Crisis Line at 602-222-9444 or 800-631-1314. For the legal process, review the Maricopa County Superior Court Mental Health Department and Public Advocate information before filing or acting on someone else's behalf. The county main line is 602-506-3011.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a civil legal process with specific statutory criteria and rights. It is not a walk-in clinic or criminal reentry programme. Use current court instructions or an appropriate crisis service; an announced treatment-bed expansion does not establish present availability.

resources.name: Heaven's Hummingbirds - Pregnancy and Infant Loss Support Group
resources.description: East Valley pregnancy and infant-loss support with a recurring in-person group associated with Mercy Gilbert and Chandler Regional Medical Centers.
resources.address: Medical Office Building at Mercy Gilbert Medical Center, 3420 S. Mercy Rd., Gilbert; third floor, McAuley Rooms A and B
resources.hours: Published group: third Monday of the month, 6-7:30 PM; email to confirm the next meeting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Pregnancy and infant-loss support, remembrance and connection with other bereaved families through a recurring East Valley group.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Contact the program about participation, current format and any registration or fee requirements. The public group notice does not state that a family must have received care at either hospital.

**Population Served**
Bereaved parents and families able to travel to Gilbert, including Mesa families affected by pregnancy or infant loss.

**How to Best Connect**
Email HeavensHummingbirds@CommonSpirit.org with questions or to RSVP. The published group meets on the third Monday, 6-7:30 PM, at 3420 S. Mercy Rd., third floor, McAuley Rooms A and B.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm the meeting before travel. This listing establishes a support group, not an emergency mental-health service or a guaranteed perinatal-hospice admission. The meeting is in a medical office building rather than the hospital's main street address.

resources.name: Teen Lifeline - Teen Crisis Phone and Text Line
resources.description: Arizona teen crisis phone and text support, with calls available 24/7 and daily teen peer counseling/texting hours.
resources.address: Mail only: P.O. Box 10745, Phoenix, AZ 85064
resources.hours: Calls open 24/7/365. Texting and peer counseling are open daily 3:00 PM-9:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Teen-focused crisis phone and text support. Calls are available 24/7; texting and teen peer counseling are available daily from 3 PM to 9 PM. Teen Lifeline also operates the separately listed Caring Contacts post-discharge programme, which has its own enrollment process.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Crisis support is designed for teens and their families. No psychiatric discharge or Caring Contacts enrollment is required to contact the crisis line.

**Population Served**
Arizona teens, including Mesa and Maricopa County youth, plus parents, schools and families concerned about a teen. The Maricopa County number is 602-248-8336; outside Maricopa County, call 1-800-248-8336.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-248-8336 anytime, or text that number daily 3–9 PM. Outside Maricopa County, the voice number is 800-248-8336. Adults concerned about a teen may also call. For Caring Contacts after psychiatric discharge, ask about referral/enrollment at intake@teenlifeline.org.

**Important Information to Know**
Voice calls are 24/7, but teen peer counseling and texting have narrower daily hours. This is youth-specific peer crisis support supervised through Teen Lifeline, not ongoing therapy or medication management.

resources.name: Andre House of Arizona - Hospitality Services for People Experiencing Homelessness
resources.description: Andre House of Arizona provides low-barrier hospitality services in Phoenix for people experiencing homelessness, including dinner, clothing closet, laundry slots, showers, hygiene kits, backpacks, blankets and guest support.
resources.address: 213 S 11th Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.hours: Dinner Saturday-Thursday 5:00-6:00 PM, line at 4:00 PM. Clothing Tuesday/Thursday 12:30-3:00 PM and Saturday 1:00-3:00 PM. Laundry Monday-Wednesday 8:30 AM-noon with limited slots. Showers Monday-Thursday 12:30-3:00 PM. Pascente Office Monday-Thursday and Saturday/Sunday 1:00-3:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Dinner service, clothing closet, laundry slots, showers, hygiene kits, backpacks, blankets and hospitality/support through the Pascente Office and porter station.

**Eligibility Requirements**
