Andre House welcomes guests seeking basic-needs support. Specific service access depends on line times, daily capacity and item availability.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness or severe poverty in the Phoenix area, including Mesa residents able to travel to downtown Phoenix.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to 213 S 11th Ave in Phoenix during the posted service time for the needed service, and arrive before the listed line time for dinner, clothing, showers or laundry. Call 602-255-0580 for current operations.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a Phoenix reserve option, not Mesa-specific. Laundry has a limited number of slots, and clothing, shower and meal lines can close or fill based on capacity.

resources.name: NATIVE HEALTH Mesa - Behavioral Health
resources.description: Mesa integrated health center offering licensed outpatient behavioral-health services, counseling, psychiatry, recovery services, traditional healing/talking circles and AHCCCS/discount-fee intake pathways.
resources.address: 777 W Southern Ave, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Behavioral-health intakes Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; walk-in and scheduled intakes available. Call the regular clinic number for after-hours advice for non-emergency concerns.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
NATIVE HEALTH Behavioral Health provides culturally appropriate outpatient behavioral-health services and resources, including individual, group and family counseling for ages six and older, psychiatric services for children and adults, recovery services, IOP/SOP and DUI education, court-ordered classes, domestic-violence services, traditional healing and talking circles. The Mesa clinic is one of the listed NATIVE HEALTH locations.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Intakes are required for behavioral-health services except Talking Circle. Bring identification or parent/guardian ID for minors, proof of guardianship when applicable, health insurance or AHCCCS information, Tribal ID or CIB if applicable, and paycheck stubs if applying for the NATIVE HEALTH Discount Fee Program. NATIVE HEALTH accepts AHCCCS Complete Care plans.

**Population Served**
Urban Native American community members and other populations in the Phoenix/Mesa area. Spanish-speaking staff are available at all NATIVE HEALTH locations.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-279-5262 for NATIVE HEALTH Mesa or behavioral-health intake questions. The Mesa clinic is at 777 W Southern Ave, Mesa, AZ 85210. For non-emergency after-hours medical or behavioral-health concerns, call the regular clinic number to reach the answering service.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a crisis line. For after-hours behavioral-health emergencies, the official page points people to the Behavioral Health Crisis Line at 602-222-9444 or 988. Confirm which services are currently delivered at Mesa versus Central Phoenix or NHW locations, especially recovery-service group schedules.

resources.name: Another Level of Community Services, LLC
resources.description: Licensed behavioral health and community re-entry campus in Phoenix offering substance-abuse services, court-approved treatment, IOP, supportive housing, medical/psychiatric services, case management, peer support, and aftercare.
resources.address: 1326 W Hadley St, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-3:00 PM; Friday 8:00 AM-1:00 PM; closed Saturday-Sunday.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
ALOCS provides an integrated 90-day reentry programme with supportive housing, intensive outpatient and court-approved substance-use treatment, medical/psychiatric services, case management, peer support and aftercare. Reentry supports also include GED assistance and career training. Court-related anger management and domestic-violence courses address behavior change.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official site emphasizes people recently incarcerated and people needing court-approved treatment, behavioral health, or re-entry support. Program-specific eligibility, payer/funding, and whether Mesa residents can enroll should be confirmed through intake.

**Population Served**
Adults in Maricopa County with re-entry, court-ordered treatment, behavioral-health, and substance-use recovery needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-218-8868, email admin@alocs.com, or use the official contact form. Office hours are Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-3:00 PM and Friday 8:00 AM-1:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
The campus is in Phoenix. Ask about programme eligibility, payer/funding, capacity, transportation and any offense-history exclusions before referral. Domestic-violence courses are not a survivor shelter or safety hotline.

resources.name: Everyone On — Low-cost internet and computer finder
resources.description: Find affordable internet service and computers by ZIP code.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Find affordable internet service and computers by ZIP code.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Anyone may use the finder. Eligibility for an offer depends on the provider, location, income or qualifying benefits.

**Population Served**
Households seeking an affordable computer or internet plan.

**How to Best Connect**
Enter the ZIP code, select applicable eligibility circumstances and review the available offers. Apply with the provider that fits the household.

**Important Information to Know**
The finder is not a grant or internet provider. Verify coverage, equipment charges, current prices and eligibility directly with the listed company.

resources.name: AllThrive 365 - Grandparents Raising Grandchildren / Kinship Care Services
resources.description: AllThrive 365 Grandparents Raising Grandchildren supports grandparents and kinship caregivers with support groups, education, resource navigation, financial-assistance opportunities, community connection and caregiving guidance.
resources.address: 1201 E. Thomas Rd., Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.hours: Resource Navigator hours are Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
GrandKin Cafe support groups in English and Spanish, educational workshops, resource navigation, financial-assistance opportunities for children's activities, community connections, and guidance or advocacy around caregiving, school, legal and family-system challenges.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For grandparents and other kinship caregivers raising relatives’ children. Support groups, financial-assistance opportunities and other services may have different intake rules. Ask which caregiving-authority and household documents are required for the particular service.

**Population Served**
Grandparents, older relatives and kinship caregivers raising children, plus the children in their care.

**How to Best Connect**
Email PatriciaD@allthrive365.org or use AllThrive's Resource Navigator. The Resource Navigator can be reached at 602-285-0505 ext. 180, Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
This is support, education, navigation and possible activity-related financial assistance, not guaranteed cash or legal representation. AllThrive is the current programme contact; older Duet forms and phone extensions may differ. Ask about the current intake requirements before collecting documents.

resources.name: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services - Form I-90 replacement Permanent Resident Card
resources.description: USCIS Form I-90 is the official federal application to replace or renew an existing Permanent Resident Card for eligible lawful permanent residents and some conditional permanent residents.
resources.address: Use the address on the USCIS appointment notice; Phoenix ASC evidence may be appointment-only for biometrics and is not a walk-in service.
resources.hours: Online filing and mail filing are generally available through USCIS. Any in-person appointment is controlled by a USCIS appointment notice.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Form I-90 is used to replace or renew an existing Permanent Resident Card, including cards that are lost, stolen, destroyed, mutilated, expired, expiring or incorrect, depending on the applicant's status and filing reason.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For lawful permanent residents and permanent residents in commuter status seeking replacement or renewal of a Permanent Resident Card. Conditional permanent residents may use I-90 for replacement of an existing card in some situations, but not to renew an expiring two-year conditional card when they must file to remove conditions.

**Population Served**
Eligible lawful permanent residents living in Mesa and Maricopa County who need to replace or renew a Permanent Resident Card.

**How to Best Connect**
Start at the USCIS Form I-90 page or USCIS online account. Call the USCIS Contact Center at 800-375-5283 if online tools do not resolve the issue or if appointment routing is needed. Attend an Application Support Center only if USCIS sends an appointment notice.

**Important Information to Know**
Filing fees, biometrics, evidence and fee-waiver eligibility depend on the filing reason and current USCIS fee schedule. Immigration legal advice should come from a licensed attorney or DOJ-accredited representative. A lost-card applicant may still need other identity evidence for the filing.

resources.name: Arizona Attorney General's Office - Life Care Planning
resources.description: The Arizona Attorney General's Office provides free Life Care Planning forms, mailed packets and presentations so Arizonans can document health care decision-makers and advance directives.
resources.address: 2005 N. Central Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free Life Care Planning packets and individual forms, including health care power of attorney, mental health care power of attorney, living will, pre-hospital medical directive/DNR forms, POLST information and presentation requests.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The forms are available to Arizonans of all ages. The Attorney General distributes forms but does not accept completed Life Care Planning packets or update registry records.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents planning for future health care decisions, including older adults, medically vulnerable adults and families helping with advance-directive planning.

**How to Best Connect**
Download forms from the official page, visit the Phoenix or Tucson Attorney General office for copies, complete the online Life Care Planning request form, or call 602-542-2123 or 800-352-8431 to request mailed packets. Packets are mailed within 10 business days.

**Important Information to Know**
For questions about registering advance directives, contact Contexture Arizona Healthcare Directives Registry at 602-368-6371 or azhdr.org. DNR printing requirements are specific; follow the official instructions exactly.

resources.name: 211 Arizona — Community-resource navigation
resources.description: Helps people in Arizona find food, health services, identification/document help and other community resources by need and location.
resources.hours: Daily 9 AM–7 PM by phone; online resource directory available separately.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Community-resource navigation across Arizona, including food programmes, identification and vital-record help, document-fee and mailing-address services, clinics, dental/vision assistance, medical equipment, benefits and healthcare transportation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The referral service is public; each referred program sets its own eligibility and availability.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents and people helping someone in Arizona, including callers needing language assistance.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 211 or 877-211-8661, daily 9 a.m.–7 p.m., or use the online resource search. English and Spanish operators and interpretation in other languages are available.

**Important Information to Know**
211 makes referrals; it does not issue records, provide clinical care, reserve appointments or guarantee funds, food or agency capacity. Check the referred provider’s intake before travel.

resources.name: Maricopa County Attorney's Office · Diversion Programs
resources.description: Maricopa County Attorney's Office diversion programs that may route eligible defendants to community-based education or treatment, including felony diversion for controlled-substance charges, Justice Court substance-use/cognitive-skills classes and Veterans Diversion.
resources.address: 225 W Madison St, Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Maricopa County Attorney's Office offers diversion programs as alternatives to traditional case processing. Felony Diversion can include cognitive-behavioral group counseling, individual counseling, case management and drug testing for eligible felony offenses including controlled-substance possession. Justice Court Diversion can place referred individuals into an 8-hour substance-use or cognitive-skills class. Veterans Diversion offers veteran-focused treatment and services with community partners.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on the charged offense, criminal history, prosecutorial discretion and program suitability. Felony Diversion generally requires qualifying offenses and minimal criminal history. Veterans Diversion is for eligible service members charged with lower-level felonies when offered and accepted.

**Population Served**
Justice-involved Maricopa County defendants or service-member defendants whose cases are eligible for prosecutor-authorized diversion. This is not general public treatment access.

**How to Best Connect**
Clients should work through their defense attorney, prosecutor, court notice or assigned case contact. For general questions, the County Attorney main phone listed on the official site is 602-506-3411. Ask which diversion program applies and what vendor/intake steps are required.

**Important Information to Know**
Participation is not self-enrollment and is not guaranteed. Treatment or classes are tied to criminal-case eligibility and successful completion may affect charges. Do not use this as a substitute for voluntary addiction treatment when a person needs immediate care.

resources.name: Chandler CARE Center — Children’s medical and dental clinics
resources.description: Provides no-cost pediatric medical and dental care for uninsured children with a Chandler residence or school connection.
resources.address: 777 E. Galveston St., Chandler, AZ 85225
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides no-cost pediatric medical and dental care for uninsured children with a Chandler residence or school connection.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Must live in Chandler and/or attend a Chandler Unified School District school and be uninsured; AHCCCS patients cannot use this clinic. Birth through age 18, with older CUSD students also eligible.

**Population Served**
Qualifying Chandler/CUSD children and students, including Mesa residents who attend a CUSD school.

**How to Best Connect**
For medical appointments call 480-812-7910; for dental appointments call 480-812-7903. The clinic is at 777 E. Galveston St., Chandler.

**Important Information to Know**
The eligibility boundary is narrower than Maricopa County. Confirm service availability, age-specific dental needs and any preventive-clinic referral before travel.

resources.name: The Salvation Army Mesa Corps — Food assistance and seasonal cooling
resources.description: Mesa Salvation Army location for emergency food inquiries and seasonal heat-relief cooling and hydration.
resources.address: 241 E 6th St, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: General office: Monday–Friday 8–11:30 AM. Heat activation: 11 AM–5 PM on Excessive Heat Warning days, May–September, including weekends but excluding federal holidays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency food-box inquiries and related basic-needs help, with pet food when available through the listed partnership. The Mesa Corps also provides indoor cooling and hydration during regular operating hours and expanded seasonal heat-relief activation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Food assistance is subject to local intake and stock. Ask whether photo identification, another ID or residency proof is needed. Indoor cooling and water are available during regular operating hours; expanded heat relief depends on a National Weather Service Excessive Heat Warning.

**Population Served**
Mesa individuals and families seeking emergency food or relief from dangerous heat, including people experiencing homelessness.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-962-9103 before a food visit to confirm stock, documents and distribution time. The location is 241 E 6th St, Mesa. Expanded heat-relief hours are 11 AM–5 PM on qualifying warning days from May through September, including weekends and excluding federal holidays.

**Important Information to Know**
Cooling is not overnight shelter or a year-round day centre. Leashed dogs may be accommodated during heat warnings only if the site’s space and safety conditions allow; confirm first. Food, pet food and same-day assistance are not guaranteed.

resources.name: The Arc of Arizona — Care Management and Independent Living Supports
resources.description: Individualized help with daily living, appointments, service navigation, budgeting and future planning through CAMILS.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Individualized help with daily living, appointments, service navigation, budgeting and future planning through CAMILS.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Designed for people with intellectual or developmental disabilities living independently, especially those with little or no government support. Scope and ongoing fees are agreed individually; a scholarship application is available for people unable to pay.

**Population Served**

Arizona adults with intellectual or developmental disabilities and families planning support.

**How to Best Connect**

Call 602-234-2721 or email arc@arcarizona.org for a free, no-obligation consultation. Ask about the person’s needs, fees and scholarship availability.

**Important Information to Know**

The consultation is free; ongoing services are not automatically free. Arc staff do not provide legal advice or act as medical professionals unless specifically established in writing. Ask for current future-planning and supported-decision-making resources.

resources.name: City of Mesa Planning Division · Community Residence Registration verification
resources.description: City of Mesa Planning Division can help verify whether a Mesa sober living home or other community residence is registered and explain the registration rules for community residences. This is a regulatory verification contact, not a housing placement or treatment provider.
resources.address: 55 N Center St, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Planning contact hours listed by the city are generally Monday-Thursday 7:00 AM-6:00 PM; Friday service may be limited by city department.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Mesa Planning Division provides information about Community Residence registration and can answer whether a home in Mesa is registered as a Community Residence. Community Residences include sober living homes, assisted living homes, and residential behavioral health homes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
This is for checking or understanding Mesa registration requirements. It does not place clients into sober living, pay rent, provide treatment, or certify that a specific home is clinically appropriate.

**Population Served**
Mesa residents, families, neighbors, missionaries, or administrators who need to check registration status or understand local sober-living/community-residence rules.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Planning Division/Planner of the Day at 480-644-4726 or email Planning.Info@mesaaz.gov. Provide the home's address and ask whether it is registered as a Community Residence.

**Important Information to Know**
City registration is separate from clinical licensing, treatment quality and suitability for a particular resident. Ask the provider about costs, admission, house rules and care needs. An unclear registration status does not by itself prove that a home has closed.

resources.name: Arizona Food Bank Network — Food finder and Hunger Hotline
resources.description: Provides a statewide food locator and help finding pantries, meals and food benefits when a local option does not fit.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides a statewide food locator and help finding pantries, meals and food benefits when a local option does not fit.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Public search and referral access; individual providers determine their own documentation, boundaries and supply limits.

**Population Served**
People seeking food in Arizona, including Mesa and Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Use Get Food or call 602-528-3434; explain location, travel limits and dietary or other access needs.

**Important Information to Know**
The network does not guarantee a listed site is open or stocked. Confirm the particular pantry before visiting; administrative offices are not assumed to distribute food.

resources.name: Fort McDowell Yavapai Nation - Domestic Violence Action Team / Domestic Violence Program
resources.description: Fort McDowell Yavapai Nation's Domestic Violence Action Team and Victim/Witness Advocate help with domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking and teen dating violence through safety planning, victim rights, shelter placement, emergency assistance and protection-order support.
resources.address: 10755 N. Fort McDowell Road, Suite 2, Fort McDowell, AZ 85264
resources.hours: Victim Advocate line generally Monday-Thursday 7:30 AM-5:30 PM; evenings, weekends and holidays call Fort McDowell Police at 480-837-1091. Call 911 for emergencies.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Victim/witness advocacy for domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking and teen dating violence, including safety planning, emotional support, explanation of criminal proceedings, shelter referrals and transportation, emergency financial assistance, court escort/orientation, victim-rights help and assistance with orders of protection or injunctions against harassment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program serves the Fort McDowell Yavapai Nation, tribal and community members, tribal government employees and enterprises. Mesa-area Native survivors outside that community should call to ask whether referral or another tribal/community resource is more appropriate.

**Population Served**
Fort McDowell Yavapai Nation tribal and community members and related community contexts affected by domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking or teen dating violence.

**How to Best Connect**
For non-emergency help call the FMYN Victim Advocate at 480-789-7678 or email rdpattea@fmyn.org. For evenings, weekends and holidays call Fort McDowell Police at 480-837-1091. For immediate danger call 911.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a culturally specific tribal resource with a defined community service area. It should be used for Fort McDowell Yavapai Nation-connected survivors or for referral guidance, not as a general Maricopa County DV intake line.

resources.name: Another Level of Community Services - Reentry Temporary Housing and Integrated Health Services
resources.description: Another Level of Community Services is a licensed Phoenix behavioral-health campus specializing in community reentry for people recently incarcerated, listing temporary housing, peer support, integrated health, employment training and GED assistance.
resources.address: 1326 W Hadley St, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-3:00 PM; Friday 8:00 AM-1:00 PM; Saturday-Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Reentry-focused behavioral-health support including temporary housing, peer support, integrated health services, employment training, GED assistance and other wellness supports.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program specializes in people recently incarcerated who need help transitioning back into the community. Housing capacity, payer requirements, behavioral-health enrollment and referral rules must be confirmed.

**Population Served**
People recently released from incarceration in Phoenix/Maricopa County who need reentry, housing and integrated service support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-218-8868, email admin@alocs.com, or visit/contact the campus at 1326 W Hadley St during posted hours.

**Important Information to Know**
The official page supports temporary housing but does not publish bed count, costs, payer rules or Mesa-specific access. Confirm these before relying on it for a housing placement.

resources.name: Mesa Public Schools - Special Education Department
resources.description: Mesa Public Schools Special Education Department provides local public-school disability education access for eligible students ages 3-22, including evaluation resources, IEP services and parent resources.
resources.address: 549 N. Stapley Dr., Mesa, AZ 85203
resources.hours: School and district office hours vary; contact the district or the student's school for current special education intake.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Special education programs and supports for students with disabilities, including educational opportunities, evaluation request resources, parent resources, Child Find information, preschool developmental screening links, specialized classes when needed and individualized planning through the school system.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The district states its special education programs serve students with disabilities ages 3-22. Eligibility is determined through the public-school evaluation and IEP process, and the child generally must be connected to Mesa Public Schools by residence/enrollment rules.

**Population Served**
Children and youth ages 3-22 with suspected or identified disabilities in the Mesa Public Schools service area, and their parents/caregivers.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Mesa Public Schools at 480-472-0200 or contact the Special Education Department through the district website. Parents can also ask their child's school about requesting a special education evaluation.

**Important Information to Know**
District-boundary, enrollment and age rules apply. Call before referral to confirm the correct Child Find, preschool screening, evaluation or enrolled-student contact for the child's age and address.

resources.name: Resurrection Street Ministry / S.T.U.F.F. - Hardship Clothing and Household Items
resources.description: Resurrection Street Ministry's S.T.U.F.F. Thrift Store offers low-cost clothing, furniture and reusable household items and states that free clothes and other accessible items are available for listed hardship groups.
resources.address: 1135 E Main St, Mesa, AZ 85203
resources.hours: S.T.U.F.F. Thrift Store: Monday-Saturday 9:00 AM-6:00 PM; Sunday closed. Chosen 2 Serve Food Pantry: Monday-Saturday 10:00 AM-2:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Low-cost thrift shopping for clothing, furniture and household items, plus stated free clothes and other accessible items for eligible hardship groups. Resurrection Street Ministry also operates the nearby Chosen 2 Serve food pantry.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The S.T.U.F.F. page lists free clothing/free-item eligibility for seniors 65 and older, veterans who have disabilities or low income, people experiencing homelessness and families in crisis. Documentation, item limits and whether furniture is ever free are not explained publicly.

**Population Served**
Mesa and greater Phoenix-area residents in need, especially seniors, qualifying veterans, people experiencing homelessness and families in crisis.

**How to Best Connect**
Call S.T.U.F.F. at 480-649-1288 to ask about free-clothing eligibility and current item availability. For Resurrection Street Ministry, call 480-615-2799 or email resurrectionstreetministry@gmail.com.

**Important Information to Know**
S.T.U.F.F. is also a thrift store, so some goods may be low-cost retail rather than free assistance. Confirm the hardship/free process before sending a client who cannot pay.

resources.name: Arizona Families F.I.R.S.T. - DCS/DES substance-use referral pathway
resources.description: Arizona Families F.I.R.S.T. is a state child-welfare and DES Jobs pathway providing expedited substance-use assessment, treatment, recovery, peer support, care coordination, and family supports through contracted providers.
resources.hours: Referral timing depends on DCS/DES and assigned providers; state office hours were not established for direct service.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Substance-use assessment, stabilization, early intervention, outpatient treatment, intensive outpatient or partial hospitalization, residential treatment, medication-assisted treatment, auxiliary services, case coordination, recovery maintenance, peer support, and family prevention education through the Arizona Families F.I.R.S.T. system.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Generally limited to adult parents or caretakers reported to DCS, families whose substance use affects child safety or reunification, and DES Jobs/TANF participants whose substance use creates a barrier to employment. DCS policy also describes eligible youth or young adults in certain DCS circumstances.

**Population Served**
Parents, caregivers, youth, young adults, and families involved with DCS or qualifying DES Jobs pathways in Arizona, including Maricopa County families.

**How to Best Connect**
Families already involved with DCS should ask their DCS Specialist about an Arizona Families F.I.R.S.T. referral. For general DCS program information, call 602-255-2500. A walk-in at the state office is not the treatment intake path.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not an open public clinic. Referral and eligibility are tied to DCS or DES Jobs involvement, and services are delivered through contracted providers. Participation does not guarantee reunification, employment outcomes, a specific provider, or immediate placement.

resources.name: AHCCCS Freedom to Work Program
resources.description: AHCCCS Freedom to Work is Medicaid health insurance for qualifying Arizonans ages 16-64 who work and have a disability.
resources.address: AHCCCS, 150 N. 18th Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.hours: Call the Freedom to Work Unit for application help; AHCCCS phone support is typically weekday business hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Freedom to Work provides AHCCCS medical coverage for qualified working individuals with disabilities, helping some people keep Medicaid coverage while employed.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants generally must be age 16-64, Arizona residents, working and paying taxes, meet citizenship or qualified-immigrant rules, have or apply for a Social Security number, receive Social Security disability or be determined blind or disabled by DDSA, not be eligible for another AHCCCS program, and meet income rules.

**Population Served**
Working Arizona residents with disabilities, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents who need Medicaid coverage while employed.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the AHCCCS Freedom to Work Unit at 602-417-6677 in Maricopa County or 800-654-8713 option 6 statewide.

**Important Information to Know**
The program may charge a premium up to $35 per month. AHCCCS listed a countable earned income limit, but current income limits should be checked during application. Approval is not automatic.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Juvenile Corrections — Reentry and transition
resources.description: Coordinates education, treatment, family services and mentoring as eligible youth return from ADJC custody.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Coordinates education, treatment, family services and mentoring as eligible youth return from ADJC custody.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For youth committed to ADJC and transitioning to conditional liberty; individual plans and available mentor matches govern access.

**Population Served**
Youth leaving Adobe Mountain School and their families, including those returning to Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Work through the youth’s assigned transition specialist or parole/case team; consult ADJC’s Re-Entry and Transition Services page.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a custody-specific transition service, not an open youth drop-in program. The current review’s page fetch was blocked; retain the saved official-page evidence without claiming the program closed.

resources.name: Sojourner Center - Emergency shelter, transitional housing and pet companion services
resources.description: Sojourner Center provides emergency shelter, transitional housing, survivor support services and pet companion services for people affected by domestic violence, sexual assault and human trafficking.
resources.address: Confidential shelter and apartment locations; mailing address P.O. Box 20156, Phoenix, AZ 85036
resources.hours: 24-hour emergency hotline: 602-244-0089. Transitional housing inquiries by email; shelter locations are confidential.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency shelter, transitional housing for up to two years, case management, child and youth services, legal advocacy, support groups, resource center help, and pet companion services including pet daycare, kennels, grooming and veterinary assistance.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault and human trafficking. Transitional housing referral and shelter placement depend on screening and availability.

**Population Served**
Adult and child survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault and human trafficking, including survivors with pets.

**How to Best Connect**
For immediate domestic violence shelter help, call the 24-hour hotline at 602-244-0089. For transitional housing referrals and information, email TransitionalHousingReferrals@sojournercenter.org. For pet companion services, email petcompanionservices@sojournercenter.org or call the general office at 602-244-0997.

**Important Information to Know**
Shelter and apartment locations are confidential. Pet capacity and transitional apartment openings must be confirmed at intake. If someone is in immediate danger, call 911.
resources.resolutionReason: Earlier delivery assigned two permanent IDs to this reviewed programme. Preserve both aliases and human state; present the secondary record to administrators for duplicate reconciliation. No registry migration, deletion or automatic unpublishing. Reconcile with sr_cedc86d5c05d5c4f93cdd09067a7168f.

resources.name: A New Leaf / MesaCAN — Weatherization assistance
resources.description: MesaCAN Weatherization Assistance helps eligible low-income Mesa households reduce energy costs and improve health and safety through measures that may include air conditioning, insulation and related work.
resources.address: 635 E Broadway Rd, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Weatherization assistance reduces energy costs for low-income households and improves energy efficiency, health and safety. MesaCAN says services may include air conditioning, insulation and more.

**Eligibility Requirements**
MesaCAN serves low-income households across the City of Mesa. Specific weatherization eligibility, ownership or landlord requirements, eligible measures, funding and wait time must be confirmed with MesaCAN.

**Population Served**
Low-income City of Mesa households that may need energy-efficiency, air-conditioning, insulation or related health-and-safety improvements.

**How to Best Connect**
Call MesaCAN at 480-833-9200 or email mesacanclient@turnanewleaf.org. The office is at 635 E Broadway Rd, Mesa, AZ 85204.

**Important Information to Know**
A home assessment, property eligibility, approval, permitted work and funding determine what can be done. These rules differ from rent or utility-bill assistance. This is not guaranteed same-day repair or unrestricted appliance replacement.

resources.name: Valleywise Health - Mesa First Episode Center
resources.description: Valleywise Mesa First Episode Center is an early-psychosis program for adolescents and young adults ages 15-25 who are experiencing unusual thoughts or behaviors, fearfulness, voices or visions others do not, withdrawal, or related early psychosis concerns.
resources.address: 950 E Main St, Mesa, AZ 85203
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Recovery-oriented behavioral-health care for adolescents and young adults experiencing early psychosis or a first episode of serious mental illness, focused on support during or after psychosis and helping the young person return to goals and daily life.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Valleywise states the First Episode Center treats patients ages 15-25 who experience symptoms such as unusual thoughts or behaviors, fearfulness or suspiciousness, hearing voices or seeing things others do not, or withdrawal from family and friends. Enrollment criteria, insurance, referral requirements and capacity must be screened by the program.

**Population Served**
Adolescents and young adults in Mesa and Maricopa County, ages 15-25, experiencing early psychosis symptoms.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Mesa First Episode Center at 602-655-6242 or Valleywise scheduling at 1-833-855-9973. The Mesa location is 950 E Main St.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a specialized early-psychosis program for ages 15–25. Call 602-655-6242 to check clinical eligibility, enrollment and appointment availability; it is distinct from the Brown Road outpatient clinic.

resources.name: AZALEA — LGBTQ2S+ inclusion and community connection
resources.description: Statewide network supporting inclusion and social connections for LGBTQ2S+ older adults.
resources.hours: Periodic meetings and events; email for current participation details.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Community members, providers, advocates and allies meet to share resources and build inclusion for LGBTQ2S+ older adults.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The alliance welcomes people of all ages who share its inclusion goals. Ask about current meetings, location or remote access and any event registration.

**Population Served**
LGBTQ2S+ older Arizonans and people who want to participate in an inclusive aging community.

**How to Best Connect**
Email info@azaleainitiative.org or use the official Community and Events pages to ask how to join.

**Important Information to Know**
This is community participation, education and advocacy, not counseling, personal care or an emergency intake service. A meeting or referral does not guarantee access to another provider.

resources.name: St. Vincent de Paul — East Valley Medical Clinic (opening not confirmed)
resources.description: Planned Mesa medical clinic for uninsured and underserved East Valley patients; current patient intake must be confirmed.
resources.address: 2352 W. Main St., Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Current public page says the East Valley Medical Clinic is opening in Mesa in Fall 2026; current patient hours were not confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Planned primary-care access through St. Vincent de Paul’s medical-clinic system. Available services, appointment access and specialty referral arrangements at this Mesa location need confirmation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The medical clinic referral language is for uninsured and underserved patients who do not already have an established primary care provider at another free clinic such as an FQHC. Other clinics and providers can refer patients.

**Population Served**
Uninsured and underserved East Valley patients once the Mesa clinic is open; the Phoenix clinic currently serves uninsured patients with no other care option.

**How to Best Connect**
Before sending a patient to the Mesa address, call 602-261-6825 to ask whether the East Valley Medical Clinic is open and accepting referrals. Provider referrals can use the official medical referral form and fax it to 602-261-6816.

**Important Information to Know**
Official pages checked for this collection still described a Fall 2026 opening. This record stays administrator-only until current patient intake is established. Ask the medical-clinic team about another active location if care is needed now.
resources.resolutionReason: Needs resolution because official evidence supports the planned Mesa clinic identity and referral contact, but the page still marks it as opening in Fall 2026 and does not confirm current patient access or hours.

resources.name: Maricopa County Correctional Health Services - Jail Mental Health Service and Transition Planning
resources.description: Maricopa County Correctional Health Services provides jail-based mental-health screening, mental-health clinics, psychiatric providers, individual/group treatment, specialized mental-health housing, SMI provider coordination, and community transition planning for people in Maricopa County jails.
resources.hours: Accessed only through Maricopa County jail, court, custody, and release-planning processes.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Mental-health screening at jail intake, mental-health clinics in each jail, psychiatric providers, individual and group treatment, specialized mental-health housing at Lower Buckeye Jail, SMI provider coordination through the Regional Behavioral Health Authority data link, and community transition planning for people with significant mental-health needs preparing to return to the community.

**Eligibility Requirements**
This is for people currently in Maricopa County jails or being served through jail/court release-planning processes. It is not a community walk-in clinic.

**Population Served**
People incarcerated in Maricopa County jails, including people with acute or ongoing mental-health needs, suicidal ideation, SMI designation, co-occurring substance-use needs, or reentry planning needs before release.

**How to Best Connect**
People in custody request care through jail health procedures. Families can provide nonemergency health information through clinicalliaison.maricopa.gov; the form is handled weekdays 8 a.m.–5 p.m. and is not an urgent-response channel. Ask the jail about release planning and continuity of medications.

**Important Information to Know**
These services are for people held in Maricopa County jails. Family information is not a request for a public outpatient appointment; use appropriate emergency procedures for immediate danger.

resources.name: City of Chandler - Chandler Connect / Homeless Navigation Services
resources.description: Chandler Connect is the City of Chandler's homeless navigation program for people experiencing unsheltered homelessness in Chandler, staffed by clinicians and certified peer support specialists who provide outreach, assessment, health and behavioral-health connections, transportation, justice-system navigation and temporary-housing connection.
resources.address: 235 S Arizona Ave, Chandler, AZ 85225
resources.hours: City page states Chandler Connect services are provided seven days a week; Neighborhood Resources office hours listed Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM for coordinated-entry location access.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Outreach, assessment, connection to health and behavioral-health services, transportation, assistance navigating the criminal-justice system, temporary housing connection, coordinated-entry style referral and supportive services toward permanent housing.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people experiencing unsheltered homelessness in Chandler. Mesa residents should call first to ask whether Chandler Connect can advise or whether Mesa/Tempe routes should be used.

**Population Served**
People experiencing unsheltered homelessness in Chandler and people physically connected to Chandler's homeless-response system.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Chandler Connect at 480-782-4349 or email homeless.outreach@chandleraz.gov. If directed to a physical coordinated-entry location, the Family Housing Hub page lists Chandler Neighborhood Resources at 235 S Arizona Ave, Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
This is city-specific and not a general Mesa outreach team. It is a strong reserve option for clients located in Chandler or moving between Chandler and Mesa.

resources.name: Southwest Human Development — Birth to Five Center of Excellence
resources.description: Multidisciplinary developmental evaluation, counseling and coordinated support for young children.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Multidisciplinary developmental evaluation, counseling and coordinated support for young children.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For children from birth through 5; intake determines the assessment and service fit.

**Population Served**
Young children and families with developmental or behavioral concerns.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-468-3430 to discuss evaluation and referral needs.

**Important Information to Know**
This is distinct from the free Birth to Five Helpline. Confirm location, fees, insurance and any home-based service arrangement.

resources.name: Arizona Board of Regents / Arizona FAFSA Coalition · FAFSA Assistance and Ask Benji
resources.description: The Arizona Board of Regents / Arizona FAFSA Coalition page connects Arizona students and families to free FAFSA help, including Ask Benji text assistance and financial-aid offices or school counselors for FAFSA questions.
resources.address: 2700 N. Central Ave., Suite 400, Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.hours: Ask Benji is text-based; event and appointment availability changes by date.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Arizona FAFSA resources include Ask Benji, a free digital FAFSA assistant, and guidance to work with high school counselors, college and career specialists, university financial-aid offices, and Federal Student Aid resources. The page explains FAFSA eligibility basics and FSA ID steps.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Most U.S. citizens and eligible noncitizens are eligible for federal financial aid if they meet federal student-aid requirements, including Social Security number rules, enrollment or acceptance in an eligible college or career-school program, satisfactory academic progress, and FAFSA certification. Help with questions is available regardless of whether aid is ultimately approved.

**Population Served**
Arizona students and families seeking FAFSA information, financial-aid access, or help starting the college/career-school aid process.

**How to Best Connect**
Text "Hi Benji" to 602-786-8171 for the Ask Benji digital FAFSA assistant. Students can also ask their school counselor, college/career specialist, or college financial-aid office for help.

**Important Information to Know**
The listed number is a text route for Ask Benji, not a voice phone line. In-person FAFSA events and virtual appointments change by date; confirm current event availability before sending a client.

resources.name: Valleywise Health — Reentry Packs document vouchers
resources.description: Could add identification-document vouchers for eligible people returning to the community once the program’s referral route is confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Could add identification-document vouchers for eligible people returning to the community once the program’s referral route is confirmed.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A 2026 community-reinvestment award identifies reentry packs, but specific participant and referral criteria remain unpublished.

**Population Served**
People transitioning back into the community through the funded Valleywise program.

**How to Best Connect**
An administrator should confirm the responsible Valleywise program and intake process before referring a client.

**Important Information to Know**
The award confirms planned document vouchers, transportation and basic-needs items; it does not establish a public walk-in service, voucher amount or eligibility at the Mesa clinic.
resources.resolutionReason: The award confirms planned document vouchers, transportation and basic-needs items; it does not establish a public walk-in service, voucher amount or eligibility at the Mesa clinic.

resources.name: Community Legal Services - Set Aside and Reentry Legal Assistance
resources.description: Community Legal Services provides civil legal aid for low-income Arizona residents, including reentry-related help with criminal record set-asides, record sealing, marijuana expungement, civil-rights restoration, and fingerprint-clearance good-cause exceptions.
resources.address: 305 S 2nd Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85003; MesaCAN satellite listed at 635 E Broadway Rd, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: Phone intake completion after online application is listed as Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-2:00 PM; satellite availability should be confirmed before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Civil legal assistance with eligible record-relief matters: conviction set-asides, certificates of second chance, sealing, qualifying marijuana expungement, civil-rights restoration, designation of an undesignated class 6 offense as a misdemeanor, and certain fingerprint-clearance or central-registry exceptions.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are for people who meet CLS income and case-type guidelines and live in a CLS service area that includes Maricopa County. Eligibility can depend on household income, assets, immigration status, case type, and available funding.

**Population Served**
Low-income people in Maricopa County and other CLS service counties, including people with criminal records trying to remove barriers to employment, housing, licensing, voting rights, or fingerprint clearance.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through the AZ Law Help intake linked from CLS, then call 602-258-3434 or 800-852-9075 between 9:00 AM and 2:00 PM, Monday-Friday, to complete the application.

**Important Information to Know**
CLS does not provide criminal defense. These are different legal remedies with distinct requirements; a set-aside does not erase a record. Have case numbers, court records and sentence information ready. Acceptance and relief are not automatic, fees may remain and some offenses are excluded. Confirm any MesaCAN satellite appointment before travel.

resources.name: Foundation for Blind Children — Prison Braille Program
resources.description: Braille instruction for participants in Arizona state prisons, producing accessible materials for students with visual impairments.
resources.hours: Access is arranged through participating prison facilities; there is no public walk-in intake.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Foundation for Blind Children’s Arizona Instructional Resource Center provides braille courses to participants in several Arizona state prisons. Participants help produce accessible educational materials.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Participation is arranged through the prison and program staff. Ask the facility about selection, prerequisites, available places and the specific training offered.

**Population Served**
People incarcerated in participating Arizona state prisons who can enter the braille-training program.

**How to Best Connect**
Start with the participating facility’s education or reentry staff. FBC Accessible Learning Services lists Brian Voeller at 602-337-8225 and bvoeller@seeitourway.org; the FBC general line is 602-331-7900. Confirm facility participation and the available training places.

**Important Information to Know**
This is training within participating prisons, not open enrollment at a community employment office. Ask facility staff about selection and access; no community/parolee enrollment is promised.

resources.name: AZPOINT — Arizona protective-order petition portal
resources.description: AZPOINT is the Arizona Judicial Branch online system for starting or updating protective-order petitions before contacting a court to file. It includes Orders of Protection, safety-planning resources, help materials, Spanish access, and statewide court-filing steps.
resources.hours: Online portal; website support line listed as 800-720-7743.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Online guided preparation for Orders of Protection, injunctions against harassment and workplace-harassment petitions. Draft information is saved for up to 90 days, and the portal provides filing instructions and links to safety resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The person must be seeking an Arizona protective order or related injunction and must still follow the court filing steps. The portal itself does not issue the order.

**Population Served**
People statewide in Arizona, including Mesa clients seeking protection from domestic violence, harassment, or related safety concerns. The portal includes Spanish access.

**How to Best Connect**
Use AZPOINT to prepare a petition and obtain its number, then follow the steps to contact the appropriate city, justice or superior court. The court determines its filing/hearing arrangements. For website support call 800-720-7743; the listed general contact is 602-452-3519. Spanish access is available.

**Important Information to Know**
Use a safe device if someone monitors your technology. Preparing a petition is not filing it or receiving an order; court review and service requirements still apply. The portal does not provide a lawyer or emergency response. Speak with a victim advocate about safety planning when safe to do so; call 911 for immediate danger.

resources.name: La Frontera EMPACT · Substance-use assessment, counseling and outpatient treatment access
resources.description: La Frontera EMPACT provides outpatient counseling, substance-abuse services, crisis intervention, prevention and behavioral-health support for adults, children and families in the East Valley/Phoenix area. The Mesa Rio De Vida office and Tempe office are listed official locations.
resources.address: Mesa Rio De Vida Office: 108 E 2nd Ave, Mesa, AZ 85210; Tempe Madison Office: 618 S Madison Dr, Tempe, AZ 85281
resources.hours: Tempe Madison: Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-8:00 PM, Friday 8:00 AM-6:00 PM, Saturday by appointment. Mesa Rio De Vida hours were not listed; call first.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Substance-use assessment or counseling access, outpatient counseling, crisis services, prevention, trauma healing, child and family programming, adult programming and co-occurring behavioral-health support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility, AHCCCS or payer rules, assessment requirements and which site handles substance-use intake depend on the program. Call before referral to confirm current SUD enrollment and site assignment.

**Population Served**
Phoenix metropolitan and East Valley clients, including Mesa and Tempe-area adults, youth and families needing behavioral-health or substance-use support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the all-offices line at 480-784-1514 or the Rio De Vida business line at 480-317-2216. For crisis support, use EMPACT's crisis hotline at 480-784-1500 or call/text 988 for immediate behavioral-health crisis support.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a co-occurring behavioral-health provider lead, not a confirmed detox or residential program. The official locations page says the website email is not for emergencies. Confirm the right office and level of care before sending a client.

resources.name: Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community - Senior Services
resources.description: Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community Senior Services provides case management, meals, transportation, recreation, health and wellness, language and culture programming, home care assistance, caregiver support, Adult Protective Services and senior home repair referral for eligible community seniors and adults with adaptive needs.
resources.address: 10005 E. Osborn Rd., Bldg. 63, Scottsdale, AZ 85256
resources.hours: Call 480-362-6350 for intake assessment and current program schedules. SHRRP home repair helpline is listed Monday-Friday, 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
SRPMIC Senior Services provides case management, congregate and home-delivered meals, transportation for healthcare appointments, shopping, errands and activities, recreation, health and wellness classes, O'odham and Piipaash language and culture programming, home care assistance, caregiver support, Adult Protective Services, and referral to the Senior Home Repair and Replacement Program.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page describes services for the Community's seniors age 55 and older and adult community members with physical and adaptive needs. Intake assessment determines eligibility for specific services such as meals, social worker or caregiver assignments and home care assistance.

**Population Served**
Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community seniors age 55 and older and adult community members with physical or adaptive needs.

**How to Best Connect**
For an intake assessment or to ask about any program, email seniorservicesinfo@srpmic-nsn.gov or call 480-362-6350. For Adult Protective Services referrals, email adultprotectiveservices@srpmic-nsn.gov or call 480-362-6350. For Senior Home Repair and Replacement Program questions, call 480-362-7800.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a tribal senior services system and is likely limited to eligible SRPMIC community members. Mesa residents who are not SRPMIC community members should be referred to county or city senior services instead.

resources.name: Copa Health / AHCCCS - Pathways of Hope Transitional Housing Facility
resources.description: Copa Health Pathways of Hope is a transitional housing programme for chronically homeless adults with serious mental illness, with support for everyday living and longer-term stability.
resources.address: Phoenix programme; ask the provider for the appropriate referral route before travelling.
resources.hours: No public walk-in hours listed; access appears tied to AHCCCS/RBHA housing pathways.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Transitional housing with daily-living skills, employment preparation, peer support and help moving toward longer-term housing stability.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The provider describes the programme for chronically homeless adults with serious mental illness. Ask about clinical, coverage and referral requirements.

**Population Served**
Adults who meet the programme's homelessness and serious-mental-illness criteria.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the existing behavioral-health care team about referral, or call Copa Health residential-services enquiries at 480-969-3800 ext. 229 and ask specifically about Pathways of Hope.

**Important Information to Know**
The provider enquiry contact is not a direct admissions or open-bed line. Work with the existing behavioral-health care team and health plan to confirm referral, coverage, current eligibility and availability before travel. A published programme size is not a vacancy count.

resources.name: Arizona Public Service - Medical Care Program
resources.description: APS Medical Care Program notifies qualifying APS customers of planned outages when a household member uses life-sustaining electric medical equipment or has a qualifying condition affecting safety and self-care.
resources.address: Mail completed application to APS Medical Care Program, P.O. Box 53933, Mail Station 3211, Phoenix, AZ 85072
resources.hours: Questions by phone 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Medical Care Program provides planned outage notifications, status and estimated restoration information so qualifying APS households can prepare for service interruptions.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The APS household must have a member dependent on medical equipment that is in use and essential to sustaining life where a service interruption longer than four hours could be dangerous, or a qualifying physical or mental condition that substantially limits ability to manage resources, daily activities or protection from hazards without assistance. A licensed medical professional must complete the verification section.

**Population Served**
APS customers with a household member who has a life-threatening illness, uses essential critical electric medical equipment, or has a qualifying condition affecting safety and self-care.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the APS Medical Care Program application, have the licensed medical professional complete the verification section, and mail it to APS Medical Care Program, P.O. Box 53933, Mail Station 3211, Phoenix, AZ 85072. For questions, call 602-371-7171 or 800-240-2014.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a discount program and does not guarantee uninterrupted service. Customers must stay current on monthly bills, renew annually, and submit a new certification after moving.

resources.name: City of Buckeye - BOLD curb-to-curb shared rides
resources.description: Buckeye BOLD provides low-cost advance-reservation curb-to-curb shared rides for approved seniors, people with disabilities and U.S. veterans for trips entirely within Buckeye city limits.
resources.address: 110 E. Irwin Avenue, Buckeye, AZ 85326
resources.hours: Monday-Friday, approximately 7:30 AM-4:00 PM in the current handbook; app listing says 7:00 AM-5:00 PM, so confirm when booking.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
BOLD is Buckeye's curb-to-curb shared-ride transit pilot. Approved riders can reserve accessible shared rides within Buckeye city boundaries.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligible rider categories are seniors age 60 or older, individuals with disabilities and U.S. veterans. Applicants must be approved before using the service, and all pickups and drop-offs must be within Buckeye city limits.

**Population Served**
Approved Buckeye riders who are seniors, people with disabilities or U.S. veterans.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online at buckeyeaz.gov/gobold or ask for an application at the dispatch office, 110 E. Irwin Ave. Book rides online, through the GO BOLD app, or by calling dispatch at 623-349-6317 at least one business day before the ride.

**Important Information to Know**
This service does not cover Mesa or trips outside Buckeye. The handbook lists a $2 one-way fare, exact-change cash/app/online payment, a 30-minute pickup window and shared rides. Confirm current hours because published snippets differ slightly.

resources.name: Neighborhood Ministries WIOA Youth Workforce Development and Neighbors on the Rise
resources.description: Neighborhood Ministries is a Phoenix community organization confirmed by City of Phoenix records as a WIOA Title I-B Youth Program workforce provider for youth ages 14-24 facing employment barriers, with job training, work experience, tutoring, and career guidance.
resources.address: 1918 W. Van Buren St., Phoenix, AZ 85009
resources.hours: Contact the organization or Phoenix workforce program for current enrollment and service schedules.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Youth workforce services under the City of Phoenix WIOA Title I-B Youth Program, including work experience, career guidance, tutoring, job training, and preparation for employment in high-demand fields, post-secondary education, apprenticeships, and industry-recognized credentials. Neighborhood Ministries also provides broader community and family supports at its Phoenix campus.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The City of Phoenix youth program serves ages 14-24 who face barriers to employment, with a heavy focus on out-of-school youth. WIOA documentation, residency, income/barrier eligibility, and whether Mesa/Maricopa County but non-Phoenix youth can enroll must be confirmed.

**Population Served**
Youth and young adults ages 14-24 facing barriers to employment, especially opportunity youth; Neighborhood Ministries is located in Phoenix.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Neighborhood Ministries at its Phoenix campus or use the official website contact route, and ask specifically for the WIOA Youth Workforce Development or Neighbors on the Rise intake. Address: 1918 W. Van Buren St., Phoenix, AZ 85009.

**Important Information to Know**
The organization's public website is not detailed about the workforce program. City of Phoenix records confirm a 2026-2027 youth workforce contract, but adult Neighbors on the Rise services, Mesa eligibility, and the current intake form should be verified before referral.

resources.name: Copa Health — Disability living, in-home, day and employment supports
resources.description: Copa provides disability-related community living, residential, in-home, day and supported-employment services in Mesa and other Arizona locations, with programme-specific referral and funding requirements.
resources.address: Headquarters: 924 N. Country Club Drive, Mesa, AZ 85201. Confirm the actual programme location.
resources.hours: Employment facility programmes: Monday–Friday 8 AM–2 PM; community work and other programme schedules vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Community living and residential group homes; in-home attendant/personal care, respite, housekeeping, habilitation and Individually Designed Living Arrangements; day, social-skills and community-participation supports. Employment Related Services offers career planning, pre-employment and computer/document-imaging training, job development, placement, supported/competitive employment and community work experiences.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Programme fit, support needs, funding authorization and openings determine access. Living and in-home services use funders including DDD, Area Agency on Aging, NACOG or health plans. Employment services accept VR, DDD, behavioral-health and health-plan referrals, single-case agreements or private pay, with an individualized service/recovery plan. These are distinct pathways, not one universal authorization.

**Population Served**
Children, adults and older adults with disabilities who meet the particular living/support programme criteria, and people with disabilities seeking employment-related services. Service area varies by programme; Maricopa County is included.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-969-3800 and describe the requested support, Mesa location and current DDD, ALTCS, VR or health-plan connection. Ask for extension 229 for residential/community living/in-home services. Employment referrals can go to referrals@copahealth.org. Confirm the service site and schedule before traveling.

**Important Information to Know**
These are disability-related services, not a general job centre, unrestricted attendant-care service or public shelter. Confirm staffing, capacity, costs and any transport arrangements. Named clinical sites and Pathways of Hope have their own access processes.

resources.name: A New Leaf / MesaCAN - SOAR Works SSI/SSDI Application Assistance
resources.description: MesaCAN materials identify SOAR Works as SSI/SSDI application help for people currently in A New Leaf shelter programs. It is a disability-income application support lead, not an emergency grant.
resources.address: 635 E Broadway Rd, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: MesaCAN fact sheet lists Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; current SOAR referral capacity and intake should be confirmed by phone or email.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
SOAR Works helps people apply for SSI and SSDI disability benefits as needed. The official MesaCAN fact sheet describes it as SSI/SSDI Outreach, Access, and Recovery support for people currently in A New Leaf shelter programs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Publicly available A New Leaf material supports a narrow access point: people currently in A New Leaf shelter programs. Broader public eligibility, capacity, and referral steps are not clearly published, so confirm before referring someone outside an A New Leaf shelter.

**Population Served**
People in A New Leaf shelter programs who may need help applying for SSI or SSDI because of disability-related income needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Call MesaCAN at 480-833-9200 or email mesacanclient@turnanewleaf.org and ask whether SOAR Works is accepting referrals and whether the client must already be in an A New Leaf shelter program.

**Important Information to Know**
SOAR is application assistance for disability benefits; it does not decide SSI/SSDI eligibility or provide immediate cash. A general Mesa resident who is not connected to an A New Leaf shelter may need another SSI/SSDI application support route.

resources.name: Mercy Care DCS CHP - Behavioral-Health Access for Children in DCS Custody
resources.description: Mercy Care Department of Child Safety Comprehensive Health Plan is the health plan pathway for behavioral and physical health care coverage for children and youth in Arizona DCS legal custody and out-of-home care.
resources.hours: Mercy Care DCS CHP Member Services: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Behavioral and physical health coverage access for children and youth in DCS legal custody and out-of-home care, including help obtaining behavioral-health services, rapid-response assessment, initial evaluations, Child and Family Team planning, routine behavioral-health appointments, and therapeutic foster-care referral when clinically recommended.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Limited to children and youth in Arizona DCS legal custody and placed in out-of-home care. Adopted children use a separate AHCCCS health-plan pathway. Consent and assigned-provider details depend on custody and placement status.

**Population Served**
Children and youth in foster or kinship placements under Arizona DCS legal custody, and their licensed or unlicensed caregivers, including Maricopa County placements.

**How to Best Connect**
Foster and kinship caregivers can call Mercy Care DCS CHP Member Services at 602-212-4983 or 1-833-711-0776 (TTY 711), Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM. For a new foster/kinship placement not assessed within 72 hours, AHCCCS lists the Integrated Rapid Response hotline at 602-633-0763.

**Important Information to Know**
This route is for the DCS/foster-care population, not general child counseling. Urgent needs and Jacob's Law timeframes have special escalation routes; life-threatening emergencies should use 911 and behavioral-health crises may use 1-844-534-4673 or 988.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Veterans' Services - Veteran Benefits Counselors
resources.description: ADVS Veteran Benefits Counselors provide free accredited benefit counseling and claims help for Arizona veterans, dependents and survivors, including VA compensation and pension claims, appeals, survivor benefits, discharge upgrades, DD214/service-record requests and state benefits.
resources.address: Administrative office: 1688 W. Adams Street, Phoenix, AZ 85007. Arrange the actual appointment location first.
resources.hours: Appointments can be in person, virtual, by phone or email; VBCs operate remotely across Arizona and at State Veteran Homes.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
ADVS Veteran Benefits Counselors provide free information, counseling and assistance with federal and state benefits earned through honorable service. VBCs can help with eligibility education, VA compensation and pension applications, appeals, VA hearing representation, survivor benefits, discharge upgrades, referrals, military service record requests, DD214 certification and state veteran benefits.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Arizona veterans, dependents and survivors can ask for counseling about federal or state benefits, military records or discharge upgrades. Each benefit has its own service, discharge and other eligibility rules; a potentially disqualifying discharge does not itself bar an inquiry about an upgrade or available options.

**Population Served**
Arizona veterans, dependents and survivors. VBCs operate remotely statewide and in Arizona State Veteran Homes.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-535-1215 to schedule with a VBC, or use the in-person or virtual appointment links on the ADVS page. ADVS states services may be provided in person, virtually, by phone or email.

**Important Information to Know**
Before an appointment, gather records from the ADVS document checklist when possible. For virtual appointments, clients need a device with camera, internet and email access, but ADVS states VBCs can still provide service by phone or email if the client lacks that equipment. This is claim and benefits help, not guaranteed benefit approval. This service does not provide an emergency cash grant.

resources.name: Chicanos Por La Causa - Staff Sergeant Parker Gordon Fox Suicide Prevention Grant Services
resources.description: Unresolved lead for Chicanos Por La Causa veteran suicide-prevention-related services: CPLC has a Mesa behavioral health location, but public official sources did not confirm an Arizona veteran SSG Fox intake route, and current VA grantee evidence conflicts with the submitted Arizona claim.
resources.address: 325 N. Stapley Drive, Mesa, AZ 85203
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
CPLC's official Arizona page confirms behavioral health services at CPLC Centro Esperanza in Mesa. The submitted veteran-specific Staff Sergeant Parker Gordon Fox Suicide Prevention Grant service could not be responsibly confirmed as an Arizona/Mesa veteran intake route from CPLC public pages.

**Eligibility Requirements**
CPLC behavioral health eligibility is not the same as veteran SSG Fox eligibility. The veteran-specific grant eligibility, intake phone/email and Arizona geography remain unresolved.

**Population Served**
CPLC serves Arizona communities and has a Mesa behavioral health site. The submitted veteran-specific service may be intended for veterans, but current public evidence does not confirm Mesa/Arizona SSG Fox access.

**How to Best Connect**
For the Mesa behavioral health location, the CPLC Arizona page lists CPLC Centro Esperanza, 325 N. Stapley Drive, Mesa, AZ 85203, phone 480-615-3800. Do not refer a client specifically for CPLC SSG Fox veteran suicide-prevention services until an administrator confirms the correct program contact and geography.

**Important Information to Know**
The VA FY2026 grantee listing identifies CPLC service counties in Texas. Arizona veteran-grant intake has not been confirmed; a CPLC Mesa office listing does not establish access to this specific grant programme.
resources.resolutionReason: CPLC Mesa behavioral health identity is supported, but veteran-specific SSG Fox program access in Arizona is not publicly confirmed and conflicts with current VA grantee-list evidence; this prevents a responsible veteran-specific referral without administrator resolution.

resources.name: Chicanos Por La Causa - De Colores Domestic and Sexual Violence Services
resources.description: CPLC De Colores offers shelter and community services for survivors of domestic or sexual violence and trafficking, including Spanish-language access and pet support.
resources.address: Community-Based Services: Vista Village Apartments, 3541 E. Van Buren St., Phoenix, AZ 85034; shelter location confidential
resources.hours: 24-hour shelter hotline.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Shelter, crisis intervention, safety planning, casework, legal/housing support, support groups, transport, youth/employment support, financial education and transitional/rapid rehousing. Pet support includes shelter, food and veterinary needs. Household supplies and transition furniture are tied to shelter services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Survivors and families are screened for programme fit, safety and available capacity. Community services also help people outside shelter or leaving shelter.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County survivors and families, including Spanish-speaking survivors and people with pets.

**How to Best Connect**
Shelter/crisis: 602-269-1515, 24 hours. Community services: 602-805-9211 or DeColoresReferrals@cplc.org; confirm appointments at Vista Village, 3541 E. Van Buren St., Phoenix.

**Important Information to Know**
The shelter address is confidential; the public community-services site is separate. Call before travel. Housing placement, supplies and furniture are not guaranteed; this is not a public household-goods closet or general law firm.

resources.name: Circle the City - East Valley Medical Respite Center planned Mesa site
resources.description: Circle the City is developing an East Valley Medical Respite Center in Mesa for people experiencing homelessness who need medical recovery support, but public official pages reviewed did not confirm that the Mesa site is open for referrals yet.
resources.address: Mesa, AZ; site planned in the East Valley near Higley and Main according to public campaign materials
resources.hours: No public intake hours confirmed for the planned East Valley center.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Planned 85-bed East Valley medical respite center intended to provide a safe place to heal for people experiencing homelessness who are recovering from illness or injury and need care that is more supportive than the street but less intensive than a hospital.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Expected medical-respite eligibility is for people experiencing homelessness who are medically stable enough to leave the hospital but too ill or injured to recover safely on the street. Current Mesa-site admission rules are not publicly confirmed.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness in the East Valley/Maricopa County who need recuperative medical respite care.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Circle the City at 602-776-0776 and ask whether the East Valley Medical Respite Center is open, accepting referrals, and what hospital/provider referral process is required.

**Important Information to Know**
Official Circle the City pages reviewed describe the East Valley site as opening in fall 2026 or as a capital campaign project. They do not confirm an active public intake route for the Mesa center. Use the existing Phoenix medical respite resource for current referrals unless Circle the City confirms the Mesa site is open.
resources.resolutionReason: Needs administrator resolution because official pages confirm the East Valley medical respite project but do not confirm current opening status, operating address, or referral/intake process for the Mesa site.

resources.name: Arizona Center for the Blind and Visually Impaired (ACBVI) - Employment Support
resources.description: Arizona Center for the Blind and Visually Impaired provides employment support for people with vision loss, including job exploration, resume assistance, internships, job placement services, assistive technology, mobility, Braille, life skills, and health supports that can strengthen work independence.
resources.address: 3100 E Roosevelt St, Phoenix, AZ 85008
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
ACBVI employment programs include job exploration, resume assistance, internships, and job placement services for people with vision loss.
