The same organization also offers assistive technology, orientation and mobility, Braille instruction, life-skills development, transportation advocacy, and whole-person health supports that may help someone prepare for work.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page describes services for individuals with visual impairments or vision loss. Exact intake requirements, funding source, and whether a Vocational Rehabilitation referral is needed should be confirmed with ACBVI.

**Population Served**
People who are blind, visually impaired, or experiencing vision loss in Arizona, including Mesa-area clients who can access the Phoenix center or ask about remote/partner options.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-273-7411 or email info@acbvi.org. The center is at 3100 E Roosevelt St, Phoenix, AZ 85008. Ask specifically for employment support and describe the client’s vision-loss needs, work goals, transportation limits, and any VR involvement.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a specialized disability employment and independence resource, not a general staffing agency. Service availability, funding, and referral requirements are not fully published on the checked page.

resources.name: Copper Springs East · Gilbert mental-health and addiction treatment
resources.description: Provides adult and senior inpatient psychiatric and addiction treatment, with outpatient partial-hospitalization and intensive-outpatient programmes in Gilbert.
resources.address: 3755 S Rome Street, Gilbert, AZ 85297
resources.hours: Copper Springs advertises 24/7 phone assessment access; location-specific walk-in and assessment process should be confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Copper Springs East in Gilbert provides adult and senior inpatient mental-health and addiction treatment, outpatient partial-hospitalization and intensive-outpatient programmes, and ECT therapy. Addiction services include detox. Ask assessment staff which treatment, campus schedule and telehealth option fit the person’s needs. Ask about the Help for Heroes programme for military members, veterans and first responders.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Gilbert location serves adults and seniors. Assessment determines clinical fit, treatment level and payment arrangements.

**Population Served**
Adults and seniors in the Phoenix area, including Mesa residents able to reach Gilbert, who need mental-health or addiction treatment.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Gilbert location at 480-667-5500. The provider lists 24/7 walk-in access at 3755 S Rome Street. Its general 24/7 line is 480-565-3035.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm insurance, costs, available treatment and transport before travel. This Gilbert page does not establish adolescent admission; ask for an appropriate youth provider when needed.

resources.name: Perinatal Mental Health Alliance of Arizona and PSI HelpLine
resources.description: Perinatal Mental Health Alliance of Arizona, the Arizona chapter of Postpartum Support International, connects pregnant and postpartum people, partners, and families with perinatal mental-health support, information, volunteers, support options, and provider resources.
resources.hours: PSI HelpLine messages can be left any time; calls and texts are returned during business hours 8:00 AM-11:00 PM Eastern. It is not a crisis hotline.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Perinatal mental-health support, information, encouragement, resource connection, Arizona chapter resources, English and Spanish HelpLine access, online support options, and provider-directory connection through Postpartum Support International.

**Eligibility Requirements**
People affected by pregnancy, postpartum, pregnancy loss, and perinatal mental-health concerns, plus partners, families, and supporters, may use the support and navigation resources. Referred providers and groups have their own availability, cost, and licensure details.

**Population Served**
Pregnant, postpartum, and perinatal people and families throughout Arizona, including Mesa and Maricopa County. English and Spanish text/phone access is listed.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 1-800-944-4773, pressing 1 for Spanish or 2 for English. Text Help to 800-944-4773 in English or text in Spanish to 971-203-7773. Use pmhaaz.org for Arizona chapter resources.

**Important Information to Know**
This is support and navigation, not emergency response, guaranteed therapy, psychiatry, or crisis dispatch. PSI says people in crisis should use emergency resources; the National Maternal Mental Health Hotline is 833-852-6262 and 988 is available for suicide/crisis support.

resources.name: Area Agency on Aging, Region One - Health Promotion Program
resources.description: Area Agency on Aging, Region One's Health Promotion program offers evidence-based healthy living classes, virtually and in person, including fall-prevention, movement, walking and continence education programs.
resources.address: 1366 E. Thomas Rd., Suite 108, Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.hours: Class schedules vary; contact the Senior HELP LINE to find a nearby or virtual class.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Evidence-based classes such as Bingocize, Geri-Fit, Matter of Balance, Mind Over Matter, Tai Chi and Walk With Ease to promote physical activity, wellness, balance, fall prevention and healthy living.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public page does not list a single age threshold, cost or universal eligibility rule. Class participation depends on current offerings, registration, location or virtual format, accommodations and available space.

**Population Served**
Older adults in Maricopa County seeking healthy living, movement, fall-prevention and wellness classes.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Senior HELP LINE at 602-264-HELP (4357) or toll-free 888-783-7500 and ask for a Health Promotion class near Mesa or a virtual option.

**Important Information to Know**
Class sites and schedules change. Confirm current Mesa availability, cost if any, accessibility accommodations and whether a clinician's clearance is needed for the client's condition.

resources.name: Terros Health / former Lifewell — Substance-use treatment access
resources.description: Terros Health/Lifewell Behavioral Wellness substance-use treatment and whole-person behavioral health access in Mesa, including outpatient SUD treatment, counseling, MAT, medication services, care coordination, telehealth and youth/family behavioral-health options.
resources.address: 1111 S Stapley Dr, Mesa, AZ 85204; Javelina Health Center: 222 E Javelina Ave, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Stapley Health Center clinic/telehealth: Monday-Thursday 7:30 AM-8:00 PM, Friday-Saturday 7:30 AM-5:00 PM, Sunday closed. Javelina Health Center: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM, weekends and federal holidays closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Terros Health provides substance-use treatment, intensive outpatient and standard outpatient treatment, relapse prevention, recovery maintenance, prevention/education, medication-assisted treatment for opioid or alcohol use disorders, counseling, medication services, psychiatry, telehealth and whole-health care. Mesa access includes Stapley Health Center and Javelina Health Center; Café Stapley supports youth behavioral-health services and includes substance-use treatment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Terros community health centers state they provide affordable care regardless of ability to pay. Appointment requests support Medicaid/AHCCCS, Medicare, commercial insurance, no insurance/self-pay and other coverage. Clinical fit, exact program assignment and payer details must be confirmed.

**Population Served**
Mesa and East Valley adults, youth and families needing substance-use or behavioral-health care. Café programming is designed for adolescents ages 12-17; adult services are available through community health centers.

**How to Best Connect**
For mental health, substance-use treatment or specialty care, call 602-685-6000 or use the appointment request form. Stapley Health Center is at 1111 S Stapley Dr, Mesa, and walk-in appointments are welcome according to the appointments page. Existing patients may also use 602-302-7900 for Stapley.

**Important Information to Know**
Ask Patient Access which site, age-specific programme and referral pathway fits. Medication treatment, residential or justice-related services have separate clinical and payer requirements. Call before a walk-in visit; a general request does not guarantee each listed service at every clinic.

resources.name: Valle del Sol Community Health - Birth to Five Services
resources.description: Valle del Sol Birth to Five Services provides early childhood mental-health and family support for infants through age five, pregnant mothers and expectant parents, including therapists, early childhood specialists, Circle of Security groups, resource navigation, walk-ins, insurance help and sliding-fee options.
resources.address: Listed programme location: 3807 N. 7th St., Phoenix, AZ 85014. Ask intake about Mesa or remote access.
resources.hours: Call 602-258-6797, walk in, or schedule online; after-hours services are available by calling the main number.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Valle del Sol Birth to Five Services offers early-childhood support specialists, therapists trained to work with very young children and caregivers, Circle of Security parenting groups, pregnancy/expectant-parent support, help with biting, tantrums, aggression, communication concerns, parental distress, postpartum depression, child welfare involvement and daycare/preschool expulsion risk.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is for families needing emotional, behavioral, relationship or parenting support for children from infancy through age five, and for pregnant mothers or expectant parents preparing for a new baby. Valle del Sol says it accepts walk-ins, works with insurance and offers sliding-fee scale options.

**Population Served**
Families across the Valley, including Phoenix and Mesa, with infants and children through age five, pregnant mothers, expectant parents and caregivers. English- and Spanish-speaking staff are listed.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-258-6797, schedule through the patient portal or use walk-in access. The Birth to Five page lists Central Phoenix at 3807 N. 7th St., Phoenix, AZ 85014; call to confirm the nearest Mesa/East Valley access point.

**Important Information to Know**
The programme serves Valley families, including Mesa, but its listed Birth to Five location is in Central Phoenix. Confirm the actual appointment site or remote option and insurance/sliding-fee arrangements before travel.

resources.name: Society of St. Vincent de Paul of Arizona - Parish Conference Thrift Gift Cards and Mesa Assistance Routing
resources.description: Society of St. Vincent de Paul of Arizona routes households to help with food, clothing, shelter, medical/dental and more; clothing or thrift support is handled through local SVdP assistance routes and varies by conference.
resources.address: Neighborhood parish conferences across Maricopa County; Mesa Dining Room: 49 W Broadway Rd, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Conference hours vary by neighborhood. Call or use the get-help route before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Help routing for food, clothing, shelter, medical and dental care and other supports. Clothing/household help may include thrift-store assistance or gift cards through local parish conference screening when available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Parish conferences serve by neighborhood boundaries and have unique volunteer-run hours and requirements. People should use the SVdP get-help route or 2-1-1 to identify the correct conference.

**Population Served**
People in need in Mesa and Maricopa County who fall within a local SVdP parish conference's service boundary.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the SVdP get-help page, call 602-266-HOPE (4673) for general guidance, or call 2-1-1 for help identifying the correct conference or assistance route.

**Important Information to Know**
Do not treat the Mesa thrift store or dining room as an unrestricted free clothing closet. Clothing or household help varies by conference, funding and screening; call first.

resources.name: City of Chandler - Chandler Flex on-demand transit
resources.description: Chandler Flex is the City of Chandler's app- or phone-booked on-demand shared public transportation service for trips within the Chandler Flex service area.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday, 5:30 AM-9:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Chandler Flex provides on-demand shared public rides in branded vehicles within its service area. Riders can request a ride by mobile app or by calling in, including trips for commuting, school activities and local errands.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Trips must fit the Chandler Flex service area, hours, vehicle capacity and fare rules. It is a Chandler service and does not generally serve Mesa trips unless a current service-area map or transfer option supports the trip.

**Population Served**
Chandler residents and visitors using the Chandler Flex zone, with reduced fares for seniors and individuals with disabilities and free student trips to or from school.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Chandler Flex link/app or call Chandler Transit for service-area questions at 480-782-3440. Confirm pickup and destination are inside the current zone before relying on the ride.

**Important Information to Know**
Flex costs $2 per ride, or $1 for seniors and people with disabilities; qualifying student trips to or from school are free. Chandler's separate first/last-mile Lyft programme offers up to a 50% discount subject to the south-of-Pecos service area and designated-stop conditions. Confirm those conditions with Chandler Transit; this is not unrestricted travel between Mesa and Chandler. Flex is also distinct from ADA Paratransit, RideChoice and fixed-route buses. For regional transfers or accessibility options, ask Chandler Transit about fixed-route buses, ADA Paratransit or RideChoice and their separate eligibility rules.

resources.name: AZCEND — Chandler-area rent, utility and mortgage assistance
resources.description: AZCEND Community Action Program provides Chandler, Sun Lakes, and Queen Creek residents with rent, utility, mortgage, and Housing Stability Rental and Utility Assistance 3 support when eligible.
resources.address: 345 S California St, Chandler, AZ 85225
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 7:30 AM-4:00 PM; Tuesday 7:30 AM-6:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Community Action Program assistance for rent, utilities including water, gas, and electricity, and mortgage costs. The HSRUA3 program may provide up to one month of past-due rent and associated late fees for eligible renting households at risk of homelessness or housing instability.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For residents of Chandler, Sun Lakes and Queen Creek. Income, residence and hardship documentation and programme-specific requirements apply. HSRUA3 prioritizes households at or below 200% of federal poverty guidelines. Its document list includes photo ID, lease, proof of residence, 30 days of income and hardship/housing-instability evidence; landlords must complete applicable vendor/W-9 requirements.

**Population Served**
Eligible households in AZCEND's listed Chandler, Sun Lakes, and Queen Creek service area. This is not a Mesa-city program but may help nearby East Valley/Maricopa County households.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-963-1423 ext. 126, email cap@azcend.org, or use the Maricopa County client portal link on AZCEND's rent and utilities page.

**Important Information to Know**
This CAP route does not serve City of Mesa residents. HSRUA3 excludes prior ERA rent recipients, while prior utility-only recipients may qualify. Funding, landlord participation and additional documentation affect approval. Gilbert has a separate AZCEND office and water-discount programme.

resources.name: St. Mary's Food Bank / AZ Food Help - Food Finder, Mobile Pantry and Home Delivery
resources.description: St. Mary's Food Bank and AZ Food Help provide food-finder navigation, direct Phoenix food distribution, and home delivery for eligible Maricopa, Yavapai, Pinal and Coconino County residents unable to travel to a pantry.
resources.address: Phoenix Neighborhood Food Center: 3131 W Thomas Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85017; administration/distribution center: 2831 N 31st Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85009; home delivery has no walk-in address
resources.hours: Phoenix Neighborhood Food Center: Monday-Friday 7:30 AM-1:30 PM. Home delivery window is generally 6:00 AM-6:00 PM after registration and scheduling. Partner pantry schedules vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
AZ Food Help is St. Mary's Food Bank's map for food pantries, mobile pantries and other food resources. St. Mary's also operates direct weekday food distribution at its Phoenix Neighborhood Food Center and a Home Delivery Program for emergency food boxes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Home delivery requires being 18 or older, certifying household income at or below 185% of the Federal Poverty Level, and meeting at least one access barrier such as disability, mental-health condition, prolonged illness, increased illness risk or lack of reliable transportation other than public transit. Someone must be present with valid photo ID at delivery. Partner pantries have their own rules.

**Population Served**
Arizona households seeking food resources, including Maricopa County residents and people with disability, illness or transportation barriers who may qualify for home delivery.

**How to Best Connect**
Use AZFoodHelp.org to search by ZIP code for nearby pantries and mobile distributions. For home delivery or additional food help, call 602-344-4124 or register through the home-delivery page. For general St. Mary's information, call 602-242-3663.

**Important Information to Know**
Mesa access will usually be through partner sites, the food finder or home-delivery screening, not the Phoenix warehouse. Home delivery is subject to scheduling and capacity; one delivery per household per week is listed as subject to change.

resources.name: Family Promise of Greater Phoenix - Homelessness Prevention and Diversion Support
resources.description: Family Promise of Greater Phoenix provides diversion and prevention-oriented housing stability support for families with children, including individualized planning, landlord communication, community-resource connection, and limited rental assistance for eligible graduate families participating in its Connections graduate program.
resources.address: 7447 E Earll Drive, Scottsdale, AZ 85251
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Diversion conversations, individualized planning, case management, help identifying safe temporary housing options, reconnecting with supportive people, landlord/property-manager communication, community-resource and housing-program connections, transportation-barrier problem solving, and limited rental assistance for eligible graduate families in the Connections program.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Families with children who are homeless or threatened with homelessness may call to learn about available services and resources. Rental assistance is limited to eligible families who previously graduated from a Family Promise program and are participating in the Graduate Program Connections.

**Population Served**
Families with children experiencing homelessness, at risk of homelessness, or maintaining housing after Family Promise program graduation.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-659-5227 to speak with a Family Promise team member. Main office: 7447 E Earll Drive, Scottsdale, AZ 85251; email info@FamilyPromiseAZ.org.

**Important Information to Know**
Family Promise states it does not provide general rental or eviction assistance to families who have not participated in one of its programs. Assistance is based on eligibility, funding, space, and family circumstances.

resources.name: Helen's Hope Chest - Clothing Boutique and Back to School
resources.description: Helen's Hope Chest provides no-cost clothing and essential items for children, youth and teens in foster or kinship care, including outfits, shoes, jackets, undergarments, pajamas and accessories every three months.
resources.address: 126 E University Dr, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost foster/kinship clothing boutique with new or like-new outfits, shoes, jackets, undergarments, pajamas and accessories every three months. Other essential supports may include books, hygiene products, diapers, infant supplies, birthday gifts, holiday gifts, quilts, school supplies, uniforms and backpacks.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For children, youth and teens in foster care or kinship care and their caregivers. Caregivers should confirm appointment needs and required placement or kinship documentation before visiting.

**Population Served**
Arizona children and youth in foster care, qualifying kinship care or guardianship, and the foster/kinship families caring for them.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-969-5411 or email info@helenshopechest.org. The Mesa location is 126 E University Dr.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general-public clothing closet. Clothing is generally available every three months, and essential-supply inventory varies by donations and seasonal program timing.

resources.name: GateWay Community College - Healthcare United at GateWay (HUG) Clinic
resources.description: GateWay Community College's Healthcare United at GateWay (HUG) Clinic is a state-licensed pro bono specialty-care teaching clinic offering free care such as pulmonary rehabilitation, physical therapy, occupational therapy and diagnostic ultrasound for underserved, uninsured or financially distressed community members.
resources.address: 555 N. 18th Street, Suite 301 & 302, Phoenix, AZ 85006
resources.hours: Administrative hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM. Services are offered during academic semesters.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free specialty care delivered by supervised healthcare students, including pulmonary rehabilitation, physical therapy, occupational therapy and diagnostic ultrasound for injuries and pregnancy.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The clinic serves community members who are underserved, uninsured or experiencing financial hardship. Patients may receive up to 24 visits or one full school year of care, and three no-shows can lead to discharge and waitlist placement.

**Population Served**
Underserved, uninsured or financially distressed community members in the Phoenix/Maricopa County area, including people with chronic conditions or specialty-care gaps.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-286-8511 for appointments other than ultrasound; self-scheduling is available for ultrasound. Email hugclinic@gatewaycc.edu. Address: 555 N. 18th Street, Suite 301 & 302, Phoenix, AZ 85006.

**Important Information to Know**
Care is tied to academic semesters and student-supervised training. Arrive early for paperwork and bring photo ID. Appointment availability and service fit should be confirmed before referral.

resources.name: International Rescue Committee in Phoenix - Refugee Cash Assistance and Case Coordination
resources.description: IRC in Phoenix provides Refugee Cash Assistance for eligible single adults and couples seeking employment, plus case coordination for emergency needs, housing stability, transportation-related essential needs, and long-term self-sufficiency for refugees and other newcomers.
resources.address: 4425 W Olive Ave, #400, Glendale, AZ 85302
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
IRC in Phoenix lists Refugee Cash Assistance as temporary financial support for eligible single adults and couples actively seeking employment. IRC also lists case coordination for emergency needs, housing stability and long-term self-sufficiency, along with refugee support, employment, health, safety and wellness, and community-integration services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Refugee Cash Assistance is for eligible single adults and couples who are actively seeking employment and who meet program rules through the State of Arizona partnership. IRC Phoenix services are aimed at refugees, asylees, asylum seekers, trafficking survivors, torture survivors and other immigrants; exact eligibility depends on immigration category and program.

**Population Served**
Refugees, asylees, asylum seekers, victims of human trafficking, survivors of torture and other immigrants in the Phoenix/Maricopa area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call IRC Phoenix at 602-433-2440 or email Phoenix@rescue.org. The office is at 4425 W Olive Ave, #400, Glendale, AZ 85302.

**Important Information to Know**
Mesa residents should ask whether their immigration category, address and resettlement-agency assignment fit IRC Phoenix intake. Refugee Cash Assistance is temporary and employment-focused; it is not general public cash assistance.

resources.name: Gilbert Public Schools · Gilbert Adult Learning Program
resources.description: Gilbert Adult Learning Program offers GED, Adult Basic Education/Adult Secondary Education, ESOL, and workplace training classes with morning and evening class times at the Gilbert Adult Learning Center.
resources.address: 55 N. Greenfield Rd., Gilbert, AZ 85234
resources.hours: GED/ABE mornings Monday and Wednesday 9:00 AM-noon; GED/ABE evenings Monday and Wednesday 5:30-8:30 PM; ESOL mornings Tuesday and Thursday 9:00 AM-noon; ESOL evenings Tuesday and Thursday 5:30-8:30 PM, subject to current registration and waitlist status.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
GED preparation, Adult Basic Education/Adult Secondary Education, English for Speakers of Other Languages, college and career readiness, computer literacy embedded in ESOL, civics education, and workplace certification classes such as Retail Industry Fundamentals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Students must be at least 16 years old and withdrawn from high school. Minors must register with a parent or legal guardian. Students must register before class, declare lawful presence in the United States, provide valid photo ID, attend regularly, and complete placement testing.

**Population Served**
Adult learners in Gilbert, the East Valley, and Maricopa County who can attend classes in Gilbert and meet adult education eligibility rules.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-497-3334, email gpsadulted@gilbertschools.net, or complete the class interest form to be added to the waitlist. Ask whether seats are available and whether the desired GED, ESOL, or workplace training class fits the client's schedule.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not in Mesa city limits. The page indicates interested students should complete the interest form to join a waitlist and staff will reach out when seats become available.

resources.name: Arizona Justice Center Legal Assistance, Social Services, and Life Coaching
resources.description: Arizona Justice Center is a Glendale/Maricopa County legal and social-service resource offering free legal consultations, navigation for housing, SNAP, IDs, legal documents, emergency housing, mailing address support, and life coaching; Arizona courts list it for Housing Stability and Domestic Violence legal-advocate support.
resources.address: 5585 W Glenn Dr, Glendale, AZ 85301
resources.hours: Monday 9:00 AM-2:00 PM; Tuesday 9:00 AM-2:00 PM; Wednesday 9:00 AM-3:00 PM; Thursday 9:00 AM-2:00 PM; Friday 9:00 AM-12:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free legal consultations, social-service navigation, life coaching, help completing SNAP applications, locating housing, obtaining identification cards, processing legal documents, veterans benefits help, emergency housing connections, and mailing address support. Arizona courts list Arizona Justice Center as an approved organization for Housing Stability and Domestic Violence legal-advocate support in Glendale/Maricopa County.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The programme assists vulnerable, low-income, homeless and crisis-affected people; the website does not publish a universal eligibility test. Case acceptance depends on the issue, capacity and conflict review. Mesa residents should confirm service-area fit.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County residents facing housing, food, legal, identity-document, or stability barriers, including people experiencing homelessness, seniors, veterans, single mothers with children, and domestic-violence survivors when the legal issue fits its approved support areas.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 623-939-6546 for legal help questions, 623-847-2772 for the main office, or use the website contact form. For after-hours or emergencies the site lists 602-377-9013, but immediate danger should go to 911.

**Important Information to Know**
The office is in Glendale and has West Valley roots. Confirm Mesa access and the exact legal or document-help scope before travel. It assists with documents and referrals but does not issue government IDs, guarantee full representation or provide a shelter bed. Ask specifically about domestic-violence advocate capacity when relevant.

resources.name: Family Reach - Financial Assistance Funds
resources.description: Family Reach offers cancer financial-assistance grants for non-medical expenses when funds are available and provides resource navigation for housing, food, utility and transportation needs; current direct grant availability is fund-specific.
resources.hours: Office hours listed by Family Reach: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM ET.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Cancer-related financial assistance grants, when funds are available, for non-medical expenses such as mortgage or rent, utilities, groceries and transportation. Family Reach also provides resource tools for housing, food, transportation and utilities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applications for direct grants must be submitted by a member of the patient's health-care team where the patient is receiving treatment. Current official page prominently lists a Clinical Trial Access Fund for patients with multiple myeloma participating in specified MMRC Horizon One or Horizon Two trials in a U.S. state or territory and within 300% FPL.

**Population Served**
Cancer patients and families in the United States, including Mesa residents, when a matching Family Reach fund or resource-navigation pathway fits their diagnosis and need.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the treating oncology team or social worker to review the Family Reach financial-assistance page and submit the application if a fund fits. For questions, call 973-394-1411.

**Important Information to Know**
Direct grants are limited by currently open funds and processed in order received. A broader cancer diagnosis does not guarantee an open grant; use the resource-finder options when no direct fund fits.

resources.name: Chicanos Por La Causa - Keogh Health Connection
resources.description: CPLC Keogh Health Connection provides free enrollment assistance and resource navigation for AHCCCS, KidsCare, Marketplace health insurance, SNAP and TANF, with community health workers/promotores available for social-service linkage.
resources.address: 3620 N. 4th Ave., Suite 200, Phoenix, AZ 85013
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:30 AM-5:00 PM; call for an appointment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Keogh Health Connection provides free enrollment assistance for AHCCCS, KidsCare, Marketplace health insurance, SNAP and TANF. Healthcare navigators and community health workers/promotores help clients work through forms, coverage processes, social-service referrals and health education.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Each benefit has its own eligibility rules. Keogh navigation is not senior-specific and Medicare counseling is not the focus of the official page.

**Population Served**
People and households needing health coverage, food or cash-benefit application assistance and related resource navigation, including Mesa residents who can use the Phoenix contact route.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-266-0397 to make an appointment or email keogh@cplc.org. The Phoenix office is open Monday-Friday 8:30 AM-5:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
Assistance does not guarantee benefit approval. This is not a dedicated Medicare-plan counseling programme; SHIP handles that need. The separate Mighty Families service has school-district boundaries and should not be assumed available throughout Mesa.

resources.name: Hacienda Healthcare - Day Treatment and Training for Adults (DTA)
resources.description: Hacienda Healthcare's Day Treatment and Training for Adults program in Phoenix serves adults age 18 and older with intellectual and physical disabilities through sensory, movement, music, recreational and community-inclusion activities.
resources.address: 1402 E. South Mountain Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85042
resources.hours: Call for intake, program schedule and medical/support fit.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Day Treatment and Training for Adults with exercises to improve movement, sensory activities, massages, weekly music therapy, individual and group activities, community outings, recreational experiences and support for special medical needs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Hacienda says the program welcomes individuals age 18 and older with intellectual and physical disabilities. Intake determines goals and program fit. DDD authorization, medical acuity criteria, transportation and openings should be confirmed.

**Population Served**
Adults with intellectual and physical disabilities in Phoenix/Maricopa County, including people with special medical support needs when the program is appropriate.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-243-4231 or contact the program at 1402 E. South Mountain Ave., Phoenix. Ask about admissions, DDD authorization, medical support capacity and transportation from Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an adult day program, not residential placement or emergency care. Transportation from Mesa and current capacity are not established on the public page.

resources.name: Southwest Gas — Third-party past-due notices
resources.description: Lets a customer arrange for a trusted person to receive notices when a Southwest Gas bill becomes delinquent.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Lets a customer arrange for a trusted person to receive notices when a Southwest Gas bill becomes delinquent.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Southwest Gas account holder arranges a designated third-party notification contact under the provider’s account rules.

**Population Served**
Southwest Gas customers who want another person notified about past-due bills.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Southwest Gas to ask about third-party notification and how the account holder and chosen contact should enroll.

**Important Information to Know**
Receiving a notice does not make the contact responsible for paying the bill. This is a notification service, not financial assistance or a guarantee against disconnection.

resources.name: St. Matthew United Methodist Church - Food Box Ministry
resources.description: St. Matthew United Methodist Church distributes free food boxes every other Saturday morning in Mesa, usually until the limited supply is gone.
resources.address: 2540 W Baseline Rd, Mesa, AZ 85202
resources.hours: Every other Saturday morning on posted 2026 dates. Arrive before about 7:15 AM; distribution normally ends when boxes are gone, usually around 8:00 AM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Food boxes intended to feed a family of four for about 3-4 days. The ministry distributes boxes every other Saturday and reports handing out an average of about 55 boxes per event.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page describes service for neighborhood families needing temporary help and does not list ID, income, residence or frequency requirements. Distribution is supply-limited.

**Population Served**
Mesa-area families and individuals needing temporary food support.

**How to Best Connect**
Drive to St. Matthew United Methodist Church, 2540 W Baseline Rd, Mesa, before about 7:15 AM on a giveaway Saturday. The line starts in the west parking lot, accessible from Baseline or Javelina. Call 480-838-7309 or email office@stmatthewmesa.org for questions.

**Important Information to Know**
Boxes are first come, first served and often gone by about 8:00 AM. Posted remaining 2026 dates from September 26 forward include October 10 and 24, November 7 and 21, and December 5 and 19; verify the date before going.

resources.name: NaloxoneAZ — Naloxone Distribution-Site Finder
resources.description: An Arizona map and location search for community naloxone distribution sites.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

An Arizona map and location search for community naloxone distribution sites.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Anyone can use the finder. Individual sites determine distribution rules, current stock and any cost.

**Population Served**

People seeking naloxone for themselves, a household member or someone else at risk of opioid overdose.

**How to Best Connect**

Search the map near the preferred location, then contact the listed site before traveling to confirm access and supply.

**Important Information to Know**

This is a supply-finding tool, not emergency dispatch or treatment. Call911 for a suspected overdose; a map listing does not guarantee that a site has naloxone available.

resources.name: Barrow Neurological Institute - Spinal Cord Injury Wellness Clinic
resources.description: Barrow Neurological Institute offers one-day interdisciplinary spinal cord injury wellness evaluations in Phoenix, with individualized recommendations for rehabilitation, adaptive equipment, psychosocial supports, community resources, peer mentors and vocational rehabilitation.
resources.address: 222 West Thomas Road, Suite 100, Phoenix, AZ 85013
resources.hours: Physician referral required; call for scheduling.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
One-day interdisciplinary evaluation for people living with spinal cord injuries or spinal cord disorders. The visit may include rehabilitation specialists, therapy evaluations, nursing, social work, community resource education, adaptive-equipment recommendations, peer mentor referrals and vocational rehabilitation recommendations.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A physician referral is required. Barrow says the referral should be for a physical or occupational therapy evaluation, attention SCI Wellness Clinic, and faxed to 602-294-5035.

**Population Served**
People with traumatic, non-traumatic, congenital or acquired spinal cord injuries or disorders who can access the Phoenix outpatient clinic.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-406-1600 or email Barrow-SCIwellness@CommonSpirit.org for information. Referring physicians fax referrals to 602-294-5035. Clinic location is Barrow Outpatient Neuro-Rehabilitation Center, 222 West Thomas Road, Suite 100, Phoenix.

**Important Information to Know**
This is specialty medical rehabilitation access, not a walk-in community resource office. Insurance, scheduling and whether the clinic is the right fit should be confirmed before travel.

resources.name: Mesa Community College · Career and Technical Education Programs
resources.description: Mesa Community College Career and Technical Education offers workforce-oriented certificates and degrees that combine career-focused study with hands-on classes and industry-advised programs across more than 40 CTE areas and 200+ degrees/certificates.
resources.address: 1833 W Southern Ave, Mesa, AZ 85202; 7110 E McKellips Road, Mesa, AZ 85207; MCC Online
resources.hours: Campus and program hours vary; use MCC enrollment/advising routes.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Career-focused certificates and applied degrees across trades, technology, healthcare, business, education and related fields. Applied Technology options include automotive service, CAD/drafting, construction, manufacturing/CNC, industrial electrical/mechanical systems, robotics, data-centre operations, cable/wire harness assembly, soldering and welding. Other CTE pathways include behavioral health and information technology.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Apply to MCC/Maricopa Community Colleges and meet the chosen credential’s requirements. Open college admission does not waive course prerequisites, placement, selective admission, clinical/licensing requirements or any applicable background checks.

**Population Served**
Mesa and Maricopa Community Colleges students seeking career-focused certificates, degrees or workforce advancement.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the MCC Career & Technical Education page to narrow the program, then contact MCC admissions/advising or call 480-461-7000. Main campuses include Southern and Dobson, Red Mountain and MCC Online.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm the specific credential, campus, term, course availability, duration, tuition, materials and prerequisites with advising. Financial-aid or WIOA eligibility must be established for the selected programme; a catalog listing is not funded enrollment or a job guarantee.

resources.name: Salt River Project (SRP) - SHARE Emergency Bill Assistance
resources.description: SRP Project SHARE energy assistance route for customers needing help with electric bills, accessed through SRP Customer Resource Counselors.
resources.hours: SRP residential customer service is available 24/7; Customer Resource Counselor hours may vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Project SHARE is SRP's Service to Help Arizonans with Relief on Energy program. SRP partners with The Salvation Army and customers to provide energy assistance, and SRP says matching contributions support the SRP Bill Assistance program for limited-income customers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Customers needing SHARE funds must be SRP customers seeking energy bill assistance. Eligibility, documents, referral office, and award availability are determined through SRP Customer Resource Counselors and the appropriate Salvation Army office.

**Population Served**
SRP customers in need of energy bill assistance, including eligible Mesa customers in SRP territory.

**How to Best Connect**
Call SRP Customer Resource Counselors at 602-236-3000 to request assistance and referral to the appropriate Salvation Army office. General SRP questions can go to 602-236-8888.

**Important Information to Know**
Obtain SRP referral instructions before visiting a Salvation Army office. Eligibility, required documents and assistance amounts depend on programme rules and available funds.

resources.name: 4th Trimester Arizona - Parent Support Villages
resources.description: 4th Trimester Arizona offers postpartum and early-parenting peer support villages, including an East Valley group in Mesa, virtual village, Black Mamas Support Village, Indigenous Parents Support, Pueblo de Mamas Latinas, Dad Village, and other parent groups.
resources.address: East Valley Village: IDEA Museum, 150 W. Pepper Pl., Mesa, AZ 85201; virtual groups also available
resources.hours: East Valley Village is listed for the 2nd Wednesday at 10:00 AM; Virtual Village is listed every 3rd Tuesday at 12:00 PM. Confirm current Eventbrite registration before attending.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
4th Trimester Arizona offers peer support, parent connection, and postpartum community through in-person and virtual Villages. The East Valley Village meets in Mesa, and the organization also lists virtual, Black Mamas, Indigenous Parents, Latino/bilingual, Dad Village, AfterGlow, and other parent support options.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Villages are support groups for pregnant, postpartum, and parenting families rather than medical care or material assistance. Registration may be required through each Village event page.

**Population Served**
Arizona parents and caregivers during pregnancy, postpartum, and early parenting, including Mesa and East Valley parents and population-specific groups for Black mothers, Indigenous parents, Latino/bilingual families, and fathers.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Village page registration link for the desired group. For East Valley, the page lists the IDEA Museum, 150 W. Pepper Pl., Mesa, AZ 85201, at 10:00 AM on the 2nd Wednesday. Call 480-269-1639 or email info@4thtrimesteraz.org for current registration and access questions.

**Important Information to Know**
This is peer and community support, not medical care, counseling, or emergency help. Meeting times, exact locations, and registration links can change, so confirm the current Eventbrite listing before sending a family.

resources.name: Banner Alzheimer's Institute - Stead Family Memory Center
resources.description: Banner Alzheimer's Institute's Stead Family Memory Center provides specialized memory and dementia evaluation, treatment, education, support services, and research opportunities, with telehealth available through Banner memory care centers.
resources.address: 901 E. Willetta St., 1st and 3rd Floors, Phoenix, AZ 85006
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; Saturday-Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Stead Family Memory Center evaluates memory and thinking concerns and provides dementia care. Family and Community Services adds education, care planning, caregiver resources and support with behavioral or daily-living changes. Banner memory-center patients and families receive the Navigator guide at no cost.

**Eligibility Requirements**
This is a medical specialty service. Access may depend on appointment availability, insurance, referral requirements, clinical fit, and travel or telehealth suitability. Banner says most major insurance is accepted, but clients should check their own plan.

**Population Served**
People with memory or thinking changes, Alzheimer's disease or related dementias, movement disorders related to cognitive impairment, and their families or caregivers.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-839-6900. The Stead Family Memory Center is at 901 E. Willetta St., Phoenix. The new patient packet lists fax 602-839-6906 and email BAIinfo@bannerhealth.com for submitting completed packet materials.

**Important Information to Know**
Clinical visits have insurance and payment rules; a free Navigator guide does not make all medical care free. Ask which family programs are available to nonpatients and whether the needed appointment can be remote. This is not emergency psychiatric care.

resources.name: Aster Aging - Holiday Helpers
resources.description: Aster Aging's Holiday Helpers program provides seasonal gifts and essential items such as blankets, non-skid socks, toiletries, nightlights and gift cards for seniors in need, especially isolated older adults connected with Aster services.
resources.address: 45 W. University Dr., Ste. A, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Seasonal program; call Aster Aging for current timing.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Seasonal Holiday Helpers gifts and essentials for older adults, including suggested items such as gift cards, nightlights, toiletries, first-aid kits, blankets, throws and non-skid socks.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Aster states donated goods are delivered to its most isolated seniors and that Holiday Helpers supports seniors in need. It does not publish a public self-referral guarantee for gifts.

**Population Served**
Older adults connected with Aster Aging in Mesa and East Valley communities, especially isolated seniors with limited support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Aster Aging at 480-964-9014 to ask whether an older adult is eligible for Aster services and whether Holiday Helpers or another Aster program can address the current need.

**Important Information to Know**
This is seasonal and program-embedded. It is not an emergency clothing closet or general household-goods pantry, and item availability depends on donations.

resources.name: Mesa Community College · Hoop of Learning
resources.description: Mesa Community College Hoop of Learning is a high-school-to-college bridge program for American Indian high school students, with year-round applications, college-credit pathway support, and culturally grounded college-transition goals.
resources.address: 1833 W. Southern Ave., Mesa, AZ 85202
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A scholarship-supported high-school-to-college bridge for Native American students, combining college-credit study with culturally relevant preparation for further education. MCC describes Hoop of Learning as a fully funded scholarship programme and lists participation as free; confirm the current cohort, covered course costs and enrollment requirements.

**Eligibility Requirements**
MCC lists these requirements: Certificate of Indian Blood, 2.0 or higher GPA, and at least six high school credits completed. Students can start as early as the second semester of freshman year, and MCC encourages students to apply even if they are unsure they meet every requirement.

**Population Served**
Native American high school students connected to Mesa Community College and the Mesa area.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through the MCC Hoop of Learning page and include a copy of the CIB and unofficial high school transcript. Call 480-461-6200 for questions.

**Important Information to Know**
The page says MCC accepts year-round applications, but the listed Fall 2026 deadline was July 5, 2026. Confirm the current start term and deadline before referral.

resources.name: Florence Immigrant & Refugee Rights Project - Legal and social services for detained adults and unaccompanied children
resources.description: The Florence Immigrant & Refugee Rights Project provides free legal and social services to adults and children in immigration detention or facing removal in Arizona, including legal education, representation, social services and advocacy.
resources.address: Administrative correspondence: P.O. Box 86299, Tucson, AZ 85754-6299; services are delivered through program arrangements.
resources.hours: Use the website contact routes; not a general walk-in clinic.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free legal education, case support and social services for detained adults and unaccompanied children, with representation in selected cases.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adult legal services focus on immigration detention. Children’s programs also assist some formerly detained or released children; screening determines fit and representation capacity. Priorities may include medical or mental-health needs, LGBTQ identity, Indigenous-language barriers and family separation.

**Population Served**
Detained immigrants and eligible unaccompanied children.

**How to Best Connect**
Detained people can use facility phones to contact the project. Phoenix general inquiries: 602-307-1008; use the website’s separate child-programme route for an eligible child. Have the person’s name, A-number if known, facility/custody or release context and hearing dates available when speaking with the appropriate programme.

**Important Information to Know**
Not every case receives an attorney. People outside the program’s scope should use another current immigration provider, especially when facing a deadline. The office cannot answer general public immigration questions, give public legal advice or provide general referrals; visits require an appointment.

resources.name: U-Turn Foundation — Youth treatment identity hold
resources.description: Historical listings describe specialized treatment for young people with sexual-behavior or offense histories.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Historical listings describe specialized treatment for young people with sexual-behavior or offense histories.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Current operation, provider identity and treatment eligibility are not established by the older registry entries.

**Population Served**
Potentially Mesa-area youth and families requiring specialized treatment.

**How to Best Connect**
Administrators should reconcile the historical provider listings and confirm current operation before sharing a client referral.

**Important Information to Know**
Preserve the rare pathway as an administrator lead; no current primary website or intake was established. An old registry entry does not prove current availability or closure.
resources.resolutionReason: Historical provider identity is documented, but current operation, intake and the reported specialized youth sexual-behavior or offense-treatment scope remain unconfirmed.

resources.name: Mercy Housing Mountain Plains - Mesa Senior Meadows
resources.description: Mercy Housing's Mesa Senior Meadows is a 40-unit affordable senior apartment community in downtown Mesa for low-income adults age 62 and older, with onsite resident services, community room, laundry, and health and wellness programming. The official property page says it is currently accepting applications.
resources.address: 333 E 6th Street, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Office hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Affordable senior apartment housing with onsite resident services, monthly newsletters/calendars, age-in-place programs, community activities, community room, on-site laundry, and health and wellness programming.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Low-income seniors age 62 and older. Applicants must meet property income and rental criteria; current vacancies and application timing should be confirmed with the property.

**Population Served**
Low-income adults age 62 and older seeking affordable housing in Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Apply link on the official Mercy Housing property page or call 480-615-7893. TTY: 800-855-2880 or 711. Property address: 333 E 6th Street, Mesa, AZ 85201.

**Important Information to Know**
Use the official application route or call the leasing office about current intake, waitlist and vacancies. An application does not guarantee an available apartment, approval or a particular processing time.

resources.name: East Valley Institute of Technology — Adult career training and basic education
resources.description: EVIT Adult Education offers Mesa-based postsecondary career training for adults age 18 and older in health care, nursing, trades, cosmetology, EMT, welding, sterile processing, surgical technology, HVAC-R, plumbing, and related fields, with admissions and financial aid routes.
resources.address: 1601 W. Main St., Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Program schedules vary by pathway; contact admissions or financial aid before applying.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Adult career/technical training, certificates, degree pathways and apprenticeships, plus Adult Basic Education and GED/HSE options. Career fields include nursing and allied health, automotive/collision repair, aesthetics/cosmetology, electrical, HVAC-R, plumbing, welding, sterile processing and surgical technology.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adult career programmes serve students 18 and older, with programme-specific prerequisites, admissions and space requirements. Adult-only programmes use the Main Campus; select high-school programmes may accept adults when space permits. Ask separately about eligibility and scheduling for ABE/GED/HSE.

**Population Served**
Mesa, East Valley, and Phoenix-area adults seeking career training, certification, trades, health care credentials, or technical education.

**How to Best Connect**
Call EVIT at 480-461-4000 or contact the Adult Education Financial Aid Office at 480-461-4027 or adultfinancialaid@evit.edu. Use EVIT's admissions links to apply, schedule a tour, or connect with admissions for the selected program.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm the exact programme, campus, start date, cost, materials, duration and licensing/certification outcome before enrollment. Financial aid, scholarships, VA benefits and apprenticeship arrangements vary by pathway.

resources.name: Phoenix Legal Action Network — public legal information; new-case intake closed
resources.description: Public immigration legal information and referrals from PLAN; new representation requests are currently not accepted.
resources.address: Mail only: P.O. Box 33364, Phoenix, AZ 85067. Office meetings by appointment.
resources.hours: Office engagements are by appointment only. The legal-services page states intake is currently closed and new cases are not being accepted.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Immigration legal information through PLAN’s knowledge center and posted referrals. Its representation program is currently closed to new cases.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Public information is available online. If representation reopens, its eligibility and case priorities must be checked then; there is no open new-case application now.

**Population Served**
Immigrants seeking legal information, including people facing removal.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the website’s knowledge center and referrals. Check the legal-services page for intake updates; general contact is 602-730-1726 or info@planphx.org.

**Important Information to Know**
New-case intake is closed. Do not wait for reopening when a legal deadline or hearing is approaching; seek a provider currently accepting that kind of case. General information is not representation or case-specific legal advice.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Child Safety Statewide Child Abuse Hotline
resources.description: Arizona Department of Child Safety Statewide Child Abuse Hotline is the statewide reporting access point for suspected child abuse, neglect, exploitation, or abandonment when domestic or family violence creates child-safety concerns.
resources.address: 3003 N Central Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.hours: Hotline is reachable 24 hours a day, seven days a week; online reporting is for mandated reporters with non-emergency concerns.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Receives reports of suspected child abuse, neglect, exploitation, or abandonment statewide. DCS assesses reports and, when criteria are met, assigns a local specialist for response. Mandated reporters may use the Guardian online portal for non-emergency reports.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Use when there is reasonable suspicion that a child is being abused, neglected, exploited, or abandoned by a parent, guardian, custodian, or qualifying household/caregiving person. If the alleged perpetrator does not have care, custody, or control of the child, the report may need to go to law enforcement only.

**Population Served**
Arizona children under 18, including children in Mesa and Maricopa County affected by family violence, neglect, exploitation, abandonment, or unsafe caregiving situations.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 1-888-SOS-CHILD (1-888-767-2445). For immediate danger call 911. Mandated reporters can use the Guardian online reporting portal only for non-emergency concerns.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a child-protection reporting and investigation pathway, not confidential survivor advocacy. Reports may trigger state involvement with the family. Survivors should receive safety planning and advocacy support when reporting could escalate danger.

resources.name: Codefy — Software Development Training
resources.description: No-cost virtual software-development and workplace-skills training, followed by a possible paid internship.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

No-cost virtual software-development and workplace-skills training, followed by a possible paid internship.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Published core requirements include age 18 or older, a high-school diploma or equivalent, a 2.0 GPA and work authorization. Partner entry routes may impose additional age or other criteria.

**Population Served**

Eligible adults seeking a software-development career through an approved partner pathway.

**How to Best Connect**

Contact Codefy about the next cohort and local partner referral. Training is scheduled Monday–Thursday, 8:30 AM–noon, for 12 weeks; confirm the applicable time zone and attendance requirements.

**Important Information to Know**

The subsequent 8–12-week paid internship depends on availability and is not guaranteed. Phoenix Indian Center is a partner, not another name for Codefy.

resources.name: Institute for Digital Inclusion Acceleration - The Hive at CCAZ Mesa / Digital Navigator Support
resources.description: The Institute for Digital Inclusion Acceleration opened a Mesa Hive at Child Crisis Arizona's Center for Child and Family Wellness, described as a free digital access and skills space with technology, workshops and digital navigators.
resources.address: 424 W. Rio Salado Pkwy, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Current public hours and walk-in or appointment rules were not confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Mesa Hive is described as a community technology space with free access to emerging technology, skill-building workshops and digital navigators. Public examples include app development, coding, robotics, video production, AI and 3-D printing.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The article describes the Mesa Hive as serving families and learners of all ages through the Child Crisis Arizona center, but does not publish current eligibility, appointment or walk-in rules.

**Population Served**
Mesa families, learners and community members needing digital access or skills support, especially families facing instability through the Child Crisis Arizona community hub.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Child Crisis Arizona at 480-834-9424 or email info@childcrisisaz.org about the Hive at 424 W. Rio Salado Parkway, Mesa. Ask for current digital-navigator availability, workshops, hours and any appointment or enrollment requirements.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm access before visiting; unrestricted walk-ins are not established. This is a free digital-learning and technology programme, distinct from Child Crisis Arizona’s clinical services.

resources.name: Matthew’s Closet — Family food and essential-items assistance
resources.description: Provides a Mesa contact for family food and essential-items assistance, with an emphasis on children and families involved with DCS.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides a Mesa contact for family food and essential-items assistance, with an emphasis on children and families involved with DCS.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Contact the organization to confirm current family eligibility, whether general pantry access is available, and appointment or documentation rules.

**Population Served**
Families needing food or basic supplies, particularly those involved with foster care or an open DCS case.

**How to Best Connect**
Call or text 602-888-1271 before travel. Food-bank records identify 2055 S Power Road; confirm the current entrance and pickup arrangement.

**Important Information to Know**
A directory’s April 2026 record date is not a provider verification date. Published weekday hours are not confirmed current; the no-cost mission does not establish unrestricted walk-in eligibility.

resources.name: Delivering Dreams Arizona - Delivering Dreams Bus Student Wardrobes
resources.description: Delivering Dreams Bus partners with high-poverty K-8 schools in the Greater Phoenix area to provide eligible students with brand-new clothing, shoes, socks, underwear, a sweatshirt and hygiene kit during school-scheduled events.
resources.address: 9224 N. 5th Street, Phoenix, AZ 85020
resources.hours: School-based events occur on each partner school's scheduled date; office contact by phone/email.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
School-based wardrobe packages for eligible K-8 students at partner schools. Each student receives clothing sized on the bus, including bottoms, shirts, a sweatshirt, shoes, socks, underwear and a hygiene kit.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligible students are signed up by personnel at partner high-poverty K-8 schools. Families do not access the bus as a public walk-in clothing closet.

**Population Served**
Clothing-insecure children attending partner schools in the Greater Phoenix area. Current public partner district examples are mostly Phoenix-area districts; Mesa school participation should be confirmed.

**How to Best Connect**
A family should ask the child's school counselor, parent liaison or front office whether the school participates. For program questions, call 602-944-7636 or email info@deliveringdreamsaz.org.

**Important Information to Know**
This is useful for school clothing needs but only through participating schools and scheduled school-day visits. It is not an emergency clothing closet for same-day household needs.

resources.name: Society of St. Vincent de Paul - Water Truck and Heat-Relief Outreach
resources.description: St. Vincent de Paul reports a seasonal water truck that conducts responsive outreach focused on delivering lifesaving services to people living outside who may not have access to heat-relief centers. The checked public page does not provide a client request line, schedule or Mesa route.
resources.address: Valley-wide seasonal outreach; no public water-truck dispatch address confirmed
resources.hours: Seasonal summer heat-relief operation; field schedule not published.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Seasonal water-truck heat-relief outreach delivering water and lifesaving heat-relief support to people living outside who may not be able to access cooling centers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
People living outside during extreme heat may be the intended recipients. Public eligibility, request criteria and geography are not stated on the checked source.

**Population Served**
Unsheltered people in the Valley during summer heat, especially those without practical access to heat-relief locations.

**How to Best Connect**
No public request line or route schedule was confirmed. For a Mesa client needing same-day cooling, use a listed cooling/respite site or emergency services when medically urgent; administrators can contact SVdP through its general channels to clarify water-truck coordination.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a useful outreach lead but not yet a responsible direct referral for a specific client because dispatch process, coverage map, field schedule and Mesa stops are unresolved.
resources.resolutionReason: Needs resolution: official SVdP heat-relief page confirms the water truck exists, but no public request route, field schedule, coverage map or Mesa access process was found.

resources.name: AZ Premier Dentistry - In-Home Mobile Dental Services
resources.description: AZ Premier Dentistry provides in-home mobile dental care for homebound, bedbound and dementia-affected geriatric patients in Maricopa County who cannot receive dental care in a traditional office.
resources.hours: Call to request information; public appointment hours are not listed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
In-home mobile dental care for people who cannot access a traditional dental office, with traveling dentistry services for homebound, bedbound and dementia-affected patients.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page focuses on homebound geriatric patients and people who cannot receive dental care the traditional way. It does not state income eligibility, insurance participation or charitable pricing.

**Population Served**
Homebound or bedbound older adults and patients with dementia in Maricopa County, Arizona.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 866-686-4423 to request information and ask about service area, fees, insurance, needed medical clearance and whether the patient can be treated at home.

**Important Information to Know**
This appears to be a private mobile dental provider, not a free clinic. Cost, insurance acceptance and low-cost options were not established on the opened official page.

resources.name: Veterans 5-9 - Nighttime and Weekend Veteran Support
resources.description: Veterans 5-9 provides nighttime and weekend-oriented veteran support and intake-form routing for needs such as homelessness, food, lodging, transportation, substance-use, mental-health, reentry and crisis stabilization.
resources.address: 1664 E Florence Blvd Suite 4 #108, Casa Grande, AZ 85122
resources.hours: Organization states it operates outside normal business hours, including nighttime and weekend times; exact live schedule is not published.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
After-hours-oriented support and case-management help for veterans and families. Public materials describe nighttime and weekend resources for substance-use, mental-health, homelessness, food, lodging, transportation and criminal-justice-cycle support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public site does not fully publish eligibility rules. Assistance is reviewed through the online intake questionnaire and depends on need, fit, service area and available resources.

**Population Served**
Veterans and veteran families in Arizona who need help outside normal business hours; Mesa and Maricopa response coverage should be confirmed before relying on the program.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the online Get Help questionnaire from the website, call 480-498-8700, or email veterans5to9@gmail.com or marcus@Veterans5-9.com. Include name and phone number in communications.

**Important Information to Know**
The provider is based in Casa Grande. Confirm Mesa/Maricopa service, current after-hours availability, program fit and funding before presenting this as a primary option.

resources.name: Arizona Women's Recovery Center - Sally's Place
resources.description: Arizona Women's Recovery Center's Sally's Place is treatment-based supportive housing for pregnant women and women with infants under 3 months who are actively seeking recovery from drug or alcohol use.
resources.address: 4201 N. 16th St., Suite 140, Phoenix, AZ 85016
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Sally's Place provides treatment-based supportive housing for pregnant women and women with very young infants who are in recovery from drug or alcohol use. Residents participate in AWRC's Women's Outpatient Program and may access family programming, career services, day care, transportation, health care, medication management, clothing/retail training, and 24-hour on-site staff support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Sally's Place is open to women who are pregnant or have recently given birth with an infant less than 3 months old, are actively seeking recovery from drug and/or alcohol use, and are enrolled in AWRC's women's outpatient substance-use program. AWRC states Sally's Place accepts clients receiving Serious Mental Illness services.

**Population Served**
Pregnant women and new mothers with infants under 3 months in Maricopa County or the Phoenix area who need recovery-focused supportive housing while participating in outpatient substance-use treatment.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Arizona Women's Recovery Center at 602-264-6214 to ask about Sally's Place intake, outpatient enrollment, current capacity, costs, and referral requirements. The listed AWRC address is 4201 N. 16th St., Suite 140, Phoenix.

**Important Information to Know**
Housing requires participation in AWRC outpatient substance-use treatment and is not general maternity housing. The official page describes six two-bedroom apartments, 12-18 month program duration, and treatment-based eligibility; capacity should be confirmed before referral.

resources.name: City of Mesa Housing Authority - Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing Voucher (HUD-VASH)
resources.description: Mesa Housing Authority identifies HUD-VASH as rental assistance for chronically homeless veterans and families, with Phoenix VA case management and clinical services and referral/access through the VA Community Resource & Referral Center.
resources.address: 200 S. Center Street, Building 1, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: VA CRRC: Monday–Friday, 7:30 AM–4:00 PM. Mesa Housing lobby hours are separate; confirm an appointment with a housing specialist.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
HUD-VASH combines Housing Choice Voucher rental assistance for chronically homeless veterans and families with VA case management and clinical services. Mesa Housing Authority administers housing programs, while Phoenix VA provides case management and clinical services for VASH.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The City of Mesa page describes HUD-VASH for chronically homeless veterans and their families. Access appears to be through VA homeless services rather than a direct public Mesa waitlist application; eligibility and voucher availability are determined through VA/HUD-VASH processes.

**Population Served**
Chronically homeless veterans and families connected to Mesa Housing Authority jurisdiction and Phoenix VA homeless services.

**How to Best Connect**
Begin with Phoenix VA CRRC at 1500 E. Thomas Road, Suite 106, Phoenix: 602-248-6040 or 602-568-7843, Monday–Friday, 7:30 AM–4:00 PM. Ask about Mesa HUD-VASH referral and eligibility. Mesa Housing is 480-644-3536; housing-specialist meetings require an appointment.

**Important Information to Know**
HUD-VASH is referral-based and depends on VA eligibility, homelessness status and voucher availability. Mesa Housing meetings with housing specialists are by appointment only.

resources.name: Where Hope Lives · Trafficking Recovery, Placement and Participant Support
resources.description: Provides age-routed trafficking-recovery placement and screened recovery programmes with housing, counseling, family support and practical participant needs.
resources.address: 3210 Grand Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85017
resources.hours: Call lines may be busy; the official page asks callers to allow up to 72 business hours for assistance unless there is an emergency.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Where Hope Lives offers human-trafficking recovery and placement help through age-routed intake. Recovery-programme supports include safe housing, trauma-informed counseling, family support, education, meals, clothing, bedding, hygiene items, transportation, medical/behavioral-care connections and case management. These are participant supports, not a public clothing closet.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For human-trafficking survivors or people seeking trafficking-related placement help. Placement hotline routes are separated by age: under 26 and age 26 or older. Availability and program fit must be screened.

**Population Served**
Human-trafficking survivors in Arizona/Phoenix pathways, including children, teens and young adults, with a separate listed line for adults 26 and older.

**How to Best Connect**
For placement under age 26 call 602-516-0033. For placement age 26 and older call 602-706-1876. General assistance office: 602-346-8716; program offices: 602-346-8786; main lobby: 602-346-8700. In immediate danger call 911.

**Important Information to Know**
This is trafficking-specific, not a general domestic-violence shelter or public material-aid programme. Placement and services depend on screening, age, capacity and safety needs. The official help page reports high call volume and up to 72 business hours for assistance; immediate danger needs emergency help. Arrange the actual safe destination through staff rather than assuming the public address is the placement site.

resources.name: West Valley Community Food Pantry
resources.description: West Valley Community Food Pantry provides emergency food boxes from its Glendale pantry with no address restrictions, one-time registration and ID requirements.
resources.address: 7205 N 51st Ave, Glendale, AZ 85301
resources.hours: Monday, Wednesday and Thursday, except holidays, 9:00 AM-12:00 noon; pantry closes promptly at noon.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency food boxes through a community pantry in Glendale.

**Eligibility Requirements**
There are no address restrictions. A client completes a one-time registration form in person. ID is required to fill out the form and pick up a box; household members can be listed, but IDs must be provided for each person included.

**Population Served**
People and households needing emergency food who can reach the Glendale pantry.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit 7205 N 51st Ave, Glendale, during pantry hours or call 623-848-8278. The registration form is not available online.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a west-valley option and may be a long trip from Mesa. It remains useful because the official page says there are no address restrictions. Confirm holiday closures before travel.

resources.name: CenturyLink Lifeline and Arizona Senior Telephone Discount Program
resources.description: CenturyLink participates in Lifeline for qualifying phone or broadband customers and offers Arizona's Senior Telephone Discount Program for qualifying Lifeline-approved seniors with landline voice service.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
CenturyLink Lifeline can discount qualifying voice or broadband service for eligible customers. Arizona also offers the Senior Telephone Discount Program through CenturyLink, which provides up to $3.14 per month off home landline telephone service for qualifying seniors already approved for Lifeline.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Customers must live in a CenturyLink service area and qualify for Lifeline through USAC. Only one Lifeline discount is available per household. For the Arizona Senior Telephone Discount Program, the customer must have voice service, be a qualifying senior, have qualified for Lifeline, and have household income at or below 100% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines.

**Population Served**
CenturyLink service-area customers in Arizona who meet federal Lifeline rules; the Arizona senior telephone discount is for qualifying senior landline voice customers.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply for Lifeline through USAC first, then notify CenturyLink with the confirmation number so the discount can be added to qualifying service. CenturyLink's Arizona assistance page also lists 1-800-244-1111 for obtaining application forms.

**Important Information to Know**
Ask CenturyLink to confirm the senior age requirement, actual address and qualifying voice plan. Federal Lifeline is one household benefit, not separate voice and broadband discounts. The state senior add-on applies only to voice service. Quantum Simply Fiber is a separate new-customer internet programme.

resources.name: A New Leaf / MesaCAN - Rent, Mortgage, and Utility Assistance
resources.description: MesaCAN provides first-come, first-served rent, mortgage, and utility assistance for low-income City of Mesa residents with past-due housing or utility bills. Assistance is not guaranteed and rent/mortgage and utility intake use different routes.
resources.address: 635 E Broadway Rd, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: Office Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM. Rent/mortgage appointment line opens first Thursday of the month, 2:00-3:00 PM or until appointments are filled. Utility orientations are Monday-Wednesday mornings beginning at 8:00 AM; age 60+ applicants do not need orientation.
resources.informationText:
