**Services Offered**
MesaCAN provides emergency rent, mortgage, and utility assistance to low-income City of Mesa residents with past-due bills. Utility funds listed by MesaCAN include City of Mesa, SRP, and Southwest Gas assistance. MesaCAN also points LIHEAP applicants to the DES LIHEAP process.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For low-income City of Mesa residents who meet the programme’s criteria. A completed utility application and supporting documents are required. Utility applicants normally attend orientation; applicants age 60 or older are exempt from orientation, not the application/document requirements. Assistance depends on funding and is not guaranteed.

**Population Served**
Low-income City of Mesa households facing eviction, mortgage delinquency, or utility shutoff or delinquency. Spanish application materials are available for utility assistance.

**How to Best Connect**
For rent/mortgage appointments call 480-750-9228 on the first Thursday of the month, 2–3 PM or until slots fill, and reach a live person. For utilities call 480-833-9200 or email mesacanclient@turnanewleaf.org. Utility orientations begin 8 AM Monday–Wednesday; ask how to submit documents if age 60 or older. Office: 635 E. Broadway Rd, Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
MesaCAN rent/mortgage and utility assistance have separate intake processes. Funding can be exhausted for the month, and application does not guarantee payment. Staff members should not be contacted directly for rental assistance; use the published appointment line.

resources.name: Agave Center for Behavioral Health
resources.description: Individual, couple and family counseling.
resources.address: 1930 S Alma School Rd, Suite C 105, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Individual, couple and family counseling.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Clinical fit, age and payer are assessed at intake; the provider profile includes children 6+ and adults.

**Population Served**
Mesa-area children, adults, couples and families.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-826-3537 to ask about a consultation, fees and appointment options.

**Important Information to Know**
The provider profile lists individual and couple sessions at$120 and Medicare participation; confirm the specific clinician and coverage. This is scheduled care.

resources.name: Chicanos Por La Causa - Workforce Solutions Youth Programs
resources.description: Phoenix youth workforce programs offer education and career preparation, paid work experiences and job support; a separate YouthBuild Phoenix pathway provides construction training.
resources.address: WIOA Youth Program: 619 N. 7th Ave., Building B, Phoenix, AZ 85007; YouthBuild Phoenix: 2830 W. Glendale Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85051
resources.hours: Program schedules and cohorts vary; call, text, email or use the online application/request forms before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free WIOA Youth support for eligible participants includes high-school/GED completion, assessment, short-term training, paid internships, mentoring, financial literacy, job development/retention and approved supplies or transport help such as books, bus passes and gas cards. YouthBuild Phoenix is a separate construction-training pathway.

**Eligibility Requirements**
WIOA Youth serves eligible young people ages 16–24; documentation, barriers and other program criteria apply. YouthBuild Phoenix lists ages 18–24, with another description mentioning 17–24: a 17-year-old should confirm eligibility directly.

**Population Served**
Eligible teens and young adults seeking Phoenix-area education and employment support. Ask which program can serve the client’s address.

**How to Best Connect**
For WIOA Youth, call or text 602-206-5718 or email Youth@cplc.org. For YouthBuild Phoenix, contact 602-483-2705 or itzel.barajas@cplc.org. Confirm enrollment and location before visiting.

**Important Information to Know**
Work placements, bus passes, gas cards and other supports depend on enrollment, eligibility, funding and available slots. They are not general public transport assistance. Confirm which Phoenix programme serves the client’s address; programmes listed for other states have different catchments.

resources.name: Planned Parenthood Arizona - Mesa Health Center
resources.description: Planned Parenthood Arizona's Mesa Health Center provides in-person and telehealth reproductive and sexual health care, including birth control, emergency contraception, STI/HIV services, pregnancy testing, gender-affirming care, vaccines, and preventive wellness care.
resources.address: 1235 S. Gilbert Rd., Suite 7, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: Tuesday 7:30 AM–4 PM; Wednesday 8:30 AM–5 PM; Thursday 7:30 AM–4 PM; Friday 7 AM–3:30 PM; weekends closed. Monday availability differs across listed service pages; confirm when booking.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Birth control, emergency contraception, HIV services including PrEP/PEP-related care, pregnancy testing and planning, sexual and reproductive concerns, STI testing and treatment, vaccines, gender-affirming care, wellness visits, Pap/HPV cervical cancer screening, chest/breast cancer screening and referral, anemia, cholesterol, diabetes, high blood pressure, and thyroid screening.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Appointments are the usual route, but walk-ins are welcome to make an appointment or check same-day availability. Insurance is not required. Uninsured clients may qualify for financial assistance and should call to ask what documentation is needed.

**Population Served**
People in Mesa needing reproductive and sexual health care, including women, men, LGBTQ+ clients, Spanish-speaking clients, and deaf or hard-of-hearing clients with advance notice for support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-277-7526 or book online. Walk-in limited services may be available for emergency contraception, pregnancy testing, birth-control pill refills, post-HIV exposure prophylaxis, and immediate treatment needs after sexual assault, subject to availability.

**Important Information to Know**
This Mesa center does not provide abortion services on site. Confirm Monday availability and your specific appointment time when booking. Payment is generally due at the visit unless arranged otherwise; ask about insurance, financial assistance and any required documents. Request Spanish or Deaf/hard-of-hearing support as needed, with advance notice for access arrangements.

resources.name: Catholic Charities MANA House - Transitional Housing for Homeless Veterans
resources.description: Catholic Charities MANA House provides transitional housing and day-center support for veterans experiencing homelessness in Phoenix, serving as a veteran-specific housing stability and support option for Maricopa County referrals.
resources.phone: Housing referral: Phoenix VA CRRC 602-248-6040; MANA questions 602-254-6785
resources.address: 2422 W. Holly St., Phoenix, AZ 85009
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Transitional veteran housing with case management and a permanent-housing plan. Accepted residents can receive career counselling, job-search/resume/interview and placement support; VA, Social Security and DES enrollment help; DD214/benefit guidance; transit passes and VA transport; and computer, kitchen/dining, laundry and shower access.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Veterans experiencing or at risk of homelessness must be referred by the Phoenix VA Community Resource and Referral Center and accepted by MANA House. Ask CRRC about current admission, household, documentation and placement requirements.

**Population Served**
Veterans experiencing homelessness in Arizona, including Mesa and Maricopa County veterans who can access the Phoenix site.

**How to Best Connect**
Start housing referrals with Phoenix VA CRRC, 1500 E. Thomas Road, Phoenix, at 602-248-6040. MANA House only accepts housing referrals through CRRC. For programme questions or separate day-center access, call MANA House at 602-254-6785 before visiting 2422 W. Holly St.

**Important Information to Know**
VA referral does not guarantee acceptance or an immediate bed. This is not walk-in emergency shelter or direct addiction treatment. Catholic Charities’ Northern Arizona SSVF programme has a separate service area and must not be presented as Phoenix MANA intake.

resources.name: Arizona Democracy Resource Center · Free Legal Clinic
resources.description: No-cost Arizona legal clinic for rights restoration, set-asides, record sealing, marijuana expungement, felony 6 reclassification, name changes, and fingerprint-clearance good-cause appeals.
resources.hours: Online scheduling and email intake; public clinic hours not listed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Arizona Democracy Resource Center's Free Legal Clinic provides no-cost support for restoring civil rights, set-asides and second chance certificates, record sealing, marijuana expungement, felony 6 reclassification, legal name changes, and fingerprint-clearance good-cause exceptions.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The clinic says it helps everyone and does not list income or county limits on the public page. Eligibility depends on the legal issue and whether the requested record-relief or name-change remedy is available.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents seeking the clinic’s specific record-relief, rights-restoration, name-change or fingerprint-clearance services; the clinic says it helps regardless of identity.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the clinic’s online meeting link or email legalclinic@azdrc.org. Have case numbers, court and sentencing documents, and any relevant payment/restitution information ready.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a focused clinic, not general legal aid. Screening does not guarantee acceptance, a filed petition or relief. The particular remedy’s eligibility, documentation, court process and fees still apply.

resources.name: Salt River Project (SRP) - Income-Qualified Discount
resources.description: Monthly SRP electric-bill credit for eligible income-qualified residential customers, with $35 and $10 tiers based on household income.
resources.hours: Customer Resource Counselor questions: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; SRP customer service is available 24/7.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The SRP Income-Qualified Discount provides a monthly electric-bill credit. SRP lists a $35 monthly credit for households at 0%-150% of the Federal Poverty Level and a $10 monthly credit for households at 151%-200% of the Federal Poverty Level.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The applicant must be an SRP customer with the account in their name, live at the service address as a permanent residence, and have total monthly household income at or below SRP's current guidelines. Proof of household income is required.

**Population Served**
Income-qualified SRP residential electric customers, including many Mesa households served by SRP.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through SRP My Account, call 602-236-8888, or download and return the application. Ask Customer Resource Counselors about documentation and annual reapplication.

**Important Information to Know**
Reapply annually and confirm current income guidelines. Approved M-Power customers receive the credit on the first of the month; it is a discount, not a loan. A separate M-Power advance has repayment rules.

resources.name: Community Medical Services · Mesa on Main Opioid Treatment Program
resources.description: Community Medical Services opioid treatment access, centered on the Mesa on Main clinic for methadone, Suboxone, counseling and peer support, with Phoenix on 7th Avenue preserved as an alternate Maricopa County clinic.
resources.address: Mesa on Main: 2940 E. Main St, Mesa, AZ 85213. Alternate Phoenix clinic: 3333 N. 7th Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85013.
resources.hours: Mesa on Main: Mon-Fri 4:30 AM-3:30 PM, Sat 6:00 AM-10:00 AM, Sun closed. Phoenix on 7th Avenue lists the same hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Community Medical Services Mesa on Main treats opioid use disorder, including heroin and fentanyl addiction, with medication-assisted treatment such as methadone and Suboxone, counseling, peer support, and psychiatry services when part of the treatment plan. Phoenix on 7th Avenue offers the same supported OTP service type as an alternate CMS clinic.

**Eligibility Requirements**
People seeking opioid-use-disorder treatment may call or visit for same-day treatment. Insurance and clinic fit should be confirmed; the Mesa page specifically states Cigna is accepted there.

**Population Served**
Mesa and Maricopa County people with opioid-use disorder. The resource is not a general detox, alcohol-only program, or residential treatment bed.

**How to Best Connect**
For Mesa on Main, call 480-977-1500 or go to 2940 E Main Street during listed clinic hours. For the Phoenix 7th Avenue alternate clinic, call 602-753-3360. Confirm dosing, intake timing, required ID, pregnancy services, and insurance before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
Same-day or walk-in intake is subject to the clinic’s actual hours and availability; it does not mean 24-hour service. Confirm dosing/intake, coverage and transfer arrangements. This is opioid treatment, not general detox, residential housing or reentry case management.

resources.name: Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community - SRPMIC Transit
resources.description: SRPMIC Transit provides free, grant-funded, ADA-accessible transportation for the Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community and nearby Scottsdale, Mesa, and Tempe areas, with connections to Valley Metro and light rail.
resources.address: 10005 E. Osborn Rd., Scottsdale, AZ 85256
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 5:00 AM-5:00 PM; last reservation 4:30 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free ADA-accessible transit for the Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community and nearby Scottsdale, Mesa, and Tempe, including connections to Valley Metro bus and light rail locations. Regular work-commute/subscription trips may be scheduled daily when available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The service is open to Community members and the general public. Riders must follow passenger requirements and reservation rules. Service-area exceptions may apply.

**Population Served**
SRPMIC Community members, nearby residents, and members of the general public traveling in the SRPMIC and nearby Scottsdale, Mesa, and Tempe service area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-362-7310 during operating hours, Monday through Friday 5:00 AM-5:00 PM. Provide name, phone number, pickup location, destination, and requested time. Reservations should be made with 24-hour notice; same-day rides are not guaranteed.

**Important Information to Know**
Last reservation is 4:30 PM. Riders should be ready 10 minutes early; drivers wait 3 minutes, or 5 minutes for ADA passengers. Verify pickup/drop-off boundaries with dispatch because the page notes service-area exceptions.

resources.name: Growing Abilities LLC — Developmental-Home Agency
resources.description: A Mesa agency listed by DES DDD for developmental-home services and placement inquiries.
resources.address: 6549 E. University Dr., Mesa, AZ
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

A Mesa agency listed by DES DDD for developmental-home services and placement inquiries.

**Eligibility Requirements**

The current DDD list identifies DDD East district. Ask the agency and DDD support coordinator about authorization, age, support needs and suitable openings.

**Population Served**

People eligible for DDD developmental-home supports and their families or support teams.

**How to Best Connect**

Call 480-374-9300 and ask about current referral procedures, the type of home needed and capacity. Coordinate any placement request with the person’s DDD support coordinator.

**Important Information to Know**

A listed agency is not a guaranteed available home. This entry is distinct from the other agency at the same street address; confirm the program and appointment location before visiting.

resources.name: AHF Imaging Center - Low Cost Imaging Clinic
resources.description: AHF Imaging Center is a low-cost Phoenix imaging clinic offering ultrasounds and EKGs with a doctor's referral and no insurance requirement.
resources.address: 1313 E. Osborn Rd., Suite 235, Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.hours: Public home page does not list hours; schedule before going.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Low-cost diagnostic imaging, including ultrasounds and EKGs with a doctor's referral. The site advertises procedure price points and appointment scheduling.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A doctor's referral is required. Insurance is not needed, and the clinic accepts cash, debit or credit payments.

**Population Served**
Phoenix and Maricopa County patients, including uninsured Mesa residents who can travel and need lower-cost ultrasound or EKG services ordered by a clinician.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-200-0437 or use the Schedule Scan link. Address: 1313 E. Osborn Rd., Suite 235, Phoenix, AZ 85014.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a full radiology center for every modality. Confirm the requested scan, referral requirements, price and appointment availability before sending a client.

resources.name: Sonoran Prevention Works - naloxone and harm-reduction supplies
resources.description: Arizona harm-reduction organization providing naloxone and supply access, overdose-prevention education, in-person outreach schedules, HIV/HCV testing at outreach events, and naloxone-by-mail for eligible Arizona participants.
resources.hours: Outreach schedules vary by county; SPW recommends texting ahead before traveling far.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Sonoran Prevention Works helps people who use drugs access naloxone, harm-reduction supplies, overdose-prevention information, in-person outreach, HIV and hepatitis C testing at outreach events, and naloxone-by-mail in Arizona.

**Eligibility Requirements**
SPW's naloxone-by-mail program requires an account application and approval. In-person supply access depends on the county schedule and current supply availability.

**Population Served**
People who use drugs and people seeking overdose-prevention supplies or education across Arizona, including Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call or text 480-442-7086, email info@spwaz.org, use the Get Supplies page to check current Maricopa County options, or use the Naloxone By Mail portal. SPW states its Tempe mailing address is not a service site.

**Important Information to Know**
Do not send clients to the mailing address for services. Check the live county schedule or contact SPW before travel, especially if coming from Mesa.

resources.name: Aster Aging - Safe at Home Community of Care
resources.description: Aster Aging, Rebuilding Together Valley of the Sun and A.T. Still University offer free East Valley fall-prevention, chronic-disease education, home-safety assessment, home-safety modification, nutrition connection and resource-navigation supports.
resources.address: 45 W. University Dr., Suite A, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Call Aster for current intake, class and home-assessment availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Safe at Home Community of Care offers free programs for East Valley older adults, including Matter of Balance, Your Heart at Home, chronic-disease self-management, a 25-point safe and healthy home assessment, home-safety modifications, resource navigation and nutrition assistance connections.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page describes the program for East Valley older adults. It does not publish income rules, modification limits, exact ZIP-code boundaries, current funding capacity or wait times.

**Population Served**
Older adults in East Valley communities who need fall-prevention support, health education, home-safety improvements, nutrition assistance connections or resource navigation to remain independent.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Aster at 480-634-1659 and ask about Safe at Home Community of Care. Confirm whether the household's Mesa address and requested service are currently eligible.

**Important Information to Know**
The page states the program is free, but home modifications and assessments may be limited by funding, partner availability, geography and household eligibility. Aster should confirm which component applies.

resources.name: Arizona Women's Recovery Center - Women's Outpatient Treatment and Supportive Housing
resources.description: Arizona Women's Recovery Center provides women-centered outpatient substance-use treatment, supportive housing, case management, medical/psychiatric support, parenting, vocational training, family support, and recovery programming.
resources.address: 4201 N 16th St, Suite 140, Phoenix, AZ 85016
resources.hours: Call or use the Get Help/contact route for current intake appointments and program hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Women-centered outpatient substance-use treatment, one-on-one and group therapy, case management, medical and psychiatric support, parenting, vocational training, supportive housing, family programming, and recovery education.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Women seeking recovery from substance use may inquire. Supportive housing is program-specific and tied to treatment; pregnancy, parenting, homelessness, incarceration history, or child-reunification needs may affect the best program fit. If you lack coverage, ask about AHCCCS application help, sliding-fee payment or substance-use grant eligibility.

**Population Served**
Women across Arizona and Maricopa County, including pregnant women, parenting women, women with children, and women seeking recovery-oriented housing or outpatient care.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-264-6214 or use AWRC's Get Help/contact route. Ask whether outpatient treatment, supportive housing, or another AWRC program is the right fit.

**Important Information to Know**
AWRC states it accepts insurance including all AHCCCS and SUBG funding. Housing is treatment-based and should not be presented as a standalone shelter. Openings and transportation from Mesa must be confirmed.

resources.name: Southwest Network - Adult SMI, General Mental Health, ACT, and Youth Transition Services
resources.description: Southwest Network provides Greater Phoenix outpatient mental and behavioral-health services for adults with SMI and general mental-health/substance-use needs, including psychiatric care, therapy, ACT teams, peer/family support, housing, transportation, language services, and sliding-fee options.
resources.address: 2700 N Central Ave, Suite 1050, Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.hours: Hours vary by clinic; call administrative office or the relevant clinic before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Psychiatric evaluations, therapy, substance-use evaluations and services, crisis intervention, suicide prevention and management of suicidal ideation, medication, nursing, case management, rehabilitation and support, personal care, life skills, employment supports, peer and family support, housing support, transportation assistance, language services, ACT teams, and onsite pharmacy access at adult clinics.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Southwest Network serves adults with serious mental illness and adults needing general mental-health/substance-use support. It accepts AHCCCS/Medicaid, AHCCCS Complete Care plans, Medicare, private insurance and cash pay; a sliding or discounted fee schedule is available based on family size and income.

**Population Served**
Adults in Greater Phoenix and Maricopa County, including Mesa residents who can access a Southwest Network clinic or referral pathway.

**How to Best Connect**
For general information call 602-304-0014 or the administrative office at 602-266-8402, or email info@southwestnetwork.org. Ask which clinic and program fits the person's location, diagnosis, payer and service needs.

**Important Information to Know**
No Mesa office was confirmed. Use this as a Greater Phoenix referral option, especially for SMI, GMHSU, ACT, and integrated outpatient needs when the person can use the assigned clinic.

resources.name: SBA Arizona District Office - Veterans Business Development Officer
resources.description: The SBA Arizona District Office Veterans Business Development Officer connects veteran, service member, and military-spouse entrepreneurs to federal, state, and local small-business programs and Boots to Business or Boots to Business Reboot contacts.
resources.address: 4041 North Central Ave., Suite 1000, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Business-development guidance and resource connection for veteran, service member, and military-spouse entrepreneurs. Veterans Business Development Officers are familiar with federal, state, and local programs and can provide schedules and points of contact for Boots to Business and Boots to Business Reboot courses.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For veterans, service members, and military spouses seeking to start, grow, or connect a small business to SBA and partner resources. This is business-focused only.

**Population Served**
Arizona veteran, service member, and military-spouse entrepreneurs, including Mesa and Maricopa County clients.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact Craig Jordan at the Arizona District Office: 602-745-7221 or craig.jordan@sba.gov. Address: 4041 North Central Ave., Suite 1000, Phoenix, AZ 85012.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not emergency financial assistance, VA benefits help, housing support, or legal aid. It is appropriate when the client's need is entrepreneurship, federal/state/local business resources, or Boots to Business information.

resources.name: Mesa Public Schools — Native American Education Program
resources.description: Culturally responsive academic support, family engagement and connections for Native American students in Mesa Public Schools.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Culturally responsive academic support, family engagement and connections for Native American students in Mesa Public Schools.

**Eligibility Requirements**

MPS enrollment and Native American Education Program enrollment forms and qualifying tribal documentation are required; the program can explain acceptable student, parent or grandparent documentation.

**Population Served**

Eligible Native American students and their families in Mesa Public Schools.

**How to Best Connect**

Contact the NAEP office about forms, academic support and current services; documents can be submitted to the office or its email address.

**Important Information to Know**

Activities and material distributions vary. The posted August 2026 supply event has passed and does not establish a current walk-in supply distribution.

resources.name: Maricopa County Human Services Department - Emergency Home Repair Program
resources.description: Maricopa County Emergency Home Repair helps eligible low- to moderate-income homeowners in the county service area address urgent health and safety repairs, especially non-functioning air conditioning and heating systems.
resources.hours: Apply online or call for current application assistance; funding is limited and applications are prioritized.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency Home Repair may assist with urgent health and safety repairs, primarily non-functioning air conditioning and heating systems. Eligible repairs may include air conditioning and heating repair or replacement, water heater replacement, minor electrical or plumbing repairs, minor accessibility modifications, and refrigerator or stove replacement.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Own and occupy the home as the primary residence for at least one year, live within the eligible county service area, have income at or below 80% of area median income and no more than $12,000 in liquid assets, and meet lawful-presence and repair-need requirements. Property taxes, mortgage and HOA dues must be current when applicable. Recent-assistance restrictions and a $25,000 lifetime assistance limit apply; provide the crisis statement and requested documents.

**Population Served**
Low- to moderate-income Maricopa County homeowners in the county program service area. Priority factors include seasonally critical HVAC failures, a household member age 62 or older, a verifiable disability, or a child under age 6.

**How to Best Connect**
First confirm the actual address is in the eligible county service area by calling 602-506-0589 or using the county programme page. Then gather the requested identity, household, income, bank, ownership, mortgage, utility and crisis-statement documents.

**Important Information to Know**
Many incorporated cities, including Mesa, are excluded; qualifying county-island addresses within them may be eligible. Funding and priorities determine access. This is not a separately established veteran entitlement, and the $25,000 limit is lifetime assistance, not an annual grant.

resources.name: Arizona Center for Youth Resources (ACYR) · Adult Education Program Options
resources.description: Arizona Center for Youth Resources offers adult education for GED/HSE preparation, ESOL, job readiness, and IT certification preparation, with morning, afternoon, evening, hybrid, and in-person options at Phoenix and Valley sites.
resources.address: 649 N. 6th Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85003; Valley class sites may include Tempe or other locations
resources.hours: Classes are available mornings, afternoons, and evenings; hybrid and in-person options vary by program and site.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
ACYR Adult Education offers HSE/GED preparation, adult basic education, ESOL, job-readiness skills, career exploration, and certification preparation such as CompTIA IT Fundamentals. Classes are offered mornings, afternoons, and evenings, with hybrid and in-person options depending on site and program.

**Eligibility Requirements**
ACYR pages describe HSE and ESOL pathways for learners age 16 and older. Depending on the pathway, students may need proof of identity or age, proof of Arizona residency, and previous school records. Staff should clarify the age rule, documentation, and free/low-cost status during intake.

**Population Served**
Phoenix-area and Maricopa County learners, including young adults and adults who need GED/HSE, English learning, foundational academic skills, job readiness, or entry-level IT preparation. Mesa residents may need to use Tempe, Phoenix, hybrid, or other Valley sites.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the online enrollment form on the ACYR adult education page, call 602-252-6721, or email ask@acyraz.org. Ask staff to match the client with the closest active site, schedule, program, and hybrid or in-person option.

**Important Information to Know**
ACYR is Phoenix-centered; there is no Mesa site listed on the official page. Confirm Tempe or hybrid access for a Mesa client before referral.

resources.name: AHCCCS - Health Insurance for Pregnant Women
resources.description: AHCCCS provides Medicaid health insurance for pregnant Arizona residents who meet income and eligibility requirements, with no monthly premium for approved Pregnant Women program members.
resources.address: AHCCCS, 150 N. 18th Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85007; apply online through Health-e-Arizona Plus
resources.hours: Health-e-Arizona Plus applications are online. AHCCCS lists main phone support at 602-417-4000 or 1-800-654-8713.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
AHCCCS health insurance for pregnant women provides medical coverage for eligible pregnant Arizona residents through Arizona Medicaid. Applications are completed through Health-e-Arizona Plus.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must generally be Arizona residents, pregnant, meet citizenship or qualified immigrant rules unless emergency-services-only coverage applies, have or apply for a Social Security number, cooperate with child support if needed, and have income under the current AHCCCS limit.

**Population Served**
Pregnant and postpartum Arizona residents, including eligible Mesa and Maricopa County residents who need Medicaid pregnancy coverage.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through Health-e-Arizona Plus from the AHCCCS pregnant women page. Call AHCCCS at 602-417-4000 or 1-800-654-8713 for questions about application routes.

**Important Information to Know**
Eligibility and income limits change and are determined by the application. The official page lists gross monthly income limits effective 02/01/2026 and states there are no monthly premiums for those who qualify.

resources.name: Immigrant Hope - Mesa low-cost immigration legal aid clinic
resources.description: Immigrant Hope - Mesa is a Mesa-based low-cost immigration legal-aid clinic serving low-income immigrants in the Phoenix metro area, with services including green card renewals or replacements, naturalization, family petitions, VAWA, U visas and DACA renewals.
resources.address: 1818 E Southern Ave, Suite 4A, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday, 10:00 AM-5:00 PM; Friday-Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Immigrant Hope - Mesa provides low-cost immigration legal advice and representation. Its listed services include citizenship through naturalization, family-based visa petitions, green card renewals or replacements, VAWA, U visas and DACA renewals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The clinic serves the low-income immigrant community in the Phoenix metro area. Its website states it cannot help at this time with asylum or court cases. Eligibility and fees depend on the immigration matter and consultation.

**Population Served**
Low-income immigrants in Mesa and the Phoenix metro area who need immigration legal help, including replacement or renewal of eligible immigration documents such as green cards.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-524-8131 or email mesa@immigranthope.org. The office is at 1818 E Southern Ave, Suite 4A, Mesa, AZ 85204, Building 2 on the east side of Redemption Mesa Church. Published hours are Monday through Thursday, 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
The initial consultation costs $30; later service charges and USCIS filing fees may apply. Ask about fee-waiver options and documents before the appointment. The clinic does not handle asylum or immigration-court cases and is not a state-ID, Social Security card or birth-certificate issuer.

resources.name: Tempe Community Council - Threadz Teen Clothes Closets
resources.description: Threadz provides free teen clothes closets with new and gently used clothing, shoes, personal hygiene items and school supplies for eligible Tempe-area middle and high school students with school ID.
resources.address: Tempe Community Council: 117 E 5th St, Suite 200, Tempe, AZ 85281; closets at Marcos de Niza, Tempe and Mountain Pointe High Schools
resources.hours: Threadz sites are open Tuesdays and Thursdays during the regular school session; check the official Locations/Times page for site-specific hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free new and gently used clothing, shoes, personal hygiene items, school supplies and other school-readiness items for teens.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Tempe middle and high school teens who are Tempe residents, attend a school in Tempe, or are enrolled in Tempe Union High School District, Tempe Elementary or Kyrene public school districts. A valid school ID is required.

**Population Served**
Eligible teens in the Tempe/Kyrene/Tempe Union school community, including Mountain Pointe High School students; this is not a Mesa Public Schools closet unless the student meets Threadz eligibility.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact Tempe Community Council at 480-858-2300 or tccinformation@tempe.gov. Students should use an open Threadz site with a valid school ID and check site-specific locations and times first.

**Important Information to Know**
Threadz is school/district-specific. It is useful for East Valley teens who meet the district rules, but should not be presented as a general Mesa youth clothing closet.

resources.name: Maricopa County Hand-in-Hand collaborative for justice-involved homeless households - current reentry scope unresolved
resources.description: Hand-in-Hand was submitted as a Maricopa County collaborative for justice-involved homeless households. Current county evidence confirms a Maricopa County Hand in Hand homelessness/housing program exists, but the current justice-involved collaborative identity, lead agency, intake route and Mesa eligibility could not be confirmed from current public pages.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Historical NACo evidence described a collaborative connecting justice-involved homeless individuals and families to housing, supportive services, physical and mental-health services, jail-to-community navigation and case management after housing placement. Current county news confirms a Hand in Hand homelessness/housing program connected to Family Bridge Homes and temporary housing/navigation services, but does not confirm the justice-involved reentry collaborative details.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Unresolved. The historical description focused on justice-involved homeless households in Maricopa County. Current county news focuses on families experiencing homelessness and a housing project in Avondale. Administrators should confirm whether a justice-involved household pathway still exists and how Mesa clients are referred.

**Population Served**
Potentially justice-involved homeless individuals and families in Maricopa County, but current public evidence only clearly supports homeless families served by Maricopa County Hand in Hand partnerships.

**How to Best Connect**
Do not send a client without administrator confirmation. Start with Maricopa County Human Services / Hand in Hand information and ask whether the justice-involved homeless-household collaborative is active, which agency leads intake and whether Mesa-area returning citizens can be referred.

**Important Information to Know**
This is retained as a useful unresolved lead, not as a ready referral. The main obstacle is not an unavailable webpage; it is an unresolved current service scope and intake route for the justice-involved reentry version of Hand-in-Hand.
resources.resolutionReason: Current county news supports an active Hand in Hand homelessness program, while the older NACo profile supports the justice-involved collaborative. Public current sources did not establish the current reentry-specific scope or intake route, preventing a responsible referral.

resources.name: Take Charge America - Nonprofit Credit Counseling and Debt Management
resources.description: Take Charge America provides nonprofit credit counseling, budgeting help, debt-management-plan screening, financial education, housing counseling options, and bankruptcy counseling/education access by phone and online. Initial credit counseling is advertised as free; optional debt management plans can have separate costs.
resources.address: 20430 N 19th Ave, Suite B155, Phoenix, AZ 85027
resources.hours: Debt management hours: Monday-Friday 7:00 AM-5:00 PM MST; housing counseling hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:00 PM MST. Online contact and counseling start routes are available.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free confidential credit counseling, personalized budget review, recommended debt solutions, financial education, and screening for debt-management plans. Take Charge America also lists housing help and bankruptcy counseling/education as service areas.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open to consumers seeking help with credit, debt, budgeting, or related financial counseling. A debt-management plan, if recommended and chosen, has separate creditor terms, enrollment requirements, and fees that should be reviewed before signing.

**Population Served**
Arizona and nationwide consumers, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents who can use phone or online counseling. The contact form includes English and Spanish language preferences.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the first-time client line at 866-750-9618 or start free counseling from the Take Charge America website. Existing clients should use the secure client portal or call 866-528-0588. The Phoenix principal location is 20430 N 19th Ave, Suite B155.

**Important Information to Know**
This is counseling and repayment planning, not a cash grant, loan, debt settlement service, or legal bankruptcy representation. The first counseling session may be free, but optional debt-management plans or specialized counseling can involve costs; ask before enrolling.

resources.name: Ability360 - 360Youth Pre-Employment Transition Services
resources.description: Ability360 360Youth provides pre-employment transition services, career exploration, and job-readiness workshops for students with documented disabilities who are preparing for work and adult life.
resources.address: 5025 E. Washington St., Suite 200, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: Ability360 main office hours are Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM; workshops may be online or in person and enrollment should be arranged with the program.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
360Youth provides Pre-Employment Transition Services, including self-advocacy instruction, workplace readiness training, counseling on post-secondary education and training, job exploration counseling, and work-based learning. The official program page is https://ability360.org/360youth/.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Students must be ages 14-22, have a documented disability, and be enrolled in an educational setting such as public, private or charter school, home school, college, or a GED program.

**Population Served**
Students with disabilities who are preparing for future employment and adult community life.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-935-3469 or email Transition@ability360.org to enroll or partner with Ability360. The main office is 5025 E. Washington St., Suite 200, Phoenix, AZ 85034, and general office hours are Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a transition and job-readiness program, not a guaranteed job placement. Current workshop schedule, school coordination, and transportation should be confirmed with the program before referral.

resources.name: Roya Health — Mesa
resources.description: Integrated counseling, psychiatry, case management and primary-care coordination, including remote care.
resources.address: 1345 E Main St, Mesa, AZ 85203
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Integrated counseling, psychiatry, case management and primary-care coordination, including remote care.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Intake determines service, age and payer fit.

**Population Served**
Children, families and other patients needing coordinated behavioral healthcare.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-300-4741 or email referrals@roya.health to request an appointment.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm the appointment suite and accepted plan; the public contact page identifies 1345 E.Main without promising every service at every site.

resources.name: San Tan Behavioral Health Trauma-Informed Therapy at the Mesa Family Advocacy Center
resources.description: San Tan Behavioral Health provides trauma-informed therapy services for victims and families who are already receiving services through the Mesa Family Advocacy Center.
resources.address: 225 E 1st St, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Contact the Mesa Family Advocacy Center before attempting access; Victim Services lists advocates Monday-Friday 7:30 AM-5:30 PM, but therapy availability and referral steps are not separately published.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
San Tan Behavioral Health provides trauma-informed therapy for eligible victims and families already receiving Mesa Family Advocacy Center services. The center coordinates the appropriate referral; this is a specific embedded counseling pathway.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Access appears limited to victims and families receiving Mesa Family Advocacy Center services. The City page does not publish a separate public San Tan intake process for this embedded therapy service.

**Population Served**
Victims and families served by the Mesa Family Advocacy Center, including people affected by sexual and domestic violence in Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Mesa Family Advocacy Center at 480-644-4075 or its questions line 480-644-4084. Ask about the embedded therapy referral, eligibility, appointment location and availability before visiting 225 E 1st St, Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general public walk-in therapy or psychiatry clinic. Confirm the required advocacy-center involvement, referral steps and clinical capacity. Center advocate hours are not necessarily therapy appointment hours.

resources.name: Rally Point Arizona - Veteran and Military Family Crisis Navigation
resources.description: La Frontera EMPACT Rally Point Arizona provides 24-hour veteran and military-family crisis prevention, intervention, peer support and resource navigation.
resources.address: La Frontera EMPACT main office: 618 S Madison Dr, Tempe, AZ 85281
resources.hours: Rally Point hotline is listed as 24-hour.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Rally Point Arizona Military Navigator Program provides crisis prevention, intervention, peer-based support and resource navigation for military service members, veterans and family members. Navigators help map out needed services, coordinate access and provide follow-up support to promote resilience and reduce future crisis.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is for military service members, veterans and their family members. Call the hotline for immediate routing and current program fit.

**Population Served**
Veterans, service members and military families in Arizona, including Maricopa County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Rally Point Arizona at 1-855-725-5948. For EMPACT crisis hotline support, call 480-784-1500 or 855-785-1500. Do not use email for emergencies.

**Important Information to Know**
Rally Point is a veteran/military-specific navigation and crisis-prevention pathway within La Frontera EMPACT. It is distinct from general outpatient counseling and from the general crisis line, although the same organization also operates broader crisis services.

resources.name: Banner - University Medicine Maternal Fetal Clinic at Banner Desert
resources.description: Banner - University Medicine Maternal Fetal Clinic at Banner Desert provides high-risk pregnancy consultation, ultrasound, fetal diagnostics, maternal-condition management, perinatal mental-health care, and perinatal substance-use services.
resources.address: 1400 S. Dobson Rd., Mesa, AZ 85202
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; Saturday-Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The clinic provides high-risk pregnancy consultation and co-management, ultrasounds, fetal diagnostics, congenital-anomaly coordination, antepartum surveillance, maternal-condition management, perinatal mental health services, and a Perinatal Substance Use Disorder Program.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The clinic focuses on high-risk pregnancies and accepts or co-manages direct referrals from providers. Insurance, records, referral needs, and appointment availability should be confirmed with the clinic.

**Population Served**
Pregnant patients with high-risk pregnancy, fetal concerns, maternal medical problems, perinatal mental-health needs, or perinatal substance/alcohol use concerns in Mesa and the regional Banner system.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-521-5700. Ask whether a provider referral is required and what records, insurance information, or financial counseling are needed. The clinic is at 1400 S. Dobson Rd., Mesa, and lists weekday hours of 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a specialty clinic, not walk-in prenatal care or emergency care. Banner says most major insurance is accepted, but patients should check their own plan and payment obligations. For pregnancy-related emergencies, Banner directs people to call 911 or go to the ER.

resources.name: Lions Optometric Vision Clinic - Free Eye Exams and Low-Cost Glasses
resources.description: Lions Optometric Vision Clinic's website describes a nonprofit vision clinic providing free eye exams, free frames and low-cost lenses for people who cannot afford adequate vision care, but the opened official page did not show a service area, physical address or direct phone number.
resources.hours: Use the website QR/form route; public hours are not listed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free eye examinations, corrective lens prescriptions, eye-health recommendations, free frames, low-cost single-vision and lined bifocal lenses, and acceptance of outside prescriptions less than two years old.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The website states the clinic serves individuals who cannot afford adequate vision care. It does not state income documents, residency rules or Arizona/Mesa service eligibility.

**Population Served**
People who cannot afford adequate vision care; specific geography is not established from the opened official page.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the QR code/form on the Lions Optometric Vision Clinic website and wait for staff to contact the client to make an appointment.

**Important Information to Know**
Administrator resolution is needed before routine referral because the opened official page did not show a physical address, phone number or Arizona/Mesa service area. The service itself appears useful, but local identity and access route are not strong enough for a confident Mesa referral without follow-up.
resources.resolutionReason: Official LOVC page confirms services and affordability mission but does not establish Arizona service area, address or phone. The unresolved geography/access gap prevents a responsible direct referral beyond a website-form lead.

resources.name: New Life Pregnancy Center, Mesa - Pregnancy Tests, Material Assistance, Classes and Counseling
resources.description: New Life Pregnancy Center in Mesa offers pregnancy tests, material assistance, food and clothing, classes, counseling, community-resource referrals, and after-abortion support through an Arizona Baptist Children's Services ministry.
resources.address: 819 S. MacDonald, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Mesa location: Monday 9:00 AM-12:00 PM and Wednesday 9:00 AM-12:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Mesa center lists pregnancy tests, material assistance, food and clothing, classes, counseling, community resources, and after-abortion support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official location page does not state detailed eligibility rules. Clients should call to confirm appointment needs, pregnancy-test process, supply availability, and any documentation.

**Population Served**
Pregnant people and families in Mesa seeking pregnancy testing, practical supplies, classes, counseling, and community-resource referrals.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-726-2307 or visit during listed Mesa hours at 819 S. MacDonald on the campus of Casa de Amor. General contact is info@newlifepregnancy.com. Ask about Spanish assistance when arranging this service.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a ministry of Arizona Baptist Children’s Services, not an established prenatal medical provider. Confirm the pregnancy-test process, current supplies (including diapers or clothing), appointments and documents. Use a licensed health provider for medical care.

resources.name: Maricopa Community Colleges Foundation · Dreamer Promise Pathway Program
resources.description: Dreamer Promise Pathway funds tuition and fees for up to two years plus stipend and wraparound supports for eligible undocumented, DACA, and Dreamer students who are current Phoenix residents enrolled at a Maricopa Community College.
resources.hours: Foundation page invites applications for Spring 2027 scholarships; deadlines vary by scholarship cycle.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Tuition and fee funding for up to two years, an annual stipend for basic needs and academic supports such as books, fees, transportation, food, and childcare, plus academic advisement, college success counseling, career advising, mentorship, and connection to Aliento community resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Students must be current Phoenix residents, Dreamer, DACA, or undocumented students, enrolled at a Maricopa Community College in at least 6 credit hours, enrolled in a CCL, 2-year, or 4-year degree pathway, maintain at least a 2.0 GPA, and have graduated from high school or earned a state-accredited GED.

**Population Served**
Undocumented, DACA, and Dreamer students who are current Phoenix residents and enrolled or enrolling at a Maricopa Community College.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Maricopa Community Colleges Foundation scholarship application link on the Dreamer Promise page or call the Foundation at 480-731-8400. Confirm Phoenix residency and scholarship-cycle deadlines before applying.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a Mesa-resident scholarship unless the student is also a current Phoenix resident. Mesa residents who are not Phoenix residents should be routed to other Maricopa scholarship or financial aid options.

resources.name: Banner Desert Medical Center - Maternity Services
resources.description: Banner Desert Medical Center in Mesa provides hospital maternity care for normal, complicated and high-risk pregnancies, labor and delivery, mother-baby care, lactation support, a Level III Perinatal Center and Level III NICU through Banner Children's at Desert.
resources.address: 1400 S. Dobson Rd., Mesa, AZ 85202
resources.hours: Hospital services are available through scheduled maternity care and hospital admission; call or use Banner provider scheduling for current access details.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Banner Desert Medical Center's maternity services include pregnancy care for normal, complicated and high-risk pregnancies, multiple-birth specialists, labor and delivery, mother and baby care, hospitalization during high-risk pregnancy through a Level III Perinatal Center, Level III neonatal intensive care, lactation consultants and connection to the Banner - University Maternal Fetal Clinic.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Patients need maternity or newborn hospital care. Insurance, physician privileges, pre-registration, financial assistance, class registration and any referral requirements should be confirmed with Banner or the patient's obstetric provider.

**Population Served**
Pregnant patients, postpartum patients, newborns, premature or sick babies, and families using Banner Desert Medical Center in Mesa or the regional East Valley hospital system.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Banner Desert maternity page to identify maternity services and provider links, ask the patient's OB/GYN about delivery at Banner Desert, or call Banner Desert Medical Center at 480-412-3000 for routing. For emergencies, call 911 or go to the ER.

**Important Information to Know**
This is hospital-based care, not a free prenatal clinic. Costs, insurance coverage, financial assistance, childbirth classes and access to specialty services should be confirmed before referral when possible.

resources.name: Worker Power — reported citizenship and DACA assistance
resources.description: Could add community application or citizenship support if a current service and enrollment route are confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Could add community application or citizenship support if a current service and enrollment route are confirmed.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Historical referral material identifies assistance; current application-clinic availability is unresolved.

**Population Served**
Immigrant community members seeking application help.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the organization’s official contact route to ask whether the reported service is currently offered.

**Important Information to Know**
Current organizing activity alone does not establish an active application clinic. Preserve this lead for administrator follow-up, without asserting closure.
resources.resolutionReason: Current organizing activity alone does not establish an active application clinic. Preserve this lead for administrator follow-up, without asserting closure.

resources.name: Mesa Community College - New Frontiers for Lifelong Learning
resources.description: Mesa Community College New Frontiers for Lifelong Learning is a non-credit, peer-led membership program for active adult community members, offering classes, social events, volunteer opportunities and wellness activities.
resources.address: 7110 E. McKellips Rd., Desert Willow Building, Room 136B, Mesa, AZ 85207
resources.hours: Leave a message by phone or email for current office help. Class and event schedules vary by semester.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
New Frontiers offers peer-led in-person and online classes, social events, volunteer opportunities, physical activities and community-learning activities through Mesa Community College's Red Mountain campus.

**Eligibility Requirements**
New Frontiers describes the program as designed by and for active adult community members and open to people interested in lifelong learning. It is not designed for people who need supervision, personal care or transportation.

**Population Served**
Active adult learners in Mesa, the East Valley and the greater Phoenix area, including winter visitors.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-461-7497 or use the email link on the New Frontiers site. The office is at Mesa Community College Red Mountain Campus, Community Connections, Desert Willow Building, Room 136 B, 7110 E. McKellips Rd., Mesa. Leave a message if staff or volunteers are away.

**Important Information to Know**
For 2026–27, an individual annual membership costs $75, plus semester fees of $20 for fall, $20 for spring and $10 for summer. Couple, social-only and institutional memberships have different prices or access. Some activities cost extra. This non-credit program provides neither personal care nor transportation.

resources.name: Arizona Perinatal Psychiatry Access Line (APAL) - Perinatal Consultation and Resource Assistance
resources.description: Arizona Perinatal Psychiatry Access Line is a free statewide University of Arizona psychiatry access line for clinicians caring for pregnant and postpartum patients, with related free live resource assistance for Arizona parents, children and care teams.
resources.address: Abrams Public Health Center, 3950 S. Country Club Rd. #200, Tucson, AZ 85714
resources.hours: Perinatal psychiatrist phone consultations and resource assistance: Monday-Friday 8:30 AM-4:30 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free statewide perinatal psychiatry consultation for clinicians caring for pregnant and postpartum patients with mental health or substance-use disorders. APAL also offers live resource assistance to help Arizona parents, children and care teams locate therapists, psychiatrists, support groups, insurance-covered options and community resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Clinical psychiatric case consultation is for medical providers/clinicians. Resource assistance can be used by anyone in Arizona calling for themselves, their child or someone they care for.

**Population Served**
Pregnant and postpartum patients indirectly through their clinicians, plus Arizona parents, children, caregivers and care teams seeking perinatal or pediatric mental-health resource navigation.

**How to Best Connect**
Arizona families can call 888-290-1336 weekdays 8:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m. for free help finding perinatal mental-health resources, regardless of insurance. Treating professionals use the separate consultation pathway described on the same program site.

**Important Information to Know**
Resource assistance is not crisis response or a promise of a treatment appointment. The program currently continues to offer help; confirm availability when calling.

resources.name: AllThrive 365 — Northwest Valley Connect
resources.description: AllThrive 365 operates or coordinates free and low-cost transportation through Northwest Valley Connect and Freedom Express for older adults and people with disabilities in specific West Valley and Wickenburg service areas.
resources.hours: Advance reservations: two days for Lyft coordination; seven days for NVC volunteer or accessible-vehicle rides.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Northwest Valley Connect offers volunteer-driver trips, low-cost wheelchair-accessible rides and Lyft coordination in listed West Valley communities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Registration and an eligibility review are required. The listed pathway is for adults age 65 or older in covered communities. Accessible vehicles serve eligible residents with disabilities who cannot use the Lyft option.

**Population Served**
Older adults and eligible people with disabilities in Sun City, Sun City West, El Mirage, Youngtown, and portions of Peoria and Surprise. Mesa-origin service is not established.

**How to Best Connect**
For Northwest Valley Connect, call 623-282-9300 to register or request transportation. AllThrive's general transportation contact is 602-285-1800 and info@allthrive365.org. Ask whether the client's home address is inside the service area before starting a ride request.

**Important Information to Know**
Request Lyft coordination two days ahead and NVC volunteer or accessible-vehicle rides seven days ahead. Confirm the fare or donation and ride availability; some rides have a $2 each-way charge or donation request. Freedom Express in Wickenburg is a separate programme.

resources.name: Fresh Start Women's Foundation - Woman Veterans Support
resources.description: Fresh Start Women's Foundation provides free woman-veteran support through personalized success coaching, workshops, referrals, and services organized around family stability, health and well-being, financial management, education/training, and careers.
resources.address: 1130 E. McDowell Road, Phoenix, AZ 85006
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free wraparound services for women veterans, including one-on-one support, workshops, resource referrals, family-law and wellness options, financial empowerment, education/training opportunities, and career support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page identifies the initiative as veteran support for women who served. Specific program eligibility, documentation, coaching availability, and workshop requirements should be confirmed when connecting.

**Population Served**
Women veterans in Arizona, with a Phoenix-based organization and remote/online connection options through Fresh Start offerings.

**How to Best Connect**
Use “Connect with us to get started” on the Veteran Support page, or call Fresh Start at 602-252-8494 and ask for women-veteran support. The main office is at 1130 E. McDowell Road, Phoenix; confirm programme appointments and remote options before visiting.

**Important Information to Know**
The initiative is funded in part through the Arizona Department of Veterans' Services/Veterans' Donation Fund. It is not an emergency cash-assistance or housing-placement program; it is best framed as coaching, workshops, and supportive navigation.

resources.name: Valley Metro — Bus, rail, trip planning and fare access
resources.description: Valley Metro and the City of Mesa provide local and regional bus and light rail service for Mesa riders, with maps, schedules, trip planning, fare information and customer service for trip-specific planning.
resources.hours: Route and rail hours vary by route, day and service change; check maps and schedules before travel.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Local bus, express/RAPID, light rail and streetcar where available, with trip planning, maps, service alerts and real-time app information. Mesa express/park-and-ride connections can support longer regional commutes. Copper Card and app fare tools support payment and pay-as-you-go Smart Fare caps on eligible trips.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Fixed-route transit is open to the public. Reduced fare, paratransit, RideChoice and special pass programs have separate eligibility rules.

**Population Served**
Mesa residents, workers, students, patients and visitors traveling within Mesa or across the greater Phoenix and Maricopa County transit network.

**How to Best Connect**
Use Valley Metro’s trip planner/maps/app or call 602-253-5000, AZ Relay 711. Check the exact origin, destination, stops, transfers and both outbound and return service. Manage/order/register/reload a physical card or view fare tools at valleymetrofares.org; cash reloads are available at participating locations.

**Important Information to Know**
Tap or scan each trip and consistently use one Copper Card or app account; their fare-cap progress does not combine. Reduced fares require approval. Express routes can have separate fares and limited peak/weekdays or directions. Check walking distance, heat exposure, evening/weekend service and the last return trip; this is fixed-route transit, not door-to-door transport.

resources.name: Mesa Vet Center - Readjustment Counseling and Referral Services
resources.description: Mesa Vet Center is a VA community-based counseling center offering no-cost confidential readjustment counseling, family/couples support, MST counseling, grief/bereavement support, transition help, and referrals for eligible veterans, service members, and families.
resources.address: 1303 South Longmore, Suite 5, Mesa, AZ 85202
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8 AM-4:30 PM; closed Saturday-Sunday; non-traditional hours may change. Vet Center Call Center is 24/7 at 877-927-8387.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost, confidential non-medical counseling for veterans, service members, and families. Services include individual and group counseling, couples/family counseling, PTSD and depression support, military sexual trauma counseling, bereavement counseling, transition help, telehealth, and referrals to VA/community resources for substance use, homelessness, benefits, education, housing, and burial questions.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Vet Center eligibility differs from VA medical eligibility. Qualifying routes may include combat/hazardous service, military sexual trauma, certain National Guard/Reserve or disaster/emergency-response service, prior qualifying Vietnam-era Vet Center use, or covered VA education-benefit use with related readjustment needs. Family participation may qualify when it supports the veteran/service member; bereavement has separate rules. VA enrollment, a service-connected disability and a particular discharge character are not required. Staff assess the specific circumstances and can help when service documents are missing.

**Population Served**
Eligible veterans, service members, National Guard/Reserve members, and family members in Mesa and the East Valley.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-610-6727 for the Mesa Vet Center or 877-927-8387 for the 24/7 Vet Center Call Center. The office is at 1303 S. Longmore, Suite 5, Mesa; call first for appointment scheduling and non-traditional hours.

**Important Information to Know**
Vet Centers provide nonmedical counseling, not emergency care, medical treatment or benefits adjudication. The 24-hour Vet Center Call Center is 877-927-8387. For the Veterans Crisis Line, call 988 and press 1, text 838255 or use its online chat. Call 911 for immediate life-threatening emergencies. Resource and benefit referrals do not provide cash, approve claims or reserve housing; substance-use clinical treatment occurs through separate providers.

resources.name: Banner Health - Pregnancy and Postpartum Adjustment Support Group
resources.description: Banner Health's Pregnancy and Postpartum Adjustment Support Group is a no-cost virtual support group for pregnant and postpartum people experiencing sadness, anxiety, isolation, birth trauma or adjustment concerns, with partners and babies welcome.
resources.address: Virtual group associated with Banner Gateway Medical Center, 1900 N. Higley Rd., Gilbert, AZ 85234
resources.hours: Banner calendar lists Thursday sessions, 12:30 PM-2:00 PM, with no group during the weeks of July 4, Thanksgiving and Christmas. Dates may change.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Pregnancy and Postpartum Adjustment Support Group offers emotional support for pregnancy and postpartum adjustment concerns such as sadness, anxiety, isolation, birth trauma, anger, worsening fears or difficulty connecting with baby. Banner lists the group as virtual through Microsoft Teams, no cost, with partners and babies welcome.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The group is for pregnant and postpartum participants experiencing adjustment or mood concerns. It is support, not emergency psychiatric care, therapy enrollment or a substitute for medical treatment.

**Population Served**
Pregnant and postpartum people and families in the East Valley who can participate virtually, including Mesa residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Use Banner's class/event page to review upcoming dates and registration details. Banner lists Michele Stanley RN as contact at 480-543-3050. Registrants receive a Microsoft Teams link from a Banner email shortly before the session.

**Important Information to Know**
Current official Banner calendar evidence supports the Banner Gateway virtual group. A prior community listing described a Banner Desert in-person group; confirm directly with Banner before relying on any Desert campus schedule.

resources.name: Arizona Voice for Crime Victims · Pro bono crime-victim legal representation and social services
resources.description: Pro bono victims' rights representation, social services, training, and education for crime victims in Arizona trial, appellate, post-conviction, and clemency proceedings.
resources.address: Mail only: P.O. Box 12722, Scottsdale, AZ 85267
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Arizona Voice for Crime Victims provides pro bono legal representation, social services, training, education, and technical assistance to help crime victims understand, assert, and enforce their rights throughout the criminal justice process.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are for crime victims with victim-rights issues. The public page does not provide a full intake test; contact the organization to confirm whether the specific victimization, court stage, and conflict situation can be served.

**Population Served**
Crime victims in Arizona courts, including city, justice, superior, appellate, clemency, federal district, federal appellate, and other proceedings when accepted.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-600-2661 or use the website contact page. Mailing address is P.O. Box 12722, Scottsdale, AZ 85267.

**Important Information to Know**
This is victims' rights representation and support, not general civil legal aid, prosecution, or criminal defense. Capacity and case fit must be confirmed directly.

resources.name: Home of Record Project - Operation Vanguard
resources.description: Home of Record Project Operation Vanguard offers rapid transitional housing, wraparound support, housing-resource navigation, and application help for veterans facing eviction, homelessness risk, or urgent housing instability.
resources.address: 745 West Dana Avenue, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Hours not published; request help online or call/email for next steps.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Rapid transitional housing, wraparound support, outreach and application help, and housing-resource navigation for veterans in urgent housing crisis.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Designed for veterans facing imminent eviction, housing instability, homelessness risk, need for transitional housing support, or help navigating social/support systems. Each application is reviewed individually and help depends on circumstances and available resources.

**Population Served**
Veterans in Mesa and surrounding Arizona communities who are at risk of homelessness or need immediate housing support.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the Request Assistance form on the website. Call 480-461-1033 or email info@homeofrecordproject.org. Address: 745 W. Dana Ave., Mesa, AZ 85210.

**Important Information to Know**
Applications are assessed individually. Funding, transitional housing and other help depend on available resources and the person’s circumstances. Ask about current intake and response time; this is a separate programme from the six-month Veterans Pathway.

resources.name: Arizona Opioid Assistance and Referral Line
resources.description: Telephone information and referral help concerning opioid use, medication questions, chronic pain and withdrawal concerns.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Telephone information and referral help concerning opioid use, medication questions, chronic pain and withdrawal concerns.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Patients, family members and caregivers may call for assistance. Referred services set their own eligibility and costs.

**Population Served**

Arizona residents affected by opioid use, including people seeking treatment and people helping someone else.

**How to Best Connect**

Call the OAR Line and describe the question or treatment need. Ask about appropriate local services and any follow-up support.

**Important Information to Know**

This line provides information and connections; it does not replace an emergency response or guarantee admission to treatment. Call911 for a suspected overdose or other immediate medical emergency.

resources.name: Catholic Charities — counseling services
resources.description: Individual, couple and family counseling, including telehealth.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Individual, couple and family counseling, including telehealth.
