Individual counseling begins at age 9. Confirm clinician, payer and fee arrangements.

**Population Served**
Arizona individuals, couples and families.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-749-4405 to schedule; ask about sliding fees and evening appointments.

**Important Information to Know**
The program lists Mercy Care, Molina and Banner University AHCCCS participation. It is counseling, not psychiatric medication management or crisis response.

resources.name: Oasis Psychological Services · Sexual Behavior Treatment Program
resources.description: Oasis Psychological Services offers a Mesa-based Sexual Behavior Treatment Program for adolescents ages 12-17 with sexual-behavior offenses or concerns, including therapy, risk assessment, family work and probation coordination when applicable.
resources.address: 1930 S Alma School Rd., Suite A216, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Specialized outpatient treatment for adolescents with sexual-behavior offenses or concerns. Reported services include individual, group and family therapy, risk assessment, individualized treatment planning and coordination with probation when applicable.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The submitted program is for adolescents ages 12-17. Acceptance of youth returning from detention or placement, payer requirements and any court/probation referral requirements should be confirmed with Oasis.

**Population Served**
Male and female adolescents ages 12-17 in the Mesa area, including youth with sexual-behavior concerns or offenses and their families.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-282-4237 or use the program website. The listed office is 1930 S Alma School Rd., Suite A216, Mesa, AZ 85210. Hours and appointment availability are not established in this record.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a youth-only treatment resource, not broad reentry case management. Confirm current clinical eligibility, insurance/self-pay expectations, court or probation coordination options and whether the program is appropriate for the youth's specific offense history before referring.

resources.name: Matthew's Crossing Food Bank - Meals to Grow Weekend Backpacks and School Food Closets
resources.description: Matthew's Crossing Meals to Grow provides weekly weekend backpack food bags and school food closets for students and families at participating East Valley school campuses.
resources.address: Distribution through participating schools; call the school or food bank for programme access.
resources.hours: Distribution schedules are set by participating schools. General food-bank contact hours: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 8–11 AM; Wednesday 4–6 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Meals to Grow weekend backpacks provide two days of meals and snacks for students. Meals to Grow food closets are stocked on local school campuses for students and families during the school week.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Access is through participating schools rather than direct household signup on the public page. Schools that want the program are told to contact Matthew's Crossing.

**Population Served**
Students and families at participating East Valley schools from kindergarten through college.

**How to Best Connect**
Families should ask their school office, counselor or student-support staff whether Meals to Grow backpacks or food closets are available. Schools can contact DENNINE@MATTHEWSCROSSING.ORG. For general questions, call Matthew's Crossing at 480-857-2296.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm the school’s current participation and student intake with school staff. The Chandler emergency-food service has a separate intake; visiting that site does not automatically enroll a student in Meals to Grow.

resources.name: Arizona’s Counseling & Psychological Services — formerly PEP
resources.description: Outpatient counseling and psychological services, available in office, at home or remotely.
resources.address: 1255 W Baseline Rd, Suites C-175/C-184, Mesa, AZ 85202
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Outpatient counseling and psychological services, available in office, at home or remotely.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Intake verifies age, clinical fit and insurance before the first appointment.

**Population Served**
Arizona individuals and families seeking counseling.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-999-3323; intake is Monday–Friday 9 a.m.–2 p.m.

**Important Information to Know**
The current provider is ACPS, formerly People Empowering People. Confirm coverage and service arrangements rather than using the older PEP phone.

resources.name: TLC Treatment Center / Transitional Living Communities - reentry identification-paper assistance
resources.description: Transitional Living Communities/TLC Treatment Center's reentry program says new re-entrants acquire essential identification papers such as Social Security card and photo ID during the program.
resources.address: 32 S Macdonald St, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Prior directory listing reported daily 7:00 AM-5:00 PM; confirm current hours, intake and location before travel.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Within the TLC reentry/transitional living program, new re-entrants participate in programming, complete a resume, apply for medical assistance, make treatment intake appointments and acquire essential identification papers such as a Social Security card and photo ID.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For TLC re-entrants or accepted program participants. Public pages do not describe this as open walk-in document help, and the FAQ refers to rules for re-entrants in the program.

**Population Served**
People entering Transitional Living Communities/TLC programming in Mesa, especially reentry and transitional-living participants.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-969-1471 or email intake@tlctreatmentcenter.org to confirm current intake, location, eligibility, costs and whether birth certificates or fees are assisted.

**Important Information to Know**
Document help is embedded in the program and may not be available to the general public. The official FAQ supports Social Security card and photo ID help but does not mention birth certificates, fee payment or public walk-in access.

resources.name: The Veterans Consortium - Discharge Upgrade Program
resources.description: The Veterans Consortium Discharge Upgrade Program is a national pro bono legal program that screens certain other-than-honorable or undesirable discharge cases and may match eligible veterans or service members with volunteer attorneys for discharge-upgrade representation.
resources.address: Mail: The Veterans Consortium Discharge Upgrade Program, 2101 L St. NW, Suite 225, Washington, DC 20037
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

The Discharge Upgrade Program screens discharge-upgrade matters and may provide free volunteer-attorney representation for unjust discharge ratings. It focuses on cases involving other-than-honorable or undesirable discharges connected to PTSD, TBI, military sexual trauma, Don't Ask Don't Tell, or related qualifying factors.

**Eligibility Requirements**

The program screens for discharge type, qualifying circumstances, medical diagnosis or symptoms where required, and at least one potentially meritorious argument. Not every applicant is accepted, and applicants must complete intake and cooperate with records review.

**Population Served**

Veterans and service members nationwide, including Mesa and Maricopa County clients who can use the remote/national intake process.

**How to Best Connect**

Use the online intake form on the Discharge Upgrade Program page or contact the program at 202-733-3324 or upgrades@vetsprobono.org. Mailing address: The Veterans Consortium Discharge Upgrade Program, 2101 L Street NW, Suite 225, Washington, DC 20037.

**Important Information to Know**

This is legal screening and possible representation, not guaranteed acceptance. Some applicants who do not meet the program criteria may receive referrals or self-help information instead. Discharge upgrades can take significant time after filing.

resources.name: Chicanos Por La Causa - Terri Cruz Family Assistance Program
resources.description: CPLC's Terri Cruz Family Assistance Program offers emergency hardship services and referrals, including APS, SRP, Southwest Gas and TEP utility assistance, funeral assistance, food box referrals, SNAP eligibility help and AHCCCS referrals when funding and eligibility allow.
resources.address: 1008 E. Buckeye Road, Suite 125, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: Utility assistance calls Monday-Wednesday 9:00 AM-12:00 PM and 2:00 PM-4:00 PM. Office hours 9:00 AM-5:00 PM, last client at 4:00 PM. Walk-in assistance Tuesdays; Wednesday and Thursday by appointment; virtual appointments available.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency hardship services and referrals through the Terri Cruz Family Assistance Program. The official page lists APS and SRP utility assistance, funeral assistance, food box referrals, SNAP eligibility assistance, AHCCCS referrals, and utility assistance information including APS, SRP, Southwest Gas and TEP Electric.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are contingent on funding availability, income verification, applicable grant requirements and prescreening. Utility callers should have the utility account number ready and must provide requested documentation if prescreened for an appointment.

**Population Served**
Vulnerable Arizona households needing emergency hardship help, including Mesa and Maricopa County households that can use phone, in-person Phoenix or virtual access.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-805-1666. For utility assistance, call Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday between 9:00 AM-12:00 PM or 2:00 PM-4:00 PM and choose Option #1. Choose Option #2 for general family assistance. The Phoenix office is at 1008 E. Buckeye Rd., Suite 125.

**Important Information to Know**
Rental-assistance funds are currently unavailable. Utility/family assistance depends on funding, prescreening, income verification and grant rules; calls are first come and help is not guaranteed. Appointments may be by telephone, in person or virtually. Confirm the applicable appointment or walk-in day before travel.

resources.name: Arizona Secretary of State - Address Confidentiality Program
resources.description: Arizona Secretary of State Address Confidentiality Program provides a substitute mailing address and an authorization card for eligible domestic violence, sexual offense and stalking survivors who enroll through a registered Application Assistant.
resources.address: Administrative office: 1901 W. Madison St, Phoenix, AZ 85009. Apply through a registered Application Assistant.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A substitute address, forwarding of eligible mail and an Address Confidentiality Authorization Card for approved participants to use under programme rules, including with state/local agencies. Enrollment support comes through registered Application Assistants.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must meet all ACP criteria: victimization by domestic violence, sexual offense or stalking; fear for safety; a recent or planned move to a place unknown to the perpetrator within Arizona; documentation supporting victimization; and adult status or a parent/guardian applying for a minor or incapacitated victim. Applicants do not apply directly with the state office.

**Population Served**
Eligible survivors of domestic violence, sexual offenses or stalking in Arizona, plus eligible co-applicants living with the primary applicant.

**How to Best Connect**
Meet in person with a registered Application Assistant at a victim-service agency or nonprofit. To find an Application Assistant, use the Secretary of State's locator or call ACP at 602-542-1653.

**Important Information to Know**
The authorization card is not general photo ID. Approval is for five years; use of the substitute address starts only after receipt of the welcome packet and card. ACP supports a safety plan but does not supply shelter, legal representation or emergency response.

resources.name: City of Mesa / Trees Matter - Mesa Neighborhood Shade Tree Program
resources.description: Mesa Neighborhood Shade Tree Program offers eligible incorporated Mesa residents up to two free desert-adapted shade trees and tree-care education through the City's Trees Are Cool Initiative and Trees Matter.
resources.hours: Trees Matter contact hours Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The program offers eligible Mesa residents up to two free desert-adapted shade trees plus education on choosing, planting, watering and caring for shade trees to reduce heat and future cooling costs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Participants must live within Mesa incorporated boundaries, not a county island; own the home or have legal right and landlord consent to plant; attend the educational event; pick up trees the day of the workshop; transport, plant and maintain the trees; and call Arizona 811 before digging.

**Population Served**
Residents within incorporated Mesa boundaries who can legally plant and maintain trees on the property, including customers of utilities other than City of Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Register through the City of Mesa program page for the listed workshop. For questions, contact Trees Matter at 480-935-9988 or MesaShadeTrees@Treesmatter.org.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not emergency cooling or utility-bill assistance. Participants must attend and pick up trees at the scheduled event, provide transport, and plant/maintain the trees themselves. The City-listed October 24, 2026 event may fill or change.

resources.name: Axiom Care - Mesa-Area Detox, Residential, Outpatient, and AHCCCS-Accessible Addiction Care
resources.description: Axiom Care's Mesa access page connects Mesa-area residents to nearby detox, inpatient residential rehab, outpatient drug and alcohol treatment, AHCCCS/Medicaid-accessible care, case management, recovery housing, and transportation help when available.
resources.address: Treatment sites near Mesa in metro Phoenix and Apache Junction; no Mesa treatment facility listed on the reviewed page
resources.hours: Call for intake and transportation planning; individual facility hours vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Alcohol and drug detox, inpatient residential rehab, outpatient drug and alcohol treatment, assessments, case management, recovery housing/transitional housing supports, insurance navigation, and community recovery-resource connection for Mesa residents through nearby locations.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adults seeking substance-use treatment may inquire. Axiom states it serves uninsured, underinsured, and AHCCCS/Medicaid clients. Level of care, transportation, and program placement depend on assessment and availability.

**Population Served**
Mesa and Maricopa/Pinal area residents who can access Axiom's Phoenix-area or Apache Junction locations, including people with AHCCCS/Medicaid or limited coverage.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-975-2194 from the Mesa access page or main line 602-626-8112. Ask about intake, AHCCCS, location assignment, and transportation from Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
The Mesa page describes facilities near Mesa, not necessarily inside Mesa. Confirm the assigned site, current bed/program opening, transportation, payer, and detox/residential/outpatient fit before referral.

resources.name: Blue Cross Blue Shield of Arizona Health Choice - Medicaid Transportation Assistance
resources.description: Blue Cross Blue Shield of Arizona Health Choice is an AHCCCS-contracted Medicaid plan; enrolled Health Choice members use Member Services to ask about covered non-emergency medical transportation and ride problems under AHCCCS plan rules.
resources.hours: Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM–5:00 PM, excluding holidays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Health Choice Arizona members can use the plan's Member Services number as the access point for AHCCCS non-emergency medical transportation questions, scheduling confirmation, and ride problem escalation for covered health services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The client must be enrolled in Blue Cross Blue Shield of Arizona Health Choice and need transportation to an AHCCCS-covered service when no other transportation is available. Plan-specific scheduling, broker/vendor, and authorization rules apply.

**Population Served**
Health Choice Arizona AHCCCS Medicaid members, including enrolled Mesa and Maricopa County members.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Member Services at 1-800-322-8670 or use the number on the member ID card. Have the appointment date and time, provider address, pickup location, AHCCCS ID, and mobility or escort needs ready.

**Important Information to Know**
Ask Member Services how to schedule the ride, how much notice is required, and where to call about a late or missed ride. If enrolled in another AHCCCS plan, use that plan’s Member Services number.

resources.name: Rio Salado College · Adult Education: GED/HSE, ESL, Career Training, and Virtual Learning
resources.description: Rio Salado Adult Education offers no-cost GED/HSE preparation, English/ESL classes, career training for enrolled adult education students, college and career navigation, tutors, in-person countywide locations, and live-online learning options.
resources.address: Rio Salado College, 2323 W. 14th St., Tempe, AZ 85281; valleywide locations and live-online classes
resources.hours: Adult education classes are offered year-round with monthly starts, morning and evening options.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
GED/HSE test preparation, English language/ESL classes, adult education student resources, college and career transition support, and career training for enrolled adult education students. Career training areas include applied technology, business, computer and information technology, and health sciences.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Rio states it serves students age 16 or older who are not in high school. Career training requires enrollment in GED test preparation or English language classes and co-enrollment in workforce preparation and industry-specific training.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County adult learners, including Mesa residents who can attend valleywide in-person locations or live-online classes, English-language learners, GED/HSE students, and adult education students preparing for college or career pathways.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Rio Salado Adult Education at 480-517-8110 or Rio main at 480-517-8000, use the adult education registration links, or request information through the Rio page. Ask for the closest current site or live-online option.

**Important Information to Know**
Adult education classes are offered at no cost to students. Class locations rotate and a dedicated Mesa classroom was not confirmed on current official pages. Career training is tied to adult education enrollment, not a standalone public trade school.

resources.name: Recovery Empowerment Network - Peer Recovery Programs and Peer & Family Referral Center
resources.description: Recovery Empowerment Network offers peer-oriented recovery and healing opportunities, empowerment centers, peer support, and self-referral access for behavioral-health recovery support in Maricopa County.
resources.address: 212 E Osborn Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.hours: Call for the selected center’s current hours and programme schedule.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Peer recovery community support, empowerment centers, self-referral access, referral support, HERO Discovery Center/young-adult peer programming, groups, recovery connection, and community support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility, service-plan authorization, payer rules, and which services require behavioral-health system enrollment should be confirmed. The current public page provides a self-referral packet but does not guarantee acceptance.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County residents seeking peer recovery and behavioral-health recovery support, including Mesa residents able to use Phoenix or referral options.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-248-0368 or download the REN self-referral packet from the official website. Ask which center, hours, and referral requirements apply.

**Important Information to Know**
REN provides peer recovery, community connection, navigation and referrals. It is not a detox, residential treatment or medication-prescribing service. Confirm any specific addiction-focused group, costs, service-plan requirements and current schedule before attending.

resources.name: Maricopa County Human Services / Wildfire - URRD and Heat Relief Repair or Replacement Services
resources.description: Maricopa County board-agenda materials surfaced through Poliscopic describe FY2026-27 Wildfire funding for county-administered URRD utility/appliance repair or replacement, utility deposits, HVAC pilot and heat-relief replacement services, but public client intake and Mesa eligibility remain unresolved.
resources.hours: Do not refer until intake routing is confirmed. Maricopa County Human Services general inquiries: 602-506-0589.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The lead describes funding for Utility/Appliance Repair or Replacement and/or Utility Deposits, an HVAC pilot and Heat Relief Repair and Replacement Services administered by Maricopa County under a Wildfire agreement.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public contract mirror says the URRD program serves individuals and families in Arizona in economic crisis and that Maricopa County administers the program outside the City of Phoenix. Current public eligibility, documents, covered utilities and City of Mesa versus county-island routing were not confirmed on an official client-facing page.

**Population Served**
Potentially eligible Maricopa County households in economic crisis needing utility deposits, utility-related repair/replacement, HVAC or heat-relief repair services; exact service area requires resolution.

**How to Best Connect**
Administrators should confirm the current client-facing intake route with Maricopa County Human Services at 602-506-0589 or the appropriate Community Action Program office before referral.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a useful unresolved lead, not a routine referral. The funding evidence was found in public agenda/contract text surfaced outside the county website; a direct official public application route and Mesa eligibility were not confirmed.
resources.resolutionReason: Targeted search found public agenda and contract text for C-22-27-004-X through Poliscopic, plus official county utility-assistance pages, but did not confirm an official county client-facing URRD/heat-relief intake route or Mesa eligibility. Retained as needs-resolution for administrator follow-up.

resources.name: Disabled American Veterans - DAV Transportation Network at Phoenix VA
resources.description: Disabled American Veterans provides free van rides to and from Carl T. Hayden VA Medical Center for veterans who do not have other transportation options and can ride in an ambulatory van.
resources.address: Carl T. Hayden VA Medical Center, 650 E. Indian School Road, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.hours: Individual van schedules vary; call the hospital service coordinator for the county route and advance notice.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
DAV vans provide free transportation for veterans to and from VA health-care centers for scheduled medical appointments, including rides connected with Carl T. Hayden VA Medical Center.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Riders must be veterans traveling to scheduled VA medical appointments and must be ambulatory, meaning able to board and exit the van without driver help. Caregiver riders need authorization from a VA attending physician or VA-certified nurse practitioner.

**Population Served**
Veterans using Phoenix VA health care, including Mesa and Maricopa County veterans who can use ambulatory van transportation to VA appointments.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Phoenix VA Healthcare System hospital service coordinator at 602-277-5551 ext. 7451. Confirm the pickup location, route schedule, advance notice, caregiver authorization and whether another VA transportation option is more appropriate.

**Important Information to Know**
DAV vans are not emergency vehicles and cannot make side trips for personal errands. Veterans who need wheelchair-accessible or special transportation should ask about Veteran Transportation Service or other VA options. Veterans using a free DAV van cannot receive travel reimbursement for that trip.

resources.name: House of Refuge — family transitional housing and resident supports
resources.description: House of Refuge provides transitional housing and wraparound support for eligible families experiencing homelessness, eviction, or domestic-violence flight in Mesa; financial relief is embedded in the housing program rather than open cash assistance.
resources.address: Housing administration: 6935 E. Williams Field Rd., Mesa, AZ 85212; resident Donation Center: 6858 E. Ursula Ave., Mesa, AZ 85212
resources.hours: Housing inquiry form is available when openings exist; call for intake. Donation Center lists Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m., closed weekends; resident shopping is arranged through the programme.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Year-long family transitional housing in furnished homes includes case management, employment/education and life-skills support, computer access and family stabilization. The resident Employment and Education Center helps with résumés, applications, job search, online classes and career/education goals. Enrolled families may receive food and donated clothing, furniture, toys and household essentials. The separate public food bank has its own community access rules.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must live in Arizona and be homeless, have an eviction notice or be fleeing domestic violence; have custody of a resident minor child or third-trimester pregnancy; and have an adult 18+ able to sign a lease. Verifiable income of at least $1,170/month is required through application, move-in and the stay; cash jobs are not accepted. Background/sex-offense exclusions and drug/alcohol-free urine testing apply. If move-in income is not employment, an adult must be able and agree to gain employment within 45 days.

**Population Served**
Arizona families with minor children, or third-trimester pregnancy, experiencing homelessness, eviction risk, or domestic-violence flight who can participate in a structured transitional housing work program.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Housing Inquiry Form when openings are available on the Need Housing page, and check back often because House of Refuge states the form appears when there are openings. For questions, call 480-988-9242 or email info@houseofrefuge.org.

**Important Information to Know**
Not immediate shelter; call 211 for that need. Published rent is $400/month including utilities; new residents also owe a $200 deposit and $400 last-month rent at move-in. Eligibility does not guarantee acceptance. Resident clothing/furniture shopping is not public shopping, and donation drop-off hours do not authorize it. Ask staff to clarify any screening or medication concern before assuming eligibility.

resources.name: Boys & Girls Clubs of the Valley · AZYouthforce Academy and Paid Internships
resources.description: AZYouthforce, a Boys & Girls Clubs of the Valley initiative, provides academy-linked paid internships and career exposure for teens and young adults, with current and recurring opportunities in digital marketing, sports leadership, trades, office, technology, finance, construction, and public service settings.
resources.hours: Internship openings and application windows change frequently.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
AZYouthforce connects young people to academy preparation and paid internships. Current and past postings show career and group internships in digital marketing, sports leadership, automotive, electrical trades, office settings, technology, finance, construction, public service, and other employer-partner fields.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility varies by internship. Postings may include age requirements, completion of AZYouthforce Academy, employer-specific requirements, transportation needs, and application deadlines. Current openings change frequently.

**Population Served**
Valley teens and young adults seeking career exploration, work experience, and paid internships. Mesa resident access and club membership requirements should be confirmed for the specific opportunity.

**How to Best Connect**
Review Current Internships and use the linked application at azyouthforce.org. Use the staff contact listed for the current opportunity; the programme has listed 602-343-1251 for general questions. Confirm age, Academy prerequisites, deadline, transport and any club-participation rule for that placement.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a career academy and paid internship pipeline, not a general job-placement office or school. Confirm the current internship, age range, application deadline, transportation, and whether the client must be a Boys & Girls Club participant.

resources.name: Family Partners — Disability Day, Home and Developmental-Home Services
resources.description: Adult day programming, respite, habilitation, attendant care, developmental homes and employment services through a DDD-contracted provider.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Adult day programming, respite, habilitation, attendant care, developmental homes and employment services through a DDD-contracted provider.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Services depend on disability-program eligibility, DDD authorization, the requested support and current capacity.

**Population Served**

People with developmental disabilities in Maricopa County and other areas served by Family Partners.

**How to Best Connect**

Call the Maricopa County office at 602-997-8300. Ask whether the desired home-based or other program can serve the household’s address; the county day program is in Peoria.

**Important Information to Know**

A county contact does not guarantee Mesa transportation or staffing. Confirm program site, payer authorization, support requirements and availability before referral.

resources.name: Circle the City - Medical Respite, Mobile Medical Care and Street Medicine
resources.description: Circle the City provides healthcare for people experiencing homelessness, including medical respite for adults recovering from acute illness or injury, mobile medical teams, street medicine, outpatient care and behavioral-health-integrated services across Maricopa County.
resources.address: Downtown clinic: 220 S. 12th Ave, Phoenix. Respite sites: 210 S. 12th Ave and 333 W. Indian School Rd, Phoenix, by referral. Mesa mobile stops rotate.
resources.hours: Mobile schedules rotate; confirm the current calendar. Clinic appointments and respite referrals have separate access arrangements.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Healthcare for people experiencing homelessness through clinic visits, mobile outreach and street medicine, including primary/preventive care, medication support, behavioral-health connection and navigation. Medical respite adds a recovery bed, meals, daily medical care, 24-hour nursing, behavioral-health and substance-use support, physical therapy, appointment transport and case management.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Clinic/mobile services depend on homelessness-related needs, the site/team schedule and clinical fit. Residential respite is for adults too ill to recover safely on the street but not needing hospital admission; clinical screening, referral coordination and bed capacity determine access.

**Population Served**
Adults and other individuals experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County, including medically vulnerable people in Mesa/East Valley outreach areas.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-516-6825 for the mobile calendar and appropriate Mesa stop. Listed partner sites include St. Vincent de Paul, 67 W. Broadway; Paz de Cristo, 424 W. Broadway; and La Mesa Ministries, 805 N. Country Club. Downtown clinic inquiries: 602-258-8282. Hospitals, clinics or outreach workers can coordinate respite through Circle the City; general routing is 602-776-0776.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm the exact site and time before travel. Clinic 220 S. 12th and respite 210 S. 12th are different addresses. Respite is medically screened recuperative care, not a general shelter or guaranteed bed. An announced Mesa/East Valley expansion does not establish an open Mesa respite intake.

resources.name: Arizona Bar Foundation Domestic Violence Legal Assistance Project (DVLAP)
resources.description: The Domestic Violence Legal Assistance Project is a statewide Arizona Bar Foundation network of legal-aid attorneys, volunteer attorneys, and lay advocates providing free civil legal help to eligible domestic-violence victims and their children.
resources.hours: Use the online application or call 866-637-5341. Response time and service level depend on screening and provider availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
DVLAP can provide free civil legal assistance for eligible domestic-violence victims and their children, including protective-order representation, divorce-form help, landlord/tenant rights information, legal advice, clinics, self-help assistance, direct representation, volunteer attorney referral, lay legal information, and court accompaniment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For victims of domestic violence and their children who are eligible after screening through Arizona's legal-aid network. Representation is not guaranteed; assistance may range from information and forms help to consultation or direct representation.

**Population Served**
Arizona domestic-violence survivors statewide, including Mesa and Maricopa County survivors with civil legal issues connected to safety and stability.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 866-637-5341 or use the Apply Now link on the Arizona Bar Foundation DVLAP page. People who need accommodations should request them in advance.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a legal-services pathway, not emergency shelter. Applicants should be screened as early as possible because protective-order hearings and housing deadlines can move quickly. Attorneys and lay legal advocates have different roles.

resources.name: RISE Pediatric Therapies - AzEIP Contractor and Early Intervention Services
resources.description: RISE Pediatric Therapies is a Mesa AzEIP provider offering in-home and community early intervention, parent coaching and pediatric therapy services after referral or service assignment.
resources.address: 4554 E. Inverness Ave., Suite C-1, Mesa, AZ 85206
resources.hours: Call for scheduling; AzEIP visit schedules depend on the child's plan and team assignment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
RISE Pediatric Therapies provides AzEIP early intervention for children from birth to age 3 with significant developmental delays, including in-home and community coaching, speech and language therapy, occupational therapy, physical therapy, developmental special instruction and service coordination. It also offers therapy for developmental disabilities through young adulthood.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Families should initiate an AzEIP referral through the official AzEIP website. If the child is eligible for the free AzEIP program, the child is assigned a team lead and early intervention team. RISE is an AzEIP provider, but families are not guaranteed assignment to RISE by request.

**Population Served**
Infants and toddlers with developmental delays or disabilities in Mesa and surrounding areas, plus children and young adults receiving therapy for developmental disabilities through RISE clinics.

**How to Best Connect**
For AzEIP, start with the DES AzEIP referral pathway. For RISE information, call 480-295-4925 or use the Get Started/Contact Us route on the RISE page. The Mesa clinic is at 4554 E. Inverness Ave., Suite C-1.

**Important Information to Know**
RISE states it does not offer diagnoses and that a child does not need a diagnosis to receive therapy. For public early intervention, the official AzEIP central referral controls evaluation and eligibility.

resources.name: Child Crisis Arizona - Halle House Independent Living Program
resources.description: Child Crisis Arizona's Halle House Independent Living Program provides apartment living, meals, and supportive services for foster youth ages 18 to 21 who remain in foster care with an Independent Living case plan, helping them practice independent living, school, work, counseling, and life skills.
resources.address: Mesa and greater Phoenix area
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Apartment living, meals, program staff guidance, supportive services, school and employment expectations, counseling participation, life-skills groups, and a supervised independent-living environment for young adults in foster care.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Youth must be ages 18 to 21, have elected to remain in the foster care system, have a case plan of Independent Living, and be referred through a case manager. The program can house up to 15 youth.

**Population Served**
Young adults ages 18 to 21 in Arizona foster care who are preparing for independent adulthood.

**How to Best Connect**
Youth cannot self-refer. Work through the youth's case manager for referral. General Child Crisis Arizona inquiries: 480-834-9424.

**Important Information to Know**
The public page does not disclose the residence address. Placement depends on foster-care status, case plan, referral approval, and capacity.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Economic Security - Unemployment Insurance Benefits
resources.description: Arizona DES Unemployment Insurance provides wage-replacement benefits for eligible workers who recently lost work through no fault of their own. Applications can be filed online or by mail.
resources.hours: Online application available anytime; call center hours should be confirmed on the DES UI contact page.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Unemployment Insurance may provide temporary wage-replacement benefits to eligible workers who recently lost a job through no fault of their own. Applicants can file an initial claim online and receive follow-up notices from DES.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on work history, wages, reason for separation, identity verification, weekly claim filing, work-search and registration requirements, and any claim-specific issues. Applicants need Social Security number, mailing address, county of residence, ID information, 18-month employment history, last day worked, and other situation-specific documents.

**Population Served**
Eligible workers throughout Arizona, including Mesa and Maricopa County workers with recent job loss or qualifying unemployment.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through DES’s official UI application page or the mail-claim form. Call 877-600-2722 for claim questions. ARIZONA@WORK offices offer no-cost computer access for filing; the workforce office does not decide UI eligibility.

**Important Information to Know**
This is unemployment insurance, not DES Family Assistance cash aid. Identity verification uses ID.me. DES registers applicants with Arizona Job Connection within two days; follow instructions to complete registration, job-search activities, weekly claims and any required virtual RESEA appointment. Application does not guarantee benefits.

resources.name: Area Agency on Aging, Region One - ElderVention Behavioral Health
resources.description: Area Agency on Aging, Region One's ElderVention Behavioral Health program helps older adults manage mental and emotional health through in-home counseling, medication education, community trainings and hoarding-disorder support.
resources.address: 1366 E. Thomas Rd., Suite 108, Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.hours: Access through the 24-Hour Senior HELP LINE.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
In-home counseling by licensed clinical social workers, community Mental Health First Aid and QPR trainings, medication education, Too Many Treasures therapy groups and support for hoarding disorder, and behavioral-health advocacy and education.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public page identifies the program for older adults. Counseling eligibility, insurance or cost, Mesa visit availability, group schedules and current capacity must be confirmed through intake.

**Population Served**
Older adults in Maricopa County who need support managing mental and emotional health, medication misuse concerns or hoarding-related challenges.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Senior HELP LINE at 602-264-HELP (4357) or toll-free 888-783-7500 and ask for ElderVention Behavioral Health.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not an emergency psychiatric service. For immediate safety danger, call 911 or use an appropriate crisis service.

resources.name: Ability360 - Life Transition Services / Reintegration to the Community
resources.description: Ability360 Life Transition Services support people newly injured or diagnosed and people in nursing or long-term-care facilities who want help reintegrating into community life.
resources.address: 5025 E. Washington St., Suite 200, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: Ability360 main office hours are Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM; use the Life Transitions contact form or call to discuss the specific transition need.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Life Transition Services include Reintegration to the Community for people newly injured or diagnosed in hospitals or rehabilitation centers and people in nursing homes or long-term-care facilities who want support returning to community life. Official page: https://ability360.org/life-transitions/.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page identifies people newly injured or diagnosed, people in hospitals or rehabilitation centers, and people living in nursing homes or long-term-care facilities who want support reintegrating. Specific referral, funding, and geographic criteria should be confirmed with Ability360.

**Population Served**
People with disabilities adjusting to a new injury or diagnosis and people seeking transition from institutional or long-term-care settings into community living.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Life Transitions contact form at https://ability360.org/life-transitions/ or call 602-296-0536. Provide the person's current setting, discharge or transition timeline, disability-related needs, and Mesa/Maricopa County address.

**Important Information to Know**
This resource can help with transition planning and support, but it does not guarantee housing, discharge approval, funding, or an immediate placement.

resources.name: Arizona Courts — Certified Legal Advocate Directory
resources.description: Official directory of certified legal advocates and approved community organizations, showing domestic-violence or housing-stability practice areas and service locations.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Official directory of certified legal advocates and approved community organizations, showing domestic-violence or housing-stability practice areas and service locations.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Anyone can consult the public directory. Each listed provider sets its own intake, eligibility, case scope and capacity.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents seeking a community legal advocate, including survivors in Mesa and Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Find an organization serving the relevant area and contact it directly about the legal issue. Check both the individual advocate’s status and the organization’s approved practice areas.

**Important Information to Know**
Organization approval does not by itself mean a particular advocate is active or accepting cases. The court licensing office does not provide legal representation. A certified advocate has a limited scope; do not assume the same services as an attorney.

resources.name: Basics for Phoenix - Beds and Basic Furniture
resources.description: Basics for Phoenix provides beds and basic furniture to Greater Phoenix families, individuals, seniors and vulnerable adults in hardship through verified referrals from schools, churches, social workers and community agencies.
resources.address: P.O. Box 71314, Phoenix, AZ 85050
resources.hours: Referral-based; call or email for current timing.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Beds, basic furniture and basic household essentials for households in true hardship, with referral coordination that may include pickup, delivery or other next steps after acceptance.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A verified partner such as a school, church, social worker or community agency must submit the referral. The site does not define every Mesa boundary or guarantee delivery, timing or an exact furniture package.

**Population Served**
Children, youth, families, individuals, seniors and vulnerable adults across Greater Phoenix who lack beds or essential furniture because of crisis, hardship or unstable housing.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the client's school, caseworker, church or agency partner to use the referral pathway. Clients can call 602-345-1191 or email office@basicsforphx.org to ask which partner route may fit.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a walk-in warehouse or direct self-service closet. Confirm coverage, referral partner status, delivery/pickup options and wait times before promising furniture.

resources.name: Community Bridges, Inc. - Community Integration Team / Shelters and Outreach / PATH Maricopa
resources.description: Community Bridges, Inc. Community Integration Team/Shelters and Outreach provides street outreach, peer navigation, shelter/healing center operations, behavioral-health and substance-use service connection, housing referral planning and PATH-related outreach for chronically homeless adults with serious mental illness in Maricopa County.
resources.address: CBI administration: 1855 W Baseline Rd #101, Mesa, AZ 85202; outreach and services occur across sites and field routes
resources.hours: 24/7 Access to Care line available; outreach schedules and site access should be confirmed by phone.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Street outreach, Community Integration Team/peer navigation, shelters and Healing Centers, housing planning, Permanent Supportive Housing/Rapid Rehousing pathways, and connections to behavioral-health, substance-use, physical-health and vocational services. PATH outreach adds document, benefit, health and housing connections.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Screening determines the programme. CBI lists pathways for people/families experiencing homelessness, veterans, homeless/runaway young adults 18–24, pregnant/postpartum women with substance-use disorders and their children, and survivors of domestic violence or trafficking. The cited Maricopa PATH track focuses on chronically homeless adults 18+ with Serious Mental Illness; that is not the eligibility test for every CBI service.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness across Maricopa County, including Mesa, with specialized pathways for people with behavioral-health needs, SMI, veterans, youth, pregnant/postpartum women and survivors.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 24-hour Access to Care at 877-931-9142 and ask for Mesa/Maricopa outreach, Community Integration Team, PATH or supportive-housing screening. Appointments: 888-224-6593 or scheduling@cbridges.com. General administration: 480-831-7566.

**Important Information to Know**
The Baseline office is an administrative contact, not established walk-in housing intake. Named Mesa properties, including Ingram, Cicero and Windemere, have programme-specific operator/referral and vacancy requirements. Confirm the correct site through CBI; an address listing does not establish an open bed.

resources.name: Governor's Office of Highway Safety - Children Are Priceless Passengers (CAPP) Program
resources.description: Arizona Children Are Priceless Passengers child passenger safety class program for public participants and drivers cited for child safety-seat violations; current Mesa-area registration details need administrator resolution.
resources.address: Statewide Arizona program; local Mesa/Banner Desert class site not confirmed
resources.hours: Class schedules and sites vary by participating provider; current Mesa/Banner Desert schedule was not confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Governor's Office of Highway Safety describes Children Are Priceless Passengers as a child passenger safety education program that provides two-hour child safety classes in English and Spanish taught by nationally certified child safety-seat technicians. Classes are open to voluntary participants and to drivers who receive a child safety-seat citation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The statewide program is open for voluntary participation and may also serve cited drivers seeking a court-recognized class option. Local providers may set registration, cost and court-document rules.

**Population Served**
Arizona parents, caregivers and cited drivers needing child passenger safety education. Mesa families may benefit if a current nearby provider is available.

**How to Best Connect**
Start with the GOHS Occupant Protection page and the court or law-enforcement instructions if the person received a citation. For Mesa families without a citation, use this as a lead to locate a current CAPP provider; the submitted Banner Desert site and phone were not confirmed.

**Important Information to Know**
This record needs administrator resolution before routine referral because the current Mesa/Banner Desert class site, registration phone, schedule and cost were not confirmed. Do not promise a free or nearby class from this record alone.
resources.resolutionReason: Statewide CAPP identity and service scope are supported by GOHS, but the submitted Mesa-area/Banner Desert access route remains unresolved after targeted official-source checking. Kept as needs-resolution because it is a useful lead but not yet a responsible direct referral for Mesa families.

resources.name: Melabiz Community Hub - youth drop-in, MYGuard and community support services
resources.description: Melabiz Community Hub is a youth and family support hub offering free programs, drop-in support, crisis intervention, mentorship, mental-health support, workforce development, clothing, hygiene/period/safe-sex kits and resource navigation for housing, food, health care, employment and education.
resources.address: 1414 W Broadway Rd Ste 234, Tempe, AZ 85282
resources.hours: Monday 10 AM-6 PM; Tuesday 2 PM-8 PM; Wednesday 2 PM-8 PM; Thursday 10 AM-4 PM; Friday 2 PM-8 PM; Saturday 11 AM-5 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free youth and family programs, crisis intervention, drop-in support, mentorship, mental-health support, workforce development, leadership/life-skills programming, clothing closet, Confidence Kits with hygiene/period/safe-sex supplies, therapy sessions for enrolled participants and resource navigation for housing, utilities, medical/dental care, food, childcare, education and employment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The website emphasizes youth and families and asks people to enroll or make a referral. Adult reentry eligibility outside the youth/family focus is not clearly stated, so confirm fit before referring an older adult returning citizen.

**Population Served**
Youth, young adults and families in Maricopa County/East Valley who need support, crisis intervention, mentorship, basic-needs supplies and navigation. The submitted evidence specifically included youth ages 12-24 and justice-involved individuals; current public page supports the youth/family focus.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-600-5463 for immediate support or use the Enroll or Make a Referral link on the website. The listed site is 1414 W Broadway Rd Ste 234, Tempe, AZ 85282. Hours are Monday 10 AM-6 PM, Tuesday 2 PM-8 PM, Wednesday 2 PM-8 PM, Thursday 10 AM-4 PM, Friday 2 PM-8 PM and Saturday 11 AM-5 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a community hub and navigation/resource-support program, not a residential reentry program. It may be especially useful for younger returning citizens or justice-involved youth, but adult eligibility should be confirmed.

resources.name: SAGE Counseling, Inc. - peer recovery, counseling and case management for justice-involved clients
resources.description: SAGE Counseling provides evidence-based counseling, assessments, case management, peer support, diversion education and group/individual counseling for court-referred and justice-system clients, with a Mesa office and referral portal.
resources.address: 1830 S Alma School Rd, Suite 104, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:30 AM-5:30 PM; weekends by appointment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Assessments, treatment planning, case management, peer support, individual counseling, group counseling, diversion education and court/criminal-justice-referred services. SAGE also helps screen for AHCCCS eligibility during admission and can assist with AHCCCS application steps when appropriate.

**Eligibility Requirements**
SAGE states almost all clients are under court supervision, in a diversion program, incarcerated or referred by the Arizona Department of Child Safety. Referring agencies can submit referrals. SAGE accepts AHCCCS ACC health plans, RBHA plans and American Indian Health Plan; self-pay/court program fees may apply depending on service.

**Population Served**
Court-supervised, diversion, incarcerated, child-welfare-referred or otherwise justice-involved clients needing counseling, substance-use/behavioral-health education, case management or peer support in Mesa/Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-649-3352 option 1 to schedule or ask questions; Spanish scheduling is option 5. Referring agencies can use the customer portal or Submit a Referral link. The Mesa office is 1830 S Alma School Rd, Suite 104. Hours are Monday-Friday 8:30 AM-5:30 PM, weekends by appointment.

**Important Information to Know**
The specific opioid-settlement peer recovery expansion was not found as a separate public program page, but SAGE's current site confirms peer support and justice-system client focus. Confirm court documents, referral requirements, payer coverage and fees before sending a client.

resources.name: Arizona DES - Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP) Nutrition Assistance
resources.description: Arizona DES Elderly Simplified Application Project simplifies Nutrition Assistance/SNAP application, interview and reporting steps for households where all applying members are age 65+ and have no earned or self-employment income.
resources.address: Arizona DES Family Assistance Administration, ESAP Unit, P.O. Box 19009, Phoenix, AZ 85005-9009
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Simplified Nutrition Assistance application process for qualifying older-adult households, including simpler paperwork, a 36-month approval period, no mid-approval contact during the approval period, possibly no renewal interview, fewer reporting requirements and medical-expense deduction options.

**Eligibility Requirements**
All applying household members must be age 65 or older and have no earned or self-employment income. Standard Nutrition Assistance eligibility rules still apply, and households not meeting ESAP criteria can use the standard Nutrition Assistance process.

**Population Served**
Arizona older-adult households age 65+ with no earned or self-employment income, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents seeking food benefits.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply by phone at 855-234-4960, online through Health-e-Arizona Plus, in person at a DES Family Assistance office, or by mail/fax using the ESAP application. Fax numbers are 602-257-7031 for 602/480/623 area codes and 844-680-9840 toll-free from other area codes.

**Important Information to Know**
Submitting an application starts the process but does not guarantee approval. ESAP households must still report when gross monthly income goes over the current limit or when a single lottery/gambling winning is $4,250 or more.

resources.name: Arizona Voice for Crime Victims - Victims' Rights Legal Representation and Social Services
resources.description: Arizona Voice for Crime Victims provides pro bono legal representation and social services to help crime victims understand, assert and enforce victims' rights in Arizona criminal justice proceedings.
resources.address: P.O. Box 12722, Scottsdale, AZ 85267
resources.hours: Call or use the website contact route; public hours are not posted.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Pro bono legal representation, victims' rights advocacy, social services, education and technical assistance for crime victims navigating the criminal justice process.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For crime victims with victims' rights issues. The program screens for case fit, conflicts, posture and capacity; it is not automatic representation.

**Population Served**
Crime victims in Arizona, including domestic-violence survivors when the need involves victims' rights in a criminal case.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-600-2661 or use the official website contact route. Be ready to describe the criminal case and victims' rights issue for screening.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a shelter, family-law clinic or general civil legal aid program. It is most useful when a survivor needs help with constitutional or statutory crime-victim rights in the criminal justice process.

resources.name: East Valley NAACP Branch 1008-B - Legal Redress complaint assistance
resources.description: East Valley NAACP Branch 1008-B helps people file Legal Redress complaints when they believe they have experienced discrimination, serving Mesa and surrounding East Valley communities.
resources.address: P.O. Box 5024, Mesa, AZ 85211
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Assistance filing a Legal Redress complaint for people who believe they have experienced discrimination. The branch is a civil-rights complaint support and community advocacy contact.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people with discrimination concerns in the East Valley branch service area. This is not attorney representation or legal advice; complaint handling and volunteer capacity should be confirmed with the branch.

**Population Served**
People in Ahwatukee Foothills, Apache Junction, Chandler, Gilbert, Mesa, Fountain Hills, Scottsdale, Tempe and Queen Creek who have discrimination concerns.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-442-1222 or use the contact information on the East Valley NAACP website. Mail can be sent to P.O. Box 5024, Mesa, AZ 85211.

**Important Information to Know**
Legal Redress is a complaint-assistance and civil-rights advocacy pathway, not a direct legal-aid intake or guaranteed attorney referral. Urgent court deadlines should also be addressed with a legal services provider.

resources.name: Arizona Youth Partnership - AIM 4 Teen Moms
resources.description: Arizona Youth Partnership's AIM 4 Teen Moms is a free statewide virtual eight-session program for teen mothers ages 14-20 with at least one child, focused on goals, career planning, contraception, and reproductive life planning.
resources.address: Administrative office: 2210 E. Fort Lowell Rd., Suite 201, Tucson, AZ 85719; program is virtual statewide
resources.hours: Virtual program schedule is determined at referral/enrollment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
AIM 4 Teen Moms is an evidence-based eight-session program with six individual sessions and two group sessions over about eight weeks. It helps teen mothers define life aspirations, plan toward career goals, build communication and strengths, consider contraception, and create a reproductive life plan.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is designed for mothers ages 14-20 with at least one child. Arizona Youth Partnership states it is provided free virtually across Arizona.

**Population Served**
Teen mothers in Arizona, including Mesa and Maricopa County teen moms who can participate virtually.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the referral form linked on the AIM 4 Teen Moms page. The page lists Stephanie King at 480-571-3498 and Stephanie@AZYP.org, with KariS@AZYP.org also shown. Arizona Youth Partnership's toll-free number is 877-882-2881.

**Important Information to Know**
This is education and parenting/reproductive-life planning support, not medical care, child care, or material assistance. Confirm current enrollment capacity, virtual schedule, and consent/guardian requirements for minors.

resources.name: Canyon Vista Recovery Center - Medical Detox, Residential, PHP and Outpatient Addiction Treatment
resources.description: Canyon Vista Recovery Center is a Mesa drug and alcohol rehab at 860 N Center St offering medical detox, residential treatment, partial hospitalization, intensive outpatient treatment, Suboxone opioid treatment, mental-health care for stable clients, and alumni support.
resources.address: 860 N Center St, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Call admissions for current assessment and admission timing; the official site states around-the-clock admissions may be available with pre-approval.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Canyon Vista provides Mesa addiction treatment including medical detox, residential care, PHP/IOP, Suboxone treatment and recovery support. Its residential mental-health programme accepts clients with or without substance-use concerns who are stable before admission, including selected anxiety, depression, bipolar and borderline-personality conditions. The programme describes psychotherapy, psychiatric care and trauma-focused treatment; admissions determines clinical fit and the actual care plan.

**Eligibility Requirements**
People seeking treatment for drug or alcohol addiction may contact admissions. Clinical fit, detox needs, residential versus outpatient placement, mental-health stability, insurance, cost, and current availability are determined through Canyon Vista's admissions process.

**Population Served**
Adults seeking addiction treatment in Mesa and the greater Phoenix area. Canyon Vista serves men and women and lists Tactical Recovery for military members, veterans and first responders; ask about the specific track’s eligibility.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Canyon Vista admissions at 888-979-1840 or use its official contact form. The provider lists 860 N Center St, Mesa, AZ 85201. Confirm the appropriate intake location before traveling.

**Important Information to Know**
Ask admissions to verify clinical fit, available treatment, insurance participation, authorization and out-of-pocket costs. Provider insurance logos do not guarantee coverage or immediate placement.

resources.name: Unlimited Potential — Adult education, English and workforce training
resources.description: Unlimited Potential offers adult education and workforce development programming in South Phoenix, including ESL, GED, computer classes, and an arboriculture workforce pathway, with phone and web contact for current class availability.
resources.address: 3146 E. Wier Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85040
resources.hours: Call for the selected class’s current schedule and enrollment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Adult education services including ESL-English as a Second Language, GED education, computer classes, and workforce development including an arboriculture program for people interested in trees, plants, outdoor work, and hands-on training.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public program page does not list schedules, costs, enrollment rules, refugee referral requirements, or explicit countywide eligibility. DES refugee English Language Training participation, if applicable, may require referral through refugee-service channels.

**Population Served**
Adults in South Phoenix and surrounding Maricopa County communities seeking English, GED, computer, or workforce-development classes, including immigrant or refugee learners when eligible through the appropriate referral path.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-305-4742 or use the contact form on the Unlimited Potential program page. Ask about current ESL, GED, computer, refugee English Language Training, arboriculture, costs, schedule, and whether a Mesa resident may participate.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm class openings, cost, location, Mesa eligibility and any remote option. Refugee-funded English training may require a resettlement or refugee-service referral, while broader adult classes can have different rules. This is education/workforce support, not immigration legal representation.

resources.name: LSS Mesa I-HELP — operator and intake to resolve
resources.description: Could preserve a Mesa women’s shelter pathway if its current operator and intake are confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Could preserve a Mesa women’s shelter pathway if its current operator and intake are confirmed.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Current programme operation and client eligibility need administrator resolution.

**Population Served**
Administrators reconciling the historically delivered Mesa I-HELP identity.

**How to Best Connect**
Review the LSS programme and the separate LSS Mesa women listing in TCAA’s current directory before making a referral.

TCAA’s own I-HELP programme has a different identity; it must not replace this historical record or inherit its human decisions. Current operator, public intake and duplicate identity remain unresolved.

resources.name: Southwest Behavioral & Health Services - In Home Permanent Supportive Housing
resources.description: Southwest Behavioral & Health Services In Home PSH is a voluntary permanent supportive housing service that provides support in a person's home and community to help maintain housing of choice.
resources.address: 3450 N 3rd St, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Voluntary permanent supportive housing supports delivered in the home and community, using recovery-based support to help participants maintain housing of their choice.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Public information does not list full eligibility, referral or subsidy rules. Clients should expect screening and possible behavioral-health or health-plan referral requirements.

**Population Served**
People needing flexible behavioral-health-linked in-home supportive housing services in the Phoenix/Maricopa County service area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call SB&H at 602-265-8338 and ask for the In Home permanent supportive housing team or housing services. Confirm Mesa reach, referral source and current availability.

**Important Information to Know**
This service may support housing stability but is not the same as an immediate shelter bed or a public rental subsidy application.

resources.name: Mahina Therapy — immigration psychological evaluations
resources.description: Provides specialized psychological evaluations supporting an immigration case when the client’s legal team recommends one.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides specialized psychological evaluations supporting an immigration case when the client’s legal team recommends one.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Consult the legal team first; evaluations are offered by secure video, with eligibility and scheduling confirmed by the practice.

**Population Served**
Immigration applicants needing psychological evidence for a supported case.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 509-255-3872 or email admin@mahinatherapy.com. Published sliding fees are $900–$1,500; payment plans are available on request.

**Important Information to Know**
Insurance is not accepted for this assessment. Reports normally take 3–5 weeks after the second interview; expedited work costs extra. This is evaluation, not legal representation.

resources.name: Fresh Start Women’s Foundation — Survivor Recovery Support
resources.description: Post-crisis survivor support including one-to-one social-work coaching, safety planning education, support groups, domestic-violence education, Address Confidentiality Program application assistance and practical resource connections.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Post-crisis survivor support including one-to-one social-work coaching, safety planning education, support groups, domestic-violence education, Address Confidentiality Program application assistance and practical resource connections.

**Eligibility Requirements**

For women seeking support after domestic or sexual violence. Ask about the appropriate program and appointment process; some hosted partner sessions have broader eligibility.

**Population Served**

Women recovering from domestic or sexual violence in the Phoenix area, including those who can travel from Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**

Call Fresh Start or use its Connect with Us link for ongoing support. Consult the current calendar for support groups and workshops.

**Important Information to Know**

Fresh Start does not provide emergency shelter or crisis intervention. Children cannot attend classes or appointments or be left unattended at the site; discuss practical attendance barriers before travel. Family-law document preparation and New Life Center guest advocacy have separate access arrangements.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Education — Homeless Education Liaison Finder
resources.description: A statewide directory connecting families and unaccompanied youth with their public-school or charter-school homeless-education liaison.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

A statewide directory connecting families and unaccompanied youth with their public-school or charter-school homeless-education liaison.

**Eligibility Requirements**

The local liaison assesses the student’s housing situation and school-support needs; contact the school even if required enrollment documents are missing.

**Population Served**

School-age children and youth whose housing is unstable, including unaccompanied youth.

**How to Best Connect**

Find the student’s school district or charter in the official contact list and ask its liaison about enrollment, attendance barriers and applicable school supports.

**Important Information to Know**

This is education navigation, not shelter placement. The liaison determines which supports and transportation arrangements apply to the student.

resources.name: City of Mesa Prosecutor's Office - Victim Services Unit
resources.description: The City of Mesa Prosecutor's Office Victim Services Unit supports victims in City criminal cases and Mesa residents seeking help with victimization, including rights, court process, protective orders, safety planning, restitution, victim compensation and ACP applications.
resources.address: Mesa Municipal Court, 250 E 1st Ave, Suite 222, Mesa, AZ 85211
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 7:00 AM-6:00 PM. No services outside business hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Victims' rights and criminal-justice information, case status support, court accompaniment, safe waiting support, protective-order petition help, safety planning, restitution request help, victim-compensation application assistance, Address Confidentiality Program application endorsement and community-resource referrals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For victims in Mesa Municipal Court criminal cases and Mesa residents seeking assistance with victimization. The unit cannot give legal advice and cannot provide services outside business hours.

**Population Served**
Mesa crime victims, including domestic-violence survivors and Spanish-speaking survivors who can use the listed Victim Services phone route.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-644-2188, email VSU@mesaaz.gov, fax 480-644-2584 or visit/correspond with the Mesa Municipal Court Suite 222 location during posted hours.

**Important Information to Know**
Communications with victim-services staff are not the same as private legal counsel; staff cannot withhold exculpatory information and must report reasonable suspicion of child abuse or neglect. Victim Impact Statements are not confidential.

resources.name: Maricopa County - County Indigent Decedent Services Program
resources.description: Maricopa County County Indigent Decedent Services provides final disposition for people who die in Maricopa County and are unclaimed, indigent, abandoned or unidentified, and offers a financial-assistance application route for direct next of kin unable to afford final arrangements.
resources.address: 301 W Jefferson St, Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
County Indigent Decedent Services provides final disposition for unclaimed, indigent, abandoned or unidentified decedents who die in Maricopa County. Direct next of kin who cannot afford final disposition may complete a CIDS NOK financial-assistance application.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The death must fall under the Maricopa County program scope. Direct next of kin applying for financial assistance must provide proof of relationship and financial records to determine need. The FAQ states applicants must be referred by a contracted funeral home for consideration, then complete an online application and upload financial documents.

**Population Served**
Direct next of kin of a decedent who died in Maricopa County and cannot afford final arrangements, plus unclaimed, indigent, abandoned or unidentified decedent cases handled by the county.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-372-0535, option 5, or email CIDS@maricopa.gov. Funeral homes not contracted with CIDS may refer an abandoned decedent by the same phone or email.

**Important Information to Know**
Legal and financial responsibility for final disposition generally falls on direct next of kin under Arizona law, but the county recognizes that some families cannot pay. If the death resulted from a crime, victim compensation may be a separate route for funeral costs.

resources.name: AHCCCS - Grievance, Appeal, and State Fair Hearing Pathway
resources.description: AHCCCS provides grievance, appeal, expedited appeal, and State Fair Hearing pathways for applicants and members challenging eligibility decisions, health-plan actions, or covered-service disputes.
resources.address: AHCCCS Office of the General Counsel, 150 N. 18th Ave., MD-15013, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Official instructions for grievances, appeals, expedited review and requests for a State Fair Hearing concerning AHCCCS decisions.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The correct process depends on whether the issue concerns eligibility, a managed-care plan, fee-for-service coverage or another specific program.

**Population Served**
AHCCCS applicants, members and their authorized representatives.

**How to Best Connect**
Follow the decision notice. Managed-care members normally use their plan’s appeals department; eligibility appeals go to the deciding agency. Fee-for-service medical-service appeals can be submitted in writing to AHCCCS General Counsel, 150 N. 18th Ave., MD-15013, Phoenix, AZ 85007, or fax 602-253-9115. For guidance call 602-417-4232 or 800-654-8713, extension 74232; confirm the correct destination and receipt.

**Important Information to Know**
Deadlines and continued-service requirements can be short, and continued services may require repayment after an unsuccessful appeal. An appeal route is not attorney representation; urgent health risks may warrant requesting expedited review under the applicable process.

resources.name: Maricopa County Assessor - Personal Exemptions and Senior Valuation Protection
resources.description: Maricopa County Assessor Valuation Relief includes personal exemptions for qualifying widowed persons, people with disability and disabled veterans, plus Senior Valuation Protection that freezes limited property value for qualifying senior homeowners.
resources.address: 301 W Jefferson St, Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.hours: Applications have annual deadlines; personal exemption applications are due by February 28, or by September 1 with an approved deadline waiver. Senior Valuation Protection applications must be filed January 1 through September 1 for the current tax year.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Assessor's Valuation Relief programs can reduce or stabilize property-tax burden for eligible homeowners. Personal Exemptions reduce assessed limited property value for qualifying widowed persons, people with total permanent disability, and disabled veterans. Senior Valuation Protection freezes the Limited Property Value for three years for qualifying senior homeowners; it does not freeze the actual tax bill.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Personal Exemptions require income and residency qualifications. The Assessor's current page lists 2026 household-income limits of $39,865 for households with no children under 18 and $47,826 for households with children under 18 or medically/physically disabled children. Senior Valuation Protection requires at least one owner age 65 or older, two years' residency, income limits based on all owners on title, and renewal every three years.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County homeowners who may qualify because of widow/widower status, disability, disabled-veteran status, or senior homeowner status.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through the Assessor forms/portal, email PE.SVP@Maricopa.gov, mail, or go in person to the Maricopa County Assessor, 301 W Jefferson St, Phoenix, AZ 85003. Call 602-506-3406 for questions.

**Important Information to Know**
This is property-tax relief, not cash assistance and not renter assistance. Deadlines are consequential. Senior Valuation Protection can be removed if ownership, residence, property status or renewal requirements change, and removal may trigger a Limited Property Value recalculation.

resources.name: Paz de Cristo Community Center - Clothing Closet / Clothe Program
resources.description: Paz de Cristo provides adult clothing through its Mesa Clothing Closet, clothing and hygiene items during shower services, professional interview clothing and seasonal items when donations allow.
resources.address: 424 W Broadway Rd, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Clothing Closet: Monday and Friday 1:00-2:00 PM. Shower clothing/hygiene is connected to shower services; call for current shower hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Adult casual clothing, professional interview attire, shower-linked hygiene items and fresh clothing including socks, underwear and t-shirts. Shoes, blankets and seasonal items may be available depending on donations.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For guests in need at the Mesa campus. The page does not list income, residency or document requirements for the clothing closet. Children's clothing is not available.

**Population Served**
