**How to Best Connect**
Complete the intake form linked on the Candelen program page or call 480-829-0500. Candelen states the team follows up after reviewing intake information.

**Important Information to Know**
Doula Parent Educators are not medical providers and cannot deliver the baby. Current capacity and enrollment timing are determined through intake.

resources.name: USCIS — document, appointment and case assistance
resources.description: Official USCIS contact and appointment routes for immigration-benefit cases, document problems and scheduled processing services.
resources.address: Use the location on the USCIS appointment notice.
resources.hours: Appointments only. Start online or through the USCIS Contact Center; do not go to the field office without an appointment or appointment notice.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Official contact for immigration-document non-delivery, temporary proof such as ADIT stamps, appointment and case questions, emergency advance-parole requests and immigration-judge-grant matters. USCIS also arranges interviews and Application Support Center biometrics through their distinct appointment processes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The case must fit a USCIS service or appointment category.

**Population Served**
Immigration benefit applicants and others with an existing USCIS service need.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the USCIS Contact Center or call 800-375-5283. The myUSCIS appointment-request service may be appropriate for an eligible in-person request. Follow the appointment notice for the exact office, time, identification and rescheduling instructions.

**Important Information to Know**
Biometrics at an Application Support Center and field-office interviews or emergency appointments are different services and can use different locations. Do not assume walk-in access. USCIS processes cases; seek an authorized legal provider for independent advice about what to file or immigration-court representation.

resources.name: Citizenshipworks - Free online citizenship application support
resources.description: Citizenshipworks is a free online nonprofit tool for preparing U.S. citizenship applications, with screening and potential connection to free online legal review or a trusted nonprofit partner.
resources.hours: Online tool available anytime; legal review or partner help depends on issue and partner availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free online naturalization application support that guides users through citizenship forms, flags issues that may need expert help, and may connect users to free legal review or a nearby trusted nonprofit partner.

**Eligibility Requirements**
This is for lawful permanent residents and others assessing eligibility for U.S. citizenship/naturalization. It is not for all immigration case types and does not replace an attorney for complicated immigration history, criminal history or removal issues.

**Population Served**
Citizenship applicants nationwide, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents who can use an online tool and email support.

**How to Best Connect**
Start at citizenshipworks.org and create or begin an online application. For support, use support@citizenshipworks.org. If the tool identifies a concern, follow its referral or legal-review instructions before filing anything with USCIS.

**Important Information to Know**
The tool is free; applicants still may owe USCIS filing fees unless they qualify for a USCIS fee waiver. Legal review depends on the application issues and partner availability. It is best for naturalization, not family petitions, DACA, asylum or court defense.

resources.name: Assistory Outreach Services - Digital Assist Program for Seniors and Food Pantry
resources.description: Assistory Outreach Services' Digital Assist Program for Seniors teaches older adults basic phone and computer skills at no cost; Assistory also operates free food distributions, including a listed Mesa food-assist site.
resources.address: 1706 E. Commonwealth Cir., Chandler, AZ 85225
resources.hours: Office hours listed by Assistory: Tuesday and Friday 9:00 AM-4:00 PM; Monday, Wednesday and Thursday by appointment; Saturday-Sunday closed. Class and food-distribution schedules should be confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Digital Assist Program for Seniors teaches basic cell-phone and computer skills at no cost so older adults can use technology more confidently and stay connected. Assistory also lists free food-assist distributions for underserved neighbors, including Mesa.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The digital program is described for seniors and elderly participants. The official page does not publish current class dates, enrollment steps, exact Mesa class locations or food-pantry intake rules.

**Population Served**
Older adults in the Phoenix metro and East Valley area who need basic technology help, plus underserved neighbors using Assistory food distributions.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Assistory Outreach Services at 602-699-4212 before referral. Ask whether DAPS is currently accepting participants, where classes or one-to-one help are held, and which food-distribution site serves the client.

**Important Information to Know**
Call before traveling to a class, pantry site or the Chandler office. Technology classes and food distributions have separate schedules and participation details.

resources.name: Pathways for Life - Studio Works / Mesa employment services
resources.description: Pathways for Life provides employment services for individuals with disabilities, including PTW Pathways to Employment, group supported employment, customized plans, skill development, local employer connections and coaching.
resources.address: 1250 E Southern Ave, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: Use the website contact route for current intake, scheduling and funding questions.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Employment services for individuals with disabilities include Pathways to Employment, group supported employment, hands-on skill building, resume and interview skills, community employer connections, personalized plans and ongoing coaching.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public page says programs are designed for individuals with developmental disabilities who want to explore or improve employment opportunities. Confirm DDD, VR, private-pay or other funding rules and whether a referral is required.

**Population Served**
People with developmental disabilities seeking employment support through the Mesa/East Valley Pathways for Life location or other Arizona locations.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Get in Touch/contact route on the Pathways for Life employment services page. Ask about Mesa employment services, funding authorization, transportation and current openings.

**Important Information to Know**
The website supports the service but gives limited public intake detail. Confirm payer/referral requirements, transportation availability and whether a Mesa client can start immediately.

resources.name: RISE Services, Inc. - Supported Employment Services
resources.description: RISE Services, Inc. Arizona provides employment services for adults with disabilities, including job-based training, supported employment, job training and coaching, employment advocacy, public transportation navigation and worksite acclimation.
resources.address: Mesa-area services; contact RISE for location details
resources.hours: Contact RISE for intake, current openings, locations and authorization requirements.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
RISE employment services help adults with disabilities find and sustain meaningful work. Services include job-based training, supported employment, job coaches, training and coaching through the employment process, resume building, mock interviews, social and communication skills, public transportation navigation, worksite acclimation and employment advocacy.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public page describes services for adults with developmental disabilities and adults with disabilities. Confirm DDD, VR, private-pay or other funding authorization, referral requirements and current capacity.

**Population Served**
Adults with disabilities and developmental disabilities in Arizona, including Mesa-area participants who can access RISE services.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Contact Us route on the RISE Arizona website and ask specifically about Mesa supported employment services, funding authorization, transportation and program openings.

**Important Information to Know**
RISE serves Mesa and surrounding Arizona communities, but the public page does not list detailed intake steps or funding rules. Confirm current location, referral source and job-coach availability before referral.

resources.name: Phoenix VA Health Care System - Community Resource and Referral Center (CRRC) / Homeless Veteran Care
resources.description: The Phoenix VA Community Resource and Referral Center is a walk-in clinic and access point for veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness, providing assessment, care coordination and referrals for housing, shelter, health care, mental health care, substance-use treatment, employment and benefits-related community supports.
resources.address: 1500 E Thomas Rd, Suite 106, Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 7:30 AM-4:00 PM, excluding federal holidays. VA recommends arriving early because same-day referrals may be harder late in the afternoon.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Walk-in homeless-veteran assessment and care coordination; connections to transitional/permanent housing, eviction prevention, community shelters, food pantries, health and mental-health care, substance-use treatment/detox and employment specialists. VA materials also describe help obtaining an ID or necessary documents. On-site health care is available to VA-eligible homeless veterans engaged with VA homeless programmes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness due to financial hardship, unemployment, addiction, depression, mental-health issues, physical-health issues or transition from jail may seek help. VA eligibility, documentation needs and program fit are determined through VA assessment.

**Population Served**
Veterans in the Phoenix VA service area, including Mesa and Maricopa County veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness.

**How to Best Connect**
Walk in to 1500 E Thomas Rd, Suite 106, Phoenix, Monday-Friday 7:30 AM-4:00 PM excluding federal holidays. Arrive early when possible. Call 602-248-6040 or email VHAPHOCRRCStaff@va.gov.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an assessment and referral access point, not a guaranteed bed, cash grant, treatment admission or document-payment service. Same-day referrals are a goal and can be harder late in the day; community shelter referrals may be offered instead. Eligibility, documents, availability and assessment determine each service.

resources.name: Arizona Hands & Voices - Guide By Your Side
resources.description: Arizona Hands & Voices Guide By Your Side provides free parent and Deaf or Hard of Hearing adult guidance for Arizona families of children who are Deaf or hard of hearing.
resources.address: PO Box 30163, Phoenix, AZ 85046
resources.hours: Use the online request/referral forms or call; guide availability and meeting times are arranged after matching.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Guide By Your Side offers emotional support, unbiased communication information, parent-to-parent guidance, Deaf or Hard of Hearing adult perspectives, early-intervention and education resource navigation, and support during transitions.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is for families with children who are Deaf or hard of hearing. Parents can request a guide; professionals can submit a family referral.

**Population Served**
Arizona families of children who are Deaf or hard of hearing, including Mesa families. Support may include newly identified babies, young children, older children and teens.

**How to Best Connect**
Parents can use the Request a Guide form; professionals can use the Refer a Family form. For questions, email gbys@azhv.org or call toll-free 866-685-1050. The program notes Spanish availability.

**Important Information to Know**
This is peer support and navigation, not audiology, therapy, diagnosis, legal representation, or guaranteed provider placement. Guide matching and response time should be confirmed at referral.

resources.name: International Rescue Committee - IRC Phoenix Health Program
resources.description: The International Rescue Committee in Phoenix Health Program supports refugees, asylees and other newcomers with patient advocacy, maternal and child health, medical care coordination and health education in partnership with local healthcare providers.
resources.address: 4425 W Olive Ave, #400, Glendale, AZ 85302
resources.hours: Contact the Phoenix office for intake hours and eligibility; public program hours are not listed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Health access support, including patient advocacy, maternal and child health, medical care coordination and health education through partnerships with local healthcare providers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
IRC Phoenix primarily serves refugees, asylees, asylum seekers, victims of trafficking, survivors of torture and other immigrants/newcomers. Program eligibility depends on immigration/refugee status, funding and client situation.

**Population Served**
Refugees, asylees, asylum seekers, trafficking survivors, torture survivors and other newcomer/immigrant communities in Phoenix and Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-433-2440 or email Phoenix@rescue.org. Office address: 4425 W Olive Ave, #400, Glendale, AZ 85302.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a health navigation and coordination program, not a walk-in clinic. Direct medical care depends on partner providers and client eligibility.

resources.name: Valley of the Sun YMCA - YMCA Housing Program / Lincoln Downtown Residence transitional housing
resources.description: Valley of the Sun YMCA's Lincoln Downtown Residence transitional housing program is a temporary housing option with fees, application requirements, income proof, ID/SSN and background check requirements.
resources.address: Lincoln Family Downtown YMCA, 350 N 1st Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Temporary transitional housing through the YMCA/Lincoln Residence Program for people needing independent-living style housing while in transition.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official indexed page says applicants need valid ID, Social Security number, background check, proof of income for the past 30 days, application fee and deposit. It is not intended as permanent housing.

**Population Served**
Phoenix metro adults who can meet income and application requirements and need temporary transitional housing.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-212-6042 or email LincolnDowntownResidence@vosymca.org to confirm the current application process, room availability, fees and location access.

**Important Information to Know**
The official page returned 404 during direct fetch, but official indexed content still describes the program. Listed costs included a $650 standard room rate, $40 application fee and $200 non-refundable security deposit. Confirm current status before sending a client.

resources.name: Valley Metro Commute Solutions - Vanpool
resources.description: Valley Metro supports shared-cost vanpools for recurring work commutes when riders can share a schedule. Ask Commute Solutions about the current vanpool contact and rules.
resources.hours: Call or email for current commute-program support hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Vanpool helps groups of commuters share a regular work trip in a van and split operating costs. It can support longer or poorly transit-served commutes when enough riders share a schedule.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A viable group, qualifying commute, driver, vehicle availability, contract and monthly payment are generally required. Employer subsidy, public-agency subsidy and program rules vary.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County workers and commuters, including Mesa origins or destinations, who need recurring work transportation and can share a schedule with other riders.

**How to Best Connect**
Start with Valley Metro’s vanpool webpage or call general Commute Solutions at 602-262-7433 for current vanpool routing. The published vanpool email is vanpool@valleymetro.org; confirm the current contact, group-size, distance, driver, pricing and subsidy rules. Ask whether ShareTheRide matching or any ride-home arrangement applies.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not an individual emergency ride, one-time appointment ride or guaranteed free service. It can be useful for clients with stable work hours who can share costs and schedule with a group.

resources.name: Marathon Staffing Mesa Office
resources.description: Marathon Staffing's Mesa office places job seekers into temporary, contract, and other local assignments, with online application, current job listings, weekday office hours, and placement staff.
resources.address: 1237 S. Val Vista Dr., Suite 216, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 7:00 AM-6:00 PM; Friday-Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Temporary and contract staffing through a Mesa office, online Apply With Marathon route, current job listings, and placement specialists. Recent listings on the Mesa page included municipal, East Mesa, Queen Creek, IT, and instructor roles, but openings change quickly.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on the specific assignment. Applicants should confirm identification and work authorization, screenings, background checks, role location, schedule, duration, transportation, and any job-specific credentials.

**Population Served**
Mesa, East Valley, and nearby Maricopa County job seekers looking for temporary or contract work through a staffing firm.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Apply With Marathon or View Jobs links on the Mesa page, call 480-654-4606, or contact the Mesa office at 1237 S. Val Vista Dr., Suite 216, Mesa, AZ 85204 during posted office hours.

**Important Information to Know**
Job listings and start times change quickly. The under-24-hour employment language from source submissions is not a guarantee; verify each role's status, pay, duration, and screening requirements.

resources.name: A New Leaf - Desert Leaf Apartments
resources.description: A New Leaf Desert Leaf Apartments is a 19-unit permanent supportive housing complex in Mesa for individuals or families affected by homelessness, domestic violence or severe mental illness, with active case management and supportive-service connections. Half of units are described as occupied by veterans.
resources.address: 44 S Horne, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: Call or email Kay-Kay Realty Leasing Office for unit inquiries; referrals may also come through partner or governmental entities.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Permanent supportive housing in a gated Mesa apartment complex, with active case management, individualized supportive services, basic-needs connection, counseling and community-resource referrals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Desert Leaf serves people who fit the supportive-housing model, including households affected by homelessness, domestic violence or severe mental illness. Official material says residents are referred through community partners and governmental entities; vacancy, screening and referral requirements must be confirmed with leasing staff.

**Population Served**
Veterans, individuals and families in Mesa needing long-term supportive housing; A New Leaf notes about half of Desert Leaf units are occupied by veterans.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Kay-Kay Realty Leasing Office at 480-834-2228 or email lamesita@kay-kay.biz. For general A New Leaf housing support, email housing@turnanewleaf.org or call 480-969-4024.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not emergency shelter. Units are limited and about half being occupied by veterans does not establish a reserved vacancy. Confirm rent, availability, screening and whether a partner/government referral or direct application is required with leasing staff.

resources.name: City of Glendale — Community Action Program
resources.description: Provides rent and utility crisis assistance for eligible Glendale households.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides rent and utility crisis assistance for eligible Glendale households.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Glendale residents must meet the programme’s crisis, income and documentation rules. Utility and rental assistance have separate requirements; prior assistance may affect eligibility.

**Population Served**
Glendale households experiencing financial crisis or housing instability.

**How to Best Connect**
Check the official CAP page for the next application window or call for help. At the September 27, 2026 research check, the portal was scheduled to open September 29 at 8:30 a.m. and close September 30 at 8:30 a.m.

**Important Information to Know**
Applications and funds are limited. Prepare identification, recent income documentation, housing documents and current utility bills; follow the posted document deadline. Mesa residents need a Mesa programme. Power AZ is no longer accepting new applications despite older referral text.

resources.name: Maricopa County Human Services - Rental assistance for non-Mesa county areas
resources.description: Maricopa County Human Services provides rental deposit or monthly rental assistance for eligible county residents outside Glendale, Mesa and Phoenix, using local Community Action Program offices and an online client portal.
resources.address: 301 W Jefferson St, Phoenix, AZ 85003; assistance is delivered through CAP offices for eligible non-Mesa county areas
resources.hours: CAP appointment availability is first-come, first-served and varies by local office.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Rental deposit or monthly rental-payment assistance for eligible Maricopa County households outside excluded cities, with application through the Human Services Department client portal or the local CAP office.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must live in Maricopa County but not in Glendale, Mesa or Phoenix; have a documented crisis event causing income loss, unexpected expenses or health/safety risk; and be past due on rent. Funding may require citizenship or qualified-noncitizen verification.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County renters in eligible non-Mesa, non-Glendale and non-Phoenix jurisdictions, including county islands or surrounding municipalities served by county CAP offices.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the county client portal or contact the local CAP office for the client's service area. For general inquiries call 602-506-0589; the county main line is 602-506-3011.

**Important Information to Know**
This county programme excludes residents within Mesa, Glendale and Phoenix; Mesa households are routed to Mesa/A New Leaf assistance. It is retained for eligible county islands and surrounding jurisdictions. Confirm the service-area boundary with the local CAP office. Appointments are first come, first served, and applying does not guarantee funding.

resources.name: EPCOR Arizona — Payment arrangements
resources.description: EPCOR Arizona offers water and wastewater customer assistance including payment arrangements, a low-income monthly credit, deployed service member bill waivers, and a disabled-veteran water bill credit for eligible customers in EPCOR territories.
resources.hours: Customer Care is available 24/7 by phone.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
EPCOR offers arrangements to spread past-due residential water or wastewater balances. Its online arrangement option allows up to three months, subject to account eligibility.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Have a qualifying EPCOR Arizona residential account and meet account-specific payment-arrangement conditions. Confirm the proposed installments before agreeing.

**Population Served**
EPCOR Arizona residential customers having difficulty paying an outstanding balance.

**How to Best Connect**
Check the EPCOR online account arrangement option, call 800-383-0834 (Customer Care available 24/7), or email mywater@epcor.com.

**Important Information to Know**
Pay the agreed installments plus current charges. An arrangement is not a grant or an indefinite disconnection ban. Low-income, disabled-veteran and deployed-service-member benefits have separate applications. This does not serve City of Mesa water accounts.

resources.name: Jabari & Amani Foundation - Pregnancy and Infant Loss Support
resources.description: Mesa-based pregnancy and infant loss support organization offering grief counseling, peer-to-peer support, referrals, and support after miscarriage, stillbirth, or infant loss in the first year of life.
resources.address: 1350 E. McKellips Rd., Suite 5, Mesa, AZ 85203
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Compassionate support for pregnancy and child loss, including grief counseling, peer-to-peer support, referrals, and an annual candlelight vigil.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official search result describes support for parents after miscarriage, stillbirth, or infant loss in the first year of life. Fees, counseling credentials, and appointment process should be confirmed before referral.

**Population Served**
Bereaved parents and families after pregnancy loss or infant loss, with a Mesa office listed.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 1-800-537-0492 or email info@jabariamanifoundation.org. The listed Mesa office is 1350 E. McKellips Rd., Suite 5, Mesa, AZ 85203.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm active hours, appointment process, fees and the qualifications and scope of the counseling offered before visiting. Ask whether the current support format fits the family’s loss and needs.

resources.name: Mesa Community College — First Things First College Scholarship
resources.description: Scholarship support for up to 24 college credits annually, including eligible tuition, fees, course materials and exam fees in early-childhood education.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Scholarship support for up to 24 college credits annually, including eligible tuition, fees, course materials and exam fees in early-childhood education.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Qualifying MCC early-childhood degree enrollment and Arizona work with or on behalf of children birth through five, or at least 15 volunteer hours monthly in an approved setting. Priority favors direct-care workers without a degree.

**Population Served**

Eligible early-childhood workers and volunteers seeking a credential or degree.

**How to Best Connect**

Begin with MCC early-childhood advising, complete the financial-aid steps, create an Arizona Early Childhood Workforce Registry account and submit the required scholarship documents.

**Important Information to Know**

Funding and eligibility require review. The college advises allowing up to two weeks after all documentation is submitted; confirm payment arrangements before tuition is due.

resources.name: Give 'Em A Break Foundation - Vehicle Repair Assistance / One-Time Hardship Support
resources.description: Give 'Em A Break Foundation provides one-time direct-to-vendor hardship assistance for full-time employed Arizonans, including car repair or vehicle breakdown assistance when an unexpected crisis threatens stability.
resources.address: Maricopa, Apache and Navajo counties, AZ
resources.hours: Online contact form; response times not published.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Give 'Em A Break provides one-time hardship assistance paid directly to verified vendors, including mechanics, landlords, utilities and other service providers. Official pages describe vehicle breakdowns and major car repairs as covered hardship examples.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be full-time employed individuals or small families facing a sudden, unexpected hardship. The foundation focuses on people who may not qualify for traditional aid and reviews each request for need and accountability.

**Population Served**
Working individuals and families in Arizona, with a focus on Maricopa, Apache and Navajo counties.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the assistance/contact form on the Give 'Em A Break website. Describe the unexpected hardship and the vendor expense for which help is requested. Response times are not published.

**Important Information to Know**
Assistance is not cash to the applicant and is not for recurring or predictable expenses. Approval is not guaranteed, and support is paid directly to verified vendors such as mechanics.

resources.name: City of Mesa Office of Homeless Solutions - Off the Streets / Sunaire shelter facility
resources.description: City of Mesa's Off the Streets program provides referral-only non-congregate emergency shelter and support services; the former hotel at 6733 E Main St has been converted into the Sunaire shelter facility for this program.
resources.address: Sunaire property: 6733 E Main St, Mesa, AZ 85205; no walk-up access
resources.hours: Referral-only program with 24/7 on-site oversight; call the Mesa Homeless Resource Line for assistance.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Referral-only emergency shelter in a non-congregate hotel-style setting, with food, clothing, case management, identification and document help, employment-service connections, mental-health and substance-use treatment connections, transportation at exit and housing-stability planning.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Mesa-based people experiencing homelessness who are referred by Mesa staff or community partners and can follow program expectations. There are no walk-up or drop-in services.

**Population Served**
Mesa residents experiencing homelessness, including families, seniors, survivors of domestic violence and other vulnerable residents identified through City/community referral channels.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Mesa Homeless Resource Line at 480-644-HOPE (4673) or email hope@mesaaz.gov. Do not send a client directly to the Sunaire property; ask about referral options and the most appropriate shelter pathway.

**Important Information to Know**
The old hotel-conversion lead is now best understood as part of Off the Streets. Construction at Sunaire was completed in April 2026, but access remains referral-only and capacity is not guaranteed.
resources.resolutionReason: The earlier delivery registered both a broad historical Off the Streets record and a Sunaire-era record. Preserve both permanent IDs and existing human state; use the broad programme for current city referral and ask an administrator to reconcile the site-era duplicate. No automatic registry migration or deletion. Reconcile with sr_a26416335c3d5c0487dafa0ee9427ee7.

resources.name: The Caritas Project - Legal Help for the Elderly Homeless / Post Eviction Liability Initiative
resources.description: Pro bono civil legal help for older people experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County.
resources.address: P.O. Box 7482, Phoenix, AZ 85011-7482 (mailing address)
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Civil legal assistance focused on older people experiencing homelessness, including legal barriers to rehousing, benefits and financial stability.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program focuses on Maricopa County’s older homeless population; contact it about the specific issue, age criteria and current case capacity.

**Population Served**
Older adults experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the referral form at thecaritasproject.org/contact/ or call 602-277-6446. The listed P.O. box is for mail, not walk-in visits.

**Important Information to Know**
A referral does not guarantee representation or a response before a court deadline. The post-eviction initiative describes developing legal strategies; it is not a promise to erase every housing debt.

resources.name: Home Builders Institute — BuildStrong Academy of Phoenix
resources.description: Tuition-free hands-on construction training, employability preparation and help connecting graduates with employers and apprenticeships.
resources.address: 3100 E. Broadway Rd., Suite 100, Phoenix, AZ 85040
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Tuition-free hands-on construction training, employability preparation and help connecting graduates with employers and apprenticeships.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Contact the academy about current enrollment, age and documentation requirements, attendance and available trades.

**Population Served**

People seeking an entry route into skilled construction work.

**How to Best Connect**

Use the Phoenix academy’s Become a Student route to discuss the next cohort before traveling to the training site.

**Important Information to Know**

Published training includes more than 300 hours, an HBI pre-apprenticeship certificate and OSHA 10-hour construction safety training. Completion does not guarantee a job or registered apprenticeship.

resources.name: DP Electric - DP University Electrical Apprenticeship
resources.description: DP University is DP Electric's employer-based, paid four-year NCCER-accredited electrical apprenticeship for DP Electric employees in Arizona and Texas, combining classroom instruction, paid field experience, wages and benefits.
resources.address: 2210 S. Roosevelt St., Tempe, AZ 85282
resources.hours: Apply through DP Electric careers; apprenticeship enrollment occurs after hire and has enrollment periods about every six months.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
DP University offers a four-year electrical apprenticeship with NCCER-accredited classroom instruction, hands-on field experience, safety and technical training, and a pathway toward journeyman-level electrician skills. DP Electric states the training costs employees nothing and participants earn wages and benefits from day one.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A person must first be hired by DP Electric. Experience requirements depend on the electrician levels DP Electric is hiring for at that time. After joining the team, employees wait for the next apprenticeship enrollment period, which DP Electric says happens every six months.

**Population Served**
People seeking an employer-based electrical construction career in Arizona or Texas, including Mesa-area applicants who can work for DP Electric and attend Tempe/company training.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the DP University page's Apply Now/careers route to review current DP Electric openings, or call the company at 480-338-2404. The Tempe office/training address submitted for this lead is 2210 S. Roosevelt St., Tempe.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not open-enrollment school. The client must be hired first, current job openings and apprentice slots vary, and enrollment timing is controlled by the employer.

resources.name: Banner - University Family Care/ACC - Medically Necessary Non-Emergency Transportation
resources.description: Banner - University Family Care/ACC arranges medically necessary non-emergency transportation for enrolled members to covered appointments through its Customer Care Center and plan transportation process.
resources.hours: Customer Care: Monday–Friday, 7:30 a.m.–5 p.m.; after-hours calls reach an answering service.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Non-emergency rides to the nearest appropriate AHCCCS-registered provider when an enrolled member cannot arrange a ride.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Banner – University Family Care/ACC members. In Maricopa County, pharmacy trips normally must be within 15 miles. Longer trips to specialty or compounding pharmacies require plan authorization; qualifying MSIC or IHS/638 pharmacy trips have a separate exception.

**Population Served**
Enrolled members in Mesa and the plan service area. This is a plan benefit, not transportation for every Banner patient. Other Banner insurance products have separate arrangements.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 800-582-8686, TTY 711, and select transportation at least 72 hours before the visit. Have the member ID, appointment details, pickup address and accessibility needs ready. Customer Care operates weekdays 7:30 a.m.–5 p.m.; calls afterward reach an answering service.

**Important Information to Know**
Same-day rides are not guaranteed. Request wheelchair or stretcher accommodation and explain companion or child-passenger needs; bring required child car seats. Cancel the ride if the appointment is canceled. Call the plan for weekend or holiday urgent-care transport. For an emergency, call 911.

resources.name: Community Bridges, Inc. - Arizona Bridge to Recovery / Mesa addiction treatment continuum
resources.description: Community Bridges provides a Mesa substance-use and behavioral-health treatment continuum, including Arizona Bridge to Recovery, EVARC inpatient, crisis-related screening, inpatient care, counseling, case management, peer support, and MAT services.
resources.hours: 24/7 Access to Care line available; site-specific admission timing should be confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Mesa inpatient and crisis-linked substance-use and behavioral-health care, including Arizona Bridge to Recovery, EVARC Inpatient, psychiatric/substance-use/medical services, counseling, case management, peer support, MAT services, and discharge planning.

**Eligibility Requirements**
CBI screens adults for the appropriate level of care. Inpatient admission requires referral through a CBI crisis clinic or another provider and depends on clinical fit and capacity. CBI describes AHCCCS, commercial insurance and other funding routes; confirm the person’s coverage and program. CBI lists funding contracts for uninsured or underinsured people; ask which options apply to the person and service.

**Population Served**
Mesa and Maricopa County adults needing substance-use, mental-health, withdrawal-management, or inpatient behavioral-health care.

**How to Best Connect**
Call CBI Access to Care at 877-931-9142, available 24/7, to determine the correct entry point. Appointment inquiries use 888-224-6593 or scheduling@cbridges.com. Arizona Bridge to Recovery is listed at 554 S Bellview, Room B; EVARC Inpatient is listed at 560 S Bellview. Confirm which program and location to use before traveling.

**Important Information to Know**
The recovery, crisis-screening and inpatient routes have different admission processes. Do not assume a Bellview address is a public walk-in inpatient admission point or that calling guarantees a bed.

resources.name: Terros Health - Maverick House
resources.description: Terros Health 29-bed male residential substance-use treatment center with counseling, personalized support plans, primary care, psychiatric services, laundry, family-style dining, and reintegration support.
resources.address: West Valley location; exact client address should be confirmed through Terros referrals
resources.hours: Residential program; referral timing and admission availability must be confirmed with Terros.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Maverick House is Terros Health's 29-bed male residential substance-use treatment center. It provides a supportive residential environment, expert counseling, personalized support plans, recovery skills, primary care, psychiatric services, laundry, family-style dining, and reintegration support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Men seeking residential substance-use treatment should be referred or screened through Terros. Clinical fit, payer requirements, and bed availability are not guaranteed by the public page.

**Population Served**
Men needing residential substance-use treatment in the Maricopa County/West Valley Terros service area.

**How to Best Connect**
Email MaverickReferrals@terroshealth.org for residential treatment referral. General Terros access is 602-685-6000.

**Important Information to Know**
The public page gives the administrative office address but not a client-facing residential address. Confirm the exact location, admission steps, cost/insurance, and current bed availability before referral.

resources.name: Mary's Mission & Developmental Center · MMDC Outpatient Clinic
resources.description: Mary's Mission & Developmental Center/MMDC Outpatient Clinic is a Mesa outpatient substance-use and behavioral-health lead in earlier programme listings, but current public identity, address, operating status and SUD intake could not be responsibly confirmed in the September 2026 review.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A historical lead for Mary’s Mission/MMDC outpatient substance-use and therapeutic services in Mesa. Current service scope needs confirmation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility, age range, referral requirements, payer rules, DUI/court linkage, youth versus adult services, current location and current outpatient SUD scope are unresolved.

**Population Served**
Current age criteria and intended outpatient population remain unresolved.

**How to Best Connect**
For administrator clarification, the provider’s historical program page lists 480-844-0011. First establish that this is still the correct MMDC contact, then confirm current services, location and intake before any referral.

**Important Information to Know**
This record is awaiting current provider and service confirmation. Conflicting historical addresses or an inaccessible webpage do not establish that the organization has closed.
resources.resolutionReason: Confirm current MMDC outpatient operation, clinic location, substance-use services, age eligibility and intake. Historical provider information does not resolve the conflicting Mesa addresses.

resources.name: City of Tempe — Orbit neighborhood circulators
resources.description: Six free neighborhood bus routes connect Tempe shopping, schools, community centers and regional transit.
resources.hours: Seven days a week; most routes run about every 15 minutes, or 30 minutes on Sundays. Check the route schedule.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Six free neighborhood bus routes connect Tempe shopping, schools, community centers and regional transit.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open to the public when the trip fits a route and schedule. No income test or transit-disability certification is required.

**Population Served**
People traveling in Tempe, including Mesa residents connecting to Tempe destinations. Orbit is not a door-to-door service.

**How to Best Connect**
Check the city’s Orbit route map and current Valley Metro schedule, or call 602-253-5000. In designated neighborhood flag zones, signal the driver at a safe boarding location.

**Important Information to Know**
Some extra Mars and Mercury buses make only short trips during ASU semesters. Check the destination sign if traveling beyond that shortened section. Regional bus or rail connections may require a separate fare.

resources.name: Assistory Outreach Services - Food Pantry / Free Food Assist Mesa
resources.description: Assistory Outreach Services has advertised first-come grocery events in Mesa, but current dates and a consistent schedule have not been confirmed.
resources.address: 7440 East Main Street, Suite 2A, Mesa, AZ
resources.hours: Needs administrator confirmation; visible Mesa event listings were past dates, with text saying monthly Saturday distribution.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Assistory Outreach Services describes Free Food Assist as accessible food for individuals and families experiencing food insecurity. Posted Mesa events offered a limited number of grocery bags that may include produce, eggs, milk, bread, protein, fruit, snacks, juice and water depending on supply.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Posted events were open to the public and first come, first served until supplies ran out. No income or document rules were listed on the visible event page.

**Population Served**
People and families experiencing food insecurity who can reach the Mesa pickup location when a current event is active.

**How to Best Connect**
Do not rely on the old event dates without checking. The posted Mesa pickup location is Maranatha Remnant Global Ministries, 7440 East Main Street, Suite 2A, Mesa. Use the website to look for updated events or administrator confirmation before referral.

**Important Information to Know**
The page visible on September 26, 2026 listed June and July 2026 Mesa events and stated that distributions would move to a monthly Saturday schedule, but it did not show a current September or future Mesa event. The current operating schedule is unresolved.
resources.resolutionReason: The official program page supports the organization, Mesa food-assist event model and address, but its visible event dates were past and the monthly schedule text conflicted with the submitted third-Saturday claim. Current Mesa distribution dates and contact route need administrator confirmation before referral.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Economic Security / ARIZONA@WORK - Reentry Employment Services
resources.description: Arizona DES and ARIZONA@WORK provide no-cost reentry workforce services for people in prison, on parole, or returning to the community, including job search, resume and interview help, job referrals, training, job coaching, veterans/disability support, and transportation or clothing help when available.
resources.address: Statewide DES/ARIZONA@WORK network; use local ARIZONA@WORK office locator for Mesa/Maricopa County access
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
DES and ARIZONA@WORK reentry workforce specialists help justice-involved job seekers prepare for work and find employment. Services include resume help, interview practice, job referrals, Arizona Job Connection help, workplace skills, technical training, job fairs, one-on-one coaching, follow-up after employment, specialized support for veterans and people with disabilities, and transportation or clothing help when available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public page describes people in prison, on parole, or returning to communities. Specific services depend on the person's status, local ARIZONA@WORK office, program funding, and workforce eligibility.

**Population Served**
Justice-involved job seekers statewide, including people returning to Mesa and Maricopa County from incarceration or supervision.

**How to Best Connect**
Email DERSReEntry@azdes.gov, use the employment-services questionnaire/office locator on the DES page, or ask a parole officer, Second Chance Center, reentry center or DES/ARIZONA@WORK office for a reentry employment specialist. Mesa community inquiries can start with the East Valley Career Center, 1001 W Southern Ave., Suite 101, at 602-372-9700.

**Important Information to Know**
Transportation/clothing support depends on eligibility and availability. DES statewide reentry employment services are distinct from Maricopa County Smart Justice, even when both connect through ARIZONA@WORK. This is employment support, not a housing or legal programme; older RED branding does not establish a separate current intake.

resources.name: The River Source - current identity/intake unresolved
resources.description: Needs-resolution lead for The River Source, an Arizona addiction-treatment provider historically associated with detox, residential and outpatient services; current official website and Mesa/Gilbert intake route are unresolved.
resources.address: 2325 W Guadalupe Rd, Suite 107, Gilbert, AZ 85233 (historical/directory outpatient address; current status unresolved); submitted Mesa address: 108 E 2nd Ave, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The submitted lead describes drug and alcohol detox, residential, outpatient and alumni programs. Older public directory evidence describes River Source Treatment Center outpatient services in the Gilbert/Mesa area.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility cannot be responsibly stated from current official evidence. Admission criteria, payment, current levels of care and whether the submitted Mesa address is operating need administrator resolution.

**Population Served**
Potentially people seeking substance-use treatment in the Mesa/Gilbert area, but the current served population is unresolved.

**How to Best Connect**
Do not refer a client until current identity and intake are resolved. The submitted phone was 866-294-9331 and older directory listings include 844-232-8338, but these should be verified before use.

**Important Information to Know**
The submitted official domain redirected to unrelated content during the 2026-09-26 check. This does not prove closure, but it creates a consequential current identity and access conflict.
