resources.name: Grad Solutions · Free Arizona Dropout Recovery High School Completion Program
resources.description: Grad Solutions is a free, fully online, accredited Arizona dropout recovery high school completion program for Arizona youth ages 16-21 who are withdrawn from high school and want a high school diploma rather than a GED.
resources.address: 1555 N. Fiesta Blvd., Gilbert, AZ 85233
resources.hours: Phone support Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:00 PM MST; courses are online and available 24/7.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free online high school diploma completion, 24/7 self-paced courses, tutoring, mentoring, student resources, transfer-credit review, work-hour elective credit, online proctored testing, graduation support, and Exceptional Student Services for students with IEPs or 504 plans.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Students must live in Arizona, be ages 16-21, and be withdrawn from high school. The program is for earning a high school diploma, not a GED.

**Population Served**
Arizona youth ages 16-21 who have left high school and need a flexible online diploma pathway, including students with work, family, disability, housing, or other barriers.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the online enrollment application on the admissions page, call 480-689-5999 Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:00 PM MST, or email info@studentswin.org. Spanish information is available through the site's Spanish option.

**Important Information to Know**
Students need a device and internet access for online coursework, though HUB locations may help with a device, internet, or study place. Adults older than 21 should be routed to adult diploma or GED options instead.

resources.name: Phoenix Office of Refugee and Immigrant Support — Resource Navigation
resources.description: City resource navigation connecting refugee and immigrant communities with employment assistance, career-training information and other community services.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
City resource navigation connecting refugee and immigrant communities with employment assistance, career-training information and other community services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Ask the office about the appropriate partner program, residency or immigration-status requirements and whether a Mesa resident can use the requested service. Each partner has its own rules.

**Population Served**
Refugees and immigrants seeking support connected with Phoenix services.

**How to Best Connect**
Email ORIS with a question about the service needed and current referral options.

**Important Information to Know**
ORIS coordinates referrals and does not promise legal representation or access to Phoenix-resident benefits. The page links a March 2025 employment event and a separate CNA-training announcement; neither establishes a current event or open cohort. Ask about current intake and whether a Mesa inquiry can be routed.

resources.name: Assistance in Healthcare Goodyear - Arizona Assistance in Healthcare
resources.description: Assistance in Healthcare Goodyear provides limited emergency financial support to cancer patients in active treatment in the Phoenix metro area, based on application information and available funds.
resources.address: P.O. Box 5157, Goodyear, AZ 85338
resources.hours: Paper application is available on the official assistance page; no public phone hours were found on the page.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency financial support for cancer patients undergoing active treatment in the Phoenix metro area. The official page provides paper applications and states assistance is based on application information and available funds.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicant must be a cancer patient in active treatment in the Phoenix metro area and must submit a complete application. Assistance is not guaranteed and maximum support limits apply.

**Population Served**
Cancer patients in active treatment in the Phoenix metropolitan area, including eligible Mesa and Maricopa County patients.

**How to Best Connect**
Download the paper application from the Assistance in Healthcare Goodyear assistance page and submit the complete application as directed. The mailing address listed is P.O. Box 5157, Goodyear, AZ 85338.

**Important Information to Know**
Financial assistance is not intended as monthly supplementation, and submitting an application does not ensure assistance. Public information did not establish a current phone number or real-time fund capacity.

resources.name: Ajo Transportation / Valley Metro - Rural Route 685 Ajo-Gila Bend-Phoenix
resources.description: Route 685 is a rural fixed-route bus connecting Ajo, Gila Bend, Buckeye and Phoenix, with limited weekday and Saturday service and fares published by Buckeye/Ajo Transportation.
resources.address: Ajo Transportation, 1248 N 2nd Ave, Ajo, AZ 85321
resources.hours: Buckeye page lists five trips Monday-Friday and two trips on Saturdays between Ajo/Gila Bend and Phoenix, plus short trips within Buckeye Monday-Friday; confirm current schedule before travel.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Route 685 provides rural bus service between Ajo/Gila Bend and Phoenix, with stops serving Buckeye and other West Valley communities and connections toward the Valley Metro system.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open public route. Reduced fares are available for riders with qualifying youth, senior, Medicare or disability eligibility and valid proof.

**Population Served**
People traveling along the Ajo, Gila Bend, Buckeye, Avondale, Goodyear, Tolleson and Phoenix corridor. It is not an interior Mesa neighborhood route.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Ajo Transportation at 520-387-6559 or 1-800-242-9483 for route, schedule, fare and flex-stop questions. For Buckeye transit questions, email transit@buckeyeaz.gov. Valley Metro customer service is 602-253-5000.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a niche reserve option for western-county or Ajo/Gila Bend travel, not a Mesa local bus or door-to-door social-service ride. Confirm the current day, time, stop and fare because service is limited.

resources.name: M.E.N.D. - East Valley Arizona Pregnancy and Infant Loss Support Group
resources.description: Faith-oriented East Valley peer support group for adults grieving miscarriage, stillbirth or infant death, with in-person Queen Creek meetings and M.E.N.D. online support options.
resources.address: Queen Creek Library, Edward Abbey Room, 21802 S. Ellsworth Rd., Queen Creek, AZ 85142
resources.hours: M.E.N.D. magazine listed East Valley Arizona meetings on the 2nd Thursday at 6:30 PM; confirm current meeting before attending.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
M.E.N.D. provides pregnancy and infant loss support groups for families who have lost a baby through miscarriage, stillbirth or infant death. The East Valley Arizona group meets in Queen Creek, and M.E.N.D. also offers online support groups including pregnancy after loss and men/fathers support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Moms, dads and adult family members grieving miscarriage, stillbirth or infant death may attend support groups. M.E.N.D. states groups are not professional counseling and children/babies generally do not attend support-group meetings.

**Population Served**
Adults and families in the East Valley, including Mesa families able to travel to Queen Creek, who are grieving pregnancy or infant loss or navigating pregnancy after loss.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact East Valley Arizona chapter contact Danielle Radler at danielle@mend.org or 602-699-6228 to confirm current meeting time and room before attending. The listed meeting location is Queen Creek Library, Edward Abbey Room.

**Important Information to Know**
M.E.N.D. is Christian/faith-oriented and peer-led, not clinical counseling. Use a licensed mental-health or crisis resource if the person needs urgent clinical support. Meeting details have changed over time, so confirm before travel from Mesa.

resources.name: Honora Healthcare Services - Day Treatment, Habilitation, Residential, Employment and Transportation Supports
resources.description: Honora Healthcare Services operates Mesa and Tempe disability supports including Day Treatment Adult, DTT/DTS, group supported employment, habilitation, residential and transportation-related supports.
resources.address: 3930 E. University Drive, Mesa, AZ 85205; 1805 E. Elliot Road, Suite 114, Tempe, AZ 85284
resources.hours: Call for current program hours, locations, intake and openings.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Day Treatment Adult program with sensory-motor, cognitive, communication, social interaction, behavioral, adaptive and community-participation skill development. The candidate also identifies DTT, DTS, GSE, habilitation, residential and transportation supports; verify the specific service line requested.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services appear intended for members with developmental disabilities or disability-related support needs. DDD authorization, program fit, location and current openings should be confirmed.

**Population Served**
People with disabilities in Mesa and Tempe needing day treatment, skill development, employment or related supports.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Mesa administrative office at 480-807-0018 or the after-hours number 602-330-3472. For the Tempe Debisi Center, call 480-656-5473 for DTA/GSE or 480-809-6779 for DTT/DTS.

**Important Information to Know**
The official page confirms current Mesa and Tempe contacts; third-party listings may show older addresses. Confirm the location, service line and authorization before referral.

resources.name: De Novo Law — family-law legal paraprofessional services
resources.description: Family-law services through legal paraprofessionals, including a free initial one-on-one consultation.
resources.address: 4140 E. Baseline Rd., Suite 101, Mesa, AZ 85206
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Family-law services through legal paraprofessionals, including a free initial one-on-one consultation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The matter must fit the practitioner’s licensed scope and be accepted by the firm. Further services are paid; obtain a fee quote.

**Population Served**
People with Arizona divorce or other family-law matters who can use Mesa-based services.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-725-2200 or request the initial consultation online. Confirm appointment arrangements before visiting.

**Important Information to Know**
Legal paraprofessionals are not attorneys and may act only within their licensed areas and scope. A free initial consultation does not make subsequent services free.

resources.name: City of Mesa Police Department - Mesa Family Advocacy Center
resources.description: The Mesa Family Advocacy Center is a multidisciplinary City of Mesa center coordinating victim advocacy, crisis intervention, protective-order assistance, safety planning, counseling referrals, forensic medical examination coordination and community-resource connections for victims of sexual and domestic violence and other crimes.
resources.address: 225 E. 1st St., Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Call for current service hours, referral and appointment instructions before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Crisis intervention, safety planning, criminal-justice advocacy, protective-order help, victims’ rights information, counseling referrals, forensic medical-exam coordination and community-resource connections. The center works with police, courts, medical partners, child-welfare investigators and prosecutors; violence-related shelter linkage and confidentiality/resource navigation may be available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services may depend on the crime, report, investigation, referral route or victim-service need. Call first to confirm whether the center can help with the specific Mesa domestic-violence situation.

**Population Served**
Victims of crime and their families in Mesa, including domestic-violence and sexual-violence survivors, adults, and children.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Mesa Police Victim Services at 480-644-4075 or the questions line at 480-644-4084 before going in person. For immediate danger call 911.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a victim advocacy and multi-agency support center, not a general homeless shelter or independent civil legal-aid firm. Confirm the needed service, appointment and entrance before travel to 225 E. 1st St. Counseling, shelter placements, examinations and attorney referrals have separate access and capacity rules.

resources.name: City of Mesa — Budget Payment Plan
resources.description: Spreads seasonal Mesa utility costs into more predictable monthly payments.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Spreads seasonal Mesa utility costs into more predictable monthly payments.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Have 12 consecutive months of utility bills at the residence and pay the account balance in full before enrollment. Gas-only customers enroll June 1–August 31; customers with combined services enroll November 1–January 31.

**Population Served**
Eligible City of Mesa utility customers planning for seasonal bill changes.

**How to Best Connect**
Review the Budget Payment Plan page or call the City contact center during the relevant enrollment period.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a discount or help with existing arrears. The budget amount may change after usage review. Payment arrangements are unavailable while enrolled, and a late payment can remove the account from the plan.

resources.name: NATIVE HEALTH · Rising Tide Recovery and Recovery Services
resources.description: NATIVE HEALTH offers individual and group substance-abuse and addictions treatment, court-ordered treatment, DUI education and Rising Tide Recovery IOP. Mesa is a NATIVE HEALTH site, while current public recovery-services schedules list IOP at Central Phoenix and NHW Community Health Center.
resources.hours: Recovery Services schedules vary. IOP listed at Central: Mon/Tue/Thu 4:00 PM-7:00 PM; NHW: Mon/Wed/Fri 3:00 PM-6:00 PM. Mesa general site hours should be confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Individual and group substance-abuse and addictions treatment, Rising Tide Recovery IOP, court-ordered treatment, probation and DCS-ordered treatment, substance-abuse group or individual counseling based on assessment, and DUI education services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Self-referred treatment is available. IOP requires 48 hours of sobriety and is an 8-week, 72-hour program. Recovery services are open to AHCCCS and self-pay clients. DUI education requires a court order and completed DUI screening, with a $50 intake fee and $25 per class listed.

**Population Served**
People seeking NATIVE HEALTH recovery services in the Phoenix/Mesa area, including self-referred clients and people with court, probation or DCS-ordered treatment. NATIVE HEALTH has Native American health-center roots; confirm language and culturally specific services at intake.

**How to Best Connect**
For recovery enrollment, call 602-513-2423 or email recoveryservices@nachci.com. The recovery page lists IOP at 4041 N Central Ave and 8800 N 22nd Ave in Phoenix; confirm the assigned site. For the Mesa office at 777 W Southern Ave, call 602-279-5262 to ask which recovery services are actually available there.

**Important Information to Know**
Do not assume IOP currently meets in Mesa; the official recovery page lists IOP at Central Phoenix and NHW Community Health Center. Confirm current Mesa addiction-service availability, insurance/self-pay costs, telehealth options and transportation before referral.

resources.name: Furnishing Dignity - Essential Home Furnishings
resources.description: Unresolved referral-based furniture and household-goods lead. Current provider identity, intake contact and Mesa service capacity require administrator verification.
resources.address: P.O. Box 51209, Phoenix, AZ 85076
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Available evidence describes essential furniture and household goods for qualifying individuals and families transitioning into permanent housing, generally through nonprofit partner referrals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Prior program material describes referral-based service for qualifying households. Current eligibility, referral partners, service area, and whether Mesa households can be served could not be responsibly confirmed from a current official provider page.

**Population Served**
The lead appears intended for low-income individuals and families recovering from homelessness, domestic violence, disability, disaster, foster-care transition, or another crisis.

**How to Best Connect**
Do not send a client directly until an administrator resolves the current identity and contact conflict. Candidate evidence lists 623-715-2155; older nonprofit records and a flyer list 480-340-3417 and info@furnishingdignity.org.

**Important Information to Know**
The previously submitted official website currently displayed unrelated casino content during live research. A donation-pickup page still listed Furnishing Dignity contact details, but that does not establish current client intake. This is a useful lead for administrator follow-up, not a ready referral.
resources.resolutionReason: Needs resolution because the official domain appeared compromised or no longer controlled by the provider, contact numbers conflict, and current client/referral intake could not be confirmed from an active official program page.

resources.name: Home Building Academy / HBI BuildStrong Academy of Phoenix
resources.description: Tuition-free training in electrical and framing skills for eligible Central Arizona adults, using HBI’s home-building curriculum, career preparation and job-placement assistance.
resources.address: 3100 E. Broadway Rd., Suite 100, Phoenix, AZ 85040
resources.hours: Enroll online or contact the academy for current cohorts, schedule and eligibility.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Nine weeks of hands-on training in home-building trades, currently electrical and framing, with career-readiness instruction, PACT/OSHA credentials and job-placement assistance.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The provider serves eligible Central Arizona participants ages 18 and older. Ask about documents, work authorization, attendance requirements and available cohorts.

**Population Served**
Adults ages 18 and over in Central Arizona/Greater Phoenix seeking an entry pathway into residential construction trades.

**How to Best Connect**
Use Enroll Today on the academy website, call 602-806-8000 or email phoenixacademy@hbi.org. Confirm the current course schedule and intake before traveling.

**Important Information to Know**
Tuition is free for accepted participants; tools, transportation and other costs should be confirmed. This record describes training in residential construction, not a housing program. Job placement is not guaranteed.

resources.name: AHCCCS — planning behavioral-health services for teens
resources.description: Guidance on transition to adult services, advocacy and potential grant-funded care.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Guidance on transition to adult services, advocacy and potential grant-funded care.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Transition policies commonly cover ages 14–21; each program has its own criteria. Mental Health Block Grant support described for children through 18 requires serious emotional disturbance and inadequate insurance.

**Population Served**
Youth approaching adulthood and their families.

**How to Best Connect**
Discuss a transition plan with the current care team. For unresolved access issues contact the Clinical Resolution Unit at 800-867-5808 or 602-364-4558; advocacy questions can go to OIFA@azahcccs.gov.

**Important Information to Know**
Grant availability and clinical eligibility must be checked; this information pathway is not an application approval.

resources.name: A New Leaf - Autumn House Domestic Violence Transitional Housing
resources.description: A New Leaf's Autumn House provides confidential East Valley transitional housing and support for domestic-violence survivors of any gender, including safety planning, employment and transportation help, counseling connections, court advocacy, transition support and pet-friendly accommodations.
resources.phone: A New Leaf DV hotline 480-890-3039; public office 480-969-4024
resources.address: Confidential East Valley location; arrange access by phone.
resources.hours: Call the domestic-violence hotline; do not go to a confidential location. Hotline access is the supported route for current screening and placement.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Autumn House offers confidential domestic-violence transitional housing, safety support, employment connections, transportation help, counseling connections, court advocacy, move-out support and pet-friendly accommodation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For survivors fleeing or affected by domestic violence, regardless of gender, who are screened by A New Leaf for program fit and available placement. Housing is not guaranteed.

**Population Served**
Domestic-violence survivors in the East Valley and Maricopa County, including survivors with pets and survivors of any gender.

**How to Best Connect**
Call A New Leaf’s domestic-violence hotline at 480-890-3039 or public office at 480-969-4024 for current screening and placement guidance. Do not travel to a confidential shelter location or treat the administrative office as shelter intake.

**Important Information to Know**
Autumn House now operates as transitional housing rather than a public walk-in emergency shelter. Confirm openings, safety planning, transportation, pet arrangements and length of stay through hotline intake.

resources.name: Residential Grass-to-Xeriscape and Tree Bonus Incentive Program
resources.description: Mesa's Residential Grass-to-Xeriscape and Tree Bonus Incentive Program offers up to $2,100 for eligible City of Mesa water customers who own single-family homes and convert living grass to approved low-water-use landscaping.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The program offers incentives up to $2,100 for future grass removal and low-water-use xeriscape conversion, including a tree bonus for up to two eligible trees. The goal is to reduce landscape water use and ongoing water costs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The applicant must be the current owner of a single-family home and a Mesa water customer. Projects must be future conversions, not already completed work. The property must have eligible living grass, usually at least 500 square feet with 70% healthy coverage, and Mesa must complete a pre-inspection and issue approval before work begins. Funding is limited and first-come, first-served.

**Population Served**
City of Mesa water customers who own single-family homes with eligible grass conversion projects.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact Mesa water conservation at 480-644-3306 or conservation.info@mesaaz.gov before starting any work. Use the city program page to review requirements and application materials.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not arrears, shutoff, or emergency water-bill help. Work started before approval is not eligible. A W-9 is required after project completion and final approval, and a 1099 may be issued. HOA or historic district rules may also apply.

resources.name: Touchstone Health Services
resources.description: Maricopa County youth and young-adult behavioral-health provider serving birth through age 25 and families, with outpatient therapy, psychiatry, care coordination, school/community services, prevention, and support for concerns including substance use.
resources.address: 15820 N 35th Ave, Suite 14, Phoenix, AZ 85053
resources.hours: Referral response after enrollment interest form is described as within 1-2 business days; service schedules vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Touchstone Health Services provides trauma-informed, family-focused behavioral-health services for youth, young adults, and families, including outpatient therapy, psychiatry, care coordination, prevention, school partnerships, community/home/telehealth services, and support for concerns including substance use, anxiety, depression, trauma, ADHD, emotional regulation, and suicidal ideation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Touchstone focuses on children from birth to 18, transition-age youth 18–25 and their families, primarily in Maricopa County. Families can self-refer; partner schools/community providers have referral routes too. Intake reviews youth participation, identity/custody documents and insurance or payment. Ask which requirements apply to the individual referral.

**Population Served**
Youth, young adults up to age 25, and families in Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Parents or guardians can call 866-207-3882 or complete the enrollment interest form. Touchstone states a representative will contact the family within 1-2 business days to review insurance/payment, answer questions, and schedule an initial intake. School and community partners have separate referral links.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm whether the Mesa school is a current partner and the available home, office, school or telehealth setting. School partnership is not required for every self-referring family. This is youth/family behavioral-health care that can address substance use, not a standalone adult detox or residential addiction programme. Use crisis/emergency services for immediate safety concerns.

resources.name: The Stone Community Health Center - Integrated Primary Care and Reentry Support
resources.description: The Stone Community Health Center is a Mesa integrated health center offering primary care, preventive services, chronic-disease management, behavioral health, IOP/substance-use treatment, court-ordered programs, reentry support, and case management.
resources.address: 423 N Country Club Drive, Suite 45, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-4:30 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Primary care, preventive services, chronic-disease management, mental health counseling, substance-abuse treatment, IOP programs, court-ordered programs, reentry support, community integration, and case management.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page says care is intended to be accessible regardless of background, income, or circumstance. It lists Aetna, Blue Cross Blue Shield, Cigna, and Medicare as major insurance providers, but AHCCCS, uninsured fees, and charity/sliding-fee details are not clearly published.

**Population Served**
Mesa, Tempe, Phoenix, and surrounding Arizona communities, including people needing integrated medical and behavioral-health care and justice-involved clients needing reentry support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-659-6359, email info@thestonecommunity.com, or use the appointment/referral route on the website. The clinic is at 423 N Country Club Drive, Suite 45, Mesa, AZ 85201.

**Important Information to Know**
Affordability for uninsured patients is not fully clear on the public page. Confirm payer options, fees, AHCCCS acceptance, and whether the requested primary-care service is available before referral.

resources.name: Luke 15 Outreach Ministry - Food and Water Outreach
resources.description: Luke 15 Outreach Ministry distributes ready-to-eat food, drinks and hygiene items to people who are poor, hungry or experiencing homelessness in the community.
resources.address: 6344 E Brown Rd, Ste 104, Mesa, AZ 85205
resources.hours: Distribution schedule is not posted on the opened official page; call before sending a client.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Street/community outreach with ready-to-eat food, drinks and hygiene items. The ministry also describes helping people connect to shelters, detox, recovery homes, family or safe places.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page does not publish formal income, document, residence or schedule requirements. Call to confirm current food box or outreach access.

**Population Served**
People who are poor, hungry, homeless or otherwise struggling in the community, with Mesa relevance from the submitted address and phone.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-389-5855 or email info@luke1517.com to ask where and when food, water or food boxes are currently available. Do not send someone to an address without confirming current distribution.

**Important Information to Know**
The official page supports food/water outreach but not a public pantry schedule. Treat food boxes and documentation expectations as call-ahead questions.

resources.name: Phoenix Electrical Joint Apprenticeship and Training Committee Electrical Apprenticeship
resources.description: Phoenix Electrical Joint Apprenticeship and Training Committee accepts online applications for the Inside Wireman electrical apprenticeship, a competitive registered apprenticeship pathway with prerequisites, document requirements and a non-refundable application fee.
resources.address: 4016 N Black Canyon Hwy, Phoenix, AZ 85017; 1520 E Indianola Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.hours: Office hours Monday-Friday 7:00 AM-4:00 PM, closed for lunch 11:30 AM-12:30 PM. Current application deadline shown: March 15, 2027 at 4:00 PM for Fall 2027.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Electrical apprenticeship application portal for the Phoenix Electrical JATC Inside Wireman apprenticeship. Applicants create a TradeSchool account, apply online, complete a Personal Experience Form and are evaluated for a limited number of apprenticeship spots.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be at least 18 by program start, provide state photo ID, high school diploma or GED, transcripts showing algebra requirements or complete the NJATC Tech Math course, and be able to meet physical, instruction and job-site travel requirements. Prior electrical experience or qualifying veteran service may waive some school/math requirements.

**Population Served**
Greater Phoenix and Maricopa County applicants pursuing the electrical trade, including Mesa-area job seekers who can travel to training and job sites within the program jurisdiction.

**How to Best Connect**
Create a TradeSchool account from the PEJATC How to Apply page and follow the Inside Wireman application instructions. For computer access or document upload problems, email webservices@pejatc.org.

**Important Information to Know**
The page says this is an application process, not registration, and the program receives more applicants than available spots. There is a $40 non-refundable application fee. Selection is not guaranteed.

resources.name: Tempe Community Action Agency - Neighbors Helping Neighbors Transportation
resources.description: Tempe Community Action Agency's Neighbors Helping Neighbors program connects Tempe seniors with volunteers for practical support such as grocery shopping, prescription pickup, transportation, pet care, and friendly calls.
resources.address: 2146 E. Apache Blvd., Tempe, AZ 85281
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Volunteer support for older adults, including grocery shopping, picking up prescriptions, transportation, pet care, friendly phone calls, and other everyday needs that help seniors remain independent at home.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The person must be a senior in Tempe and must contact the Neighbors Helping Neighbors Service Line to check eligibility and availability.

**Population Served**
Seniors in Tempe.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Neighbors Helping Neighbors Service Line at 480-389-1444 to check eligibility and availability. TCAA's services site is 2146 E. Apache Blvd., Tempe, AZ 85281.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a Mesa program. Use it only for Tempe seniors or when a Resource Specialist confirms cross-boundary eligibility. Volunteer availability may vary.

resources.name: Arizona State University Counselor Training Center
resources.description: ASU Counselor Training Center provides confidential weekly counseling at no cost for ASU students and very low cost for community members, through advanced supervised graduate clinicians, plus affordable ADHD, learning-disorder and autism assessments at the Polytechnic location.
resources.address: Tempe campus for counseling; assessments also offered at ASU Polytechnic in Mesa
resources.hours: Services follow academic semester schedules and counselor-in-training availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Confidential weekly counseling through advanced graduate students under supervision, in-person appointments on the Tempe campus, telehealth appointments, and affordable assessments for ADHD, learning disorders and autism spectrum disorder at the Polytechnic location.

**Eligibility Requirements**
ASU students, faculty, staff and members of the broader community may inquire. Services are provided as part of graduate clinical training, are offered by semester and depend on counselor-in-training capacity. Assessment fit and current fees should be confirmed before referral.

**Population Served**
ASU students and community members in Arizona, including Mesa residents able to use Tempe in-person care, telehealth or Polytechnic assessments.

**How to Best Connect**
Request an appointment by emailing the Counselor Training Center through the website's posted email link or by calling 480-965-5067.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a training clinic and not emergency care. Care follows ASU academic schedules, which can affect openings and continuity. Ask about telehealth requirements, semester timing, fees and assessment waitlists.

resources.name: Jewish Family & Children's Service - Older Adults Services / Senior Concierge
resources.description: Jewish Family & Children's Service provides older-adult enrichment, in-home counseling, case management, advocacy, behavioral-health services for eligible adults 55 and older, and Senior Concierge referrals to resources such as education, socialization and transportation.
resources.address: 4747 N. 7th St., Suite 100, Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.hours: Call for current intake, class and referral availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
JFCS Older Adults Services include senior enrichment and Creative Aging classes, online classes and events, in-home counseling, case management, advocacy, resource navigation, behavioral-health services for eligible adults 55 and older, and Senior Concierge referrals to resources such as education, socialization and transportation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Senior enrichment and Creative Aging are designed for adults 60 and older. Creative Aging serves Maricopa County residents, with many classes in Scottsdale. Behavioral-health services have separate rules: age 55 and older and enrollment in AHCCCS or Arizona Long Term Care. Ask which in-home or community service is available for the person’s Mesa address.

**Population Served**
Older adults in Maricopa County and their family members or caregivers, with some online enrichment options that can be accessed remotely.

**How to Best Connect**
For in-home services, call 602-762-7319. For Senior Concierge resource referrals, call 480-721-8619. General JFCS phone is 602-256-0528.

**Important Information to Know**
JFCS is faith-rooted but states it serves people regardless of faith or background. Some services have payer, age or location limits, and enrichment classes are not clinical care or custodial in-home care.

resources.name: Arizona Recovery Housing Association — Certified Home Search
resources.description: A public search route for Arizona recovery homes, with information about certification and housing standards.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

A public search route for Arizona recovery homes, with information about certification and housing standards.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Anyone can search. Each home sets admission rules, rent, population served and other conditions.

**Population Served**

People seeking sober or recovery housing and helpers comparing options across Arizona.

**How to Best Connect**

Use the home search to identify an operator, then ask that operator about the specific house’s current certification, vacancies, costs, rules and access to treatment or transportation.

**Important Information to Know**

Association membership and certification of an individual home are different. A directory entry is not a placement guarantee, clinical treatment license or confirmation of an available bed.

resources.name: United Cerebral Palsy of Central Arizona - Early Intervention services
resources.description: United Cerebral Palsy of Central Arizona participates in Arizona Early Intervention Program services for children birth to three with delays or disabilities in northern and central Maricopa County.
resources.address: 1802 W. Parkside Lane, Phoenix, AZ 85027
resources.hours: Call UCP for current early-intervention referral details; general UCP campus hours vary by program.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provider-delivered early intervention team services for children birth to three with delays or disabilities, including occupational therapy, physical therapy, speech-language support, developmental specialists and support coordination using family coaching in home/community settings.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Early intervention is for infants and toddlers birth to age three with qualifying developmental delays or disabilities. AzEIP referral/eligibility and service-region assignment apply.

**Population Served**
Young children birth to three with delays or disabilities and their families in UCP's northern and central Maricopa County early-intervention territory.

**How to Best Connect**
Call UCP of Central Arizona at 602-943-5472 and ask about early intervention or AzEIP service area fit. Families may also use the statewide AzEIP central referral pathway if unsure which provider serves their ZIP code.

**Important Information to Know**
The UCP page describes northern and central Maricopa County service travel. Mesa may or may not be inside UCP's current AzEIP assigned territory, so confirm ZIP-code assignment before treating UCP as the serving provider.

resources.name: SAAVI Services for the Blind — Ability Builds Confidence classes
resources.description: SAAVI Services for the Blind offers free Ability Builds Confidence classes and nonvisual-skills orientation for people new to vision loss, families and others wanting to learn blindness skills and resources.
resources.address: 2920 N. 7th St., Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.hours: Ability Builds Confidence classes are held in person Tuesdays 10:00 AM-noon in Phoenix and Tucson except holidays; some marked classes may be virtual for registered participants.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Ability Builds Confidence classes covering cane skills, home and kitchen adaptations, accessible technology, Braille, vocational rehabilitation, Social Security disability benefits, myths about blindness, support networks, training options and practical tools for adapting to vision loss.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The free ABC program is for people new to vision loss or wanting to learn about the blindness community. SAAVI states attendees do not need to be blind or low vision to participate. Other SAAVI programs may have separate referral, age or rehabilitation rules.

**Population Served**
People with blindness or vision loss, families, caregivers and community members in Arizona, including Mesa residents who can attend the Phoenix training center or eligible virtual classes.

**How to Best Connect**
Register online or call the Phoenix location at 602-795-0195. Register once to attend all ABC classes and ask about transportation, class topics, virtual availability, childcare, English interpretation and other requested assistance.

**Important Information to Know**
ABC is free and tools are available during class at no additional cost, but most classes are in person. Some classes may be virtual for registered participants, and assistance requests should be made at least two days before class.

resources.name: St. Mary's Food Bank Skills Center - Community Kitchen
resources.description: St. Mary's Food Bank Skills Center Community Kitchen is a no-cost 9-week food-service training pathway for adults with barriers to employment, with application, Wednesday information session, interview and job-readiness requirements.
resources.address: 3003 W. Thomas Rd., Phoenix, AZ 85017; information session behind WIC
resources.hours: Information session: Wednesday at 10 AM, about one hour. Training: Monday–Friday, 7 AM–3 PM; confirm the next cohort.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Community Kitchen is a 9-week food-service training program for adults with employment barriers. It prepares students for dishwasher, prep or line cook work and may include ServSafe Food Handler or Food Protection Manager certification.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be at least 18, authorized to work in the U.S., face a barrier to employment and be ready for full-time training and subsequent work. The program requires a background check, an initial drug test and random tests during training; it excludes people with arson histories or registered sex-offender status. Applicants must live in a shelter, their own or rented housing, or a halfway house. Ask staff about individual eligibility.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County adults with employment barriers who can attend training at the Phoenix Skills Center.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online, drop off an application at St. Mary’s Food Bank, fax it to 480-780-3799 or apply through an agency partner. Call 602-343-3183 for help. The agency portal lists a Wednesday 10 a.m. information session at 3003 W. Thomas Rd., behind WIC; confirm the session and next cohort. Admission includes an interview.

**Important Information to Know**
Community Kitchen is tuition-free for accepted participants and runs nine weeks, Monday–Friday, 7 a.m.–3 p.m. Seats, certification and employment are not guaranteed. Housing is not provided. Confirm travel arrangements and readiness for the full schedule.

resources.name: Adecco Staffing - Central Phoenix/East Valley Temporary Staffing
resources.description: Adecco Staffing's Tempe office provides temporary staffing and recruitment access for the Central Phoenix/East Valley market, with job-search links for current openings and a staffed local office.
resources.address: 1600 W. Broadway Rd., Suite 350, Tempe, AZ 85282
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Adecco provides temporary staffing, permanent recruitment, onsite management, and job-seeker access to current openings through its local Tempe branch and online job search.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on the specific job order. Applicants should expect employer-specific screening, documentation, shift, transportation, background, and skill requirements.

**Population Served**
Job seekers in the Tempe, Mesa, Central Phoenix, and East Valley labor market who are looking for temporary, contract, or direct-hire placements.

**How to Best Connect**
Search and apply online through Adecco's job seeker links or call the Tempe branch at 480-831-1131. The office is open Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM at 1600 W. Broadway Rd., Suite 350, Tempe.

**Important Information to Know**
Individual postings are time-limited. Adecco warns that it does not ask for payment during recruiting; verify recruiter emails and do not pay fees to get a job.

resources.name: Chicanos Por La Causa · Centro Esperanza / Corazon SUD services
resources.description: CPLC behavioral-health and substance-use services including Centro Esperanza Mesa integrated SUD/mental-health outpatient treatment for adults and Corazon Phoenix residential substance-use treatment.
resources.address: 325 N Stapley Dr, Mesa, AZ 85203
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Chicanos Por La Causa provides behavioral-health and substance-use services. Official pages support Centro Esperanza in Mesa as CARF-accredited for outpatient integrated SUD/mental-health treatment for adults. CPLC Corazon in Phoenix provides residential adult substance-use treatment with group, individual, family, and couples therapy, nightly 12-step support groups, and treatment for people on MAT such as methadone or Suboxone. CPLC also lists outpatient substance-abuse services at Centro de la Familia in Maryvale.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adults seeking integrated outpatient SUD/mental-health care at Centro Esperanza or residential SUD treatment at Corazon. Eligibility, funding, SMI requirements, SABG/MHBG access, and current openings must be confirmed with the specific site.

**Population Served**
Adults in Mesa and Maricopa County, including Spanish-speaking clients and clients seeking culturally responsive care. Official pages state services are available in English and Spanish on site and interpretation is available for other languages.

**How to Best Connect**
For Mesa Centro Esperanza, call 480-615-3800 or go to 325 N Stapley Dr, Mesa, AZ 85203. For Corazon residential SUD treatment, call 602-233-9747; official substance-abuse page lists 3639 W Lincoln St, Phoenix, AZ 85009, while the Arizona region page lists a different W Van Buren address, so confirm the current Corazon address before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
Centro Esperanza outpatient care in Mesa and Corazon residential treatment in Phoenix have different intake and location rules. Corazon’s published addresses differ, so call its intake number to confirm the current site before traveling. Do not assume the Mesa office supplies residential treatment.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Economic Security - Nutrition Assistance (SNAP / NA) and Health-e-Arizona Plus
resources.description: Arizona DES Nutrition Assistance is the state's SNAP grocery-benefit program, with online, phone, mail, fax, in-person and community-assistor application routes.
resources.hours: Phone interviews: Monday-Friday 7:00 AM-3:00 PM, excluding holidays. DES offices: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM, excluding holidays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Nutrition Assistance provides monthly grocery benefits through Arizona's SNAP program for households that qualify. DES also offers emergency processing for qualifying urgent situations.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility is based on household circumstances, income and required verification. Applicants must complete an eligibility interview and provide requested documentation. DES notes that some requirements may be waived or adjusted when they are difficult or dangerous for domestic violence, sexual harassment, sexual assault or stalking survivors. Ask about student-specific eligibility rules and allowable medical expenses for household members age 60 or older.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents, including Mesa and Maricopa County households, who meet Nutrition Assistance rules.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through Health-e-Arizona Plus, mail or fax an application, request a mailed application at 1-855-432-7587, visit a DES office if virtual access is not available, or work with a community assistor. Phone interviews can be completed at 1-855-432-7587.

**Important Information to Know**
Applying does not guarantee approval. DES lists eligibility interviews by phone Monday-Friday 7:00 AM-3:00 PM and in person at DES offices Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM. Be ready with income information, ID, Social Security numbers and citizenship verification if applicable.

resources.name: Clarvida Arizona — Supported Employment and Housing
resources.description: Community-based supported employment and housing services for people receiving behavioral-health support, including help finding and keeping meaningful work.
resources.address: Tempe office: 2131 E. Broadway Rd., Suite 14, Tempe, AZ 85282
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Community-based supported employment and housing services for people receiving behavioral-health support, including help finding and keeping meaningful work.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Services depend on intake assessment, program eligibility, coverage and referral or funding requirements. Ask specifically about the supported-employment or supported-housing program.

**Population Served**

People with mental-health needs in the provider’s Arizona service areas, including Tempe.

**How to Best Connect**

Call the Arizona office or Tempe office and ask for the appropriate program’s intake contact. Confirm whether a Mesa resident can receive services locally.

**Important Information to Know**

Supported housing does not mean an immediate apartment or shelter bed. Confirm program access, appointment site, costs and authorization before referral.

resources.name: findhelp — Local food and social-service search
resources.description: Offers a ZIP-code search for food assistance and other free or reduced-cost services.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Offers a ZIP-code search for food assistance and other free or reduced-cost services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The directory is publicly searchable; each listed program determines its own eligibility and intake.

**Population Served**
People searching for support in Mesa, Maricopa County or another U.S. community.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the website to search the relevant ZIP code and food need, then follow the individual provider’s contact instructions.

**Important Information to Know**
Listing details are leads to confirm directly. A search result does not establish current capacity or approval; the site itself does not distribute food.

resources.name: Maricopa County Correctional Health Services · Jail-based Medication Assisted Treatment and SBIRT
resources.description: Maricopa County Correctional Health Services provides jail-based opioid treatment, continuity methadone, MAT through drug-court collaboration, counseling, discharge planning, withdrawal monitoring and SBIRT screening for people in county jails.
resources.hours: Available only through Maricopa County jail/court processes; family or providers should use county/jail communication routes.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Jail-based medication-assisted treatment, Opioid Treatment Program certification across six jails, continuity methadone for people enrolled before arrest, methadone for pregnant opioid-dependent patients, MAT collaboration with drug courts, mental-health counseling, discharge planning, withdrawal monitoring, SBIRT screening, brief intervention and referral to community treatment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Only for people in Maricopa County jails or connected through court/jail processes. Continuity methadone is for people already enrolled before arrest, while some MAT may be initiated in custody through drug-court collaboration or CHS criteria.

**Population Served**
People incarcerated in Maricopa County jails, including people with opioid dependence, pregnant opioid-dependent patients, and people with substance-use or mental-health needs preparing for release.

**How to Best Connect**
This is accessed through jail medical/Correctional Health Services, court, drug court or release-planning processes. Families or outside providers should communicate medication and treatment information through approved jail/CHS channels. The county main line is 602-506-3011.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a community walk-in treatment provider. It is important for continuity of care and release planning, but outside missionaries cannot enroll a client unless the person is in the relevant jail/court process.

resources.name: Guadalupe Community Action Program - Housing, Utility Assistance, HEAF and URRD
resources.description: Town of Guadalupe CAP routes Guadalupe residents to rental, mortgage and utility assistance and offers HEAF-funded Southwest Gas and utility repair/replacement/deposit assistance.
resources.address: 9241 S Avenida Del Yaqui, Guadalupe, AZ 85283
resources.hours: Contact the CAP office for current application hours and funding status.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Housing and utility assistance routing for Guadalupe residents, including Maricopa County rental, mortgage and utility assistance for water, power and gas. Guadalupe HEAF includes Southwest Gas current/past-due charges and deposits plus Utility Repair Replacement and Deposit assistance for utility deposits and utility-related appliances or systems.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The page serves Guadalupe residents. Southwest Gas HEAF help requires income at or below 200% of current federal poverty guidelines and customer-of-record or accepted name-proxy status. URRD requires income at or below 200% FPL, ownership of the appliance/system, U.S. citizen or legal-resident status for the primary applicant, a complete documented application and qualified inspection for the proposed repair or replacement.

**Population Served**
Town of Guadalupe residents needing rental, mortgage, water, power, gas, deposit or utility-related repair assistance.

**How to Best Connect**
Call CAP at 480-505-5363 or the Town main number at 480-730-3080. Ask about submitting HEAF/URRD documents at the CAP office or to lnunez@guadalupeaz.org or McOrdova-paredes@guadalupeaz.org. The county Client Portal handles other rental, mortgage and utility assistance routes. Confirm the correct application for the need.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a Mesa program. Southwest Gas assistance is listed up to $400 once in a 12-month period; URRD is listed up to $4,500 once in a 12-month period. Funding, documents and provider coverage should be confirmed before referral.

resources.name: New Eyes eyeglass e-voucher program
resources.description: New Eyes provides a national online e-voucher for a basic pair of prescription eyeglasses for financially eligible people in the United States who already have a current glasses prescription.
resources.address: PO Box 332, 830 Morris Tpke, Suite 401, Short Hills, NJ 07078
resources.hours: Online application; no public phone confirmed. Email questions to info@new-eyes.org.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A basic pair of eyeglasses with clear single-vision or lined bifocal lenses through an emailed e-voucher. Optional lens upgrades may be available for discounted out-of-pocket fees.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be low-income individuals in the United States and must have an eyeglasses prescription dated within the last 24 months, including pupillary distance measurement. Applications are online; it is optimal for a social service agency or health advocate to apply, but individuals without agency access may apply directly with proof of eligibility.

**Population Served**
Financially eligible people in the United States, including Arizona residents, who already have a valid eyeglass prescription.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through the New Eyes application page. For questions, email info@new-eyes.org.

**Important Information to Know**
New Eyes does not pay for the eye exam. Each application has a non-refundable administrative application fee. If approved, the e-voucher is emailed with instructions for ordering glasses online.

resources.name: Catholic Charities Community Services Arizona - My Sister's Place Domestic Violence Shelter
resources.description: My Sister's Place is a confidential East Valley domestic-violence shelter operated by Catholic Charities, offering free shelter, 24-hour staffing, case management, safety and stability planning, food, counseling encouragement, documentation help, school and benefits connections and referrals.
resources.address: Confidential East Valley/Chandler shelter location; Catholic Charities administrative address: 5151 N. 19th Avenue, Phoenix, AZ 85015
resources.hours: 24-hour hotline and 24-hour staffed shelter.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
My Sister's Place provides confidential domestic-violence shelter in the East Valley with free services, food and kitchen access, 24-hour staffing, weekly case management, safety and stability planning, documentation and ID help, school enrollment help, employment or resume support, state-assistance connection and counseling encouragement for adults and children.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For individuals and families fleeing domestic violence. Shelter entry depends on hotline screening, safety needs, available space and program fit.

**Population Served**
Domestic-violence survivors in the East Valley and Maricopa County, including individuals, families, adults with children and men as reflected in Catholic Charities and CPLC shelter-list materials. Telecommunications relay is available by dialing 7-1-1.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the My Sister's Place 24-hour hotline at 480-821-1024. Do not go to or publish a shelter address; the location is confidential. Ask about available language assistance when arranging shelter intake.

**Important Information to Know**
All services at My Sister's Place are described as free for clients. CPLC's current shelter list identifies My Sister's Place as serving singles and families and service animals only; ask Catholic Charities to confirm current animal accommodations and space availability.

resources.name: Women's Health Innovations of Arizona - Maternal Mental Health Counseling and Family Therapy
resources.description: Women's Health Innovations of Arizona provides specialized maternal mental-health counseling and family therapy for pregnancy, postpartum, parenting, PMADs, grief, trauma, teen-parent concerns and early-childhood wellness, with in-office and telehealth options.
resources.address: Gilbert: 1355 S. Higley Rd. #113, Gilbert, AZ 85296; Tempe: 9280 S. Kyrene Rd. #119, Tempe, AZ 85284; telehealth available
resources.hours: Use the consultation form, call or email for scheduling; public office hours were not listed. In-office and telehealth options are listed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
WHI provides counseling across the lifespan with specialized expertise in maternal mental health, children, teens and trauma. Services include PMAD support for postpartum depression, anxiety, OCD, PTSD and related concerns; parenting support; couples/family involvement; support groups; psychiatry; healthy family home visits; trauma therapy; grief counseling; teen parent support; child counseling; and early childhood wellness support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Clients seeking perinatal, parenting, child, teen, family, grief or trauma counseling can request consultation. Insurance and self-pay options vary; an initial intake/screening fee and hourly rates are listed, and AHCCCS plans and several commercial plans are listed as accepted.

**Population Served**
Pregnant and postpartum people, women, parents, partners, families, children, teens and teen parents in Arizona, with Gilbert and Tempe locations and telehealth.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-339-7119, email intake@whiarizona.com or use the online consultation form. Locations are in Gilbert and Tempe; telehealth is listed for therapy options.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a mental-health counseling provider, not emergency crisis care. The website instructs people experiencing a mental-health crisis to dial 911. Fees, insurance participation and appointment availability should be confirmed at intake.

resources.name: Maricopa County Human Services Department · Workforce 2 You accelerated job training
resources.description: Maricopa County Workforce 2 You is a no-cost accelerated training initiative for targeted Maricopa County communities and barrier-impacted workers, with WDD career centers available for Mesa residents to ask about current cohorts, training funds, and related county workforce services.
resources.address: East Valley Career Center, 1001 W. Southern Ave., Suite 101, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost accelerated job training cohorts leading to industry-recognized credentials, plus county workforce routing to adult, dislocated worker, youth, apprenticeship, and training services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The 2026 Workforce 2 You expansion names Guadalupe, Surprise, and Buckeye cohorts and targets veteran, low-income, dislocated, and other workers most in need of vocational support. Mesa residents should ask Maricopa County Workforce Development whether a current cohort, WIOA training service, or related county option is available to them.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County job seekers with barriers to employment, including veterans, low-income workers, dislocated workers, and residents of underserved communities.

**How to Best Connect**
Start with Maricopa County Workforce Development at 602-506-0589 or the East Valley Career Center in Mesa at 602-372-9700. Ask specifically about Workforce 2 You, current cohorts, training funds, and whether Mesa residents can use a county alternative if cohorts are location-limited.

**Important Information to Know**
Current public announcements do not name Mesa as a 2026 Workforce 2 You cohort site. This is still a useful county workforce lead, but staff should confirm current cohort geography, funding, schedule, transportation support, and application steps before presenting it as an open Mesa training seat.

resources.name: Mesa Youth Creative Agency — Teen Design Jobs
resources.description: Paid creative work and mentoring in design, painting, photo/video and related projects for selected Mesa high-school students.
resources.address: Historic Irving, 155 N. Center St., Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Published teen schedule: Monday, Tuesday and Thursday 4–6 PM; Wednesday 2–6 PM during the school year.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Paid creative work and mentoring in design, painting, photo/video and related projects for selected Mesa high-school students.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Applicants must be at least 14, enrolled in a Mesa Public Schools high school and Mesa residents. They must provide their own transportation and attend the published after-school schedule.

**Population Served**

Mesa high-school teens interested in creative careers.

**How to Best Connect**

Contact the agency or monitor its Teen Jobs page for future openings. Prepare creative work samples and a résumé when applying.

**Important Information to Know**

The page currently says openings are closed. This is a future opportunity to monitor, not an available job. The teen schedule differs from office hours; confirm current terms when hiring reopens.

resources.name: University of Arizona - NOPAL harm-reduction outreach
resources.description: The University of Arizona NOPAL Initiative provides low-barrier naloxone, fentanyl/xylazine test strips, safer-use equipment, overdose-response training, education and peer-led navigation/advocacy.
resources.hours: Street-outreach and training schedules are not posted as a public walk-in clinic; contact program staff first.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Naloxone kits, fentanyl/xylazine test strips, safer-use equipment, educational materials, overdose-response training, community education, clinical education and peer-led navigation/advocacy to help participants access health care and social services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Low-barrier harm reduction for people who use drugs and for organizations or community groups seeking overdose-prevention education. A public self-service Mesa schedule was not found.

**Population Served**
People who use drugs and communities affected by overdose risk in the Phoenix metro area, including unsheltered individuals reached through county-supported harm-reduction outreach.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact Tiffany Randall at tiffanyrandall@arizona.edu or 602-827-2240. Other listed NOPAL contacts include Irene Garnett at 602-827-2080 and Hernan Villegas at 602-827-2341. Confirm the current outreach site or training option before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
This is harm reduction, training and navigation, not detox, residential treatment or medication prescribing. Exact Mesa access points may vary.

resources.name: Maricopa County Office of the Public Advocate - Court-appointed representation
resources.description: The Maricopa County Office of the Public Advocate provides legal representation when appointed by Superior Court for indigent juveniles in delinquency cases, parents and children in dependency/severance matters, and people facing court-ordered mental health evaluation or treatment.
resources.address: Maricopa County, AZ
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Court-appointed legal representation for indigent people in specific Maricopa County Superior Court matters: juvenile delinquency, dependency and severance proceedings, and court-ordered mental health evaluation or treatment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Representation is provided when the office is appointed by Maricopa County Superior Court. This is not a walk-in civil legal-aid clinic and is not a direct substitute for hiring an attorney.

**Population Served**
Indigent juveniles charged with delinquency offenses, parents and children in dependency or severance proceedings, and adults facing court-ordered mental health evaluation or treatment in Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
For questions about an appointed case, call the Mesa line at 602-372-2815 or the Durango line at 602-372-9560. A person who needs appointed counsel should raise inability to afford counsel with the court handling the case.

**Important Information to Know**
The key access point is court appointment, not self-referral. It does not provide general family law, housing, benefits, consumer, or criminal-defense help outside the appointment categories.

resources.name: Arizona Legal Women and Youth Services (ALWAYS) - New Roads to Success
resources.description: Arizona Legal Women and Youth Services (ALWAYS) New Roads to Success provides no-cost legal help for eligible young people to remove legal barriers to employment, housing, education, fingerprint clearance, criminal-history set-asides, and identity documents.
resources.address: Mailing address: 24 W. Camelback Rd., Box A335, Phoenix, AZ 85013; office location is confidential
resources.hours: Call before visiting; ALWAYS keeps its law office location confidential and provides the address only for scheduled appointments.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost legal services for eligible young people, including help with good-cause exceptions for fingerprint clearance cards, criminal history or conviction set-aside requests, and government-issued identity documents.

**Eligibility Requirements**
ALWAYS serves youth and young adults age 26 or younger who live in Maricopa or Pima County and have been impacted by homelessness, couch-surfing, shelter/transitional/group-home living, abuse, domestic violence, sex or labor trafficking, or foster care. ALWAYS does not represent clients in pending criminal charges or dependency/severance matters.

**Population Served**
Young people in Maricopa or Pima County facing legal barriers connected to homelessness, trafficking, abuse, domestic violence, or foster care history.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-248-7055 or use the online inquiry linked from the New Roads to Success page. The law office address is confidential, so clients should not attempt a walk-in visit.

**Important Information to Know**
This is no-cost civil legal help for eligible young people, including identity-document barriers and some barriers after criminal history. It is not general adult record clearance or defense of pending criminal charges, and does not handle dependency/severance matters. The mailing address is not a walk-in law office.

resources.name: Social Security Administration - new Social Security number pathway for domestic violence survivors
resources.description: The Social Security Administration may assign a new Social Security number in exceptional cases when evidence shows a person is being harassed, abused or endangered, including domestic violence situations, and a new number would help reduce danger.
resources.hours: Social Security telephone service: Monday-Friday, 8:00 AM-7:00 PM local time. An appointment and case-specific evidence are required for the exceptional new-number process.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
SSA can consider assigning a new Social Security number when evidence shows the person is being harassed or abused, or their life is endangered. SSA helps complete the required statement and application in person.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A new number is exceptional. Applicants must apply in person at a Social Security office and present evidence of harassment, abuse or life endangerment; current SSN; proof of citizenship or work-authorized immigration status; proof of age; proof of identity; and legal name-change evidence if the name has changed. Documents must be originals or issuing-agency certified copies.

**Population Served**
Domestic violence, harassment, abuse and life-endangerment survivors nationwide, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents who can document the danger and meet SSA evidence requirements.

**How to Best Connect**
Call SSA at 1-800-772-1213 or TTY 1-800-325-0778 to ask about applying for a new Social Security number due to domestic violence, harassment, abuse or life endangerment, and to identify the appropriate office appointment route.

**Important Information to Know**
Changing the number is a major step and does not erase records under the former SSN. Financial, medical, employment and other records may remain under the former number and name. Survivors who only need a lost-card replacement should use the ordinary replacement-card service instead. The SSA guide also lists the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-SAFE (7233).

resources.name: St. Andrew the Apostle Roman Catholic Church - Mother's Lifeline Closet
resources.description: St. Andrew the Apostle's Mother's Lifeline is an outreach ministry that provides practical assistance such as diapers, wipes, infant/toddler clothing up to 2T and gift cards to mothers of infants and toddlers in crisis situations.
resources.address: 3450 W Ray Rd, Chandler, AZ 85226
resources.hours: Caring Ministries / Good Samaritans office hours are Monday-Thursday 9:00-11:00 AM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Practical baby and toddler assistance through Mother's Lifeline, including diapers, diaper wipes, clothing up to size 2T and gift cards when available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For mothers of infants and toddlers in crisis situations and of limited economic means. The page says mothers may be referred by hospital social workers, women's shelters, pregnancy hotlines or word of mouth.

**Population Served**
New mothers and mothers of infants and toddlers in the East Valley, generally Tempe, Chandler, Mesa and Gilbert. Support is provided to all faiths and parishes.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Caring Ministries office at 480-899-1990 ext. 203 during Monday-Thursday 9:00-11:00 AM office hours to ask about Mother's Lifeline intake and current supplies.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a volunteer church outreach, not a walk-in public baby store. Items depend on donated inventory and volunteer availability; call before sending a client.

resources.name: Phoenix Rescue Mission Workforce Development
resources.description: Phoenix Rescue Mission offers job assistance and workforce development tied to community and recovery services, including GED/diploma support, vocational and educational help, career coaching, resume/interview preparation, job search and benefits enrollment assistance.
resources.address: Glendale Community Center, 5401 W Ocotillo Rd, Glendale, AZ 85301
resources.hours: Call for appointment; confirm current location and whether walk-ins or nonresidential participants are accepted before travel.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Workforce development and job assistance may include vocational and educational services, GED or high school diploma support, communication and professional skills, career guidance, resume and interview preparation, job search help, training-grant navigation and benefits application help.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Access appears to differ by route. Prior official workforce content described adults who would benefit from career coaching at the Glendale Community Center; DES-listed services may be limited to adults enrolled in residential programming. Call to confirm current nonresidential eligibility.

**Population Served**
Adults facing poverty, homelessness, addiction recovery or other barriers to employment in Maricopa County who can access Phoenix Rescue Mission services or the Glendale location.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-346-3351 or email careerhelp@phxmission.org and ask specifically about Workforce Development at 5401 W Ocotillo Rd in Glendale. The main Mission help line is 602-233-3000.

**Important Information to Know**
The standalone workforce page currently redirects, but useful evidence still supports workforce services. Because Glendale is far from Mesa and eligibility may be limited to program participants, confirm appointment availability, location and nonresidential eligibility before referral.

resources.name: A New Leaf — outpatient counseling access to clarify
resources.description: Possible family counseling through the historically listed Dorothy B. Mitchell and La Mesita clinics.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Possible family counseling through the historically listed Dorothy B. Mitchell and La Mesita clinics.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Current program eligibility and public enrollment need confirmation.

**Population Served**
Mesa-area families seeking affordable counseling.

**How to Best Connect**
Administrators can ask A New Leaf at 480-969-4024 which counseling programs currently accept referrals.

**Important Information to Know**
The historical clinic names and 480-733-3050 scheduling route are not established by the current service listing. Resolve the active program and intake before offering this record to missionaries.

resources.name: MO Med Trans — non-emergency medical transportation
resources.description: A Mesa-area non-emergency medical transportation service listed in the Area Agency on Aging resource guide.
resources.hours: Call to confirm current scheduling and availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A Mesa-area non-emergency medical transportation service listed in the Area Agency on Aging resource guide.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Call to establish whether the provider can accept the proposed trip and passenger needs. Current fees, health-plan participation and any authorization requirements are not established.

**Population Served**
People seeking transportation to health appointments in the Mesa area, subject to provider confirmation of the actual pickup and destination.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-800-3130 before making plans. Describe the trip, passenger mobility, any wheelchair or other equipment, companion needs and how payment would be made.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm that the service is operating, obtain a quote and arrange the return trip. Do not assume wheelchair or stretcher capacity, insurance coverage, or same-day availability. For emergencies, call 911.

resources.name: Banner Health - Pregnancy and Infant Loss Support Group, Banner Gateway
resources.description: Banner Gateway's Pregnancy and Infant Loss Support Group is a virtual support group for mothers who have experienced miscarriage, fetal loss or newborn loss, regardless of whether the loss occurred at Banner Gateway.
resources.address: Virtual group associated with Banner Gateway Medical Center, 1900 N. Higley Rd., Gilbert, AZ 85234
resources.hours: Banner calendar lists virtual sessions on scheduled dates; confirm the current calendar before registering.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Pregnancy and Infant Loss Support Group provides virtual peer/support group space for grief after miscarriage, fetal loss or newborn loss. Banner says all mothers are welcome regardless of whether the loss occurred at Banner Gateway Medical Center.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The group is for mothers who have had a miscarriage, fetal loss or newborn loss. It is a support group, not emergency care or individual grief counseling.

**Population Served**
Mothers and families in the East Valley, including Mesa residents, affected by pregnancy or infant loss who can participate by Microsoft Teams.

**How to Best Connect**
Register through Banner's class/event calendar. Banner lists Michele Stanley as contact at 480-543-3050. Microsoft Teams is required, and registrants receive a meeting link from a Banner email before the class.

**Important Information to Know**
Calendar-based support groups can be rescheduled or cancelled. Confirm the current date, registration status and whether partners or family members may participate before referral.

resources.name: ViewFinder Low Vision Resource Center - Mesa low-vision evaluation and store
resources.description: ViewFinder Low Vision Resource Center in Mesa offers low-vision evaluations, specialty glasses, optical and digital magnification, text-to-speech readers, glare filters, task lights, daily-living aids, demonstrations, home training, peer support, and resource navigation for people with vision impairment.
resources.address: 1830 S. Alma School Rd. #131, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Mesa office listed as open 8:00 a.m.-4:30 p.m. on the checked page; call to schedule and confirm current hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Low-vision consultation/evaluation, specialty glasses, optical magnification, digital magnification, text-to-speech readers, glare filters, task lights, daily living aids for blindness, assistive devices, in-person demonstrations, online and local peer support groups, occupational-therapy home training for daily activities and accessibility tools, referral forms, and a low-vision resource directory.

**Eligibility Requirements**
People with low vision or vision impairment may contact the center or schedule a consultation. The site does not state that services are free; cost, insurance, and referral requirements should be confirmed directly.

**Population Served**
People with low vision, blindness, progressive vision loss, failed standard refraction, or functional vision barriers in Mesa and the Phoenix metro area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-924-8755 to schedule or ask about walk-in demonstrations at the Mesa office. The Mesa office is at 1830 S. Alma School Rd. #131.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a specialty low-vision resource center, not a free routine eye exam clinic. It is most useful after a client has an eye diagnosis, current eye records, or needs assistive devices and functional low-vision support.

resources.name: Resilient Health — adult housing support
