resources.address: Apply online; confirm any assigned evaluation or pet drop-off location with AHS.
resources.hours: Online application is reviewed after submission; AHS says review occurs within 72 hours and capacity may delay assistance.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Temporary foster care or boarding for pets for 30-90 days through Project Home Away From Home, in partnership with PetSmart. The program is intended to keep pets and people together during a crisis.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For a household crisis such as hospitalization/recovery, domestic-violence safety needs, involuntary housing loss or active-duty deployment. Pets must be healthy and behaviorally suitable; normally no more than two per household. A reunification plan, spay/neuter and required vaccinations are conditions. AHS may provide these services, which can delay entry.

**Population Served**
Pet owners in the Arizona Humane Society/Maricopa County service context who are in crisis and need temporary safe care for pets while stabilizing housing, safety or health needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Project Home Away From Home application or Contact Us link on AHS’s Resources to Keep Your Pet page. Ask about eligibility, costs, safe communication and capacity. Applications are normally reviewed within 72 hours; reply within 48 hours of staff contact to avoid losing a place.

**Important Information to Know**
This is pet care, not human shelter or guaranteed immediate rescue. Evaluations can be one to three weeks away when space permits. Owners must communicate weekly about reunification; placement and timing depend on suitability, vaccination needs and capacity.

resources.name: Foundation for Blind Children · S.O.A.R. Transition Program
resources.description: Foundation for Blind Children's S.O.A.R. is a 9-month transition program for blind and visually impaired young adults preparing for employment, internships, volunteering, college, trade school, and independent adult life.
resources.address: Phoenix-area Foundation for Blind Children program; contact program staff before visiting
resources.hours: Program commitment is September through May; current application dates on the page are old, so contact staff for the next enrollment window.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
SOAR supports blind and visually impaired young adults through one-on-one check-ins, small group workshops, job readiness, networking, advocacy, disability rights, education and employment planning, college or trade-school planning, career readiness, and support toward a first job, internship, or volunteer experience.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The page describes ideal candidates as young adults ages 14-22 who are committed to growth, willing to work with a SOAR instructor, and enrolled and in good standing with Arizona Vocational Rehabilitation Services with a current Individual Plan for Employment. Active VR client status is required to apply.

**Population Served**
Blind and visually impaired young adults in Arizona who are preparing for work, volunteer roles, internships, college, trade school, or independent living.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact Madeline Hillebrand, Youth Transition Specialist, at 602-331-7929 or use the web form on the SOAR page. Ask for current application dates and how to connect with Vocational Rehabilitation if the client is not already an active VR client.

**Important Information to Know**
The posted application dates are outdated, but the program page remains live and describes the service and contact route. Enrollment is not guaranteed and depends on VR status, interview, and cohort availability.

resources.name: Treasure House - Supported Living Residence for Young Adults with IDD
resources.description: Treasure House is a supported living residence for young adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities in Glendale, with a structured admissions process and current full-capacity/waitlist notice.
resources.address: 7815 W. Aspera Blvd., Glendale, AZ 85308
resources.hours: Use the inquiry form or email for admissions; housing is currently full per official page.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Residential supported living for young adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities, including a single-bedroom apartment, utilities, internet, 14 meals per week, transportation within a 20-mile radius, employment readiness support and coaching, 24/7 staff support, activities and outings.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Residents are young adults with an IDD seeking productive and fulfilling lives in a residential setting. Treasure House states it is not appropriate for individuals whose psychiatric or serious emotional disturbance impacts behavior, who have serious medical conditions requiring daily or weekly monitoring/intervention, or who require 24-hour supervision.

**Population Served**
Young adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities who may be a fit for a community-based supported living model in Glendale.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the online initial inquiry form or contact kady@treasurehouse.org about the waitlist. General contact is 602-714-8189 or info@treasurehouse.org.

**Important Information to Know**
Treasure House states it is currently at full capacity and housing is not immediately available. The page lists a $500 application review fee, $1,000 non-refundable reservation fee if added to the waitlist, and a resident share of $4,100 monthly. This is a limited-access reserve option, not an emergency housing referral.

resources.name: Rummel Construction - Heavy Equipment Operator and Heavy Equipment Mechanic Apprenticeships
resources.description: Rummel Construction offers Department of Labor and Arizona-registered Heavy Equipment Operator and Heavy Equipment Mechanic apprenticeships, selected from Rummel's incumbent workforce, with on-the-job experience, technical training and completion credentials.
resources.address: 7520 E Adobe Dr, Scottsdale, AZ 85255
resources.hours: Apply through current job postings; apprenticeship selection occurs after employment and current openings vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Rummel Construction has Heavy Equipment Operator and Heavy Equipment Mechanic apprenticeship programs registered with the U.S. Department of Labor and the State of Arizona. The programs combine on-the-job experience with technical training and lead to an industry-recognized USDOL completion certificate.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Rummel states apprentices are chosen from its incumbent workforce, so a person generally needs to be hired by Rummel first and then be selected for apprenticeship. Job openings have separate experience, license, safety and work-location requirements.

**Population Served**
People seeking construction careers with a Scottsdale-based employer working across Arizona, including Mesa-area job seekers who can reach assigned projects or work locations.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the official Work at Rummel page and job-postings link to apply for open roles. Ask recruiting staff when an employee can be considered for the heavy equipment operator or mechanic apprenticeship.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not open public enrollment into an apprenticeship classroom. It is a useful earn-while-you-learn lead for people ready to work for Rummel first; current hiring, jobsite location and apprenticeship timing must be confirmed.

resources.name: StrongHearts Native Helpline - 24/7 Native Domestic and Sexual Violence Helpline
resources.description: StrongHearts Native Helpline is a 24/7 confidential and anonymous domestic and sexual violence helpline for Native Americans and Alaska Natives, offering culturally responsive peer support, advocacy, safety planning, crisis intervention, health/forensic-care information and Native-centered referrals.
resources.hours: 24/7 by phone, text and chat.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
StrongHearts provides free peer support and advocacy, domestic and sexual violence information, personalized safety planning, crisis intervention, referrals to Native-centered providers, health-option information, help finding local sexual-assault/forensic-care resources and general jurisdiction/legal advocacy referral information.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Native Americans and Alaska Natives affected by domestic or sexual violence, and for supporters seeking culturally grounded guidance. It is a remote helpline, not a local shelter placement program.

**Population Served**
Native American and Alaska Native survivors nationwide, including Mesa residents and nearby tribal communities.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 1-844-762-8483, text START to 1-844-762-8483, or use the chat icon on the StrongHearts website. The site gives safety and privacy guidance for monitored devices.

**Important Information to Know**
StrongHearts is confidential and anonymous but national/remote. Local shelter, transportation, forensic exam access and tribal-jurisdiction questions still require case-by-case local handoff.

resources.name: Ability360 - Durable Medical Equipment Loan Closet
resources.description: Short-term loans of donated medical equipment such as manual wheelchairs, walkers and shower equipment, arranged through Ability360 Information and Referral when available.
resources.address: 5025 E Washington St, Suite 200, Phoenix, AZ 85034; Mesa office listed by Ability360 at 205 E Southern Ave, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Ability360 main office hours: Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM; call first to check equipment availability and appointment needs.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Short-term donated durable medical equipment loans, including manual wheelchairs, walkers and shower equipment when available. Information and Referral staff can discuss alternatives if the needed item is unavailable.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The loan closet is for people with disabilities who need available equipment. Equipment is inventory-dependent and generally provided as-is; larger or motorized equipment may not be available.

**Population Served**
People with disabilities in Ability360 service areas, including Maricopa County and Mesa-area residents who can contact Ability360 for disability-resource navigation or equipment availability.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Information and Referral contact at 602-296-0536 or email TriciaS@ability360.org before visiting. Ask what equipment is currently available, loan period, pickup location, required documents, and whether the Mesa office can help with intake.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general furniture closet. Inventory changes and equipment is provided as-is. The older published policy describes loans up to 90 days and excludes motorized equipment, hospital beds and Hoyer lifts. Confirm current operation, loan terms, suitability, paperwork and pickup before travel; the Mesa office is not a confirmed equipment pickup site.

resources.name: Community Bridges, Inc. - Rio Fresco Healing Center / Rio Fresco Hotel to Housing
resources.description: CBI Rio Fresco is listed by Community Bridges as a Phoenix hotel-to-housing location within its shelters, outreach and healing-center network, offering temporary indoor shelter with supportive services and housing planning through CBI access pathways.
resources.address: 2425 S 24th St, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: Access appears referral/system based; call CBI before sending a client.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Hotel-to-housing/healing-center site connected to CBI's shelter and outreach continuum. CBI describes its shelter and healing-center model as safe indoor places with case management, behavioral-health services, individualized housing plans, housing resources, peer navigation and employment opportunities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Program fit and referral route must be screened through CBI or the homelessness response system. Public sources do not support walk-up intake at Rio Fresco.

**Population Served**
Adults experiencing homelessness in the Phoenix/Maricopa County homelessness response system who are appropriate for a CBI shelter, healing center or hotel-to-housing placement.

**How to Best Connect**
Call CBI's 24/7 Access to Care line at 877-931-9142 or appointments at 888-224-6593 and ask specifically about Rio Fresco Hotel to Housing or current shelter/healing-center access.

**Important Information to Know**
CBI's Arizona locations page lists Rio Fresco - Hotel to Housing at 2425 S 24th St, Phoenix. The separate Rio Fresco project page is informational and does not provide client intake. Do not send a client to the site without confirming referral route and availability.

resources.name: Banner Poison and Drug Information Center - Maricopa County Caring Contacts program
resources.description: Maricopa County's Caring Contacts program is a county-contracted suicide-prevention follow-up program operated through Banner Poison and Drug Information Center for patients connected from two Phoenix emergency departments, offering follow-up within 24-48 hours, safety planning and navigation to insurance, behavioral health and wraparound services.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Caring Contacts program provides suicide-prevention follow-up after participating emergency-department contact. Maricopa County describes follow-up within 24-48 hours, a safety plan, and navigation to insurance, behavioral-health and wraparound services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public county page describes the program as connecting patients from two Phoenix emergency departments to Banner Poison and Drug Information Center. It does not describe general community self-referral.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County emergency-department patients connected through the participating Phoenix emergency departments after suicide-risk or related crisis contact.

**How to Best Connect**
No direct public self-referral phone is listed for Caring Contacts. People in immediate crisis should call or text 988. Administrators or providers can contact Maricopa County's Suicide Education and Prevention Coordinator listed on the county page at 602-571-9422 or Kelsey.Manders@maricopa.gov to clarify program access.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a useful suicide-prevention lead but not currently a routine community referral. The unresolved access issue is which emergency departments participate and whether any outside referral is possible.
resources.resolutionReason: The participating emergency departments and patient referral/enrollment route have not been established. County coordinator contact is for administrator clarification, not crisis or counseling intake.

resources.name: GateWay Community College - Trade and Technical Training Clock Programs
resources.description: GateWay Community College Trade and Technical Training offers hands-on clock-hour programs that can lead to certification in fields such as healthcare, machining, welding, beauty/wellness, EMT, medical assisting, billing/coding and HVAC.
resources.address: 108 N. 40th Street, Phoenix, AZ 85034; additional program sites include Central City, 18th Street, Deer Valley, CEI and Phoenix Forge
resources.hours: Program start dates vary and are subject to change or cancellation; use Get Started, information sessions or phone before enrolling.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Hands-on trade and technical clock-hour programs taught by industry professionals. GateWay states students can earn certification in as little as six months and lists current/coming program starts for ECG technician, pharmacy technician, phlebotomy, collision repair, CNC machining, welding, aesthetician, cosmetology, massage therapy, EMT, medical assisting, medical billing/coding and HVAC residential installation/service.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Admission, tuition, financial aid, prerequisites, schedules and licensure/certification requirements vary by program. Some start dates may be canceled or changed.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County students and adults seeking hands-on career training in Phoenix-area GateWay/Maricopa Community Colleges locations.

**How to Best Connect**
Use GateWay's Get Started, Chat Now, information session links or call 602-286-8000. Main Washington Campus: 108 N. 40th Street, Phoenix.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not Mesa-based but is within Maricopa County. Start dates on the page extend into 2026-2027 and are explicitly subject to change; confirm costs, location and current enrollment before referral.

resources.name: HOM, Inc. - Permanent Supportive Housing and Rapid Re-Housing Administration
resources.description: HOM, Inc. administers Permanent Supportive Housing, Rapid Re-Housing, Mainstream and other rental-assistance operations for nonprofit and public partners, including eligibility processing, vouchers/tickets, inspections, rent calculations, landlord payments, security deposits and utility deposits.
resources.address: 5326 E. Washington St., Suite 5, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Rental-assistance administration for Permanent Supportive Housing, Rapid Re-Housing, Mainstream and other permanent housing programs. HOM handles income eligibility, orientations, vouchers or tickets, housing-search coordination with service providers, inspections, rent calculations, landlord contracts and payments, security deposits, utility deposits and tenancy-related liaison work.

**Eligibility Requirements**
HOM states nonprofit supportive-service partners determine homeless status and other program-specific eligibility for many programs. Mainstream vouchers serve very low-income disabled households. Most homeless assistance is not a direct public application to HOM.

**Population Served**
Vulnerable individuals and families experiencing homelessness or housing instability in Arizona partner programs, including people with disabilities in Mainstream housing pathways.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the appropriate coordinated-entry, behavioral-health or service-provider referral path first. For HOM program questions, call HOM Central AZ at 602-265-4640. Current participants and providers can use HOM's resident/provider tools and housing specialist routes.

**Important Information to Know**
HOM is primarily an administrator and landlord/tenant payment partner, not a general shelter or open housing waitlist for walk-ins. A client usually needs to be referred or already connected to a partner program.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Economic Security - Grant Diversion Program
resources.description: DES Grant Diversion is a one-time lump-sum Cash Assistance payment option intended to help an eligible family cover expenses while moving toward full-time employment.
resources.hours: Discuss during the DES Cash Assistance eligibility interview.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
One-time lump-sum payment of Cash Assistance benefits to help with expenses while a family seeks full-time employment. It is an alternative to ongoing TANF Cash Assistance when the option fits the household.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The family must meet Cash Assistance eligibility requirements, be eligible for at least one dollar of Cash Assistance in the approval month, not have received Cash Assistance in the application month or Grant Diversion in the month before application, and not have received Grant Diversion in the prior 12 months. Current TANF Cash Assistance recipients cannot apply for Grant Diversion.

**Population Served**
Arizona families eligible for Cash Assistance who may be able to move toward full-time employment with a one-time payment instead of ongoing monthly assistance.

**How to Best Connect**
Start with the DES Cash Assistance application through Health-e-Arizona Plus, mail/fax, or DES office routes. Talk to the eligibility interviewer about whether Grant Diversion is right for the family.

**Important Information to Know**
Cash Assistance eligibility must be determined before Grant Diversion can be released. The payment is received on an EBT card, not paid to vendors. Employment does not need to be lined up, but the benefit is intended to help a family move from long-term Cash Assistance to full-time employment.

resources.name: Tempe Municipal Court - Compliance Assistance Program (CAP) Packet
resources.description: Tempe Municipal Court's Compliance Assistance Program helps eligible people resolve past-due court financial obligations through a payment plan so Tempe court-related MVD holds or suspensions can be released after the required down payment.
resources.address: Tempe Municipal Court, 140 East Fifth Street, Tempe, AZ 85281
resources.hours: Call the court for current financial-services hours; the official CAP page says in-person appearance is not required and clients may call to learn how to participate.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
CAP helps people with eligible Tempe Municipal Court cases set up a payment plan for past-due financial obligations that may be blocking driver license reinstatement or vehicle registration renewal. After the required down payment is received, the court issues an MVD release for Tempe Municipal Court suspensions or holds.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The person must have eligible Tempe Municipal Court financial obligations. A specific down payment and agreement to make affordable monthly payments are required. Outstanding warrants must be resolved before completing the CAP process.

**Population Served**
People with Tempe Municipal Court cases, including Mesa or East Valley clients whose driving privileges or vehicle registration are affected by Tempe court debt.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-350-8271 to ask how to participate and what down payment is required. The court's CAP page also lists court-financial@tempe.gov and Tempe Municipal Court, 140 East Fifth Street, Tempe, AZ 85281. Ask whether the client can submit the packet remotely and whether any warrant, added charge or MVD requirement remains.

**Important Information to Know**
CAP only addresses Tempe Municipal Court suspensions or holds. The client must still contact Arizona MVD about any other reinstatement requirements. Failure to maintain the payment agreement can lead to default, added fees and another suspension or registration hold.

resources.name: ASU Law Lodestar Mediation Clinic
resources.description: ASU Law's Lodestar Mediation Clinic provides supervised student mediation in participating Maricopa County Justice Court civil cases, offering neutral dispute resolution before trial.
resources.address: 111 E Taylor St, Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.hours: Court-connected mediation schedule depends on the participating Justice Court.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides neutral mediation services through supervised law students for participating civil cases, helping parties try to resolve disputes before trial.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Available to litigants in participating Maricopa County Justice Court civil cases when the court offers or refers the case to mediation. It is not a general public legal-advice intake program.

**Population Served**
Civil litigants in participating Maricopa County Justice Courts.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the assigned Justice Court whether the case is eligible for Lodestar Mediation Clinic or other court-connected mediation before the hearing or trial date.

**Important Information to Know**
Mediators are neutral and do not represent either side or provide legal advice. Parties who need legal advice should contact a lawyer or legal-aid provider separately.

resources.name: Valleywise Community Health Center — Chandler
resources.description: Provides an East Valley community health center with on-site dental services in Chandler.
resources.address: 811 S. Hamilton St., Chandler, AZ 85225
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides an East Valley community health center with on-site dental services in Chandler.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Confirm insurance, sliding-fee screening and new-patient or referral requirements for the needed service.

**Population Served**
Children and adults able to attend the Chandler health center.

**How to Best Connect**
Call appointments at 833-855-9973 or the clinic at 480-344-6100; location 811 S. Hamilton St., Chandler.

**Important Information to Know**
Medical hours are weekdays 7 a.m.–5:30 p.m. and Saturday 7–11 a.m.; dental weekdays 7:30 a.m.–4 p.m. Confirm the particular appointment and fee.

resources.name: East Valley Regional Veterans Court
resources.description: East Valley Regional Veterans Court is a municipal problem-solving court program that connects eligible veterans with pending misdemeanor cases in participating East Valley courts to court supervision, treatment plans and veteran-specific resources.
resources.address: 140 East Fifth Street, Tempe, AZ 85281
resources.hours: Court schedule and appearances depend on the case; ask the attorney, prosecutor, judge or court about current enrollment timing.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Problem-solving court pathway that helps eligible veterans address pending misdemeanor charges and related needs such as medical conditions, unemployment, homelessness, mental health, substance use, education and VA or social-service treatment connections.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The person must be a veteran charged with a misdemeanor violation filed in a participating East Valley municipality, and the case must be approved for Veterans Court. Prosecutors may refuse admission when required by law or the interests of justice.

**Population Served**
Veterans, including active-duty service members and veterans regardless of discharge status or length of service, with eligible cases in participating municipal courts such as Chandler, Carefree-Cave Creek, Fountain Hills, Gilbert, Paradise Valley, Scottsdale and Tempe.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the defense attorney, prosecutor or judge to determine eligibility. For general questions, contact Tempe Municipal Court at 480-350-4311 or court-inquiries@tempe.gov.

**Important Information to Know**
Mesa Municipal Court is not listed as a participating municipality on the official page. This is not a general walk-in legal clinic; it is tied to active municipal court cases.

resources.name: Be Connected - Military/Veteran/Family Suicide Postvention Support
resources.description: Be Connected Postvention provides confidential, no-cost support in Arizona after a suicide loss involving a service member, veteran or family member, including grief counseling referrals, care navigation, support planning and organizational or community guidance.
resources.hours: Support line Monday-Friday, 8 a.m.-5 p.m. Mountain/Arizona time; 988 is 24/7 for immediate crisis.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Be Connected Postvention offers grief counseling referrals, care navigation, emotional support, practical guidance, individualized care plans, crisis response guidance, staff training and community healing initiatives after suicide loss involving a service member, veteran or family member.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Anyone in Arizona affected by a suicide loss involving a service member, veteran or their family member may reach out. Organizations and communities impacted by suicide may also request support.

**Population Served**
Arizona individuals, families, organizations and communities affected by the suicide of a service member, veteran or family member. A person does not have to be a veteran or in the military to receive help.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the support request form on the Postvention page, email prevention@arizonacoalition.org, or call 866-4AZ-VETS (866-429-8387) for general information and support Monday-Friday, 8 a.m.-5 p.m. Mountain/Arizona time.

**Important Information to Know**
Services are confidential and free. The programme expects to respond to a support form within two business days, so it is not a crisis line. For veteran crisis support, call 988 then press 1 or text 838255. Other callers can contact 988; call 911 for immediate danger.

resources.name: AHCCCS — Non-emergency medical transportation
resources.description: Covered non-emergency rides for eligible AHCCCS members unable to provide, secure or pay for transportation to covered care. Arrange access through the member’s plan or applicable fee-for-service route.
resources.phone: Use health-plan Member Services; AHCCCS general 602-417-4000 or 800-654-8713
resources.address: Statewide benefit arranged through the member's AHCCCS health plan
resources.hours: Arrange rides in advance through the AHCCCS health plan Member Services number on the member's insurance card; plan hours and notice rules vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
AHCCCS covers medically necessary non-emergency transportation for most members who cannot arrange or pay for transportation to covered medical or behavioral health services. Members generally arrange rides through their health plan's Member Services number.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The person must be an eligible AHCCCS member, have no other transportation option, and be traveling to an AHCCCS-covered service. Non-emergency transportation is not covered for Federal Emergency Services Program members.

**Population Served**
Eligible AHCCCS members in Arizona, including Mesa and Maricopa County, who lack transportation to covered care.

**How to Best Connect**
Start with Member Services on the health-plan card; fee-for-service members should confirm their applicable AHCCCS route. Have appointment/provider and pickup details, mobility devices, oxygen/IV needs, child car-seat and other accommodation needs ready. For unresolved plan problems, AHCCCS lists its Clinical Resolution Unit at 602-364-4558 or 800-867-5308.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not emergency transport or a ride service for errands. Advance notice, authorization, distance, pharmacy-trip and accommodation rules depend on the plan, member status and trip. Same-day service may be unavailable. General AHCCCS and resolution-unit numbers are not routine ride-booking lines.

resources.name: U.S. Probation, District of Arizona — Supervision-linked treatment
resources.description: Provides an officer-arranged pathway to contracted treatment and residential services, including specialized treatment catchments serving Mesa.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides an officer-arranged pathway to contracted treatment and residential services, including specialized treatment catchments serving Mesa.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Federal supervision, assessment, authorization and provider placement rules apply.

**Population Served**
People on federal probation or supervised release in the District of Arizona.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the assigned federal probation officer about authorized treatment, costs and the appropriate contracted provider.

**Important Information to Know**
Contract catchment listings establish service arrangements, not an open public intake or current vacancy. This is distinct from a Bureau of Prisons residential reentry placement.

resources.name: Banner – University Family Care/ALTCS — member medical transportation
resources.description: Plan-arranged non-emergency transportation to the nearest appropriate AHCCCS-registered provider when an enrolled member cannot arrange a ride.
resources.hours: Customer Care: Monday–Friday, 7:30 a.m.–5 p.m.; after-hours answering service.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Plan-arranged non-emergency transportation to the nearest appropriate AHCCCS-registered provider when an enrolled member cannot arrange a ride.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Banner – University Family Care/ALTCS members. Pharmacy trips in Maricopa County normally have a 15-mile limit; longer specialty or compounding trips need authorization, with a separate exception for qualifying MSIC or IHS/638 pharmacies.

**Population Served**
Enrolled ALTCS members in the plan’s Arizona service area, including Mesa. Banner ACC members use a different plan contact.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Customer Care at 833-318-4146, TTY 711, at least 72 hours before the visit. Give appointment, pickup, mobility and passenger details. Explain child-seat needs in advance.

**Important Information to Know**
One companion is normally allowed; additional minor children or passengers with medical needs have special rules. Same-day transport is not guaranteed. Ask the plan about weekend or holiday urgent-care trips; call 911 for an emergency.

resources.name: The ALS Association - Independence & Mobility Program / ALS equipment and communication-device access
resources.description: The ALS Association's Independence & Mobility Program helps people with ALS access mobility, daily living, ramp and communication equipment when insurance is delayed or unavailable, subject to inventory.
resources.phone: 602-297-3800; use national care-services form if phone changes
resources.address: Arizona care services team; historical Arizona office listed at 360 E. Coronado Rd. #140, Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.hours: Use the care-services support form or call the local care services team; equipment availability varies.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Education and access pathways for ALS-related durable medical equipment, mobility aids, bathroom and transfer devices, bedroom items, daily living aids, ramps, augmentative and alternative communication tools, speech-generating devices and virtual home assessment referrals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Condition-specific to people living with ALS. Equipment access is intended for people with ALS who have no coverage for needed equipment or, in some cases, coverage but an immediate and critical medical need. Requests typically involve the ALS clinic, neurologist, Speech Language Pathologist or local Care Services team.

**Population Served**
People living with ALS and their families/caregivers in Arizona who need mobility, independence or communication support.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the ALS Association Connect with Us for Care Services & Support form or contact the local Care Services team. The Arizona phone historically listed for ALS equipment resources is 602-297-3800; confirm current Arizona contact through the official support form.

**Important Information to Know**
Equipment is free of charge where available, but inventory is limited and specific requested items are not guaranteed. Work with the ALS clinic, neurologist or SLP to identify appropriate equipment and documentation.

resources.name: Teen Lifeline - Caring Contacts
resources.description: Teen Lifeline Caring Contacts supports Arizona teens recently discharged from psychiatric facilities through caring calls, texts, letters, peer connection, care packages, and personalized resources during the year after discharge.
resources.address: P.O. Box 10745, Phoenix, AZ 85064
resources.hours: Referral questions by email; hotline calls 24/7/365 and texting/peer counseling 3:00 PM-9:00 PM daily.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Post-discharge caring contacts for teens recently discharged from psychiatric facilities, including phone calls, texts, letters, encouragement, peer connection, birthday and anniversary contacts, a care package, and resources personalized to the teen and family.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For teens recently discharged from inpatient psychiatric care or psychiatric facilities. Enrollment and referral process should be confirmed with Teen Lifeline; referral questions go to intake@teenlifeline.org.

**Population Served**
Arizona teens at high risk during the transition after psychiatric hospitalization, including Mesa and Maricopa County youth, plus their families.

**How to Best Connect**
Email intake@teenlifeline.org for referral-process questions or partnership/enrollment details. Teens and families can also call or text 602-248-8336 for hotline support.

**Important Information to Know**
Caring Contacts is an adjunct support program, not clinical monitoring, emergency response, therapy, or medication management. It begins after enrollment and is meant to encourage ongoing treatment and reintegration.

resources.name: East Valley Institute of Technology - Registered Apprenticeships and Pre-Apprenticeships
resources.description: EVIT offers paid registered-apprenticeship pathways and pre-apprenticeships for high school and adult/postsecondary students in electrical, HVAC-R, plumbing, welding/structural metal fabrication and airframe mechanic beginning August 2026.
resources.address: 1601 W. Main St., Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Use the request-information form or email before applying; program and cohort timing varies by pathway.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
EVIT apprenticeship programs provide hands-on training, paid work-based learning, coordinator guidance after completion of an EVIT-approved pre-apprenticeship, and pathways in electrical, HVAC-R, plumbing, structural metal fabricator/welding and airframe mechanic.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page says high school and postsecondary students may participate, and that completing an EVIT-approved pre-apprenticeship is the first step toward eligibility to apply for a registered apprenticeship. Specific enrollment requirements are in EVIT's course catalog and vary by pathway.

**Population Served**
High school and adult/postsecondary students in Mesa and Arizona apprenticeship partnerships who want paid trade training.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the apprenticeship request-information form, email apprenticeship@evit.edu, apply through EVIT's application link, or call 480-461-4000. The main campus is 1601 W. Main St., Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
Airframe mechanic is listed as beginning August 2026. The public page says the current application is for pre-apprenticeship; employer sponsors, cohort openings, prerequisites and costs should be confirmed with EVIT before relying on a start date.

resources.name: Mesa Community College · GED/HSE Testing Services
resources.description: Mesa Community College GED/HSE Testing provides local GED and Arizona Civics testing by appointment at the Southern and Dobson and Red Mountain campuses, with registration through GED.com and published campus instructions.
resources.address: Southern and Dobson Campus, 1833 W. Southern Ave., Mesa, AZ 85202; Red Mountain Campus, 7110 E. McKellips Rd., Mesa, AZ 85207
resources.hours: GED testing by appointment Tuesday-Thursday.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Local testing for the GED high school equivalency exam and Arizona Civics section at MCC testing centers. The page explains test sections, scheduling, youth override steps, campus testing locations, and score access through GED.com.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Test takers must create a GED.com account, register for sections, select appointment times, and pay online. Candidates ages 16 or 17 must bring an official high school withdrawal, notarized parent or guardian permission, and official non-expired photo ID to a GED Testing Center for an override before scheduling.

**Population Served**
Mesa and East Valley residents ready to take GED/HSE and Arizona Civics tests, including younger testers who meet Arizona override requirements.

**How to Best Connect**
Create an account and schedule through GED.com. Call MCC Southern and Dobson at 480-461-7000 or Red Mountain at 480-654-7200 for campus testing questions.

**Important Information to Know**
The MCC page lists two different GED section prices, $41 and $35, while Civics is listed as $9; confirm the current GED.com price before payment. Testing is separate from GED preparation classes and all five sections cannot be completed in one day.

resources.name: Arizona Safety Net — Free and low-cost clinic directory
resources.description: Helps compare charity, free and low-cost clinic options in the Phoenix metropolitan area.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Helps compare charity, free and low-cost clinic options in the Phoenix metropolitan area.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Public directory; each clinic has separate location, insurance, patient and fee requirements.

**Population Served**
Uninsured or underserved clients seeking an alternative clinic in Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the medical or dental clinic directory, then call the clinic selected for the client’s needs.

**Important Information to Know**
The network is not a walk-in clinic. Specialist referrals generally need an established participating primary-care provider.

resources.name: Arizona MVD — ID cards, replacements and optional tribal designation
resources.description: Arizona MVD is the official issuing agency for Arizona identification cards and replacement ID cards, with online-start and in-person completion options and limited no-fee categories.
resources.address: Mesa/Gilbert SE Regional MVD: 4123 E Valley Auto Dr, Mesa, AZ 85206
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Arizona state identification cards and replacement credentials, with online application/start and MVD or authorized Third Party completion as applicable. Enrolled members of federally recognized tribal nations can also request the optional Native American designation on a state ID, driver license or instruction permit.

**Eligibility Requirements**
ID-card applicants need proof of identity, a full Social Security number and two Arizona residency proofs; a name-change document is needed when names differ. Cards are available at all ages. The optional Native American designation requires qualifying tribal-enrollment proof, such as a tribal ID, enhanced tribal card, Certificate of Indian Blood or accepted tribal/BIA birth affidavit. Confirm current document rules.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents and eligible applicants needing a state ID or replacement credential, including Mesa clients.

**How to Best Connect**
Start at AZMVDNow.gov or use any MVD or authorized Third Party office. Mesa clients can use the Mesa/Gilbert SE Regional MVD at 4123 E Valley Auto Dr. Call 602-255-0072 to confirm current office hours, appointment needs and documents before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
Standard ID and replacement fees are listed at $12. People 65+, eligible SSI recipients, minors in DCS care and qualifying homeless veterans may qualify for free standard cards; this does not apply to Travel IDs. ADOT requires the full SSN but not a Social Security document for that item. Driver-license/reinstatement rules are separate. Ask the specific ADCRR facility/reentry contact about pre-release document coordination.

resources.name: Maricopa County - ADA Accommodation and Grievance Program
resources.description: Maricopa County's ADA Coordinator accepts reasonable-modification, effective-communication and grievance requests for access to County programs, services, activities and employment processes.
resources.address: 301 W. Jefferson St., Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.hours: Requests for meetings or events should be made at least 3 business days in advance when possible; later requests are still considered individually.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Maricopa County provides a route to request reasonable modifications, sign-language interpreters, captioning, CART, accessible documents and other auxiliary aids for County programs, services, activities and meetings. The ADA Coordinator also receives County ADA access complaints and grievances.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The request must relate to disability access in a Maricopa County program, service, activity, meeting or employment process. This does not cover private businesses or non-County services.

**Population Served**
People with disabilities who need access to Maricopa County-operated services, public meetings, activities, programs or employment practices.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the County accommodation request link, contact the relevant County department, or contact the ADA Coordinator at ADA.help@maricopa.gov or 602-506-0583. Provide the event, service, date, needed accommodation and contact information.

**Important Information to Know**
The County asks for 3 business days' notice when possible, but evaluates late requests based on circumstances. The ADA does not require actions that would fundamentally alter a County program or impose undue burdens; grievance rights remain available if access is denied.

resources.name: Southwest Autism Research & Resource Center - Kathryn G. Bosco Mesa Campus Community School and Family Resource Team
resources.description: SARRC's Kathryn G. Bosco Mesa Campus provides an inclusive Community School for young children and a Family Resource Team route for Mesa autism service navigation.
resources.address: 2165 N. Power Rd., Mesa, AZ 85215
resources.hours: SARRC general hours are Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM; contact the Family Resource Team before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Mesa campus offers SARRC's inclusive Community School for children with and without autism, ABA-based classroom support for children with ASD, parent training and Family Resource Team help for families seeking Mesa campus program information.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Community School Mesa campus is for children ages 15 months to 5 years. It serves children with and without autism; ASD supports and other campus programs may have diagnosis, assessment, payer, tuition, age and opening requirements.

**Population Served**
Families with young children, including children with autism, in Mesa and Maricopa County; Spanish-language family contact is publicized.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Family Resource Team at 602-606-9806 or use the online contact route. For Spanish, call 480-887-0784 or use the Spanish online contact route. Ask which Mesa programs are currently active, age fit, openings, tuition, insurance and next steps.

**Important Information to Know**
The official Mesa page says new programs were rolling out throughout the year, so do not assume every SARRC service is active at the Mesa campus. Confirm current service availability and whether the requested service is clinic-, home-, school- or community-based.

resources.name: Maricopa County Department of Public Health - South Phoenix Healthy Start
resources.description: Maricopa County South Phoenix Healthy Start provides free maternal and infant family support, case management, screenings, fatherhood support, childbirth and parenting education, doula services, community resources, and counseling referrals.
resources.address: 2737 W. Southern Ave., Tempe, AZ 85282; located inside WIC
resources.hours: Call 602-372-1166 or use the referral form; class and service calendars vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Healthy Start provides free family support and referrals, including case management, preventive and developmental screenings, fatherhood workshops and case management, childbirth/parenting/health/safety education, labor, delivery and postpartum doula services, community resources, and counseling services including behavioral-health and addiction referrals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program serves families who are expecting and/or parenting a child under 18 months, as well as people of reproductive age. Current geography, enrollment, and capacity should be confirmed through the referral form or phone contact.

**Population Served**
Expecting families, parents with children under 18 months, fathers, mothers, and people of reproductive age in Maricopa County, including Mesa-area families when accepted by program criteria.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Maricopa County Healthy Start referral link on the Services and Referrals page or call 602-372-1166. The public contact address is 2737 W. Southern Ave., Tempe, inside WIC.

**Important Information to Know**
Healthy Start is family support and care coordination, not guaranteed prenatal medical care or emergency help. Because the program name and page identify South Phoenix Healthy Start, Mesa residents should confirm geographic eligibility.

resources.name: Arizona State University - Veterans Upward Bound
resources.description: ASU Veterans Upward Bound is a free federal TRIO college-preparation program helping eligible Veterans in Maricopa and northern Pinal Counties build academic skills and transition to technical certificates, associate degrees, or a first bachelor’s degree.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Veterans Upward Bound supports college and training readiness. Participants may receive academic tutoring, career exploration, soft-skills development, help with financial-aid and scholarship applications, referrals to Veterans Administration information, and help transitioning to the college of their choice.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The ASU page states VUB is offered at no cost to eligible Veterans in Maricopa and northern Pinal County who are low-income or first-generation potential college students and need to improve academic skills for postsecondary study. Federal TRIO and service criteria apply.

**Population Served**
Eligible Veterans in Maricopa County and northern Pinal County, including Mesa Veterans preparing for college or training.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact ASU veteran support at 480-965-7723 and ask for current Veterans Upward Bound intake, application, location and meeting format. The former direct programme page redirected; use current ASU veteran-student routing rather than an older intake address.

**Important Information to Know**
VUB is a preparation and support program, not tuition payment. Admission to a college, VA education-benefit approval, and financial-aid awards are separate processes.

resources.name: Arizona Crime Victim Rights Law Group · No-cost counsel of record for crime victims
resources.description: No-cost nonprofit legal representation for crime victims asserting victim rights throughout Arizona criminal justice proceedings.
resources.address: P.O. Box 2323, Scottsdale, AZ 85252-2323
resources.hours: Call or email for intake; public office hours are not posted.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Arizona Crime Victim Rights Law Group provides legal services at no cost to crime victims and appears as counsel of record in pretrial, trial, sentencing, restitution, probation, release, parole, appeal, and post-conviction matters. It also analyzes civil, probate, or domestic-relations needs and may represent or refer.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The service is for eligible victims of crime involved in local, state, or federal criminal proceedings. The public page does not give a complete intake test; the organization should be contacted for case-specific eligibility.

**Population Served**
Victims of theft, fraud, violent crimes, vehicular crimes, property crimes, and family members or survivors who lost a loved one due to a crime.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-946-0832 or email info@azvictimrights.org with the case status, court dates, restitution issues and safety concerns. P.O. Box 2323, Scottsdale, AZ 85252-2323 is a mailing address.

**Important Information to Know**
This is crime-victim-rights counsel, not general criminal defense, shelter or a general family-law clinic. Related civil/probate/domestic-relations issues may be assessed for representation or referral. Eligibility, conflicts and capacity determine whether a particular case is accepted.

resources.name: Maricopa County Department of Public Health - Cavity Free AZ Sealant Program
resources.description: Maricopa County Office of Oral Health administers a school-based dental sealant program with screenings, sealants, oral health education and referrals at no cost for eligible 2nd and 6th grade students at qualifying schools.
resources.address: 301 W. Jefferson St., Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.hours: School-based schedule varies by participating school; interested schools or parents should call or use the parent form.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Dental screenings, dental sealants, oral health education and referrals delivered through qualifying schools.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program serves 2nd and 6th grade children attending schools where at least 50% of students participate in the National School Lunch Program. Services are at no cost to the school or child.

**Population Served**
Children in eligible Maricopa County schools, including qualifying Mesa schools if their school participates.

**How to Best Connect**
Parents can complete the county's parent interest form or contact their child's school. Schools and families can call Cecilia Little at 602-506-6946 to check eligibility and get information.

**Important Information to Know**
This is school-based prevention, not a walk-in dental clinic. Participation and service dates depend on school eligibility and scheduling.

resources.name: Arizona OIC — Learning Center, career training and job placement
resources.description: Arizona OIC offers Learning Center education services, career training, job placement assistance, skills assessments, career counseling, resume development, financial counseling, and free case-managed workforce support at its Phoenix site.
resources.address: 701 S. Central Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.hours: Learning Center Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:00 PM; closed holidays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Arizona OIC's Learning Center provides education services, and its career services provide free career training, job placement assistance, skills assessments, job training, career counseling, resume development, financial counseling, and individual case management for unemployed people preparing for the workforce.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Class participation requires an application at the Arizona OIC office. Adult Mesa service-area rules, income criteria and class costs beyond free career services are not fully published; confirm directly. The separately described youth summer programme is for eligible City of Phoenix residents ages 14–21; confirm its current season and enrollment.

**Population Served**
Economically disadvantaged and unemployed job seekers in the Phoenix area who can travel to the Central Avenue office for education, job training, and career services. Mesa residents should confirm acceptance before travel.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-254-5081, email azoic@azoic.org, or visit the office at 701 S. Central Ave., Phoenix to apply for classes. The Learning Center is open Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:00 PM and closed holidays.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a useful reserve option but is Phoenix-based. Confirm current classes, cost, Mesa eligibility, and whether the service needed is education, career training, or job placement.

resources.name: Arizona WIC — Statewide clinic finder
resources.description: Finds WIC clinics and an application route when a particular Mesa clinic does not fit a family’s location or schedule.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Finds WIC clinics and an application route when a particular Mesa clinic does not fit a family’s location or schedule.

**Eligibility Requirements**
WIC serves qualifying pregnant, postpartum or breastfeeding participants, infants and children under five; income and nutrition-risk screening apply.

**Population Served**
Arizona families seeking infant or young-child nutrition benefits and support.

**How to Best Connect**
Search the official clinic locator by city, ZIP or address, or call 800-252-5942 for an appointment route. Ask the clinic what documentation to bring.

**Important Information to Know**
Each clinic has its own hours and appointment capacity. The accompanying adult is not automatically eligible for benefits personally, and this research date is not agency confirmation.

resources.name: Arizona Board of Regents — Teacher Student Loan Program
resources.description: Education loans covering eligible tuition, fees and instructional materials for students preparing to become teachers at participating private colleges. The loan can be satisfied through the required teaching service.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Education loans covering eligible tuition, fees and instructional materials for students preparing to become teachers at participating private colleges. The loan can be satisfied through the required teaching service.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Arizona residence, qualifying U.S. citizenship or lawful presence, enrollment in an eligible teacher-preparation program, annual FAFSA and a signed loan agreement. Award duration depends on the degree or certification route.

**Population Served**

Eligible students preparing for teaching careers through participating Arizona private colleges.

**How to Best Connect**

Ask the participating institution’s financial-aid office about application and the current agreement. Review all financial and service obligations before accepting funds.

**Important Information to Know**

Recipients generally owe one year of teaching in an Arizona public school for each funded year and have 12 months after completion to begin service, subject to approved deferral rules. Failure to meet requirements can require repayment. Earlier awards before 2023 have different terms.

resources.name: City of Mesa Housing and Community Development - Fair Housing Coordinator complaint assistance
resources.description: City of Mesa Housing and Community Development provides Fair Housing information, materials and complaint assistance, and forwards received housing discrimination complaints to the Arizona Attorney General Civil Rights Division for investigation.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Assistance, information and materials for Fair Housing questions and complaints. The City forwards complaints it receives to the Arizona Attorney General's Office Civil Rights Division for investigation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people with fair-housing questions or suspected housing discrimination involving protected classes such as race, color, religion, sex, disability, national origin or familial status. It is not legal advice or attorney representation.

**Population Served**
Mesa residents, housing seekers and other people dealing with housing discrimination issues connected to Mesa housing.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact City of Mesa Housing and Community Development, Attn: Fair Housing Coordinator, at 480-644-5000, TDD 480-644-2778 or fairhousing@mesaaz.gov.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a local government complaint-assistance and referral/forwarding route, not a substitute for legal counsel. For landlord-tenant disputes that are not discrimination complaints, the page points users to tenant-rights and legal-aid resources.

resources.name: Community Bridges, Inc. - Permanent Supportive Housing and Rapid Rehousing
resources.description: Community Bridges, Inc. provides Permanent Supportive Housing and Rapid Rehousing with wraparound services for individuals and families experiencing homelessness, including people with significant behavioral-health, substance-use, domestic-violence, trafficking, veteran, or pregnancy/postpartum needs. Listed Arizona sites include Mesa supportive-housing locations.
resources.address: Mesa and Phoenix-area supportive housing sites
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Permanent Supportive Housing and Rapid Rehousing with wraparound services, individualized care plans, onsite or co-located support, and connections across CBI's behavioral-health and substance-use continuum.

**Eligibility Requirements**
CBI describes the program for individuals and families experiencing homelessness, especially people with chronic homelessness or significant barriers to stable housing. Specific property eligibility, referral source, clinical requirements, and vacancies must be screened directly.

**Population Served**
Individuals and families experiencing homelessness, including pregnant or postpartum women with substance-use disorders and their children, survivors of domestic violence or human trafficking and their children, veterans, and people needing behavioral-health/recovery support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call CBI's access line at 877-931-9142 or use the Make an Appointment route on the official supportive-housing page. Ask which Mesa or Maricopa County housing program and referral pathway fits the client's situation.

**Important Information to Know**
The public page lists Mesa-area housing sites but does not clearly publish a single self-referral application for every property. Treat this as a supported housing lead requiring CBI screening, not a guaranteed immediate placement.

resources.name: Chandler Regional Medical Center / CommonSpirit Health - Community Outreach Immunization Program
resources.description: CommonSpirit/Dignity Health's Community Outreach Immunization Program offers no-cost appointment-based immunization clinics for eligible children and adults through Chandler Regional Medical Center community outreach.
resources.address: 777 E. Galveston St., Chandler, AZ 85225
resources.hours: Appointments are needed for all clinics. Call or email for current appointment times and sites.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost immunization clinics for children and adults. The official page lists routine pediatric/adolescent vaccines and notes limited adult vaccine availability by location and season.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Children under age 19 qualify if uninsured, covered by insurance that does not cover vaccines, enrolled in AHCCCS, or American Indian/Alaska Native. Adults without insurance or whose insurance does not cover immunizations are also listed as eligible.

**Population Served**
Eligible children, adolescents and adults in the East Valley/Maricopa County who need no-cost immunizations.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-728-2004 or email azimmunizations@commonspirit.org for an appointment. Bring the child's immunization record and any school letters; a parent or legal guardian must be present for children's appointments.

**Important Information to Know**
The official page confirms immunizations, not a full clinic. A prior listing mentioned hearing and vision screenings for children, but that service was not confirmed on the opened official page; ask the program directly if that is needed.

resources.name: Arizona Center for the Blind and Visually Impaired - Food Program and Food Pantry for Adults with Vision Loss
resources.description: ACBVI supports adults with vision loss through whole-person health services that include nutritious meals; City of Phoenix grant information also describes weekday meals and pantry access for clients.
resources.address: 3100 E Roosevelt St, Phoenix, AZ 85008
resources.hours: Call 602-273-7411 to ask about intake, program schedule and whether food pantry access is limited to active ACBVI clients.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
ACBVI provides vision-loss services centered on independence, vocation and whole-person health. Its public page states whole-person health support includes nutritious meals, accessible transportation, behavioral health support, access to medical care and social activities. City of Phoenix food grant information describes weekday meals and food pantry access for ACBVI clients.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is for adults who are blind, visually impaired, DeafBlind, or living with combined vision and hearing loss. Food access may be tied to ACBVI client enrollment or participation, so call before referral.

**Population Served**
Adults with vision loss, including adults who are blind, visually impaired, DeafBlind, or living with combined vision and hearing loss in the Phoenix/Maricopa County area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-273-7411 or email info@acbvi.org to ask about intake and whether the client can access meals, pantry support, transportation or other whole-person health services.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a disability-specific service pathway, not a public pantry. Mesa clients should confirm service fit and transportation before referral because the center is in Phoenix.

resources.name: Purpose Healing Center - Phoenix and Scottsdale Addiction Treatment
resources.description: Purpose Healing Center provides Arizona addiction treatment through Scottsdale and Phoenix locations, including medical detox, residential inpatient rehab, PHP, IOP, outpatient care, MAT-related detox support, aftercare, and co-occurring mental-health treatment.
resources.address: Scottsdale: 8712 E Via de Commercio, Scottsdale, AZ 85258; Phoenix: 1841 N 24th St, Phoenix, AZ 85008
resources.hours: Admissions staff is advertised as available 24/7 by phone.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Medical detox, residential inpatient rehab, partial hospitalization, intensive outpatient programs, outpatient rehab, aftercare, family support, evidence-based therapy, and dual-diagnosis mental-health/addiction treatment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
People seeking alcohol or drug treatment may call admissions. Clinical fit, level of care, transportation, and insurance coverage are determined through admissions and insurance verification.

**Population Served**
Adults seeking addiction and co-occurring mental-health treatment in Scottsdale, Phoenix, and nearby Maricopa County communities, including Mesa residents who can travel or use available transportation.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-579-3319 for admissions. Confirm whether Scottsdale, Phoenix, or another location is appropriate and ask specifically about transportation from Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
Purpose says it accepts nearly all AHCCCS plans and many private insurance plans, but does not accept Medicare at this time. Transportation is listed as available with a call-for-details limitation.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Revenue - Unclaimed Property Claim Program
resources.description: Arizona Department of Revenue's Unclaimed Property program lets owners and heirs search for money or assets held by the state and file a claim with identity and ownership evidence.
resources.address: 1600 W Monroe St, Phoenix, AZ 85007; Unclaimed Property Unit mailing addresses vary by form
resources.hours: Unclaimed Property phone support is listed Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM for requesting a claim form.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free search and claim process for unclaimed money or property held by Arizona, such as uncashed checks, deposits, insurance proceeds, accounts, overpayments, or other reported property.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A name match is not enough. The claimant must submit a claim form and positive proof that they are the rightful owner or authorized heir/representative, including identity and evidence connecting the owner to the reported address or property holder.

**Population Served**
Arizona property owners, heirs, and authorized representatives, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents who may have unclaimed property held by the state.

**How to Best Connect**
Search and file through the Arizona Department of Revenue Unclaimed Property website. If the claimant cannot print a form, call 602-364-0380 Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM to request a claim form.

**Important Information to Know**
This returns the claimant's own property; it is not hardship funding. ADOR's FAQ says claims are processed within 90 days of receipt, so it should not be treated as same-week emergency money.

resources.name: Trans Spectrum of Arizona and The Queer Center - Phoenix Dream Boutique and YouPhoria Project
resources.description: The Phoenix Dream Boutique provides free gender-affirming clothing, jewelry, toiletries and, through the YouPhoria Project, binders, tucking garments, packing shorts and other shapewear by appointment.
resources.address: Phoenix appointment site; street address provided through appointment process
resources.hours: By appointment only. Operating hours: every Tuesday 7:30-9:00 PM; 2nd and 4th Saturdays 12:30-2:00 PM; closed holidays and holiday weekends.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free gender-affirming clothing, jewelry and toiletries for transgender and gender-expansive people. The YouPhoria Project provides free gender-affirming undergarments and shapewear such as binders, tucking panties, packing shorts, breast plates and forms.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The boutique is exclusively for transgender and gender-expansive individuals and is by appointment only. Guests under 18 must be accompanied by a legal guardian for the full appointment.

**Population Served**
Transgender and gender-expansive people in the Phoenix area, including Mesa residents who can schedule and travel to an appointment.

**How to Best Connect**
Submit the appointment request form on the Phoenix Dream Boutique page. The public page does not publish the street address; use the official appointment process for details. Private appointments may be available only during the first 30 minutes of operating hours.

**Important Information to Know**
Do not send a client without an appointment. Clothing donations were paused until fall on the page inspected 2026-09-26, but guest appointments remained described; inventory and appointment availability may vary.

resources.name: Terros Health - Pinchot Gardens Residential Recovery
resources.description: Residential substance-use treatment for women, including pregnant women and women parenting children, with supervised treatment, counseling, primary and psychiatric care, childcare, laundry, parenting, skills-building, culinary classes, and family-style dining.
resources.address: 3301 E Pinchot Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85018
resources.hours: Residential program; referral timing and availability must be confirmed with Terros.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Pinchot Gardens Residential Recovery provides 24/7 structured residential substance-use treatment for women. Terros describes intensive supervised treatment, individual and group counseling, primary and psychiatric care, child care, laundry services, parenting classes, skills-building, culinary classes, family-style dining, and reintegration support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Women seeking residential substance-use treatment should contact Terros for referral and screening. The program specifically includes women who are parenting or pregnant; clinical fit, payer requirements, and bed availability must be confirmed.

**Population Served**
Women with substance-use disorder, including pregnant women and women with children.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-808-2825 or email womensresidential@terroshealth.org for referrals and information. The listed address is 3301 E Pinchot Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85018.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm whether children can stay onsite in the specific circumstance, what documentation is needed, current capacity, insurance/payment, and transportation before referral.

resources.name: Maricopa Community Colleges · Achieving a College Education (ACE)
resources.description: Achieving a College Education (ACE) is a free early-college bridge program for Maricopa County high school sophomores facing barriers, offering up to 24 college credits toward a degree or certificate through participating Maricopa Community Colleges, including Mesa Community College.
resources.address: Mesa Community College ACE contact: 1833 W. Southern Ave., Mesa, AZ 85202
resources.hours: Application and notification timelines vary by college; ACE recruiting and application activity generally occurs during sophomore year.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free college-credit early-college program that helps high school students finish high school strong, plan next steps, and earn up to 24 college credits toward a degree or certificate at a Maricopa Community College or transfer university.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Students should be Maricopa County high school sophomores with at least 6 high school credits who are working hard despite barriers such as financial challenges, first-generation college status, foster care, transitional housing, single-parent household, work, or parenting responsibilities. Application materials include an essay, two recommendations, unofficial transcript, commitment statement, and release forms; some colleges may interview applicants.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County high school students, including Mesa Community College ACE applicants, who face barriers to college access and want to earn college credits early.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the ACE application link on the Maricopa page or contact Mesa Community College ACE at 480-461-6200. Ask the student's high school counselor whether ACE recruiters are visiting and which campus is the best fit.

**Important Information to Know**
All ACE colleges except Rio Salado are in-person; Rio Salado offers a fully online program. Applications are time-sensitive and generally tied to sophomore-year recruitment, with college-specific timelines.

resources.name: Beacon Group — Pre-Employment Transition Services
resources.description: No-cost workshops in job exploration, further education, workplace readiness, work-based learning and self-advocacy.
resources.address: 1951 W. Camelback Rd., Suite 400, Phoenix, AZ 85015
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

No-cost workshops in job exploration, further education, workplace readiness, work-based learning and self-advocacy.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Students ages 14–22 with a documented disability who are enrolled in an education setting. The provider includes public, private, charter, home-school, college, GED and vocational education settings.

**Population Served**

Students with disabilities preparing for work, including Maricopa County students when workshop arrangements fit.

**How to Best Connect**

Call Beacon’s Phoenix office at 602-685-9703 or complete its contact form. Individuals and school staff can ask about workshops and local arrangements.

**Important Information to Know**

Confirm dates, Mesa access and any transportation arrangement. The workshops prepare students for work; they do not guarantee a job or replace individualized VR services.

resources.name: Axiom Community of Recovery — Reentry and peer support
resources.description: Offers peer recovery, workforce development and practical reintegration support, including prison in-reach and housing navigation.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Offers peer recovery, workforce development and practical reintegration support, including prison in-reach and housing navigation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Confirm current enrollment, funding and program fit; post-treatment support is described as a nine- to twelve-month pathway.

**Population Served**
People rebuilding after substance-use treatment or incarceration in the Phoenix area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-325-2937 and ask about current reentry enrollment and access from Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
Housing navigation is not a guaranteed bed. Match this nonprofit’s identity separately from Axiom Care’s RCBM and Set for Success programs.

resources.name: AZ Veterans Resource Center — case management and family/peer support
resources.description: AZ Veterans Resource Center is a Mesa veteran-led, trauma-informed resource and wellness center offering one-on-one case management, housing and employment support, wellness programming, peer/family support and community connection.
resources.address: 1833 W Main St., Suite 103, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8 AM-4 PM; Saturday by appointment; Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
One-on-one case management and resource navigation for veterans and family members, including help identifying immediate needs, housing and employment support, wellness and healing programs, peer/family support, community events and connections to trusted partner organizations.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For veterans and veteran family members seeking veteran-centered support. Specific housing, employment, benefits or wellness resources depend on assessment and partner-program eligibility.

**Population Served**
Veterans and veteran family members in Mesa and Arizona partner networks.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-834-2105, email info@azvrc.org or visit 1833 W Main St., Suite 103 during posted hours. Calling first is best for same-day availability.

**Important Information to Know**
Housing, employment and benefit help begins with assessment and service connections; funding, placement and approval are not guaranteed. Use 1833 W. Main St., Suite 103, rather than the older Azura/Centennial address. Separate partner services, including tax preparation, can have their own locations and schedules.

resources.name: Neighborhood Ministries - Food Bank
resources.description: Neighborhood Ministries operates a Friday drive-through emergency food bank in inner-city Phoenix with large family food boxes and wraparound-service connections.
resources.address: 1918 W Van Buren St, Phoenix, AZ 85009
resources.hours: Food bank Fridays 8:30 AM-11:00 AM, drive-through distribution. Office Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Neighborhood Ministries' Food Bank provides drive-through emergency food boxes with shelf-stable food, meat, dairy and fresh produce when available, and connects families to other wraparound services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official food bank page does not list Mesa eligibility, ID or document rules. Call before referring a client from outside the immediate Phoenix area.

**Population Served**
Low-income families in inner-city Phoenix and surrounding communities who can attend the Friday drive-through distribution.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to 1918 W Van Buren St, Phoenix on Fridays from 8:30 AM to 11:00 AM or call 602-252-5225.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a Phoenix reserve option, not Mesa-local. The provider describes culturally relevant food for primarily Latinx families, but the page does not establish Mesa-specific service-area access.

resources.name: Dignity Foundation - Dignity Kids
resources.description: Dignity Kids is a Dignity Foundation referral-partner program where referred families can shop for child-specific essentials such as cribs, car seats, high chairs, diapers and wipes.
resources.address: 6501 E Greenway Pkwy, Suite 103-502, Scottsdale, AZ 85254
resources.hours: Referral-only; call or use the referral-partner process for current appointment timing.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A shopping experience for referred families to select child-specific essentials such as cribs, car seats, high chairs, diapers and wipes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Families must be referred through trusted community organizations or referral partners. Child age range, safety rules and inventory are not fully published and should be confirmed by the referring agency.

**Population Served**
Referred families with children who need foundational child-safety and care items while stabilizing their household.

**How to Best Connect**
