Work through a caseworker or nonprofit partner that can submit a Dignity Foundation referral. For questions, call 602-848-2422 or email ktrapp@dignityfoundation.org.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a direct public baby-supplies closet. Inventory, appointment scheduling, car-seat or crib safety standards and transportation assistance should be confirmed before referral.

resources.name: AllThrive 365 — Wickenburg Community Action Program
resources.description: A local Community Action Program access point for eligible Wickenburg-area households needing rental, utility or weatherization assistance.
resources.address: 466 W Wickenburg Way, Wickenburg, AZ 85390
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
AllThrive's Wickenburg resource center operates a Community Action Program office connecting local households with rental and utility assistance and weatherization resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on the assistance program, the household's assigned service area, income and other required documents. The resource center must confirm current funding and intake.

**Population Served**
Households in the Wickenburg-area catchment served by this office. City of Mesa residents should use their own local intake.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 928-684-7894 and ask specifically for Community Action Program assistance. The center is at 466 W Wickenburg Way. Arrange the appropriate intake before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a distant county reserve option for clients living in its service area, not a Mesa walk-in fund. Center activities and meal services have separate schedules and eligibility; they do not establish CAP approval.

resources.name: DES Family Caregiver Support and Arizona Caregiver Resource Line
resources.description: DES Family Caregiver Support connects unpaid caregivers to information, local resources, support, respite options and the Arizona Caregiver Resource Line, working with Area Agencies on Aging and the Arizona Caregiver Coalition.
resources.hours: Arizona Caregiver Resource Line: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-4:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Information about available caregiver services, assistance accessing supportive services, counseling/support groups/training, respite care and limited supplemental services. Lifespan Respite may be consumer-directed respite or adult day health center respite.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Caregiver support and respite rules differ by programme. DES describes older-caregiver respite/supplemental services tied to substantial help with at least two daily-living activities and a moderate/high risk assessment for respite. Lifespan Respite has separate constant-care, other-funding and living/proximity requirements; confirm the current Arizona Caregiver Coalition rules for the particular option.

**Population Served**
Arizona unpaid family caregivers, including caregivers in Mesa and Maricopa County caring for older adults, people with disabilities or people with long-term-care needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Arizona Caregiver Resource Line at 888-737-7494 Monday-Friday, 9:00 AM-4:00 PM. Ask about local Area Agency on Aging options, Lifespan Respite, adult day health center respite and current funding or provider capacity.

**Important Information to Know**
The Family Caregiver Reimbursement Program is no longer taking applications. DES states it does not directly pay a caregiver simply to care for a spouse, relative, neighbor or loved one; paid caregiver pathways usually involve ALTCS eligibility and a contracted home-health agency.

resources.name: Desert Financial Foundation — Adult Learners Scholarship
resources.description: A recurring scholarship supporting adult education at Arizona colleges, universities and certification programs. The published 2026 award is $3,000.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

A recurring scholarship supporting adult education at Arizona colleges, universities and certification programs. The published 2026 award is $3,000.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Age 25 or older, current Desert Financial membership in good standing, demonstrated financial need and eligible Arizona study apply. The 2026 cycle requires study in 2026–2027 and graduation no earlier than spring 2027.

**Population Served**

Eligible adult credit-union members returning to or continuing education.

**How to Best Connect**

The current application period has ended. Monitor the official scholarship page or ask the foundation about the next cycle.

**Important Information to Know**

Future dates, award amounts and eligibility may change. Do not treat the visible Apply button as evidence that applications are open.

resources.name: Arizona Board of Regents — AzLEAP College Grants
resources.description: Need-based grants for Arizona undergraduate students at participating colleges and universities. The published maximum is $2,500 per academic year; typical awards may be smaller.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Need-based grants for Arizona undergraduate students at participating colleges and universities. The published maximum is $2,500 per academic year; typical awards may be smaller.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Arizona residence, at least half-time undergraduate enrollment at a participating Arizona institution, and substantial financial need established through FAFSA and Pell Grant eligibility. The institution determines the award.

**Population Served**

Low-income Arizona undergraduate students, including qualifying Mesa Community College students.

**How to Best Connect**

Ask the college financial-aid office about AzLEAP. MCC is on the 2026–2027 participating list and is marked as automatically considering admitted students through its aid process; there is no separate application to the Board of Regents listed for MCC.

**Important Information to Know**

Eligibility does not guarantee the maximum amount. Award timing, funds and institution-specific administration should be confirmed before relying on the grant.

resources.name: United Cerebral Palsy of Central Arizona - Pediatric Therapy and Home and Community Based Services
resources.description: United Cerebral Palsy of Central Arizona provides pediatric therapy and DDD home- and community-based attendant care, habilitation and respite for children and adults with physical or developmental disabilities.
resources.address: 1802 W. Parkside Lane, Phoenix, AZ 85027; UCP Downtown East Clinic, 5025 E. Washington St. #102, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: Laura Dozer Campus: Monday-Friday 7 AM-6 PM. UCP Downtown East Clinic: Monday-Friday 8 AM-6 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
UCP offers pediatric occupational, feeding, physical and speech therapy, AAC, motor-disorder supports, DME or wheelchair evaluation, upper-extremity splinting, home- and community-based attendant care, habilitation and respite.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Pediatric therapy serves children of all abilities and diagnoses, with special focus on physical challenges, delays and disabilities. HCBS is for children and adults served by Arizona DDD; DDD eligibility and authorization are required for those services.

**Population Served**
Children with cerebral palsy, motor disorders, developmental delays, physical disabilities and other diagnoses; children and adults with physical or developmental disabilities needing DDD HCBS in Central Arizona.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-943-5472 for general services, use the therapy referral form for pediatric therapy, or call 602-695-5789 for HCBS support. Ask about Mesa home-service availability, insurance, DDD authorization, private pay and current openings. Bilingual English/Spanish therapists are available; request the preferred language and confirm language support for any HCBS service.

**Important Information to Know**
Therapy payer participation, private-pay costs, scholarship options, DDD authorization and home-service availability must be confirmed. UCP lists Phoenix and Downtown East clinic sites rather than a Mesa clinic.

resources.name: National Community Health Partners - Housing for Heroes: Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF)
resources.description: National Community Health Partners Housing for Heroes is a VA SSVF-funded housing support program serving Maricopa, Pinal, and Yuma Counties with case management, housing assistance, temporary housing, utility assistance, benefit acquisition, transportation related to housing plans, and HUD-VASH deposit support.
resources.address: Maricopa County office: 1232 E. Broadway Rd. #211, Tempe, AZ 85282
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Veteran-family homelessness prevention and rapid rehousing through case management, housing search, budgeting and benefits navigation. Depending on the case plan, help can include rent, utilities, security/utility deposits, temporary housing, transportation, emergency supplies and connections to legal/employment support. HUD-VASH participants may qualify for SSVF deposit help under separate rules.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Very-low-income veteran households experiencing homelessness or at risk of losing housing must meet SSVF rules. Screening considers housing need, income and the sustainable housing plan. HUD-VASH recipients may qualify for deposit support if they have not received SSVF deposit assistance in the past two years.

**Population Served**
Veterans and veteran families in Maricopa, Pinal, and Yuma Counties, including Mesa and East Valley households in Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Maricopa Intake Form on the Housing for Heroes page or call 480-361-0177. The Maricopa coordinator can be reached at 520-330-8095 or LWilson@nchponline.org. Confirm arrangements for the office at 1232 E. Broadway Road, #211, Tempe.

**Important Information to Know**
SSVF is targeted housing stabilization, not a general rent fund or guaranteed immediate motel placement. Assistance depends on eligibility, case management, a sustainable housing plan, and available funds.

resources.name: Arizona Friends of Foster Children Foundation - Keys to Success Housing Support
resources.description: Arizona Friends of Foster Children Foundation's Keys to Success program serves eligible current and former Arizona foster youth ages 16-26 with individualized transition support across education, employment, housing and financial literacy, including a public youth referral form.
resources.address: 360 E Coronado Rd, Suite 190, Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.hours: Use the online referral form or call AFFCF for program questions; coaching and services are engagement-based.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Transition coaching and support built around education, employment, housing and financial literacy. Housing support may include coaching, planning, resource connection and help stabilizing independent living rather than a dedicated housing unit.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Youth must be ages 16-26, reside in Maricopa, Pima or Yavapai County, have been in Arizona foster care at any time after age 15 or reunified with biological family after age 14, demonstrate commitment to career-development services and sign the youth participation agreement.

**Population Served**
Eligible Arizona foster-care-experienced youth and young adults ages 16-26 in Maricopa, Pima or Yavapai County, including Mesa-area youth.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Refer a Youth form on the Keys to Success page or call AFFCF at 602-252-9445. Be ready to explain the youth's foster-care history, county of residence, age, current housing concern and willingness to participate.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not an emergency shelter or apartment provider. Housing help is part of a broader transition program and depends on eligibility, engagement and available resources.

resources.name: A New Leaf / MesaCAN - Arizona Diaper Distribution Pilot Program
resources.description: A New Leaf/MesaCAN is listed by Wildfire as the Maricopa and Pinal County Community Action Agency access point for the Arizona Diaper Distribution Pilot Program, offering free diapers or pull-ups for qualifying families when supplies and funding are available.
resources.address: 635 E. Broadway Rd., Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: Wildfire lists distribution during the third full week of the month, Monday-Friday 8:30 AM-4:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Arizona Diaper Distribution Pilot Program provides free diapers or pull-ups through local Community Action Agencies. The Mesa access site for Maricopa and Pinal counties is A New Leaf/MesaCAN.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Families apply through their local Community Action Agency and need birth certificates for each child, a photo ID, and proof of income from the past 30 days. Eligibility and quantity depend on pilot-program rules, funding, and inventory.

**Population Served**
Low-income families in Maricopa and Pinal counties who need diapers or pull-ups for children in their care, including Mesa families applying through MesaCAN.

**How to Best Connect**
Call A New Leaf/MesaCAN at 480-833-9200 before visiting. Wildfire lists the Mesa location as 635 E. Broadway Rd. and distribution during the third full week of the month, Monday-Friday 8:30 AM-4:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a pilot and supply-dependent program. Confirm current application status, appointment requirements, diaper sizes, pull-up availability, and whether the distribution week has changed before sending a family.

resources.name: Central Arizona Shelter Services - Rapid Re-Housing and Prevention
resources.description: CASS Rapid Re-Housing and Prevention helps Maricopa County individuals and families secure or keep housing through short-term rent and utility help, security deposit support, case management, landlord mediation, tenancy skills, budgeting, benefits enrollment, and coordinated-entry housing resources.
resources.address: 230 S 12th Avenue, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Short-term rental and utility assistance, security deposit support, case management, tenancy skills, landlord mediation, budgeting help, benefits enrollment, and housing navigation to help people secure housing or prevent a return to homelessness.

**Eligibility Requirements**
CASS describes the program as working in partnership with Maricopa County Coordinated Entry. Assistance is not a general walk-in fund and depends on assessment, program fit, and available funding.

**Population Served**
Individuals and families in the Phoenix/Maricopa County area who are experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness and are connected to appropriate housing resources.

**How to Best Connect**
For immediate shelter or housing-resource access, call 2-1-1 and ask about Coordinated Entry or CASS housing supports. The CASS services page also directs people needing immediate help to 2-1-1.

**Important Information to Know**
Help is capacity- and eligibility-limited. Calling or being assessed does not guarantee rent assistance, a deposit, or a housing placement.

resources.name: Life Wireless - Arizona Lifeline Free Phone Service
resources.description: Life Wireless offers Arizona Lifeline cellular service for qualifying low-income customers, with a free listed monthly plan that includes unlimited talk, unlimited text and data subject to coverage and plan terms.
resources.hours: Apply online by ZIP code/email; support and coverage checks are web-based.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Life Wireless lists an Arizona Lifeline plan with free monthly cellular service, unlimited nationwide calling, unlimited text messaging and high-speed data.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility can be based on participation in SNAP, Section 8 Federal Public Housing Assistance, SSI, Medicaid, Veterans Pension or Survivors Pension, qualifying Tribal programs, or income at or below 135% of Federal Poverty Guidelines. Lifeline is limited to one benefit per household and cannot be combined with another Lifeline offer.

**Population Served**
Eligible low-income Arizona individuals and households in Life Wireless coverage areas.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Arizona Lifeline page to enter ZIP code and email and start the application. Check coverage for the actual Mesa or Maricopa County address before relying on service.

**Important Information to Know**
Coverage and service are not available in all areas, plans can change without notice, and taxes or fees may be charged separately. Device inclusion was not confirmed from the page and should be checked during application.

resources.name: The Welcome to America Project - Career Bridge Program
resources.description: The Welcome to America Project Career Bridge Program helps resettled refugees in Arizona with prior education, certification or professional experience move toward career-aligned work through CV help, interview preparation, industry-specific job readiness training, mentorship, employer referrals, free training and family budget guidance.
resources.address: 1711 W. University Drive, Suite 158, Tempe, AZ 85281
resources.hours: Contact page lists office/drop-off hours Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Saturday 8:00 AM-11:00 AM; Career Bridge meetings or enrollment should be arranged before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Career Bridge helps resettled refugees move from initial survival jobs toward work closer to their prior training or professional goals. Services include CV building, interview preparation, industry-specific job readiness training, mentorship, employer connections/referrals, free training and family budget guidance.

**Eligibility Requirements**
WTAP lists Career Bridge eligibility as ORR-designated status, an Employment Authorization Document, and helpful but not required English proficiency plus prior experience, certification or education. Confirm current enrollment fit with WTAP before referral.

**Population Served**
Refugees recently relocated to Arizona through the U.S. resettlement program, including newcomer families and working professionals in Maricopa County who can connect with WTAP.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Career Bridge enrollment link on the WTAP Career Bridge page, or call 602-490-0088 or email info@wtap.org. WTAP also lists its Tempe location at 1711 W. University Drive, Suite 158; arrange enrollment or an appointment before sending a client in person.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general public job center. It is specifically for refugees/newcomers with work authorization and is especially relevant for people with prior education, certification or professional experience. Capacity, cohort timing and employer referrals are not guaranteed.

resources.name: Catholic Charities Community Services Arizona - Familias Unidas Immigration Legal Services
resources.description: Catholic Charities Community Services Arizona provides low-cost immigration legal help in Maricopa County, including citizenship applications, family petitions, work authorization, case-status information, asylum/deportation representation, and petitions for battered spouses and children.
resources.address: 5151 N. 19th Avenue, Phoenix, AZ 85015
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Low-cost immigration consultations, document preparation and representation for accepted matters. Listed services include citizenship/naturalization, family petitions, work authorization, pending-case information, asylum/deportation matters and petitions for battered spouses or children. Related social-service connections may be available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on the immigration relief sought, case facts, conflicts, fees and capacity. Ask about the particular matter; there is no single status rule covering all survivor and asylum remedies.

**Population Served**
Immigrants, refugees, citizens seeking family reunification and other people with supported immigration legal needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the local immigration-services contact at 602-749-4415, or Catholic Charities at 855-316-2229, to arrange intake and confirm the service location.

**Important Information to Know**
Low-cost does not mean free. Confirm acceptance, fees, representation and deadlines for the particular matter, especially asylum/removal or simple lost-document replacement. Bring relevant immigration documents, notices and prior filings to the arranged consultation; not every matter is accepted.

resources.name: Promise Arizona - Immigration Services and Citizenship Workshops
resources.description: Promise Arizona provides community-based immigration assistance focused on N-400 citizenship applications, I-90 green-card renewals, and citizenship workshops, with bilingual contact information and weekday hours.
resources.address: 410 E Southern Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85040
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM for immigration-service questions.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Promise Arizona's immigration page provides N-400 citizenship application pre-screening, I-90 green-card renewal pre-screening, and links to upcoming citizenship workshops. The page provides bilingual English/Spanish instructions.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Citizenship and green-card renewal help depends on the applicant's immigration status, document history, and current federal requirements. The public page does not clearly state attorney representation, fee rules, or full case-screening criteria.

**Population Served**
Arizona immigrant community members, including Spanish-speaking residents and Maricopa County clients who can contact or travel to the Phoenix office.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-288-3663 or use the immigration page's prescreening and workshop links. The office address is 410 E Southern Ave, Phoenix. The page lists immigration-service question hours as Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
Use this as a citizenship and green-card-renewal assistance/workshop route, not as confirmed broad immigration-court representation. Confirm fees, appointment requirements, and whether the client's exact issue is within current scope before travel.

resources.name: Holy Cross Catholic Church Conference - St. Vincent de Paul Society Mesa
resources.description: The Holy Cross St. Vincent de Paul Conference provides food, clothing and other assistance to neighbors in need through a Mesa parish-based conference with message-based intake.
resources.address: Holy Cross Catholic Parish, 1244 S Power Rd, Mesa, AZ 85206
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 7:00 AM-12:00 PM, according to the parish page.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Holy Cross St. Vincent de Paul provides food, clothing and other assistance to neighbors in need. The page also notes socks are distributed to people who are homeless year-round.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The conference serves neighbors in need through the local parish conference model. Exact service boundary, documentation and whether clothing is provided directly or by voucher should be confirmed when calling.

**Population Served**
Mesa-area neighbors in need, including people experiencing homelessness who come to the office for interview and assistance.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-985-4259 and leave a message; the conference says calls will be returned. The office is at the north end of the Holy Cross grounds and is open Monday through Thursday from 7:00 AM to noon.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a local access point and may be more practical than calling the general SVdP office for nearby Mesa residents. Assistance is volunteer-run and neighborhood/conference based, so clients should not assume same-day clothing, furniture or household vouchers are guaranteed.

resources.name: City of Mesa Utilities - Utility Bill Payment Extension and Payment Arrangements
resources.description: City of Mesa utility customers with a past-due balance can request payment arrangements or payment-extension guidance to help get their account back on track.
resources.address: 55 N. Center St., Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Contact Center representatives Monday-Thursday 7:00 AM-6:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Payment arrangements and payment-extension guidance for eligible City of Mesa utility customers with past-due utility bill balances. The page also points customers to MesaCAN and Aster Aging for additional assistance.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The customer must have a City of Mesa utility account with an outstanding balance. Eligibility may be affected by four payment arrangements in a 12-month period, two or more broken arrangements in a 12-month period, current Budget Billing enrollment, a final Mesa utility bill, or a returned last bill payment.

**Population Served**
City of Mesa utility customers who need more time to pay a past-due municipal utility bill.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-644-2221 Monday–Thursday, 7 a.m.–6 p.m. to request an arrangement or ask about the account. For delinquent-account, extension, arrangement or returned-check issues, contact creditservices@mesaaz.gov. The city also points to MesaCAN and Aster Aging for separate assistance.

**Important Information to Know**
Pay current charges plus the arranged installment. An arrangement does not forgive debt; breaking it may result in disconnection. The stated summer/excessive-heat disconnection protection concerns electricity, not a blanket protection for gas or water.

resources.name: MCSO REDEEM Jail Substance Abuse & Re-Entry Program - current access unresolved
resources.description: REDEEM is a reported Maricopa County jail substance-use and reentry program. Evidence supports the lead as a county/MCSO jail program concept, but the current public award page did not surface the program details and no public enrollment route was confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Historical descriptions identify REDEEM as an eight-week in-custody substance-use and reentry curriculum for sentenced medium/high-risk inmates, covering substance-use treatment, cognitive restructuring, release preparation, anger management, parenting and related supports. Current operation and access need confirmation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Unresolved. The lead appears limited to people in the Maricopa County jail system, likely based on sentence status, risk level, facility placement and jail program screening.

**Population Served**
Potentially sentenced people in Maricopa County jail custody with substance-use and reentry needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Do not send as a public referral until MCSO or Maricopa County confirms the current program name, facility availability and enrollment route. If a client is in custody, ask jail programs or classification staff whether REDEEM or its successor is available.

**Important Information to Know**
The current referral route and active programme details need administrator confirmation before it can be used as a client referral.
resources.resolutionReason: The submitted source did not currently expose the REDEEM detail in bounded checks, while county search evidence indicates a REDEEM jail substance-use/reentry program. Current availability, intake and facility access remain consequentially unresolved.

resources.name: AZRSOL — New Directions Reentry Stipend
resources.description: Offers a one-time award of up to $250 toward qualifying practical expenses after release.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Offers a one-time award of up to $250 toward qualifying practical expenses after release.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The current application requires an Arizona ADCRR sexual-offense conviction, Arizona residence outside custody, release within twelve months and income below 150% of federal poverty guidelines. A later incarceration for another offense needs the specified connection to the qualifying history.

**Population Served**
Qualifying Arizonans returning from custody with sexual-offense histories.

**How to Best Connect**
Download the current New Directions application from AZRSOL’s reentry-resources page and follow its submission instructions; document income and expenses.

**Important Information to Know**
Funding and approval are not guaranteed. The saved application was updated July 20, 2026 and is not valid after June 30, 2027; recheck the form before applying. It covers limited practical expenses, not ongoing support.

resources.name: Maricopa County Human Services Department - Senior & Adult Independent Living Program (SAIL)
resources.description: SAIL provides no-cost case management for eligible Maricopa County seniors and adults with diagnosed physical disabilities, coordinating in-home supports such as home-delivered meals, homemaking, personal care, adult day health care and referrals to other aging resources.
resources.phone: Senior HELP LINE 602-264-4357 or 888-783-7500; TTY 711; Deaf/HOH text 520-775-1899; county inquiries 602-506-0589
resources.address: In-home assessment and telephone screening; no public walk-in intake is established.
resources.hours: Area Agency on Aging Senior Help Line is described by the county as 24-hour. County general inquiries can be made during county business hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost county case management, in-home assessment, referrals and monitoring of changing needs. Coordinated supports can include adult day health, home-delivered meals, homemaking/grocery-shopping help and personal care. Weekday home-delivered meals may fit assessed homebound clients unable to prepare meals safely; the provider determines service details.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program serves Maricopa County residents who are age 60 or older, or age 18 or older with a diagnosed physical disability and eligible for SSI disability payments. Priority is given to people with the greatest economic and social need.

**Population Served**
Seniors and adults with physical disabilities in Maricopa County who need help remaining independent at home.

**How to Best Connect**
Start by calling the Area Agency on Aging Senior Help Line at 602-264-4357, toll-free 888-783-7500, TTY/TDD 711, or HOH/Deaf text line 520-775-1899. For county general inquiries, call 602-506-0589.

**Important Information to Know**
An in-home assessment can take up to two hours. Eligibility, funding and provider capacity determine services; waits and short-term support are possible, and a meal provider may request a contribution. SAIL is not direct cash assistance, a public ride service or an immediate meal-order line. Archived county supply/mobility pilots are not established current offers.

resources.name: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps - Phoenix Job Corps Center
resources.description: Phoenix Job Corps Center is a federally funded no-cost career training and education program for eligible low-income young adults, with hands-on training, education support, campus life and placement help.
resources.address: 518 S 3rd St, Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.hours: Apply online anytime; admissions review and center schedules vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Job Corps offers no-cost career technical training, education toward a high school diploma or equivalent, hands-on training in in-demand fields, campus support and career transition support. Phoenix Job Corps is the local center for Maricopa County applicants.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Generally, Job Corps students are low-income young adults ages 16 through 24 who meet citizenship, residency or other approved status requirements, background requirements and readiness expectations. Admissions staff review each application.

**Population Served**
Eligible young adults in the Phoenix and Mesa area who need no-cost residential or center-based career training and education support.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through the Job Corps application portal or call 800-733-JOBS / 800-733-5627. After the online application, an admissions representative reviews eligibility and training availability.

**Important Information to Know**
Admissions staff assess eligibility and any exceptions. Application review can take time and popular trades may have waitlists. Ask about current intake, residential arrangements, available training and support needs. Identity, age, income, status documentation and background-check authorization may be required; admission and employment are not guaranteed.

resources.name: AzDA Cares Foundation - Give Kids A Smile Arizona
resources.description: AzDA Cares Foundation's Give Kids A Smile Arizona is an event-based free dental care and oral-health education program for underserved children, offering cleanings, screenings, fluoride treatments and some basic restorative procedures at participating events.
resources.hours: Event dates vary. The official page says recent events are finished and upcoming dates are being planned; join the email list for updates.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Event-based free dental services and education for children, including cleanings, screenings, fluoride treatments and some basic restorative procedures.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is described for children in underserved communities who might not otherwise have access to adequate dental care. Event-specific registration, age limits and site rules must be checked for each event.

**Population Served**
Children in underserved Arizona communities, including Phoenix metro events that have included Midwestern and ASDOH/Mesa-related sites.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Give Kids A Smile page to sign up for Arizona event information. AzDA Cares lists office hours Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, and a mailing address at 3193 N Drinkwater Blvd, Scottsdale, AZ 85251.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not continuous clinic care. The official page says recent events were finished and upcoming dates were being planned, so confirm a current date, site and registration route before presenting it as an appointment option.

resources.name: AARP Foundation - Senior Community Service Employment Program, Arizona
resources.description: AARP Foundation SCSEP in Arizona helps eligible adults age 55 and older gain paid on-the-job training through local nonprofit or public host agencies, with Maricopa County listed in its service area.
resources.address: 4520 North Central Ave, Suite 575, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.hours: Work Resources Helpline Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-6:00 PM Eastern Time.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
AARP Foundation's Senior Community Service Employment Program helps adults age 55 and older gain skills for better jobs through paid on-the-job training at local nonprofit or public agencies. Participants earn modest income while building work experience.

**Eligibility Requirements**
SCSEP generally serves unemployed low-income adults age 55 and older. AARP Foundation staff screen for eligibility and local availability; slot limits or waitlists may apply.

**Population Served**
Older adults in Arizona counties served by AARP Foundation SCSEP, including Maricopa County and Mesa residents. Spanish-language helpline support is available.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the AARP Foundation Work Resources Helpline at 855-850-2525 to check eligibility and get application assistance. The Arizona listing shows 4520 North Central Ave, Suite 575, Phoenix, AZ 85012.

**Important Information to Know**
SCSEP is paid training and job-search support, not a guaranteed permanent job. Local slots may be limited, and acceptance depends on eligibility and availability.

resources.name: Streets of Joy - Food Center
resources.description: Streets of Joy Food Center provides first-come, first-served food boxes in Mesa with staples such as milk, eggs, meat, vegetables, bread and fruit when available.
resources.address: 451 E 4th Pl, Mesa, AZ 85203
resources.hours: Wednesdays 2:00 PM-4:00 PM; Saturdays 1:00 PM-4:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Food boxes with basic nourishment such as milk, eggs, meat, vegetables, bread and fruit when available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official food center page says there are no requirements. Distribution is first come, first served.

**Population Served**
Mesa households needing food support.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to Streets of Joy, 451 E 4th Pl, Mesa, during posted Food Center hours. Call 480-757-6921 or email info@streetsofjoy.com with questions.

**Important Information to Know**
Food contents depend on supply, and first-come service can run out. The page does not state a household visit limit, so call if frequency matters.

resources.name: Father Matters - Job & Training Institute Reentry Program
resources.description: Father Matters Job & Training Institute Reentry Program offers pre- and post-release employment training for people currently incarcerated and releasing to Maricopa County, including customer-service occupational skills, Arizona Career Readiness Credential, career planning, employer connections and supportive assistance.
resources.address: 3146 E. Wier Ave., Suite 26, Phoenix, AZ 85040; program page also lists RM 28
resources.hours: In-custody clients should ask their correctional officer about the next information or enrollment session; released clients can call or schedule a call.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Eight-week pre-release training in customer-service skills, Arizona Career Readiness Credential/job readiness, career planning, life skills, mentoring and transition planning. Continuing support for up to one year after release can include case management, employer connections, retention/workshops/job fairs and practical help such as ID/birth-certificate or work-shoe vouchers, bus cards, clothing, food/household supplies and eyeglasses referrals. Confirm which supports are available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Official eligibility is currently incarcerated, releasing to Maricopa County, male or female, and releasing within 120 days.

**Population Served**
Men and women currently incarcerated and preparing to release to Maricopa County, with post-release support for returning community members.

**How to Best Connect**
In custody, ask the correctional officer when Father Matters' next information or enrollment session will be held. Community contact: 602-774-3298, info@fathermatters.org, or schedule a call through the website.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a reentry program, not a general public job center. Availability depends on facility access, enrollment sessions and post-release eligibility. The official page shows both RM 28 and Suite 26 references at the Wier Avenue address; call before visiting.

resources.name: Arizona Foster Youth — Public College Tuition Waiver
resources.description: A tuition-and-fee waiver for eligible current and former foster youth attending Arizona public community colleges or universities, after applicable financial aid.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

A tuition-and-fee waiver for eligible current and former foster youth attending Arizona public community colleges or universities, after applicable financial aid.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Qualifying foster-care or adoption history connected to age 14, public Arizona college enrollment, FAFSA and program eligibility apply. The current administrator says the first disbursement must occur before age 23; ask about continuing eligibility and required documentation.

**Population Served**

Eligible foster youth and former foster youth attending Arizona public colleges, including Mesa Community College.

**How to Best Connect**

Start with the Arizona ETV/Tuition Waiver application and the college financial-aid office. Contact Foster Success to establish foster-care eligibility; the institution determines how the waiver applies to its aid package.

**Important Information to Know**

The waiver does not pay housing, meals or books. Its eligibility differs from the Education and Training Voucher grant; do not assume qualifying for one automatically provides every benefit of the other.

resources.name: Society of St. Vincent de Paul - Workforce Opportunities Program and Rosalie's Place
resources.description: Society of St. Vincent de Paul provides workforce readiness and job opportunities through job search and skill building, case management, Rosalie's Place workforce housing, Neighborhood Brigade paid transitional work and support with workplace items.
resources.address: Mesa Dining Room: 49 W Broadway Rd, Mesa, AZ 85210; Rosalie's Place/Ozanam Manor: 320 W Watkins Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85003; Washington Street Shelter: 2739 E Washington St, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: Use SVdP location/contact routes; access may depend on site, housing status or program enrollment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Workforce Opportunities includes job search and skill building, resume help, soft-skills coaching, job search assistance, financial planning, workplace items, dedicated case management, Rosalie's Place workforce housing for people working or seeking full-time employment, Neighborhood Brigade low-barrier paid work and Workforce X-WING support for shelter residents.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility varies by track. Rosalie's Place is for individuals who are working or actively seeking full-time employment to end homelessness. Neighborhood Brigade is for residents at Ozanam Manor and Washington Street Interim Housing Communities. Confirm whether Mesa Dining Room guests or nonresidents can access specific workforce supports.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness or major employment barriers in Valley SVdP programs, including some Mesa and Phoenix locations.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the official Workforce Readiness page and listed SVdP locations to ask about the appropriate track. Mesa Dining Room is listed as a work-readiness location, but housing and brigade programs are Phoenix-site connected.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a strong employment resource for people already connected to SVdP housing or guest services. Access for Mesa-area nonresidents is not fully public, so confirm site-specific intake before referral.

resources.name: Community Bridges, Inc. - Bellview Mesa addiction recovery / co-occurring services
resources.description: Community Bridges' Bellview Mesa recovery campus lead, including Arizona Bridge to Recovery/Center for Hope and adult East Valley addiction recovery listings, for substance-use and co-occurring recovery services distinct from CPEC crisis stabilization.
resources.address: 554-560 S Bellview, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Substance-use and co-occurring recovery services at CBI's Bellview Mesa campus. CBI's Arizona locations list Arizona Bridge to Recovery and Center for Hope at 554 S Bellview; Mercy Care separately lists East Valley Addiction Recovery Center for adults at 560 S Bellview.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adults or program-specific populations whose recovery, detox/residential or co-occurring treatment needs fit the Bellview program. Screening determines the correct CBI service and site.

**Population Served**
Mesa and Maricopa County residents needing addiction recovery or co-occurring behavioral-health/substance-use treatment, including justice-involved people when an appropriate CBI track applies.

**How to Best Connect**
Call CBI's 24/7 Access to Care line at 877-931-9142 or appointments at 888-224-6593 and ask which Bellview program, entrance and level of care applies before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
The official CBI site currently names Arizona Bridge to Recovery and Center for Hope at 554 S Bellview, while Mercy Care lists East Valley Addiction Recovery Center at 560 S Bellview. Use CBI intake to confirm the current name and address for the service needed.

resources.name: VA Veteran Readiness and Employment (Chapter 31)
resources.description: VA Veteran Readiness and Employment, Chapter 31, offers education, job placement, reemployment, self-employment, and independent-living tracks for eligible veterans and service members whose service-connected disability affects work.
resources.hours: Online application available through VA.gov; call VA benefits hotline for help.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
VR&E provides five support tracks: reemployment, rapid access to employment, self-employment, long-term education/training, and independent living. The goal is to help eligible veterans and service members prepare for, find, keep, or adapt employment and live as independently as possible.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is for veterans or service members with a service-connected disability that impacts ability to work. VA determines eligibility and entitlement.

**Population Served**
Eligible veterans and service members nationwide, including Mesa residents, especially those with service-connected disabilities affecting employment.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through the VA VR&E page or call 800-827-1000 for help with benefits questions. Veterans may also ask the Phoenix VA Regional Benefit Office about VR&E appointments.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not an immediate general job-placement program for all veterans; a VA eligibility/entitlement determination is required.

resources.name: Local First Community Kitchen - Mesa Choice Food Pantry at El Rancho del Sol
resources.description: Local First Arizona's Mesa Community Kitchen runs a resident-embedded choice food pantry, community garden and cooking education at El Rancho del Sol affordable housing.
resources.address: El Rancho del Sol / Del Sol Apartments, 659 E Main St, Mesa, AZ 85203
resources.hours: Choice pantry is described as bi-monthly; submitted volunteer evidence listed first and third Thursday pantry operations 2:30-4:30 PM. Confirm with Local First or property staff before referral.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Choice food pantry, community garden, food rescue and cooking/nutrition education embedded at the El Rancho del Sol affordable housing community.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Access appears limited to residents of El Rancho del Sol / Del Sol Apartments. The official page does not support surrounding-neighborhood public walk-in access.

**Population Served**
Families and residents of the El Rancho del Sol affordable housing community in Mesa, including children and adults participating in cooking clubs and pantry access.

**How to Best Connect**
Residents should contact El Rancho del Sol property/community staff or Local First Arizona for the current pantry schedule. Local First Arizona's main phone is 602-956-0909.

**Important Information to Know**
This is useful for residents of that housing community, not a general Mesa pantry. Outside referrals should not be sent unless Local First or site staff confirms public access.

resources.name: The New Frontier Foundation - Healing Clinic and Immigration Legal Services Support for Undocumented Survivors
resources.description: The New Frontier Foundation supports undocumented immigrants who survived domestic violence or human trafficking through healing services, support groups, and immigration legal-services support.
resources.address: 550 W. Portland St., Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.hours: Call before referral; current appointment hours and legal partner process are not fully posted.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Healing clinic services, therapy-related support, support groups, and assistance connected to immigration legal services for undocumented survivors of domestic violence or human trafficking.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public description focuses on undocumented immigrants who have survived domestic violence or human trafficking. Exact intake steps, documentation, and whether legal help is direct representation or partner/financial support should be confirmed.

**Population Served**
Undocumented immigrant survivors of domestic violence or human trafficking in Phoenix and Arizona.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 623-688-0854 and ask about healing clinic intake, survivor support groups, and immigration legal-services support. Confirm appointment location before sending a client.

**Important Information to Know**
Public language supports immigrant survivor help but does not clearly prove in-house immigration representation. Use the resource for survivor-centered healing and legal-service support, with a clear warning to confirm legal scope and current capacity.

resources.name: GoTEN - Phoenix Training Center Refugee Employment and Job Readiness Support
resources.description: GoTEN is a faith-based Phoenix ministry serving refugee neighbors through English, sewing, kids programs, employment support, job-readiness help, networking and relationship-based practical support.
resources.address: PO Box 36343, Phoenix, AZ 85067; Phoenix Training Center location should be requested from GoTEN
resources.hours: Contact form states the team normally responds within two business days; class and training-center schedules vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
GoTEN describes free services and local Phoenix work with refugee neighbors, including English classes, sewing classes, kids programs, employment support, networking, job-readiness skills and practical relationship-based help.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Public pages focus heavily on volunteer and ministry participation and do not publish a standard client intake eligibility form. Services appear intended for refugee neighbors in Phoenix; legal/refugee status, neighborhood access, class capacity and participant intake should be confirmed.

**Population Served**
Refugee and displaced communities in Phoenix, including Syrian, Afghan, Somali, Iraqi, Rohingya and other refugee neighbors identified on GoTEN pages.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-462-7000, email info@goten.org or use the GoTEN contact form and ask how a refugee neighbor can access employment support or job-readiness services. Mailing address: PO Box 36343, Phoenix, AZ 85067.

**Important Information to Know**
GoTEN is faith-based and much of the public website is volunteer-facing. Confirm participant intake, exact training-center location, transportation, language access and whether employment help is currently available before referral.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Health Services - Children and Youth with Special Health Care Needs / Medical Services Project
resources.description: Arizona Department of Health Services Office for Children with Special Health Care Needs provides statewide information and referral, systems-of-care resources, transition and family support information for children and youth with special health care needs; Medical Services Project details should be confirmed.
resources.address: 150 N. 18th Avenue, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.hours: 211 lists Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM for the ADHS OCSHCN office.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
OCSHCN provides information and referrals for families of children and youth with ongoing physical health, developmental, behavioral or emotional conditions. The ADHS page lists resources for medical home, transition to adulthood, sensory screening, family and young adult advisors, and Medical Services Project information.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The 211 listing states no restrictions and no documents needed for the information/referral service. Medical Services Project eligibility and referral workflow should be confirmed directly with ADHS or the listed program contact before relying on it for care access.

**Population Served**
Arizona children and youth with special health care needs and their families, including Mesa and Maricopa County families.

**How to Best Connect**
Call ADHS OCSHCN at 602-364-1454 or visit the CYSHCN website. Ask specifically whether Medical Services Project referrals are currently accepted and what documentation is required.

**Important Information to Know**
The official ADHS page was reachable in search-indexed form but blocked direct page fetch during this check. The retained referral is usable for information/referral contact; detailed Medical Services Project eligibility and active referral procedures need confirmation with ADHS.

resources.name: Veterans First LTD - Women Veterans and Veteran Family Assistance
resources.description: Veterans First LTD offers veteran programs and events in Phoenix, including women-veteran art, muster, mingle and stand-up events, plus selected programming for male veterans and music/instrument lessons.
resources.address: 8433 N. Black Canyon Highway, Suite 164, Phoenix, AZ 85021
resources.hours: Event schedules vary; office/program hours are not published.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Veteran events and programs including Heal Her Art for women veterans, Homeless and Struggling Women Veterans Stand Up, Muster and Mingle for Women Veterans, Rest and Recreation for Male Veterans, and Instruments for Success. Public materials list email contacts for program-event information.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility varies by event or program. Public pages do not fully state hand-up assistance criteria, funding availability or Mesa-specific reach.

**Population Served**
Greater Phoenix veterans, with specialized programming for women veterans and some offerings for male veterans and veteran families.

**How to Best Connect**
For program-event information, email eventreg@veteransfirstltd.org. Call 602-841-7663. The Phoenix office address is 8433 N. Black Canyon Highway, Suite 164.

**Important Information to Know**
Many offerings are periodic events rather than daily assistance. The listed February 2026 Stand Up date has passed; confirm current dates, eligibility, funding and whether the requested help is currently available.

resources.name: All Aboard Services — Respite, Habilitation and Attendant Care
resources.description: In-home and community respite, daily-living assistance and skill-building through Arizona DDD services.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

In-home and community respite, daily-living assistance and skill-building through Arizona DDD services.

**Eligibility Requirements**

For children and adults with developmental disabilities. DDD authorization, care needs, staffing and service location must fit the requested service.

**Population Served**

Families in Maricopa and Pinal Counties, including Mesa households when service can be arranged.

**How to Best Connect**

Call 480-625-5045, email info@allaboardaz.com or use Request Services on the website. Ask about authorization and caregiver availability for the household’s schedule.

**Important Information to Know**

County coverage does not guarantee immediate staffing or every type of support. Confirm care requirements, payer authorization and start arrangements.

resources.name: City of Scottsdale Vista del Camino Community Center - Rent, Utility, and Mortgage Assistance
resources.description: City of Scottsdale Vista del Camino Community Center assesses Scottsdale residents for crisis assistance programs, including rent, utility and mortgage assistance, to help stabilize households and prevent homelessness.
resources.address: 7700 E. Roosevelt St., Scottsdale, AZ 85257
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM, excluding city holidays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Vista del Camino assesses Scottsdale residents in crisis and connects them with available city assistance programs, including rent, utility and mortgage assistance.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public page describes service for Scottsdale residents. Assistance programs may require an eligibility interview, documentation and compliance with SAVE requirements for income-based city programs.

**Population Served**
Scottsdale individuals and families experiencing crisis, basic-needs instability or risk of homelessness.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-312-2323 or visit Vista del Camino at 7700 E. Roosevelt St. during posted weekday hours. The Scottsdale and Maricopa County client portals are also linked from the city page.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a Mesa utility-assistance program. Mesa residents should be routed to Mesa-specific utility assistance unless they have a Scottsdale service-area connection. Assistance depends on eligibility, documents and available program funding.

resources.name: Ability360 - Center for Independent Living Services and Information & Referral
resources.description: Ability360 is a Center for Independent Living offering disability information and referral, independent-living skills, peer support, advocacy, transition services, employment-related support and disability-resource navigation.
resources.address: 5025 E. Washington St., Suite 200, Phoenix, AZ 85034; Gilbert/Mesa office: 205 E. Southern Ave., Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Main office hours are Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM; call before visiting the Mesa office to confirm the right staff and service are available.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Disability information/referral, independent-living skills, peer support, advocacy, transition support, home-modification referrals, employment-related support and resource navigation. Transportation and assistive-technology questions can be routed through Information and Referral. Ability360 planning material also describes orientation/mobility training for bus, light rail and dial-a-ride; ask about current training access.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Independent-living services are for people with disabilities. Some programs have separate eligibility, funding, service-area, school-status, age or referral rules.

**Population Served**
People with disabilities in Ability360 service areas, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents; some programs also support families, students and people newly adjusting to disability.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Information and Referral at 602-296-0536 or email TriciaS@ability360.org. Mesa office: 480-655-9750, 205 E. Southern Ave.; main office: 5025 E. Washington St., Suite 200, Phoenix. Confirm the required staff/service and current site hours before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
This is disability navigation and independent-living support, not guaranteed ride provision, cash aid or home modifications. Ask whether the specific programme, training, voucher or remote/Mesa service is currently available and what separate criteria apply.

resources.name: PAN Foundation - Disease-Fund Grants
resources.description: PAN Foundation disease-fund grants help eligible patients pay medication copays, health insurance premiums and, for some active grant recipients, transportation expenses related to health needs.
resources.address: Nationwide online and telephone program
resources.hours: Apply online anytime. Phone applications are Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:30 PM Eastern Time.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Disease-specific patient assistance grants for medication copays, health insurance premiums and transportation grants when the person already has an active copay or premium grant. Grants generally cover a 12-month eligibility period when approved.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility varies by disease fund. Applicants usually need a covered diagnosis, covered medication or treatment expense, health insurance information, household income information and an open fund. Transportation grants require a current PAN copay or premium grant.

**Population Served**
United States patients, including Mesa residents, who have high out-of-pocket costs for covered disease-specific treatment and meet fund rules.

**How to Best Connect**
Search the disease fund list and apply online through the PAN/TotalAssist portal, or call 866-316-7263 Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:30 PM Eastern Time. Spanish phone help is available through the same number.

**Important Information to Know**
This is financial assistance, not a clinic and not general cash aid. Open funds, covered products, income limits and grant amounts change frequently.

resources.name: Terros Health — homeless outreach
resources.description: Provides health-oriented homeless outreach with practical hygiene and meal support.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides health-oriented homeless outreach with practical hygiene and meal support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Programme access and any clinical coverage requirements depend on the service; ask the team for screening.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness who need help connecting with medical, mental-health, substance-use or sexual-health support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Terros Patient Access at 6026856000 and ask for homeless outreach, its current locations and referral arrangements.

**Important Information to Know**
The 3003 NCentral Avenue Suite 400 address is administrative, not a confirmed drop-in site. The provider describes meals and showers but does not publish a dependable public schedule on the programme page.

resources.name: Maricopa County Human Services Department - Senior & Adult Independent Living (SAIL) Program
resources.description: Maricopa County Senior & Adult Independent Living is listed under the county's Senior Services and Community Resilience Division, which supports independent housing, prevents homelessness and connects eligible residents to senior/adult independent living services.
resources.address: 301 W. Jefferson Street, Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Independent-living support for eligible seniors and adults, plus connection to county services intended to maintain housing independently, prevent homelessness and stabilize crises.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on the Senior & Adult Independent Living Program rules and county screening. The opened county page lists SAIL as a program to help individuals live independently in their own homes but does not publish full eligibility details on that page.

**Population Served**
Older adults and adults with disabilities or independent-living needs in Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply for services through the Maricopa County Human Services client portal or call 602-506-0589 for general inquiries. The related senior help line listed in the submission is 602-264-4357.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not an emergency shelter. Use it for housing-stability and independent-living crises where a senior or adult with disabilities needs county service connection; exact services and eligibility should be confirmed during intake.

resources.name: EOIR — immigration legal-provider lists and credential checks
resources.description: Finds additional immigration-court legal providers and recognized organizations when a listed clinic cannot help.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Finds additional immigration-court legal providers and recognized organizations when a listed clinic cannot help.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Anyone can consult the lists; each provider decides case eligibility and acceptance.

**Population Served**
People seeking immigration representation or checking a nonattorney representative’s credentials.

**How to Best Connect**
Select the relevant immigration court or state from EOIR’s provider lists; contact the selected provider directly.

**Important Information to Know**
Listing does not guarantee representation or endorsement. Use the current roster, including pending-renewal status.

resources.name: AZCEND - Family Resource Centers and Family Support & Assistance
resources.description: AZCEND Family Resource Centers in Chandler and Gilbert provide early childhood classes, family support, emergency diaper assistance by appointment, Child Watch during AZCEND programs, benefits navigation, health screenings, and community resources.
resources.address: Chandler FRC: 451 W. Frye Rd., Chandler, AZ 85225; Gilbert FRC: 132 W. Bruce Ave., Gilbert, AZ 85233
resources.hours: Chandler FRC: Monday-Thursday select hours; locations page lists Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-4:00 PM in rooms M3/M4 and Fridays by appointment only. Gilbert FRC: Monday-Friday 7:30 AM-4:00 PM on program page; locations page lists Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM and Friday 8:30-11:00 AM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
AZCEND Family Resource Centers offer early literacy and parent-child activities, family support for households with children ages 0-5, emergency diaper assistance by scheduled appointment, resources and referrals, Child Watch while parents participate in AZCEND programs, DES benefits application help at Chandler, and health screenings or mobile medical services when scheduled.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Family Support & Assistance Program is for families in the community with children ages 0-5. Giggles, Squiggles and Squirms is for children ages 3-5 and their parents, with no fees and limited space. Emergency diaper help requires a scheduled appointment. Mesa residency eligibility is not clearly stated on the official page.

**Population Served**
Families with young children who can access AZCEND's Chandler or Gilbert Family Resource Centers, especially families needing early childhood support, diaper help, benefits navigation, or health screenings.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-428-5446 ext. 201 or email chandlerfrc@azcend.org for Chandler and gilbertfrc@azcend.org for Gilbert. Benefits Connection at Chandler is listed through 480-963-1423 ext. 105.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a useful East Valley reserve option, but the official Family Resource Center page identifies Chandler and Gilbert sites rather than a Mesa site. Confirm whether a Mesa family can use the desired service before referral, especially emergency diapers or classes with limited space.

resources.name: Workforce Center @ Mesa
resources.description: Free Mesa workforce center offering job-search support, resume help, interview preparation, workshops, training and apprenticeship referrals, hiring events, specialized reentry/disability/veteran supports, social-service referrals and a professional clothing boutique.
resources.address: 635 E. Broadway Road, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, 8:30 AM–2:30 PM; Wednesday by appointment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Workforce Center @ Mesa provides free employment and career support, including resume development, AZ Job Connection resume posting, career guidance, customized job search help, workshops, interview preparation, occupational skills training and apprenticeship referrals, financial wellness workshops, Job Club hiring events, specialized services for veterans, people with disabilities and reentry job seekers, social-service referrals and a professional clothing boutique.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The center welcomes community members looking for job-search support; clients do not have to be Mesa residents. Communities served include adults 18 or older, citizens or non-citizens authorized to work in the United States, veterans, reentry or justice-involved job seekers, people experiencing housing insecurity, people with disabilities, businesses and nonprofit organizations. Training funds or specialized services may require additional eligibility review.

**Population Served**
Job seekers and employers in Mesa and the East Valley, including adults, veterans, people with disabilities, reentry or justice-involved job seekers and people experiencing housing insecurity.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the City Workforce Center at 480-594-2501 or 480-572-1429. The center is at 635 E. Broadway Rd., Mesa. Published hours are Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 8:30 AM–2:30 PM; Wednesday is by appointment. For the ARIZONA@WORK workshops linked by the City, email HSDTrainingTeam@Maricopa.gov. Confirm the hours and intake for the particular service before visiting.

**Important Information to Know**
Services are free, but occupational training, apprenticeship, supportive services and boutique access depend on assessment, programme rules, schedules or inventory. Veterans have priority of service, not guaranteed jobs or funding. Ask about the Smart Justice partner connection where relevant. This center does not process unemployment-benefit applications; DES UI is 877-600-2722. The County East Valley Career Center is a separate location.

resources.name: Special Olympics Arizona — Healthy Athletes
resources.description: Special Olympics Arizona offers free scheduled health, dental and vision screenings adapted for people with intellectual disabilities.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free health, dental, vision and related screenings adapted for people with intellectual disabilities at scheduled events. Services provide screening results and follow-up recommendations; confirm event registration and any eyewear availability.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Contact Special Olympics Arizona about athlete or event participation and the specific screening’s eligibility.

**Population Served**
Special Olympics athletes and, for some programs, other people with intellectual disabilities.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-230-1200 or email hello@soaz.org to ask which upcoming event includes the needed health discipline.

**Important Information to Know**
These are event-based screenings and follow-up recommendations, not all definitive medical or dental treatment. Confirm eyewear availability and any registration requirement.

resources.name: Sun Life Health - Enrollment Services
resources.description: Sun Life Health Enrollment Services helps patients apply for Sun Life sliding fee discounts and public or marketplace benefits, including AHCCCS/Medicaid, SNAP, dental and medical discounts, OB/GYN packages, orthodontics, and Marketplace plans.
resources.address: Available through Sun Life Health locations, including Mesa
resources.hours: Enrollment appointment hours were not listed; call or ask at a Sun Life location.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Enrollment help for Sun Life Health's Sliding Fee Discount Program, dental discount, medical discount, OB/GYN packages, orthodontics, AHCCCS/State Medicaid, SNAP, and Healthcare.gov Marketplace plans.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Discount eligibility is based on household size and income. AHCCCS, SNAP, Marketplace, dental, OB/GYN, and orthodontic eligibility depends on each program's rules.

**Population Served**
Sun Life Health patients and applicants at Sun Life locations, including Mesa patients needing help with health coverage or service discounts.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 520-381-0394 to speak with an Enrollment Specialist or email contact@slfhc.org. Mesa patients can also ask at the Mesa clinic.

**Important Information to Know**
Enrollment help does not guarantee approval for AHCCCS, SNAP, Marketplace coverage, or Sun Life discounts. Bring income, household, insurance, and identity documents if available.

resources.name: City of Chandler — Utility payment arrangements
resources.description: Offers a payment-arrangement contact for Chandler utility customers.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Offers a payment-arrangement contact for Chandler utility customers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The household must have a City of Chandler utility account. Available arrangements depend on account circumstances and city rules.

**Population Served**
Chandler utility customers who are struggling to pay their bill.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Utility Services Monday through Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m., or ask at City Hall, 175 S. Arizona Avenue, Suite A. Have the account details ready.

**Important Information to Know**
A payment plan does not erase the debt or guarantee a grant. Staff may also identify outside assistance agencies. This is separate from Mesa’s utility system.

resources.name: A New Leaf - Freedom Through Housing Reentry Housing Assistance
resources.description: Freedom Through Housing is an A New Leaf reentry housing-support pathway referenced in A New Leaf's own newsletter, helping a formerly incarcerated person with shelter assistance, case management, housing, job connection and stability planning after release. Public operational details are limited, so clients should inquire directly before relying on it.
resources.address: A New Leaf administrative address: 868 E University Dr, Mesa, AZ 85203
resources.hours: No public walk-in hours or dedicated intake schedule is posted. Contact A New Leaf before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Freedom Through Housing is described by A New Leaf as helping a formerly incarcerated client with shelter assistance, case management, housing, job connection and stability planning after release.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Public eligibility rules are not posted. The supported public evidence shows service for a person released from prison who needed housing support; clients should ask A New Leaf whether the program is currently accepting referrals and what documentation or release status is required.

**Population Served**
People facing reentry barriers after incarceration, including people who are homeless or need help stabilizing after release. A New Leaf's story specifically involved a disabled formerly incarcerated adult.

**How to Best Connect**
Call A New Leaf at 480-969-4024 or start through the A New Leaf website and ask specifically about Freedom Through Housing or reentry housing assistance. Do not assume walk-in availability for this specific program.

**Important Information to Know**
A New Leaf’s July 2024 newsletter supports the programme identity, but current public service pages do not give dedicated intake details. Ask the agency whether Freedom Through Housing or an equivalent reentry pathway currently accepts referrals, and confirm capacity, costs and criteria. The administrative office is not a promised walk-in shelter.

resources.name: Maricopa Community Colleges · Fast Track Training
resources.description: Maricopa Community Colleges Fast Track Training offers certificates and microcredential pathways that can prepare learners for career entry, advancement, or skill upgrades in weeks or months, with free application and districtwide program search.
resources.address: Maricopa Community Colleges districtwide; filter by college or online location before applying
resources.hours: Program schedules vary by certificate, microcredential, college, and term.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Fast Track certificates and microcredential pathways designed to build job skills quickly, help learners start a career, upgrade professional skills, and stack credentials toward larger degree goals. Pathways include employer-developed microcredentials and focused certificate tracks.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Everyone can apply to Maricopa Community Colleges, but specific certificates and microcredentials may have prerequisites, placement rules, program costs, financial-aid limits, location limits, and term availability.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County adults and students seeking short career training through a community college, including Mesa residents who can attend MCC, another Maricopa college, or an online option.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Fast Track page to review certificates and microcredential pathways, then apply through Maricopa's Apply Now route or contact the selected college or program advisor.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a program-search pathway, not one single class. Confirm the exact program's location, start date, cost, credit or noncredit status, transferability, and whether financial aid applies.

resources.name: Community Partners Integrated Healthcare — Phoenix
resources.description: Integrated behavioral healthcare and specialized community support.
resources.address: 1515 E Osborn Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Integrated behavioral healthcare and specialized community support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Mercy Care lists this Phoenix site as an integrated health home; confirm clinical eligibility, assignment and payer.

**Population Served**
Adults needing ongoing behavioral-health care who can use the Phoenix location.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-604-0000; members can also discuss referral with their plan or case manager.

**Important Information to Know**
Appointment and program requirements vary; this is not a Mesa clinic.

resources.name: Keys to Change - Project Connect
resources.description: Keys to Change Project Connect is a traveling one-day pop-up resource event that brings Key Campus partners and local providers to neighborhoods across Maricopa County. It is a possible mobile access route to document, housing and risk-prevention partners when current events include those services.
resources.hours: Event dates and locations vary. The official programs page did not list a current public calendar in the captured page; call Keys to Change or use the Project Connect link to confirm the next event and providers.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Project Connect brings Key Campus partners and local service providers into rotating Maricopa County neighborhoods for real-time homelessness and risk-prevention resources. When identification or document partners attend, it may create a mobile access point for ID-related help.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Intended for people experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness who can attend a listed event. Provider-specific eligibility applies for any document, shelter, benefits or legal service offered at an event.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness or housing instability in Maricopa County neighborhoods served by Project Connect events.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Keys to Change at 602-282-0853 or use the Project Connect link from the Keys to Change programs page to confirm the next event location, hours and whether ID/document partners will be present before referral.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a guaranteed ID clinic. The official programs page confirms the traveling pop-up resource model but does not guarantee that Homeless ID Project or another document provider attends every event, and it did not show a current event calendar in the page text reviewed.

resources.name: Express Employment Professionals - Mesa Staffing Office
resources.description: Express Employment Professionals Mesa connects job seekers with temporary, part-time and full-time jobs across office services, light industrial, skilled trades and related positions, with online job search, phone, email and in-person access.
resources.address: 849 N. Dobson Road, Suite 107, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; Friday 8:00 AM-3:00 PM; Saturday-Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Express Employment Professionals connects job seekers with local employers and job openings, including temporary, part-time and full-time positions. The Mesa office works across office services, light industrial and skilled trades roles and provides online job search, apply-now and local recruiter contact routes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
