Applicants must meet the hiring requirements for current Express openings. Job availability, background checks, drug screening, skill testing, schedule, transportation or worksite requirements may vary by employer and position.

**Population Served**
Job seekers in Mesa and nearby East Valley employer markets seeking staffing, temp-to-hire, temporary, part-time or full-time work.

**How to Best Connect**
Search jobs or apply online from the Mesa Express site. Clients can also call 480-820-3700, email jobs.mesaaz@expresspros.com, or visit 849 N. Dobson Road, Suite 107, Mesa during posted office hours.

**Important Information to Know**
Openings change frequently and should not be treated as permanent resource facts. Ask about any position-specific equipment, transportation, testing or onboarding expectations before accepting a job.

resources.name: Catholic Charities Community Services Arizona - My Sisters' Place Domestic Violence Shelter
resources.description: My Sisters' Place is a free, confidential East Valley domestic-violence shelter with 24-hour hotline intake, case management, safety planning, counseling and referrals for housing, medical care, transportation, clothing and other needs.
resources.address: Confidential shelter location
resources.hours: Shelter is staffed 24 hours a day. Call the 24-hour hotline for intake and current availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free confidential domestic-violence shelter with private or shared rooms, food, kitchen access, case management, service planning, counseling for adults and children, help replacing documents, school and employment support, benefits connections and referrals for housing, medical and dental care, transportation and clothing.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For individuals and families fleeing abuse who are screened for shelter fit, safety and bed availability. The shelter location is confidential.

**Population Served**
Domestic-violence survivors in the East Valley, including individuals without children, families and men as well as women.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the My Sisters' Place 24-hour hotline at 480-821-1024. Do not attempt to visit a shelter location without intake coordination. Ask about available language assistance when arranging shelter intake.

**Important Information to Know**
Services are free, but placement depends on screening, safety and capacity. The Catholic Charities public office is not the confidential shelter destination. My Sisters’ Place shelter is separate from the agency’s Pathways community counseling/advocacy programme.

resources.name: Cover Arizona - Insurance Navigator Program
resources.description: Cover Arizona offers free help from trained community assisters to apply for AHCCCS/Medicaid, KidsCare/CHIP, Marketplace coverage and Medicare Supplement enrollment, with Spanish and interpretation support including ASL.
resources.address: Arizona statewide remote and local assister network
resources.hours: Use the online Find Help route or call from the website; appointment availability varies by assister.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free health insurance application and enrollment help for AHCCCS/Medicaid, KidsCare, Marketplace coverage and Medicare Supplement enrollment. Cover Arizona also helps people understand documents and application steps.

**Eligibility Requirements**
There is no fee for assistance. Eligibility for coverage depends on the health program, household, income, immigration/citizenship rules and enrollment timing.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents who need health insurance help, including families, children, uninsured adults and people needing language support.

**How to Best Connect**
Use Cover Arizona's Find Help online tool or call through the website to connect with a trained assister. Gather ID, birth certificates, immigration or visa paperwork when relevant, proof of Arizona residency, income information and employer information.

**Important Information to Know**
Cover Arizona helps with applications and navigation; it does not decide eligibility or pay medical bills. The website states Spanish help is available and interpretation is available in several languages including ASL.

resources.name: A-Z Shining Smiles · Free Dental Care Matching
resources.description: A-Z Shining Smiles is a Mesa-based nonprofit that reviews applications from people facing dental-care barriers and matches accepted patients with dental providers for no-cost care, from cleanings to more advanced procedures, plus oral-health education, hygiene supplies and future-care navigation.
resources.address: Mesa, AZ
resources.hours: No public clinic hours are posted. Apply online; email for questions. The site says Spanish is spoken.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Dental-care matching for accepted applicants, including no-cost care through dental providers for basic cleanings through more advanced procedures, oral-health education, a dental care kit and help exploring affordable future dental-care options.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official intake page says eligibility is based on financial or insurance-related challenges, unmet dental-care needs, commitment to improving and maintaining oral health, and completion of the patient intake and assessment process. Completing the online oral-health course before applying may give priority consideration.

**Population Served**
People facing barriers to dental care. The organization lists its location as Mesa, Arizona; the page does not publish a fixed clinic address or a strict city/county service boundary.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Apply for Care button on the official Get Care page and consider completing the online oral-health education course first. Email info@azshiningsmiles.org with questions.

**Important Information to Know**
This appears to broker donated or matched dental care rather than operate a walk-in clinic. Capacity, provider availability, timelines and full eligibility details are not publicly guaranteed, so frame this as an application for possible help.

resources.name: ASU Law First Amendment Clinic
resources.description: ASU Law’s First Amendment Clinic offers free consultations and selected supervised legal help involving speech, press, assembly, religion, public records and government-access issues.
resources.hours: Availability and case selection depend on clinic capacity and semester timing.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
First Amendment consultation and selected supervised representation for speech, press, assembly/protest, religion, public-records and government-access issues, including government restrictions on expression.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The matter must involve a First Amendment issue and be accepted by the clinic after review. Case acceptance depends on clinic scope, conflicts, and capacity.

**Population Served**
People, journalists, and community members with First Amendment legal issues in Arizona or regionally, including Mesa and Maricopa County matters when accepted.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the clinic page’s Request a free consultation link. Describe the issue, any government actor, relevant deadline and help requested. Confirm any in-person appointment with the clinic.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a specialized clinic, not general civil legal aid. Requests do not guarantee acceptance or representation; conflicts, priorities, capacity and semester timing matter. Flag urgent court or records deadlines when requesting help.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Health Services · AZRx / ArrayRx Prescription Discount Card
resources.description: AZRx / ArrayRx is a state-backed free prescription discount card for Arizona residents that can reduce out-of-pocket prices for FDA-approved prescriptions and some over-the-counter drugs and diabetes supplies at participating pharmacies.
resources.address: Digital or printable card accepted at participating pharmacies
resources.hours: ArrayRx customer service: Monday-Friday 7:30 AM-5:30 PM Pacific Time.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A free prescription discount card that can be downloaded digitally or printed, used at participating pharmacies, and used to compare prescription prices.

**Eligibility Requirements**
ADHS and ArrayRx state that Arizona residents qualify with no age or income limits and no membership fee. Each person should get their own card.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents, including Mesa residents, especially people paying out of pocket, between insurance plans, or comparing a discount price with an insurance copay.

**How to Best Connect**
Enroll online through the AZRx/ArrayRx card site or call 800-913-4146 for customer-service help. Show the card at a participating pharmacy before paying.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not insurance and does not guarantee the lowest price for every medication. Discounts vary by medication and pharmacy, and purchases may not count toward insurance, Medicare or Medicaid deductibles or out-of-pocket limits.

resources.name: Adolescent Substance Abuse Program (ASAP) - Mesa Adolescent IOP
resources.description: ASAP provides a specialty in-person intensive outpatient counseling program for youth ages 12-18 involved with drugs or alcohol, including group therapy, parent participation, drug testing, and relapse-prevention support.
resources.address: 2530 S Alma School Rd, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Phone open Monday-Friday 9:00am-9:00pm.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Ten-week adolescent substance-use IOP with in-person group therapy three nights per week, parent night/family participation, drug testing, evidence-based counseling, relapse prevention, and discharge recommendations.

**Eligibility Requirements**
ASAP ordinarily serves ages 12–18 with a substance-use disorder; exceptions may be considered after assessment. Parents or caregivers participate in admission and treatment. The provider lists private insurance and several AHCCCS plans; call to confirm the specific plan, authorization and cost.

**Population Served**
Adolescents ages 12-18 and their families in Mesa/East Valley and other Valley locations.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-434-0249. The Mesa site is at 2530 S Alma School Rd, Mesa, AZ 85210; confirm current group nights and admission interview timing.

**Important Information to Know**
This is live, in-person outpatient counseling only, not telehealth, detox, residential care, or inpatient care. Verify insurance and out-of-pocket costs directly.

resources.name: The Salvation Army - Phoenix Elim House Domestic Violence Shelter
resources.description: The Salvation Army's Phoenix Elim House is identified by Salvation Army and Maricopa County court resources as a domestic-violence refuge/shelter for families with children, with safety planning, crisis counseling and children's activities.
resources.address: Confidential Phoenix shelter; do not use public Salvation Army campus addresses as walk-up shelter addresses
resources.hours: Maricopa County court resources list Elim House as an emergency shelter contact; call 602-267-4111 before going anywhere.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Phoenix Elim House is described as a safe haven/refuge for families affected by domestic abuse, with up to 120 days of support, personal goal and safety-plan development, crisis counseling and recreational activities for children.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Public sources support a domestic-violence shelter/refuge for families with children; current bed configuration, gender eligibility, child-age rules and intake process must be confirmed by phone.

**Population Served**
Domestic-violence survivors and families in Phoenix/Maricopa County who may need confidential emergency shelter. It may be a reserve option for Mesa survivors if transportation and eligibility fit.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-267-4111 and ask for Elim House Domestic Violence Shelter intake. Do not send a client to a street address unless shelter staff gives instructions.

**Important Information to Know**
Call to confirm current beds, household/child-age and gender rules, language access and transportation. National wording about capacity is ambiguous, and public listings may mix Elim House with other Salvation Army family services. The County court lists bilingual help. Do not use a public campus address as a shelter destination; placement is not guaranteed.

resources.name: Medstar Medical Transport - Phoenix Area Non-Emergency Medical Transportation
resources.description: Medstar Medical Transport provides non-emergency medical transportation in the Phoenix area and beyond, including wheelchair, stretcher, bariatric, behavioral health, hospice, long-distance, companion flight, and cancer-treatment transportation.
resources.address: 1811 S Alma School Rd, Suite 154, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Private non-emergency medical transportation for ambulatory, wheelchair, stretcher, bariatric, Broda chair, behavioral health, hospice, long-distance, companion flight, event/special occasion, and recurring treatment transportation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public page does not list income or insurance eligibility rules. Riders or caregivers must request a ride and speak with dispatch before the trip is confirmed.

**Population Served**
People in the Phoenix area and beyond who need non-emergency medical transportation, including people with mobility needs or ongoing treatment appointments.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-469-2149 or use the online request-a-ride form. The site says a ride is not confirmed until the requester has spoken with dispatch.

**Important Information to Know**
This appears to be a private provider. Confirm rates, insurance or AHCCCS participation, pickup address, destination, accessibility needs, and dispatch confirmation before referring a client to depend on the ride.

resources.name: Southwest Behavioral & Health Services - Mesa Outpatient
resources.description: Southwest Behavioral & Health Services Mesa Outpatient offers individual, group, and family counseling, medication services, psychiatric care, skills training, case management, and primary-care services at a Mesa clinic.
resources.address: 1255 W. Baseline Rd., Suite 138, Mesa, AZ 85202
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-7:00 PM; Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; Saturday-Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Mesa outpatient behavioral-health services including individual, group, and family counseling; medication services; psychiatric care; skills training; case management; and primary-care services. SB&H also provides counseling and psychiatric services for depression, anxiety disorders, substance abuse, relationship and domestic issues across its system.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Call for appointment and intake screening. SB&H states no one will be denied access due to inability to pay and offers sliding-fee discounts based on family size and income. It accepts Medicare and Medicaid/AHCCCS assignment for covered services.

**Population Served**
Mesa and greater Phoenix adults, youth, and families needing outpatient behavioral-health care, psychiatric services, case management, primary-care integration, or co-occurring substance-use support when clinically appropriate.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Mesa Outpatient clinic at 480-820-5422. The clinic is at 1255 W. Baseline Rd., Suite 138, Mesa, AZ 85202. SB&H also has a contact/schedule appointment form on the Get Help page.

**Important Information to Know**
The Mesa page supports outpatient counseling, psychiatry, case management and primary care; it does not establish every system specialty or residential service at this address. Confirm age fit, SUD groups/IOP or medication options, insurance coverage, fee screening and current appointments. A system sliding-fee policy does not mean every service or medicine is free.

resources.name: Gompers - Employment, Day Training, In-Home Services, Transportation and Assistive Technology
resources.description: Gompers provides Phoenix-area services for people with disabilities, including Day Training for Adults, in-home services, employment services, transportation and assistive technology-related support through its program departments.
resources.address: Phoenix metro area; contact Gompers for current program site
resources.hours: Use the online contact form; program schedules and transportation depend on the service.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Day Training for Adults, employment services, in-home respite/habilitation/attendant care, transportation for ambulatory and non-ambulatory passengers, assistive technology inquiries and program-department routing through the contact form.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Gompers serves people with disabilities, including adults age 18 and older for DTA. Funding, DDD/RSA authorization, age, location, transportation and current openings should be confirmed for each department.

**Population Served**
People with disabilities in the Phoenix metro area, including adults needing day training, employment supports, in-home supports or transportation connected to Gompers programs.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Gompers Contact Us form and select the relevant department: Day Training for Adults, In-Home Services, Employment Services, Transportation or Assistive Technology. Provide phone and email for follow-up.

**Important Information to Know**
The official contact page provides a practical department-routing form but does not list full eligibility or Mesa coverage. Confirm DDD/RSA funding, transportation boundaries and current program openings.

resources.name: Christ Church / City Hope Arizona - Mesa Day Respite Center and City Hope Mesa Center
resources.description: Christ Church / City Hope's Mesa Day Respite Center is a seasonal City of Mesa-listed respite and heat-relief site offering air-conditioned space, water, rest areas, meals, navigation services, medical care, showers and pet-friendly access when active.
resources.address: 655 E University Dr, Mesa, AZ 85203; day-respite entrance through N Hobson parking lot when operating
resources.hours: City-listed day respite schedule: Monday-Saturday 9:30 AM-6:30 PM during the posted heat season. City Hope Mesa Center food distribution separately lists Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday 9:00-11:30 AM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Seasonal day respite with cooling, water, rest areas, meals, navigation services, medical care, showers and pet-friendly access when the respite center is operating. City Hope's regular Mesa Center also offers no-cost food distribution.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people needing heat relief and homeless-service support in Mesa. City Hope food distribution may ask for government-issued ID and may limit visits by center and month.

**Population Served**
People in Mesa needing day respite, cooling, hydration, hygiene, basic-needs support or pet-friendly relief during heat season.

**How to Best Connect**
For day respite, go to Christ Church/City Hope at 655 E University Dr during posted respite hours and use the N Hobson parking-lot entrance. Call 480-805-1031 to confirm current operations, especially outside peak heat season.

**Important Information to Know**
The day-respite and City Hope food-distribution schedules are different. Confirm the day-respite schedule and seasonal opening separately before travel.

resources.name: Chicanos Por La Causa - CPLC Housing Counseling / Financial Empowerment Services
resources.description: Chicanos Por La Causa provides HUD-approved housing counseling, financial assessment, individualized action plans, foreclosure/eviction prevention counseling, and affordable-housing navigation.
resources.address: 1402 S Central Ave, Building A, Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
HUD-approved housing counseling for landlord-tenant conflicts, mortgage delinquency, pending foreclosure, fraud, financial assessment, individualized financial action plans, homebuyer education, and affordable-housing decision support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open to individuals and families seeking housing counseling. Down-payment assistance described on CPLC's program page is for first-time homebuyers in Phoenix with household earnings at or below 80% AMI; other counseling services have their own program rules.

**Population Served**
Arizona households needing housing counseling or financial empowerment support, including Phoenix/Central Arizona clients who can access the Phoenix office or online form.

**How to Best Connect**
Call CPLC Housing Counseling Services in Phoenix at 602-253-0838 or complete the online assistance form linked from the housing counseling page.

**Important Information to Know**
This is counseling and navigation, not confirmed direct rent or utility payment assistance. CPLC's separate Family Assistance page states it does not have rental assistance funds.

resources.name: Crossroads —360 Clinic Mesa
resources.description: Psychiatric assessment, medication management, substance-use treatment and basic medical care.
resources.address: 244 N Extension Rd, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Psychiatric assessment, medication management, substance-use treatment and basic medical care.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Admissions includes a phone assessment and insurance/eligibility review.

**Population Served**
Mesa-area people seeking co-occurring behavioral-health and recovery care.

**How to Best Connect**
Call admissions 602-263-5242 or the clinic 602-730-3388.

**Important Information to Know**
The clinic is distinct from residential Right Track placement. Ask about the needed service, insurance and appointment; crisis symptoms require an appropriate urgent response.

resources.name: A New Leaf Community Alliance Against Family Abuse (CAAFA)
resources.description: A New Leaf's Community Alliance Against Family Abuse provides emergency shelter, legal advocacy, case management, support groups, sexual-assault victim advocacy, food boxes, and outreach for survivors in Pinal County and eastern Maricopa County.
resources.address: Public office: 2066 Apache Trail #101, Apache Junction, AZ 85120; arrange shelter access by phone.
resources.hours: Call the CAAFA shelter number for current shelter/intake status. Program staff should not be contacted directly for services.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency shelter, legal advocacy/assistance, case management, support groups and empowerment sessions, sexual-assault victim advocacy, food boxes, outreach and education for survivors of family, domestic and sexual abuse. The programme describes 16 shelter beds; openings require screening.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For individuals and families experiencing domestic or sexual abuse in Apache Junction, Pinal County, and eastern Maricopa County. Shelter and services depend on screening, safety needs, and availability.

**Population Served**
Survivors and families of all genders experiencing domestic or sexual abuse, especially in Apache Junction, Pinal County, and the eastern Maricopa County edge of the Mesa service area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the CAAFA shelter at 480-773-2359. A New Leaf says program staff should not be contacted directly for services. For business needs only, CAAFA lists 480-982-0205. Spanish-language access is listed for CAAFA outreach; ask for the language and service needed when calling.

**Important Information to Know**
The public office is not a guaranteed walk-in shelter or legal-advocacy intake. Confirm safety planning, capacity, transportation and accommodations by phone. Ask whether any needed attorney representation can be arranged; advocacy is not automatically legal representation. CAAFA remains a distinct A New Leaf programme serving the Pinal/eastern Maricopa area.

resources.name: Labor Systems · Mesa Temp Agency
resources.description: Labor Systems' Mesa office is a local temporary staffing agency where job seekers can apply for work and browse temporary jobs in construction, industrial manufacturing, skilled trades, hospitality, professional services and related fields.
resources.address: 420 E Southern Ave, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Office hours are not posted on the page; call before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Temporary staffing and job matching through a Mesa office, with online Apply Here and Find a Job routes. Work may include construction, industrial manufacturing, professional services, skilled trades, hospitality, short-term assignments, longer-term staffing and possible direct-hire support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public page does not publish a full applicant checklist. Applicants should complete the online application and ask about work-eligibility documents, safety gear, background or drug-screen rules, transportation and assignment requirements.

**Population Served**
Mesa and East Valley job seekers looking for temporary or possible longer-term work through a staffing agency.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online from the Mesa Labor Systems page or call 480-649-6004. Office: 420 E Southern Ave, Mesa, AZ 85210. Email mes1@laborsystems.com. Confirm application hours before visiting.

**Important Information to Know**
Current openings, pay, start timing, equipment requirements and transportation expectations vary by assignment. Applying does not guarantee a same-day placement.

resources.name: Mesa Community College - Mesa Market and We Care Wednesday Food Distributions
resources.description: MCC’s Mesa Market offers students free food/hygiene supplies and donated clothing at Southern & Dobson. Separately scheduled We Care Wednesday food distributions also welcome community members.
resources.address: 1833 W Southern Ave, Mesa, AZ 85202; 7110 E McKellips Rd, Mesa, AZ 85207
resources.hours: Mesa Market fall/spring: Southern & Dobson Tue/Wed 10:00 AM-3:00 PM and Fri 11:00 AM-2:00 PM, closed first Wednesday monthly; Red Mountain Mon/Thu 10:00 AM-3:00 PM. We Care Wednesday: first Wednesday at Southern & Dobson and third Wednesday at Red Mountain, 10:00 AM-12:00 PM. Hours subject to change.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Weekly free food and hygiene supplies through Mesa Market for MCC students. Donated clothing is outside the market in KSC 35S at Southern & Dobson only. Separately, We Care Wednesday provides scheduled campus food distributions for students, staff and community members in need.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Mesa Market food/hygiene and donated clothing are for MCC students; Red Mountain lists food/hygiene but not donated clothing. We Care Wednesday is open to students, staff and community members needing food assistance.

**Population Served**
MCC students needing weekly pantry support, plus community members who can attend We Care Wednesday distributions.

**How to Best Connect**
Mesa Market: call the Care Team at 480-461-7288 or visit the appropriate pantry during current hours; Southern & Dobson clothing is at KSC 35S. We Care Wednesday: contact Balbina Garcia at 480-461-7397 and confirm that month’s campus/date on the event page.

**Important Information to Know**
The programmes have different access rules. Mesa Market is not a public pantry; We Care Wednesday is a scheduled distribution, not continuous access. Check term/event hours and inventory. Donated clothing sizes and types are not guaranteed.

resources.name: Eyes On Site - Mobile Eye Care for Elderly and Disabled Patients
resources.description: Mesa-based mobile optometry provider serving elderly and disabled patients in nursing homes, long-term care, rehabilitation settings, group homes and private homes across Arizona.
resources.address: 2826 E. Baseline Rd., Suite 101, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: Regular office schedule listed as Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; Saturday-Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Eyes On Site provides mobile medical eye care and vision services for people who have difficulty traveling to a traditional optometry office. Services include eye exams, disease screening and monitoring, prescriptions, glasses options and referrals when needed.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The service is designed for elderly and disabled patients and residents of care facilities or private homes. Insurance, private pay, facility contracts, travel area and mobile referral requirements should be confirmed before scheduling.

**Population Served**
Elderly and disabled patients throughout Arizona, including people in nursing homes, long-term care facilities, rehabilitation facilities, group homes and private homes.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-626-8925, email info@eyesonsite.com or fax 480-704-4036. The website says mobile referral forms can be emailed or faxed; the Mesa office is at 2826 E. Baseline Rd., Suite 101.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a medical provider, not an established free service. Ask about accepted insurance, private-pay exams, travel/mobile fees, glasses costs and any current first-pair discount or other help. Confirm scheduling and whether a home visit is available for the client’s location.

resources.name: Miracle Flights — child medical flights and service-dog travel
resources.description: Miracle Flights provides free commercial medical flights for pediatric patients age 17 and under traveling for specialty medical care, with assistance for the child and up to two parents or legal guardians when eligible.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Miracle Flights arranges free commercial flights for medical patients age 17 or younger, with up to two accompanying parents or legal guardians under programme rules. A separate service-dog pathway supports retrieval or required training for people of all ages, with one medically necessary caregiver when approved.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Medical patients need a verified treatment appointment and medical clearance for commercial air travel. Financial review uses household size, current gross household income and tax documentation. Submit the application and supporting documents at least 14 days before departure; confirm the current financial limits.

**Population Served**
U.S. children and families needing travel for medical care, and people of any age needing qualifying service-dog travel, including Arizona residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through the online flight-request process with appointment, clearance, travel and financial documents. Arrange any flight changes through Miracle Flights at 800-359-1711, not directly with the airline.

**Important Information to Know**
Travel is for U.S. destinations; U.S. territories and new international flights are excluded. Elective procedures and compassionate travel are not covered. One-way travel home from treatment can qualify, but an outgoing treatment trip needs a return plan. This does not supply local ground transportation.

resources.name: IRS — Free Tax Preparation and VITA/TCE Locator
resources.description: A national locator for free volunteer tax-return preparation, including VITA and tax counseling focused on older adults.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A national locator for free volunteer tax-return preparation, including VITA and tax counseling focused on older adults.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Individual sites set their income and tax-return scope. IRS does not impose a single VITA program-wide income cap. Sites commonly serve people with limited income, disabilities or limited English; TCE particularly serves people age 60 and older.

**Population Served**
Eligible taxpayers, including Mesa residents seeking an appropriate local or remote free-preparation site.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the IRS VITA/TCE locator or call 800-906-9887. Check the chosen site’s current schedule, appointment instructions, documents and tax situations it can handle.

**Important Information to Know**
Most locations are seasonal, and the locator is updated regularly from February through April. This is a service finder, not an IRS tax-debt appeal or emergency-payment program.

resources.name: ELAINE - Transportation Assistance Program
resources.description: ELAINE provides transportation and navigation for Arizona's homeless and underserved people to healthcare, food, housing, court, benefits, employment and other critical errands.
resources.address: 1075 W Jackson St, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.hours: Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM–4:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
ELAINE provides transportation and related navigation to reduce barriers to healthcare, prescriptions, food access, housing appointments, court and case management, DES/Social Security/bank visits, employment, education and critical errands.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The site describes service for Arizona's homeless and underserved people, including low-income, uninsured and senior clients. Exact referral requirements, ride limits and geographic availability should be confirmed when scheduling.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness and underserved Arizonans, including low-income, uninsured and senior community members.

**How to Best Connect**
To check ride availability or schedule a ride, call 602-848-1717 or email elainerides@elaineaz.org during posted hours. General inquiries can use elaineinfo@elaineaz.org.

**Important Information to Know**
ELAINE is not general public transit. Ride availability, service geography and referral requirements may vary, so confirm before relying on a ride for a time-sensitive appointment.

resources.name: Mesa Community College · Bridging Success
resources.description: Mesa Community College Bridging Success connects current and prospective students with foster-care experience to campus champions who help with admissions, registration, paying for classes, schedules, career preparation, mentoring, and basic-needs resources.
resources.address: 1833 W. Southern Ave., Mesa, AZ 85202
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Foster Youth Champions and coaches help with admissions and registration, enrolling in and paying for classes, building class schedules, health and well-being, employment, housing and financial resources, career preparation, mentorship, counseling, disability resources, TRIO, and other campus connections.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The page is designed for foster youth connected to Mesa Community College. It does not state one formal cutoff, so prospective participants should ask whether their foster-care history and enrollment stage qualify for specific supports.

**Population Served**
Current and prospective Mesa Community College students with foster-care experience.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Bridging Success champion lead at 480-461-7277 or use the MCC Bridging Success page to contact a Foster Youth Champion. Ask which champion fits the student’s immediate need, such as admissions, financial aid, career services, counseling, DRS, or TRIO.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a campus support pathway, not a separate scholarship guarantee. Help with paying for classes means connection to financial-aid and campus resources, not guaranteed funding.

resources.name: Mesa Community College · Welding Certificates
resources.description: Mesa Community College's Welding program offers Certificate of Completion and Associate degree pathways that prepare students for welding careers using modern industrial equipment and practices, with specific certificate tracks such as fundamentals, GMAW/FCAW, GTAW, SMAW pipe and SMAW plate.
resources.address: 1833 W Southern Ave, Mesa, AZ 85202
resources.hours: Campus and program hours vary; contact the program director or MCC advising.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Welding training for students preparing for careers in the welding industry, with certificates and associate degree pathways. The program page describes modern industrial equipment and advanced practices and links to pathway maps, program information and enrollment routes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Students must apply to MCC/Maricopa Community Colleges and meet requirements for the selected welding pathway. Course availability, prerequisites, placement, materials and safety requirements may vary by term.

**Population Served**
Mesa and Maricopa Community Colleges students seeking welding skills, certificates or degree pathways for trade employment.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Welding page's Request Information or Become a Student route, or call MCC at 480-461-7000. The candidate source lists a program contact phone of 480-461-7131; confirm the current program director/contact from the page before relying on that direct number.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm term availability, campus, costs, required equipment/materials, course sequence, financial aid and WIOA eligibility before referral. Program completion does not guarantee employment.

resources.name: CDC — Where to Write for Vital Records
resources.description: Locates the official issuing office for birth, death, marriage and divorce records from other states and territories.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Locates the official issuing office for birth, death, marriage and divorce records from other states and territories.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Anyone can use the directory; access to a particular record depends on the issuing jurisdiction.

**Population Served**
People who need a record from outside Arizona or need to identify the correct records office.

**How to Best Connect**
Select the state or territory where the event occurred, then follow the linked issuing office requirements.

**Important Information to Know**
CDC does not hold or issue these individual records, pay fees, or waive identification requirements.

resources.name: HealthWell Foundation · Disease-Fund Copay, Premium, Deductible, and Treatment Assistance
resources.description: HealthWell Foundation provides disease-fund grants for insured patients whose health insurance is not enough to cover treatment costs such as copays, premiums, deductibles, supplies and selected out-of-pocket expenses.
resources.address: Nationwide telephone and online program; mailing address P.O. Box 489, Buckeystown, MD 21717
resources.hours: Contact Center hours Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM Eastern Time.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Financial assistance through open disease funds for prescription-drug coinsurance, copayments, deductibles, health-insurance premiums and selected out-of-pocket healthcare costs. Approved grants generally run for a rolling 12 months, with reapplication possible if funding is available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The patient must have a covered disease fund, have health insurance that covers part of treatment, use an eligible medication or treatment for that disease fund, meet income guidelines that vary by fund, and receive treatment in the United States.

**Population Served**
Insured patients receiving treatment in the United States, including Mesa residents, whose diagnosis and treatment match an open HealthWell disease fund.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through HealthWell or call 800-675-8416 Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM Eastern Time. Providers, pharmacies or social workers can use the HealthWell provider or pharmacy portals when applying for a patient.

**Important Information to Know**
Check the current disease fund, eligible medication/treatment and that fund’s income rule before applying; funds open and close frequently. HealthWell does not pay the full treatment cost for uninsured patients, and an award does not cover every expense. Renewal depends on an open fund and continuing eligibility.

resources.name: ComTrans - Behavioral Health, Hospital, and Crisis Transport Services
resources.description: ComTrans provides contracted transportation for behavioral health agencies, hospitals, nonprofits and government agencies, and lists a Maricopa County crisis transportation phone number.
resources.phone: Maricopa County crisis access: 602-222-9444; routine trips through the arranging agency or health plan
resources.hours: Crisis transport is described as 24/7/365. Other transportation appears contract-based and should be arranged through the referring agency or provider.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
ComTrans transports consumers to counselors, physicians, behavioral health programs, hospitals, school and social-service appointments through agency contracts. It also lists 24/7/365 crisis transport services that move people in crisis to safe destinations for intervention.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Trips are arranged under covered agency, hospital, behavioral-health, nonprofit, school or government contracts. ComTrans does not accept direct individual one-time bookings.

**Population Served**
Children and adults served by contracted behavioral-health, hospital, nonprofit, school or government partners, and people in Maricopa County crisis transport situations.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the treating provider, arranging agency or health plan to authorize and arrange covered transportation. For a Maricopa County behavioral-health crisis, call 602-222-9444; this is crisis access, not the routine ComTrans reservation desk. Agencies can use the ComTrans website to inquire about contracts.

**Important Information to Know**
Contract coverage and agency authorization determine access. The listed 24-hour crisis service does not make ordinary medical or errand trips open public transportation.

resources.name: Soldier's Best Friend - Service and Therapeutic Companion Dogs for Veterans with PTSD/TBI
resources.description: Soldier's Best Friend pairs eligible U.S. military veterans living with military service-related PTSD or TBI with a rescued or veteran-owned dog and provides service-dog or therapeutic companion dog training at no placement or training fee.
resources.address: 14505 N. 75th Ave., Peoria, AZ 85381
resources.hours: Training requires private and group sessions two days per week for at least 6 to 9 months; office hours not published.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Soldier's Best Friend pairs accepted veterans with a rescued dog or evaluates a veteran-owned dog, then trains the veteran/dog team for service-dog or therapeutic companion-dog work related to PTSD or TBI symptoms.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be U.S. military veterans with military service-related PTSD or TBI. The application packet requires provider confirmation of diagnosis, references, a VA medical release, DD214, home inspection, interview, and acceptance review.

**Population Served**
Veterans from any U.S. military branch who can train in Arizona; the program is especially relevant for veterans with PTSD, TBI, and a suitable home situation for a dog.

**How to Best Connect**
Request an application through the website, email contact@soldiersbestfriend.org, or call 623-218-6486. Training locations include Phoenix, Tucson, Prescott, Sierra Vista, Flagstaff, Yuma, and Kingman; out-of-state veterans must travel or relocate to Arizona during training.

**Important Information to Know**
There are no placement or training fees during the training period. Veterans are responsible for transportation, housing/meals if relocation is needed, and dog care costs after graduation. Acceptance and dog placement are not immediate and depend on program review and dog fit.

resources.name: Molina Healthcare of Arizona - Non-Emergency Medical Transportation through MTM/Veyo
resources.description: Molina Healthcare of Arizona partners with MTM/Veyo for non-emergency medical transportation for Molina Medicaid members, including routine reservations and urgent same-day categories when criteria are met.
resources.hours: MTM/Veyo booking line Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-6:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Non-emergency medical transportation to covered medical appointments for Molina Medicaid members through MTM/Veyo. The page lists standard, wheelchair, and stretcher vehicle types and urgent same-day trip categories such as discharges, dialysis, urgent care, cancer treatment, pre/post-surgery, wound care, and same-day mental health when criteria are met.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The person must be a Molina Healthcare of Arizona Medicaid/AHCCCS member and the ride must be for a covered medical appointment or approved urgent trip.

**Population Served**
Molina Medicaid members in Arizona, including Maricopa County members.

**How to Best Connect**
Call MTM/Veyo at 833-474-5060 at least three business days before the appointment, Monday through Friday from 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM. Have the AHCCCS ID, appointment date/time, provider name/address, pickup address, vehicle type, and passenger needs ready. For questions, call Molina Member Services at 800-424-5891, TTY 711.

**Important Information to Know**
Be ready 30 minutes before pickup. Return pickup may take up to 60 minutes after calling when the end time was unknown. One additional passenger is permitted; confirm any special escort needs when booking. Members supply required child-safety seats and personal mobility equipment. Urgent-trip categories still require plan approval and are not emergency transport.

resources.name: Denova Collaborative Health - Dobson Ranch Mesa clinic
resources.description: Denova Collaborative Health Dobson Ranch is a Mesa integrated outpatient clinic offering primary care, therapy/behavioral healthcare, psychiatry, addiction treatment, case management, in-person appointments, and virtual care for children through seniors.
resources.address: 2120 W Guadalupe Rd, Suite 6, Mesa, AZ 85202
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 7:00 AM-5:00 PM; closed Saturday-Sunday. Call to confirm holiday hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Primary care, family medicine, therapy and behavioral healthcare, psychiatry, addiction treatment, case management, in-person appointments, and virtual care.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Children, adults, and seniors whose needs fit Denova outpatient services may inquire. Appointment availability, clinical fit, and insurance or payment requirements apply.

**Population Served**
Mesa and Arizona residents from children to seniors, including people seeking integrated physical and behavioral healthcare, psychiatric care, therapy, LGBTQ+ care, or addiction treatment.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Engagement Center at 602-230-7373 or use the Dobson location page to make an appointment. The clinic is at 2120 W Guadalupe Rd, Suite 6, Mesa, AZ 85202.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an outpatient clinic, not a crisis receiving center. Confirm accepted insurance, same/next-day appointment availability, and whether the specific clinician or service needed is available at Dobson or by virtual care.

resources.name: Finishing Trades Institute of Arizona — Apprenticeships
resources.description: Registered apprenticeship instruction for finishing-trade careers such as painting, drywall finishing and glazing, combined with work experience.
resources.address: 210 N. 24th St., Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Registered apprenticeship instruction for finishing-trade careers such as painting, drywall finishing and glazing, combined with work experience.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Applicants must be at least 18, have a diploma or GED, provide proof of age and authorization to work in the U.S., and have reliable transportation. Trade aptitude and ability to perform essential functions with reasonable accommodations also apply.

**Population Served**

Arizona applicants pursuing finishing-trade careers.

**How to Best Connect**

The provider currently invites in-person applications during business hours. Call the apprenticeship office before visiting to confirm hours, available trades and required documents.

**Important Information to Know**

Selection, employment, training costs, wages and openings vary by trade and employer. Applying does not guarantee immediate work.

resources.name: Synergy Transitional Housing Inc. - Synergy Transitional Housing
resources.description: Synergy Transitional Housing Inc. is a Mesa nonprofit that connects justice-involved adults and other eligible adults to transitional housing, case management, employment pathways and community support.
resources.address: 864 W Southern Ave, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Transitional-housing connection, case management, employment/job-readiness support and community connections. The provider also describes behavioral-health referrals and counseling/MAT/IOP supports; confirm which programme delivers each and whether a separate clinical intake is needed.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The site describes adults rebuilding stability after incarceration, inpatient substance-use treatment, housing instability or other major disruptions. Ask about admissions, supervision/offense restrictions, fees and coverage, house rules, licensing/certification and openings.

**Population Served**
Adults in Mesa who are justice-involved, leaving treatment, homeless or rebuilding stability after major disruption.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-690-6901. The listed location is 864 W Southern Ave, Mesa, AZ 85210.

**Important Information to Know**
Housing is not established as free or inclusive of clinical treatment. Confirm the exact programme, included services, cost, bed availability and intake at the listed location before travel.

resources.name: Arizona Fair Housing Center · Fair housing enforcement, eviction-prevention legal advocacy, and housing counseling
resources.description: Mesa-based fair-housing organization providing fair-housing enforcement, education, complaint support, and limited-scope eviction-prevention legal advocacy.
resources.address: 237 W. Main St. #204, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Arizona Fair Housing Center assists victims of housing discrimination, provides fair-housing education and enforcement support, and offers limited-scope legal advocacy and eviction-prevention information.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Fair-housing help relates to housing discrimination and protected classes under the Fair Housing Act, including race, color, national origin, religion, sex, disability, and familial status. Eviction-prevention legal advocacy depends on the tenant's housing issue and service availability.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents facing housing discrimination or eviction-related housing instability, with a Mesa office lead and broader metro Phoenix/surrounding-area relevance.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Arizona Fair Housing Center website for home, limited-scope legal advocacy, and eviction-prevention information. The submitted public phone is 602-548-1599; confirm current intake before relying on a same-day court-deadline referral.

**Important Information to Know**
Evictions move quickly. The official support page emphasizes that tenants may have only days between notice, hearing, and lockout. Legal advocacy is limited-scope and should not be assumed to be attorney representation.

resources.name: City of Mesa Electric Utility / Trees Matter - Mesa Electric Shade Tree Program
resources.description: Mesa Electric Shade Tree Program offers City of Mesa residential electric customers up to two free desert-adapted shade trees after workshop participation, through the City's Trees Are Cool Initiative and Trees Matter.
resources.hours: Trees Matter contact hours Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The program offers City of Mesa electric customers up to two free desert-native or desert-adapted shade trees and workshop education to reduce heat and future cooling costs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Participants must be City of Mesa residential electric customers, not SRP customers; own the home or have explicit landlord permission to plant; attend a workshop; pick up trees; have suitable south or west planting space; avoid overhead and underground utility conflicts; and transport, plant and maintain the trees.

**Population Served**
City of Mesa residential electric customers who can legally plant and maintain shade trees at eligible homes.

**How to Best Connect**
Check the City program page for workshop registration windows. For questions, contact Trees Matter at 480-935-9988 or MesaShadeTrees@Treesmatter.org.

**Important Information to Know**
Workshops are periodic and may be closed between seasonal offerings. This program is not for SRP customers and is not emergency cooling, bill payment or tree planting labor; participants plant and maintain the trees themselves.

resources.name: Southwest Autism Research & Resource Center (SARRC) - Teen and Adult Services / Employment Services
resources.description: Southwest Autism Research & Resource Center offers autism-specific teen and adult services, including independence skills, ABA-based community supports, pre-employment programming, employment services and orientation.
resources.address: Multiple Valley locations; confirm the programme’s assigned campus, community site or remote access before travel.
resources.hours: General SARRC hours reported Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM; program schedules vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Autism-specific independence, executive-functioning, advocacy and social-skills support, ABA-based home/community/on-the-job interventions, Learn4Independence, CommunityWorks, Transition Academy and employment services. Employment help can include job search, interviewing, onboarding, retention, workplace social skills and job coaching, at SARRC, in the community or by telehealth when available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Age, diagnosis, assessment, fees, insurance and waitlists vary by programme. Employment services list VR-funded Rehabilitation Instructional/Job Development and Retention services and private pay; free orientation and VR guidance are available. Employment Bootcamp is separately listed as free for autistic people 16+; confirm its current schedule.

**Population Served**
Autistic teens and adults, and their families, in the Phoenix metro area, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents who can access SARRC locations or approved home/community services.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Family Resource Team at 602-606-9806, use SARRC's Contact Us Online/Request Services route, or call 480-887-0784 for Spanish. Ask which teen/adult or employment program fits the person's age, goals, payer and location.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an autism-specific resource, not a general cross-disability provider. Confirm costs, insurance/VR funding, telehealth/community access, location and current openings before referral.

resources.name: Sundt Construction - Department of Labor-Approved Craft Apprenticeships
resources.description: Sundt Construction offers Department of Labor-approved craft apprenticeship programs in concrete construction, heavy equipment operation, pipefitting, industrial ironwork, heavy equipment technician work and construction labor, using NCCER curriculum and paid work experience.
resources.address: 2630 S 20th Pl, Phoenix, AZ 85034; headquarters in Tempe
resources.hours: Apprenticeship and job schedules vary by trade and project; Arizona after-hours training is available for some tracks.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Sundt offers paid craft training and Department of Labor-approved apprenticeship programs in Concrete Construction, Heavy Equipment Operation, Pipefitting, Industrial Ironworker, Heavy Equipment Technician and Construction Laborer. Training uses nationally recognized NCCER curriculum and combines project experience with classroom learning.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Apprenticeship access appears tied to Sundt employment or hiring for qualifying craft roles. Requirements vary by job, trade, project, background, safety, travel and schedule.

**Population Served**
People pursuing construction careers in Arizona and other Sundt markets, including Mesa-area job seekers who can meet worksite and training schedule requirements.

**How to Best Connect**
Use Sundt's careers and skilled-workforce pages to find current craft openings, then ask recruiting or craft training staff about Arizona apprenticeship eligibility and schedule.

**Important Information to Know**
Not every apprenticeship track is necessarily recruiting in Maricopa County at the same time. Confirm an open qualifying job, training location, wage, schedule and travel expectations before referral.

resources.name: Mesa Police Department Victim Services Unit - Victim Services and Victim Compensation Navigation
resources.description: Mesa Police Department Victim Services is a city access point for Mesa crime victims and witnesses, providing advocacy, safety planning, victim rights information, referrals and victim-compensation navigation.
resources.hours: Victim advocates: Monday–Friday, 7:30 a.m.–5:30 p.m.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Support for Mesa crime victims and witnesses, including safety planning, victim-rights information, case-process guidance, law-enforcement liaison, protective-order information, compensation navigation and referrals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people affected by criminal events in Mesa. Crime-victim compensation has separate county and state eligibility and application rules.

**Population Served**
Mesa crime victims and witnesses, including people affected by domestic or sexual violence and other crimes.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Mesa Police Victim Services at 480-644-4075 or 480-644-2002, or email PDVSU@mesaaz.gov. Advocates are available Monday–Friday, 7:30 a.m.–5:30 p.m. Ask about the appropriate location before visiting.

**Important Information to Know**
This unit helps people navigate support and compensation; it does not pay compensation or provide legal advice. The Mesa City Prosecutor’s Victim Services Unit is a separate contact. Call 911 for immediate danger.

resources.name: AllThrive 365 — Healthy Homes air-conditioning assistance
resources.description: Provides air-conditioning assistance for eligible homeowners without a working home cooling system.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides air-conditioning assistance for eligible homeowners without a working home cooling system.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Own and occupy the home in La Paz, Maricopa, Pinal, Yavapai or Yuma County, meet the programme’s income limit of 200% of the federal poverty level, and lack home cooling. Older adults, people with disabilities and households with small children receive priority.

**Population Served**
Eligible homeowners in the five counties, including Mesa homeowners within Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call or email the Healthy Homes team to explain the cooling problem and ask about current assessment and application steps. The website’s household assessment form is not an application for services.

**Important Information to Know**
Funding, assessment, repair scope and availability must be confirmed. AllThrive’s separate weatherization programme excludes some cities; that exclusion does not describe Healthy Homes eligibility.

resources.name: Valleywise Behavioral Health Center — Mesa and Outpatient Psychiatry
resources.description: Mesa behavioral-health center with inpatient services and a separately accessed outpatient psychiatry clinic. Outpatient screening, appointment hours and self-pay rules differ from campus and specialty services.
resources.address: 570 W. Brown Rd, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Campus services are listed 24/7. Outpatient psychiatry: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m., by appointment; no walk-ins.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Inpatient behavioral-health services and a distinct outpatient psychiatry pathway for assessment, medication management and psychotherapy. Valleywise also describes interpreter, care-management/social-service and telehealth support. Ask the system about appropriate ACT or adolescent/teen psychosis specialty routing; not every linked specialty is established at this Mesa site.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Outpatient psychiatry needs no referral but begins with a 15–30 minute telephone screening and may redirect the caller if another service fits better. Inpatient, court-related and specialty programmes have separate assessment, referral, age and payment rules.

**Population Served**
Mesa and Maricopa County patients seeking behavioral-health stabilization or outpatient psychiatric care, including child appointments when accepted by the applicable service.

**How to Best Connect**
For general scheduling, call 1-833-855-9973 or request a call back. For the Mesa center, call 602-344-5011. To make an appointment at the Mesa Outpatient Psychiatry Clinic, call 480-344-2100. The center is at 570 W. Brown Rd.

**Important Information to Know**
The outpatient clinic alone states no insurance acceptance and lists $50 initial assessment, $30 medication management, $12 therapy or combined visits, and $7 child appointments; confirm current charges and discuss cost concerns. These fees do not describe inpatient or other Valleywise care. A 24-hour campus is not 24-hour walk-in outpatient access, and this entry does not establish detox availability. For an immediate crisis use 988; call 911 for a medical emergency.

resources.name: Inter Tribal Council of Arizona Area Agency on Aging Region 8 - Public Benefits Outreach Program
resources.description: Free, objective and confidential public-benefits counseling for tribal elders and people with disabilities, covering Medicare, Medicaid, Social Security, ALTCS, veterans benefits, Indian Health Service, appeals and fraud prevention.
resources.address: 2214 N. Central Ave., Suite 100, Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.hours: Call the SHIP helpline and select option 2, or contact ITCA during business hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Public Benefits Outreach Program provides free health-benefits education and counseling for tribal elders and people with disabilities. Topics include Medicare, Medicaid/AHCCCS, Social Security, ALTCS, veterans benefits, Indian Health Service, appeals, other public benefits and Medicare fraud and abuse prevention.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is for tribal elderly people and people with disabilities served through ITCA's Area Agency on Aging. Correct counselor or local routing may depend on tribal community and affiliation.

**Population Served**
Tribal elders and people with disabilities in Arizona, including caregivers and family members seeking public-benefits guidance.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 800-432-4040 and select option 2 for the SHIP helpline. For ITCA program information, contact Mary Weston at 602-258-4822 or mary.weston@itcaonline.com.

**Important Information to Know**
The program counsels, educates and advocates; it does not approve benefits. Clients in Mesa who are not connected to a participating tribal community may also need local benefits help through Aster, SHIP Region One or NATIVE HEALTH.

resources.name: HonorHealth Desert Mission - Adult Day Health Care
resources.description: HonorHealth Desert Mission Adult Day Health Care provides affordable daytime support for seniors with memory loss, physical functioning changes or health-related challenges, including meals, enrichment, RN nursing care, personal care, social services, counseling and caregiver respite.
resources.address: 303 E. Eva St., Phoenix, AZ 85020
resources.hours: Call for current program hours, transportation area and enrollment availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Adult day health care provides supervised daytime programming, meals, enrichment, nursing care by an RN, personal care, social services, counseling and respite for caregivers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is for seniors with memory loss, physical functioning changes or health-related challenges. Enrollment, health fit, financial assistance, payer rules and transportation availability require intake confirmation.

**Population Served**
Phoenix-area older adults who need adult day health care and caregivers who need respite.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-786-1060 and ask about Adult Day Health Care intake, fees, financial assistance, transportation boundaries and whether a Mesa client can be served.

**Important Information to Know**
Mesa transportation and service-area fit are uncertain. Treat this as a Phoenix reserve option unless Desert Mission confirms practical access for the client.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Health Services Bureau of Vital Records - statewide vital records, amendments and delayed registration
resources.description: ADHS Bureau of Vital Records is the state vital-records authority for Arizona birth and death records, including delayed birth registration, corrections, amendments, mail ordering and VitalChek expedited ordering.
resources.address: 150 N 18th Ave, Ste. 120, Phoenix, AZ 85007; mailing address PO Box 6018, Phoenix, AZ 85005
resources.hours: Monday-Friday, 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; closed weekends and state holidays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The ADHS Bureau of Vital Records maintains and issues Arizona vital records and handles state-level specialty services such as delayed birth registration, foreign-born registration, adoptions, and corrections or amendments. It is the appropriate state contact when a county vital-records office cannot resolve an Arizona birth or death record issue.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be legally entitled to request or amend the Arizona record and must provide the identity, relationship, legal authority and supporting evidence required for the specific record or amendment. Arizona cannot issue birth or death records from other states.

**Population Served**
People who need Arizona birth or death records, delayed Arizona birth registration, or Arizona vital-record amendments, including Mesa and Maricopa County clients with complex or historical record issues.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-364-1300 or 888-816-5907. Use the ADHS Vital Records website for the current application, mail instructions, online ordering options and specialty-service instructions. The state office lists 150 N 18th Ave, Ste. 120 in Phoenix and mailing address PO Box 6018, Phoenix, AZ 85005.

**Important Information to Know**
ADHS has reported that the Bureau no longer provides same-day walk-in certificate issuance for ordinary certificate copies; local county vital-records offices may be better for same-day Arizona certificate service. State specialty services, including delayed birth registration and older corrections or amendments, may require an appointment or special evidence. VitalChek is an expedited vendor option and may add vendor fees.

resources.name: notMYkid — youth behavioral health and family navigation
resources.description: notMYkid provides youth and family prevention, behavioral-health, early-intervention and substance-use recovery programming for Arizona teens, young adults, parents and schools.
resources.address: 5310 E Shea Blvd, Scottsdale, AZ 85254
resources.hours: Use the Family Navigator/Get Help Now route or call; public office hours were not posted on the program page.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Behavioral health services, prevention education, Project REWIND early intervention, substance-use prevention, substance-use recovery, teen mental-health support, parent support, school/educator programs and family navigation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Behavioral health services are listed for teens and young adults ages 10-24 on campus and virtually for Arizona youth. School, parent and prevention programs have program-specific access. Confirm cost, insurance, grant-funded availability and Mesa-family telehealth options.

**Population Served**
Arizona teens, young adults, parents/families, schools and educators dealing with or trying to prevent mental-health and substance-use challenges.

**How to Best Connect**
Use Get Help Now or Talk to a Navigator on the official site, call 602-652-0163, or email info@notmykid.org. The mailing address is 5310 E Shea Blvd, Scottsdale, AZ 85254.

**Important Information to Know**
This is prevention, early intervention, counseling, recovery support and navigation, not detox, residential treatment, MAT or emergency crisis response. Confirm appointments, fees and whether the requested service is virtual, campus-based or school-based.

resources.name: Valle del Sol East Valley — integrated care and medication-assisted treatment
resources.description: Valle del Sol's East Valley clinic in Mesa provides psychiatric evaluations, medication management, counseling, integrated mental health, family practice/pediatrics and medication-assisted treatment, with AHCCCS, Medicare, private insurance and sliding-scale/self-pay options described by Valle del Sol.
resources.address: 334 W. 10th Pl, Suite 100, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: East Valley clinic: Monday-Friday 7:00 AM-5:00 PM; Saturday-Sunday closed. Dosing hours: Monday-Friday 4:30 AM-11:00 AM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Psychiatric evaluation, medication management, counseling, integrated mental health, telehealth psychiatry when in-person visits are not possible, family practice, pediatrics and medication-assisted treatment at the East Valley clinic.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adults and youth needing behavioral-health or integrated medical care may call or schedule. Valle del Sol says no referral is needed to start psychiatry, accepts Medicaid/AHCCCS, Medicare and private insurance, offers sliding-scale fees based on income, and works with patients regardless of ability to pay.

**Population Served**
Mesa and East Valley clients, including English- and Spanish-speaking clients, adults, youth and families needing psychiatry, counseling or integrated care.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-258-6797 or use the online schedule-an-appointment link. The East Valley clinic is at 334 W. 10th Pl, Suite 100, Mesa. After-hours services are available by calling the same main number.

**Important Information to Know**
Dosing hours are earlier than ordinary clinic hours. Confirm the specific medicine/service, first-intake and dosing steps, payer coverage, sliding-fee paperwork, telehealth access and any same-day availability. Ask whether the East Valley or Southeast Valley Mesa clinic is appropriate; after-hours phone access is not a promise of walk-in dosing.

resources.name: Area Agency on Aging, Region One - Benefits Assistance Program / SHIP Counseling
resources.description: Area Agency on Aging Region One's Benefits Assistance Program provides objective Medicare counseling, Medicare cost-saving screening, appeals/problem-resolution help, and basic Social Security/SSI information.
resources.address: 1366 E Thomas Rd, Suite 108, Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.hours: 24-Hour Senior HELP LINE is available by phone; Benefits Assistance appointments and counseling arrangements should be requested through Area Agency on Aging.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Certified Medicare counselors and volunteers provide objective information about Medicare, Medicare Advantage, Medicare Supplements, Medicare drug coverage, Medicare cost-saving programs, appeals/problem resolution, Medicare scams/fraud education, and basic information on Social Security and SSI.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Best fit for older adults, Medicare beneficiaries, people approaching Medicare, younger adults with disabilities who need Medicare-related counseling, and caregivers. Specific benefit eligibility depends on the program being screened.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County older adults, people with disabilities, Medicare beneficiaries, and caregivers, including Mesa residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the 24-Hour Senior HELP LINE at 602-264-4357 or toll-free 888-783-7500. Text/SMS contact listed by the agency is 520-775-1899. Ask for Benefits Assistance Program counseling and confirm whether phone, remote, Mesa-area, or homebound accommodations are available.

**Important Information to Know**
This is benefits counseling and screening, not direct cash. It may help identify Medicare Savings Programs, SSI/Social Security next steps, claims issues, or appeals options, but application decisions come from the benefit agencies.

resources.name: Native American Connections - Affordable Housing for Individuals and Families
resources.description: Native American Connections provides income-based and market-rate affordable apartment rentals for individuals, families, and seniors in Phoenix and Glendale, with more than 400 affordable units, resident services, onsite and community resource connections, and an online application route.
resources.address: 3216 N 3rd Street, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Affordable apartment rentals, income-based and market-rate housing, resident services, onsite and community resource connections, health and wellness support, financial literacy, family-strengthening activities, and community programming.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be at least 18, meet NAC affordable-housing rental criteria, provide proof of income and ID verification, and pay a $40 application fee per applicant age 18 or older. Applicants must have sustainable income at the time of application.

**Population Served**
Low-income individuals, families with children, and seniors seeking affordable housing in the Phoenix metro area. NAC housing programs are open to all people, with specialized communities for families, seniors, chronically homeless individuals, and homeless youth.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Get Started or Apply Now link on NAC's affordable-housing page. NAC administrative address: 3216 N 3rd Street, Phoenix, AZ 85012.

**Important Information to Know**
Individual properties have different unit sizes, income limits, screening criteria, fees, and availability. The current official affordable-housing page provides an Apply Now route; confirm openings and property-specific criteria before referral.

resources.name: Habitat for Humanity Central Arizona — Veteran housing and repairs
resources.description: Provides a veteran-focused pathway to homeownership, essential home repairs and accessibility modifications.
resources.address: 2830 West Glendale Avenue, Suite 33, Phoenix, AZ 85051
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides a veteran-focused pathway to homeownership, essential home repairs and accessibility modifications.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must meet the relevant Habitat requirements, including income guidelines for homeownership, and document military veteran status. Repair eligibility is assessed for the household and property.

**Population Served**
Veterans and their families in Maricopa County and selected parts of Pinal County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-268-9022 and ask for Family Services, or submit the website contact form. Ask which programme serves the specific address and need.

**Important Information to Know**
Homeownership involves an affordable mortgage rather than a free home. Approval, work scope and timing depend on assessment and capacity; this is not assured immediate emergency repair.

resources.name: Control Alt Delete - One-Time Emergency Escape Assistance
resources.description: Control Alt Delete provides one-time, advocate-referred emergency help to remove immediate barriers to escaping current domestic violence, such as emergency rides, hotel accommodations, grocery assistance, basic needs and security measures.
resources.hours: Online advocate referral form is available on the Get Help page. Response and funding are not guaranteed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
One-time emergency escape assistance for current domestic-violence situations, including possible cab rides, hotel accommodations, grocery assistance, basic immediate needs and security measures.

**Eligibility Requirements**
An advocate must submit the referral for assistance. Services are for people escaping current domestic violence, are based on available funding, must fit the agency's scope and may require documentation.

**Population Served**
Domestic-violence victims in Arizona and the Phoenix metropolitan area who are working with an advocate and need immediate barriers removed to leave abuse.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask a victim/shelter advocate, police or prosecutor advocate, crisis response team, family advocacy center or similar professional to submit the Get Help form and monitor email follow-up. There is no public intake phone on the page. Call 911 for immediate danger.

**Important Information to Know**
Survivors cannot self-refer, and assistance is not guaranteed. There is no public intake phone on the official page; the form and advocate email follow-up are the actionable route.

resources.name: The Porch / One Life Church — community resource hub
resources.description: The Porch at One Life Church is a Mesa resource hub where people can get support, classes and access to resource stores; 2-1-1 evidence supports Friday food, clothing, hygiene and Wi-Fi access, while the official page frames services through a free Neighbor/points model.
resources.address: E. University Drive, Mesa; call to confirm The Porch entrance. Listings differ between 2051 and 2052; church general campus/office is 2130 E. University Dr.
resources.hours: Call for current hub/classes/store and cooling schedules. Older 2-1-1 resource hours: Friday 11 a.m.–3 p.m.; City 2026 cooling listing: Friday 9 a.m.–1 p.m.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Community support, classes and resource-store access through free Neighbor membership and participation points. Referral evidence describes food, clothing, hygiene items and Wi-Fi; the City also lists a seasonal cooling connection. These activities can have different hours and access rules.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page says anyone is welcome to stop by and that becoming a Neighbor is free. It also says greater access to resources works through becoming a Neighbor, attending weekly classes, earning points and shopping in resource stores. 2-1-1 lists no restrictions for the Friday distribution.

**Population Served**
People in Mesa needing practical support, food, clothing, hygiene items, classes or community-resource access.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-834-9120 or email info@onelifeaz.church. Ask for the current Porch entrance, first-visit access, class/store rules and available supplies. For cooling, confirm that the seasonal service is still active and its hours.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not an unrestricted open pantry, coordinated-entry assessment or overnight shelter. Official church and referral/cooling listings use different addresses and schedules; confirm the specific service before travel. Resource access may depend on participation and inventory.

resources.name: Arizona Legal Women and Youth Services (ALWAYS) · Legal services
