resources.description: No-cost legal services for eligible youth and young adults impacted by homelessness, trafficking, abuse, domestic violence, or foster care, including immigration, family law, survivor justice, community clinics, and criminal-history barriers.
resources.address: Mail only: 24 W. Camelback Rd., Box A335, Phoenix, AZ 85013; law office location is confidential.
resources.hours: Law office location is confidential; call for appointments or current intake.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost civil legal consultations, accepted-case representation and referrals supporting safety, stability and self-sufficiency. Services include immigration, survivor/family-related legal needs and barriers involving work, housing or identity documents. Immigration screening may cover DACA, trafficking/crime-victim remedies and Special Immigrant Juvenile matters when within the programme’s scope. Its New Roads to Success practice helps eligible clients request conviction set-asides and good-cause exceptions for employment fingerprint-clearance cards, and obtain government identity documents. The trafficking-survivor practice also lists victim representation and compensation claims.

**Eligibility Requirements**
General services focus on people 26 or younger in Maricopa or Pima County affected by homelessness/couch-surfing, shelter/transitional/group-home living, abuse or domestic violence, sex/labor trafficking or current/prior foster care. Trafficking survivors of any age, including men, may qualify for the applicable services; ask about the specific matter and geographic fit.

**Population Served**
Eligible youth, young adults and survivors of human trafficking.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-248-7055 or use the online inquiry. Mail addresses do not establish walk-in intake.

**Important Information to Know**
Acceptance depends on legal need, conflicts and capacity; no representation is guaranteed. The eligibility page excludes pending criminal charges and dependency/severance actions, while the survivor page separately lists victim representation in criminal court; clarify which practice applies to the matter. Its name does not make all women or all youth eligible. It is not a shelter or crisis hotline, and its mailing address is not walk-in intake.

resources.name: Arizona Public Service - Energy Support and Energy Support with Medical
resources.description: APS Energy Support and Energy Support with Medical provide monthly APS electric-bill discounts for income-qualified APS customers, with a medical variant for households using critical electric medical equipment.
resources.hours: Online applications available; call program representative for questions.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Energy Support gives qualified APS customers a monthly discount of up to 25% or 60%. Energy Support with Medical gives qualified customers with critical electric medical equipment a discount of up to 35% or 60% and planned outage notifications.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The customer must have APS electric service, meet household income guidelines and provide proof of household income or qualifying public-assistance documentation. Energy Support with Medical additionally requires qualifying critical medical equipment at home. Customers must reapply every 24 months.

**Population Served**
Income-qualified APS residential customers, including APS-served parts of Maricopa County. The medical option serves households relying on electricity for critical medical equipment.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online from the APS Energy Support page or apply by mail using APS's application instructions. For questions, call 844-309-5655.

**Important Information to Know**
Verify the client is an APS customer before referral. The discount applies to electricity costs only and not taxes, franchise fees or some other bill components. Funds and program rules are subject to change.

resources.name: Prisma Community Care - Health Clinic and PrEP Services
resources.description: Prisma Community Care provides affordable LGBTQ-affirming primary care, mental health care, HIV/STI testing and treatment, PrEP/PEP, HIV care, gender-affirming care, navigation and social support in Phoenix.
resources.address: 1101 N. Central Ave., Suite 200, Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.hours: Wellness Center: Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-7:00 PM, Friday 8:00 AM-3:00 PM. HIV/STI testing clinic: Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-6:00 PM, Friday 8:00 AM-2:00 PM; testing ends one hour before closing and requires appointment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Primary care, mental health care, HIV/STI testing and treatment, PrEP, PEP, HIV care, sexual health and wellness, gender-affirming care, navigation services, AHCCCS enrollment, lab-assistance cost coverage, pharmacy cost/coverage help through participating pharmacies and social support services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Prisma accepts Medicare, AHCCCS/AIHP and many commercial plans. People without insurance may use low self-pay rates or a sliding-fee scale based on income and ability to pay. No-cost HIV/STI testing is available by appointment through grant funding.

**Population Served**
2SLGBTQIA+ people, people of color, people affected by HIV, uninsured and underinsured patients, and others who have faced discrimination in healthcare in the Phoenix metro area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-307-5330, request an appointment online or schedule a new-patient phone call before going to the clinic. Address: 1101 N. Central Ave., Suite 200, Phoenix, AZ 85004. For possible HIV exposure within 72 hours, call the PEP Hotline at 602-595-8170.

**Important Information to Know**
HIV/STI testing is by appointment; walk-ins are not accepted. Same-day appointment availability may be checked by phone. This is in Phoenix, not Mesa, but it is a strong specialty option for LGBTQ-affirming care and HIV prevention.

resources.name: U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Arizona - Bankruptcy Self-Help Center and volunteer attorney consultations
resources.description: The U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Arizona provides bankruptcy self-help information plus scheduled free 20- to 30-minute volunteer attorney consultations for eligible Chapter 7 or 13 individuals and individual creditors.
resources.address: 230 N. 1st Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.hours: Self-Help Center hours are listed as 8:30 AM-4:00 PM daily; volunteer attorney consultations are by appointment only.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Bankruptcy process information, walk-in Self-Help Center access, and scheduled free 20- to 30-minute consultations with volunteer attorneys in person or by telephone.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The consultation service is available only to individuals who have filed or are considering filing Chapter 7 or Chapter 13 bankruptcy and to an individual creditor in a bankruptcy case. Volunteer attorneys do not consult on Chapter 11 cases. Users must first watch bankruptcy education videos and complete an online questionnaire.

**Population Served**
People in the District of Arizona, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents, who are considering or involved in individual Chapter 7 or Chapter 13 cases, or individual creditors in a bankruptcy case.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the court's online scheduling application after watching the bankruptcy education videos and completing the questionnaire. The Phoenix Self-Help Center is on the 1st floor of the U.S. Bankruptcy Courthouse at 230 N. 1st Ave.; phone information lines include 866-553-0893 and 602-682-4000.

**Important Information to Know**
This is brief advice and self-help, not full representation. The court warns that its information is not a substitute for competent legal counsel.

resources.name: Over-Flo Missions - MesaCAN Emergency Food Box Distribution
resources.description: Over-Flo Missions distributes emergency food boxes every Thursday at A New Leaf's MesaCAN location and also lists a last-Saturday food-box distribution connected to its community feast.
resources.address: A New Leaf / MesaCAN, 635 E. Broadway Rd., Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: Emergency food boxes at A New Leaf/MesaCAN: Thursday 1:00-3:00 PM. Last-Saturday food-box distribution: 9:30-10:30 AM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency food boxes at A New Leaf in Mesa/MesaCAN. Over-Flo also describes snack bags for unsheltered people and a last-Saturday food-box distribution connected to a community meal.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page describes service to homeless individuals and families with food insecurity, but does not publish detailed document, income or residence requirements. Call to confirm current intake expectations.

**Population Served**
People and families experiencing food insecurity or homelessness who can access the Mesa distribution.

**How to Best Connect**
For Thursday emergency food boxes, go to A New Leaf/MesaCAN during the 1:00-3:00 PM window and call Over-Flo Missions at 480-606-2049 with questions. Confirm the exact entrance at 635 E. Broadway Rd. before referral.

**Important Information to Know**
The Over-Flo page names the MesaCAN host site but does not show the street address in that section; the saved local evidence gives 635 E. Broadway Rd. Confirm same-week operation before sending someone.

resources.name: Christ Cares Ministries - Christ Cares for Kids
resources.description: Christ Cares for Kids provides diapers, clothing and other items for children newborn to age 5, and links families with community services. The ministry reports most families served are below the federal poverty level.
resources.address: 4018 N 40th St, Phoenix, AZ 85018
resources.hours: Mondays and Wednesdays 8:00 AM-11:00 AM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Diapers, clothing and other items for children newborn through age 5, plus help linking families with community services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For families with young children age 5 and younger who need support. The official page does not publish income documentation, residency limits or item frequency rules.

**Population Served**
Phoenix-area families with children newborn through age 5, especially low-income families; the ministry states more than 98% of families served fall below the federal poverty level.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit during Monday or Wednesday 8:00 AM-11:00 AM hours at 4018 N 40th St, Phoenix, or contact info@christcaresclinic.org. The general phone is 602-955-0617.

**Important Information to Know**
This is faith-based and Phoenix-centered. Mesa access is not specifically stated; confirm before sending a Mesa family and ask about current diaper/clothing sizes and inventory.

resources.name: Jacob's Hope - Inpatient Specialty Care Nursery and Family Support for Substance-Exposed Newborns
resources.description: Jacob's Hope is a Mesa nonprofit specialty care nursery providing 24-hour medical care for substance-exposed newborns and family support for mothers, caregivers, and agencies, including education, room-in support, DCS case-plan help, and links to housing, MAT, recovery, food, transportation, and OB care resources.
resources.address: 1150 N. Country Club Dr., Unit 12, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Newborn specialty care is described as 24-hour care; call or use the referral forms for admission and family-support details.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
24-hour specialty nursery care for substance-exposed newborns experiencing withdrawal, Eat/Sleep/Console support, family education, room-in support, discharge planning and DCS case-plan help. Family care coordination may connect caregivers to recovery/MAT providers, housing/legal resources, WIC, OB care, infant supplies/food, peer support and transportation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Pregnant people, recently delivered mothers, caregivers, families, hospitals, and agencies may reach out about substance-exposed newborn care or worries about a baby's health. Admission depends on clinical appropriateness, referral information, and capacity.

**Population Served**
Mothers, newborns, grandparents, partners, caregivers, hospitals, and agencies supporting a substance-exposed baby or a family affected by substance use in Mesa and Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-398-7373. Families can use the Self & Family Referral form, and hospitals or agencies can use the Agency Referral route on the website.

**Important Information to Know**
Admission, transport and placement depend on the newborn’s clinical needs, medical coordination and capacity. Self/family inquiries do not guarantee nursery admission. This is not general adult detox, independent legal representation or direct adult medication prescribing. Ask separately whether any Crisis to Care grant-funded supports are currently offered.

resources.name: Arizona DCS — Services for incarcerated parents
resources.description: Coordinates case planning, available services and appropriate parent-child contact for incarcerated parents in a DCS dependency case.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Coordinates case planning, available services and appropriate parent-child contact for incarcerated parents in a DCS dependency case.

**Eligibility Requirements**
An active dependency case and applicable court orders govern participation; facility rules also affect access.

**Population Served**
Detained or incarcerated parents whose children have an Arizona DCS dependency case.

**How to Best Connect**
Work through the assigned DCS specialist and dependency attorney; ask the facility’s correctional officer or jail program coordinator to help arrange approved participation.

**Important Information to Know**
The policy supports involvement where possible; it does not override a court restriction or guarantee reunification. Parent-child contact may use approved alternatives when in-person visits are unavailable.

resources.name: NATIVE HEALTH Mesa — food pantry, nutrition programmes and WIC
resources.description: Mesa food pantry, child snacks and seasonal nutrition activities, waitlisted senior food boxes and a separately administered WIC clinic at NATIVE HEALTH Mesa.
resources.address: 777 W. Southern Ave., Building B, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Pantry: Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–noon and 1:30–3 p.m. WIC: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday, 7 a.m.–4 p.m.; Thursday, 9 a.m.–6 p.m. Confirm individual programme schedules.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Mesa TEFAP pantry with fresh/nonperishable food, child snacks during clinic hours, seasonal Kid’s Cafe summer meals, Read It and Eat produce bags and CSFP senior boxes. Donor-dependent programmes include Indigenous Young Chefs and Urban Native American Senior Food Bags. A separate Mesa WIC clinic provides nutrition benefits.

**Eligibility Requirements**
TEFAP requests name, Maricopa County address, birth date and income self-declaration; financial documents are not needed. Child snacks are for under-18s. CSFP lists 60+, Arizona address, photo ID/birth date, income criteria and annual enrollment/monthly pickup. WIC has separate pregnancy/postpartum/breastfeeding or child-under-five and other WIC rules; local or temporary Maricopa County residence applies. Confirm the specific programme.

**Population Served**
Mesa and Maricopa County households needing food support, including families with children, seniors and Native American/urban Indigenous elders or families for specific culturally focused programs.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-279-5262; pantry questions go to Susan Levy, ext. 11027, or slevy@nachci.com; CSFP/Native senior-bag questions to Olivia, ext. 11022. WIC appointments: 800-470-5930. Confirm the programme’s building/entrance at 777 W. Southern Ave. and hours before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
Mesa and Central CSFP are listed full; ask about the waitlist. Seasonal meals and donor-supported supplies are not guaranteed year-round. Native identity is not established as a requirement for every service. Pantry, senior boxes, culturally focused programmes and WIC have different rules.

resources.name: AHCCCS Office of Human Rights — SMI rights and Special Assistance
resources.description: Arizona public behavioral-health rights advocacy and technical assistance for people with a Serious Mental Illness designation, with designated advocates for those qualifying for Special Assistance.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Advocacy for AHCCCS members with a Serious Mental Illness designation, including help understanding and exercising rights, accessing entitled behavioral-health services, self-advocacy education, Special Assistance representation, and participation in treatment planning, discharge planning, SMI appeals, grievances and investigations.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Technical assistance is available concerning Arizona serious-mental-illness rights. An assigned advocate requires Special Assistance eligibility; SMI rights are not limited to Medicaid enrollment.

**Population Served**
Arizonans with a Serious Mental Illness designation and related public behavioral-health rights, including people not enrolled in Medicaid; natural supports, guardians or representatives may assist.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 800-421-2142 or email OHRts@azahcccs.gov. Explain the rights or service-access issue and ask whether technical assistance or Special Assistance is appropriate.

**Important Information to Know**
This office provides rights/service-access assistance, not therapy, medication or crisis care. Technical assistance and an assigned Special Assistance advocate have different rules. If the direct OHR route does not connect, ask for OHR through AHCCCS at 602-417-4000 or 800-654-8713.

resources.name: St. Vincent de Paul — Queen of Peace food assistance
resources.description: Provides a neighborhood food-box contact through the Queen of Peace conference in downtown Mesa.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides a neighborhood food-box contact through the Queen of Peace conference in downtown Mesa.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Conference service boundaries and current assistance rules apply; the wider SVdP network routes households by address.

**Population Served**
Households seeking food support in the conference’s Mesa neighborhood.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-366-4953 before travel and give the household address. Ask about the current pickup site, documents and whether any delivery is available.

**Important Information to Know**
Older calendars describe a narrow service area and scheduled pickup/delivery, but those details require confirmation. Parish office or Mass hours are not pantry hours; no delivery is guaranteed.

resources.name: Tailor Made for Success - Men's Professional Attire and Career Support
resources.description: Tailor Made for Success, associated with Dress for Success Arizona, provides unemployed and underemployed men with professional attire for job search and interviews plus resume, interview, career coaching, networking and mentorship support.
resources.address: 3110 N Central Ave, D-200, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.hours: Appointments available upon request. Dress for Success Arizona hours: Monday-Thursday 9:00 AM-4:30 PM; 2nd and 4th Saturday by appointment only; closed Friday.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Tailor Made for Success provides men with professional attire tailored for job search and interviews. It also offers interview styling, resume and job-interview training, career coaching, networking, mentorship and related wrap-around support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is for unemployed and underemployed men preparing to enter or advance in the workforce. Appointments are available by request through the program's service request/contact link.

**Population Served**
Men who need professional attire and job-search support in the greater Phoenix area, including Mesa clients who can access the Phoenix location or remote intake.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the request-services/contact link on the Tailor Made for Success page, call 602-489-7397 or email services@dfsarizona.org. The listed office is Dress for Success Arizona at 3110 N Central Ave, D-200 in Phoenix.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a professional/workforce attire program, not a general clothing closet. Advanced appointments are encouraged; walk-in services may depend on availability and wait times.

resources.name: AZCrimeVictimHelp — victim legal resources
resources.description: Legal information and resource connections for crime victims in Arizona.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Legal information and resource connections for crime victims in Arizona.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Individual programs determine case eligibility, geography and capacity.

**Population Served**
Crime victims and people helping them locate appropriate legal support.

**How to Best Connect**
Use AZCrimeVictimHelp to find information and contact a listed service for the relevant need.

**Important Information to Know**
The portal does not itself provide emergency response or promise attorney representation.

resources.name: East Valley Institute of Technology · Adult Basic Education and High School Equivalency/GED Program
resources.description: EVIT Adult Basic Education helps qualifying learners age 16 and older build academic, digital, financial, workforce, and GED/HSE skills through tuition-free ABE when eligible, with online and in-person coursework and links to career training programs.
resources.address: 1601 W. Main St., Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
EVIT Adult Basic Education helps adults build skills for work, college, and life. Services include GED/HSE preparation, adult basic education, reading, writing, math, science, social studies, economics, digital literacy, financial literacy, workforce preparedness, individualized or small-group tutoring, self-paced coursework, and support while attending selected career training programs. ABE coursework is available online and in person; career and technical education programs are in person.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be age 16 or older, not enrolled or required to be enrolled in secondary school, lawfully present in the United States under Arizona law, and meet at least one qualifying need: assistance with reading, math, and/or computer skills; lack of a secondary diploma or equivalent; or English language learner status. ABE programs are tuition-free for those who qualify.

**Population Served**
Mesa and East Valley learners seeking adult basic education, GED/HSE, digital or financial literacy, workforce preparation, or support toward certifications in high-demand industries.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Apply for ABE link on the EVIT Adult Basic Education page or call EVIT at 480-461-4000. EVIT is located at 1601 W. Main St., Mesa. Classes are offered in 9-week sessions; use the course catalog and admissions links to confirm schedule.

**Important Information to Know**
Additional funding may be available to assist with tuition for CTE courses, but career training programs have separate program costs and requirements. EVIT states lack of English language skills is not a barrier to admission and participation in EVIT CTE programs. Confirm the exact program, schedule, tuition, and funding before enrollment.

resources.name: Disabled American Veterans East Valley Chapter 8 - Claims Assistance and Medical Appointment Rides
resources.description: Disabled American Veterans East Valley Chapter 8 provides no-cost local help with VA disability claims, benefits and appeals, appointment scheduling, veteran resources, and related support such as medical-appointment ride information.
resources.address: 655 N. Gilbert Road, Mesa, AZ 85203
resources.hours: Mesa office Monday-Friday 9 AM-noon and one Saturday monthly. Claims appointments Monday/Tuesday/Friday; walk-ins Wednesday/Thursday. Confirm satellite-clinic appointments directly.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free confidential assistance preparing VA disability claims, benefit and pension requests or appeals, plus referrals for veteran resources and medical-appointment transportation. The chapter also has a separate application for limited one-time financial assistance.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Veterans seeking VA disability, benefits, pension, or appeal help may contact the chapter. Specific representation, financial assistance, and transportation support depend on DAV rules, documentation, and availability.

**Population Served**
Veterans in Mesa, the East Valley, and nearby Arizona communities, including disabled veterans and veterans needing local claims-navigation support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-890-2424 or use the chapter appointment route on the website. Visit 655 N. Gilbert Road during posted hours; use appointments for Monday/Tuesday/Friday claims work and walk-ins for Wednesday/Thursday morning claims help.

**Important Information to Know**
Chapter service officers help prepare claims; formal accredited representation may involve DAV National Service Officers. The separate assistance application offers up to $300 toward eligible rent, utility or transportation needs, subject to documentation and available funds; a larger balance requires a plan to cover the remainder. Confirm ride arrangements and all appointment schedules before traveling.

resources.name: VA Discharge Upgrade or Correction Instructions Tool
resources.description: VA online tool that asks situation-specific questions and gives customized instructions, forms, and submission routing for a discharge upgrade or correction; it does not file the application.
resources.hours: Online tool available through VA.gov; VA benefits hotline Mon-Fri 8:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m. ET for general help.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The VA discharge-upgrade/correction tool helps former service members identify how to apply for a discharge upgrade or correction. It provides customized step-by-step instructions, needed forms, and the correct submission address or review board based on answers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A person may use the tool if they believe their discharge character or discharge paperwork is incorrect or should be upgraded. Stronger cases may involve evidence related to PTSD, TBI, military sexual trauma, sexual orientation policy, harassment, or other service-connected circumstances.

**Population Served**
Veterans and former service members nationwide, including Mesa residents, who need to seek a discharge upgrade or correction.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the VA online tool and answer the questions. For benefits questions, call 800-827-1000 or seek help from an accredited attorney, claims agent, or Veterans Service Organization representative.

**Important Information to Know**
The tool gives instructions but does not submit the application. A VA Character of Discharge review may affect VA benefit eligibility but does not change the DD214; a military board process is needed for DD214 changes.

resources.name: Friendly House - Victim Advocate Services
resources.description: Friendly House Victim Advocate Services supports adult Maricopa County primary and secondary crime victims with advocacy, transportation assistance, relocation assistance when applicable, victim compensation navigation, court advocacy, safety planning, and referrals.
resources.address: 802 S 1st Ave, Suite 2, Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.hours: Leave voicemail with a safe callback number if calling the victim advocate line.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Victim advocacy for primary and secondary crime victims, including individual advocacy, transportation assistance, relocation assistance when applicable, safety planning, victim compensation help, referrals, and court advocacy.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Friendly House states clients must be age 18 or older and live in Maricopa County.

**Population Served**
Adult primary and secondary victims of crime living in Maricopa County, including Mesa residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-416-7245 and leave a voicemail with a safe phone number for callback, or email FHVAS@friendlyhouse.org. The main Friendly House office is at 802 S 1st Ave, Suite 2, Phoenix.

**Important Information to Know**
This is advocacy and navigation with some transportation or relocation assistance when applicable, not a guaranteed direct cash program. For immediate danger, call 911; the page also lists 24-hour crisis lines.

resources.name: City of Mesa - Limited-Income Utility Programs
resources.description: City of Mesa limited-income utility programs include a Senior Water Rate discount and a seasonal Summer Electric Assistance credit for income-qualified City electric customers, plus general City utility customer service/payment-arrangement access.
resources.phone: 480-644-2221; Summer Electric Assistance 480-644-6907; Aster application help 480-964-9014
resources.hours: City utility customer contact hours for the Senior Water Rate page: Monday-Thursday 7:00 AM-6:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The City of Mesa's Limited Income Senior Rate Program gives qualifying seniors a 30% discount on the Water Service Rate component of a City utility bill. The Summer Electric Assistance Program gives eligible City of Mesa electric customers limited short-term bill relief during July, August and September by removing the monthly service charge and the first 80 kWh usage charge.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For the Senior Water Rate, the applicant must be age 60 or older, be the utility account holder, live full-time at the service address, and meet the limited-income threshold listed by the City. For Summer Electric Assistance, the customer must be income-qualified, live in Mesa's Electric Service Area and receive electric service from the City of Mesa, not SRP. Summer Electric Assistance has a seasonal application window.

**Population Served**
Limited-income City of Mesa utility customers; the water discount is for seniors, and Summer Electric Assistance is for qualifying City electric customers only.

**How to Best Connect**
For Senior Water Rate, call 480-644-2221 or email contactcenter@mesaaz.gov; Aster Aging can help seniors with the application at 480-964-9014 or socialservices@asteraz.org. For Summer Electric Assistance, call 480-644-6907 or email energyresources.info@mesaaz.gov. City utility customer contact hours listed for the Senior Water Rate page are Monday-Thursday 7:00 AM-6:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
Summer Electric Assistance is not for SRP customers and the 2026 application window listed by the City was April 1 through August 1, 2026; late applications do not receive retroactive credit. The Senior Water Rate discount is not retroactive and applies after review and approval. These programs reduce bills; they are not unrestricted cash grants.

resources.name: Area Agency on Aging, Region One — legal-service referrals
resources.description: Older-adult legal-service navigation through the regional aging agency.
resources.address: 1366 E Thomas Rd, Suite 108, Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Information and referral to legal assistance and other services for older adults in Maricopa County.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The aging agency and each receiving legal program determine eligibility and current service availability.

**Population Served**
Older Maricopa County residents and people assisting them.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Senior HELP LINE at 602-264-4357 and ask about legal assistance for the person’s situation.

**Important Information to Know**
The aging agency is not the same organization as the Arizona Senior Citizens Law Project. The independent clinic serves county residents age 60 or older without an income cap; other programs may use different rules.

resources.name: Mesa VA Clinic
resources.description: Mesa VA Clinic is a local Phoenix VA Health Care System clinic offering mental-health care and connection into VA health services for eligible Veterans in Mesa and the East Valley.
resources.address: 4135 South Power Road, Suite 103, Mesa, AZ 85212-3625
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 7:30 AM-4:00 PM; closed Saturday-Sunday. Service hours may vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Mesa VA Clinic is a local VA clinic in Mesa. The official VA location page lists mental-health care for concerns such as addiction, depression, anxiety, trauma, PTSD, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, OCD, grief, anger, and relationship stress, with connection into the broader Phoenix VA system.

**Eligibility Requirements**
VA eligibility and clinical/appointment rules apply. The listed mental-health service needs no referral but ordinarily uses appointments. VA describes same-day mental-health help and possible access for some people without prior enrollment; ask VA to screen the individual situation.

**Population Served**
Veterans in Mesa and the East Valley who are enrolled in, eligible for, or seeking connection to Phoenix VA Health Care services.

**How to Best Connect**
Use VA Health Connect at 888-214-7264 for scheduling or routing. Visit the clinic at 4135 South Power Road, Suite 103, Mesa, AZ 85212-3625. Facility hours are Monday-Friday 7:30 AM-4:00 PM, with service-specific hours subject to change.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm which service is available at Mesa and whether another VA location or referral is needed; this is not the full Phoenix VA hospital or a 24-hour crisis clinic. For Veterans Crisis Line support, call 988 then press 1 or text 838255. Call 911 for immediate danger or a medical emergency.

resources.name: City of Phoenix Office of Homeless Solutions - 24/7 Heat Respite and Navigation Center
resources.description: The City of Phoenix 2026 24/7 heat respite center at 20 W Jackson St provides around-the-clock cooling space, water, navigation services, and connections to shelter and other resources during the heat season, with 2-1-1 transportation help to cooling centers.
resources.address: 20 W Jackson St, Phoenix, AZ
resources.hours: Open around the clock during the posted Phoenix heat-relief season starting May 1, 2026. 2-1-1 heat-relief transportation information line listed daily 9:00 AM-7:00 PM starting May 1.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Around-the-clock heat respite with cooling space, water, navigation services, and connection to shelter and other resources. Phoenix also directs people needing transportation to cooling centers or heat relief to call 2-1-1 during posted hours.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Phoenix page describes the 24/7 respite center as available for anyone who may need it during the heat-relief season. It is a Phoenix seasonal site, not a Mesa-specific shelter program.

**Population Served**
People needing heat relief in Phoenix and Maricopa County, including people experiencing homelessness or heat-related medical vulnerability who can reach the site.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to 20 W Jackson St, Phoenix, AZ during the active heat-relief season. Call 2-1-1 to ask about transportation or a closer cooling/respite site before sending someone from Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a seasonal weather-response resource. It should not be treated as long-term shelter or a guaranteed route into a bed. Confirm current seasonal operation, transportation and closer Mesa options before travel.

resources.name: Save the Family — family housing and supportive services
resources.description: Mesa/East Valley family housing programmes with case management and parent/child supports. Family Housing Hub and programme screening control entry; related ARM affordable rentals have separate eligibility and waitlist rules.
resources.address: 125 E University Dr, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; closed Saturday and Sunday.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Rapid Re-Housing, Tenant Based Rental Assistance and Step Up to Independence combine family housing support with case management, career/budgeting/parenting/life-skills learning, in-house mental-health access and child supports such as food, school supplies, education-plan help and counseling. Clothing and household assistance depend on participant case management and available supplies. ARM affordable rentals, career development and veteran programmes retain separate intake rules. Prior Mesa/Gilbert eviction-prevention referrals require confirmation of current funding.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Save the Family accepts incoming clients from the Family Housing Hub, the centralized intake and referral source for housing and human services. Step Up to Independence has a pre-screen questionnaire. ARM affordable units require income eligibility, verifiable income, waitlist participation, and compliance with ARM rules; the ARM waitlist was temporarily closed to new applications on the official page reviewed.

**Population Served**
Homeless and impoverished families and children in Mesa and the East Valley, plus eligible low-income individuals and families for ARM affordable rentals.

**How to Best Connect**
Families at risk of or currently homeless should start with Family Housing Hub. For Step Up to Independence, complete Save the Family's pre-screen if referred. For general questions, call 480-898-0228 or contact the Mesa office during business hours. Current ARM applicants should use the ARM email/update process on the official ARM page.

**Important Information to Know**
Neither a call nor Family Housing Hub referral guarantees shelter, rent assistance or a unit. Clothing/household help is participant support, not a public closet or furniture bank. Do not rely on unconfirmed eviction-prevention funds for a court or lockout deadline. ARM new-application status and the separate career/veteran programmes must be checked through their own routes; this broad record is not a reentry-specific programme.

resources.name: City of Mesa Housing and Community Development - HOME Tenant-Based Rental Assistance
resources.description: City of Mesa HOME Tenant-Based Rental Assistance can support low-income households with time-limited rent assistance, security deposits, and qualifying utility deposits. Mesa funds both nonprofit subrecipient TBRA programs and a limited city-administered TBRA deposit route tied to Housing Choice Voucher households.
resources.address: 200 S Center Street, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Lobby hours: Monday-Thursday 7:30 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Tenant-based rental assistance for low-income households that may pay part of rent for up to 24 months, provide security deposit assistance, and provide utility deposit assistance when paired with security deposit assistance. HOME-ARP funding can also support tenant-based rental assistance, supportive services, prevention services, housing counseling, affordable housing, and non-congregate shelter activities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program serves low-income individuals and families. HOME-ARP targets households who are homeless, at risk of homelessness, fleeing domestic violence, sex trafficking, or sexual assault, or otherwise facing housing instability. Specific intake may be through a nonprofit subrecipient or the City's limited in-house TBRA process.

**Population Served**
Low-income Mesa households and vulnerable households experiencing or at risk of homelessness or housing instability within the City of Mesa jurisdiction.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact City of Mesa Housing and Community Development at 480-644-3536 or CommunityDevelopment@mesaaz.gov to ask which HOME TBRA or HOME-ARP intake route is currently active. Office/lobby location: 200 S Center St, Mesa, AZ 85210.

**Important Information to Know**
The funding page partly addresses agency applicants, not a standing household application. Ask which city or nonprofit route is active, its eligibility and funding. The described limited city deposit route is tied to Housing Choice Voucher households; do not apply that condition automatically to every nonprofit TBRA programme. Listed HOME-ARP funding purposes do not guarantee that each activity currently accepts clients.

resources.name: Jewish Family & Children’s Service — Integrated Health and Substance-Use Care
resources.description: Integrated mental-health, substance-use and primary-care services, with help coordinating treatment and community resources.
resources.address: 880 N Colorado St, Gilbert, AZ 85233
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Integrated mental-health, substance-use and primary-care services, with help coordinating treatment and community resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**

JFCS lists acceptance of all AHCCCS health plans. Certain children may qualify for block-grant treatment funding when Medicaid coverage is unavailable or an eligibility decision is pending; funding rules require assessment.

**Population Served**

Children, adolescents, adults and older adults, including Mesa-area households seeking East Valley care.

**How to Best Connect**

New clients call 602-256-0528 for an appointment and appropriate placement. The East Valley Healthcare Center is in Gilbert; its local number is 480-820-0825. Existing clients contact their usual center.

**Important Information to Know**

Confirm which substance-use services the selected clinic provides, coverage and appointment availability. The described child block grant is not a promise of free adult treatment or unrestricted funding.

resources.name: Resurrection Street Ministry / S.T.U.F.F. - Vehicle Placement for People in Need
resources.description: Resurrection Street Ministry and S.T.U.F.F. Thrift Store accept vehicle donations and state that donated vehicles are passed on to provide transportation to people in need.
resources.address: 1135 E. Main St., Mesa, AZ 85203
resources.hours: Call the store/ministry for current hours, application steps and availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
S.T.U.F.F. accepts vehicle donations through Resurrection Street Ministry and says vehicles are passed on to provide transportation to people in need. The store also provides free clothes and accessible items to certain eligible groups.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The page does not publish vehicle applicant rules. For free clothes and other accessible items, it lists seniors age 65 and over, veterans who have disabilities or are low income, people experiencing homelessness, and families in crisis.

**Population Served**
Arizona or Mesa-area people in need may be considered, but exact vehicle-placement service area and priority rules are not published. The thrift store/ministry is located in Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-649-1288 or visit 1135 E. Main St., Mesa, AZ 85203 to ask whether vehicle placement is active, what documentation is needed and whether there is a waitlist or referral process.

**Important Information to Know**
Vehicle availability is donation-dependent and not guaranteed. The page does not publish application steps, insurance or registration help, vehicle condition standards, wait time or frequency of placements, so missionaries should confirm directly before relying on this option.

resources.name: Ebony House Behavioral Health Outpatient Services · Adult, youth and maternal recovery outpatient care
resources.description: Ebony House Behavioral Health Outpatient Services provides outpatient substance-use and behavioral-health services for adults, youth, families, pregnant/postpartum women and youth, including counseling, substance recovery support and referrals in Phoenix/Maricopa County.
resources.address: 1616 E Indian School Road, Suite 100, Phoenix, AZ 85016
resources.hours: Call for current intake and program hours; site-specific schedules were not fully listed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Outpatient adult services for mild to moderate impairment, youth behavioral-health outpatient services, maternal recovery programming with behavioral-health and substance-use recovery services, counseling, substance-treatment support, family support, and referrals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility and payer/funding depend on program. The official page states Ebony House is supported in part by AHCCCS Complete Care health plans, Arizona Department of Child Safety and other public sources, but clients should confirm current funding and enrollment rules.

**Population Served**
Adults, children, young adults, pregnant and postpartum women and youth, and families affected by substance abuse, behavioral challenges, HIV/AIDS, child abuse or family-preservation needs. Ebony House states it serves people from all races and ethnic backgrounds.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-249-7495 for the Indian School outpatient office or 602-276-4288 for the main organization contact. Ask about adult outpatient substance-use treatment, youth behavioral health, maternal recovery, AHCCCS/funding, and current appointment availability.

**Important Information to Know**
Current official pages clearly support outpatient and maternal recovery services; residential or inpatient claims from directories should be confirmed before referral. This is a Phoenix location, so Mesa clients need transportation or remote options if available.

resources.name: Gila River Indian Community - Gila River Transit
resources.description: Gila River Transit is a no-fare deviated fixed-route service serving the Gila River Indian Community, with route deviations available by advance request and connections to Valley Metro through the West End Shuttle.
resources.address: 291 W Casa Blanca Rd, Sacaton, AZ 85147
resources.hours: Route schedules vary; call ahead for route-deviation requests.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Gila River Transit operates no-fare deviated fixed-route bus service. Riders can request a special stop or route deviation up to three-quarters of a mile from a route, and buses include accessibility accommodations and bike racks.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open to riders using the Gila River Transit route system. Route deviations require advance request by phone, at least two hours and up to one day ahead according to the FAQ.

**Population Served**
Gila River Indian Community riders and others using the Gila River Transit route system, including riders with disabilities needing route deviation.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 520-562-6020 for route information or to request a special stop/deviation. Check current routes and schedules on the Gila River Transit website before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not Mesa local service. It may be relevant for tribal or rural Maricopa/Pinal edge trips and connections, but the trip must fit the Gila River route network.

resources.name: Ability360 - Benefits 2 Work Arizona (WIPA Work-Incentives Counseling)
resources.description: Ability360 Benefits 2 Work Arizona provides Social Security work-incentives and disability-benefits counseling for people receiving SSDI or SSI who want to work or increase earnings.
resources.address: 5025 E. Washington St., Suite 200, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: Ability360 main office is listed Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; call/email for B2W intake.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Benefits 2 Work Arizona helps disability-benefit recipients understand Social Security work incentives, SSI, SSDI, Medicare, Medicaid/AHCCCS interactions and how work may affect cash and health benefits.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The service is for people who receive SSDI and/or SSI and are considering work or already working. Ability360 also notes work incentives for students under age 22. Full WIPA service may require referral through the Ticket to Work Help Line.

**Population Served**
People with disabilities who receive Social Security disability benefits, including transition-age students and adults planning employment.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact Ability360 B2W at 602-443-0720, 866-304-WORK (9675), or B2W@ability360.org. To generate a WIPA referral, call the Ticket to Work Help Line at 866-968-7842 or use ChooseWork.SSA.gov.

**Important Information to Know**
This is benefits planning, not emergency cash, benefit approval or guaranteed employment. Discuss proposed work or increased hours before assuming how SSI/SSDI, Medicare or AHCCCS will change. Bring current benefit letters and work information if available; counseling does not guarantee unchanged benefits.

resources.name: First Way Pregnancy Center - Material Support
resources.description: First Way Pregnancy Center provides free material goods for mothers and fathers through Baby Bucks earned by completing classes, including diapers, formula, infant clothing, maternity clothing, strollers, and pack-n-plays.
resources.address: 3501 N 16th Street, Phoenix, AZ 85016
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Class-linked Baby Bucks can be exchanged for available baby/maternity goods such as diapers, wipes, formula, layettes, basic care kits, bottles/pacifiers/bibs, blankets, infant/maternity clothing, tubs, strollers and pack-and-plays. The page also describes newborn/gift items; selection depends on stock.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Parents earn Baby Bucks by completing pregnancy or parenting classes. Maternity clothing is listed as available three times during pregnancy. Call to confirm class enrollment, pickup rules, and whether Mesa residents may participate.

**Population Served**
Pregnant and parenting mothers and fathers who can participate in the Phoenix center's education and support program.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-261-7522 or email info@1stway.net. The center is at 3501 N 16th Street, Phoenix.

**Important Information to Know**
Material support is not described as a walk-in giveaway; it is connected to class participation and Baby Bucks. Inventory and large baby items depend on current supply.

resources.name: Freedom Sober Living / Caballero House — identity resolution
resources.description: A historical Arizona licensing lead described Caballero House as sober living in Mesa.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A historical Arizona licensing lead described Caballero House as sober living in Mesa.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Current operator, licensing status, household rules, costs and admissions contact need administrator confirmation.

**Population Served**
Potentially adults seeking recovery housing in Mesa; the current programme identity is unresolved.

**How to Best Connect**
An administrator should reconcile the historical ADHS entry and 928-255-8700 contact with a current operator and licence before referral.

**Important Information to Know**
The old licensing sheet shows a March 2025 expiry. That does not prove closure. The similarly named FreedomSoberLiving.com provider uses a different phone; the match has not been established.
resources.resolutionReason: Current operator, licence and practical intake route have not been reconciled with the historical Mesa entry.

resources.name: Paz de Cristo Community Center - The Well / Mental Health First Aid Connection Program
resources.description: Paz de Cristo's The Well partnership is a nonclinical mental-health first-aid connection effort where trained volunteers listen, accompany, and link Paz clients to vetted resources.
resources.address: 424 W Broadway Rd, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Paz de Cristo access times vary by service; call 480-464-2370 before relying on The Well availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Nonclinical listening, accompaniment, Mental Health First Aid-informed support, and connection to vetted local mental-health resources for Paz de Cristo neighbors.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public article describes support for Paz de Cristo clients and neighbors experiencing homelessness or food insecurity. It does not describe open therapy enrollment or diagnostic services.

**Population Served**
Mesa neighbors using Paz de Cristo basic-needs services, especially people experiencing homelessness or food insecurity.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Paz de Cristo at 480-464-2370 or visit the Mesa center and ask whether The Well volunteers are currently available.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not therapy, diagnosis, crisis intervention, or medication care. The public article announced the effort for summer 2026, so current schedule and on-site availability should be confirmed before referral.

resources.name: Maricopa County Department of Public Health - Office of Vital Registration East Valley office
resources.description: Maricopa County Public Health Office of Vital Registration issues certified Arizona birth and death certificates and handles eligible record corrections or amendments, with an East Valley office in Mesa.
resources.address: 331 E Coury Ave, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM; Wednesday 9:00 AM-4:30 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Issues official certified copies of Arizona birth and death certificates and processes eligible corrections or amendments. A certified birth certificate can be a foundational document for an Arizona ID, Social Security card, passport or benefits application.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Arizona vital records are restricted. The requester must be legally eligible for the record requested and must provide the application, fee and required identification or an allowed notarized-signature route.

**Population Served**
Eligible requesters for Arizona birth and death records, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents. This office does not retrieve out-of-state records.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit the East Valley office at 331 E Coury Ave in Mesa, call 602-506-6805, or use the county's mail or online ordering routes. Bring eligibility evidence, identification or notarized forms as required for the specific request.

**Important Information to Know**
The official page listed $20 per certified copy and $30 for corrections and major changes. Applicants without photo ID may need the notarized-signature route or help from an ID navigator. A completed application does not guarantee eligibility for a restricted record.

resources.name: Maggie’s Place · Maternity Homes and Resident Support
resources.description: Provides screened maternity housing for homeless pregnant adults, including Hannah House in Mesa when space and fit allow, with infant and resident-family supports.
resources.address: Confidential residential homes; arranged interviews/support at Family Success Center, 4001 N. 30th St., Phoenix, AZ 85016
resources.hours: Family Success Center generally lists 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; Wednesday is listed closed in one section, so call to confirm. Housing intake and residential access are separate.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Maternity housing and supportive community include infant needs, food, trauma-informed/resiliency programming, case management, parenting/family learning and care connections during pregnancy and the baby’s first year. Residents or alumni may access separately screened Family Success Center programmes and donation-closet goods; confirm the applicable participation rules and inventory.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Maternity-home applicants must be homeless and pregnant, age 18 or older, willing to live in community, free from immediate physical danger and without other children in their immediate care. Intake requests proof of pregnancy. Admission depends on screening, programme fit and capacity; ask how medical, medication or recovery needs affect suitability.

**Population Served**
Homeless pregnant women and pregnant/parenting women served by Maggie's Place in the Phoenix/Valley area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call maternity intake at 602-246-3724 and leave a message if unanswered. An appropriate referral may proceed to an interview at the Family Success Center. For ongoing family/center or donation-closet questions, call 602-262-5555 or email email@maggiesplace.org.

**Important Information to Know**
Residential addresses are confidential. The Phoenix Family Success Center is an arranged interview/support location, not the Mesa home. Admission is not immediate or guaranteed and may take days to weeks. For urgent housing, use 211 or an appropriate safety route. Continuing family, reunification and recovery services have separate criteria; a center visit or goods request does not secure a housing place.

resources.name: Encircle Families - Family Support and Parent-to-Parent Disability Navigation
resources.description: Encircle Families, formerly Raising Special Kids, provides no-cost parent-to-parent support, training, coaching and systems navigation for Arizona families raising children with disabilities or special health care needs.
resources.address: 5025 E. Washington St., Suite 204, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: Call, email or use the Refer a Family form; public walk-in hours were not established.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost family and parent-to-parent support, trained parent mentors, parent leadership, practical care-system/resource navigation, IEP support, positive family coaching, transition navigation and training. Specific supports include NICU, military-family and refugee/asylee mentorship programmes; Spanish-language events/trainings vary by schedule.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are for parents, caregivers and family members of children with disabilities or special health care needs. Specific trainings or programs may require registration or a referral form.

**Population Served**
Arizona parents, caregivers and families of children and youth with disabilities or special health care needs, including Mesa families, Spanish-speaking families, military families, refugee/asylee families and families navigating transition-age needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-242-4366 or 800-237-3007, email info@encirclefamilies.org, or use the official Refer a Family form.

**Important Information to Know**
Older directories may still use the Raising Special Kids name. This is peer support, training, coaching and systems navigation; it is not emergency medical care, therapy authorization or a school-district decision-maker.

resources.name: HireQuest Direct - Phoenix East / Mesa On-Demand Staffing
resources.description: HireQuest Direct Phoenix is a Mesa-based on-demand staffing office serving Mesa, the Phoenix East Valley and Greater Phoenix with temporary assignments, on-demand labor, temp-to-hire positions and direct-hire recruiting.
resources.address: 1130 W. University Dr., Suite 108, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Call or email for current office hours and same-day assignment process; job openings change frequently.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
On-demand staffing and job placement for temporary assignments, temp-to-hire positions and direct-hire recruiting. Listed industries include construction, warehousing, logistics, manufacturing, hospitality, janitorial services, live events, traffic control and general labor. Current opening examples included welding, demolition labor, general labor and baggage handling.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Job requirements depend on the assignment. HireQuest states candidates are screened for reliability, safety, attendance and job readiness. Applicants should ask about ID/work authorization, background/drug screening, PPE, transportation and pay timing.

**Population Served**
Mesa, East Valley and Greater Phoenix job seekers seeking temporary, day-labor, temp-to-hire or labor staffing assignments.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-207-1828, email Mesa@HQDirect.com, use the Find a Job route, or visit 1130 W. University Dr., Suite 108, Mesa after confirming hours.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a private staffing agency, not a public workforce program. Jobs and rates change quickly; the listed openings are examples from the page and should be confirmed before relying on them.

resources.name: Health insurance appeals and consumer complaint process
resources.description: Arizona DIFI consumer pathway for state-regulated insurance complaints, denied health insurance claims/services, expedited and external review, surprise billing, and regulated financial-institution complaints.
resources.address: 100 North 15th Avenue, Suite 261, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
DIFI provides consumer complaint and health-care appeal information for state-regulated insurance matters, including denied health insurance claims, denied requests for services, expedited review, external independent review, surprise billing, and insurance or financial-institution complaints.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The issue must fall within DIFI jurisdiction. DIFI states that some problems require using the insurer's appeal process first and that it does not handle AHCCCS/Medicaid, Medicare, self-funded employer plans, COBRA, TriCare, federal/state employee benefit plans, or matters requiring a court decision.

**Population Served**
Arizona consumers with state-regulated insurance or regulated financial-institution complaints.

**How to Best Connect**
Use DIFI's online complaint or health-care appeals portal. Consumer Protection Division phone is 602-364-3100.

**Important Information to Know**
DIFI cannot act as a lawyer, give legal advice, decide liability, or extend legal or policy deadlines. Complaint records may become public records under Arizona law.

resources.name: Azura / Mesa United Way - Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA)
resources.description: Azura / Mesa United Way VITA provides free tax preparation for low- and moderate-income taxpayers, helping eligible households file returns and claim credits such as the Earned Income Tax Credit.
resources.address: 137 E University Dr, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Published summer 2026 schedule, June 2–September 29: Tuesday 1–5 p.m. and Thursday 9 a.m.–1 p.m.; walk-in, no appointment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The VITA program provides free tax preparation and filing help for qualifying taxpayers. It can help households file accurately and claim refunds or credits such as the Earned Income Tax Credit.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The published Mesa summer 2026 program lists household income below $89,000. Tax-return complexity and site rules also apply; ask the program to confirm that it can prepare the return.

**Population Served**
Low- and moderate-income taxpayers in Mesa and the East Valley who need free tax preparation.

**How to Best Connect**
During the published summer schedule, visit 137 E University Drive on Tuesday afternoons or Thursday mornings. Call 480-834-2122 or email VITA@AzuraCares.org to check current availability and the documents to bring.

**Important Information to Know**
The published summer schedule ends September 29, 2026. Check later site/season schedules and income limits; the $89,000 summer limit is not a universal VITA threshold. This is tax preparation and refund/credit access, not emergency bill payment or tax-dispute representation; a Low Income Taxpayer Clinic may fit an IRS dispute.

resources.name: Dignity Foundation - Dignity Threads
resources.description: Dignity Threads is a Dignity Foundation referral-partner program where referred individuals can choose clothing, shoes and accessories suited to entering or returning to the workforce.
resources.address: 6501 E Greenway Pkwy, Suite 103-502, Scottsdale, AZ 85254
resources.hours: Referral-only; call or use the referral-partner process for current appointment timing.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A shopping experience for referred individuals to choose clothing, shoes and accessories tailored to professional needs as they enter the workforce.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Access is through trusted community organizations or referral partners. The person should need workforce clothing and be referred for Dignity Foundation services.

**Population Served**
Referred individuals preparing for employment or workforce entry who need professional clothing, shoes and accessories.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the client's caseworker or nonprofit agency whether they are a Dignity Foundation referral partner. Existing partners can submit a referral. For questions, call 602-848-2422 or email ktrapp@dignityfoundation.org.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a walk-in work-clothing closet. Confirm Mesa referral partners, appointment location, sizing, transportation assistance and which employment stages qualify.

resources.name: Staff Sergeant Alexander W. Conrad VA Health Care Clinic
resources.description: Staff Sergeant Alexander W. Conrad VA Health Care Clinic is a Gilbert/East Valley VA outpatient clinic offering primary care, mental-health care, dentistry/oral surgery for eligible Veterans, laboratory services, women’s health, rehabilitation, telehealth, and specialty services.
resources.address: 3285 South Val Vista Drive, Gilbert, AZ 85297-7000
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 6:00 AM-5:30 PM; closed Saturday-Sunday. Some services have different hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Primary care and specialty services, including mental-health therapy and psychiatry, medications when indicated, dentistry and oral surgery, laboratory services, women’s health, audiology/speech services, physical medicine and rehabilitation, nutrition, imaging and telehealth. Service-specific referral and appointment rules apply.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are for Veterans eligible for VA health care. Some services require referral or an order; dental care depends on VA dental eligibility. The location page notes that appointment and referral requirements vary by service.

**Population Served**
Veterans in Gilbert, Mesa, the East Valley, and the Phoenix VA Health Care System service area.

**How to Best Connect**
Use VA Health Connect at 888-214-7264 for scheduling or routing. Visit 3285 South Val Vista Drive, Gilbert, AZ 85297-7000. Facility hours are Monday-Friday 6:00 AM-5:30 PM; service hours may differ.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a useful East Valley option for Mesa clients, especially when a service is not available at the Mesa clinic. Dental/oral surgery is not open to every Veteran; confirm VA dental eligibility and referral requirements before sending a client for dental care.

resources.name: American Cancer Society - Road To Recovery
resources.description: American Cancer Society Road To Recovery provides free rides to cancer-related medical appointments where trained volunteer drivers and local availability permit.
resources.hours: Call well in advance; ACS says rides can take several business days to coordinate. Helpline phone is available 24/7.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Road To Recovery gives free rides to cancer-related medical appointments when volunteer drivers are available in the client's area.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Patients must be traveling to a cancer-related medical appointment. Other requirements may apply, such as needing a caregiver to accompany a patient who cannot walk without help or who is under age 18.

**Population Served**
People with cancer who need transportation to cancer-related medical appointments, including Arizona clients if the program is available near them.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the American Cancer Society at 1-800-227-2345 to ask about Road To Recovery availability near the client and to schedule. Call several business days before the appointment.

**Important Information to Know**
Availability depends on local volunteer drivers and scheduling time. This should not be treated as guaranteed urgent transportation for same-day or frequent treatment trips.

resources.name: City of Scottsdale - Scottsdale Trolley
resources.description: Scottsdale Trolley is a fare-free fixed-route trolley network with three routes and connections to Valley Metro Transit and Tempe Orbit.
resources.address: Scottsdale, AZ fixed trolley routes
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 5:45 AM-7:45 PM; no service on New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Fourth of July, Labor Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas. Check route times and detours before travel.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Three free fixed trolley routes connect Scottsdale destinations with regional transit. They serve shopping areas, schools, parks, libraries and community centers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open public fixed-route trolley service. Riders must use a current trolley route and schedule.

**Population Served**
Scottsdale residents, workers and visitors traveling along the trolley routes.

**How to Best Connect**
Check the City of Scottsdale route maps, detours and schedules or call Scottsdale Trolley at 480-312-3787. Posted weekday service spans 5:45 AM–7:45 PM, with no service on the listed holidays. Check the specific stop and route before traveling.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not door-to-door transportation. Trolleys run on fixed routes, and current detours can affect stops and travel times.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Health Services - Power Me A2Z Folic Acid Education and Distribution Program
resources.description: ADHS Power Me A2Z provides free multivitamins with folic acid through an online quiz and order form for Arizonans ages 18-45 who can get pregnant, with vitamins mailed to Arizona addresses.
resources.address: Statewide Arizona mailing program
resources.hours: Online order form available; ADHS general public hours are Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM, closed weekends and state holidays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Power Me A2Z provides health education and free multivitamins with folic acid. Folic acid is emphasized for people who can get pregnant because it helps prevent serious birth defects when present before pregnancy.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The order form states the vitamins are for Arizonans ages 18-45 who can get pregnant, and vitamins can only be delivered to Arizona mailing addresses.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents ages 18-45 who can get pregnant, including people planning pregnancy, people not planning pregnancy, and people in early pregnancy who need folic acid education and vitamins.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Power Me A2Z online free vitamins quiz/order form. A public program phone was not clearly listed; ADHS general public information is 602-542-1025 for general department questions.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a prevention and vitamin-mailing program, not prenatal medical care. A person who is pregnant or may be pregnant should still connect with prenatal care and follow medical advice about vitamins and medication safety.

resources.name: Copa Health - Copa Connect Autism Travel Respite Care
resources.description: Copa Connect autism travel respite and activity support in Mesa, with trained respite caregivers, one-on-one or group settings, individualized visit plans, therapeutic recreation activities, outings, and service-animal accommodation.
resources.address: Listed office: 924 N. Country Club Dr., Mesa, AZ 85201; arrange the actual visit/respite location with staff.
resources.hours: Call to arrange an Individualized Visit Plan.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Autism travel respite and activity support, including trained caregivers, one-on-one or group settings, activity support, planned therapeutic recreation, social and recreational activities, outings with or without the child, service-animal accommodation, and individualized visit plans.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page describes the service as autism respite supports connected to Mesa's Autism Friendly City initiative. It does not publish age, diagnosis, payer, or fee rules; those must be confirmed before scheduling.

**Population Served**
Families and caregivers of autistic children or family members needing respite and activity support in the Mesa context.

**How to Best Connect**
For information or to schedule an Individualized Visit Plan, call 480-969-3800 ext. 202 and ask for Jessica.

**Important Information to Know**
This is specialized travel, outing, recreation and self-care respite. The page welcomes service animals and describes IBCCES-certified staff. Confirm age, cost, funding authorization, service area, availability and actual visit location; free low-income access is not established.

resources.name: Mesa Public Schools Community Education · Mesa Adult Education and Family Literacy
resources.description: Mesa Public Schools Community Education Adult Education offers GED/HSE preparation, ESL/English classes, integrated education and training, family literacy, GED testing information, registration timelines, and adult education support for Mesa learners.
resources.address: 155 N. Center St., Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Community Education office: Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM; Friday 8:00 AM-4:15 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
GED/high-school-equivalency preparation and testing information, English-language learning, English Language Civics/citizenship-test preparation, Integrated Education and Training, family literacy and transition support toward college and careers. The programme is an ARIZONA@WORK partner.

**Eligibility Requirements**
U.S. citizens, permanent residents, and people lawfully present in the United States are eligible to attend classes. People who are not citizens, permanent residents, or lawfully present are directed to call 480-472-7259 for other options. Registration, placement testing, orientation, term timing, and possible fees vary by class.

**Population Served**
Mesa adult learners seeking GED/HSE preparation, English learning, family literacy, integrated education and training, or pathways toward college and career readiness.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-472-7259, email Adult_Ed@mpsaz.org or use the official registration link. The office is 155 N. Center St., Mesa. Check the current term’s registration, paperwork, testing and orientation deadlines; classes do not offer continuous immediate enrollment.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm actual class location, format, schedule, fees and required documentation. Citizenship preparation is education, not immigration legal representation. People outside the page’s stated status categories are directed to call about other options.

resources.name: The Network/La Red - 24-Hour LGBTQ+ Partner-Abuse Hotline
resources.description: The Network/La Red operates a free 24-hour hotline for LGBTQ+, kink and polyamorous communities experiencing partner abuse, with emotional support, information, referrals, safety planning and crisis intervention available by toll-free phone.
resources.address: PO Box 6011, Boston, MA 02114
resources.hours: 24-hour hotline.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Network/La Red's 24-hour hotline provides confidential emotional support, information, referrals, safety planning and crisis intervention for LGBTQ+ people and people in kink or polyamorous communities who are being abused or have been abused by a partner. It also supports friends, family and coworkers with questions about domestic violence in LGBTQ+ communities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For LGBTQ+ people, and people in kink or polyamorous communities, affected by partner abuse. Hotline support is free. Housing and in-person services are centered outside Arizona and should not be treated as Mesa shelter placement.

**Population Served**
LGBTQ+, transgender, queer, kink and polyamorous survivors nationwide who can use the toll-free hotline, including Mesa callers needing identity-specific support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 800-832-1901 toll-free. The Boston local voice hotline number is 617-742-4911. If asking for a callback, state whether it is safe to leave a message and whether blocked numbers can be received.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a remote hotline, not a local Arizona shelter. Use it alongside Arizona shelter, protective-order and emergency resources when a client needs local placement or court help.

resources.name: Hospice of the Valley - Supportive Care for Dementia / Dementia Care and Education Campus
resources.description: Hospice of the Valley provides no-cost Supportive Care for Dementia, in-home dementia education, 24/7 phone support, GUIDE-model support for eligible Medicare beneficiaries, low-cost RISE respite and Dementia Care and Education Campus resources for people with dementia and caregivers.
resources.address: 3811 N. 44th St., Phoenix, AZ
resources.hours: Supportive Care for Dementia phone support is described as 24/7. Call before visiting the Dementia Care and Education Campus.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Supportive Care for Dementia offers no-cost support for families caring for someone with Alzheimer's disease or another dementia, including home visits from dementia educators, behavior-management coaching, help with medications and placement options, 24/7 phone access to a nurse or social worker, physician consultation, GUIDE-model dementia support for eligible Medicare beneficiaries, low-cost RISE respite, classes, support groups and memory cafe resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Supportive Care for Dementia helps families at different stages of dementia, before hospice is needed. GUIDE has additional Medicare and clinical requirements: Original Medicare must be primary, and Medicare Advantage or PACE does not qualify. Hospice, long-term nursing-home or Memory Care Unit residence and enrollment with another GUIDE provider also affect eligibility. Ask the dementia team which support or respite pathway fits.

**Population Served**
People living with Alzheimer's disease or other dementias and their caregivers in Maricopa County, northern Pinal County and the Tucson area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the dementia team at 602-636-6363 for Supportive Care for Dementia and GUIDE questions. The Dementia Care and Education Campus main line is 602-767-8300. Hospice of the Valley also lists 602-530-6900 as available anytime.

**Important Information to Know**
Supportive Care for Dementia is distinct from hospice and may serve people long before hospice is appropriate. GUIDE and RISE respite have separate eligibility and availability limits, so families should ask which pathway fits the client's insurance, stage of dementia and location.

resources.name: Arizona Family Institute
resources.description: Counseling for adults, couples and families, including trauma, anxiety and relationship concerns.
resources.address: 2500 S Power Rd, Suite 120, Mesa, AZ 85209
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Counseling for adults, couples and families, including trauma, anxiety and relationship concerns.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Appointment and clinician fit are determined at intake.

**Population Served**
Mesa-area adults, couples and families.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-382-1257 or use the provider’s appointment request.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm fees, insurance and availability; this counseling practice is not a crisis service or a prescribing clinic.

resources.name: City of Mesa / Valley Metro - East Valley Paratransit and RideChoice
