Activities may include cultural workshops, storytelling, language revitalization, community events and mentorship. The Language & Culture team also hosts elder convenings or gatherings when scheduled.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Young Elder Program is for people age 55 and older who participate in an interview, pass a criminal background check and commit to a minimum of 10 hours per month. Elder gathering details should be confirmed before attending.

**Population Served**
Indigenous elders age 55 and older in the Phoenix metropolitan area and local Indigenous youth connected through mentoring or cultural programming.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Phoenix Indian Center at 602-264-6768 or email languageculture@phxindcenter.org. The center is at 4041 N. Central Ave., Building B, Phoenix. Use the official application or event registration links when open.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a cultural, social-connection and intergenerational mentorship pathway, not benefits case management or emergency assistance. The official page states the program is available without regard to race, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity and other protected statuses, but the cultural focus is Indigenous elder programming.

resources.name: ADWAS / National Domestic Violence Hotline - The Deaf Hotline
resources.description: The Deaf Hotline is a free, confidential, 24/7 ASL-accessible hotline for Deaf survivors experiencing abuse, offering safety planning, crisis intervention, emotional support, education, advocacy and referrals.
resources.hours: 24/7 ASL hotline.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Deaf Hotline provides ASL-accessible hotline support for people experiencing abuse, including safety planning, crisis intervention, emotional support, relationship education, advocacy and referrals to Deaf-accessible programs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Deaf survivors experiencing abuse or people seeking Deaf-accessible abuse support. It is a national remote service and not a local shelter.

**Population Served**
Deaf survivors of relationship abuse, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents who need culturally and linguistically accessible support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 855-812-1001. The hotline is listed as free, confidential and available 24/7 with ASL access. The website also provides contact and program-finder options.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a Mesa in-person provider. Use it when local services are not accessible in ASL or when a Deaf survivor wants confidential, culturally specific support; local shelter placement still needs a shelter or DV hotline call.

resources.name: Universal Service Administrative Company - Lifeline Survivor Benefit Under the Safe Connections Act
resources.description: Emergency Lifeline support for qualifying survivors of domestic violence, human trafficking, and related crimes after a mobile line-separation request.
resources.address: Mail only: Lifeline Support Center, PO Box 1000, Horseheads, NY 14845
resources.hours: Support Center: 7 days a week, 9:00 AM-9:00 PM Eastern Time.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Lifeline Survivor Benefit under the Safe Connections Act offers emergency Lifeline support for up to six months and up to a $9.25 monthly discount for phone, internet, or bundled services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Provide proof of a line-separation request showing the survivor’s name, provider and request date within the past 12 months. Qualify through income at or below 200% of federal poverty guidelines, existing Lifeline eligibility or an accepted benefit; the broader survivor list includes WIC, school meals and Pell Grants. The benefit lasts up to six months.

**Population Served**
Survivors of domestic violence, human trafficking, and related crimes nationwide, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through LifelineSupport.org or mail a paper application and documentation to Lifeline Support Center, PO Box 1000, Horseheads, NY 14845. For help, call 800-234-9473 or email LifelineSupport@usac.org.

**Important Information to Know**
The survivor benefit is temporary, lasting up to six months. After that, the survivor must qualify for standard Lifeline to continue a Lifeline discount. If proof of line-separation request is not available yet, the person can apply for standard Lifeline and reapply as a survivor later.

resources.name: A New Leaf - La Mesita Apartments
resources.description: La Mesita Apartments is A New Leaf's long-term affordable apartment community in Mesa, with studio through four-bedroom units, resident support services and some units connected to the City of Mesa Project-Based Voucher pathway.
resources.address: 2254 W Main St, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Call or email property management for leasing/availability. PBV units are referral-only through the Mesa Project-Based Voucher access route.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Long-term affordable rental housing with studio through four-bedroom apartments, onsite support services, financial wellness and parenting classes, workforce services, onsite computer lab, Head Start/child services and some City of Mesa Project-Based Voucher units for households transitioning from homelessness.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Some affordable units serve households at or below 60% of area median income and some at or below 30% of area median income. Project-Based Voucher units require referral through Mesa's PBV process for eligible households transitioning from homelessness.

**Population Served**
Low-income individuals and families in Mesa, including some households transitioning from homelessness who need supportive services.

**How to Best Connect**
For ordinary affordable-unit inquiries, call 480-969-5233, email lamesita@kay-kay.biz or use the official available-units link to Kay-Kay Realty. For PBV units, use Mesa’s separate referral process: adults without minor children through the appropriate homeless access point, families with minor children through Family Housing Hub. Confirm vacancies and the correct route.

**Important Information to Know**
Do not present La Mesita Apartments as a current walk-in emergency family shelter. Current A New Leaf public material describes La Mesita Apartments as long-term affordable housing. Availability, leasing criteria and PBV openings must be confirmed before referral.

resources.name: SAAVI Services for the Blind — adult training, education and employment
resources.description: SAAVI Services for the Blind offers comprehensive blindness training and job-readiness services, including Braille, orientation and mobility, access technology, independent living, remedial education, ESL as needed, advocacy, counseling, and workforce preparation.
resources.address: 2920 N. 7th St., Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.hours: Schedules vary by programme. Comprehensive training can be about 40 hours weekly for an average of nine months; confirm the proposed service plan.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Comprehensive nonvisual-skills training in Braille, orientation/mobility, accessible technology, independent living and job readiness, with advocacy/counseling and possible residential support. Education/employment services can support resumes, volunteer experience, tutoring/remedial education, goal-related ESL, GED, vocational certification and postsecondary pathways.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The adult training program is for blind individuals, including people new to blindness, people with prior training who want new skills, and people experiencing vision loss for the first time. Referral, rehabilitation, residential, and funding requirements should be confirmed with SAAVI and any Vocational Rehabilitation connection.

**Population Served**
Blind and low-vision adults in Arizona who need nonvisual-skills training, education support, job readiness, or help returning to work or postsecondary education.

**How to Best Connect**
For Phoenix adult services, contact the Phoenix Center Director through SAAVI or call the Phoenix location at 602-795-0195. Ask about adult comprehensive training, job readiness, VR/RSA linkage, virtual options, residential availability, and fees.

**Important Information to Know**
Comprehensive training can be intensive, averaging nine months full-time; other education/employment services may differ. Confirm fees, VR authorization, referrals, transport, residential eligibility, remote access and capacity. This is distinct from SAAVI’s introductory Ability Builds Confidence classes.

resources.name: Mesa / Maricopa Community Colleges — financial aid and FAFSA help
resources.description: Maricopa Community Colleges Financial Aid helps current and prospective students with FAFSA, grants, work-study, scholarships, financial aid forms, school codes, and one-on-one FAFSA consultation, including Mesa Community College students.
resources.phone: Financial aid 480-731-8900; MCC Southern & Dobson 480-461-7000; Red Mountain 480-654-7200
resources.address: MCC Southern & Dobson: 1833 W. Southern Ave., Mesa; Red Mountain: 7110 E. McKellips Rd., Mesa; phone/virtual help also available.
resources.hours: Financial aid phone assistance: Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-6:00 PM and Friday 10:00 AM-5:00 PM, modified during specific times of year.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
FAFSA and financial-aid help, scholarships, grants, loans, work-study, academic-progress and course-eligibility questions, payment options and student-form/to-do guidance. District resources offer 30-minute individual FAFSA consultations; MCC provides campus, phone and virtual service options and links to programmes such as Maricopa Promise.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on the aid type, student status, program, FAFSA information, enrollment level, satisfactory academic progress, citizenship or eligible noncitizen rules for federal aid, scholarship rules, and whether courses apply to the student's program of study.

**Population Served**
Students and prospective students at Maricopa Community Colleges, including Mesa Community College students who need help paying for college or completing financial aid steps.

**How to Best Connect**
Call district financial aid at 480-731-8900 or book the FAFSA consultation linked on the district Financial Aid page. For MCC campus/virtual service options, use https://www.mesacc.edu/financial-aid or campus numbers: Southern & Dobson 480-461-7000; Red Mountain 480-654-7200.

**Important Information to Know**
Awards and rules vary by aid type, status, course/programme and year, including 2026–27 changes. Confirm eligibility for the particular certificate, noncredit/workforce course or immigration/documentation situation. Aid does not automatically transfer between schools; monitor Student Center tasks, college email and deadlines.

resources.name: Awakening Recovery Center - Intensive Outpatient Addiction Treatment and Family Support
resources.description: Awakening Recovery Center provides intensive outpatient addiction treatment, continued aftercare, individual counseling, family therapy/education, consultation/referrals, and telehealth services for Arizona clients near Mesa.
resources.address: Tempe: 1204 E Baseline Rd, Suite 208, Tempe, AZ 85283; Apache Junction: 350 W Superstition Blvd, Suite 119, Apache Junction, AZ 85120
resources.hours: Call location-specific numbers for schedules and intake appointments.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Intensive outpatient addiction treatment, continued aftercare for up to one year, individual counseling, family program/education, consultation and referrals, telehealth services, and practical recovery supports such as connection to 12-step fellowship, work, education, relationships, and sobriety planning.

**Eligibility Requirements**
People seeking help with addiction or alcoholism may call. Clinical fit, payer contracts, telehealth availability, and whether a higher level of care is needed should be confirmed during intake.

**Population Served**
East Valley and Arizona clients, including Mesa residents who can access Tempe, Apache Junction, or telehealth services; families affected by addiction.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Tempe at 480-209-1977, Apache Junction at 480-474-8797, or use the website contact route. Ask which location or telehealth option is appropriate for Mesa clients.

**Important Information to Know**
This is IOP/outpatient and aftercare support, not detox or residential treatment. Directory claims about AHCCCS should be verified directly with Awakening before relying on them.

resources.name: Immigration Advocates Network — nonprofit legal-services directory
resources.description: Finds additional free or low-cost nonprofit immigration legal providers by place or detention facility.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Finds additional free or low-cost nonprofit immigration legal providers by place or detention facility.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The directory is public; provider eligibility, fees and capacity vary.

**Population Served**
People needing another immigration legal-service option.

**How to Best Connect**
Search Arizona, the relevant county or detention facility, then contact the listed organization.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm current intake and credentials before relying on a listing; the directory itself does not represent clients.

resources.name: VA Phoenix Health Care System — care and programme navigation
resources.description: Helps eligible veterans connect with Phoenix VA care and its distinct clinical, caregiver and homelessness programmes.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Navigation to Phoenix VA primary and specialty care, mental-health and substance-use treatment, rehabilitation, pharmacy, caregiver support and homelessness assistance. Carl T. Hayden VA Medical Center provides hospital, emergency and specialty services at 650 E. Indian School Road, Phoenix, including dental and oral surgery for veterans meeting the narrower dental eligibility rules. Individual clinics and programmes have separate locations, intake routes and schedules.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Most clinical care requires VA health-care eligibility, enrollment, clinical need and appointments or referrals. Dental, caregiver and housing programmes have separate criteria. Emergency and same-day mental-health access have different rules; veteran status alone does not guarantee every benefit.

**Population Served**
Eligible veterans in central Arizona, including Mesa, and families or caregivers where the particular programme permits.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Phoenix VA main line at 602-277-5551 or toll-free 888-214-7264 and ask for the relevant clinic, service or coordinator. Mesa VA Clinic offers its listed local outpatient services; the Carl T. Hayden hospital is at 650 E. Indian School Road in Phoenix. Confirm the actual location and appointment route before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
The main hospital is open 24 hours, but that schedule does not apply to every clinic or department. The Community Resource and Referral Center, caregiver programme and specialty clinics remain distinct contacts. Navigation does not reserve shelter, housing or a clinical appointment. For veteran crisis support call 988 then press 1 or text 838255; use 911 for a medical emergency.

resources.name: St. Joseph the Worker - MOM's House / Workforce Villages Reentry Program
resources.description: MOM’s House offers short-term landing housing and job-readiness help for women leaving Perryville, with partner referral and possible transition to St. Joseph the Worker’s employment-linked Workforce Villages programme.
resources.address: Mesa employment office: 1833 W. Main St., Suite 128, Mesa, AZ 85201; housing location must be arranged separately.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Short-term MOM’s House reentry housing and job-readiness support for women leaving Perryville. The provider describes a connection to Televerde Foundation PATHS pre-release coaching and possible progression to the 90-day Workforce Villages programme, with full-time employment support, life skills, financial literacy and saving for independent housing.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The current official article describes women returning home from Perryville Prison and participants who enroll in Televerde Foundation's PATHS program six months before release. Current referral source requirements, openings, offense-history restrictions and work-readiness rules must be confirmed with St. Joseph the Worker.

**Population Served**
Justice-impacted women returning from incarceration in Arizona, especially women leaving Perryville Prison who need employment-linked housing and workforce support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-755-JOBS (5627) and ask about MOM's House / Workforce Villages reentry. St. Joseph the Worker also has a Mesa employment office at 1833 W. Main Street #128, Mesa, but the housing site may be separate.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a specialized partner-linked reentry pathway, distinct from general Mesa employment services and not an open public shelter. Confirm pre-release referral timing, current beds, eligibility, transport and whether progression to Workforce Villages is available; none is automatic.

resources.name: Heart of Mesa - Food Pantry
resources.description: Heart of Mesa offers a Thursday food pantry in the church office and says everyone is welcome and no one is turned away.
resources.address: 851 N. Stapley Dr., Mesa, AZ 85203
resources.hours: Food pantry Thursday 11:00 AM-1:00 PM. Church office hours Monday, Tuesday and Thursday 9:00 AM-2:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Food pantry at the church office for people who need food. The church also describes a bus ministry that may help some people with transportation barriers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page says everyone is welcome to come get food as needed and no one is turned away. It does not list ID, income, residence or appointment requirements.

**Population Served**
Community members who can reach Heart of Mesa during the Thursday pantry window.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to the church office at 851 N. Stapley Dr., Mesa, on Thursday between 11:00 AM and 1:00 PM. Contact the church office during posted office hours to ask about rides or current pantry operation.

**Important Information to Know**
The pantry window is limited to two hours weekly. Transportation through the bus ministry should be confirmed before relying on it.

resources.name: Valley of the Sun YMCA - Military Outreach and Discounted Military Membership
resources.description: Valley of the Sun YMCA offers free six-month YMCA memberships to eligible Title 10 military families through the Military Outreach Initiative and discounted memberships for active duty, retired and veteran military personnel.
resources.hours: YMCA branch hours vary; apply at a branch welcome center or email for information.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Military Outreach Initiative memberships provide free six-month access to Valley of the Sun YMCA locations for eligible deployed military personnel and military families. Valley of the Sun YMCA also offers preferred-rate military memberships with no joining fees for active duty, retired and veteran military personnel.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The free Military Outreach Initiative is limited to Title 10 Department of Defense groups listed by the YMCA, including families of deployed National Guard and Reserve, active duty assigned to independent duty locations, relocated spouses of deployed active-duty personnel and Community-Based Wounded Transition Unit. Discounted military membership requires military ID.

**Population Served**
Eligible military families, active-duty personnel, retired military personnel and veterans using Valley of the Sun YMCA locations in Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
For discounted military membership, go to the welcome center at any Valley of the Sun YMCA branch with military ID. For questions, email Military@vosymca.org.

**Important Information to Know**
Free sponsored membership and discounted military membership have different eligibility rules. Confirm participating branches, current charges and the activities included before enrolling.

resources.name: Hope's Crossing - Fundamentals of Freedom / Bridge to Success
resources.description: Hope's Crossing is a women-focused reentry nonprofit offering life skills, cognitive behavioral transformation, professional development, emotional support, job-skills training, housing assistance, case management, benefits navigation, clothing, family reunification and workshop-based support for women transitioning from prison, addiction or homelessness.
resources.address: 1632 W Camelback Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85015
resources.hours: Public page lists Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-4:00 PM, Friday-Saturday 9:00 AM-2:00 PM, Sunday closed; Friday hours should be confirmed because the listing is internally inconsistent.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Women's reentry services, including life skills, cognitive behavioral transformation, professional development, emotional support, job-skills training, housing assistance/navigation, case management, community navigation, benefit applications, clothing, family reunification, and workshops such as Fundamentals of Freedom.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The organization serves women in transition from prison, addiction, or homelessness. Current age limits, cohort enrollment, virtual option, costs, and housing-assistance capacity should be confirmed before referral.

**Population Served**
Women in the Phoenix metro and Maricopa County area who are returning from incarceration or rebuilding after criminal-legal involvement, addiction, homelessness, or trauma.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-795-8098, email CreateHope@HopesCrossing.org for general questions, or email enrollment@hopescrossing.org for workshop signup.

**Important Information to Know**
Housing help should be described as assistance or navigation unless current placement capacity is confirmed. This is a women-focused service and may not fit men.

resources.name: NATIVE HEALTH Mesa - Psychiatric Services
resources.description: NATIVE HEALTH Mesa offers psychiatric evaluations and medication management for adolescents and adults age 12 and older after a full behavioral-health intake, with culturally appropriate integrated health access and MAT available across NATIVE HEALTH locations.
resources.address: 777 W Southern Ave, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Behavioral-health intake scheduling through the clinic; after-hours nonemergency advice through regular clinic number. Public psychiatric page does not list a separate Mesa psychiatric schedule.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Psychiatric evaluations and ongoing medication management through Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioners. NATIVE HEALTH Behavioral Health also provides professional and confidential behavioral-health services and resources, counseling-related services, recovery services, traditional healing/talking circles, MAT availability, and after-hours advice through regular clinic numbers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Mesa psychiatric services are for ages 12 and older. Ask intake about payer, discount-fee eligibility and clinical fit; age 6 services at other sites do not define Mesa psychiatry.

**Population Served**
Mesa adolescents and adults seeking psychiatric services, including urban Native American community members and other populations. NATIVE HEALTH states Spanish-speaking staff are available at all locations.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-279-5262, extension 12079, or email erodriguez@nachci.com. Mesa is at 777 W Southern Ave. General behavioral-health intake is weekdays 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; confirm the actual psychiatry appointment schedule.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a crisis line. For behavioral-health emergencies after hours, NATIVE HEALTH points to crisis resources including 602-222-9444 and 988. Confirm current scheduling, payer rules, and whether any counseling or recovery-service group must occur at another NATIVE HEALTH site.

resources.name: Superstition Community Food Bank - Emergency Food Assistance and Senior CSFP Boxes
resources.description: Superstition Community Food Bank provides same-day registration and grocery distributions for eligible East Valley households, including TEFAP food and senior CSFP boxes with a waitlist.
resources.address: 575 N Idaho Rd, Suite 701, Apache Junction, AZ 85119
resources.hours: Food distribution Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 2:00 PM-4:00 PM; closed Wednesdays, weekends and state/federal holidays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency and supplemental groceries through Superstition Community Food Bank, including TEFAP commodities and CSFP senior food boxes. The food bank says each household may receive food twice per calendar month and that same-day registration is available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Households must live within the food bank's area in Maricopa or Pinal Counties and meet financial eligibility; the page references help for households at or below 185% of the Federal Poverty Level. Valid ID is required, and proof of residency may be required depending on the program. Proxy letters are required if someone picks up food for an incapacitated client. CSFP senior boxes may have a waitlist.

**Population Served**
Eligible East Valley households in Maricopa and Pinal Counties, including Apache Junction, Gold Canyon, northwest Pinal County and East Mesa households, and eligible seniors for CSFP.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to 575 N Idaho Rd, Suite 701, Apache Junction, AZ 85119 during distribution hours, or call 480-983-2995 before visiting if service-area or document questions could affect the referral.

**Important Information to Know**
The site is outside Mesa city limits but official materials refer to Maricopa and Pinal County service and East Valley hunger relief. Confirm that a specific Mesa address is within current service guidelines before sending a client who has transportation barriers.

resources.name: Scottsdale Recovery Center - Homes for Heroes
resources.description: Scottsdale Recovery Center Homes for Heroes is a veteran-focused housing, recovery, and employment-support program connected to Scottsdale Recovery Center's addiction and behavioral-health treatment setting.
resources.hours: 24/7 information and intake line listed for Scottsdale Recovery Center.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Veteran-focused housing, recovery, and employment support. The official Homes for Heroes page frames the program around helping veterans rebuild through housing, recovery, and employment support, and lists Scottsdale Recovery Center treatment properties including detox, outpatient, structured sober living, and Homes for Heroes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official public page does not publish detailed Homes for Heroes eligibility, insurance, cost, bed count, or clinical admission criteria. Expect screening for veteran status, recovery/behavioral-health needs, safety, funding, and fit with available programming.

**Population Served**
Veterans with housing instability and recovery or behavioral-health support needs in Scottsdale/Arizona, including potential Maricopa County clients.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Homes for Heroes number 888-773-1744 or Scottsdale Recovery Center's 24/7 information and intake line 602-346-9142. Ask specifically for current Homes for Heroes eligibility, costs, insurance/funding, bed availability, and whether Mesa/Maricopa referrals are accepted.

**Important Information to Know**
This appears tied to a treatment/recovery provider, so insurance, clinical fit, out-of-pocket cost, and capacity matter. Do not describe it as free housing unless the provider confirms funding for the specific client.

resources.name: Paralyzed Veterans of America Arizona Chapter - Veteran Benefits Assistance, Medical Equipment, and Accessibility Advocacy
resources.description: Paralyzed Veterans of America Arizona Chapter supports veterans and others with spinal cord injury, disease/dysfunction, and disability through advocacy, benefits-oriented support, accessibility, communication, education, activities, and sports.
resources.address: 1001 E. Fairmount Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.hours: 211 lists Monday-Friday 9 AM-4:30 PM; confirm before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Helps veterans and others navigate benefits and disability-related resources, and advocates for accessible buildings and health care. The Arizona 211 listing also identifies durable medical equipment and supplies for veterans with neurological or other medical conditions.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Different services have different rules. For some medical equipment, bring veteran identification and a doctor’s note or prescription. The 211 listing states no charge for veterans and their families; charges for other people vary. Ask about eligibility and the specific item needed.

**Population Served**
Arizona veterans with spinal cord injury, disease or other disabilities, their families and others seeking disability advocacy or benefits guidance.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-244-9168 or use the AZPVA contact route. The chapter address is 1001 E. Fairmount Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85014.

**Important Information to Know**
Equipment depends on available stock and any required clinical documentation. Confirm availability before traveling. For formal VA claims representation, ask whether a chapter contact or an accredited PVA National Service Officer should handle the case.

resources.name: City of Phoenix Human Services Department - Targeted One-Time Crisis Assistance
resources.description: Temporary Phoenix crisis program applying $600 to a utility account for households that completely lost SNAP benefits on or after October 1, 2025.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Targeted One-Time Crisis Assistance provides eligible households with $600 applied toward a utility account and $100 in transportation assistance.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Currently reside in Phoenix OR receive City of Phoenix water service, and have completely lost SNAP benefits on or after October 1, 2025 without reinstatement. Assistance is limited to once per household during July 1, 2026–June 30, 2027, while funds remain.

**Population Served**
Phoenix households or Phoenix water-service customers affected by complete SNAP benefit loss.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the BenefitLossAssistance application link, call 602-262-7627 or email benefitlosshelp@phoenix.gov. Have identification, SNAP case details and utility account information ready, with proof of qualifying Phoenix residency or water service as instructed.

**Important Information to Know**
Up to $600 utility assistance and $100 transportation assistance depend on eligibility and available funds. Ordinary Mesa utility accounts do not qualify unless the household meets the Phoenix residency or Phoenix-water-customer route.

resources.name: Veterans Community Project of Glendale Veterans Village
resources.description: Veterans Community Project of Glendale is a planned transitional tiny-home village for veterans experiencing homelessness in the greater Phoenix metro area, with 50 homes, 1:1 support, outreach and case management planned, but local opening/intake is not yet confirmed.
resources.address: 7570 N 63rd Ave, Glendale, AZ 85301
resources.hours: No local public intake hours are confirmed for the Glendale village while infrastructure work is underway.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Planned transitional tiny-home village with 50 fully furnished homes, 1:1 support, preventive outreach, case management, benefits navigation, permanent-housing goals, and community space. VCP's broader assistance page also describes outreach services for acute needs, housing help, emergency assistance, mental-health needs, IDs, benefits assistance, hygiene kits and warm handoffs near operating villages.

**Eligibility Requirements**
VCP states that people who served qualify regardless of discharge status, length of service or type of service, and that help is for veterans experiencing or at risk of homelessness. The Glendale village's current opening and local intake readiness are not confirmed.

**Population Served**
Veterans experiencing or at risk of homelessness in the greater Phoenix metro area once the Glendale site is operational; VCP also allows supporters to reach out on behalf of a veteran in crisis.

**How to Best Connect**
Call VCP at 816-599-6503 or use the VCP contact route to ask whether Glendale is accepting assistance requests or residential referrals. Do not send a client to the Glendale address without confirming current operations.

**Important Information to Know**
Needs administrator resolution before routine referral: the official Glendale page says infrastructure work is underway and the Village Center will go vertical soon, so the site appears not fully open for residential placement even though VCP has a general assistance contact route.
resources.resolutionReason: Needs resolution: official VCP pages support the planned Glendale village and general assistance model, but show Glendale under construction and do not confirm open local residential intake.

resources.name: Arizona Industries for the Blind - Training and Employment for People Who Are Blind or Visually Impaired
resources.description: Arizona Industries for the Blind is a nonprofit social enterprise providing training, personal and professional development, and dignified employment for people who are blind or visually impaired throughout Arizona through supply, scanning, warehousing, and distribution business lines.
resources.address: 515 N 51st Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85043
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Arizona Industries for the Blind creates, sustains, and improves employment for people who are blind or visually impaired. Its business lines include AbilityOne Base Supply Centers, digital document conversion, and warehousing/distribution operations in Phoenix and other Arizona locations. The site describes training, personal development, and professional development opportunities through employment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The main page supports employment for people who are blind or visually impaired, but it does not publish participant eligibility steps or a separate service intake page. Current job openings and referral expectations should be checked through the Careers route or by contacting AIB.

**Population Served**
People who are blind or visually impaired throughout Arizona, including Mesa-area job seekers who can access Phoenix-area operations or other AIB employment sites.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Careers link on the AIB website or call 623-233-7900 to ask whether the person should apply for current openings, seek a Vocational Rehabilitation referral, or request another employment pathway.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a social-enterprise employer, not a general public job center. The official site supports the employment model but does not prove any specific role is currently open.

resources.name: Housing Authority of Maricopa County - Mainstream Vouchers
resources.description: HAMC's Mainstream Vouchers are a referral-based rental assistance pathway for households that include a non-elderly adult with disabilities.
resources.address: 8910 N. 78th Avenue, Building D, Peoria, AZ 85345
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Referral-based rental assistance through HAMC's Mainstream Voucher program.

**Eligibility Requirements**
HAMC describes Mainstream Vouchers for households that include a person with disabilities who is at least 18 and not yet 62 at the effective date of the initial Housing Assistance Payment contract. HAMC states this is referral based.

**Population Served**
Very-low-income households in HAMC jurisdiction that include a non-elderly adult with a disability.

**How to Best Connect**
Work through the client's case manager, disability-service provider, behavioral-health provider, housing navigator or other referral source. For HAMC questions, call 602-744-4500.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a walk-in or open general Section 8 application. Confirm referral source, current voucher availability and whether the client's address or desired housing location falls under HAMC rather than the City of Mesa Housing Authority.

resources.name: Ability360 Sports & Fitness Center and Adaptive Recreation
resources.description: Ability360 Sports & Fitness Center is an accessible fitness, aquatics, adaptive sports, recreation, and wellness facility for people with disabilities and their family members.
resources.address: 5031 E. Washington St., Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: Fitness center general hours listed by Ability360: Monday-Friday 6 AM-7:30 PM, Saturday 8 AM-2 PM, Sunday closed; pool and sport-court schedules vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Sports & Fitness Center provides adaptive sports, accessible recreation, aquatics, fitness programs, group classes, outdoor recreation, and related events that support independence, health, and wellbeing. The official page is https://ability360.org/sports/.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The facility is designed for people with disabilities and their family members. Membership, class registration, reservations, sport-specific requirements, and fees vary by activity.

**Population Served**
People with disabilities and family members in the Phoenix/Mesa/Maricopa County area who can access the Phoenix facility or off-site adaptive recreation events.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-386-4566 for membership, reservations, schedules, and accessibility questions. The facility is at 5031 E. Washington St., Phoenix, AZ 85034. Group classes require reservations; Ability360 states reservations are recommended but not required for aquatic use and not needed for the fitness center.

**Important Information to Know**
The facility is in Phoenix, not Mesa. Transportation, membership cost, class availability, and adaptive-sport participation requirements should be confirmed before a client travels.

resources.name: U.S. Department of State - lost or stolen U.S. passport reporting and replacement
resources.description: The U.S. Department of State provides the official process to report a valid U.S. passport lost or stolen, cancel it, and apply in person for a replacement passport.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides official lost or stolen U.S. passport reporting and cancellation. Reporting can be done online through the Department of State form filler or by mailing Form DS-64. A replacement passport requires a separate in-person application using the standard passport application route.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For U.S. citizens whose valid U.S. passport was lost or stolen. Expired passports should not be reported as lost or stolen through this process. Replacement applications require proof of citizenship, proof of identity, photo and fees unless a specific waiver applies.

**Population Served**
U.S. citizens in Mesa and Maricopa County who need to cancel and replace a lost or stolen valid U.S. passport.

**How to Best Connect**
Report the passport online through the State Department's Online Form Filler for fastest cancellation, or complete and mail Form DS-64. To replace it, apply in person at a passport acceptance facility using Form DS-11 and current Department of State instructions.

**Important Information to Know**
Reporting a passport lost or stolen does not replace it; it cancels the passport and it cannot be used for travel even if found later. Applicants missing all identity or citizenship evidence may need birth-certificate or court-record recovery first. Passport fees and processing times apply unless the Department identifies a specific fee waiver, such as certain disaster-related replacements.

resources.name: Southwest Gas - Low Income Ratepayer Assistance (LIRA)
resources.description: Southwest Gas Low Income Ratepayer Assistance gives eligible Arizona customers a recurring discounted basic service charge and reduced per-therm rate.
resources.hours: Call Southwest Gas or use MyAccount for current application steps; customer assistance number is 877-860-6020.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
LIRA provides a discounted monthly basic service charge and a 30% reduction on the per-therm natural-gas rate year-round for eligible Southwest Gas Arizona customers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Southwest Gas Arizona rate information lists LIRA eligibility at 250% of the federal poverty level. The account must be a Southwest Gas Arizona customer account and current application processing should be confirmed with Southwest Gas.

**Population Served**
Income-qualified Southwest Gas Arizona customers, including Mesa and Maricopa County households in Southwest Gas territory.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Southwest Gas Customer Assistance at 877-860-6020 or use the LIRA link from Southwest Gas Arizona rates/special-program pages. Have the account information and household income documentation ready.

**Important Information to Know**
LIRA is a rate discount, not one-time crisis payment assistance. A household may still owe unpaid balances and should separately ask about bill assistance, Energy Share or installment options if behind.

resources.name: AHCCCS / Arizona Behavioral Health Corporation / HOM, Inc. - AHCCCS Housing Program (AHP)
resources.description: The AHCCCS Housing Program provides permanent supportive housing subsidies and limited housing-related supports for eligible AHCCCS members, primarily members with a Serious Mental Illness designation and some members with General Mental Health/Substance Use Disorder needs.
resources.address: 150 N. 18th Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Permanent supportive housing subsidies paid directly to landlords through the contracted housing administrator. Limited housing-related supports may include deposits, move-in assistance, eviction prevention, damages related to occupancy, and supportive services through AHCCCS managed care plans.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program primarily serves AHCCCS members with a Serious Mental Illness designation. Limited housing may be available for some members with General Mental Health/Substance Use Disorder needs, with priority based on service utilization, complex conditions, or receipt of specific behavioral health services.

**Population Served**
Eligible AHCCCS behavioral-health members across Arizona, including Maricopa County members in Central Arizona RBHA/health-plan pathways who need permanent supportive housing.

**How to Best Connect**
A client should work through their AHCCCS health plan, behavioral-health provider, case manager, or Regional Behavioral Health Authority pathway. AHCCCS lists Mercy Care as the Central Arizona RBHA resource and identifies Arizona Behavioral Health Corporation/HOM, Inc. as the statewide housing administrator.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a walk-in general rent fund. Members are expected to pay up to 30% of income toward rent, with the subsidy paid directly to the landlord. Housing-related payments are limited by budget availability, and clinical residential facilities are not eligible AHP settings.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Education - Exceptional Student Services Dispute Resolution
resources.description: Arizona Department of Education Exceptional Student Services provides special-education dispute-resolution pathways for IDEA Part B concerns, including facilitated IEP, mediation, state complaints and due process.
resources.address: 1535 W. Jefferson St., Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.hours: Public office hours were not stated on the page; contact by email or main phone during business hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
ADE dispute resolution provides information and forms for facilitated IEP, mediation, state complaints, due process complaints, Child Find resources, surrogate parent information and related special-education dispute processes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Use this pathway for alleged violations of IDEA Part B, special-education concerns for students with IEPs, or concerns for students in the process of being evaluated for special education. General education issues and Section 504 discrimination issues may need different routes.

**Population Served**
Arizona students with disabilities or suspected disabilities in the public education system and their parents or guardians, including Mesa-area families.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the forms and request links on the ADE Dispute Resolution page. Contact the ESS Dispute Resolution inbox listed on the page or call 602-542-3084 for questions.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a special-education legal/process pathway, not tutoring, therapy or general school advocacy. Families with urgent school safety or discrimination issues may need additional routes such as the local district, OCR or legal advice.

resources.name: Affirm — Arizona sexual and reproductive health-center finder
resources.description: Find low- or no-cost sexual and reproductive healthcare across Arizona, including Title X health centers.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Find low- or no-cost sexual and reproductive healthcare across Arizona, including Title X health centers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Each clinic and program applies its own eligibility and fee rules; confirm the services and confidential-care arrangements needed.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents seeking reproductive, STI or related preventive care, including adolescents.

**How to Best Connect**
Search by ZIP code and call the selected health center directly to book.

**Important Information to Know**
Affirm’s office is not the treatment site. A listing does not confirm current appointment capacity or every service at a clinic.

resources.name: American Academy of Ophthalmology - EyeCare America
resources.description: EyeCare America is an American Academy of Ophthalmology public-service program that uses eligibility screening to connect eligible uninsured or underinsured adults with volunteer ophthalmologists for no-cost medical eye exams when available.
resources.address: Nationwide program with local ophthalmologist matching when available
resources.hours: Phone support Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-2:00 PM Pacific Time. Online screening is available through the website.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Eligibility screening and referral for medical eye exams by volunteer ophthalmologists for eligible uninsured or underinsured adults. It is focused on medical eye care, not retail glasses.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Official AAO indexed content describes access for uninsured and underinsured individuals age 18 and older. Final eligibility and local availability are determined through EyeCare America's screening process.

**Population Served**
Adults needing medical eye care, especially uninsured or underinsured adults and people at risk for eye disease, when a participating volunteer ophthalmologist is available locally.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the See If You Qualify screening on the EyeCare America website. For questions, call 877-887-6327 or email eyecareamerica@aao.org.

**Important Information to Know**
Not urgent/emergency eye care or a same-day referral service. Medical-eye-exam referral does not guarantee local availability or payment for glasses/refraction, medicines, injections, diagnostic/facility charges or surgery. Ask the programme about the exact exam, any covered follow-up and possible out-of-pocket costs before arranging care.

resources.name: Peer Outreach Recovery & ReEntry Services (PORRS)
resources.description: PORRS provides non-clinical peer recovery support, recovery coaching, health-system navigation and reentry navigation from a Mesa office, with referral form and phone/email access.
resources.address: 423 N Country Club Dr, Suite 34, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: A referral source can submit the PORRS referral form; PORRS says a team member will contact the referral source within two business days.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Peer recovery support, recovery coaching, relapse-prevention planning, community health outreach, health-system navigation to PCPs, behavioral health, MAT and social services, reentry navigation for ID, housing, employment, benefits and treatment linkages, and family/system navigation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
PORRS identifies reentry, probation, parole and diversion clients as a core population, with veteran/service-member and Native-community focus. It describes AHCCCS community-health/peer-support and AIHP participation; confirm the individual payer, referral rules, service area and current capacity.

**Population Served**
Veterans, service members, Native/American Indian and Alaska Native community members, and justice-involved people in Arizona facing substance use, mental-health or reintegration barriers.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the PORRS Client Referral Form from the website and send it to PORRS. Call 602-816-1493 or email Admin@peeroutreachaz.org. The Mesa office is at 423 N Country Club Dr, Suite 34.

**Important Information to Know**
Peer support and navigation are not detox, residential care, medication prescribing, guaranteed housing/job placement or an established document-fee fund. Partner eligibility and openings control referred services. The site’s two-business-day referral response is a stated target; confirm staffing and follow-up for the request.

resources.name: Child Crisis Arizona - Emergency Children's Shelter
resources.description: Licensed emergency children's shelter in Maricopa County for children ages 2-10, open 24/7 year-round, with temporary care, meals, clothing, medical attention, educational support, counseling, and parent/caregiver emergency access based on availability.
resources.address: Call to arrange the appropriate intake and location.
resources.hours: Open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, year-round.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Temporary emergency shelter for children, including around-the-clock nurturing care, meals, clothing, personal care items, medical screenings, health attention, educational support, and counseling.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page describes the shelter as for children ages 2 through 10 in Maricopa County. Children may be placed through Arizona Department of Child Safety, Tribal Social Services, or by community members/parents/caregivers who temporarily cannot provide care. Access is based on availability.

**Population Served**
Children ages 2-10 who need temporary safe shelter and parents/caregivers in emergency situations in Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Parents or caregivers needing help should call 480-834-9424. For suspected abuse or neglect, call the Arizona Department of Child Safety hotline at 888-767-2445.

**Important Information to Know**
This is child-only temporary care, not shelter for an adult survivor and children together. The current programme is called Emergency Residential Services/Emergency Children’s Shelter; an older Crisis Nursery name does not establish different ages. The separate teen-boy foster group home is not established as a public youth shelter. Call before referral; availability is not guaranteed.

resources.name: Maricopa Community Colleges · Maricopa Promise Scholarship
resources.description: Maricopa Promise Scholarship provides eligible new students at any of the ten Maricopa Community Colleges with $600 per semester for four consecutive semesters plus cohort support services such as counseling, tutoring, mentorship, resume and career services, events, orientation, and recognition.
resources.hours: Apply online while funding is available; awards are first-come, first-served for eligible students.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Maricopa Promise Scholarship gives eligible students $600 each semester for four consecutive semesters toward tuition and attendance costs, plus a cohort experience with free support services such as counseling, tutoring, mentorship, resume and career services, welcome orientation, events, celebrations, and graduation recognition.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must have a high school degree or equivalency, have an active admissions application at a Maricopa Community College, be new to postsecondary education, enroll or plan to enroll in at least 6 credit hours, be eligible for in-state tuition, have declared a financial-aid-eligible certificate, associate, or bachelor's program, submit FAFSA, be Pell eligible, and meet satisfactory academic progress standards.

**Population Served**
Eligible new postsecondary students at any of the ten Maricopa Community Colleges, including Mesa Community College students.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Apply Now link on the Maricopa Promise Scholarship page or contact Maricopa financial aid at 480-731-8900 for questions about eligibility and funding status.

**Important Information to Know**
Funding is first-come, first-served for eligible students. This is a different scholarship from Mesa College Promise and has its own eligibility rules, including Pell eligibility and new-student requirements.

resources.name: Clarvida - Youth and Family Support Program (YFSP) Arizona
resources.description: Clarvida's Arizona Youth and Family Support Program (YFSP) supports justice-involved youth and their families in Maricopa, Mohave, and Coconino Counties with community transition, family support, interpersonal skills, life skills, employment readiness, practical living skills, cognitive restructuring, and Maricopa-only mental-health counseling.
resources.hours: Use the program page or Clarvida location/service finder; public page does not list a direct Arizona intake phone.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Youth and family support for justice-involved youth, including community transition from out-of-home or structured care, safety planning, family support, community referrals, interpersonal skills, life skills, employment readiness, housing/transportation/medical-benefit navigation, cognitive skills development, and Maricopa County general mental-health counseling.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public page identifies the program for justice-involved youth and families. It does not publish whether youth must be system-referred, so referral source, current county availability, and enrollment rules should be confirmed with Clarvida.

**Population Served**
Justice-involved youth and their families in Maricopa, Mohave, and Coconino Counties; Maricopa County has additional comprehensive youth programming and mental-health counseling listed.

**How to Best Connect**
Start with the YFSP Arizona program page and its Find Services Near Me route, or use Clarvida's Arizona location/service finder to request the correct Arizona contact.

**Important Information to Know**
The public page supports service scope and county coverage but does not list a direct phone, address, cost, or referral authority. Confirm access before promising services to a family.

resources.name: Mesa Public Library — adult learning, computers and digital help
resources.description: Adult literacy/GED/English/citizenship resources and referrals, computer classes, digital help and public computer/Wi-Fi access through Mesa library branches and online tools.
resources.address: Main Library: 64 E. 1st St., Mesa, AZ 85201; additional Mesa Public Library branches
resources.hours: Branch hours, classes and HOTspot help schedules vary; check the current calendar and registration requirements.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Adult basic education/literacy, GED, ESL/citizenship and digital-learning resources; English conversation/literacy practice; introductory computer classes, online tutorials and card-based platforms such as LinkedIn Learning. Branches offer public computers, free Wi-Fi, printing/copying and selected fax/accessibility services. HOTspot provides personal help with devices, apps and digital tasks.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Public resource webpages are open to all. Online learning tools and regular computer sessions generally need a Mesa library card/PIN; a 15-minute Express computer session may be available without a card. Free @mesa Wi-Fi needs no password and uses the visitor’s device. Classes/events can require registration; referred adult-education providers set their own fees, status, placement and enrollment rules.

**Population Served**
Mesa library users needing learning resources, English/citizenship preparation, digital skills or on-site internet/computer access, including older adults and job seekers. These are not senior-exclusive services.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-644-3100, visit a branch or use the library adult-education pages and event calendar. Main Library is 64 E. 1st St.; public computers are at Main, Red Mountain, Gateway and Dobson Ranch, not Mesa Express. For formal courses, linked providers include Mesa Adult Education at 480-472-7259 and Rio Salado Adult Education at 480-517-8110.

**Important Information to Know**
HOTspot is digital assistance from staff, not a loaned internet hotspot. This is on-site access, not home-internet bill aid. Printing/copying carry per-page charges; outgoing fax is free at selected branches. Confirm equipment, class dates and branch rules. Library referrals do not replace comprehensive GED instruction or immigration legal representation.

resources.name: Ability360 - Home Modification Program
resources.description: Ability360 Home Modification Program helps qualifying people with disabilities and seniors obtain accessibility and safety modifications such as ramps, widened doors, grab bars, modified sinks and toilets, and relocated switches.
resources.address: 5025 E. Washington St., Suite 200, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: Ability360 main office hours are Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM; call the Home Modification Program before beginning any project.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Ability360's Home Modification Program facilitates accessibility and safety modifications for residences. Typical modifications include ramps, widened door openings, grab bars, modified sinks and toilets, and relocated electrical switches.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people with disabilities and/or seniors needing accessibility changes, primarily low-to-moderate-income households in eligible funding areas. CDBG, ALTCS or other funding can have different address, income, disability, ownership and landlord-permission rules. Confirm the Mesa address and proposed work before starting.

**Population Served**
People with disabilities and seniors in eligible Maricopa County funding areas, including possible Mesa residents when their address and project meet program rules.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-256-2245 or use the official Home Modifications page to ask about eligibility, funding area, application steps, landlord/homeowner requirements and whether the requested modification can be considered.

**Important Information to Know**
The current provider page describes the programme as free for qualifying people. Confirm current cost, active funding boundaries, covered work, approvals and wait time; a qualifying need does not guarantee an available project or funding.

resources.name: ACCEL - Adult Services
resources.description: ACCEL Adult Services provides lifelong learning, independent-living skills, day services, employment training, supported employment, and in-home supports for adults with developmental disabilities.
resources.address: 5301 S. McClintock Dr., Tempe, AZ 85283
resources.hours: Day and employment services are offered Monday-Friday 7:30 AM-3:30 PM at facilities; call for admissions and location-specific schedules.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Adult day/lifelong-learning and independent-living services, employment training, job development/search skills, work-behavior preparation, group/individual and integrated community employment with job coaching. In-home options include attendant care, hourly habilitation and respite. Support levels address communication, coping, social skills, independence and community participation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Members must be age 18 or older and have developmental disabilities. Potential members must qualify through the Division of Developmental Disabilities, Rehabilitation Services funding, or have a private-pay source.

**Population Served**
Adults with developmental disabilities, including autism spectrum disorder, behavior disorders, and intellectual disabilities, in Tempe/East Valley and other ACCEL service areas.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Adult Services East at 480-564-5323 or Metro at 602-997-2331. Use the Adult Services admissions contact form to ask about the Tempe/East Valley location, DDD or VR funding, private pay, transportation, and current capacity.

**Important Information to Know**
Transportation services may be available but are not guaranteed. Confirm the right campus, current openings, funding authorization, support level, daily schedule, and whether in-home services can reach the person's Mesa address.

resources.name: Casa Mesa Estates — affordable family rentals
resources.description: Affordable family apartment rentals in Mesa, listed in HUD and Arizona housing-agency directories.
resources.address: 1251 S Mesa Drive, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Affordable family apartment rentals in Mesa, listed in HUD and Arizona housing-agency directories.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Ask management for current income limits, rental screening, household-size rules, fees and application requirements.

**Population Served**
Households seeking affordable family rental housing in Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-834-6728 and ask about Casa Mesa Estates at 1251 S Mesa Drive, current management and the application or waiting-list process.

**Important Information to Know**
Directory information does not establish current vacancies or subsidy availability. Confirm the current rent, requirements and appointment before visiting.

resources.name: ARIZONA@WORK Maricopa County — East Valley Career Center
resources.description: ARIZONA@WORK Maricopa County East Valley Career Center is the Mesa comprehensive public workforce access point for job seekers and employers, connecting clients to adult, youth, vocational rehabilitation, reentry, education, training, and partner services.
resources.address: 1001 W Southern Ave., Suite 101, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Monday–Thursday, 8 AM–7 PM; Friday, 8 AM–5 PM. Confirm appointment requirements.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Career guidance, assessment, job matching/search, resumes, computer access, workshops, job fairs and financial-literacy support. Individualized pathways can include occupational training, education support, paid experience, internships and apprenticeships. Staff route adults/dislocated workers, eligible youth, veterans, people with disabilities and reentry clients to appropriate county or partner programmes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
County services cover Maricopa residents outside the City of Phoenix workforce jurisdiction. Adult workforce applicants generally must be 18+ and authorized to work; youth programmes serve eligible ages 14–24 under separate rules. Individualized services/funds require screening and documents. WIOA adult priorities include public-assistance recipients, low-income or basic-skills-deficient applicants and priority for veterans/eligible spouses within applicable groups.

**Population Served**
Mesa and East Valley job seekers in Maricopa County outside City of Phoenix jurisdiction, including adults, youth, veterans, people with disabilities, and justice-involved job seekers who need a public workforce access point.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-372-9700 or visit 1001 W. Southern Ave., Suite 101, Mesa. Create an Arizona Job Connection account and use the County Client Portal for service applications. For workshops ask 602-506-0589 or HSDTrainingTeam@maricopa.gov. Confirm the appointment and programme schedule.

**Important Information to Know**
Training money, paid experience and supportive services depend on assessment, eligibility and funding. The City Workforce Center at 635 E. Broadway is a separate access point; use its own contact. County workforce services do not process unemployment-insurance applications, which go to DES.

resources.name: We Drive AZ - Free Car Repair and Cars for Veterans in Need
resources.description: We Drive AZ is a veteran-run nonprofit serving veterans and eligible family members in Maricopa County with free car repair, safety-related maintenance and possible donated cars for veterans in need.
resources.hours: Apply online; arrange assessment and service timing through the program.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
We Drive AZ offers free car repair and maintenance help for veterans in need, with services that may include brakes, tires, battery testing and replacement, engine diagnostics, essential repairs and some on-site repair options. The organization also describes a cars-for-veterans program using donated vehicles.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants for car repair services must provide proof of military service or veteran status, show financial hardship or inability to afford needed repairs, live in Maricopa County, and understand that eligibility depends on repair urgency, repair type and availability.

**Population Served**
Veterans and eligible veteran family members across Maricopa County, including Mesa veterans, especially those facing financial hardship and transportation barriers to work, medical appointments or family obligations.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Apply for Car Repair Assistance link on the We Drive AZ car-repairs or eligibility page and provide the requested military-service and hardship documentation. Use the website contact form with questions.

**Important Information to Know**
Services are availability-dependent and may have a waiting period. We Drive AZ prioritizes urgent and safety-related repairs, and not every requested repair can be approved. Vehicle placement depends on donated vehicles and program resources.

resources.name: 2-1-1 Arizona Transportation Hotline and Ride United essential rides
resources.description: 2-1-1 Arizona Transportation Hotline screens for short-term essential rides for health, employment, food, economic stability, legal, housing and education needs when no other transportation resource is available.
resources.hours: Live assistance daily 9:00 AM–7:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The 211 Arizona Transportation Hotline screens for free, short-term essential rides while funding and local capacity last. Eligible purposes can include health care, employment, food, economic stability, legal needs, housing and education. The broader 211 service also connects callers with community resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Rides are for situations where no other transportation resource is available and depend on individual program rules, local driver supply and funding. Clients must be 18 or older unless a parent or guardian accompanies the minor.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents with short-term essential-trip barriers, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents, when funding and local ride capacity are available.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 211 or 877-211-8661 for live help daily, 9:00 AM–7:00 PM, or visit 211arizona.org. Explain the trip purpose, pickup and destination, timing, and why other transportation is unavailable. Screening determines whether ride assistance is available.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a last-resort, short-term ride resource and not an ongoing commute, taxi or guaranteed same-day ride service. Program rules, ride limits, eligible destinations and scheduling are confirmed during screening.

resources.name: Maricopa Information Technology Institute Programs
resources.description: Maricopa Information Technology Institute (MITI) provides IT workforce training, industry certifications, internships, workforce skills, hiring events, scholarships/funding options, and employer connections through Maricopa Community Colleges.
resources.address: Maricopa Community Colleges / Mesa Community College; district office 2411 W. 14th St., Tempe, AZ 85281
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Technology workforce training and education through Maricopa Community Colleges. Listed programs include AWS cloud, Apple technology, IT fundamentals, Jamf, Python applications, workforce professional skills, internships, industry certifications, hiring events, industry tours, mentoring, recruitment connections, and interviews with industry partners.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility varies by program. Credit courses require college enrollment; noncredit courses and boot camps may have separate registration requirements. Costs, prerequisites, and financial aid/funding differ by course.

**Population Served**
Students, job seekers, and current workers pursuing IT reskilling or upskilling through the Maricopa Community College system, including Mesa Community College students.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the MITI request-information link or contact listed MITI staff: Diane Meza at 480-461-7823, Tyler Rowles at 480-461-7209, or the MITI program coordinator through the page. The page also links to Apply Now and Find a Class.

**Important Information to Know**
Course formats and time commitments vary. Funding may include grants, WIOA, scholarships, and financial aid, but availability is program-specific. Confirm current cohort dates, costs, prerequisites, and whether a class is online or local.

resources.name: The 3000 Club - Market On the Move Phoenix Warehouse and Seasonal Produce Distributions
resources.description: The 3000 Club's Market On the Move offers low-cost produce boxes at its Phoenix warehouse and seasonal host sites, with no qualification required but a cash donation required.
resources.address: 1741 W Rose Garden Ln, Suites 6-10, Phoenix, AZ 85027
resources.hours: Phoenix warehouse summer/early fall 2026 public schedule: Tuesday 3:00 PM-6:00 PM, Wednesday 11:00 AM-4:00 PM, Thursday 3:00 PM-6:00 PM, Friday 11:00 AM-4:00 PM. Host-site alerts vary by season.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Low-cost produce access through Market On the Move at the Phoenix warehouse and seasonal host sites. The program is first come, first served and may offer pop-up host sites when produce and weather conditions allow.

**Eligibility Requirements**
No qualification is listed for public Market On the Move access. The current schedule says walk-in only, no online ordering, no pre-ordering, no delivery and no EBT.

**Population Served**
Members of the public who can travel to the Phoenix warehouse or current host site and pay the required cash donation.

**How to Best Connect**
Check the current Market On the Move schedule and alerts before going. The Phoenix warehouse is at 1741 W Rose Garden Ln, Suites 6-10, Phoenix, AZ 85027. Text or call 623-980-7357 for Phoenix questions.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a free emergency pantry and not Mesa-specific at present. The official schedule lists a $10 cash donation per order, no EBT, no delivery and no pre-ordering. Mesa host sites are seasonal or historical unless current alerts add one.

resources.name: Mesa Community College - Senior Citizen Tuition Rate
resources.description: Mesa Community College offers a Senior Citizen Tuition Rate that gives eligible Maricopa County residents age 65 and older 50% tuition savings on credit courses at Mesa campuses or online.
resources.address: Southern and Dobson Campus: 1833 W. Southern Ave., Mesa, AZ 85202; Red Mountain Campus: 7110 E. McKellips Rd., Mesa, AZ 85207
resources.hours: Eligible students may enroll any time before the first class meeting; campus and Enrollment Center hours vary by term.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Senior Citizen Tuition Rate gives eligible students a 50% tuition savings for credit courses at Mesa Community College, including Southern and Dobson, Red Mountain and MCC Online options.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Students must be age 65 or older at the time of enrollment, be Maricopa County residents and be eligible for in-state tuition. The discount applies to credit courses only.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County residents age 65 and older who want to take credit classes at MCC campuses or online.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the MCC senior discount page to begin enrollment, or contact Mesa Community College at 480-461-7000. Eligible students should enroll before the first class meeting and confirm payment deadlines with Cashier Services.

**Important Information to Know**
The discount does not apply to clock-hour courses, non-credit courses, course fees or registration fees. Normal refund and payment-deadline rules still apply.

resources.name: AHCCCS / Solari Crisis & Human Services - Housing and Health Opportunities (H2O) Program
resources.description: AHCCCS/Solari H2O connects narrowly eligible Medicaid members with authorized housing/tenancy supports. Eligibility combines housing circumstances, an SMI designation and qualifying health or correctional-release criteria.
resources.address: Statewide programme; no ordinary public walk-in application.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Housing-related Medicaid support for eligible members, such as transitional housing, tenancy support and approved moving or accessibility costs. Services require eligibility confirmation and authorization.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For qualifying adult AHCCCS members. The current referral criteria combine homelessness indicators AND a Serious Mental Illness designation AND either a chronic health condition or correctional release scheduled within 90 days or occurring within the past 90 days. Solari verifies housing circumstances and program eligibility.

**Population Served**
Eligible Arizona Medicaid members with the combined housing, behavioral-health and health or recent-incarceration circumstances.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the health-home provider to keep the member’s housing circumstances, SMI and relevant health/release information accurate in programme records. Work with the health plan, provider or release case manager. For H2O questions call 855-814-4673 or 480-546-7135, or email H2Omembersupport@solari-inc.org.

**Important Information to Know**
AHCCCS identifies potential participants through its data process and Solari confirms eligibility; outside referrals are not currently accepted. A phone inquiry does not substitute for selection/authorization or guarantee housing, money or a particular service. This is not public cash aid or an ordinary shelter application.

resources.name: NourishPHX — food, clothing and Job and Resource Center
resources.description: NourishPHX Job and Resource Center provides employment support embedded in basic-needs services, including one-on-one career road mapping, resumes, mock interviews, employment attire, job-readiness classes, job-search computer access, job transportation assistance, job fairs and employer information.
resources.phone: General 602-254-7450; Job and Resource Center 602-775-5744; other inquiries 602-775-5740
resources.address: 501 S 9th Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.hours: Food/clothing walk-in: Monday–Friday, 9–11 a.m. SNAP/AHCCCS computer access is listed 9 a.m.–2 p.m.; employment and other services require schedule/appointment confirmation.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Food boxes, produce, clothing/shoes, household/hygiene goods, diapers/formula and resource referrals. Additional offerings include senior food boxes, seasonal June/July Kids Cafe and SNAP/AHCCCS self-service computers. Job and Resource Center provides career planning, resumes, mock interviews, job-readiness classes, computer job search, employment attire, job-transport help and employer/job-fair connections.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official services page says no appointment is necessary for the food pantry and clothing closet and asks clients to bring ID or, if no ID, a piece of mail with current address. Employment-program eligibility, class schedules and transportation assistance rules should be confirmed with the Job and Resource Center.

**Population Served**
Vulnerable individuals and families in the Valley who can reach the Phoenix site and need employment support alongside food, clothing and other basic needs.

**How to Best Connect**
For food/clothing, visit 501 S. 9th Ave., Phoenix, during weekday 9–11 a.m. drop-in hours; call 602-254-7450 for questions. Employment appointments: 602-775-5744; other inquiries: 602-775-5740. Confirm separate programme hours, screening and travel from Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
Food/clothing need no appointment, but bring ID or current-address mail if no ID. Other services can require appointments or separate eligibility, including senior boxes and job-transport help. Seasonal child meals are not a year-round offer. Confirm holidays, supplies and programme availability before a long trip.

resources.name: City of Tempe - Youth Transit Pass Program
resources.description: Tempe Youth Transit Pass Program gives eligible Tempe and qualifying Guadalupe youth ages 6-18 free rides on Valley Metro bus, streetcar and light rail.
resources.address: Tempe Transit Store, 200 E. Fifth St., Tempe, AZ 85281
resources.hours: Transit Store pass pickup: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM, excluding holidays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Youth Transit Pass Program provides a free transit pass for eligible youth to ride all Valley Metro bus routes, streetcar and light rail.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Youth must be ages 6-18 and meet Tempe residency rules; school-based access is available at listed Tempe-area high schools for students who live in Tempe or Guadalupe. Documentation requirements vary by age and pickup site.

**Population Served**
Tempe youth ages 6-18 and certain Guadalupe youth using the school-based route.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to the Tempe Transit Store at 200 E. Fifth St. during listed weekday hours or call 480-350-4311. Bring the required proof of residency, birth certificate and parent/guardian ID unless using a school-based verification route.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not available to most Mesa youth. Lost passes may require a $5 replacement fee and are limited to three replacements per year.

resources.name: City of Phoenix - Phoenix Family Advocacy Center / Victim Services Division
resources.description: Phoenix Family Advocacy Center assists victims of domestic violence, sexual violence and other violent crimes with safety planning, criminal-justice navigation, orders of protection, Address Confidentiality Program applications, trauma support, community resources and referrals.
