resources.description: U.S.VETS Phoenix serves homeless and at-risk veterans and veteran families in Maricopa County with outreach, transitional and permanent housing, SSVF, free mental-health and substance-use support, workforce development, case management and aftercare.
resources.phone: Housing outreach: 602-757-9723 or 602-859-7329; SSVF: 602-441-0612; mental health: 602-717-6682; Career Center: 602-717-0206
resources.address: M.D. Hawkins Veterans Center: 12027 N. 28th Dr., Phoenix, AZ 85029; Administrative office: 3507 N. Central Ave., Suite 200, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.hours: SSVF: Monday–Friday, 7:00 AM–4:00 PM and by appointment. Aftercare: 9:00 AM–5:00 PM. Confirm the specific programme location and appointment; these are not universal facility hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Veteran outreach, transitional and permanent housing support, SSVF housing stabilization, mental-health and substance-use services, employment support, case management and aftercare. Programme participants may receive clothing, household goods, furniture, move-in or utility help according to assessed need and available funds or inventory.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on the program. SSVF is for low-income veteran families who are homeless or at risk of homelessness. Housing, counseling, workforce and case-management services have separate screening, documentation and capacity rules.

**Population Served**
Homeless and at-risk veterans and veteran families in Phoenix and Maricopa County, including Mesa-area veterans who can access Phoenix-based services.

**How to Best Connect**
For housing outreach, call 602-757-9723 or 602-859-7329. For SSVF, call 602-441-0612. For mental health and wellness, call 602-717-6682. For the Career Center, call 602-717-0206.

**Important Information to Know**
Different programmes use different intake numbers, sites and eligibility rules. Confirm openings, discharge/income documentation and the appropriate location. Clothing and household goods are programme-linked assistance, not an unrestricted public furniture or clothing bank.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Economic Security - LIHEAP and Power AZ Status
resources.description: Arizona DES LIHEAP helps eligible low-income households pay heating or cooling utility bills, reduce energy crises, and make energy costs more affordable; Power AZ is no longer accepting new applications.
resources.hours: LIHEAP service line Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
LIHEAP helps eligible Arizona households with heating/cooling costs. Regular benefits range from $160 to $640 under the programme calculation; a qualifying crisis may allow up to $500 after the regular benefit is exhausted. One regular and one crisis benefit are allowed per 12-month period.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Meet energy-need, income and applicable citizenship/immigration requirements. SNAP or Cash Assistance participation can establish categorical income eligibility, while other programme requirements still apply. Crisis help requires an urgent eligible energy problem. Benefit scoring considers factors including young children, older adults, disability and veteran household members.

**Population Served**
Eligible Arizona households, including Mesa residents. The benefit scoring considers energy burden and household members who are older adults, children, veterans or people with disabilities.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through the A-to-Z Arizona Portal or by paper application. Call 866-494-1981, Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM–5:00 PM, or contact a local Community Action Agency for application or grievance help.

**Important Information to Know**
DES states Power AZ funds are exhausted: applications submitted on or before September 21, 2026 will still be reviewed, but applications after September 21, 2026 cannot be accepted or processed for Power AZ. LIHEAP remains separate and is subject to funding and eligibility.

resources.name: Valley Center of the Deaf - Deaf, DeafBlind, and Hard-of-Hearing Independent Living Services
resources.description: Valley Center of the Deaf provides free accessible services for Deaf, DeafBlind, and hard-of-hearing people, with ASL-accessible support that promotes independent living, self-determination, and community connection.
resources.address: Valley Center of the Deaf - Apache ASL Trails, 2428 E. Apache Blvd., Tempe, AZ 85281; Disability Empowerment Center, 5025 E. Washington St., Suite 114, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; contact VCD to schedule a time to meet for services.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Valley Center of the Deaf empowers Deaf, DeafBlind and hard-of-hearing people to live independently and achieve personal goals. Staff are described as bilingual in English and ASL, and services are designed to be accessible and fill gaps in the community.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are free to Deaf, DeafBlind, and hard-of-hearing individuals. Call VCD to schedule and confirm which service, location, language access, and support-provider option is currently available.

**Population Served**
Deaf, DeafBlind, and hard-of-hearing people in the Phoenix metro area, including Mesa/East Valley residents who can access the Tempe or Phoenix locations.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the general line at 602-267-1921 or videophone 480-428-0397 to schedule services. The Tempe location is 2428 E. Apache Blvd.; the Phoenix Disability Empowerment Center location is 5025 E. Washington St., Suite 114.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm whether the needed help is case management, advocacy, employment, independent-living, DeafBlind support, or SSP-related support. ACDHH contractor arrangements may change, so verify the current SSP pathway when that is the specific need.

resources.name: Beyond the Hurt - Household Goods and Basic Needs for Single Mothers
resources.description: Beyond the Hurt supports single mothers, at-risk youth and domestic-violence survivors with education, advocacy and supportive resources. Recent referral evidence identifies household goods, hygiene items, baby equipment and related basic needs by appointment.
resources.address: 813 W Buckeye Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.hours: Appointments only; closed Saturday-Sunday.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Supportive resources for single mothers, at-risk youth and domestic-violence survivors. Recent referral evidence identifies household items, hygiene products, kitchenware, bedding/linens, clothing, baby equipment and related basic needs, usually by appointment or program participation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official site identifies single mothers, at-risk youth and domestic-violence survivors as its focus. Public details do not fully list documentation, income rules or inventory limits, so confirm eligibility when scheduling.

**Population Served**
Single mothers, at-risk youth and domestic-violence survivors in the Phoenix/Maricopa County area who need stabilizing resources and support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-882-5701 or email info@BeyondtheHurt.org. The official site says hours are appointment only and asks people to contact through the Contact Us page.

**Important Information to Know**
Operating details and inventory are not fully published on the official page. Do not send a client as a walk-in without confirming appointment, documents, service fit and item availability.

resources.name: Central Arizona Shelter Services - The Haven
resources.description: CASS The Haven is an emergency shelter designed for adults age 55 and older, offering private non-congregate units, meals, age- and accessibility-informed shelter, case management, medical and behavioral-health connections, public benefits support, and housing navigation.
resources.address: Near I-17 and Northern Avenue, Phoenix, AZ 85051
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency shelter for older adults with private non-congregate units, meals, accessibility-informed design, wraparound case management, medical and behavioral-health connections, public benefits support, and housing navigation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
CASS describes The Haven as a shelter exclusively for adults age 55 and older. Current placement requires referral or shelter coordination and depends on availability.

**Population Served**
Adults age 55 and older experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 2-1-1 for coordinated shelter bed availability and ask about age-friendly shelter referrals to The Haven. CASS lists the location generally as I-17 and Northern in Phoenix rather than a detailed public intake address.

**Important Information to Know**
The public page gives a general location and does not publish a walk-up intake process. Do not promise a bed; use 2-1-1 or CASS shelter coordination to screen availability and fit.

resources.name: Foster Success Education Services · Arizona Education and Training Voucher Program
resources.description: Arizona Education and Training Voucher provides financial, academic, and college support for eligible current and former foster youth in Arizona who are enrolled in qualified postsecondary or vocational programs.
resources.email: Application help: AZETV@FosterEdServices.org; ETV/tuition-waiver questions: AzETV@fostersuccess.org; college coaching: AzETV@azdcs.gov
resources.hours: Rolling applications; select the appropriate academic year and confirm its deadline.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Federally funded, state-administered financial support, academic support, college coaching, and student support for eligible young people with foster-care experience who are enrolled in qualified colleges, universities, vocational education, degree, or certificate programs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be current or former young people in U.S. foster care on or after their 16th birthday for ETV, or adopted from U.S. foster care with adoption finalized after their 16th birthday for ETV. They must also be under age 26, Arizona residents, U.S. citizens or qualified non-citizens, have personal assets under $10,000, be enrolled in a qualified accredited program, make satisfactory academic progress, and maintain a minimum 2.0 GPA each term. Arizona Tuition Waiver has related but different age and foster-care timing rules.

**Population Served**
Arizona current and former foster youth and eligible young adults with foster-care or adoption histories who are pursuing postsecondary education or vocational training.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Arizona ETV application for the correct academic year. Call 219-426-2166 or email AZETV@FosterEdServices.org for signup help; AzETV@fostersuccess.org is also listed for eligibility and tuition-waiver questions. Request college-coaching referral through the DCS Education Specialist at AzETV@azdcs.gov. Ask how to provide the required student details securely.

**Important Information to Know**
The program is Arizona-specific even though Foster Success lists an Indiana mailing address. Students should confirm award limits, tuition waiver fit, required transcripts, FAFSA or school documentation, and academic-year deadlines.

resources.name: Little Eyes International — Arizona pediatric eye-care access
resources.description: Could add child eye treatment and surgery beyond routine exam-and-glasses assistance once the intake route is resolved.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Could add child eye treatment and surgery beyond routine exam-and-glasses assistance once the intake route is resolved.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The organization describes Arizona child eye care; public individual eligibility and intake instructions require confirmation.

**Population Served**
Underserved children in Arizona with visual or pediatric eye-treatment needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Administrator should establish the current patient referral route and relationship to Complete Vision Care or Gift of Sight before a missionary referral.

**Important Information to Know**
The current primary site confirms monthly Arizona clinics and surgical care, but provides no clear patient application or direct intake contact. A clinical partner’s phone is not yet confirmed as this program’s intake.
resources.resolutionReason: The current primary site confirms monthly Arizona clinics and surgical care, but provides no clear patient application or direct intake contact. A clinical partner’s phone is not yet confirmed as this program’s intake.

resources.name: Salt River Project (SRP) - Safety Net Past-Due Alerts
resources.description: SRP notification service allowing customers to designate someone to receive mailed past-due electric-bill notices.
resources.hours: SRP customer service is available 24/7 by phone.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
SRP Safety Net lets a customer choose another person to be notified if the electric bill becomes past due, helping a family member, friend, or caregiver intervene before service is disrupted.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The SRP customer must add a Safety Net contact through SRP My Account or by phone. The Safety Net contact does not need to be an SRP customer.

**Population Served**
SRP residential customers who want another trusted person notified about past-due account status.

**How to Best Connect**
Log in to SRP My Account or call SRP at 602-236-8888 to add a Safety Net contact.

**Important Information to Know**
Safety Net is notification only. Adding someone does not give that person account control, account access, or responsibility for the bill.

resources.name: Ability360 - Home Care Services
resources.description: Ability360 Home Care Services provides non-medical in-home attendant care, personal care, homemaking, respite, companion care, DDD habilitation, private-pay care and family-caregiver employment options.
resources.address: Gilbert/Mesa office: 205 E. Southern Ave., Mesa, AZ 85210; main office: 5025 E. Washington St., Suite 200, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: Home Care Services office hours are Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM, Saturday-Sunday closed; call ahead because hours may vary by location.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Ability360 Home Care Services offers non-medical in-home support, including attendant care, personal care, housekeeping, companion care, homemaking, respite care, DDD habilitation and support for some family caregivers to become paid caregivers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services may be available through ALTCS carriers, DES/DDD or private pay. Eligibility depends on payer authorization, care needs, service area and caregiver availability.

**Population Served**
Seniors, people with disabilities, people with developmental disabilities, ALTCS members and families needing non-medical in-home support in Maricopa, Pima, Pinal and Gila County service areas. Ability360 states services are available in English and Spanish.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 1-800-501-0555 or email care@ability360.org to request care. The Gilbert/Mesa office is listed at 205 E. Southern Ave., Mesa, phone 480-655-9750. Ask whether health plan authorization is needed, whether private pay is available and what caregiver availability looks like.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not emergency caregiving and not automatically free. Authorization, plan participation, private-pay rates and caregiver availability must be confirmed. The Mesa office supports local access but does not guarantee immediate staffing.

resources.name: Defenders of Children - Legal Services for Children, Survivors and Protective Caregivers
resources.description: Defenders of Children provides trauma-informed legal education, advocacy, and selected representation for Arizona legal issues involving vulnerable children, protective caregivers, survivors, and related family or civil matters.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:30 AM-4:30 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Legal education, advocacy, and selected representation for Arizona matters within Defenders of Children's expertise, including family law, related civil legal issues, crime-victim representation, civil-rights restoration, and Tribal law. Services may connect to child safety, protective caregivers, survivors, education, housing, employment, consumer, public benefits, immigration, or other related civil issues when the case fits the program.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Anyone with an Arizona legal issue within the organization's expertise may request help. Services are available without regard to income, age, gender, familial status, or immigration status, but the organization says it lacks capacity to help everyone who applies.

**Population Served**
Vulnerable Arizonans statewide, especially children, protective parents or guardians, survivors, and families facing child abuse, neglect, safety, or related civil legal problems.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Intake Department at 602-710-1903. People who face barriers using the telephone may email intake@defendersofchildren.org. The office lists Monday-Friday 8:30 AM-4:30 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a legal-services organization, not a crisis shelter or emergency hotline. Representation is not guaranteed until the organization accepts the case. Its public services page should be used to confirm whether a specific matter fits the current practice areas.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Corrections, Rehabilitation & Reentry - release identification and documentation
resources.description: ADCRR coordinates release documentation for eligible Arizona state-prison inmates, including MVD identification credentials and, when obtainable, birth certificates and Social Security cards.
resources.address: 701 E Jefferson St, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
ADCRR coordinates release identification and employment documents for eligible state-prison releases. This can include MVD nonoperating identification and obtainable birth certificates or Social Security cards. Its separate release policy provides a time-limited Released Offender Identification Card or affidavit for eligible releases.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Rules depend on the document and release circumstances. The state-prison MVD/document pathway applies to eligible felony releases intending to reside in Arizona. The separate correctional release card has custody, detainer and release-status restrictions; ask the assigned release staff which documents apply. This does not establish a county-jail or federal-release service.

**Population Served**
People preparing to leave Arizona Department of Corrections, Rehabilitation and Reentry custody, including releasees returning to Mesa or Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
The practical route is through the person's assigned ADCRR reentry, case-management or community corrections contact before release. For general ADCRR contact, call 602-542-5497 or use the Department Orders/Policy page for the current Inmate Release System order.

**Important Information to Know**
Arrange documents before release through the case or release team. Correctional release cards and affidavits generally expire after 30 days, sooner for some registration circumstances; follow the date and instructions on the issued document. These are not permanent MVD credentials or a public walk-in ID service. If expected documents were not provided, contact ADCRR or Community Corrections for next steps.

resources.name: Arizona Legal Women and Youth Services - Opportunity Through Immigration
resources.description: Arizona Legal Women and Youth Services provides no-cost immigration legal help for vulnerable youth and trafficking survivors, including DACA, T visas, U visas, Special Immigrant Juvenile status and identity documents.
resources.address: 24 W Camelback Rd, Box A335, Phoenix, AZ 85013
resources.hours: Use the online inquiry or phone route; no public walk-in hours are posted.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free immigration legal assistance for eligible young people, including DACA, T visas for trafficking survivors, U visas for domestic-violence and other qualifying crime victims, Special Immigrant Juvenile status for abused or neglected children in foster care, and identity documents.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The general youth programme serves people age 26 or younger in Maricopa or Pima County affected by homelessness, abuse, domestic violence, trafficking or current/former foster care. ALWAYS also lists T-visa help for trafficking survivors of any age through its Justice for Survivors practice; ask which practice and eligibility apply.

**Population Served**
Eligible youth and young adults, including immigrants experiencing homelessness, abuse or domestic violence and current or former foster youth; a separate practice serves trafficking survivors of any age.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-248-7055 or use the online inquiry. Mail addresses do not establish walk-in intake.

**Important Information to Know**
Case acceptance depends on legal need and capacity. The organization does not handle pending criminal, dependency or severance proceedings.

resources.name: Copa Health — Florian outpatient counselling
resources.description: Provides individual and group counselling for adults, including approaches such as DBT and EMDR.
resources.address: 4250 East Florian Avenue, Building 2, Mesa, AZ 85206
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides individual and group counselling for adults, including approaches such as DBT and EMDR.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Contact the clinic to confirm clinical fit, payer arrangements, referrals and available appointments.

**Population Served**
Adults seeking outpatient mental-health counselling in Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-844-1653 for Copa Florian at 4250 East Florian Avenue, Building 2, Mesa, AZ 85206.

**Important Information to Know**
Florian is a separate location from Copa’s East Valley integrated health home. It is not presented as a walk-in crisis service or an opioid dosing clinic; specific treatment and fees require confirmation.

resources.name: Valle del Sol Community Health - Southeast Valley Integrated Mental Health
resources.description: Valle del Sol's Southeast Valley Mesa location offers psychiatric evaluations, medication management, counseling, integrated mental health, and links to mental-health services for kids, teens, adults and school-based care.
resources.address: 4135 S Power Rd, Suite 108, Mesa, AZ 85212
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; Saturday-Sunday closed. After-hours services are available by calling 602-258-6797.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Psychiatric evaluations, medication management, counseling, integrated mental health, and access to Valle del Sol mental-health services for children, teens, adults and school-based care.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on clinical need, age, payer and appointment availability. Confirm insurance participation and any sliding-fee assistance directly with the clinic when scheduling.

**Population Served**
Mesa and Southeast Valley children, teens, adults and families seeking outpatient mental-health care.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-258-6797 or use the online scheduling link. The clinic is at 4135 S Power Rd, Suite 108, Mesa. After-hours services are available by calling the same number.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm requested service, age range, telehealth option, language needs, accepted plan or fee arrangement, and first available appointment when contacting Valle del Sol.

resources.name: Maricopa County Juvenile Probation / Healthy Boundaries Court
resources.description: Healthy Boundaries Court is a Maricopa County juvenile collaborative court for youth charged with sexual offenses. It coordinates the youth's treatment provider, judge, probation officer, prosecutor and attorney to support treatment progress, family healing, accountability and aftercare.
resources.address: 1810 S. Lewis Street, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Court access depends on juvenile court/probation involvement. Contact the Juvenile Department for case-specific information.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Healthy Boundaries Court is a collaborative juvenile court process where the treatment provider, judge, probation officer, prosecutor and youth's attorney work together to guide treatment progress. The program uses rewards and consequences, supports youth and family healing, and holds hearings during treatment and aftercare.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For youth in Maricopa County juvenile court who are charged with sexual offenses. Participation is through the juvenile court/probation process, not voluntary community self-enrollment.

**Population Served**
Youth under juvenile court jurisdiction in Maricopa County who are charged with sexual offenses, including youth and families connected to the Southeast Juvenile Court Center in Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Work through the assigned juvenile probation officer, defense attorney or juvenile court team. The Juvenile Department can be contacted at juveniledept@jbazmc.maricopa.gov or 602-506-4533. The Southeast Juvenile Court Center is at 1810 S. Lewis Street, Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a court-involved youth pathway, not adult reentry support and not a public treatment provider. Because cases involve sensitive juvenile and victim issues, referrals should go through the court/probation team.

resources.name: Maricopa County — Help with Homelessness directory
resources.description: Provides a public directory of coordinated-entry and homelessness access routes across Maricopa County.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides a public directory of coordinated-entry and homelessness access routes across Maricopa County.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The directory is public; eligibility is decided by each assessment or service programme.

**Population Served**
Families, single adults and people seeking the correct regional assessment route.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the County directory to identify the appropriate programme. Families can start with 211, daily 9 a.m.–7 p.m.; ask about current assessment locations.

**Important Information to Know**
The County administrative office is not a shelter or walk-up assessment centre. Some partner phone listings can lag behind the provider; the current family route is 211.

resources.name: Chicanos Por La Causa - Housing Counseling, Supportive Housing, and Grace House Transitional Housing
resources.description: CPLC offers housing counseling and supportive housing services for people facing housing barriers, and CPLC Corazón offers Grace House transitional housing exclusively for former Corazón residential-treatment clients transitioning out of services.
resources.address: CPLC Housing Counseling: 1402 S. Central Ave, Bldg A, Phoenix, AZ 85004; CPLC Corazón: 3639 W Lincoln St, Phoenix, AZ 85009
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
CPLC provides HUD-approved housing counseling, supportive housing services, resident service coordination, and referrals to help people maintain housing stability. CPLC Corazón also offers Grace House transitional housing for former Corazón residential treatment clients who are continuing outpatient counseling, case management, sobriety, employment search, and independence planning.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Grace House is exclusively for former CPLC Corazón residential treatment clients. Supportive Housing Services eligibility varies by program and may include homelessness or major housing barriers; CPLC specifically names previous criminal history among barriers its supportive housing work may address.

**Population Served**
Low-income people and people experiencing homelessness or housing instability in Maricopa County, including people with previous criminal history when they fit the specific housing program criteria. Corazón/Grace House serves people leaving that residential substance-use treatment program.

**How to Best Connect**
For CPLC Housing Counseling, call 602-253-0838. For Supportive Housing Services in Maricopa County, call 602-609-7556, TDD/TTY 711, or email SHS@cplc.org. For CPLC Corazón, call 602-233-9747. Ask directly whether a justice history affects eligibility and whether the client fits Grace House or another CPLC housing route.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a reentry-specific provider and should be treated as a reserve housing lead. Grace House is not open to all returning citizens; it is tied to successful transition out of CPLC Corazón residential treatment. General affordable housing and housing counseling do not guarantee available units or financial assistance.

resources.name: Mesa Community College Counseling Department - Personal and Urgent Counseling
resources.description: Mesa Community College Counseling Department provides in-person and distance counseling services for students, including personal counseling, referral help, crisis response, career and academic counseling, self-enrichment, and substance-abuse prevention support.
resources.address: Southern and Dobson Campus, 1833 W. Southern Ave., Mesa, AZ 85202; Red Mountain Campus, 7110 E. McKellips Rd., Mesa, AZ 85207; MCC Online
resources.hours: Appointments are scheduled through the Counseling Department; college operating hours and academic calendars apply.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
In-person and distance counseling services for MCC students, including personal counseling for concerns interfering with achievement, referrals to agencies and services, academic counseling, career counseling, self-enrichment support, crisis response, AOD compliance, life-skill facilitation, Peervention volunteers, and substance-abuse prevention.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Limited to Mesa Community College students and MCC counseling services. It is not a substitute for ongoing specialty psychiatric care or emergency services.

**Population Served**
Mesa Community College students at Southern and Dobson, Red Mountain, and online.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-461-7588 to schedule counseling for either Southern and Dobson or Red Mountain. The page also links a request-an-appointment form. If the office is closed and immediate help is needed, MCC directs people to 911, 988, MCC Police non-emergency 480-461-7046, EMPACT Crisis Line 480-784-1500 or 602-222-9444, and other crisis resources.

**Important Information to Know**
This is student support tied to the college. Availability follows college operations and appointment capacity; after-hours crises are routed externally.

resources.name: Matthew's Crossing Food Bank - Emergency Food Boxes and Food Programs
resources.description: Matthew's Crossing Food Bank provides emergency food boxes and several East Valley food programs including senior boxes, mobile marketplace, homebound deliveries and Meals to Grow school food support.
resources.address: 1368 N. Arizona Ave., Unit 112, Chandler, AZ 85225
resources.hours: General food bank hours: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 8:00-11:00 AM; Wednesday 4:00-6:00 PM. School, mobile marketplace and delivery schedules vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency food boxes, senior food boxes for qualified people age 60+, monthly fresh-food pop-up distributions, homebound deliveries, holiday boxes, Meals to Grow weekend backpacks and on-campus food closets.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Emergency food box registration generally requires valid photo ID. Senior boxes are for qualified individuals age 60 and older. Meals to Grow is school-based through participating schools. Homebound delivery depends on need and program capacity.

**Population Served**
Chandler/East Valley neighbors needing food assistance, including seniors, homebound neighbors, students and families at participating schools. Mesa households should confirm service area before travel.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-857-2296 or email info@matthewscrossing.org. For student support, ask the school counselor, social worker or front office whether Meals to Grow backpacks or food closets are available.

**Important Information to Know**
This is Chandler-based and may be most practical for southeast Mesa or Mesa-adjacent clients. Confirm current Mesa eligibility, documents and program-specific capacity before referral.

resources.name: Mesa Community College - Student Care Services and Mesa Market Basic-Needs Supports
resources.description: Mesa Community College Student Care Services helps enrolled students stay in school by connecting them with food, hygiene, clothing, shelter referrals, transportation and other community or campus supports. Financial assistance may be explored but is not guaranteed.
resources.address: Southern & Dobson Campus: 1833 W Southern Ave, Mesa, AZ 85202; Red Mountain Campus: 7110 E McKellips Rd, Mesa, AZ 85207
resources.hours: Use the online Care Team Referral route or call the campus; campus service hours vary by office and semester.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Care Team support and referrals for basic needs affecting enrollment, including food, housing or shelter referrals, transportation, hygiene support, clothing and essential items, counseling referrals, academic resources, disability resources and campus/community support connections.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Mesa Community College students. Financial assistance and specific resource availability are not guaranteed and depend on student situation and program funds.

**Population Served**
MCC students at Southern & Dobson, Red Mountain, and MCC Online who are facing housing instability, food needs, transportation barriers, hygiene or clothing needs, or other obstacles to staying enrolled.

**How to Best Connect**
Submit a Care Team Referral through the MCC Student Care Services page or call MCC at 480-461-7000. For student-care questions, the submitted phone was 480-461-7288; confirm the current office route if the main line redirects.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a student support and referral program, not public shelter or guaranteed emergency financial aid. Non-students should use community homeless-service routes.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Child Safety - transition-to-adulthood vital records and identification support
resources.description: Arizona DCS policy requires specialists to support youth in out-of-home care with transition records, including Social Security card access for youth age 14+ on written request and birth certificate, Social Security card and state ID arrangements for youth age 16+ unless ineligible.
resources.hours: Access is case-specific through DCS specialists and case teams; it is not a public walk-in document desk.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
For youth in DCS out-of-home care, DCS specialists must follow policy to provide or arrange key transition documents, including a certified birth certificate, Social Security card and state identification card for youth age 16 and older unless ineligible. DCS must also provide a Social Security card to a child age 14 or older within 120 days after receiving the child's written request.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Limited to youth in Arizona DCS custody or out-of-home care and related transition-to-adulthood case planning. Access is through the assigned DCS specialist and case process.

**Population Served**
Arizona youth in DCS out-of-home care, including youth placed in Mesa or Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Work through the assigned DCS specialist, case team or placement supports. The public DCS line 1-877-543-7633 can route general questions, but the document pathway is case-specific.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a public-system duty for eligible youth, not a general ID clinic. Foster parents and kinship caregivers may also request a child's Social Security number for a lawful purpose under the policy, but document issuance for youth should be coordinated with the specialist.

resources.name: Gallus Medical Detox Centers · Scottsdale
resources.description: Scottsdale medical detox center offering 24/7 medically supervised inpatient detox for adults withdrawing from alcohol, opioids and other substances.
resources.address: 4326 N 75th St, Scottsdale, AZ 85251
resources.hours: 24/7 medically supervised inpatient detox; call before travel.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Gallus Medical Detox Scottsdale provides medically supervised inpatient detox for adults using IV and oral medication protocols for withdrawal from alcohol, opioids and other drugs. The program includes medical monitoring, individualized treatment plans and aftercare/referral support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adults needing detox should call for screening. Gallus states it works with most major insurance providers as an out-of-network provider and does not accept Medicaid or Medicare at this time.

**Population Served**
Adults in Scottsdale/Maricopa County and statewide Arizona who can travel to Scottsdale for inpatient medical detox, including Mesa residents when clinically and financially appropriate.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-764-3819 or toll-free 888-306-3122. Confirm substance treated, medical appropriateness, insurance/self-pay responsibility and admission timing before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
Gallus is detox/withdrawal management, not ongoing residential rehab, outpatient counseling, sober living or methadone maintenance. Clients often need a next-step treatment plan after detox.

resources.name: Arizona Autism United - Family Support Team and East Valley Center
resources.description: Arizona Autism United provides autism-focused therapy, DDD supports, respite, attendant care, diagnostic and counseling services, plus free Family Support Team navigation for autism and developmental-disability systems.
resources.address: East Valley Center: 4309 E. Florian Ave., Mesa, AZ 85206; services may also be home, school, community or telehealth based depending on program
resources.hours: Call or use online service/family-support routes; program locations, schedules and waitlists vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Arizona Autism United offers ABA therapy, speech and language therapy, occupational therapy, AAC device evaluations, DDD parent-provider help, habilitation, respite, attendant care, diagnostic evaluations, psychotherapy and counseling, clinical family coaching, family support, school consultation and autism-awareness training.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are autism-focused. Therapy, DDD services, respite, attendant care, evaluations and family support each have different age, diagnosis, payer, authorization, location, referral and availability rules. Family Support is free and does not require being a current AZA United client.

**Population Served**
Children, families and individuals affected by autism in Arizona, including Mesa and Maricopa County families needing therapy, DDD-funded supports, respite or autism system navigation.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-773-5773, use the Contact page, or book with the Family Support Team. For family support, parents and family members can request coaching and systems-navigation help at no cost. Ask specifically about East Valley Center services at 4309 E. Florian Ave. in Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
This is autism-specific. Confirm whether the service is clinic-, home-, school-, community- or telehealth-based; ask about insurance, DDD/ALTCS authorization, waitlists, age ranges, provider availability and Mesa service area.

resources.name: U.S.VETS Phoenix - Ashley's Place for Women Veterans
resources.description: Ashley's Place at U.S.VETS Phoenix provides two supportive homes for women veterans, with counseling, case management, health, transportation, career and life-skills supports focused on transition to permanent housing.
resources.address: Phoenix, AZ; residential addresses not publicly listed
resources.hours: Call or email for screening; residential addresses and live availability are not public.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Two supportive homes for women veterans, with one-on-one and group counseling, case management, healthcare connections, transportation assistance, career and life-skills training, and support toward permanent housing.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For women veterans who fit U.S.VETS Phoenix screening and program availability. Veteran status, documentation, support needs and housing fit will be assessed by program staff.

**Population Served**
Women veterans in the Phoenix/Maricopa County area who need supportive housing and transition support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Ashley's Place at 602-499-3859 or 602-397-4555, email ashleysplace@usvets.org, or contact the U.S.VETS Phoenix outreach team at 602-757-9723 or 602-859-7329.

**Important Information to Know**
The residential addresses are not published. Screening and openings are required; a contact does not guarantee placement.

resources.name: Salt River Project (SRP) - Medical Preparedness Program
resources.description: SRP outage notification and preparedness program for residential customers using approved electric-dependent life-support equipment at home.
resources.address: Medical Preparedness Program PAB275, SRP, P.O. Box 52025, Phoenix, AZ 85072-2025
resources.hours: Resource counselors: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; SRP customer service is available 24/7 for after-hours questions or mailed applications.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Medical Preparedness is an outage preparation and notification program for SRP customers who require electricity to operate qualifying medical life-support equipment. Planned outage notice helps the household decide whether to stay home or leave temporarily.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The patient must use SRP-approved electric-dependent FDA Class III medical equipment at home, such as dialysis equipment, ventilator, infant apnea monitor, feeding or infusion pump, suction machine, oxygen concentrator, LVAD or SynCardia Total Artificial Heart. The SRP account must be on a billed residential price plan. Physician verification is required within 60 days and every three years.

**Population Served**
SRP residential customers with a household member using qualifying medical life-support equipment, including eligible Mesa and Maricopa County customers in SRP territory.

**How to Best Connect**
Call SRP resource counselors at 602-236-3000 Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM to enroll. After hours, call 602-236-8888 for questions or to request a mailed application. Completed applications can be emailed to crc_medical@srpnet.com, faxed to 602-629-7909 or mailed to SRP.

**Important Information to Know**
Plan for backup power and safe alternatives; enrollment does not guarantee uninterrupted electricity or remove bill obligations. M-Power customers should ask about changing to an eligible billed plan. The legacy $17 medical credit is closed to new participation under the current 2026 rider, so new Medical Preparedness enrollment does not promise that discount.

resources.name: Maricopa County Human Services Department - Hand in Hand Street Outreach
resources.description: Maricopa County Hand in Hand Street Outreach dispatches outreach teams to known homeless gathering areas in unincorporated Maricopa County and listed targeted communities. Teams connect people with housing, food/benefits, mental and physical health care, substance-use services, case management, transportation, employment and long-term care.
resources.hours: Submit requests through the county service-request form for covered areas; general inquiries can call 602-506-0589.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Street outreach teams that go into covered communities where people experiencing homelessness are known to gather and connect them to housing, food and benefits, mental and physical health services, substance-use services, case management, transportation, employment and long-term care.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For individuals experiencing homelessness in unincorporated Maricopa County or the targeted communities listed by the county. Mesa city is specifically listed outside coverage.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness in covered unincorporated or targeted Maricopa County areas, including county islands or nearby covered communities outside Mesa city limits.

**How to Best Connect**
For covered areas, submit a request through the county page with as many location details as possible, or call 602-506-0589 for general questions. Mesa city callers should use Mesa-specific outreach routes or 2-1-1 instead.

**Important Information to Know**
Mesa city locations are outside this programme; use Mesa outreach or 2-1-1 for those locations. County islands or other listed communities may qualify. Transportation is part of assessed outreach support, not a standalone ride service, and depends on available resources.

resources.name: Streets of Joy — Second Chance and transitional living
resources.description: Offers structured transitional-living pathways, including a program for people recently released from custody.
resources.address: 451 E 4th Place, Mesa, AZ
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Offers structured transitional-living pathways, including a program for people recently released from custody.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Second Chance requires release within thirty days, proof of dates, a clean drug test and sixty working days of volunteer service. Other tracks have different work, income, service and payment rules.

**Population Served**
Qualifying adults seeking structured transitional living in Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-757-6921 and ask which program applies before arrival at 451 E 4th Place, Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
The employed track lists $175 weekly due on entry; the SSI/SSDI track lists $650 on entry and light-duty volunteer work. Confirm all current costs and requirements; this is not an unrestricted free bed.

resources.name: Arizona MVD - driver-license reinstatement and restricted-driving pathways
resources.description: Arizona MVD provides official steps to check license status, resolve compliance items, reinstate eligible suspensions, apply after revocation and review restricted-driving permit options.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Arizona MVD license suspension/revocation pages explain how to reinstate an eligible suspension, apply after a revocation, check an AZ MVD Now compliance timeline, and evaluate restricted driving permits for qualifying insurance or DUI-related suspensions.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Requirements depend on the underlying suspension or revocation. A driver may need court clearance, required documents, SR-22 proof, alcohol/drug screening, an ignition interlock, a revocation investigation packet, waiting periods and applicable fees.

**Population Served**
Arizona drivers, including Mesa residents, who need to understand official MVD reinstatement or restricted-driving steps after a suspension or revocation.

**How to Best Connect**
Start at AZMVDNow.gov to check license status and compliance items, or visit an MVD or Authorized Third Party office. For MVD assistance, call 602-255-0072. Use the restricted-driver-permit page if the person may qualify for limited driving privileges.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an official pathway, not legal advice, court advocacy or fee assistance. Court obligations, insurance proof, screening, interlock rules and fees are case-specific; clients should check their own compliance timeline before paying a third party.

resources.name: Arizona Commission for the Deaf and the Hard of Hearing - AzTEDP
resources.description: ACDHH's Arizona Telecommunications Equipment Distribution Program provides free telecommunications and alerting equipment for eligible Arizona residents who are Deaf, hard of hearing, DeafBlind/CVHL or speech-impaired.
resources.address: 100 N. 15th Ave., Suite 104, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM. Appointments are strongly recommended for in-person service.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
AzTEDP provides free telecommunications equipment such as amplified phones, Bluetooth options, TTYs, speech devices and signaling, flashing or vibrating alert devices.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is for U.S. citizens who live in Arizona and are Deaf, hard of hearing, DeafBlind/CVHL or speech-impaired. ACDHH states equipment is provided regardless of income.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents with qualifying hearing, combined vision-hearing or speech disabilities, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-542-3365, videophone 602-761-9541 or toll-free 866-223-3412, or email aztedp@acdhh.az.gov. Staff offer phone, email, Zoom and arranged in-person help. Appointments are strongly recommended for the Phoenix office.

**Important Information to Know**
Equipment depends on assessed communication need. AzTEDP does not provide hearing aids or general phone-bill help. Landline CapTel service ended in January 2025; ask staff about current equipment and connection options.

resources.name: AHCCCS - Medicare Savings Programs
resources.description: AHCCCS Medicare Savings Programs may pay Medicare premiums and, at lower income levels, Medicare deductibles and coinsurance for eligible Arizona Medicare beneficiaries.
resources.address: 150 N. 18th Avenue, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.hours: Apply online through Health-e-Arizona Plus or use the AHCCCS Medicare Cost Sharing application; MSP processing is generally listed as 45 calendar days when complete.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Help with Medicare costs through Arizona Medicare Savings Programs. AHCCCS says eligible Medicare beneficiaries may have Medicare premiums, co-payments and deductibles paid, with lower-income applicants qualifying for broader Part A and B cost sharing and higher-income applicants possibly qualifying for Part B premium help.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicant must be an Arizona resident, be a U.S. citizen or qualified immigrant, have or apply for a Social Security number, be entitled to Medicare Part A, and be under the applicable income limit. AHCCCS listed 2026 income limits on the official page; eligibility is decided through application review.

**Population Served**
Arizona Medicare beneficiaries with low income, including eligible Mesa and Maricopa County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through Health-e-Arizona Plus or print the AHCCCS Medicare Cost Sharing and AHCCCS Health Insurance application. AHCCCS member questions can go to 602-417-4000 or 1-800-654-8713.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not cash paid to the client; it reduces approved Medicare costs. Income is reviewed under program rules and AHCCCS may request documentation before deciding eligibility.

resources.name: A New Leaf - DVSTOP Domestic Violence Safe Temporary Overflow Program
resources.description: A New Leaf DVSTOP provides short-term emergency safe placement, often in a hotel or temporary safe location, when Maricopa County domestic-violence shelters are full and hotline screening finds high danger and program criteria are met.
resources.hours: Domestic-violence hotline access; no public walk-up hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Short-term emergency safe placement in a temporary location or hotel when domestic-violence shelters are full, plus basic needs while a longer-term shelter or housing option is pursued.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For domestic-violence survivors who call the hotline, are assessed as high risk and meet set criteria. Assistance is not guaranteed and depends on screening, danger level, fit, funding and availability.

**Population Served**
Domestic-violence survivors in Maricopa County, including individuals and families who can be hard to place in regular shelters, such as large families, men, people with disabilities and late-term pregnant survivors.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-890-3039 for screening and ask about DVSTOP when shelters are full and safe temporary placement is needed. DVSTOP@turnanewleaf.org is also listed; email is not an immediate-response safety route. Placement locations are arranged after screening.

**Important Information to Know**
This is assessed emergency overflow placement, not a general hotel voucher or guaranteed bed. Call the service line rather than programme staff directly; if it cannot arrange placement, ask for direct shelter and safety-planning options.

resources.name: Jewish Family & Children's Service - Real World Job Development
resources.description: JFCS Real World Job Development supports current and former foster-care youth and low-income youth ages 16-24 with GED support, job training, paid apprenticeships, job referrals, case management and mentoring.
resources.address: 2033 N. 7th Street, Phoenix, AZ 85006
resources.hours: Call for current intake and enrollment capacity.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Real World Job Development provides intake and assessments, literacy skills, GED education and support, job training, paid apprenticeships, case management, job referrals, guidance and mentorship, individual and group living-skills training, and information/referral services. JFCS says it partners with ARIZONA@WORK and local businesses that can provide paid onsite job training or apprenticeships.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program serves young people ages 16-24 and is specifically designed for current and former foster-care youth and low-income youth facing significant barriers to education, training and employment opportunities.

**Population Served**
Greater Phoenix youth and young adults ages 16-24, especially current or former foster youth and low-income youth with barriers to school, training and work.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Real World Job Development contact number at 602-279-0084. Program location listed on the official page is 2033 N. 7th Street, Phoenix. Ask about Mesa-area access, eligibility documents, current openings and transportation.

**Important Information to Know**
Paid apprenticeships and placements depend on employer partners and enrollment capacity. Auxiliary aids and services are available upon request for individuals with disabilities.

resources.name: City of Mesa Housing Authority - Incoming Housing Choice Voucher Portability
resources.description: City of Mesa Housing Authority's incoming portability process gives current Housing Choice Voucher holders a defined route to move their voucher to Mesa. The current public housing authority must send portability documents to Mesa before the household arrives.
resources.address: Mesa Housing Authority, MS-9870, Attn: HCV Portability, PO Box 1466, Mesa, AZ 85211-1466
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 7:30 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Incoming Housing Choice Voucher portability review for households moving to Mesa with an eligible voucher from another public housing authority. Mesa is billing incoming portability requests until further notice and reviews documents, eligibility, payment standards, occupancy standards, background checks, and debts to other housing authorities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The household must already be an HCV participant or applicant from another public housing authority and must meet Mesa Housing Authority requirements. Applicant port-ins must be income-eligible in Mesa's jurisdiction. Adults are subject to criminal and sex-offender background checks.

**Population Served**
Voucher holders or eligible voucher applicants moving into Mesa Housing Authority jurisdiction.

**How to Best Connect**
The current public housing authority must mail, email, or fax portability paperwork before the household arrives. Send to Mesa Housing Authority, MS-9870, Attn: HCV Portability, PO Box 1466, Mesa, AZ 85211-1466; fax 480-644-2923; email portability@mesaaz.gov. Call 480-644-6536 for portability questions.

**Important Information to Know**
Mesa does not accept hand-delivered portability documents from participants. After all required documents are received, allow about 10 business days for staff review and initial contact.

resources.name: Mayo Clinic in Arizona - Charitable Care and Financial Assistance
resources.description: Mayo Clinic offers charitable care, financial assistance, payment plans and uninsured financial advocacy for eligible medically necessary Mayo Clinic services at its Arizona campuses.
resources.address: 13400 E. Shea Blvd., Scottsdale, AZ 85259; Arizona services also include Mayo Clinic Specialty Building and Hospital in Phoenix
resources.hours: Patient Account Services for Mayo Clinic in Arizona: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM Mountain time.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Financial assistance, charitable care, reduced-cost medically necessary services, extended payment plans, emergency care regardless of ability to pay, and uninsured-patient financial advocacy through ElevatePFS for people receiving or needing Mayo Clinic care.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on medically necessary services, referral/provider request, insurance and other payment sources, household income, assets, household size and confirmation of application for available coverage such as Medicaid when eligible. International patients are generally not eligible.

**Population Served**
Patients receiving medically necessary Mayo Clinic care in Arizona who are uninsured, underinsured or experiencing financial hardship.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Mayo Clinic Patient Account Services at 844-217-9591. Arizona patients may also visit Registration and Business Services at Mayo Clinic Building, Scottsdale campus; Mayo Clinic Specialty Building, Phoenix campus; or Mayo Clinic Hospital, Phoenix campus.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a routine safety-net clinic entry point. It is most useful when a client has Mayo Clinic care, an approved referral or a specialty need connected to Mayo. Applications can be submitted through Patient Online Services if the patient has an account, or by electronic/PDF application with supporting documents.

resources.name: Family Care Center - Mesa Therapy, Psychiatry, Medication Management and TMS
resources.description: Family Care Center's Mesa clinic provides outpatient therapy, psychiatry, medication management, psychological services, TMS and a mental-health intensive outpatient program for children, teens, adults, couples and families, with in-person and telehealth options.
resources.address: 1910 S. Stapley Dr, Suite 209, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; Saturday-Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Outpatient mental-health therapy, individual therapy, couples counseling, family counseling, child and teen therapy, psychiatry, medication management, adult/child/geriatric psychiatric care, psychological services, TMS, and a Mesa mental-health intensive outpatient program.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Family Care Center says the Mesa clinic is accepting new patients and serves all ages. It accepts most major Arizona insurance plans, VA benefits, out-of-network and self-pay patients; exact network status, self-pay cost and provider fit must be confirmed before scheduling.

**Population Served**
Children, teens, adults, seniors, couples and families in Mesa and Maricopa County seeking private outpatient mental-health care.

**How to Best Connect**
New patients call 888-374-5066 or use the online Make an Appointment link. Existing patients call 480-351-8020. The clinic is at 1910 S. Stapley Dr, Suite 209, Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a private outpatient clinic, not an emergency crisis centre. Its Mesa mental-health intensive outpatient programme generally meets three hours on four days per week for five to six weeks; it is not a substance-use IOP. Confirm the current schedule, age fit, clinician availability, insurance/VA authorization and costs. TMS and other treatment options require clinical assessment.

resources.name: Valley Metro - RideChoice
resources.description: Valley Metro RideChoice is a subsidized same-day ride option using taxi, rideshare and wheelchair-accessible providers for eligible riders in participating communities; Mesa eligibility is listed for ADA paratransit-certified riders.
resources.address: 4600 E. Washington St., Suite 101, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: RideChoice representatives are listed as available 24 hours per day, every day of the year, including holidays, after enrollment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
RideChoice provides subsidized direct rides through local taxicabs, rideshare companies such as Uber or Lyft, and local companies with wheelchair-accessible vehicles. It can be more flexible than scheduled ADA paratransit after enrollment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility varies by participating community. Current RideChoice materials list Mesa with ADA paratransit-certified eligible people; age 65+ alone is listed for some other communities and should not be treated as Mesa eligibility unless Valley Metro confirms it for the client's residence.

**Population Served**
ADA paratransit-certified Mesa residents and other eligible riders in participating Maricopa County communities.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-716-2100 for enrollment. Once eligible, call 602-716-2111, available 24 hours every day, to arrange RideChoice trips. Give pickup/destination addresses, travel time, provider preference and accessibility needs. Confirm companion, personal-care-attendant and service-animal arrangements before booking.

**Important Information to Know**
The published base allowance is 20 trips monthly, at $3 for the first eight miles and $2 per additional mile. Ask about extra work, school or medical trips and confirm current fares and accessible-vehicle availability. Mesa requires ADA paratransit certification; age 65 alone does not qualify. Arrange companions, attendants and service animals at booking; drivers do not enter homes or provide personal-attendant care.

resources.name: UMOM New Day Centers - New Day Center Family Emergency Shelter
resources.description: UMOM's New Day Center Family Emergency Shelter provides safe temporary shelter and individualized support for families with children experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County; access starts through Family Housing Hub rather than a direct walk-in guarantee.
resources.address: 3333 E Van Buren St, Phoenix, AZ 85008
resources.hours: Use Family Housing Hub/2-1-1 first; direct shelter walk-in access is not established.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Safe temporary shelter for families with children, fresh meals seven days a week, one-on-one case management, employment services, advocacy with property managers, landlords, courts and partner agencies, community-resource connection and onsite child-supportive services such as Boys & Girls Club and children's health clinic supports.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For vulnerable and at-risk households with children experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County. Families should complete Family Housing Hub coordinated-entry screening; shelter placement depends on eligibility, safety, household fit and availability.

**Population Served**
Families with children experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County, including Mesa families when matched through Family Housing Hub.

**How to Best Connect**
Start with Family Housing Hub by calling 2-1-1, visiting 211arizona.org, dialing 877-211-8661 or calling UMOM/FHH at 602-595-8700. Do not assume direct arrival at the UMOM campus will produce placement.

**Important Information to Know**
Family Housing Hub screening does not guarantee a UMOM shelter bed. Keep phone contact active because shelter outreach may come from an unfamiliar number when a spot opens.

resources.name: Valleywise Health - Mesa Behavioral Health Specialty Clinic / Mercy Care Services
resources.description: Valleywise Mesa Behavioral Health Specialty Clinic provides specialized behavioral-health services for adults with Mercy Care RBHA benefits and a Serious Mental Illness designation, including assessments, medication management, counseling, peer support, case management, crisis intervention, and housing/employment support.
resources.address: Valleywise Community Health Center - Mesa, 950 E. Main St, Mesa, AZ 85203
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 7:00 AM-6:00 PM at Valleywise Community Health Center - Mesa location listing.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Specialized behavioral-health care through Valleywise's Mesa Behavioral Health Specialty Clinic, including assessments, individual service planning, medication management, nursing services, substance-abuse treatment, medication support, counseling, recovery education, peer support, health promotion, family support and education, housing and employment support, skills training, case management, psychoeducation, home-care training and crisis intervention.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Mesa specialty clinic currently accepts patients who are at least 18, have depression, anxiety, mania or psychosis, have Mercy Care RBHA benefits, and have a Serious Mental Illness designation. Valleywise says members must be enrolled with Mercy Care RBHA.

**Population Served**
Adults in Mesa/Maricopa County with Mercy Care RBHA benefits and an SMI designation who need ongoing specialty behavioral-health services.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Valleywise scheduling at 1-833-855-9973 or the Mesa Community Health Center at 602-655-6200. Ask specifically for Mesa Behavioral Health Specialty Clinic / Mercy Care Services and confirm Mercy Care RBHA enrollment requirements.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general outpatient clinic for all payers. Eligibility restrictions are consequential: adults need Mercy Care RBHA benefits and an SMI designation. The listed site is 950 E. Main St, not the Brown Road Behavioral Health Center.

resources.name: Mesa Public Schools Community Education · Mesa Parent University
resources.description: Mesa Public Schools Parent University offers free in-person and virtual classes for parents, caregivers, staff, and other adults, including parenting skills, academic topics, Spanish-language classes, and interpretation when requested.
resources.address: Community Education, 155 N. Center St., Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Community Education office: Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM; Friday 8:00 AM-4:15 PM
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Mesa Parent University provides free in-person and virtual classes to help adults build skills for stronger families and communities. Class types include parenting skills, suicide awareness, academic topics such as reading and kindergarten preparation, Spanish-language classes, and social-emotional learning. Classes include certification hours.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page states all adults are welcome and Mesa residency is not required. Participants must meet in-person and online class requirements. Childcare is not provided, and children are not allowed in classes unless the class specifically invites students.

**Population Served**
Parents, caregivers, Mesa Public Schools families, staff, and other adults who want parent education, academic family-support classes, or Spanish-language family learning.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Parent University registration form, email parent-u@mpsaz.org, or call 480-472-0233 for Parent University questions. Community Education is at 155 N. Center St., Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
The official Parent University page supports parenting, academic, and family learning classes; it does not support the submitted claims that Parent University itself offers GED preparation, English classes, or adult basic education. For GED or ESL, use Mesa Adult Education instead.

resources.name: Reclaim Your Future — marijuana-expungement resources
resources.description: Public education, downloadable petition materials and legal-aid provider links for Arizona marijuana expungement.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Public education, downloadable petition materials and legal-aid provider links for Arizona marijuana expungement.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The court remedy has offense, date and other legal requirements. Providers on the linked directory screen separately.

**Population Served**
People seeking information about qualifying Arizona marijuana records.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the current website’s materials and provider directory. Check the court’s current forms before filing.

**Important Information to Know**
The grant-funded direct legal-aid program concluded June 30, 2026. Do not treat old clinic announcements or its former phone intake as an active representation offer.

resources.name: Internal Revenue Service - lost CP565 ITIN assignment-notice recovery
resources.description: The IRS directs taxpayers who lost the CP565 notice containing their assigned ITIN to contact the agency, which can help restore proof of an existing Individual Taxpayer Identification Number without filing a new ITIN application.
resources.hours: IRS phone assistance hours vary by line and service; start with 800-829-1040 or the IRS contact route linked from the ITIN page.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The IRS provides the official contact route when a taxpayer cannot find the CP565 Notice of ITIN Assignment that showed an assigned ITIN. This can help recover evidence of an existing tax identification number.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people who already were assigned an ITIN and lost the CP565 notice. This is not a new ITIN application and is not for people eligible for a Social Security number.

**Population Served**
U.S. individual taxpayers with an assigned ITIN, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents who need proof of their federal tax identification number.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the IRS ITIN page's contact route or call IRS individual taxpayer assistance at 800-829-1040. Be prepared to verify identity and explain that the CP565 ITIN assignment notice is missing.

**Important Information to Know**
An ITIN is for federal tax purposes only. It does not authorize work, provide immigration status, qualify a person for Social Security benefits, or serve as identification outside the federal tax system. The IRS page does not promise a specific replacement format or timeline.

resources.name: Companion Pets in Crisis - Housing-barrier Support for Unhoused People and Veterans with Pets
resources.description: Companion Pets in Crisis is a Phoenix-based volunteer nonprofit that helps unhoused people and veterans keep pets healthy and with them by providing pet food, supplies, wellness support, vaccinations, spay/neuter vouchers, ESA documentation resources, and outreach that can reduce pet-related shelter or housing barriers.
resources.address: Phoenix, Arizona
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Pet food, essential pet supplies, vaccinations, wellness exams, spay/neuter vouchers, ESA documentation resources, street and shelter outreach, and other pet-retention help intended to reduce housing and shelter barriers for people with pets.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official site describes support for unhoused individuals and veterans with pets. Detailed eligibility, schedules, and service availability must be requested through CPIC's contact route.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness, especially veterans, who have companion animals in the Phoenix/Maricopa County area.

**How to Best Connect**
Email info@cpicaz.org or use the contact/resources routes on the CPIC website. Because no conventional client intake phone is published, confirm location, schedule, and available assistance before sending a client.

**Important Information to Know**
CPIC does not advertise direct housing placement. Its value is reducing pet-related barriers that can block shelter, housing, or service access.

resources.name: Redemption West Mesa · El Puente Community Center ESL and Civics Classes
resources.description: El Puente Community Center at Redemption West Mesa offers first-level ESL classes and civics classes for the Mesa community, especially the adult Hispanic community, with direct phone and email registration.
resources.address: 1818 E. Southern Ave., Suite 5, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: Class schedule not posted; call or email before attending.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
First-level ESL classes and civics classes in a community center focused on adult education, English communication, family, and community connection.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The page does not list formal eligibility rules or costs. It emphasizes service to Mesa and especially the Hispanic community; call or email to confirm whether classes are open to all community members and whether registration is required.

**Population Served**
Mesa residents, especially Spanish-speaking and Hispanic adults seeking beginning English and civics learning.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-524-8131 or email mesa@redemptionaz.com to register or ask questions. The center is at 1818 E. Southern Ave., Suite 5 in Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
A faith-based community education programme, not an immigration legal-services provider. Confirm the current class schedule, cost, language level, childcare and capacity. Ask whether the civics class addresses the citizenship preparation the person needs.

resources.name: The Worker / St. Joseph the Worker - Mesa Employment Services
resources.description: Free employment help from a Mesa office, including job-search planning, resumes, interview preparation, employer connections and screened assistance with work clothing, transportation, uniforms and tools.
resources.address: 1833 W Main St Suite 128, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Public website says clients can come into the Phoenix or Mesa office; specific daily office hours were not listed. Call before travel if timing matters.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free Mesa employment support includes job-search plans, employer referrals, résumés, interview coaching and professional attire. Qualifying newly employed participants may receive transport, uniforms or work tools. Staff can explain separate housing and reentry programmes, which have their own admissions.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Employment services are described as free for unemployed or underemployed people. Newly employed resource assistance generally requires recent permanent, direct-hire W2 employment, 25-40 hours weekly, at least minimum wage and employer verification from a company email. Ask about current resource rules and conviction-related employer restrictions.

**Population Served**
Job seekers and newly employed clients in Mesa and Maricopa County, including people with housing insecurity or justice-involvement barriers who need employment-based stabilization.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to the Mesa office at 1833 W Main St Suite 128 or call 602-755-5627. Bring a resume if available, a strong desire to work, photo ID and a cell phone if possible. Clients missing documents may need help from Homeless ID Project before employment can be secured. Newly employed clients should have employers send verification to jobs@theworkeraz.org.

**Important Information to Know**
This is the Mesa employment office, not Workforce Villages or MOM’s House housing. Job placement and material help are not guaranteed; eligibility, documentation, funding and employer conviction-related rules apply. General intake is described as walk-in, but confirm Mesa hours and resource-specific steps. A housing referral has separate admission requirements and is not emergency shelter.

resources.name: Mental Health America of Arizona - Free Mental-Health Peer Support Groups
resources.description: Mental Health America of Arizona runs free peer support groups for adults diagnosed with mental illness, including in-person Maricopa County groups and virtual groups for general mental health, bipolar/depression, and OCD support.
resources.hours: Group schedules vary. Current examples include virtual groups Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday, and Saturday and in-person groups in the Phoenix metropolitan area; call before attending.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free peer support groups offering shared experience, coping ideas, mutual acceptance, empowerment, information, education, and social connection for people living with mental illness. Current group types include bipolar/depression, OCD, and general mental-health peer groups, with several video-meeting options.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The in-person groups are listed for individuals age 18+ diagnosed with a mental illness. Family members and loved ones may come with a loved one for support. No registration is required for listed in-person groups; virtual group information is requested through the form.

**Population Served**
Adults living with mental illness in Maricopa County and Arizona residents who can access virtual peer groups, including Mesa residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Peer Support Group Coordinator Andy Arnowitz at 480-994-4407 before first attendance or to confirm meeting details. Use the support-groups page form for virtual/video group information.

**Important Information to Know**
These groups are peer support, not professional advice, therapy, medication management, or crisis care. Schedules, links, and facilitator availability can change, so call before attending.

resources.name: HA.P.I. — English Learning
resources.description: Community English-language instruction for Latino adults and families, with an emphasis on communication, employment readiness and participation in community life.
resources.address: 715 W. 5th St., Tempe, AZ 85281
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Community English-language instruction for Latino adults and families, with an emphasis on communication, employment readiness and participation in community life.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Contact the program about enrollment, current fees, language level, required documents and whether the chosen class accepts participants from the client’s city.

**Population Served**

Latino adult learners and families in the Tempe/East Valley area.

**How to Best Connect**

Call or email HA.P.I. before traveling to the Westside Multigenerational Center. Ask about the next class series and available evening instruction.

**Important Information to Know**

Older listings describe session fees and schedules that have not been reconfirmed. This is a language-learning program; admission does not establish eligibility for immigration benefits or college credit.

resources.name: A New Leaf Domestic Violence Court Advocacy
resources.description: A New Leaf's Court Advocacy Program helps survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, or stalking with Orders of Protection, Injunctions Against Harassment, safety planning, procedural guidance, and court-process support in English or Spanish.
