The base dental hygiene visit is listed as $70, with additional costs possible. Care generally takes four or more multi-hour appointments because students provide services under faculty supervision. This is not a full restorative or emergency dental clinic.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Health Services - 24-Hour Breastfeeding Hotline
resources.description: Arizona Department of Health Services/Arizona WIC promotes a 24-hour breastfeeding hotline for breastfeeding questions and support for Arizona residents.
resources.address: Statewide phone hotline
resources.hours: 24 hours a day by phone.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Arizona 24-hour Breastfeeding Hotline answers breastfeeding questions and offers telephone support for lactation and feeding concerns. Arizona WIC materials also connect families to nutrition education and breastfeeding support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The hotline is available to Arizona residents with breastfeeding questions. It is not a medical emergency service and does not replace pediatric, obstetric or emergency care.

**Population Served**
Pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding parents, infants and families in Arizona, including Mesa and Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 1-800-833-4642 any time. For urgent infant dehydration, weight loss, medication reaction, fever, breathing problems or other medical concerns, contact a medical provider or emergency care instead.

**Important Information to Know**
Use this as a telephone lactation support and referral resource. Interpreter availability, clinical scope and escalation options should be confirmed during the call if language or urgent medical concerns are present.

resources.name: AARP Foundation and City of Mesa - Experience Corps Mesa
resources.description: AARP Foundation Experience Corps Mesa, hosted by the City of Mesa, trains adults age 50 and older as literacy tutors in select Mesa Public Schools, offering meaningful service, structure and social connection.
resources.address: 64 E. First St., Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Volunteer literacy tutoring program that trains adults over 50 on an evidence-based curriculum and places them in select Mesa Public Schools for one-on-one tutoring with elementary students.

**Eligibility Requirements**
School staff select children for tutoring; families should ask the child’s school about participation rather than enroll directly. Volunteer tutors must be 50+, hold a high-school diploma/GED, pass background and basic-literacy checks, attend 25 hours of annual training, and commit at least five hours weekly during the school year.

**Population Served**
Adults age 50 and older seeking meaningful volunteer service and social connection, and Mesa elementary students selected by school staff for literacy tutoring.

**How to Best Connect**
For child reading support, contact the child’s school first. For volunteering or participating-site information, call 480-644-5050 or email education.info@mesaaz.gov. Prospective tutors attend an information session and complete an application and interview.

**Important Information to Know**
Tutoring occurs during the school day at selected Mesa Public Schools, not an open tutoring clinic. Tutoring volunteers are not paid employees; ask about the current school-year schedule and placements.

resources.name: Modivcare - Arizona Facility Transportation Resources
resources.description: Modivcare's Arizona facility resources page gives medical facilities processes and forms for arranging covered non-emergency medical transportation, including single trips, standing orders, mileage reimbursement forms, and facility coordination phone/fax numbers.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Facility-facing non-emergency medical transportation scheduling resources for covered Modivcare clients in Arizona. The page includes TripCare, single-trip request forms, standing orders, mileage reimbursement forms, discharge arrangements, and facility coordinator confirmation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The patient must be covered by a plan or program that uses Modivcare for transportation. Facilities must use the appropriate reservation process and forms; standing orders must be completed by a facility representative.

**Population Served**
Patients in Arizona whose health plan or facility-arranged benefit contracts with Modivcare, including people needing wheelchair, stretcher, bariatric, discharge, dialysis, mental health, or other medical transportation when covered.

**How to Best Connect**
Facilities can call the Arizona facility line at 888-589-6163 or fax single-trip/standing-order forms to 888-589-6164. Patients should verify with their health plan or facility whether Modivcare is the assigned transportation broker.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general public ride line. Plan coverage varies, and the facility process is mainly for medical providers, hospitals, dialysis centers, nursing homes, mental health facilities, and substance-abuse clinics arranging trips for covered clients.

resources.name: Jewish Family & Children's Service - Shelter Without Walls
resources.description: Jewish Family & Children's Service Shelter Without Walls is a confidential nonresidential program helping domestic-violence survivors live independently and safely through safety planning, referrals, lay legal advocacy, court accompaniment, counseling, support groups, immigration assistance, and case management.
resources.address: JFCS main office: 4747 N. 7th St., Suite 100, Phoenix, AZ 85014; arrange service location by phone.
resources.hours: Call 602-452-4640 or Spanish assistance 602-534-3087 for intake; public hours are not posted.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Nonresidential domestic-violence survivor services include individualized safety planning, shelter and community referrals, crime-victim referrals, employment readiness, lay legal advocacy, protective-order help, court preparation and accompaniment, domestic-violence education, support groups, counseling, immigration assistance, and case management.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For survivors of domestic violence who want to live independently and need support doing so safely. Mesa residents should call to confirm service-area fit and whether support is remote, mobile, or requires travel.

**Population Served**
Survivors of all ages, faiths, gender orientations, and backgrounds, including Spanish-speaking survivors and survivors with children.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-452-4640 or 602-534-3087 for assistance in Spanish. Cases are handled confidentially.

**Important Information to Know**
This programme supports survivors living or seeking to live safely outside shelter. It offers shelter referrals and lay legal advocacy, not an emergency shelter bed or guaranteed attorney representation. Intake is confidential; arrange the appropriate service location and format before travel.

resources.name: VALLEYLIFE - Vocational Services / Ticket to Work / Pre-ETS
resources.description: VALLEYLIFE provides vocational services for people with disabilities, including supported employment, job development and placement, work adjustment training, job coaching, group and individual supported employment, Ticket to Work benefits coaching and Pre-Employment Transition Services for students with disabilities.
resources.address: 1142 W. Hatcher Rd., Phoenix, AZ 85021
resources.hours: Main office Monday-Friday 8:30 AM-4:30 PM. Pre-ETS classes are listed Monday, Wednesday and Thursday 1:00-1:45 PM; confirm current schedule before attending.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
VALLEYLIFE helps people with disabilities obtain and maintain employment through supported employment, work adjustment training, job development and placement, job coaching, group and individual supported employment, benefits counseling, Ticket to Work services and Pre-Employment Transition Services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Routes vary by service. Supported Employment is available to people referred by Mercy Care; work adjustment, job development and coaching are available to people referred by Vocational Rehabilitation; group and individual supported employment are provided to people referred by DDD. Ticket to Work is for Social Security disability beneficiaries ages 18-64. Pre-ETS participants must be students in secondary, postsecondary or another recognized education program and ages 14-22.

**Population Served**
People with disabilities in the Phoenix metro area who need employment support, including students with disabilities and adults connected through Mercy Care, Vocational Rehabilitation, DDD or Ticket to Work.

**How to Best Connect**
For vocational program questions, contact Jennifer Baier at 602-216-6393 or jbaier@valleylifeaz.org. For Ticket to Work, call 602-216-6393 or email tickettowork@valleylifeaz.org. The main office is at 1142 W. Hatcher Rd. in Phoenix.

**Important Information to Know**
Referral and funding rules matter. Ask which pathway applies before promising service, especially for Mesa clients who may need VR, DDD, Mercy Care or Ticket to Work authorization. The page lists a main office phone of 602-371-0806 as well as vocational contact phone 602-216-6393.

resources.name: Arizona DES Division of Child Support Services - Child Support Services / AZCARES Portal
resources.description: Arizona DES Division of Child Support Services helps parents and caretakers establish paternity, establish support orders, and collect child, medical, and spousal support from parents with court orders.
resources.address: PO Box 40458, Phoenix, AZ 85067
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
State child-support services for parents and caretakers, including help getting a child support order, collecting child, medical, and spousal support when there is a court order, and establishing paternity for children of unmarried parents.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Available to Arizona parents and caretakers who need IV-D child support services or have an Arizona child support case. Case-specific rules, documents, and fees may depend on the family situation and court order.

**Population Served**
Arizona parents, caretakers, and children, including Mesa and Maricopa County families whose household stability depends on formal support collection.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through the DES child support page or AZ Child Support Portal, or call 602-252-4045 or 1-800-882-4151. Mail correspondence can be sent to PO Box 40458, Phoenix, AZ 85067.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not emergency cash assistance. It can help establish or enforce ongoing support, but timing depends on the legal and case process.

resources.name: Aster Aging - Benefits Enrollment Center and Outreach/Social Services
resources.description: Aster Aging provides free Benefits Enrollment Center help and outreach/social services in Mesa, including benefits screening, application assistance, resource navigation and aging/chronic-condition support for older adults and people with disabilities.
resources.address: 45 W. University Dr., Suite A, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Call or use the contact form to arrange an appointment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Aster's Benefits Enrollment Center helps people on Medicare connect with resources for health care, prescriptions, food, utilities and more, including Medicare Part D Extra Help, Medicare Savings Program, Medicaid/AHCCCS, SNAP, LIHEAP and City of Mesa Utility Assistance. Outreach & Social Services also offers needs assessments, information and referral, food supplement programs, resource navigation and education related to aging needs and chronic health conditions.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Benefits Enrollment Center page focuses on individuals on Medicare and states Aster can help older adults and people with disabilities learn about public benefits, be screened for eligibility and receive enrollment assistance. Specific benefits have their own age, income, disability, residency and documentation rules.

**Population Served**
Mesa and East Valley older adults, people with disabilities, caregivers and low-income households seeking benefits or resource navigation.

**How to Best Connect**
For Benefits Enrollment Center help, call 480-634-1659 or complete the benefits contact form. For Outreach & Social Services, call 480-962-5612 or complete the social services contact form. Aster's main office is at 45 W. University Dr., Suite A, Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
Aster helps screen, apply and navigate; the agency administering each benefit decides eligibility and approval. Bring information about current benefits, Medicare status, income, household and the bill or need. People not on Medicare should ask whether the current Benefits Enrollment Center scope covers their request, or use broader outreach support.

resources.name: New Freedom · Core Re-Entry Program and Outpatient Transition Services
resources.description: New Freedom provides justice-affected recovery and reentry programming, including a 90-day core reentry program, safe housing, meals, therapy, peer support, case management, outpatient services, DUI services, relapse-prevention groups, transportation supports, vocational training and women-specific reentry services.
resources.address: 2532 W Peoria Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85029; women's facility contact route listed separately
resources.hours: Program hours vary; contact admissions/referral before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
New Freedom offers a 90-day residential Core Re-Entry programme with housing, meals, therapy, peer support and case management. Enrolled participants may receive clothing/hygiene, release transportation, document help, employment and housing support, GED/technology help and legal/fine-mitigation advocacy. Separate outpatient services offer counseling, groups, peer support and case management, including early-release Transition Bill programming and Freedom Beyond Felonies. DUI services are a separate self-pay route.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Justice-affected adults are screened for the appropriate programme. The Core FAQ excludes required sex-offender registration and arson charges and lists Health Choice Arizona, Mercy Care and Arizona Indian Health Plan; confirm current coverage and which restrictions apply to the specific outpatient track. Transition Bill programming is for qualifying early release under SB 1067. Freedom Beyond Felonies serves people with at least 15 total years incarcerated. DUI services have separate conviction and payment requirements.

**Population Served**
Justice-affected adults returning from incarceration, including men and women in gender-specific cohorts, people with DUI convictions, women needing a women-specific facility, and people with long incarceration histories.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the official referral link. Incarcerated people can write to ATTN: New Freedom, PO Box 84107, Phoenix, AZ 85071. Outpatient: 602-584-7531 or transitionsprogram@newfreedomaz.com. Women’s facility inquiries: 602-859-4053 or Communications@newfreedomaz.com. New Freedom Project material-support questions: connect@nfproject.org. Ask which location and admission route fits before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
Residential housing and basic-needs help require programme acceptance; they are not a public shelter, clothing bank or general employment centre. Outpatient participation does not automatically include housing or all residential benefits. Confirm clinical fit, offense restrictions, payer authorization, release transportation and current capacity. This is not an established general-public detox or opioid-treatment clinic.

resources.name: Arizona Operating Engineers — Apprenticeships
resources.description: Registered operating-engineer training combining work experience with classroom instruction for construction equipment careers.
resources.address: Training center: 10797 W. Randolph Rd., Casa Grande, AZ 85194
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Registered operating-engineer training combining work experience with classroom instruction for construction equipment careers.

**Eligibility Requirements**

The provider requests a high-school diploma or GED and driver’s license or photo ID. Confirm age, screening, assessment, current selection and document requirements. Suitable transportation is necessary because assignments may be anywhere in Arizona.

**Population Served**

Arizona applicants pursuing operating-engineer careers who can reach statewide worksites and Casa Grande instruction.

**How to Best Connect**

Contact the apprenticeship office or download the application packet. Ask about current intake and required travel.

**Important Information to Know**

The published program includes 80 hours of pre-training, approximately 432 classroom hours and at least three years/6,000 work hours. Application does not guarantee an immediate assignment; confirm costs, wages and lodging or travel needs.

resources.name: Community Bridges, Inc. - Center for Hope / Arizona Bridge to Recovery reentry lead
resources.description: Community Bridges operates Mesa behavioral-health and substance-use services including Center for Hope and Arizona Bridge to Recovery on Bellview, with 24/7 access-to-care and appointment lines; the specific named ReEntry Program at Center for Hope could not be confirmed on current public pages.
resources.address: 554 S Bellview, Mesa, AZ 85204; administration 1855 W Baseline Rd #101, Mesa, AZ 85202
resources.hours: 24/7 Access to Care Line; appointment scheduling available through CBI.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Community Bridges provides a behavioral-health and substance-use continuum including inpatient care, residential services, crisis stabilization, health homes, peer support, shelters/outreach, supportive housing, and community education/outreach. Current Arizona locations list Center for Hope and Arizona Bridge to Recovery at 554 S Bellview in Mesa.

**Eligibility Requirements**
CBI eligibility depends on the specific behavioral-health, substance-use, crisis, residential, or housing service requested. Public pages do not confirm the submitted named ReEntry Program at Center for Hope or its admission rules.

**Population Served**
People needing behavioral-health, substance-use, crisis, inpatient, residential, or recovery support in Arizona, including Mesa-area clients. Justice-involved people may be appropriate if they meet the clinical or program criteria, but the current public page does not define a dedicated reentry track.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the 24/7 Access to Care Line at 877-931-9142 or appointments at 888-224-6593; email scheduling@cbridges.com for scheduling. Ask specifically whether CBI currently operates a ReEntry Program at Center for Hope and what referral route, payer, clinical criteria, or supervision documentation is required.

**Important Information to Know**
This resource is retained for administrator resolution because the CBI organization, Mesa sites, Center for Hope, Arizona Bridge to Recovery, and intake lines are supported, but the exact named ReEntry Program at Center for Hope and its admission route are not established on current public pages. Do not describe it as guaranteed reentry housing or unrestricted placement without confirmation.
resources.resolutionReason: The provider and Mesa locations are credible and actionable, but targeted official checks did not confirm the specific named ReEntry Program at Center for Hope or its admission path; responsible referral requires CBI confirmation of the exact program identity and eligibility.

resources.name: Behavioral Systems Southwest, Inc. · Phoenix Residential Re-Entry Center
resources.description: Behavioral Systems Southwest operates the Phoenix Residential Re-Entry Center, a 70-bed residential reentry center contracted through the Federal Bureau of Prisons and U.S. Probation for eligible federal justice-system clients.
resources.address: 2846 E. Roosevelt Road, Phoenix, AZ 85008
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Residential and nonresidential reintegration services using cognitive-behavioral and skill-building approaches. The Phoenix location is described as a 70-bed residential reentry center contracted through the Federal Bureau of Prisons and U.S. Probation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
This is a restricted federal placement pathway, not open self-referral. Eligibility and assignment are controlled by the Federal Bureau of Prisons or U.S. Probation.

**Population Served**
Eligible federal justice-system clients in the District of Arizona who are placed into the Phoenix residential reentry center or related services.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-273-6293 for the Phoenix location, but clients should also work through their BOP case manager, U.S. Probation officer or assigned federal reentry contact. The listed address is 2846 E. Roosevelt Road, Phoenix, AZ 85008.

**Important Information to Know**
A missionary or client cannot assume walk-in admission. Staff should confirm the exact Phoenix unit and number for a particular federal referral because directory entries may vary.

resources.name: Father Matters — Workforce Assistance
resources.description: Job-search, application, résumé and interview assistance, technology access, career guidance and help addressing work-clothing or transportation barriers.
resources.address: 3146 E. Wier Ave., Room 28, Phoenix, AZ 85040
resources.hours: Monday–Thursday, 9 AM–4 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Job-search, application, résumé and interview assistance, technology access, career guidance and help addressing work-clothing or transportation barriers.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Contact Father Matters about appointments, intake requirements and availability of practical support; the public program page does not state a single income or residency test.

**Population Served**

Men and women seeking employment support in the Phoenix area.

**How to Best Connect**

Arrange an in-person, virtual or phone appointment. Ask for Workforce Assistance; the published location is inside Brooks Community School.

**Important Information to Know**

This general workforce service is distinct from the pre-release reentry program. Support items and job opportunities depend on individual circumstances and availability.

resources.name: Lexington Learning Center - Mesa Adult Day, In-Home, Respite, and Employment Services
resources.description: Lexington Learning Center provides Mesa adult day programs, home- and community-based services, respite, habilitation, attendant care, and employment services for people with developmental disabilities.
resources.address: 1555 S. Gilbert Rd., Ste. 108 and Ste. 111, Mesa, AZ 85204; 9132 E. Southern Ave., Mesa, AZ 85209
resources.email: General: info@lexingtonservices.com; Hampton day programme: hamptondta@lexingtonlearning.com; Ellsworth day programme: ellsworthdta@lexingtonlearning.com
resources.hours: Call or submit the enrollment form; provider schedules, transportation, and program openings vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
DDD-funded adult day programmes, independent-living skills, attendant care, habilitation, respite and home/community-based supports. Employment options include Pathways/Transition to Employment, group supported employment and individual supported employment; ask which programme and site fit the member’s plan.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are for members with developmental disabilities. Adult day services are described as DDD-funded, and in-home, respite, habilitation, and employment supports may require DDD authorization, an individual plan, provider fit, and available staffing.

**Population Served**
People with developmental disabilities in Mesa who need adult day, in-home/community support, caregiver respite, habilitation, or supported employment services.

**How to Best Connect**
Call in-home services at 480-447-8229, Mesa-Hampton day program at 480-788-6107, Mesa-Ellsworth day program at 480-401-2527, employment programs at 480-401-2558, or the general line at 480-900-1009. Families may also use the enrollment form on the Learning Center page.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm DDD authorization, current openings, transportation boundaries, behavioral or medical support capacity, and which Mesa site fits the person's needs. Employment services and day programs are separate contacts.

resources.name: Cox Communications - Lifeline Home Phone and Internet Service
resources.description: Cox Lifeline applies the federal Lifeline discount to qualifying Cox phone or internet service where available, with eligibility verified through the National Verifier or state administrator and one federal Lifeline benefit per household.
resources.hours: Online address check and National Verifier qualification; service steps are provided after entering the service address.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Cox Lifeline can lower the monthly cost of qualifying Cox phone or internet service for eligible low-income consumers where Cox Lifeline is available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility may be based on SNAP, SSI, Federal Public Housing Assistance, Veterans Pension or Survivors Benefit, Medicaid, qualifying Tribal programs, or other state-specific criteria. Consumers must be qualified by the National Verifier or a state administrator and may receive only one federal Lifeline benefit per household.

**Population Served**
Low-income households in Cox service areas where Lifeline phone or internet discounts are available, including potentially eligible Maricopa County addresses after address screening.

**How to Best Connect**
Start on the Cox Lifeline page and enter the home service address. Follow the steps to qualify through the National Verifier or state process, then complete the Cox-specific application steps provided for that address.

**Important Information to Know**
Cox states Lifeline discounts for phone and internet are available only in limited areas where Cox has recently deployed new service and received federal funding; address availability must be checked. The Lifeline benefit is non-transferable and limited to one discount per household.

resources.name: City of Mesa Housing Authority - Family Unification Program
resources.description: City of Mesa Housing Authority's Family Unification Program is a special Housing Choice Voucher pathway for families whose child-welfare involvement is affected by inadequate housing and for eligible foster-care-transition youth who are homeless or at risk of homelessness.
resources.address: 200 S Center St, Building 1, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 7:30 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Special-purpose Housing Choice Vouchers for eligible Family Unification Program families and youth. FUP family vouchers help preserve or reunify families when lack of adequate housing is a primary factor in child welfare placement or delayed reunification; FUP/FYI youth vouchers help eligible former or transitioning foster youth with rental assistance and related supports.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Mesa states the program assists families involved in the child welfare system who face unstable housing and homelessness. It also serves youth ages 18 to 24 who have left foster care and lack adequate shelter, are homeless, or are at risk of homelessness. Access is through Department of Child Safety/caseworker referral.

**Population Served**
Mesa families involved with child welfare because of housing instability and eligible former or transitioning foster youth.

**How to Best Connect**
This is not a public walk-in voucher application. Contact the Department of Child Safety caseworker for referral information. For Mesa Housing Authority questions, call 480-644-3536 or email hcvwaitinglist@mesaaz.gov.

**Important Information to Know**
Referral availability, voucher supply and detailed eligibility must be confirmed by the caseworker and Mesa Housing Authority. Do not present this as an open general Section 8 application.

resources.name: U.S.VETS Phoenix - Phoenix Career Center and Workforce Development
resources.description: U.S.VETS Phoenix Workforce Development and Career Center helps veterans translate military experience into civilian employment through career counseling, resume and interview help, job-search support, employer connections, training referrals and supportive employment needs.
resources.address: 3507 N Central Ave, Suite 200, Phoenix, AZ 85012; Career Center listing also references Phoenix service sites
resources.hours: Supportive Services for Veteran Families hours are Monday-Friday 7:00 AM-4:00 PM and by appointment; career center hours should be confirmed with the workforce contact.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
U.S.VETS Phoenix offers workforce development, a Career Center and career counseling for veterans. Services may include translating military experience to civilian employment, career development planning, job search, interview preparation, resume help, training and certification connections, employer relationships, transportation, licensure or exam fees, tools, uniforms and professional work attire when available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are for veterans. Some services are prioritized for veterans who are homeless, at risk of homelessness, low-income or enrolled in U.S.VETS housing/supportive programs. A DD-214 or service letter may be required for some Career Center services.

**Population Served**
Veterans in Greater Phoenix and Maricopa County, including Mesa veterans seeking employment help, especially those experiencing homelessness or housing instability.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact the Phoenix workforce development contact, Tera Calhoun, at 602-717-0206 or tcalhoun@usvetsinc.org. Veterans needing broader Phoenix services can call the main office at 602-717-6682.

**Important Information to Know**
The public page supports current workforce development, but exact Career Center site, appointment rules and available supportive items should be confirmed before sending a client.

resources.name: Revive Recovery Center - Mesa Addiction PHP and Intensive Outpatient Treatment
resources.description: Revive Recovery Center provides Mesa partial hospitalization, intensive outpatient, alcohol treatment, substance-abuse treatment, admissions, and insurance verification for people with substance-use and mental-health needs.
resources.address: 127 W Juanita Ave, Suite 110, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00am-5:00pm.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Partial hospitalization, intensive outpatient treatment, alcohol treatment, substance-abuse treatment, mental-health disorder treatment, admissions support, and insurance verification from a Mesa clinic.

**Eligibility Requirements**
People seeking outpatient or day-treatment addiction/mental-health care may inquire. Clinical fit, age range, medication support, insurance, and schedule are determined through admissions.

**Population Served**
Mesa and East Valley clients seeking substance-use and mental-health treatment at PHP or IOP levels of care.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 866-311-7152 or use the contact form. The Mesa clinic is at 127 W Juanita Ave, Suite 110, Mesa, AZ 85210, with listed office hours Monday-Friday 8:00am-5:00pm.

**Important Information to Know**
The official contact page supports PHP/IOP and substance-use services but does not fully answer medication-treatment or payer details. Confirm insurance, current groups, and whether outside prescribers are needed.

resources.name: Crossroads - Red Mountain Campus and Right Track Residential Treatment
resources.description: Crossroads' Residential Right Track program is a 45-day structured residential addiction-treatment program for adults, with admissions assessment, counseling, peer support, recovery meetings and aftercare planning.
resources.address: Crossroads admissions: 2002 E Osborn Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85016; Red Mountain Campus: 143 S Center St, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Admissions and assessment hours should be confirmed before travel; after-hours contact is available by phone/text.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Residential Right Track is a 45-day residential addiction-treatment program with assessment, individual and group counseling, peer mentoring, recovery meetings, life-skills and relapse-prevention work, and aftercare planning. It is housing-related because the client lives in treatment; it is not general emergency shelter or permanent housing.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adults age 18 and older seeking help for substance use, alcohol use, co-occurring mental-health needs or repeated return to use may inquire. Admission depends on assessment, clinical fit, insurance or funding, and bed availability.

**Population Served**
Adults in Arizona seeking residential recovery support. Crossroads has multiple campuses; the Mesa Red Mountain campus is for men, and Crossroads also describes services for pregnant women through its broader network.

**How to Best Connect**
Call admissions at 602-263-5242 or email admissions@thecrossroadsinc.org. Ask which campus is appropriate, whether detox is needed first, what funding or insurance is accepted, and whether a bed is available before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
Residential treatment is not general shelter or permanent housing. Crossroads does not currently operate a detox unit and can refer for detox or a different level of care when needed. Confirm campus, assessment schedule, insurance, scholarship/block-grant options and bed availability through admissions before travel.

resources.name: Ability360 - This Is MY Life
resources.description: Ability360 This Is MY Life teaches self-determination, self-advocacy, rights, goal-setting, and problem-solving skills for people with developmental disabilities in the DDD system.
resources.address: 5025 E. Washington St., Suite 200, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: Call or email the program manager; Ability360 main office hours are Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
This Is MY Life provides skill training in self-determination, making choices, goal planning, problem solving, rights and responsibilities, and self-advocacy at DDD planning meetings and in daily life. Official page: https://ability360.org/this-is-my-life/.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is for people with developmental disabilities in the Arizona DES Division of Developmental Disabilities system. The page advises asking a DDD Support Coordinator for a referral or contacting the program directly.

**Population Served**
People with developmental disabilities who need support building self-advocacy, self-determination, rights knowledge, and goal-setting skills.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the person's DDD Support Coordinator for a referral, or contact Lynn Black, This Is MY Life Program Manager, at 602-443-0729 voicemail or LynnB@ability360.org.

**Important Information to Know**
The program is DDD-linked and should not be treated as a general counseling or legal-rights representation program. The official material describes it as free and no DDD service dollars used, but current referral status should be confirmed.

resources.name: Tumbleweed Center for Youth Development - Arizona successor-program lead
resources.description: Historical Arizona Tumbleweed youth-services lead. Current public evidence shows the submitted tumbleweedprogram.org site is a Billings, Montana provider, while UMOM historical material says UMOM absorbed Arizona Tumbleweed youth programs in 2017. No current Arizona Tumbleweed drop-in intake was established.
resources.address: Current Arizona successor location not established; UMOM main campus 3333 E Van Buren St, Phoenix, AZ 85008
resources.hours: Current Arizona successor-program hours not established.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Historically, Tumbleweed Center for Youth Development served Phoenix-area homeless youth and young adults with resource centers, emergency and transitional housing, life counseling and related services. Current Arizona service under the Tumbleweed name was not established in this check.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Historically served youth and young adults, but current Arizona successor eligibility, ages and intake route are unresolved.

**Population Served**
Potentially youth and young adults experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County, but the current program identity and access route require administrator confirmation.

**How to Best Connect**
Do not use tumbleweedprogram.org for Arizona referrals; that site lists Billings, Montana. Contact UMOM or Maricopa County youth homeless-service access routes to identify the current local youth pathway.

**Important Information to Know**
This is retained only as a needs-resolution lead. Public evidence cannot support sending Mesa youth to a current Tempe/Phoenix Tumbleweed drop-in center. The old Tumbleweed identity should not be represented as current until UMOM or another official local source confirms the successor route.
resources.resolutionReason: Needs resolution: the submitted Tumbleweed website is a Montana provider, while UMOM historical material shows Arizona Tumbleweed programs were absorbed by UMOM; no current Arizona intake, address or service model was confirmed.

resources.name: EEOC Phoenix District Office - discrimination charge intake
resources.description: The EEOC Phoenix District Office accepts employment-discrimination charge intake by telephone, video, in-person appointments, and the EEOC Public Portal, with accommodations for people who cannot use the portal.
resources.address: 3300 N. Central Ave., Suite 690, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.hours: Phoenix office Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM. Appointments are strongly recommended.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Federal employment-discrimination charge intake, intake interviews by telephone, video, or in person, Public Portal scheduling, and information about next steps for filing a charge.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The issue must fall within EEOC employment-discrimination jurisdiction and deadlines. Strict filing deadlines apply, and intake or investigation is not private legal representation.

**Population Served**
Arizona workers and job applicants, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents, with potential employment discrimination claims.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the EEOC Public Portal to schedule an intake appointment by phone, video, or in person. Call 800-669-4000 if the portal is inaccessible or difficult to use. Deaf or hard-of-hearing callers may use 844-234-5122 by videophone or 800-669-6820 TTY. Walk-ins without appointments are screened, but appointments receive priority.

**Important Information to Know**
Charge deadlines can be short. The EEOC process is an administrative enforcement route, not a private attorney-client representation.

resources.name: Dignity Health Early Childhood Oral Health Program / First Teeth First
resources.description: First Things First Southeast Maricopa-listed oral health program from Dignity Community Care/Chandler Regional Medical Center providing child tooth-decay checks, fluoride protection, dental referrals, and oral-health checks for pregnant people.
resources.address: CARE Campus outreach site: 466 S. Bellview St., Mesa, AZ 85204; confirm session location.
resources.hours: Scheduled outreach sessions; call for current dates.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Early-childhood oral-health screening, education, fluoride prevention and dental referrals, including oral-health checks for pregnant participants. CARE Campus lists free screening, education and referral sessions through this partnership.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The CARE Campus listing serves expectant mothers and children through age five who are not enrolled in kindergarten. Other outreach sessions have their own regional, age and appointment requirements; confirm the family’s eligibility with the programme.

**Population Served**
Pregnant participants and families with young children who qualify for the current East Valley or CARE Campus outreach session.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-728-5709 for the Dignity early-childhood oral-health programme. For CARE Campus dates and registration at 466 S. Bellview St., Mesa, call 480-833-8987.

**Important Information to Know**
This is screening and prevention, not full adult restorative dental care. Confirm the current session, any cost, registration, fluoride availability and referral process before travel.

resources.name: Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community Family Advocacy Center
resources.description: Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community Family Advocacy Center provides a coordinated response for victims of domestic violence, child abuse, sexual assault, elder abuse, and other family-related violence, including advocacy, protective-order help, relocation assistance, counseling, and case management.
resources.address: 10005 E Osborn Rd, Scottsdale, AZ 85256
resources.hours: Call the SRPMIC main number or Family Advocacy Center contact route before visiting; public pages do not state walk-in hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Coordinated services for victims of domestic violence, child abuse, sexual assault, elder abuse, and other family-related violence. Services listed include victim advocacy and support, help with protective orders, emergency relocation assistance, trauma counseling, case management, collaboration with law enforcement and prosecutors, and forensic interviews for children who are victims or witnesses of crime.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Public pages describe services for Community victims and families but do not fully state whether services are limited by tribal membership, residence, case jurisdiction, or referral source. Confirm eligibility before routing someone who is not connected to the Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community.

**Population Served**
Victims and families connected with the Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community and nearby tribal-service systems in Maricopa County, including domestic-violence and family-violence survivors.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-362-7400 and ask for the Family Advocacy Center. Confirm appointment, eligibility, and safe contact before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general public Mesa domestic-violence program. It is a tribal-service pathway near Mesa/Scottsdale, and eligibility or case jurisdiction should be screened first.

resources.name: Oxford House - Mesa recovery residences
resources.description: Oxford House provides self-run, self-supported sober living homes for people in recovery; Mesa-area houses should be checked through the official vacancy locator or application route rather than relying on stale individual-house details.
resources.phone: Use official house contacts from oxfordvacancies.com; Oxford House national 800-689-6411
resources.address: Use official vacancy locator for current Mesa houses; submitted lead named Sundance at 5028 E Dartmouth St, Mesa, AZ 85205 but current official vacancy listing did not confirm that house in this check
resources.hours: House contacts and vacancies change frequently; use the official vacancy locator or online application.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Peer-run sober living in self-supporting Oxford Houses where residents share expenses, maintain a drug- and alcohol-free home, interview applicants and support each other in recovery.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be in recovery, be able to live drug- and alcohol-free, not be disruptive and pay their equal share of expenses. A house interview and member vote are part of the admission process.

**Population Served**
People in recovery from substance-use disorder who need sober shared housing in Mesa or the surrounding area. Some houses are for men, some for women and some may serve women with children; the exact house must be checked in the live vacancy locator.

**How to Best Connect**
Use oxfordvacancies.com to find current Mesa houses and openings, call the contact person for any house with a vacancy, or submit the official online application to all nearby houses with openings.

**Important Information to Know**
The submitted Sundance address/phone and gender details conflict with later directory snapshots and were not confirmed on the live official vacancy page during this check. Treat Sundance as a lead, but refer through Oxford's official vacancy locator or application route.

resources.name: Phoenix 32nd Street VA Clinic
resources.description: Phoenix VA clinic offering primary care, mental-health counseling, ophthalmology and low-vision rehabilitation for eligible veterans.
resources.address: 400 North 32 nd Street, Phoenix, AZ 85008
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Primary care, mental-health counseling and support, ophthalmology, and low-vision or blindness rehabilitation. Contact the clinic about the required department, referral and appointment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
VA healthcare eligibility and any specialty assessment or referral requirements apply. Mental-health access can include people not yet enrolled; ask VA about the appropriate route.

**Population Served**
Eligible veterans, including Mesa residents able to travel to Phoenix for specialist care.

**How to Best Connect**
Call VA Health Connect at 888-214-7264 to ask about the clinic or an appointment. The clinic is at 400 North 32 nd Street; service hours vary.

**Important Information to Know**
A clinic’s operating hours do not mean every specialty accepts walk-ins. Confirm the specific department, referral and appointment before travelling. Same-day mental-health access is described separately.

resources.name: Lutheran Social Services of the Southwest · Refugee Women's Empowerment Program
resources.description: Lutheran Social Services of the Southwest's Refugee Women's Empowerment Program offers refugee women skill-building, education, and socialization through sewing, computer, vocational English, health, nutrition, leadership, childcare training, and on-site childcare in Phoenix and Tucson.
resources.address: 3636 N. Central Ave., Suite 300, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.hours: Contact LSS-SW for current class schedules and enrollment process.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Sewing classes, computer classes, vocational English classes, women's health classes, nutrition classes, leadership development, library tours, on-site childcare, Kith & Kin childcare training, in-home childcare certification, cloth diaper classes, babysitting certification, and related skill-building and socialization supports.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is specifically tailored to refugee women. Current enrollment, referral requirements, whether services are limited to existing LSS-SW refugee clients, and class availability should be confirmed directly.

**Population Served**
Refugee women in Phoenix and Tucson communities, including women from Afghanistan, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Somalia, Burma, Cuba, and other refugee communities.

**How to Best Connect**
Call LSS-SW at 480-396-3795 or use the contact route on the Women's Empowerment page. Ask about current Phoenix classes, eligibility, language support, childcare availability, and whether a Mesa-area refugee woman can enroll.

**Important Information to Know**
This is refugee women’s education, integration and skill-building, not immigration legal representation or guaranteed job placement. Use LSS-SW programme intake for enrollment; RefugeeMade sales are a separate shopping route. Confirm the current class site and childcare before travel.

resources.name: Saddleback Communications — Tribal Lifeline and Link Up
resources.description: Offers telephone-service discounts through the provider serving the Salt River community.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Offers telephone-service discounts through the provider serving the Salt River community.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Reside in the provider’s service area on qualifying Tribal lands and meet the applicable income or benefit criteria. Tribal-land eligibility is based on the address, not an assumption about ethnicity.

**Population Served**
Eligible households in Saddleback’s Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community service area.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact Saddleback for the current Tribal Lifeline or Link Up application and documentation instructions. The provider lists an office at 10190 E. McKellips Road, Scottsdale.

**Important Information to Know**
Lifeline is limited to one benefit per household. Link Up and Lifeline do not pay old telephone debt. Ask about the exact current discount, service and installation terms; older printed income-dollar tables are not current guidelines.

resources.name: Olive Branch Community of Hope - Food Closet
resources.description: Eastern Phoenix food closet offering no-cost monthly food boxes, emergency bags and homeless bags through Olive Branch Community of Hope and Mount of Olives Lutheran Church.
resources.address: 3546 E Thomas Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85018
resources.hours: Thursday food closet distribution; official page lists Thursday 1:00-4:00 PM and also references 12:30-3:30 PM. Confirm current arrival window before travel.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Olive Branch Community of Hope offers no-cost monthly food boxes through the Food Closet at Mount of Olives Lutheran Church. The page also names emergency bags and homeless bags as other food opportunities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page says monthly food boxes are available at no cost to community members. New guests who are Arizona residents are asked to provide picture ID.

**Population Served**
Community members needing food assistance in the eastern Phoenix area, including people who may need emergency or homeless food bags.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to the distribution center at 3546 E Thomas Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85018, located to the left of the sanctuary, during Thursday operational hours. Email obcohfoodcloset@gmail.com for food-closet questions.

**Important Information to Know**
The official page contains two Thursday time windows, so confirm the current distribution window before sending someone from Mesa. This is a reserve option outside Mesa.

resources.name: Maricopa County Family Treatment Court
resources.description: Maricopa County Family Treatment Court is a voluntary treatment-court pathway for parents with open dependency cases involving substance-use allegations, supporting treatment engagement, sobriety, accountability, and reunification-related goals.
resources.hours: Court referral timing applies; no public walk-in hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Voluntary family treatment-court pathway that supports parents during substance-abuse treatment, coordinates accountability, and connects the court case with recovery and family-stability goals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Parents must have an open dependency case in Maricopa County with substance-use allegations. The judge can make a referral during hearing, an attorney can refer, and the parent may self-refer using the court's FTC contact route.

**Population Served**
Parents with substance-use concerns in active Maricopa County child-welfare/dependency cases, and their families.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the dependency attorney, judge, DCS Specialist or case team about Family Treatment Court. Programme information: 602-372-4506, the Arizona Judicial Branch’s listed social-work supervisor route. County referral information also lists FTC2@jbazmc.maricopa.gov; confirm the appropriate referral steps for the active case.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general public treatment clinic. It is court-based and voluntary for eligible dependency-case parents. Confirm current court contacts and whether the case is procedurally eligible before relying on it.

resources.name: Arizona Spinal Cord Injury Association - Resource Facilitation, Peer Mentoring and Support Groups
resources.description: Arizona Spinal Cord Injury Association offers spinal-cord-injury-specific peer mentoring, support groups, resource connections, social activities and adaptive transportation information for Arizona residents.
resources.address: 5025 E. Washington St., Suite 110, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: Call or email to confirm current support groups, mentoring availability, transportation options and appointments.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
AZSCIA connects people with spinal cord injuries to peer mentoring, support groups, resource information, social/community activities, adaptive transportation or van-rental information, and related disability resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are focused on people with spinal cord injuries and their families or support networks. Specific groups, transportation or mentoring options may have separate schedules, fees or availability.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents with spinal cord injuries, including Maricopa County and Mesa-area residents who can use phone, virtual, Phoenix-area or statewide connections.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-507-4209, toll-free 888-889-2185 when available, or email info@azspinal.org. Confirm current group schedules and whether support is virtual or in-person before attending.

**Important Information to Know**
The main website was not accessible through the research tool, but current public newsletter evidence and a public state spinal/head-injury resource page support ongoing contact and activities. This is support and navigation, not medical treatment or guaranteed transportation.

resources.name: Asylum Program of Arizona
resources.description: Provides legal-assistance funding and attorney connections for non-detained asylum seekers in Arizona.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides legal-assistance funding and attorney connections for non-detained asylum seekers in Arizona.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program screens claims and financial need; funding and attorney capacity govern assistance.

**Population Served**
Non-detained asylum seekers and torture survivors seeking protection.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 520-261-7888 or email asylumservicesaz@gmail.com to ask about screening.

**Important Information to Know**
Assistance may involve reduced or shared attorney costs. The Tucson mailing address does not establish a county-only restriction; confirm meeting arrangements.

resources.name: Centennial Village - Affordable Senior and Mobility-Accessible Housing
resources.description: Centennial Village provides affordable independent living apartments in Mesa for senior adults age 62+ and adults with mobility impairment, with an official online pre-application route to its waiting list.
resources.address: 130 W Brown Rd, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Compliance and leasing by appointment only. All apartments are rented and no guided tours are available according to the contact page.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Affordable independent housing in Mesa for seniors and adults with mobility impairment. Applicants can submit an online pre-application for the waiting list; standard and mobility-feature apartments have separate wait estimates.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Senior applicants must be age 62 or older at pre-application for standard units. Adults under 62 must have a mobility impairment to remain on the waitlist. Applicants seeking mobility units should select the mobility option; a medical provider verification letter will be required when the office requests verification of need.

**Population Served**
Independent senior adults age 62+ and adults with mobility impairment who are seeking affordable housing in Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the pre-application link on the official Pre-Application & Forms page. Questions: 480-833-6036. Leasing and compliance visits require an appointment at 130 W. Brown Rd., Mesa; guided tours are not currently offered.

**Important Information to Know**
Published estimates are 18-24 months for standard apartments and 24-36 months for mobility-feature apartments. All units are currently rented; a pre-application is for the waiting list, not a vacancy promise. Confirm current income, rent, documentation and waiting-list rules.

resources.name: OCJ Kids - Emergency Removal Resources and Transition Support
resources.description: OCJ Kids provides DCS-linked emergency removal resources and transition support for Arizona foster and at-risk children, including resources for children when removed from home and ongoing support for foster, group-home and aged-out youth.
resources.address: 21630 N 9th Ave #103, Phoenix, AZ 85027
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency removal resources for children removed from home, group-home and foster-youth support, aged-out youth support, and community resources connected to Arizona child welfare partners.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Official access is framed around Arizona DCS, foster/group-home partners, foster children, at-risk children and aged-out youth. Public walk-in access for clothing or kits is not posted.

**Population Served**
Arizona foster and at-risk children, children removed from their homes, youth in foster homes or group homes, and youth exiting foster care.

**How to Best Connect**
Call OCJ Kids Phoenix at 602-439-2171. Because access appears partner-mediated, ask whether a DCS caseworker, group home, foster-care agency or Transition Success Center must request specific items.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general clothing closet. The supported route is through foster-system partnerships, and exact item inventory, Mesa placement access and direct referral steps should be confirmed before promising goods.

resources.name: WomensLaw.org — Legal Information Email Hotline
resources.description: Written U.S. legal information about domestic violence, sexual assault and stalking. An attorney answers or reviews every response.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Written U.S. legal information about domestic violence, sexual assault and stalking. An attorney answers or reviews every response.

**Eligibility Requirements**

For survivors and others with relevant U.S. legal-information questions. The service supports all survivors and is not limited to women.

**Population Served**

Survivors seeking legal information, including people in Arizona who can safely use an online account.

**How to Best Connect**

Use the official Email Hotline form on a device and account the abusive person cannot monitor. Responses are normally provided within one to five business days.

**Important Information to Know**

This service provides information, not legal advice, representation or telephone callbacks. It is not for urgent deadlines or immediate danger. Accounts and their information are deleted after90days under the published policy.

resources.name: Maricopa County Department of Public Health - High Risk Perinatal Program (HRPP)
resources.description: Free Maricopa County in-home community health nursing for eligible families and newborns transitioning from NICU to home, with health and development monitoring during the first year, parent education, and community referrals.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free in-home community health nursing for eligible high-risk infants after NICU discharge, with health and developmental monitoring during the first year as needed, parent education and support, and connections to community/family resources, including postpartum mental-health referrals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Parents of babies in Maricopa County who require 5 or more days of NICU care are eligible, or families may qualify with a physician referral. At hospital discharge, the hospital typically provides a referral to a Community Health Nurse.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County families with newborns transitioning from NICU to home, especially medically vulnerable or high-risk infants.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-350-5119 or email Mary.Anthony@maricopa.gov for information. Families can also ask the NICU hospital discharge team or physician about referral.

**Important Information to Know**
No enrollment charge. This is infant/community health nursing, not psychotherapy or universal newborn home visiting. Ask about physician-referral eligibility if NICU care was shorter than five days or occurred outside the county, and confirm timing after discharge.

resources.name: A New Leaf - Rapid ReHousing
resources.description: A New Leaf Rapid ReHousing provides coordinated-entry rental subsidy, move-in cost help, rent and utility assistance, temporary case management, support services, workforce assistance and referrals for families and individuals experiencing homelessness.
resources.address: No public office for service delivery; staff meet participants in the community. Administrative address: 868 E University Dr, Mesa, AZ 85203
resources.hours: Coordinated entry required; A New Leaf directs all families and single clients to call 2-1-1 for assistance.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Rental subsidy, move-in costs including application fees, rent and utility assistance, temporary case management, support services, workforce assistance and referrals to help participants obtain and maintain housing.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For families and individuals currently experiencing homelessness across the Valley who are assessed through coordinated entry. Singles are evaluated through the Single Coordinated Entry System, and families through the Family Housing Hub. Assistance amount and duration depend on case-management assessment, income, debt and funding.

**Population Served**
Families and individuals experiencing homelessness in the Valley, including Mesa and Maricopa County clients who enter through coordinated entry.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 2-1-1 for coordinated-entry assistance before expecting A New Leaf Rapid ReHousing. Program staff meet participants in the community; there is no physical office for walk-in service. For program questions, email Housing@turnanewleaf.org.

**Important Information to Know**
Assistance may continue up to 12 months according to assessment, income/debt review and funding, but it is determined month to month and not guaranteed. Coordinated entry does not promise a unit, subsidy or programme placement. This is not immediate cash or a motel voucher.

resources.name: Arizona Attorney General's Office — Consumer Information and Complaints
resources.description: The Arizona Attorney General Consumer Information and Complaints Unit accepts consumer fraud complaints online or by downloadable form and provides a public enforcement route for fraud, scams, and deceptive practices.
resources.address: 2005 N. Central Ave., Attn: Consumer Information and Complaints, Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Online and paper complaint intake for people who believe they have been victims of consumer fraud. Complaints can include supporting documents and may be used for consumer protection review, informal dispute routing, and public enforcement patterns.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The complaint must involve a consumer issue within Arizona Attorney General authority. The office does not handle every private dispute and does not replace private legal advice.

**Population Served**
Arizona consumers, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents. This route may be especially relevant for older adults, people affected by scams, debt or consumer fraud, and identity-theft-adjacent consumer issues.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the online consumer complaint form, or download a complaint form and mail it to 2005 N. Central Ave., Attn: Consumer Information and Complaints, Phoenix, AZ 85004, or fax it to 602-542-4579. For information, call 602-542-5763 in Phoenix, 520-628-6648 in Tucson, or 800-352-8431 outside metro Phoenix. The official complaint page links online forms in English and Spanish.

**Important Information to Know**
The Attorney General represents the public interest, not the individual complainant as private counsel. Filing a complaint may not stop lawsuits, collections, eviction deadlines, or court dates.

resources.name: Arizona Center for Empowerment — immigration services and classes
resources.description: Provides citizenship application support, DACA-renewal help and English or citizenship classes.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides citizenship application support, DACA-renewal help and English or citizenship classes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Confirm current appointment, class, fee and program requirements with ACE.

**Population Served**
Immigrant community members and families seeking practical application or learning support.

**How to Best Connect**
Use Get Help or Schedule Consultation on ACE’s services page.

**Important Information to Know**
Do not assume broad legal or court representation. The service request form is preferable to conflicting older office addresses.

resources.name: Puente Human Rights Movement - Migra Watch rapid response and defense line
resources.description: Puente Human Rights Movement's Migra Watch is a community-defense network for monitoring and verifying immigration enforcement activity, solidarity accompaniment, court accompaniment, and rapid-response support.
resources.address: 1937 W Adams St, Phoenix, AZ 85009
resources.hours: Published response hours are not stated; call the defense line for current availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Migra Watch monitors and verifies immigration enforcement activity, offers solidarity accompaniment, supports community members at risk of detention, and provides court accompaniment or rapid-response support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public page does not list formal eligibility rules. It is intended for immigrant community members and families facing enforcement activity or needing accompaniment or rapid-response support.

**Population Served**
Phoenix metropolitan immigrant and working-class communities, including Mesa-area community members when Puente can respond or provide guidance.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the defense line at 480-506-7437 for enforcement activity reporting, court accompaniment, or rapid-response support. General Puente support is 602-252-1283.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a substitute for 911 or retained legal counsel. Response hours, Mesa coverage, and availability are not guaranteed, so callers should ask for current safe-use instructions and next steps.

resources.name: KP Staffing · Warehouse and Light Industrial Staffing Serving Mesa
resources.description: KP Staffing's Phoenix-based team serves Mesa and East Valley employers and job seekers with temporary, temp-to-permanent and direct-hire opportunities in light industrial, warehouse, skilled trades and professional/clerical roles, using a talent-network form and job-seeker routes.
resources.hours: Online talent-network form; contact timing not posted on the Mesa page.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Staffing and recruiting for Mesa-area warehouse, light industrial, skilled trades and professional/clerical jobs. The page describes temporary, temp-to-permanent, direct-hire and payroll services, a short application process, Explore Jobs and Join Our Talent Network routes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Public eligibility requirements are not posted. Job seekers should expect to complete the talent-network/application process and meet job-specific experience, background, safety, transportation and documentation requirements.

**Population Served**
Mesa and East Valley job seekers seeking warehouse, manufacturing, light industrial, skilled trades or clerical staffing opportunities.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Job Seekers, Explore Jobs or Join Our Talent Network form on the KP Staffing Mesa page. The page identifies a Phoenix-based team serving Mesa; it does not verify a separate Mesa office address.

**Important Information to Know**
Current openings, pay, shifts, worker phone contact and in-person office access are not clearly posted on the Mesa page. Applying or joining the talent network does not guarantee immediate placement.

resources.name: Terros Health - Mesa Integrated Behavioral Health: Stapley and University Health Centers
resources.description: Terros Health Mesa integrated-care access through Stapley and University Health Centers, offering counseling, psychiatry, medication services, substance-use treatment, case/care coordination, telehealth, Medicaid eligibility/social-services enrollment and selected education/employment supports.
resources.address: 1111 S Stapley Dr, Mesa, AZ 85204; 262 E University Dr, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Stapley clinic/telehealth Monday-Thursday 7:30 AM-8:00 PM, Friday-Saturday 7:30 AM-5:00 PM, Sunday closed. University clinic/telehealth Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM, weekends closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Terros Health's Mesa community health centers provide integrated behavioral-health and whole-person care. Stapley Health Center offers primary medical care, children's services, Arizona Families FIRST, telehealth, Medicaid eligibility help, social-services enrollment, care coordination, individual/group/couples/family counseling, specialty counseling including EMDR and DBT, substance-use treatment, justice services, medication services, MAT and psychiatry. University Health Center offers social-services enrollment, individual and group counseling, substance-use treatment, psychiatry, medication services, care coordination, psychosocial rehabilitation, supported education/GED, culinary skills, basic computer skills, peer-support training/certification and employment support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
New patients should call for appointment, clinical fit, payer screening and which Mesa site best matches the needed service. Terros describes community health centers as serving everyone regardless of ability to pay, but current eligibility, insurance and documentation requirements should be reviewed at intake.

**Population Served**
Mesa and Maricopa County residents needing outpatient counseling, psychiatry, medication services, co-occurring substance-use treatment, care coordination, integrated primary/behavioral health, children's services, recovery supports or education/employment-related psychosocial rehabilitation.

**How to Best Connect**
For Stapley, new patients call 602-685-6000 and existing patients call 602-302-7900; the site is 1111 S Stapley Dr, Mesa, AZ 85204. For University, new and existing patients call 602-685-6000; the site is 262 E University Dr, Mesa, AZ 85201.

**Important Information to Know**
Services and appointment requirements differ between Stapley and University; confirm the exact clinic and programme. Café Stapley youth services, Javelina justice services and Bridging the Gap have separate intake. Terros clinic numbers do not dispatch mobile crisis teams; use 988 or the appropriate crisis line for crisis screening rather than wait for a clinic callback.

resources.name: STARS - Scottsdale Training and Rehabilitation Services - DTA, Competitive Integrated Employment, Work Center and Community-Based Employment Support
resources.description: STARS provides cognitive and developmental disability programs in Scottsdale, including day training for adults, competitive integrated employment, work center and community-based employment support.
resources.address: 7507 E. Osborn Rd., Scottsdale, AZ 85251; 11130 E. Cholla St. #H-110, Scottsdale, AZ 85259
resources.hours: Campus/program hours should be confirmed; main site lists Scottsdale campuses and contact phone.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Day Training for Adults, Work Center, Competitive Integrated Employment and Community-Based Employment Support. CIE includes job exploration, resumes, interviews, job-placement connections, individual onsite training and longer-term employment support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Day/work programmes focus on cognitive and developmental disabilities. CIE also lists physical disability and VR or DDD eligibility, with private-pay options. Confirm legal working age, assessment, support needs, programme authorization and funding for the particular service.

**Population Served**
People with cognitive and developmental disabilities in Scottsdale and the greater Maricopa County area who can access STARS campuses or employment programs.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-994-5704; relay users can dial 711. For CIE, email bramirez@starsaz.org or use the official admissions/contact forms. Ask which campus or community programme fits, and whether Mesa transportation is available.

**Important Information to Know**
STARS is not Mesa-based. Confirm whether the program accepts Mesa residents, whether transportation or DDD/private-pay funding is available, and current openings before referral.

resources.name: Without Walls Church Community Food Distribution - Drive-through Food Distribution
resources.description: Without Walls Church Community Food Distribution is a monthly third-Saturday Mesa drive-through food distribution, first come first served and no fee, with a car required for loading.
resources.address: 1303 S Lindsay Rd, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: 2-1-1 lists every third Saturday of the month, 9:00 AM-11:00 AM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Monthly drive-through food distribution in Mesa, first come first served.

**Eligibility Requirements**
2-1-1 lists no fee and says participants must come in a car so the food box can be loaded. No registration or income requirement is listed in the public referral record.

**Population Served**
People who can travel by vehicle to the Mesa church distribution site for monthly food assistance.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to 1303 S Lindsay Rd, Mesa, AZ 85204 on the third Saturday from 9:00 AM to 11:00 AM, or call 480-838-2587 to confirm the current month before going.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a drive-through model; pedestrians or clients without a vehicle may not be able to use it. The official church page confirms the church identity, phone and address, while detailed food-distribution rules come from 2-1-1's listing last assured March 12, 2026.

resources.name: Southwest Behavioral & Health Services - Community Living
resources.description: Southwest Behavioral & Health Services Community Living provides community-based residential behavioral-health support in houses, facilities and shared apartments, including Mesa locations.
resources.address: Administrative office: 3450 N 3rd St, Phoenix, AZ 85012; Mesa facilities include Brookside, Casa del Este, Casa Verde and La Hacienda
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Community-based residential settings with behavioral health interventions, crisis planning, counseling, medication support, homelessness support, skills training, personal care and independent-living skill building.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The page describes services for adults needing behavioral-health community living supports. Admission route, health-plan authorization and current openings must be confirmed with SB&H.

**Population Served**
Adults with behavioral-health needs who can benefit from supported community living in Maricopa County, including Mesa facilities.

**How to Best Connect**
Call SB&H at 602-265-8338 and ask about Community Living eligibility and referral requirements. The administrative office is 3450 N 3rd St, Phoenix, AZ 85012.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not general emergency shelter. Length of stay, facility placement and treatment frequency vary by individual need and program authorization.

resources.name: Dynamic Living Counseling · Substance Abuse Programs / DUI and court-linked outpatient counseling
resources.description: Dynamic Living Counseling is an ADHS-licensed outpatient behavioral health counseling agency with a Mesa/Gilbert office. It offers substance-abuse programs, DUI/Level 2 education, domestic violence, anger management, ethics and other court-linked or personal counseling services.
resources.address: 1555 S Gilbert Rd, Suite 103, Mesa, AZ 85204; 1501 E Osborn Rd, Suite 103, Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.hours: Call for current appointment and group schedules; two Valley office locations are listed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Outpatient behavioral-health counseling specializing in DUI-related issues, substance abuse, domestic violence, anger management, EAP and personal counseling. Substance-abuse programs use the evidence-based Living in Balance curriculum and work with local, county and state court systems.

**Eligibility Requirements**
People may be court-ordered, employer-recommended, family-recommended, or seeking affordable professional counseling. Insurance participation is limited on the public page; Blue Cross Blue Shield plans are named and the site says to check back for Medicare, AHCCCS and commercial plan updates.

**Population Served**
Adults needing outpatient counseling, DUI education, court-linked substance-abuse programming, or related behavioral-health groups in Mesa/Gilbert or Phoenix. The site notes discounts may be available for active and retired military veterans, police and fire personnel.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-688-2907 or 520-353-3043 and ask about the Mesa/Gilbert office, program schedule, whether self-referrals are accepted for general substance-use counseling, and what court paperwork or payment is needed.

**Important Information to Know**
This is outpatient counseling and education, not detox, residential treatment, MAT, crisis care, or guaranteed AHCCCS-covered care. Confirm payer, costs, court compliance requirements and appointment availability before referral.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Economic Security - Cash Assistance
resources.description: Arizona DES Cash Assistance provides temporary cash benefits and supportive services to needy Arizona families with dependent children, including some non-parent relatives requesting help for dependent children.
resources.hours: Telephone interviews Monday-Friday 7:00 AM-3:00 PM; DES office access generally Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM, excluding holidays. Confirm the local office.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Cash Assistance provides temporary cash benefits and supportive services to help Arizona families with dependent children meet basic needs and work toward self-sufficiency. Some applicants may be evaluated for Grant Diversion instead of ongoing monthly benefits.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on dependent children, Arizona residency, citizenship or qualified noncitizen status, resources, monthly income rules, required verification, and program compliance. Adults receiving benefits generally must sign a Personal Responsibility Agreement unless applying only for children.

**Population Served**
