Classes, mentoring, brief solution-focused counseling, pregnancy testing and prenatal education, postpartum mental-health support, job coaching, case management and referrals. Material programmes can include food, clothing, diapers, baby items, toiletries and utility help. Hope on the Road offers partner/mobile outreach; faith-based classes are among the programme options.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The current programme page welcomes women without general fees or eligibility restrictions. Ask about appointments, specific class enrollment and available materials. A programme flyer links Hope Provides goods to engagement in activities, so confirm whether the requested item requires participation.

**Population Served**
Women and teen girls in crisis, including pregnant and parenting women, mothers, and women affected by domestic or intimate partner violence.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-715-0999 or use the official programs/locations pages to choose a center or Hope on the Road site. Mesa-area clients may ask about the Apache Junction center, Phoenix center, or a mobile/partner site.

**Important Information to Know**
Availability differs by centre and current supplies; confirm the service location and schedule. Donation-drop-off hours are not client appointment hours. This is not an emergency shelter, crisis hotline or full medical clinic; use the appropriate emergency or domestic-violence intake route for urgent safety needs.

resources.name: Arizona Justice Project · Re-Entry Assistance
resources.description: Arizona Justice Project provides re-entry assistance through its social-work team for accepted Project clients returning to Arizona communities, including help with housing, benefits, health insurance, employment, training, education, family reunification, mental health, food and identification needs.
resources.address: 4001 N 3rd Street, Suite 401, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
For accepted Arizona Justice Project clients, the social-work team begins release planning before release and continues after release. Help may include housing, benefits, health insurance, employment, vocational or technical training, education, family reunification, mental-health care, rehabilitation, food and identification needs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Direct re-entry assistance is limited to Arizona Justice Project clients, generally people whose wrongful-conviction or manifest-injustice cases the Project has accepted. Nonclients are directed to outside resources.

**Population Served**
Arizona Justice Project clients returning to Arizona communities, including Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Accepted clients should work with their assigned Arizona Justice Project legal or social-work team. For programme questions use info@azjusticeproject.org; prospective clients should follow the website’s case-review application process. The office is 4001 N. 3rd St., Suite 401, Phoenix.

**Important Information to Know**
Reentry and document support are for accepted Project clients. A new legal inquiry does not establish acceptance, provide general walk-in case management or guarantee funding for documents, housing or other needs.

resources.name: Phoenix Rescue Mission - Will Work / Glendale Works identity-document case management
resources.description: Phoenix Rescue Mission Will Work / Glendale Works offers paid day work and case management for people experiencing homelessness, including help securing IDs and documents needed for employment or housing; Mesa residents may face geographic and transportation barriers.
resources.address: Currently described by provider as Glendale Works; call for current work-program location before travel.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Will Work / Glendale Works provides paid day work, breakfast and lunch, employment preparation and individualized case management. The official page says case managers help participants secure IDs and documents needed for employment or housing.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For men and women experiencing homelessness who participate in the active Will Work location. Participation is not permanent employment and depends on program availability and local city partnership.

**Population Served**
Adults experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County communities where Phoenix Rescue Mission operates Will Work programs. The direct Will Work page identifies Glendale Works; the broader housing page also referenced active programs in Glendale, Phoenix and Scottsdale.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-233-3000 and ask about Glendale Works or the current Will Work program location, participation requirements and whether ID-document help is available before referring a Mesa client.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a stand-alone ID service and not Mesa-based. It is best treated as a reserve option for a person already engaging Phoenix Rescue Mission or able to access the active work-program location.

resources.name: Arizona Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program (SFMNP)
resources.description: Arizona Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program provides a once-yearly produce coupon booklet for low-income seniors age 60+ to buy fresh Arizona-grown fruits, vegetables and herbs at authorized farmers markets and farm stands.
resources.hours: Applications open seasonally; for 2026, eligible participants may apply beginning March 1 and the annual application window closes September 30.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Seasonal Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program coupons for fresh, nutritious, unprepared, locally grown fruits, vegetables and herbs from authorized farmers markets, farm stands and CSA programs. Qualifying seniors may receive one $50 coupon booklet when funding is available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Participants must be at least 60 years old and have income at or below 185% of annual poverty income guidelines, or be participating in the Commodity Senior Food Program. Coupon availability is first come, first served and varies by funding.

**Population Served**
Low-income Arizona seniors age 60+, including eligible seniors in Maricopa County and Mesa who can use authorized participating locations.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online or by paper application through the Arizona Farmers Market Nutrition Program. To request a paper application or ask questions, call 833-836-8253 ext. 4. Check AZFMNP for current application dates, voucher availability, waitlist notices and participating locations.

**Important Information to Know**
For 2026, DES says eligible participants may apply beginning March 1 and coupons are mailed directly to eligible recipients. The application window closes September 30 each year, but coupons can run out before then.

resources.name: West-MEC · Adult Education Career Training Programs
resources.description: West-MEC Adult Education offers adult career training programs in the West and Northwest Valley, including aviation maintenance, dental assisting, HVAC-R, pharmacy technician, precision manufacturing, and welding, with admissions help, FAFSA guidance, tours, and start-date information.
resources.address: Central Campus: 6997 N. Glen Harbor Blvd., Glendale, AZ 85307; Northeast Campus: 1617 W. Williams Dr., Phoenix, AZ 85027; Northwest Campus: 13201 W. Grand Ave., Surprise, AZ 85374; Southwest Campus: 500 N. Verrado Way, Buckeye, AZ 85326
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
West-MEC Adult Education provides career training programs designed for adults who want technical skills and a faster route into the workforce. Current listed programs include aviation maintenance technology, dental assisting, HVAC-R, pharmacy technician, precision manufacturing, and welding technology. The page includes start dates, FAFSA guidance, financial-aid contact, program exploration, tours, and the adult student portal.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on the program, admissions process, start date, tour and application steps, and financial-aid rules. Six listed programs are financial-aid eligible. Veterans may ask about GI Bill educational benefits.

**Population Served**
Adults seeking hands-on career training in Maricopa County, especially people able to attend West-MEC campuses in Glendale, Phoenix, Surprise, or Buckeye. This is a reserve option for Mesa clients who can commute and need a program not available closer to Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 623-738-0046 or email adulted@west-mec.org. To start, express interest in the adult student portal, complete the interest form for the program and location, validate email, and wait for an admissions representative to schedule a program tour. Financial aid questions can go to 623-738-0047.

**Important Information to Know**
Current official pages do not support the older GED partnership claim, so this record is limited to current adult career training. Campuses are concentrated in the West and Northwest Valley; verify commute, program location, start date, tuition, supply costs, and aid before referring a Mesa client.

resources.name: Arizona DES - Senior Community Service Employment Program (SCSEP) / Mature Worker Program
resources.description: Arizona DES Senior Community Service Employment Program provides paid part-time community-service training, assessment, job skills development, counseling and job-search support for low-income unemployed adults age 55+.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Supervised paid training at nonprofit/government host agencies, usually about 20 hours weekly at the applicable highest federal, state or local minimum wage. Includes assessment, supportive-service planning, job skills, limited education, job-search help, counseling and transition toward unsubsidized employment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be 55+, Arizona residents at enrollment, unemployed, work-authorized, at or below 125% of federal poverty guidelines, and have an employment barrier such as limited literacy/English, disability, poor job prospects or homelessness risk. Registration with Arizona Job Connection is required.

**Population Served**
Low-income unemployed Arizona adults age 55+, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents. Priority is given to groups including minorities, limited-English-speaking individuals, American Indians and people with greatest economic or special employment needs.

**How to Best Connect**
For Maricopa County, DES lists AARP Foundation as the DES grantee at 928-395-2261 and national grantee options including NICOA at 505-292-2001 and Easterseals at 602-841-0403. Call the grantee directly and ask to enroll in SCSEP.

**Important Information to Know**
Places are limited and a waiting list may apply; this is training, not a permanent-job guarantee. DES describes SCSEP income as excluded for HUD housing and SNAP, while other benefits such as AHCCCS may be affected. Confirm the treatment of wages with each benefit administrator.

resources.name: FIBCO Family Services Outreach / Clothing and Toiletries
resources.description: FIBCO Family Services offers basic-needs help in downtown Phoenix, including access to clothing, food, and resource connection for individuals and families facing financial hardship.
resources.address: 1141 E Jefferson St, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Friday 10:30 AM-12:30 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
FIBCO Family Services provides basic-needs help, including clothing access, food support, and connection to other resources for people facing financial constraints.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page does not list detailed eligibility rules. 2-1-1 evidence describes help for people with very low income or experiencing homelessness; clients should call or use the get-started route to confirm current requirements.

**Population Served**
Individuals and families in need who can reach the downtown Phoenix site, including low-income households and people experiencing homelessness.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-698-6453, use the official website's get-started route, or visit during posted open hours at 1141 E Jefferson St, Phoenix. Confirm clothing availability before traveling from Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
Specific clothing sizes, shoes, toiletries, food-box availability, and any visit limits depend on current inventory. The Phoenix site may be a significant trip for Mesa clients.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Health Services · Well Woman HealthCheck
resources.description: ADHS Well Woman HealthCheck offers breast cancer screening access through Well Woman clinics, including free clinical breast exams and mammograms for eligible uninsured or underinsured patients ages 40-65 and symptomatic patients age 21 or older, plus covered diagnostic tests when needed after screening.
resources.address: Participating clinics include Mesa and Maricopa County locations
resources.hours: ADHS operating hours are Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM. Clinic hours and appointment availability vary by participating screening location.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Clinical breast exams, mammograms and covered diagnostic tests following screening when needed through Well Woman clinic locations. The broader program also supports breast/cervical cancer screening and navigation through participating providers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
ADHS states that uninsured or underinsured patients ages 40 to 65 and symptomatic patients age 21 or older can receive free clinical breast exams and mammograms. Service-specific eligibility should be confirmed with the selected clinic. Screening also has financial eligibility rules; confirm the current household-income limit with the selected clinic.

**Population Served**
Arizona patients needing breast cancer screening, especially uninsured or underinsured women and symptomatic adults who meet program rules.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the ADHS screening-location map to find a participating clinic near Mesa or call ADHS at 602-542-4611 for program information. Schedule directly with the participating clinic.

**Important Information to Know**
This is screening and diagnostic follow-up after screening, not emergency care. The provider map and appointment availability should be checked before referral, and age/symptom/insurance rules can affect eligibility.

resources.name: Epilepsy Foundation Arizona - Epilepsy Helpline, Support Groups and Seizure Education
resources.description: Epilepsy Foundation Arizona provides epilepsy-specific helpline navigation, support groups, education, seizure first-aid training, camps/events and community support for people and families affected by epilepsy.
resources.address: 3104 E. Camelback Rd., Suite 2292, Phoenix, AZ 85016
resources.hours: Call or check the Arizona local page for current support-group dates, classes, events and registration requirements.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Epilepsy Foundation Arizona offers local helpline navigation, support groups, seizure-recognition and first-aid education, educational programs, camps/events, SUDEP support and community connections. Ask about current child and teen programmes, including Camp Candlelight and support adapted to seizure needs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services focus on people affected by epilepsy and seizure disorders, their families and caregivers. Individual groups, camps and events may have registration, age, diagnosis or schedule requirements.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents affected by epilepsy, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents and family caregivers.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Arizona office at 602-282-3515 or use the local Epilepsy Foundation Arizona page to find current events, support groups and education programs.

**Important Information to Know**
This is education, support and navigation, not emergency seizure care or direct clinical treatment. Some support groups are virtual or scheduled events, so confirm current dates and registration before referral.

resources.name: Aliento - Support for DACA Recipients, Dreamers and Immigrant Families
resources.description: Aliento supports students, Dreamers and immigrant families through immigrant-student resources, DACA and know-your-rights links, detention/removal preparation planning, higher-education guidance, healing/arts programs, leadership development and community workshops.
resources.address: 4747 N 32nd St, Phoenix, AZ 85018
resources.hours: Use the resource links, office-hours sign-up or contact form for current programmes.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Aliento provides non-legal support for students, Dreamers and immigrant families. Current resources include a detention/removal preparation plan, undocumented higher-education pathway guidance, DACA resources, know-your-rights links, immigrant-student mental health tools, office-hours sign-up, arts and healing programs and leadership development.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Most resources are aimed at students, Dreamers, mixed-status and immigrant families, educators and community supporters. Specific workshops, office hours, fellowships, clubs or school partnerships may have their own sign-up process.

**Population Served**
Arizona students, Dreamers, immigrant families, mixed-status families and educators, including Mesa and Phoenix-area school communities referenced on Aliento’s site.

**How to Best Connect**
Use alientoaz.org/resources for current guides and sign-ups, including higher-education office hours. The website contact form supports questions and referrals. Confirm any appointment before traveling to the listed office at 4747 N. 32nd St., Phoenix.

**Important Information to Know**
Aliento is not an immigration law office and should be paired with an authorized legal provider for legal advice, form preparation, representation, asylum or immigration-court needs. It is valuable for education access, preparation planning, wellness and community support.

resources.name: Arizona Job Connection — Jobs and Approved Training Search
resources.description: Arizona’s online job bank provides job searches, résumé tools, account-based applications and a searchable list of training providers and programs.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Arizona’s online job bank provides job searches, résumé tools, account-based applications and a searchable list of training providers and programs.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Job eligibility depends on each employer. Training-list inclusion does not establish individual funding eligibility or local workforce approval.

**Population Served**

Arizona job seekers and people comparing career-training options.

**How to Best Connect**

Search the official site; create an account when needed to save or apply. The help desk assists with account problems. Ask the local ARIZONA@WORK office about approved training and funding.

**Important Information to Know**

Some state-listed training is unavailable in a particular local workforce area. Check program approval, costs and authorization before enrolling or expecting reimbursement.

resources.name: NATIVE HEALTH WIC - Mesa Clinic
resources.description: NATIVE HEALTH WIC - Mesa provides WIC nutrition education, breastfeeding support, healthy food benefits and referrals for eligible families in Maricopa County.
resources.address: 777 W. Southern Ave., Building C, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Mesa WIC: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday 7:00 AM-4:00 PM; Thursday 9:00 AM-6:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
WIC healthy food benefits, nutrition and wellness information, breastfeeding support, peer counseling, online nutrition education and referrals to doctors, dentists, TANF, SNAP and AHCCCS.

**Eligibility Requirements**
WIC serves eligible pregnant, postpartum or breastfeeding participants, infants and children under five. Applicants must live in or temporarily reside in Maricopa County and meet WIC income/qualifying-programme and nutrition requirements. Ask about required identification, residency, income and child immunization records.

**Population Served**
Pregnant women, recently postpartum women, breastfeeding women, infants, children under five and caregivers including mothers, fathers, grandparents, foster parents and legal guardians.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 800-470-5930 to make an appointment for any NATIVE HEALTH WIC location. The Mesa clinic is at 777 W. Southern Ave., Building C, Mesa. Ask about Spanish assistance when arranging this service.

**Important Information to Know**
WIC is for qualifying families regardless of Native identity. Benefits depend on eligibility and nutritional assessment. Ask about phone appointments; recipients of a NATIVE HEALTH WIC text may reply with questions. Fathers, grandparents, foster parents and guardians can seek help for eligible children.

resources.name: Arizona Chapter Associated General Contractors Apprenticeship Trust Fund - Heavy Equipment Operator Apprenticeship Lead
resources.description: The Arizona Chapter Associated General Contractors posted enrollment for a Heavy Equipment Operator Apprenticeship Program with a direct coordinator contact; the public enrollment announcement is stale, so this is a useful apprenticeship lead that requires current intake confirmation.
resources.address: 1825 W. Adams St., Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
AZAGC's heavy-equipment apprenticeship lead describes an employer-linked construction training route for heavy equipment operation. The organization is a construction association with education and apprenticeship programs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Current eligibility requirements are not fully published on the checked announcement. Applicants should ask about age, work authorization, driver license, employer sponsorship, orientation, fees, class location, and whether grant-funded supports are available.

**Population Served**
People seeking heavy equipment or heavy civil construction apprenticeship opportunities in Phoenix and participating Arizona employer settings, including Mesa-area job seekers who can commute.

**How to Best Connect**
Call AZAGC at 602-252-3926 or contact Corey Foster at cfoster@azagc.org. Ask for the next Heavy Equipment Operator or heavy civil apprenticeship orientation and whether applications are currently open.

**Important Information to Know**
The official page checked was a May 1, 2024 enrollment announcement with a June 7 orientation date. It does not prove immediate 2026 enrollment. Treat this as a reserve apprenticeship lead until AZAGC confirms the next cohort.

resources.name: Arizona Friends of Foster Children Foundation — Supplemental Clothing Grants
resources.description: Advance-approved reimbursement for clothing and shoes for eligible children and youth in foster care.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Supplemental clothing and shoe reimbursement: up to $200 for ages0–13 or $250 for ages14 and older, once per calendar year.

**Eligibility Requirements**

For eligible dependent children in foster care; placement/status must be confirmed through the appropriate caseworker. Active extended-foster-care participants ages18–20 may qualify. Ask about interstate placements.

**Population Served**

Children and young adults in foster care, including qualifying Mesa and Maricopa County placements.

**How to Best Connect**

Apply through AFFCF before buying anything. Its application page explains online and paper options; allow roughly7–10 business days for review. A caregiver or caseworker can help confirm status.

**Important Information to Know**

Approval must precede purchase. Submit the combined receipts within60 days of approval and by December15. This is reimbursement, not a walk-in closet or a promise of same-day cash.

resources.name: Home Base Arizona
resources.description: Home Base Arizona connects Arizona veterans, service members, military families, and families of the fallen to behavioral health, wellness, resiliency, outpatient interest, Warrior Health and Fitness, adventure, and national intensive clinical program options.
resources.address: Mail only: Home Base at ASU, Mail Code 9020, 550 N. 3rd St., Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Behavioral health and wellness programming for invisible wounds of war. Arizona offerings include outpatient-services interest, Warrior Health and Fitness in Phoenix, adventure events, and virtual resiliency programs; national options include intensive clinical programs in Boston for warriors and families of the fallen.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Arizona page identifies eligible populations as Arizona veterans, service members, military families, and families of the fallen. Specific clinical eligibility, referral criteria, schedule, and whether care is virtual, Arizona-based, or out-of-state depend on the program.

**Population Served**
Arizona veterans, service members, military families, and families of the fallen, including Mesa and Maricopa County households.

**How to Best Connect**
Click "Get Care" or the Arizona outpatient interest form on the official page. Contact Dana West, Veteran Outreach Manager, at 833-865-0500 or HBArizona@massgeneralbrigham.org.

**Important Information to Know**
Arizona outpatient interest is not a confirmed local clinical appointment. Ask intake which services are currently available locally, virtually or through the Massachusetts intensive programme and what travel or eligibility rules apply. The ASU mailing address is not a confirmed walk-in clinic.

resources.name: DynamiCare Health · Opioids digital recovery coaching and contingency-management program
resources.description: DynamiCare Health offers a digital opioid recovery coaching and accountability program with telehealth recovery coaching, app-based appointment check-ins, at-home substance testing and financial rewards. Maricopa County lists DynamiCare as an opioid-settlement funded project to enhance the local OUD treatment network.
resources.address: Digital/telehealth program; no local walk-in address
resources.hours: DynamiCare lists text/call support Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM ET; program coaching schedule depends on enrollment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Digital opioid recovery support, telehealth recovery coaching, random breath and saliva testing through an app, verified treatment-attendance check-ins, reminders, and financial rewards for successful substance tests and appointment check-ins.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Individuals can call or text DynamiCare to discuss whether the program fits. Maricopa County funding indicates deployment in the county OUD treatment network, so local no-cost or referral-based access may depend on county contracts, participating providers, payer status or program capacity.

**Population Served**
People seeking support for opioid recovery, including Maricopa County clients where DynamiCare is available through direct subscription, insurance, treatment-provider partnership or county-funded participation.

**How to Best Connect**
Call or text DynamiCare at 855-539-6264 for a confidential, no-obligation conversation. If the person is already in OUD treatment, ask their provider whether DynamiCare enrollment is available through Maricopa County's network.

**Important Information to Know**
This is remote recovery coaching and contingency-management support, not detox, residential treatment, emergency care, methadone/buprenorphine prescribing, or a guaranteed free county benefit. Confirm cost, eligibility and whether the person needs a provider referral.

resources.name: Community Bridges - CPEC Mesa Crisis and Inpatient Access
resources.description: Adult psychiatric crisis screening and stabilization with an assessed pathway to CPEC inpatient care in Mesa; contact CBI for the correct entrance and level of care.
resources.address: 358 E. Javelina Ave., Suite 102, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: 24/7 access to care; crisis/inpatient access should be confirmed by phone before transport when possible.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Adult psychiatric crisis observation/stabilization and an assessed pathway to CPEC inpatient care. CBI inpatient services include psychiatric and co-occurring substance-use care, nursing/medical support, counseling, case management, peer support and discharge planning according to clinical needs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
CBI states inpatient clinics accept referrals from CBI Crisis Care Clinics and outside providers. Adults 18 and older may walk into CBI Crisis Care Clinics to be screened for psychiatric inpatient care. CBI states its psychiatric inpatient clinics contract with AHCCCS plans, major commercial insurers and other funding for uninsured or underinsured people.

**Population Served**
Adults in Mesa and Central Arizona needing urgent psychiatric crisis stabilization or inpatient behavioral-health care, including people with co-occurring substance-use needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Call CBI’s 24-hour access number, 888-224-2087, to confirm the correct crisis-care entrance and screening route. CPEC Inpatient is listed at 358 E. Javelina Ave., Suite 102, Mesa. Providers can use CBIReferrals@cbridges.com. Call 911 for an immediate medical or safety emergency.

**Important Information to Know**
Walk-in crisis screening and inpatient admission are different steps; clinical assessment, referral and capacity determine placement. Confirm insurance or available uninsured funding. This is not the Bellview residential site or Mesa Heritage outpatient clinic.

resources.name: Disability Rights Arizona - Protection and Advocacy for Beneficiaries of Social Security (PABSS)
resources.description: Disability Rights Arizona's PABSS program assists SSI and SSDI beneficiaries with disabilities who are working toward employment goals and need legal support or self-advocacy resources for employment-related barriers.
resources.address: 5025 E. Washington St., Suite 202, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: DRAZ posted that new intakes were closed September 21-28, 2026 and reopening Monday, September 28, 2026 at 8:00 AM; check current intake status before applying.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Protection and Advocacy for Beneficiaries of Social Security helps Social Security disability beneficiaries with employment-related legal barriers, including access to vocational rehabilitation, education, transportation and accommodations. DRAZ may provide legal support and self-advocacy resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people who receive SSDI or SSI due to disability and are seeking to achieve employment goals or financial independence. Case acceptance depends on DRAZ priorities, merit and resources.

**Population Served**
Arizona SSI and SSDI disability beneficiaries who want to work or are addressing employment-related barriers.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through the DRAZ online intake form or call 602-274-6287 or 800-927-2260. Explain that the issue involves Social Security disability benefits and work or employment supports.

**Important Information to Know**
This is advocacy for work-related barriers, not routine Social Security application help or benefits planning for every case. Intake does not guarantee representation, and temporary intake closures may apply.

resources.name: EPCOR Arizona — Deployed service member bill relief
resources.description: Offers a possible water or wastewater bill waiver during an eligible service member’s deployment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Offers a possible water or wastewater bill waiver during an eligible service member’s deployment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Be an eligible active-duty service member temporarily deployed away from an EPCOR-served residence that remains unoccupied. Programme space and EPCOR account requirements apply.

**Population Served**
Deployed military households with qualifying EPCOR Arizona water or wastewater service.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact EPCOR or email redacted deployment orders showing the deployment duration; the provider says it does not need the destination. Ask which service accounts can be enrolled.

**Important Information to Know**
The regular bill resumes when deployment ends. This is not a general veteran discount or relief for City of Mesa accounts; EPCOR’s disabled-veteran and income credits are separate programmes.

resources.name: Cactus Garden Mental Health Services
resources.description: Adult psychiatric assessment and medication management, in person or through Arizona telehealth.
resources.address: 7165 E University Dr, Suite B 14-155, Mesa, AZ 85207
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Adult psychiatric assessment and medication management, in person or through Arizona telehealth.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adults 18+; medication suitability is determined clinically.

**Population Served**
Arizona adults seeking outpatient psychiatric care.

**How to Best Connect**
Call or text 480-913-5872 or email Frontoffice@cactusgardenmhs.com. Ask about the accepted plan or private-pay arrangement.

**Important Information to Know**
The practice now lists Mercy Care acceptance. Private-pay initial visits are$230 and follow-ups$135; limited sliding fees may be available. It does not prescribe, taper or continue benzodiazepines; coordinate existing treatment with the current prescriber.

resources.name: Family Promise of Greater Phoenix - Family Shelter and Stabilization
resources.description: Family Promise of Greater Phoenix's 60-day Emergency Shelter Program helps families with at least one child, including families with pets, through a phone screening, private overnight shelter, meals, family day-center support, school/daycare enrollment help, pet care, employment support, insurance access, budgeting and next-step housing planning.
resources.address: Family Promise of Greater Phoenix, 7447 E Earll Drive, Scottsdale, AZ 85251
resources.hours: Call for phone screening and current placement arrangements.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The 60-day family emergency shelter programme includes meals, day-centre services, case management, school/daycare enrollment support, employment and housing navigation, health-insurance connections and budgeting. Enrolled families may access showers, laundry, mail, Wi-Fi, pet support, bus passes and programme van shuttles between sites. Prevention/graduate Connections services, including qualifying graduate rent or utility help, are a separate pathway.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Shelter applicants must have at least one child with them and complete screening; household fit and available space determine acceptance. Families with pets may inquire, but pet accommodation depends on placement/capacity. Direct rent and utility assistance is for eligible programme graduates participating in Connections, not general new callers.

**Population Served**
Families with children experiencing homelessness or facing an immediate housing crisis in the Greater Phoenix area, with facilities in south Scottsdale, Glendale and Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-659-5227 for a phone screening with the Social Work Team. Main office: 7447 E Earll Drive, Scottsdale, AZ 85251; email info@FamilyPromiseAZ.org.

**Important Information to Know**
Phone screening does not guarantee a bed or a Mesa placement. Ask staff for the actual day-centre and overnight destination. Meals, employment help and transport are participant supports, not a public pantry, career center or bus-pass programme. Pet arrangements and practical supports depend on placement, enrollment and resources; new shelter callers should not expect graduate rent/utility assistance.

resources.name: Paz de Cristo Community Center - Meals, Basic Needs and Empowerment
resources.description: Paz de Cristo is a Mesa direct-service hub providing nightly meals, emergency food boxes, showers, hygiene items, adult clothing, mail service, Arizona ID vouchers, birth-certificate help, water stations, job support, bus-ticket help when available, and shelter/housing navigation through coaches and partner agencies.
resources.address: 424 W Broadway Rd, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Dinner daily 5:15-6:30 PM. Food boxes first three Tuesdays 9-11 AM; confirm any additional Tuesday and seasonal changes. Adult clothing Monday/Friday 1-2 PM; showers Wednesday 9 AM-1 PM. Adult ID vouchers Tuesday 1-2 PM; birth-certificate help Wednesday 10-11 AM. Mail weekdays 4-6 PM, excluding holidays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Nightly meals, food boxes, adult clothing, showers/hygiene, mail, adult Arizona ID vouchers and birth-certificate fee/paperwork help. Employment coaching, SNAP computer access, limited bus tickets and partner referrals help with practical barriers. No overnight beds.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Dinner welcomes everyone. Food boxes require photo ID and recent proof of housed address, such as postmarked mail from the last 30 days. ID vouchers are adult-only, first come up to 20; no groups or outside organisations. Birth-certificate help requires a physical state ID, not a copy. Clothing is for adults, not children.

**Population Served**
Mesa and East Valley neighbors facing hunger, poverty, homelessness or basic-needs barriers.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit 424 W. Broadway Rd., Mesa during the specific service period. Call 480-464-2370 for the current calendar; ask for ext. 2150 for SNAP/computer access. Confirm bus-ticket and clothing-voucher availability. The food-box pages differ about additional Tuesdays beyond the first three.

**Important Information to Know**
Each service has its own rules and limited capacity. The mailroom cannot accept packages. No general rent/utility cash assistance or driver-license reinstatement is established. ID help may require additional state residency documentation; birth-certificate help will not bypass its physical-ID requirement. Confirm partner locations rather than assume Copa Health is onsite.

resources.name: Mesa Community College Applied Behavioral Health Certificate of Completion
resources.description: Mesa Community College's Applied Behavioral Health Certificate of Completion is a one-year career-ready training pathway for entry-level mental health and behavioral health support roles, with advisor contact and Mesa campus access.
resources.address: Southern and Dobson Campus, 1833 W. Southern Ave., Mesa, AZ 85202; Red Mountain Campus, 7110 E. McKellips Rd., Mesa, AZ 85207; online options may apply
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A one-year Applied Behavioral Health Certificate of Completion with real-world mental health training, service-learning, trauma-informed care, bedside care, crisis intervention, communication skills, and eligibility to take the Nurse Assistant State Board certification.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Prospective students must follow Mesa Community College admission and program advising steps. Clinical, background, schedule, tuition, prerequisite, and certification requirements should be confirmed with the program advisor.

**Population Served**
Mesa Community College students and job seekers interested in entry-level behavioral health, mental health support, hospital, school, residential facility, counseling, psychology, nursing, or human-services pathways.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact program advisor Breshae Greenberg at 480-654-7764 through the official MCC page. Ask about start date, campus, online availability, tuition, clinical/background requirements, and whether the certificate fits the client's career goal.

**Important Information to Know**
This is college training, not immediate job placement. The page lists Southern and Dobson, Red Mountain, and MCC Online locations; confirm where the required courses and service-learning components are offered in the desired term.

resources.name: Southwest Gas - Energy Share
resources.description: Southwest Gas Energy Share provides emergency natural-gas bill assistance for current Southwest Gas customers facing an unexpected financial hardship, with applications handled by local nonprofit agencies.
resources.hours: Local agency schedules vary; call before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency assistance toward Southwest Gas natural-gas bills for customers facing hardships such as job loss, illness, family separation, or another financial emergency.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For current Southwest Gas customers facing an unexpected financial hardship. Energy Share does not require meeting federal poverty guidelines; the local agency screens the request and available funds.

**Population Served**
Southwest Gas customers in Arizona, including eligible Mesa and Maricopa County customers in the Southwest Gas service area.

**How to Best Connect**
Use Southwest Gas’s Energy Share partner list to identify the agency serving the household. City of Mesa customers can ask MesaCAN at 480-833-9200 about current Southwest Gas assistance and required documents. Have the account and bill ready.

**Important Information to Know**
Funding and partner participation vary, and this is bill assistance rather than unrestricted cash. For a suspected gas leak, call 911 and Southwest Gas’s emergency line at 877-860-6020; that emergency number is not the financial-assistance intake.

resources.name: EZ Medical Transportation - Maricopa County Non-Emergency Medical Transportation
resources.description: EZ Medical Transportation provides non-emergency medical transportation throughout Maricopa County, including wheelchair-accessible and stretcher transportation for healthcare trips.
resources.address: Maricopa County, AZ
resources.hours: Call to schedule Monday-Saturday 5:00 AM-9:00 PM; 24-hour notice required.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
EZ Medical Transportation drives passengers to dialysis, surgery, dental, physical therapy, pharmacy visits and other healthcare needs. It lists wheelchair-accessible vehicles and stretcher transport.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The website presents the service as a NEMT provider serving Maricopa County. Riders should confirm rates, payer acceptance, mobility needs and whether the requested trip is eligible.

**Population Served**
People in Maricopa County who need non-emergency medical transportation, including people who use wheelchairs or need stretcher transport.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 1-866-592-3963 to schedule a ride. The site states calls are taken Monday-Saturday from 5:00 AM to 9:00 PM and that 24-hour notice is required.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not emergency ambulance transport. Confirm cost, insurance or facility payment arrangements and availability before relying on the ride.

resources.name: Goodwill of Central and Northern Arizona - Career Services and Career Pathways
resources.description: Goodwill of Central and Northern Arizona provides no-cost career services, online My Career Advisor resources, skills training, resume assistance, career coaching, certifications, job leads and hiring events.
resources.address: Multiple access routes; online My Career Advisor plus Goodwill career centers in Central and Northern Arizona
resources.hours: Online services are available through My Career Advisor; career center hours vary by location. Call 602-535-4444 for nearest in-person help.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost career services including skills training, career coaching, resume review, certifications, hiring events, community-resource access, career assessments, computer and soft-skills training, job leads, interview skills, job postings, job-search strategies, labor-market information and one-on-one coaching.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Goodwill describes its career services as free of charge to help clients land a job and advance a career. Specific training classes, certifications or veteran-center services may have separate registration or documentation requirements.

**Population Served**
Job seekers in central and northern Arizona, including Mesa clients using online/phone services and any nearby career center options confirmed by Goodwill.

**How to Best Connect**
Start through Goodwill's employment services page or MyCareerAdvisor, or call 602-535-4444 for assistance and the nearest career center.

**Important Information to Know**
No current Mesa career-center address was confirmed on the opened official page. Mesa clients can still use online services and the central assistance line. Confirm current training cohorts and the nearest in-person career center before sending a client across town.

resources.name: Pathway to Work - DDD and Vocational Rehabilitation Employment and Day Services
resources.description: Pathway to Work provides DDD day treatment and supported employment plus Vocational Rehabilitation-funded Pre-ETS, work-adjustment training, job development, job placement, retention and job coaching.
resources.address: 1445 E. Guadalupe Rd., Tempe, AZ 85283
resources.hours: Use the website contact route for programme schedules and current enrollment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Pathway to Work offers Day Treatment and Training for community access and independent-living skills, DDD employment services, group-supported employment, individual-supported employment, employment support aide, VR Pre-Employment Transition Services, work-adjustment training, job development, placement, retention and job coaching.

**Eligibility Requirements**
DTA participants must be at least 18, have completed K-12 education, not have significant medical needs, be capable of self-toileting with minimum assistance and be ALTCS eligible. VR Pre-ETS, work-adjustment training and job development/retention require referral from a Vocational Rehabilitation counselor.

**Population Served**
Adults with developmental or intellectual disabilities using DDD/ALTCS services and students with disabilities ages 14-22 who are enrolled in an educational program and referred through VR for Pre-ETS.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the contact link on azpathwaytowork.org to ask about the specific programme, DDD or VR referral, current capacity, transportation and Mesa access. VR clients should coordinate with their counselor. The listed site is 1445 E. Guadalupe Rd., Tempe; arrange intake before visiting.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not open walk-in employment placement. DDD/ALTCS or VR authorization, individualized goals, medical/support needs, transportation and capacity determine whether a Mesa resident can participate.

resources.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs - Veterans Burial Allowance, Plot, and Transportation Benefits
resources.description: VA burial allowance, plot/interment allowance, and transportation reimbursement may help eligible payers cover some burial, funeral, plot, interment, or remains-transportation costs for qualifying veterans.
resources.hours: VA national benefits phone support is Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-9:00 PM Eastern Time.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Federal VA burial benefits may reimburse eligible payers for some burial and funeral costs, plot or interment costs, and transportation of a veteran's remains to a final resting place or national cemetery when rules are met.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The person applying generally must have paid or be responsible for costs and not be reimbursed by another organization. The veteran must not have received a dishonorable discharge and must meet one of VA's qualifying death or benefit-status circumstances. Time limits differ for service-connected and non-service-connected deaths.

**Population Served**
Eligible surviving spouses, children, parents, estate representatives, friends, funeral homes, cemeteries, or organizations paying burial-related costs for qualifying veterans nationwide, including deaths in Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through VA.gov or by mail using VA Form 21P-530EZ to the VA Pension Intake Center. Call VA at 800-827-1000 for benefits questions; TTY users can use 711.

**Important Information to Know**
Amounts depend on date and circumstances of death and the type of allowance claimed. Needed documents may include death certificate, itemized receipts for transportation, DD214 or separation documents, and medical records for service-connected claims.

resources.name: Arizona Disabled Veteran Foundation - Emergency Financial Assistance
resources.description: Arizona Disabled Veteran Foundation provides emergency financial assistance to local veterans, Arizona National Guard or Military Reserve members, and their families who face unforeseen hardship, subject to application and board approval.
resources.address: PO Box 39487, Phoenix, AZ 85069
resources.hours: Call or email for current application status, documentation, and funding availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The foundation provides emergency financial assistance to local veterans and their families who have experienced unforeseen hardship. It also describes assistance for Arizona National Guard or Military Reserve members and their families.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Assistance is by application and approval by a panel made up of the Board of Directors. The official page describes case-by-case decisions for unforeseen emergency circumstances and financial need. Current covered expenses, required documents, payment method, and fund availability should be confirmed directly.

**Population Served**
Local Arizona veterans, including disabled and non-disabled veterans, their spouses and in rare cases children, plus Arizona Guard or Reserve members and families facing unforeseen hardship.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-448-3263, email foundationdata@outlook.com, or download the Financial Assistance Form from the official page. Mailing address is PO Box 39487, Phoenix, AZ 85069.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a useful veteran-specific reserve lead but not an entitlement. The official page does not clearly state Mesa-specific coverage, current fund balance, award caps, or whether payments go to vendors or applicants, so confirm those details before relying on assistance.

resources.name: Nobody's Perfect Inc. · DDD Supported Employment and Barry's Bargains Work Site
resources.description: Nobody's Perfect Inc. is a DDD qualified vendor providing supported employment and vocationally based support for adults with developmental disabilities, including community-based thrift store work at Barry's Bargains in Mesa and transportation connected to its vocational day program and enclaves.
resources.address: Barry's Bargains Thrift Store: Power Road and Main Street, Mesa, AZ; main office 18911 E San Tan Boulevard, Queen Creek, AZ 85142
resources.hours: Thrift stores, including Barry's Bargains: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-3:45 PM; not open weekends.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Supported employment services, vocationally based day program supports, community-based thrift store jobs and transportation supports for adults with developmental disabilities. Barry's Bargains Thrift Store at Power Road and Main Street in Mesa is staffed by Group Supported Employment members and support staff.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official site states Nobody's Perfect Inc. is a Qualified Vendor for Arizona Division of Developmental Disabilities supported employment services. Access likely requires DDD eligibility/authorization and coordination through a DDD support coordinator.

**Population Served**
Adults with developmental disabilities and their families, especially people seeking vocational, employment, recreation, socialization and independent-living support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-840-9351 or email admin@nobodysperfectinc.org. Main office: 18911 E San Tan Boulevard, Queen Creek, AZ 85142. Ask about DDD authorization, supported employment and Mesa Barry's Bargains worksite access.

**Important Information to Know**
The site gives store and donation hours but not a formal client intake page. Do not send a client to the thrift store expecting enrollment; confirm service authorization and intake through the main office or DDD support coordinator.

resources.name: Mesa Fire and Medical Department - MFMD Monthly Immunization Clinics
resources.description: Mesa Fire and Medical Department hosts free monthly immunization clinics for eligible children from birth through age 18, plus seasonal flu shots for ages 6 months and older from October through February.
resources.address: Superstition Springs Center, 6555 E. Southern Ave., Mesa, AZ 85206
resources.hours: Second Wednesday of each month, 5:00 PM-7:00 PM. Seasonal flu shots only for ages 6 months and older October-February.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free child immunizations, including Hepatitis A and B, Hib, DTaP, HPV, polio, meningitis, MMR, pneumococcal, rotavirus, varicella, Tdap and seasonal influenza. Free flu shots only are available for anyone age 6 months and older during October through February clinic months.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Child must be uninsured, insured through AHCCCS, covered by an insurance plan that does not cover immunizations, or Native American/Alaskan Native. The city states it can no longer immunize privately insured children whose plans cover immunizations, regardless of deductible.

**Population Served**
Eligible children from birth through age 18 in Mesa, plus seasonal flu-shot recipients age 6 months and older during listed months.

**How to Best Connect**
Clinics are held the second Wednesday of the month from 5:00 PM to 7:00 PM at Superstition Springs Center. The exact mall location can change; text mall concierge at 480-409-7900 or call the mall at 480-924-5050 before arrival. For program questions call 480-644-3459 or Maricopa County at 602-506-6767.

**Important Information to Know**
Bring all immunization records. The clinic location inside the mall is subject to change, so confirm the exact location before going.

resources.name: Paz de Cristo Employment Pathways and Barrier-Removal Services
resources.description: Paz de Cristo is a Mesa basic-needs provider offering meals, showers, clothing, haircuts, document help and barrier-removal supports; its official page states it provides pathways to employment and helps guests obtain tools needed to start or return to work.
resources.address: 424 W Broadway Rd, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Showers are listed Wednesdays 9:00 AM-1:00 PM; contact Paz de Cristo for employment-pathway schedules and document-help availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Paz de Cristo provides hot meals, emergency food boxes, showers, clothing, haircuts, help with adult Arizona IDs and birth certificates, and stated pathways to employment by removing barriers that keep guests from starting or returning to work.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Public pages describe help for neighbors in need who are facing hunger, poverty or homelessness. Specific eligibility and appointment requirements for document help or employment pathways are not fully listed publicly.

**Population Served**
People in Mesa and the East Valley who are experiencing poverty, food insecurity or homelessness and need basic-needs help plus barrier-removal support for work.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit or contact Paz de Cristo at 424 W Broadway Rd in Mesa. Ask specifically about Empower services, document help and employment pathways. Shower hours are listed Wednesdays 9:00 AM-1:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
This is employment-related barrier removal inside a basic-needs community center, not a standalone placement agency. Confirm current staff availability, schedules and whether job placement is direct or referral-based.

resources.name: Feeding America — National food-bank finder
resources.description: Finds regional food banks and their local pantry or meal networks by ZIP code.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Finds regional food banks and their local pantry or meal networks by ZIP code.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public finder has no enrollment requirement; local distribution programs have their own rules.

**Population Served**
People seeking food nationwide, including clients moving or travelling beyond the Mesa service area.

**How to Best Connect**
Enter the client’s intended service ZIP code, then contact the listed food bank about local pickup options.

**Important Information to Know**
A food-bank warehouse is not necessarily a public pantry. The finder does not guarantee hours, a particular item or immediate availability.

resources.name: The Nile Health Network - Day Program / Day Treatment for Adults
resources.description: The Nile Health Network operates a Mesa Day Program / Day Treatment for Adults for adults with developmental disabilities, with DDD authorization and ALTCS approval needed for funding.
resources.address: 500 W. Southern Ave., Suite 33, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Year-round Monday-Friday, 8 hours each day, except New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Day Program / Day Treatment for Adults with developmental disabilities, including community skills exploration, personal care, health oversight, skill acquisition, independence and inclusion activities, and behavioral support or nursing depending on individual needs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The service is authorized by the Division of Developmental Disabilities. The official page states individuals must be approved through Arizona Long Term Care Services (ALTCS) to qualify for funding.

**Population Served**
Adults with developmental disabilities who need a Mesa-based day program and meet DDD/ALTCS funding requirements or another approved payment arrangement.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-307-6810 or use the contact form on the Day Program page. Ask about DDD authorization, ALTCS funding, current availability, nursing/behavioral support needs and transportation.

**Important Information to Know**
Funding and attendance are not automatic. Confirm DDD authorization, ALTCS approval, openings, participant support needs, transportation and any private-pay alternatives before referral.

resources.name: Town of Guadalupe - Community Action Program notary and application support
resources.description: Town of Guadalupe Community Action Program offers free notary services by appointment for Guadalupe residents and computer/phone access to county human-services applications; the notary service can support notarized vital-record or identity-document applications when allowed by the issuing agency.
resources.address: 9241 S Avenida Del Yaqui, Guadalupe, AZ 85283
resources.hours: Food distribution Tuesday 7:00-9:00 AM; notary services are by appointment for Guadalupe residents. Call CAP before visiting for notary or computer access.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Offers appointment-based free notarization for Guadalupe residents and computer or phone access to county human-services applications.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Free notarization is for Guadalupe residents by appointment. The notary and receiving agency each set the applicable proof and document requirements.

**Population Served**
Guadalupe residents needing notarization or help accessing a public-service application.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-730-3080 and request a CAP appointment for the specific service. The office is at 9241 S Avenida Del Yaqui, Guadalupe.

**Important Information to Know**
Notarization is not a guaranteed solution when someone has no acceptable identification. This program does not itself replace IDs or promise payment of document fees; Mesa residents should ask about a service in their own community.

resources.name: Foster Arizona - Foster Arizona Housing Program
resources.description: Foster Arizona Housing Program provides young adults ages 18-24 who are transitioning out of foster care or deemed at risk of homelessness with a safe place to live and support around financial, vocational, educational, personal and housing goals.
resources.hours: Use the website contact route; public page does not list walk-in hours or live openings.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Transitional housing and support for young adults, including a safe place to live and resources while participants work on financial, vocational, educational, personal and housing goals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For young adults ages 18-24 who are transitioning out of foster care or are deemed at risk of homelessness. Exact application steps, current openings, documentation and service geography must be confirmed with Foster Arizona.

**Population Served**
Arizona young adults ages 18-24 connected to foster-care transition or at risk of homelessness.

**How to Best Connect**
Use Foster Arizona's website contact route from the What We Do page to ask about the Young Adult Housing Program and current application steps. Public sources checked did not list a direct phone number or walk-in intake.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a supported program identity but has limited public intake detail. Do not promise immediate housing; confirm location, openings and referral requirements before sending a young adult.

resources.name: Rising Phoenix Wellness Services · Intensive outpatient treatment
resources.description: North Scottsdale intensive outpatient care for substance-use and mental-health concerns, including therapy, psychiatric support and medication-assisted recovery when clinically appropriate. The provider states that it does not accept Medicaid.
resources.address: 21803 N Scottsdale Rd, Building A, Unit 110, Scottsdale, AZ 85255
resources.hours: Admissions inquiries 24/7; treatment sessions are scheduled.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Intensive outpatient treatment combines group and individual therapy, psychiatric support, case management and family involvement. Medication-assisted recovery may form part of an individual treatment plan.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Admissions assesses clinical fit. IOP is for people able to live outside a residential setting; someone needing medical detox or acute crisis care may require another level of care. Ask about age criteria, commercial insurance coverage and self-pay costs. The provider states that it does not accept Medicaid.

**Population Served**

People seeking structured outpatient help for substance-use and/or mental-health concerns in the Scottsdale and Phoenix area.

**How to Best Connect**

Call 480-589-0895 for admissions information; inquiries are accepted 24/7. Treatment is at 21803 N Scottsdale Rd, Building A, Unit 110, Scottsdale, AZ 85255. The website also lists 480-618-4791. Confirm session times and payment arrangements before traveling.

**Important Information to Know**

This record describes outpatient care, not a confirmed methadone dispensing program or on-site residential detox. Virtual IOP is marked as coming soon; do not assume it is available.

resources.name: Arizona Friends of Foster Children Foundation - Focus Forward Fund
resources.description: Arizona Friends of Foster Children Foundation's Focus Forward Fund provides emergency and education-stability assistance to postsecondary students with Arizona foster-care backgrounds so unexpected costs do not derail school or vocational training.
resources.address: 360 E Coronado Rd, Suite 190, Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency and postsecondary-support funding for foster-care-experienced students. Categories include educational, emergency, empowerment, and vocational-study needs. Funds are intended for unexpected costs such as car problems, textbooks, utilities, deposits, or other approved education-stability expenses, not long-term ongoing expenses or non-emergencies.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must have reached age 16 as a ward of the court in Arizona or in tribal foster care in Arizona, be age 16 through 26, and be enrolled in college, university, or an accredited vocational program after high school. AFFCF confirms foster-care eligibility after application. Proof of enrollment, budget, description of need, and documentation are required; employment proof is requested if applicable.

**Population Served**
Arizona foster-care-experienced postsecondary or vocational students ages 16 through 26, including eligible Mesa and Maricopa County students.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Focus Forward Fund application on the AFFCF page. Have proof of enrollment, current-month budget, relevant cost documentation, and a description of need ready. Call AFFCF at 602-252-9445 for questions.

**Important Information to Know**
Requests are committee-reviewed and not guaranteed. Students can make up to two requests per calendar quarter, cannot request the same category more than once in 12 months unless guidelines allow, and no funds are available for purchases made before application and approval. Typical turnaround is two to five business days.

resources.name: Native American Fatherhood and Families Association - NAFFA Wellness Re-Entry / Recovery Modality
resources.description: Native American Fatherhood and Families Association is a Mesa-based organization offering culturally rooted training curricula, including NAFFA Wellness Re-Entry / Recovery Modality training for agencies; direct veteran-client intake for this lead is not confirmed on official public pages.
resources.address: 525 W. Southern Ave., Suite 100, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Official pages confirm training curricula for agencies and facilitators, including NAFFA Wellness Re-Entry / Recovery Modality training, suicide prevention, family strengthening, youth, and family-violence topics.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public training page describes certification-style training for agencies and facilitators, not a direct public intake program for veterans. Any veteran-specific referral eligibility remains unconfirmed.

**Population Served**
Native families and communities are central to NAFFA's work. The submitted lead suggests Native and justice-involved veteran relevance, but official public pages reviewed do not confirm a direct veteran-client service.

**How to Best Connect**
Administrators can contact NAFFA at 480-833-5007 or through the training page to ask whether any local veteran reentry or recovery services accept direct referrals. The office address is 525 W. Southern Ave., Suite 100, Mesa, AZ 85210.

**Important Information to Know**
Do not send a veteran client as though this is a confirmed direct-service intake. Keep as an administrator follow-up lead unless NAFFA confirms veteran referral access, service area, and intake steps.
resources.resolutionReason: Needs resolution: official site verifies organization identity and re-entry/recovery training, but direct veteran-client intake, service scope, and referral pathway are not supported by the official page reviewed.

resources.name: Save the Family · Veteran Family Support and Housing Navigation
resources.description: Save the Family provides family housing and self-sufficiency supports in the East Valley, with specific programs and staff dedicated to military veterans and Valor on Eighth, an affordable housing community created with veteran women and families in mind.
resources.address: Agency intake: 125 E. University Dr., Mesa, AZ 85201. Valor on Eighth housing: 1001 E. 8th St., Tempe, AZ.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM; closed Saturday and Sunday.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Veteran-specific family housing services and Valor on Eighth affordable housing, which was developed with veteran women and families in mind. Save the Family also offers enrolled families case management, career services, budgeting, parenting and life-skills classes, child programmes and in-house mental-health/substance-use counseling. Ask which supports apply to the particular veteran or housing programme.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on Save the Family program, family status, housing need, availability, and referral or application route. Veteran-specific openings and Valor on Eighth criteria are not fully published on the page.

**Population Served**
East Valley families, including military veteran families and veteran women/families connected to Valor on Eighth.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Save the Family at 480-898-0228 or use its Find Help route. Agency intake is at 125 E. University Drive, Mesa, with posted Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM–5:00 PM office hours. Ask specifically about veteran-family services or Valor on Eighth, a separate housing property at 1001 E. 8th St., Tempe. Confirm the actual appointment or leasing location before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
The Mesa agency office is not the Valor residence. Eligibility, referrals and openings vary by programme; no immediate shelter bed, vacancy or unrestricted access to all family services is promised.

resources.name: Community Bridges - Mesa Heritage Integrated Outpatient Care
resources.description: Community Bridges Mesa Heritage Clinic is a Health Homes/outpatient integrated-care location offering behavioral-health, psychiatric medication, addiction medicine, MAT, counseling, case management, peer support and primary-care related services.
resources.phone: CBI access 888-224-2087; appointments 888-224-6593; Mercy Care-listed clinic 480-838-5550
resources.address: 460 N Mesa Dr, Suite 201, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Call for appointments and current programme availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Coordinated outpatient physical and behavioral care, psychiatric medication management, addiction medicine/MAT, counseling, case management and peer support. Ask about clinic-specific ACT, intensive outpatient and ambulatory withdrawal-management pathways and their current referral requirements.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adults are screened for clinical fit, payer authorization and the requested programme. Mercy Care ACC-RBHA members with SMI have a specifically listed integrated-health-home pathway and should coordinate with their case manager. Other patients should ask CBI which clinic and enrollment route fit.

**Population Served**
Mesa residents and other Arizona clients needing coordinated outpatient physical, behavioral and substance-use care.

**How to Best Connect**
Call CBI access at 888-224-2087 or scheduling at 888-224-6593 and ask for Mesa Heritage, 460 N. Mesa Dr., Suite 201. Mercy Care lists 480-838-5550 for the clinic; its SMI members should also contact their case manager. Confirm the particular service and appointment before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
This is outpatient/integrated care, not the CPEC crisis receiving centre. ACT, withdrawal management, intensive outpatient and health-home services have different clinical and funding criteria; a clinic listing does not guarantee immediate admission to each programme.

resources.name: Society of St. Vincent de Paul - Companion Animal Program
resources.description: St. Vincent de Paul's Companion Animal Program helps people experiencing or at risk of homelessness keep pets safe and cared for through pet pantry supplies, shelter/transitional-housing pet support, wellness clinics and appointment-based basic veterinary care.
resources.address: Mesa Dining Room: 49 W Broadway Rd, Mesa, AZ 85210; Companion Animal Clinic: 310 W Watkins Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.hours: Pet pantry availability depends on SVdP site schedules; veterinary clinic appointments are required.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Pet food and supplies through SVdP pet pantries, wellness support, vaccinations, microchipping, licensing help, basic veterinary care by appointment, and support to keep owners and companion animals together during homelessness or shelter stays.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For pet owners experiencing or at risk of homelessness and for economically vulnerable pet owners using SVdP services. Veterinary services are appointment-based and are not emergency animal care.

**Population Served**
People experiencing or at risk of homelessness with companion animals, including Mesa guests using the Mesa Dining Room pet pantry and clients able to access Phoenix clinic services.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-329-5034 or ask staff at an SVdP dining room or shelter about Companion Animal Program access. Use the Mesa Dining Room for local pet pantry inquiries and the Phoenix clinic for appointment-based basic veterinary care.

**Important Information to Know**
This program reduces a real shelter barrier for pet owners, but it is not a full-service emergency veterinary hospital. Current clinic appointment availability, spay/neuter timing and Mesa pantry inventory should be confirmed before referral.

resources.name: Terros Health - Javelina Health Center
resources.description: Terros Health Mesa justice-services health center partnered with Maricopa County Adult Probation, offering whole-person care for people on probation, including counseling, substance-use treatment, medication services, MAT, care coordination and social-services enrollment.
resources.address: 222 E. Javelina Ave., Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Clinic and telehealth Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM; weekends and federal holidays closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Javelina Health Center provides primary medical care, telehealth, Medicaid eligibility help, social-services enrollment, care coordination, individual counseling, substance-use treatment, justice services, medication services and medication-assisted treatment. Terros describes the center as part of a partnership with Maricopa County Adult Probation to provide whole-health care to people on probation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
People on probation or otherwise connected to justice services should call to confirm referral route, payer requirements and whether self-referral is allowed for the needed service. Some services may require probation, court, AHCCCS or Terros referral.

**Population Served**
Adults in Mesa/Maricopa County with justice-system involvement, especially people on Maricopa County Adult Probation needing integrated behavioral-health, substance-use, primary-care and reentry stabilization support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Javelina Health Center at 480-364-0406. For general Terros appointment routing, call 602-685-6000. The site is at 222 E Javelina Ave, Mesa, AZ 85210.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not the same as a general Terros outpatient clinic. Confirm whether the client should use Javelina, Bridging the Gap, adult probation, or another Terros site, and ask whether probation/court referral is required.

resources.name: First Place Global - Maricopa County IDA Center for Education, Training & Employment / Be Ready Jobseekers
resources.description: First Place Global's Maricopa County IDA Center for Education, Training & Employment prepares individuals with autism and/or intellectual/developmental disabilities for employment through Be Open + Be Ready, Be Ready Jobseekers, work readiness and workforce/workplace development.
resources.address: 3001 N. 3rd St., Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.hours: Enroll or contact through the website; program schedules, costs and resident/non-resident access should be confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Workforce and workplace development for people with autism and/or intellectual/developmental disabilities. The employment page lists the Maricopa County IDA Center for Education, Training & Employment, Be Open + Be Ready, Be Ready Jobseekers, Learn4Independence, job readiness, job search and preparation, onboarding and task programs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The page supports a focus on neurodiverse individuals and people with autism and/or I/DD, but does not fully spell out eligibility, costs, cohort requirements or whether every service is open beyond First Place-Phoenix residents. Confirm before referral.

**Population Served**
Neurodiverse adults and people with autism and/or intellectual/developmental disabilities in Maricopa County who need work-readiness or employment preparation.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the employment page's Be Ready Jobseekers enrollment link or the First Place Global contact route. The page lists 3001 N. 3rd St., Phoenix and 602-464-6610.

**Important Information to Know**
Some employment metrics on the page refer specifically to First Place-Phoenix residents. Do not promise open enrollment, job placement or low/no cost until First Place confirms program fit.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Economic Security - Arizona Refugee Resettlement Program
resources.description: Arizona Department of Economic Security administers the Arizona Refugee Resettlement Program, which coordinates benefits and contracted services for eligible refugees and other ORR-eligible newcomers. For ID recovery, this is a population-specific route for navigating immigration/status documentation and benefit records through DES and contracted resettlement agencies.
resources.hours: Call DES or use the DES Refugee Resettlement Program page to identify the correct contracted provider and intake route; hours and appointment rules vary by provider.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
DES coordinates eligible refugee/humanitarian newcomer services, including cash and medical assistance information, domestic medical examinations, health promotion, case management and contracted-provider referrals. Agencies can help navigate status documentation and benefit records.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Refugees and other ORR-eligible populations, including qualifying asylees, Cuban/Haitian entrants, SIV holders and trafficking survivors, are screened under status, income and programme rules. DES describes RCA/RMA limits of up to eight months for qualifying dates from January 1, 2026, or up to four months for earlier dates; each benefit has its own eligibility.

**Population Served**
Eligible refugees and ORR-eligible newcomers living in Arizona, including clients in Maricopa County. Programmes include eligible refugee households and families, needs-based cash assistance, and income-tested medical assistance for some people denied or losing AHCCCS coverage.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact the assigned resettlement agency or DES Refugee Resettlement at 602-542-4446 ext. 4 to identify the correct local provider. Benefits applications may use FAA or Health-e-Arizona Plus; ask which route fits the client’s status and dates.

**Important Information to Know**
This is coordination/navigation, not a general ID-replacement office. Initial medical screening generally has a separate 90-day window. A refugee FAA office’s first-year routing rule does not extend cash or medical benefit duration. RMA is separate from AHCCCS Medicaid.

resources.name: Veterans Medical Leadership Council - Returning Warrior Veteran Crisis Assistance
resources.description: Veterans Medical Leadership Council's Returning Warrior Program provides limited crisis financial assistance for Maricopa County veterans, usually through Phoenix VA Health Care System social-worker referral. Help may include rent or mortgage, utilities, auto repair, food, transportation, clothing, and other basic needs paid directly to the payee.
