resources.description: The Salvation Army Mesa Silvercrest is a HUD Section 8/202 subsidized senior residence in Mesa offering studio and one-bedroom apartments for qualified seniors age 62+ and people with disabilities.
resources.address: 255 E 6th St, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Call the residence for current intake, waitlist and office hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Low-income subsidized independent apartments through The Salvation Army Silvercrest Senior Residence program, including one-bedroom and studio units for qualified residents.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page says Silvercrest residences serve seniors age 62 and older and people with disabilities who qualify through HUD Section 8/202 programs.

**Population Served**
Low-income seniors and people with disabilities seeking subsidized housing in Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Call The Salvation Army Mesa Silvercrest at 480-649-9117. The residence is at 255 E 6th St, Mesa, AZ 85201.

**Important Information to Know**
The public page confirms the residence and eligibility population but does not publish current vacancies, rent, wait time or an online application. Contact the residence before sending a client.

resources.name: VA Phoenix Veteran Transportation Service
resources.description: Phoenix VA Veteran Transportation Service provides veteran-specific buses, shuttles, and wheelchair-accessible transportation for patients, separate from ambulatory-only DAV vans.
resources.address: 650 East Indian School Road, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.hours: Call contacts directly to schedule and confirm hours, eligibility, and route availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Veteran Transportation Service offers veteran-specific transportation, including buses, shuttles, and wheelchair-accessible transport for VA patients.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For eligible VA health-care patients needing covered health appointments. Confirm appointment authorization, Mesa pickup coverage, advance notice and capacity with Phoenix VA. Special-mode transport such as a wheelchair van or stretcher may require medical-necessity authorization and provider involvement; it is not the same pathway as ambulatory-only DAV vans.

**Population Served**
VA Phoenix health-care patients needing transportation, including veterans with mobility needs in central Arizona and Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Phoenix VA at 602-277-5551 and ask for Veteran Transportation Service; current listed contacts include ext. 7799, with alternates 7650 or 7642. Named contacts include Marzette King (marzette.king@va.gov) and William Ihle (william.ihle@va.gov). If staffing has changed, use the main line for routing. Book ahead and confirm the specific trip and accessibility needs.

**Important Information to Know**
This is scheduled medical transportation, not emergency transportation. Confirm whether a specific Mesa pickup address, wheelchair need, caregiver rider, and appointment type can be served.

resources.name: Maricopa County Justice Courts — eviction case resources
resources.description: Court information about eviction cases, forms and links to tenant legal-help resources.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Court information about eviction cases, forms and links to tenant legal-help resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Use the Justice Court and precinct handling the actual case. A separate provider determines legal-aid eligibility.

**Population Served**
Tenants and other parties in Maricopa County Justice Court eviction matters.

**How to Best Connect**
Read the case paperwork for the court, hearing date and response instructions, then use the court website’s eviction resources.

**Important Information to Know**
Court information is not legal representation. Do not use the county Human Services general number as the court’s case-contact number or miss a hearing while seeking help.

resources.name: Valleywise Health - Mesa Assertive Community Treatment
resources.description: Valleywise Assertive Community Treatment in Mesa is an intensive team-based program for people with serious mental illness, offering community or clinic-based support, counseling, medication support, substance-use treatment, peer/family support, housing and employment assistance, case management, crisis intervention, and 24/7 on-call support for ACT members.
resources.address: 570 W Brown Rd, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: ACT office hours Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; 24/7 on-call support is available to enrolled ACT members.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Flexible team-based treatment at home or in clinic for people with serious mental illness, including substance-abuse treatment, medication support, counseling, recovery education, peer support, health promotion, family support and education, housing and employment assistance, skills training, crisis intervention, care coordination and case management.

**Eligibility Requirements**
ACT is not general walk-in care. It is intended for people with serious mental illness and high service needs, and access is usually determined through clinical eligibility, behavioral-health system assignment and team capacity.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County adults assigned or referred to the Mesa ACT team who need intensive ongoing support for serious mental illness.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the ACT direct number at 480-344-2255 or Valleywise scheduling at 1-833-855-9973. The Mesa location is Valleywise Behavioral Health Center - Mesa, 570 W Brown Rd.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a specialty program with eligibility limits, not routine outpatient therapy or an emergency room. People in immediate behavioral-health crisis should use 988 or the regional crisis line; existing ACT members may use the team's on-call support.

resources.name: Traditions Transitional Living
resources.description: Phoenix transitional living program for people in recovery, with intake office hours, phone/email access, and modest client fees that do not fully cover program costs.
resources.address: 2429 W Vista Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85021
resources.hours: Office/intake hours listed: Monday-Thursday 9am-10pm; Friday 9am-12am; Saturday 9am-12am; Sunday no intake, meetings only. Confirm before travel because page has a duplicated Saturday label.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Traditions Transitional Living provides transitional living support for people in recovery. The official page describes a privately funded program with modest client fees and intake office hours.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Specific sobriety, program, gender, background, and payment eligibility rules are not listed on the public page. Prospective clients should call or email for intake screening and house/program requirements.

**Population Served**
People seeking transitional living support in substance-use recovery in the Phoenix/Maricopa County area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-535-5958 or email traditionstransliving@hotmail.com. The mailing/location address listed is 2429 W Vista Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85021.

**Important Information to Know**
The page says client fees are modest but does not list exact cost. Confirm current openings, house rules, fees, transportation expectations, and whether the program matches the client's recovery stage before referral.

resources.name: Chrysalis - Emergency Shelter, Transitional Housing, Counseling, and Lay Legal Advocacy
resources.description: Chrysalis provides a 24/7 domestic-violence hotline and integrated survivor services including emergency shelter, transitional housing, counseling, case management, transportation, basic-needs help, safety planning, court accompaniment and lay legal advocacy.
resources.address: 2055 W Northern Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85021
resources.hours: 24/7 support hotline: 602-955-9059. Public office/service schedules should be confirmed by phone.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
24-hour domestic-violence hotline, emergency shelter, transportation, case management, safety planning, basic-needs assistance, adult and child counseling, support groups, transitional housing for up to two years, economic advocacy, lay legal advocacy, court accompaniment and legal-resource navigation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For individuals and families impacted by domestic abuse. Shelter and housing require hotline/intake screening and depend on safety fit and availability.

**Population Served**
Domestic-abuse survivors and families in Phoenix and Maricopa County, including Mesa-area survivors who can access the hotline and are accepted through screening.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Chrysalis' 24-hour hotline at 602-955-9059 for immediate domestic-violence support and placement guidance. The listed address is a public contact address, not a confirmed confidential shelter location.

**Important Information to Know**
Lay legal advocates do not provide legal advice. Housing, transportation and basic-needs help depend on program intake, eligibility and current resources.

resources.name: Native American Connections - Native American Coordinated Entry
resources.description: Native American Connections provides a coordinated-entry access point where Native American individuals experiencing homelessness can begin a Maricopa County Coordinated Entry housing assessment and connection to housing resources and services.
resources.hours: Official page does not publish a walk-in schedule for NAC coordinated entry; begin by phone or email.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Coordinated-entry assessment and routing for Native American individuals experiencing homelessness, helping clients begin the regional housing assessment process and access housing resources and services when available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Native American individuals experiencing homelessness. Assessment does not guarantee shelter, housing placement or a subsidy.

**Population Served**
Native American individuals experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County, including Mesa residents who can use the phone/email route.

**How to Best Connect**
Call NAC's Housing Specialist at 602-648-9739 or email PSHinquiry@nativeconnections.org to start the housing assessment process and ask whether an in-person appointment is needed.

**Important Information to Know**
Start by phone or email; no Mesa walk-in schedule is published. Assessment does not guarantee shelter, a subsidy or housing placement. Families should use Family Housing Hub at 602-595-8700; youth and other single adults have separate coordinated-entry routes.

resources.name: Area Agency on Aging, Region One - Caring Circles AmeriCorps
resources.description: Area Agency on Aging, Region One's Caring Circles AmeriCorps program provides social support to older adults, including medical rides, grocery shopping, friendly visits and technology help.
resources.address: 1366 E. Thomas Rd., Suite 108, Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.hours: Access through the 24-Hour Senior HELP LINE.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Social support for older adults such as transportation to medical appointments, grocery shopping, friendly visits and help with technology. The program also offers AmeriCorps service roles with a stipend, education award, training and professional development for eligible members.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Client eligibility, service frequency and Mesa coverage are not fully listed on the public page and should be screened through the Senior HELP LINE. The listed age-55 requirement applies to AmeriCorps members, who must also have reliable transportation and obtain an Arizona Level One Fingerprint Clearance Card.

**Population Served**
Older adults needing social-support help, and adults age 55+ interested in structured AmeriCorps service.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Area Agency on Aging Senior HELP LINE at 602-264-HELP (4357) or toll-free 888-783-7500 and ask about Caring Circles AmeriCorps client support or member opportunities. Text access is listed at 520-775-1899.

**Important Information to Know**
The public page gives examples of client support but limited client eligibility details. Availability, Mesa coverage, frequency and waitlists must be confirmed through intake.

resources.name: Gila River Indian Community - Enrollment/Census Office tribal ID and CIB services
resources.description: Gila River Indian Community's Enrollment/Census Department issues and manages tribal enrollment records, Tribal Identification cards and Certificates of Indian Blood. It also supports address updates and mail-in/notarized request options for some records for eligible members or applicants.
resources.address: 525 West Gu u Ki, Sacaton, AZ 85147
resources.hours: Call 520-562-9790 to confirm hours, appointments, fees, mail-in options and required proof before visiting or mailing requests.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Enrollment and census services, Tribal Identification cards, Certificates of Indian Blood, enrollment processing, address updates and mail-in or notarized request options for some records.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Gila River Indian Community members and eligible applicants. The Community determines enrollment, ID and certificate requirements.

**Population Served**
Gila River Indian Community members and eligible applicants, including people near southeast Maricopa County and Mesa who need tribal documentation.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 520-562-9790 before visiting 525 West Gu u Ki, Sacaton, AZ 85147. Ask which documents, forms, notarization and fees are required for the specific ID or certificate request.

**Important Information to Know**
The office is outside Mesa and services are restricted to members or eligible applicants. Tribal ID or CIB documents may be important supporting proof for Arizona ID, benefits, voting or services.

resources.name: Universal Service Administrative Company / FCC - Lifeline
resources.description: Federal Lifeline provides eligible households a monthly discount on phone, internet or bundled service through participating providers after National Verifier approval.
resources.address: Mail only: Lifeline Support Center, PO Box 1000, Horseheads, NY 14845
resources.hours: Support Center: 7 days a week, 9:00 AM-9:00 PM Eastern Time.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Lifeline gives qualifying households a monthly discount of up to $9.25 on phone, internet or bundled service. Households on qualifying Tribal lands may receive an enhanced discount up to $34.25.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Qualify through household income at or below 135% of the federal poverty level or accepted benefits such as SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, Federal Public Housing Assistance, Veterans Pension/Survivors Benefit or qualifying Tribal programmes. Generally, one Lifeline benefit is allowed per household. Enhanced support requires a qualifying Tribal-land address.

**Population Served**
Eligible low-income households nationwide, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents whose address is served by a participating provider. The program also describes extra safeguards for survivors of domestic violence or human trafficking.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through LifelineSupport.org/National Verifier, then choose a participating provider after approval. Call 800-234-9473 or email LifelineSupport@usac.org for help. Mail applications to Lifeline Support Center, PO Box 1000, Horseheads, NY 14845.

**Important Information to Know**
Annual recertification may be required; report relevant changes within 30 days. Free-service plans generally require use at least once every 30 days. Provider, plan, device costs and actual address coverage vary; a free device is not guaranteed. Lifeline is separate from the expired Affordable Connectivity Program.

resources.name: Air & Space Forces Aid Society — Standard Assistance
resources.description: Interest-free loans or grants for qualifying Air Force and Space Force emergencies, including basic living costs, vehicle or home repairs, medical needs, furniture, adoption, family emergencies and domestic-violence support.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Interest-free loans or grants for qualifying Air Force and Space Force emergencies, including basic living costs, vehicle or home repairs, medical needs, furniture, adoption, family emergencies and domestic-violence support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligible groups include active-duty members and dependents, Guard/Reserve members regardless of duty status, retirees receiving retirement pay, and specified survivors. Academy and basic-training students have limited emergency-travel eligibility. Spouse applications need the required military identification and authority.

**Population Served**
Qualifying Air Force and Space Force members and families, including Arizona households.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through portal.afas.org and upload the requested budget and documents. An AFAS caseworker determines the appropriate help. Use the national number for questions; local Luke intake details should be confirmed.

**Important Information to Know**
An award may be a repayable loan. Loans generally run 12 months, cannot exceed 24 months, and must be repaid within the current enlistment. Approved assistance is paid to the member by Zelle or bank ACH.

resources.name: VFW Dode Morris Post 1760 - Medical Equipment Loan Program
resources.description: VFW Dode Morris Post 1760 in Mesa loans donated medical equipment to veterans and veteran family members, including wheelchairs, walkers, a motorized scooter when available, walking boots, shower chairs, canes, crutches, and a wheelchair trailer hitch.
resources.address: 65 S. MacDonald, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Normal post hours listed as Sunday-Thursday 10:00 AM-9:00 PM; Friday-Saturday 10:00 AM-11:00 PM. Call to confirm equipment-loan availability before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Loans donated medical equipment such as wheelchairs, walkers, walking boots, shower chairs, canes, crutches, a wheelchair trailer hitch, and a motorized scooter when available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Borrowers must show proof of being a veteran, such as VFW membership, another veteran-organization membership, military ID, or similar proof, plus current contact information. Motorized scooter loans may require a deposit and/or VFW membership.

**Population Served**
Veterans and veteran family members in the Mesa area who need temporary medical equipment.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-964-9937 or use the VFW contact route before visiting. The post is at 65 S. MacDonald, Mesa, AZ 85210.

**Important Information to Know**
Inventory changes because equipment is donated. Scooter availability is especially limited and has additional requirements. Confirm availability and pickup arrangements before sending a veteran.

resources.name: Salvation Army Chandler — heat respite
resources.description: Offers heat respite and basic daytime support at the Salvation Army Chandler site.
resources.address: 85 E Saragosa Street, Chandler, AZ
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Offers heat respite and basic daytime support at the Salvation Army Chandler site.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Confirm the current seasonal operating dates, entry rules and available amenities before travel.

**Population Served**
Unhoused people and other vulnerable residents seeking relief from heat in Chandler.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask Chandler Community Connection at 4807824349 to confirm the Salvation Army site at 85 ESaragosa Street and the current schedule.

**Important Information to Know**
The City describes cots, showers, laundry, meals and pet access, but its article does not establish that the older May–September 9 a.m.–7 p.m. schedule remains current in 2026. Day respite is not proof of overnight shelter.

resources.name: La Frontera EMPACT-Suicide Prevention Center - Trauma Healing Services
resources.description: La Frontera EMPACT-SPC Trauma Healing Services provides free, confidential services for victims of crime, including domestic violence, sexual assault, trafficking, stalking, assault, hate crime, homicide-survivor, and other victimization-related trauma support.
resources.address: Mesa Family Advocacy Center, 225 E. 1st St., Mesa, AZ 85201; services also listed in Tempe, Phoenix, Mesa, and Glendale
resources.hours: Trauma/sexual assault hotline 480-736-4949 is listed as 24/7. Appointments and Mesa service location should be confirmed by phone.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free crime-victim trauma support: a round-the-clock hotline with mobile crisis help, individual/family therapy for up to 20 sessions, groups and advocacy. Advocates explain victim rights and compensation, help with police reports and protective-order forms, coordinate sexual-assault forensic exams and connect people with resources. Group options include trauma/wellness skills, parent-focused support, separate men’s and women’s trauma groups, and an ASU sexual-violence healing pathway.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For crime victims and people affected by another person’s victimization, including domestic or dating violence, physical or sexual abuse, trafficking, stalking, neglect and other listed crimes. The programme serves all ages and genders, with English and Spanish services. Call to confirm the particular service, group, location, screening and current capacity.

**Population Served**
Crime victims and survivors in Maricopa County service areas, including Mesa, Tempe, Phoenix, and Glendale. The program includes domestic-violence, sexual-assault, trafficking, stalking, and other victimization-related trauma needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Trauma Healing Services at 480-736-4949 or 866-205-5229 for intake and the appropriate location. When referred to Mesa Family Advocacy Center, confirm the appointment and entrance at 225 E 1st St, Mesa; embedded services are not a general walk-in clinic.

**Important Information to Know**
This is crime-victim trauma support and advocacy, not a domestic-violence shelter or general outpatient counseling program. Confirm whether services will occur at Mesa Family Advocacy Center, telehealth, or another EMPACT location.

resources.name: South Mountain WORKS - harm-reduction and overdose-prevention outreach
resources.description: South Mountain WORKS provides youth substance-use prevention, harm-reduction education, community outreach and county-funded overdose-prevention/naloxone outreach focused on African American churches and communities.
resources.address: 6825 S 7th St, Suite 8516, Phoenix, AZ 85042
resources.hours: Program and outreach schedules vary; contact the coalition for current presentations, outreach and community events.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Substance-use prevention, harm-reduction information, presentations, workshops, town halls, public information campaigns, peer leadership activities and Maricopa County-supported overdose-prevention/naloxone outreach through community and church-based partnerships.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public sources do not list individual eligibility rules. Services appear to be community, youth, school, church and coalition-partner oriented; contact the coalition to request or locate current programming.

**Population Served**
South Phoenix and Maricopa County community members, with youth prevention work and county-supported outreach focused on African American churches and communities.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-730-4428 or email harmreduction@southmountainworks.org. The coalition address is 6825 S 7th St #8516, Phoenix, AZ 85042.

**Important Information to Know**
This is prevention and harm-reduction outreach, not detox or clinical treatment. Confirm current event or naloxone distribution details before referral.

resources.name: Justa Center - Resource & Day Center Path to Housing for Homeless Seniors
resources.description: Justa Center is a resource and day center for adults 55+ experiencing homelessness, offering in-person intake, day services, document help, benefits access and personalized Path to Housing support.
resources.address: 1001 W. Jefferson Street, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.hours: Member services daily 7:00 AM-2:30 PM; June-October 7:00 AM-7:30 PM. Intake interviews daily 7:00 AM-9:00 AM, first come, first served, max 6 per day, no phone intakes or holiday intakes.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Day/resource services include meals, showers, laundry, lockers, mail, secure original-document storage, computer/printer access, benefits partners, veteran outreach, a nurse clinic and housing navigation. Path to Housing helps gather IDs, Social Security cards, birth certificates and DD214s for housing applications.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For adults age 55 or older experiencing homelessness. Day Center membership begins with an intake interview on the first visit.

**Population Served**
Homeless seniors age 55+ in the Phoenix/Maricopa region, including older veterans and medically vulnerable seniors.

**How to Best Connect**
Go in person to 1001 W. Jefferson Street, Phoenix. Intake interviews are daily 7:00 AM-9:00 AM; suggested arrival 6:30 AM; first come, first served; maximum 6 intakes per day. No phone intakes or holiday intakes. Call 602-254-6524 or email info@justacenter.org with questions.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a day/resource centre, not overnight shelter. Housing or document-fee payment is not guaranteed; ask about out-of-state records. Phoenix travel and the maximum six new intakes per day matter, especially for Mesa clients. Intake is not available by phone or on holidays.

resources.name: Pitchfork Pantry - ASU Polytechnic Food Pantry
resources.description: Pitchfork Pantry provides free food, rescued groceries, toiletries, clothing and resources for Arizona State University students, including a Polytechnic campus location in Mesa.
resources.address: Student Success Center, CNTR 160, Mesa, AZ 85212
resources.hours: Current Polytechnic pantry hours are not visible on the opened homepage; confirm through Pitchfork Pantry or ASU before travel.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free food, fresh produce, rescued groceries, toiletries, essential clothing and resources for ASU students through weekly distributions and campus pantry locations.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are for college students/ASU students experiencing need. The opened page does not show the specific verification process or Polytechnic hours.

**Population Served**
Arizona State University students, including students at the Polytechnic campus in Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Pitchfork Pantry website's Get Food/Contact options and confirm Polytechnic campus hours before travel. The listed Polytechnic location is Student Success Center, CNTR 160, Mesa, AZ 85212.

**Important Information to Know**
This is student-limited. Do not send non-students as a general public food pantry referral.

resources.name: Community Housing Partnership, Inc. - Low-Income Housing Application
resources.description: Community Housing Partnership, Inc. provides permanent low-income housing for individuals and families in the Phoenix metropolitan area and offers a public apply-for-housing pathway through eligibility review, property viewing and online application.
resources.address: 609 N. 9th Street, Phoenix, AZ 85006; mailing address PO Box 7387, Mesa, AZ 85216
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Permanent low-income rental housing for individuals and families, with an online process to check eligibility, view properties and apply. Property management is handled through Beehive Property Management.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must meet the provider's low-income housing requirements and any property-specific requirements. Current openings, income limits, screening criteria and waitlist status must be confirmed during application.

**Population Served**
Individuals and families seeking low-income housing in the Phoenix metropolitan area. This may be useful for Mesa clients who can live in the broader metro area.

**How to Best Connect**
Start with the Apply for Housing page, which links to eligibility, property viewing and the application. Call 602-253-6905 or email website@chpaz.org for questions.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not emergency shelter. Properties are Phoenix-metro rather than Mesa-specific, and availability may be limited by property openings and screening.

resources.name: The Salvation Army Mesa Corps - Utility and Rent Assistance Inquiry
resources.description: The Salvation Army Mesa Corps is a local emergency-assistance access point for Mesa households, including utility assistance when funds and provider programs are available, and possible referral or screening for other local needs.
resources.address: 241 E 6th St, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Call before visiting; services and registration vary by location and current funding.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Local Salvation Army emergency assistance may include utility help, food, and referral or screening for other basic needs. The candidate specifically identifies utility and rent-assistance inquiry through the Mesa Corps.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on the Mesa Corps' current service area, utility provider or assistance fund, household need, documentation, and available funds. Rent assistance is not confirmed as a standing general benefit and should be asked about separately.

**Population Served**
Mesa-area households seeking emergency help through the local Salvation Army corps.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Mesa Corps at 480-962-9103 before visiting the E 6th Street location. The Southwest Division advises contacting the local Salvation Army for up-to-date service and registration information.

**Important Information to Know**
Availability changes by location and date. Do not promise rental aid or unrestricted cash; ask which utility or emergency-assistance funds are open and what documents the client must bring.
resources.resolutionReason: Earlier delivery assigned two permanent IDs to this reviewed programme. Preserve both aliases and human state; present the secondary record to administrators for duplicate reconciliation. No registry migration, deletion or automatic unpublishing. Reconcile with sr_67f3f61ed3b950ada4597ec6122c7fea.

resources.name: Social Security Administration - replacement Social Security card service
resources.description: Social Security Administration provides the official free replacement Social Security card process. Applicants may be able to start online, or may need an appointment at a local office or card center; approved cards are mailed.
resources.address: Use SSA online start, appointment scheduler and office locator to confirm the current card-service location; do not rely on an old local office address without checking.
resources.hours: National phone support is listed Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-7:00 PM in most U.S. time zones. Office/card-center hours depend on the current SSA locator and appointment notice.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides free replacement Social Security card requests. Some applicants can start and complete the request online; others must make an appointment at a local office or card center.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be eligible for the requested Social Security card action and must provide required identity and citizenship or immigration-status evidence when SSA asks for it.

**Population Served**
People eligible for a replacement Social Security card, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Start at SSA's replacement-card page or call 800-772-1213 and say the request is for a replacement Social Security card. Use SSA's current locator and appointment process before sending a client in person. Local offices do not print cards; approved replacement cards are mailed.

**Important Information to Know**
SSA says the replacement card is free and is mailed after the request is completed, typically in 5 to 10 business days. Many situations do not require a physical card if the person knows the number, but employers or agencies may still request it. People without stable mailing or identity documents may need assistance before applying.

resources.name: ICNA Relief Arizona - Food Pantry and Mobile Pantry Services
resources.description: ICNA Relief Arizona operates a Tempe community food pantry and multiple mobile food pantry locations, with a Muslim-led humanitarian service model.
resources.address: 5030 S. Mill Ave, Suite C5, Tempe, AZ 85282; mobile pantry sites in Phoenix, Tempe and Glendale
resources.hours: Tempe pantry Sundays 10:00 AM-1:00 PM. Other mobile sites include 1st/3rd Friday 2:00-4:00 PM at ICCP Phoenix, 2nd Thursday 2:30-4:30 PM at St. Margaret Catholic Church in Tempe, 3rd Wednesday 9:00-11:00 AM at Casa Pedro Senior Housing, and 4th Wednesday 1:00-3:00 PM at UICA Glendale.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Groceries and pantry food through ICNA Relief Community Food Pantry in Tempe and recurring mobile food pantry distributions around Maricopa County.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official Arizona page lists pantry locations and times but does not publish income, residence, document or visit-frequency rules. Call the food pantry coordinator before first referral.

**Population Served**
People and families needing food assistance who can reach the Tempe pantry or one of the mobile pantry sites.

**How to Best Connect**
For food pantry information, contact coordinator Ahmad Seyam Behroz at 480-590-2564 or ahmad.behroz@icnarelief.org. The Tempe pantry is at 5030 S. Mill Ave, Suite C5.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm the distribution and any documents before travel. The Arizona office can also answer questions about its separate diaper and community-assistance programmes. A national refugee-services link does not establish local immigration legal help or refugee case management.

resources.name: City of Mesa - Coordinated Mental-Health Crisis Response
resources.description: City of Mesa coordinated mental-health crisis response routes emergencies through 911, crisis support through 988, and may involve police, fire/medical, Solari, behavioral-health professionals or crisis teams depending on safety and clinical need.
resources.hours: Emergency response 24/7 through 911; 988 crisis support 24/7.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Coordinated public-safety and behavioral-health response for mental-health crisis, including dispatcher assessment, possible police/fire/medical response, connection with Solari or other crisis resources, crisis teams with behavioral-health professionals and emergency medical support, and Mesa Police Mental Health Support Team assistance with detainers, provider coordination and recurring crisis needs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Use for people in the City of Mesa experiencing a mental-health crisis or safety concern. 911 is for emergencies and immediate danger; 988 is for crisis support when emergency response is not required.

**Population Served**
People in Mesa experiencing crisis signs such as suicidal thoughts, intense anxiety or depression, substance-use crisis, family concerns, dementia/elder-related issues, disorientation, hallucinations or behaviors that may require evaluation or support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 911 for emergencies or immediate danger. Call or text 988 for crisis support. Dispatch determines whether police, fire/medical, behavioral-health resources, Solari or a combined response is appropriate.

**Important Information to Know**
This is crisis response and referral, not continuing therapy. The response may include police, fire/medical or behavioural-health teams according to dispatch assessment, safety and legal criteria. A specific team, transport or receiving facility is not guaranteed; a mental-health detainer may be used when legally appropriate.

resources.name: True North Transitional Living - Transitional Living and Case Management
resources.description: True North Transitional Living is a Mesa nonprofit describing transitional housing and case management support for homeless individuals, with phone and staff email contact routes.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Transitional housing programs and case management support focused on physical health, relationships and psychological well-being for homeless individuals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public site does not list detailed eligibility, costs, referral source, address or availability. Call or email to confirm admission requirements before referral.

**Population Served**
Homeless individuals in Mesa seeking transitional living and case management support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 805-407-3639, email sarahl@truenorthtransitionalliving.org, or email cmcnew@truenorthtransitionalliving.org.

**Important Information to Know**
The website has limited operational detail. Before arranging transportation, confirm the actual residence, whether housing is directly provided, admission requirements, costs and current openings. A mailing address is not a confirmed residential intake site.

resources.name: Arizona Public Service - Safety Net
resources.description: APS Safety Net lets APS customers designate a trusted person to receive bill copies and past-due notices and help set up payment arrangements, reducing risk of missed bills and service disruption.
resources.address: Mail application to APS, P.O. Box 53933, Phoenix, AZ 85072-9207
resources.hours: Apply online, by mail or by phone.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Safety Net lets an APS customer choose a friend or relative to receive a copy of the monthly energy bill, past-due notifications and the ability to help set up a payment arrangement.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The customer must have an APS account and designate a Safety Net partner. The partner is not financially responsible for the account.

**Population Served**
APS customers who want a trusted reminder partner, including older adults, medically vulnerable customers, people with disabilities or customers who need help tracking bills.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online from the APS Safety Net page, mail the application to APS at P.O. Box 53933, Phoenix, AZ 85072-9207, or call 602-371-7171 or 800-253-9405 to apply by phone.

**Important Information to Know**
Safety Net does not provide money, waive bills or automatically authorize full account management. It is a reminder and support tool; APS Guest Roles are a separate option for broader online account access.

resources.name: Cox/Spectrum - Low-Cost Internet Plans
resources.description: Cox/Spectrum offers low-cost home-internet plans for qualifying households, with address-based service and eligibility checks.
resources.hours: Online address check and application available through the website.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The current affordable-internet page lists Internet Assist and an Internet 100 option. Internet Assist advertises $15 per month for qualifying households, while the page also identifies a $25 standard qualifying rate. The modem is included; optional Wi-Fi can add $10 per month and installation charges may apply.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Internet Assist lists National School Lunch Program, Community Eligibility Provision and Supplemental Security Income participation. All SSI types are included. The actual service address, documentation and offer check determine availability and price.

**Population Served**
Households meeting the programme’s benefit and service-address requirements, including eligible Mesa households.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the online address field on the low-cost internet page to check availability and eligibility, then follow the online application prompts. Gather eligibility documentation before applying.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm the final monthly rate, installation costs and optional Wi-Fi charge before ordering; $15 is not guaranteed for every applicant. Internet 100 advertises $30 per month for the first year, then standard rates. Do not assume Lifeline is available through this provider at every Arizona address; check participating providers by ZIP.

resources.name: Arizona State University - Pat Tillman Veterans Center
resources.description: ASU Pat Tillman Veterans Center assists active-duty, veteran and veteran-dependent ASU students with military education benefits, campus support, peer connection and transition resources.
resources.address: Tempe campus: Memorial Union, Lower Level, Room 75, Tempe, AZ; ASU also lists Downtown Phoenix, Polytechnic, West and ASU Online contacts
resources.hours: ASU campus locations list Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Assistance for ASU military-affiliated students with military education benefits, student checklists, GI Bill-related processes, campus connection, wellness and veteran/dependent student support. ASU also identifies a VetSuccess on Campus resource.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For prospective or current ASU active-duty, veteran, veteran-dependent and other military-affiliated students. Education benefits require the applicable VA/DoD or dependent-benefit eligibility and ASU enrollment steps.

**Population Served**
ASU military-connected students and families, including Mesa/East Valley students attending Tempe, Polytechnic, Downtown Phoenix, West, ASU Online or other ASU locations.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-965-7723 for the Pat Tillman Veterans Center and ask for support at the student’s campus, including Polytechnic in Mesa, Tempe, Downtown Phoenix or West. ASU Online military support is 480-884-1537. The Tempe office is in Memorial Union, lower level, Room 75; confirm the desired campus location and hours through ASU’s contact directory.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an ASU student support and benefits-certification resource, not a public veteran-benefits office for people not connected to ASU. Students should also complete required ASU benefit forms and checklists each term.

resources.name: Recovia - Mesa Baywood
resources.description: Mesa multidisciplinary intensive outpatient program treating substance-abuse disorders related to chronic pain recovery, with mental-health counseling, physical therapy and medical support.
resources.address: 6553 E Baywood Ave, Suite 209, Mesa, AZ 85206
resources.hours: Hours were not listed on the page reviewed; call or submit the Get Started form.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Recovia Mesa Baywood specializes in chronic pain, mental health and substance use when necessary. The official location page says all programs integrate mental-health counseling, physical therapy and medical support through a mind-body approach with licensed behavioral-health specialists, physical therapists and medical practitioners. Recovia describes itself as a multidisciplinary intensive outpatient program treating substance-abuse disorders related to chronic pain recovery and lists virtual care/telehealth among its locations/program routes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Ask the intake team whether the person’s chronic pain, mental-health or substance-use needs fit the program. Confirm age criteria, required referrals, insurance or self-pay costs and whether in-person or telehealth treatment is appropriate.

**Population Served**
Mesa-area people with chronic pain recovery needs, co-occurring mental-health concerns, and substance-use concerns where Recovia's outpatient model is clinically appropriate.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-712-4600 or use the Get Started/contact form. The Mesa Baywood office is at 6553 E Baywood Ave, Suite 209, Mesa, AZ 85206, west on Baywood Ave at Power Rd across from the Banner Heart Hospital parking garage. The page says to enter the main doors and go to the second floor, middle of the building by the stairs, Suite 209.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an outpatient/intensive outpatient multidisciplinary program, not residential detox or methadone dosing. It may be especially useful when substance use is tied to chronic pain recovery. Confirm whether a client needs substance-use treatment, chronic-pain treatment, mental-health care, or a combined plan, and confirm insurance/costs before referral.

resources.name: Valley Metro - Reduced Fare Program
resources.description: Valley Metro reduced fare lowers local bus and light rail costs for eligible youth, seniors, Medicare cardholders and people with disabilities through reduced-fare accounts in the Copper Card or app Smart Fare system.
resources.address: Valley Metro fare accounts online; in-person options vary by fare type and location
resources.hours: Online fare account management is available through ValleyMetroFares.org; call customer service for current in-person options and hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Reduced fare accounts lower local bus and light rail costs for eligible riders. Riders can use a Copper Card or the Valley Metro app and Smart Fare fare-capping after reduced-fare approval.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Reduced fare is available for youth age 18 and under, seniors age 65 and older, Medicare cardholders and people with disabilities. Documentation and account approval may be required to access reduced Smart Fare.

**Population Served**
Eligible Valley Metro riders in Mesa and the regional transit service area who use fixed-route bus or light rail.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply for or manage reduced fare at https://www.valleymetrofares.org/. For help, call Valley Metro customer service at 602-253-5000 or AZ Relay 711 and ask about current in-person reduced-fare options.

**Important Information to Know**
Reduced fare is a transit discount, not cash aid or door-to-door transportation. Trips paid through a Copper Card and trips paid through the app do not combine toward one fare cap. Cash reload options are available for people who do not use digital payment; ask customer service about current locations. Express/RAPID and other special services may have different fares.

resources.name: Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community - Legal Services Office
resources.description: Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community Legal Services Office provides civil legal representation to enrolled Community Members in Community, Arizona State, Federal, and other Tribal Courts, with listed help in family, consumer, housing, benefits, estate planning, restoration of rights, repossession, and civil-warrant matters.
resources.address: 10005 E Osborn Rd, Scottsdale, AZ 85256
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Legal Services Office provides civil legal representation and assistance to enrolled Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community members. Listed areas include family law, orders of protection, consumer protection, housing and landlord/tenant issues, public benefits, estate planning, restoration of rights, vehicle repossessions, setting aside civil warrants, and some non-community-court traffic matters. LSO also provides notary service for documents it assists in preparing.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page states LSO serves enrolled Community Members of the Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community. The office does not handle Community Court traffic tickets, criminal cases, or parent representation in dependency actions; those matters are routed to the Defense Advocate Office at 480-362-5660.

**Population Served**
Enrolled Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community members with eligible civil legal matters in Community, Arizona State, Federal, or other Tribal Courts.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the SRPMIC main number at 480-362-7400 and ask for the Legal Services Office, or use the official LSO page's contact link. The public SRPMIC address is 10005 E Osborn Rd, Scottsdale, AZ 85256. Confirm the appointment and office location before traveling.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general public legal-aid clinic for all Mesa residents. It is a tribal-service pathway limited to enrolled Community Members, with important exclusions for criminal, Community Court traffic, and parent dependency representation.

resources.name: AllThrive 365 — Maricopa County weatherization
resources.description: FSL Home Improvements is the Arizona Department of Housing weatherization provider for Maricopa County outside Phoenix and Mesa.
resources.address: 3051 S. 45th St., Phoenix, AZ 85040
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Weatherization Assistance can improve energy efficiency and reduce heating, cooling, and water-heating costs through measures such as air-leak control, insulation, duct work, low-flow fixtures, and heating/cooling equipment testing or tune-ups when identified by an energy audit.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Income-eligible homeowners and renters with landlord permission may qualify within AllThrive’s Maricopa County weatherization area, which excludes incorporated Phoenix and Mesa. Confirm the exact service address.

**Population Served**
Income-eligible households in AllThrive’s county weatherization catchment outside Phoenix and Mesa city limits.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-808-0429 or email mcwap@allthrive365.org for current weatherization eligibility, documents, funding and intake.

**Important Information to Know**
Mesa residents use MesaCAN for this weatherization route. AllThrive’s separate Healthy Homes AC programme has different geography and can serve qualifying Mesa households. Weatherization is assessed property work and can involve a waiting list; it is not immediate bill payment.

resources.name: Maricopa County / HOM, Inc. - Threshold Landlord Engagement Program
resources.description: Maricopa County's Threshold program is a HOM, Inc.-administered landlord engagement program that expands housing options for people experiencing or exiting homelessness by offering landlords incentives, rent assurances and guarantees through the homeless-services system.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Threshold increases housing opportunities for people experiencing or exiting homelessness by recruiting landlords and offering technical support, financial incentives, rent and other guarantees that reduce landlord risk. County materials describe rent reductions, acceptance of households with eviction history or justice involvement, and housing placements supported by case managers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Public materials describe Threshold as serving individuals and families experiencing homelessness and housing instability through the county homeless housing system. Access appears to be through homeless-services practitioners, coordinated entry, vouchers or case managers rather than direct public self-application.

**Population Served**
Individuals and families in Maricopa County who are experiencing homelessness or exiting homelessness and need landlords willing to rent despite barriers such as limited rental history, poor credit or eviction history.

**How to Best Connect**
For a client, connect through the regional homeless-services/coordinated-entry route or the client's existing housing case manager. This is not a walk-in rent assistance program for the general public.

**Important Information to Know**
Threshold primarily pays incentives and guarantees to property owners and supports housing providers. It should not be presented as direct cash assistance to a client. The practical referral path is through authorized homeless-service providers and case management.

resources.name: Veterans For Humanity - 22 A Day Is 22 Too Many Suicide Prevention Program
resources.description: Veterans For Humanity describes a veteran-led suicide-prevention and stabilization program with outreach, peer connection, screening, safety education and referrals, but current public contact and Mesa/Maricopa service details need confirmation.
resources.address: 3910 S Rural Rd, Suite 103, Tempe, AZ 85282
resources.hours: Current service hours are not confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Veteran-led suicide-prevention and stabilization support described as outreach, public awareness, peer connection, screening, safety education and referral connection. The provider states this is not clinical treatment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Publicly available details do not clearly state eligibility, intake rules, current service area or whether services are available to Mesa/Maricopa veterans on request.

**Population Served**
Veterans; current evidence suggests Tempe/Phoenix-area relevance, but the precise active service area needs confirmation.

**How to Best Connect**
An administrator should use the organization’s website contact route to confirm active intake, Mesa coverage and the current phone/address before referral. The submitted 480-696-0626 contact is not independently confirmed. For veteran crisis support, call 988 then press 1 or text 838255.

**Important Information to Know**
Current intake, contact and service-area details remain unresolved. Do not present this as clinical treatment or guaranteed crisis response. This uncertainty does not establish that the organization has closed.
resources.resolutionReason: Needs resolution: official web presence supports program identity at a high level, but contact, intake, clinical boundaries and Maricopa service area could not be responsibly confirmed from accessible primary-source content.

resources.name: VA Phoenix Health Care System - Women Veteran Care
resources.description: Phoenix VA Women Veteran Care helps women Veterans navigate VA health care and offers women’s primary care, gynecology, maternity and postpartum support, mammograms/ultrasounds, mental-health counseling, and wellness services.
resources.address: 650 East Indian School Road, Phoenix, AZ 85012-1839
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Women Veteran Care offers navigation through the Women Veterans Program Manager and comprehensive women’s health services, including primary care, gynecology, maternity care, childbirth education, postpartum support, ultrasounds, mammograms, mental-health care, counseling, and lifestyle wellness services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are for women Veterans using or seeking Phoenix VA care. Specific services may require VA enrollment, clinical eligibility, appointment scheduling, and referrals depending on the service and location.

**Population Served**
Women Veterans in the Phoenix VA Health Care System service area, including Mesa and Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Use VA Health Connect at 888-214-7264 or Phoenix VA main line 602-277-5551 and ask for the Women Veterans Program Manager. Services may occur at the main medical center, Conrad clinic or another VA/partner site; confirm the specific location and referral steps.

**Important Information to Know**
Availability at Mesa versus Phoenix, Gilbert, or another VA site should be confirmed when scheduling. Maternity, mammography, mental-health, and specialty-care pathways may have separate appointment or referral steps.

resources.name: AllThrive 365 - Homebound Adult Services
resources.description: AllThrive 365 Homebound Adult Services offers free volunteer-powered rides to medical appointments and essential services for older adults who have permanently stopped driving.
resources.address: 1201 E. Thomas Rd., Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free volunteer help with medical and essential-service rides, accompanied grocery shopping or grocery pickup and delivery, friendly visits and calls, paperwork, technology and minor home-safety tasks. Grocery assistance may require a home visit before volunteer matching.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are for older adults who have permanently stopped driving because of age-related or physical limitations and want support to remain independent in their homes and communities. AllThrive states services are provided regardless of income level.

**Population Served**
Homebound or non-driving older adults who need practical volunteer support to remain independent and connected.

**How to Best Connect**
The person seeking service should call 602-274-5022 ext. 124 for phone intake and confirm their Mesa address can be served. After intake, request medical rides at least four business days ahead. Volunteer matching and an actual ride still must be arranged.

**Important Information to Know**
The service transferred from Duet to AllThrive 365 and remains dependent on local volunteers. Initial matching can take weeks or months. Medical rides need at least four business days’ notice; if no driver is found, the program says it notifies the client 24 hours before the trip. Confirm the home’s service-area eligibility and keep a backup plan. Services are free regardless of income.

resources.name: Aster Aging - Home Care
resources.description: Aster Aging creates individualized low-cost non-medical home-care plans for seniors and adults with disabilities, including personal care, light housekeeping, laundry, meal preparation and respite for family caregivers.
resources.address: 45 W. University Dr., Suite A, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Service hours, assessment timing and caregiver availability are determined through intake.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Aster Home Care provides non-medical in-home support through individualized care plans. Service options include bathing and grooming help, light housekeeping, laundry, meal preparation and professional respite so family caregivers can take a break.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Aster describes the service for seniors and adults with disabilities who can remain at home longer with personal care or housekeeping assistance. Specific fee, subsidy, payer, service boundary and capacity rules are determined through intake.

**Population Served**
East Valley seniors and adults with disabilities who need low-cost in-home personal care, homemaking or respite support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call an Aster Outreach Specialist at 480-962-5612 or complete the Home Care interest form on Aster's website. Ask about current service area, fees, wait time, assessment and whether the needed tasks are within scope.

**Important Information to Know**
The official page calls the options affordable and low-cost but does not publish hourly rates, subsidy criteria or current caregiver capacity. This is not emergency care.

resources.name: Father Matters - Reentry Mentoring / Family Law Assistance / Job & Training Institute
resources.description: Father Matters provides reentry mentoring and family-strengthening support, including pre-release and post-release mentorship, parenting and relationship classes, court/custody education, employment and education readiness, food pantry access, family reunification support, and referrals to health, behavioral health, substance-use, and case-management services.
resources.address: 3146 E Wier Ave, Ste 26, Phoenix, AZ 85040
resources.hours: Call or email for intake; public page does not list walk-in hours for the reentry program.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Reentry mentoring and practical family support, including transition planning, post-release mentorship, parenting and relationship classes, court/custody education, employment and education readiness, family reunification support, food pantry access, and referrals to health, mental-health, substance-use, and case-management programs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The reentry mentoring page lists men and women age 18 or older, people in pre-release or post-release status from prison or jail, adults convicted of a crime, and pregnant individuals or parents with children under age 6. Some program materials list service-area limits within Maricopa County, so Mesa eligibility should be confirmed.

**Population Served**
Justice-involved adults, especially parents and pregnant individuals, preparing for release or recently released in Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-774-3298, email info@fathermatters.org, or use the website contact route to ask about reentry intake and whether the client fits the current service area.

**Important Information to Know**
Official reentry materials describe free services for currently incarcerated or recently released parents. Confirm geography, program openings, and whether the client needs a facility referral.

resources.name: St. Vincent de Paul of Arizona - Medical equipment through thrift stores
resources.description: St. Vincent de Paul of Arizona lists medical equipment availability through its Valley thrift stores; clients should call ahead to ask whether the needed durable medical equipment is available.
resources.address: Medical equipment may be available through St. Vincent de Paul Valley thrift stores; call ahead for the needed item.
resources.hours: Thrift-store hours vary by location; call the store or general HOPE line before travel.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Access to donated or thrift-store medical equipment such as mobility or home-health equipment when available. Earlier materials described a medical equipment loan closet, but recent St. Vincent de Paul resource sheets state medical equipment is available at Valley thrift stores and clients should call ahead.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Recent St. Vincent de Paul public materials do not list a formal medical-equipment eligibility rule. Availability depends on donated inventory at thrift stores. Older materials described loans for low-income, elderly, or disabled community members, but the current route should be confirmed before referral.

**Population Served**
People in the Phoenix metro area, including Mesa/Maricopa clients, who need low-cost or donated durable medical equipment and can contact or travel to a St. Vincent de Paul thrift store.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the HOPE line at 602-266-4673 or the relevant St. Vincent de Paul thrift store before travel and ask whether the specific item is available. The prior loan-closet phone 602-261-6896 appeared in older materials; call the main route if that number is not current.

**Important Information to Know**
Do not present this as a confirmed no-cost loan closet without staff confirmation. Current public materials describe medical equipment availability through thrift stores, which may mean purchase or donation-based access rather than a guaranteed free loan.

resources.name: Oakwood Creative Care - Medicare GUIDE Model Dementia Support
resources.description: Oakwood Creative Care's GUIDE Model program provides dementia care navigation, caregiver support, respite through adult day clubs, assessments and 24/7 dementia support for eligible Medicare beneficiaries living with dementia and their caregivers.
resources.address: The Hub Mesa, 6915 E. Main St., 1st Floor, Mesa, AZ 85207
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Dementia care navigation, care-plan development, caregiver training and support, respite through Oakwood adult day clubs, community support groups, education, social events, clinical assessment and a 24/7 dementia support line.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A clinician-confirmed dementia diagnosis and Original Medicare Parts A and B as primary coverage are required. Medicare Advantage, Special Needs Plans and PACE do not qualify. The person cannot be using Medicare hospice, living long-term in a nursing home or Memory Care Unit, or enrolled with another GUIDE participant. CMS and the provider determine eligibility and enrollment.

**Population Served**
People living with dementia and family caregivers in Mesa and nearby Oakwood service areas.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-625-3867 to review coverage and eligibility. The Hub Mesa is at 6915 E. Main St., 1 st Floor, Mesa. Oakwood also lists a main office number, 480-498-2533.

**Important Information to Know**
Medicare GUIDE coverage is eligibility-specific and does not guarantee enrollment or immediate respite space. Oakwood also lists free general access to some Hub community connections and private-pay Hub membership for people who do not meet GUIDE requirements.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Education — Refugee Student Support
resources.description: Provides a school-system route for newcomer enrollment and education-access questions.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides a school-system route for newcomer enrollment and education-access questions.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program supports schools and refugee or newcomer students; local school enrollment processes still apply.

**Population Served**
Newcomer students, families and the school staff assisting them.

**How to Best Connect**
Use Refugee Student Support’s contact information or call the department at 602-542-5393 to locate the right specialist.

**Important Information to Know**
This is education-system guidance, not immigration legal representation or a separate school-admission application.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Veterans' Services - Arizona State Veteran Home - Phoenix
resources.description: Arizona State Veteran Home - Phoenix is a state-operated, Medicare-certified skilled-nursing facility for eligible Arizona Veterans and spouses who need physician-determined skilled nursing care, including long-term care, memory care, rehabilitation, nursing, recreation, and social services.
resources.address: 4141 North Silvestre Herrera Way, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
ASVH-Phoenix provides skilled nursing care, long-term care beds, a memory-care unit, Medicare/rehab-focused beds, nursing, therapeutic recreation, social services, physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, resident activities, and an onsite Veteran Benefits Counselor.

**Eligibility Requirements**
An applicant must be an honorably separated Veteran or the spouse of a Veteran, must require skilled nursing care as determined by a physician, and must have documented evidence of absence of tuberculosis. Admission also depends on application review, payer/payment arrangements, and bed availability.

**Population Served**
Eligible Arizona Veterans and spouses who need skilled nursing care, including residents from Maricopa County and Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Admissions at 602-248-1594. The main line is 602-248-1550. The facility is at 4141 North Silvestre Herrera Way, Phoenix, AZ 85012. Admission forms are available from the ADVS ASVH-Phoenix page.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a skilled-nursing facility, not general senior housing or assisted living. Confirm openings, clinical fit, payer requirements, and required medical documents directly with admissions before referral.

resources.name: HonorHealth Cancer Care - Social Services Transportation Resource Help
resources.description: HonorHealth Cancer Care social workers help cancer patients find resources for transportation to appointments and other practical needs related to treatment.
resources.address: HonorHealth Cancer Care locations in the Phoenix metro area
resources.hours: Call to request a cancer-care social-work consultation; response time is not established.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
HonorHealth Cancer Care social workers help patients identify resources for transportation to appointments, insurance questions, childcare during treatment, financial issues and other cancer-related support needs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The page describes service for people receiving HonorHealth cancer care. Transportation help is resource navigation, not a guaranteed ride benefit.

**Population Served**
HonorHealth cancer patients and their caregivers in the Phoenix metro HonorHealth Cancer Care network.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 855-485-4673 to make an appointment with cancer care social services. Ask specifically for help with transportation barriers to treatment appointments.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a transportation provider. Available ride resources may depend on the patient's treatment location, diagnosis, insurance, financial situation and current partner programs.

resources.name: Consulate General of Mexico in Phoenix - Mexican identity documents and civil registry records
resources.description: The Consulate General of Mexico in Phoenix provides direct Mexican identity and civil-registry services, including passports, matrícula consular, voter credentials, Mexican birth certificates, birth/marriage/death registrations, certified copies and notarial acts for eligible Mexican nationals and families in its consular jurisdiction.
resources.address: 320 E McDowell Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.hours: Appointments and requirements vary by service. Use MiConsulado/citas.sre.gob.mx or call the consulate before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Mexican passport, matrícula consular, voter credential, civil registry services, birth certificate access, birth/marriage/death registration, certified copies and notarial acts.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Mexican passports and matrícula consular require proof of Mexican nationality and identity, personal appearance and, for matrícula, consular-district residence. Birth registration can cover a person born outside Mexico to a parent who proves Mexican nationality. Other registry, voter and notarial actions have their own nationality, original-document and appointment requirements; minors and record discrepancies require the applicable checklist.

**Population Served**
Mexican nationals and families in the Consulate General of Mexico in Phoenix jurisdiction, including people living in Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Schedule through Mi Consulado at citas.sre.gob.mx or phone/WhatsApp 424-309-0009; choose the exact document or Registro Civil service. General consulate inquiries: 602-242-7398. Confirm the current originals, copies and fees before visiting 320 E McDowell Road, Phoenix.

**Important Information to Know**
A matrícula consular establishes Mexican identity/nationality and consular registration; it does not establish lawful U.S. immigration status or replace U.S. immigration documents. This is a direct consular document service, not hardship-fee assistance. Fees and required documents differ by service.

resources.name: HandsOn Greater Phoenix - Veteran Assistance Program
resources.description: HandsOn Greater Phoenix mobilizes volunteer teams to complete home-improvement projects for eligible active or retired military members and spouses or widows, including weatherization, safety repairs, accessibility modifications, painting, code/HOA cleanup, and minor repairs.
resources.address: 1125 E. Southern Ave. Ste. 200, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Volunteer teams complete home projects for eligible military-connected households. Past projects include weatherization, minor safety repairs, accessibility modifications such as ramps and grab bars, single-story painting, code/HOA violation cleanup, landscaping/debris cleanup, and minor general repairs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page says applicants must be active or retired military or a spouse/widow of a service member. Homes must be permanent structures; if retired, discharge must be honorable or medical. High-need homes have higher priority.

**Population Served**
Valley veterans, active or retired military members, and eligible spouses or widows whose homes can be served by volunteer teams.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Veteran Assistance Application linked on the program page. Questions can go to Vicente Martinez at 623-352-3231 or vicente@handsonphoenix.org. HandsOn Greater Phoenix lists 1125 E. Southern Ave. Ste. 200, Mesa, AZ 85204.

**Important Information to Know**
HandsOn states it cannot complete work requiring a permit or a licensed/bonded contractor. Project timing and selection depend on volunteer and corporate partner availability, so approval and timing are not guaranteed.

resources.name: Federal Bureau of Prisons - Residential Reentry Management Field Office Phoenix
resources.description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons Residential Reentry Management Field Office in Phoenix is the federal RRM office for Arizona and Southern Nevada, connected to Residential Reentry Center and home-confinement contract management for federally adjudicated adults.
resources.address: 230 N 1st Ave, Suite 405, Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.hours: 211 lists Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; confirm directly before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Federal residential reentry management office connected to BOP Residential Reentry Center and community-placement contract administration. It is an access point for federal reentry systems rather than a general community reentry nonprofit.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Limited to federally adjudicated adults and people under Federal Bureau of Prisons reentry authority. Placement is usually managed through BOP/unit team, RRM, contractor, and federal supervision processes.

**Population Served**
Federal offenders in Arizona and Southern Nevada, including people returning to Maricopa County from federal custody.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-333-0537 or use the BOP RRM Phoenix page. People still in custody should work through their BOP unit team or federal reentry contact; do not treat the Phoenix office as a walk-in housing provider.

**Important Information to Know**
This is federal-only and not appropriate for state prison, county jail, or probation-only clients unless there is a federal BOP connection. No one is housed at the office address.

resources.name: Southwest Gas — Weatherization and energy-efficiency assistance
resources.description: Southwest Gas Arizona special programs include LIRA bill discounts, no-cost weatherization for income-qualified customers, installment plans for outstanding bills, third-party notification, language/relay accommodations, and medically fragile priority restoration after outages.
resources.hours: Call Southwest Gas for current program intake and account review; hours were not established in this preparation.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Southwest Gas supports no-cost weatherization for qualifying households. Approved work can include caulking, insulation, weather-stripping, ductwork and window repairs to improve energy efficiency.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Income-qualified Southwest Gas residential customers in Arizona may qualify, including owners and renters. Confirm household, property, landlord-consent and local delivery requirements.

**Population Served**
Income-qualified households receiving Southwest Gas service in Arizona, including eligible Mesa and Maricopa County addresses.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Southwest Gas at 877-860-6020, relay 711, to confirm weatherization eligibility, required documents and the local provider for the service address.

**Important Information to Know**
Weatherization is assessed property work, not a bill-payment grant. LIRA discounts, payment arrangements, medical priority restoration and third-party bill notices are separate programmes with their own rules.

resources.name: Victory Place — Affordable single-occupancy apartments
resources.description: Provides permanent affordable studio and one-bedroom housing in Phoenix, including an option for veterans.
resources.address: 850 East Jones Avenue, Phoenix, AZ 85040
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides permanent affordable studio and one-bedroom housing in Phoenix, including an option for veterans.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Leasing staff assess income, assets and other application requirements. Each unit is limited to the named resident; this is not family housing.

**Population Served**
Single adults seeking affordable housing, including veterans and working individuals.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact leasing at 602-243-2774 or vpleasing@cantwell-anderson.com. Use the property’s application or arrange a visit.

**Important Information to Know**
Availability, rent and any veteran preference must be confirmed. This is leased housing, not emergency shelter, and is distinct from the Axiom John McCain treatment centre on the broader campus.

resources.name: Resurrection Street Ministry - Food Assistance, Mobile Pantry and Senior/Veterans Food Program
resources.description: Resurrection Street Ministry offers food boxes at its Mesa pantry, a weekly Mesa drive-through mobile pantry, off-site food distributions and a senior/veteran CSFP bonus-box program.
resources.address: Main office: 1135 E Main St, Mesa, AZ 85203; Chosen 2 Serve pantry: 1119-1121 E Main St, Mesa, AZ 85203; Monday mobile pantry: Journey of Grace Church, 955 E University Dr, Mesa, AZ 85203
resources.hours: Chosen 2 Serve pantry: Monday-Saturday 10:00 AM-2:00 PM. Mesa mobile pantry at Journey of Grace: Mondays 4:30-6:00 PM, visit up to twice monthly. Senior/Veterans program: second and third Thursday monthly 9:00-11:00 AM by appointment; new site to be posted when available.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Food boxes with dairy, breads, produce, vegetables, baked goods, snacks, non-perishable foods and non-food items; meat, deli items and hygiene items when available. Also offers a weekly Mesa drive-through mobile pantry and Senior/Veterans Food Program with CSFP staple box plus RSM bonus box.

**Eligibility Requirements**
General food distributions require photo ID and limit visits to twice monthly. The Senior/Veterans Food Program requires an appointment, picture ID and proof of address. Ask staff about the separate senior CSFP qualification and veteran-under-60 bonus-food route; veteran status alone does not establish CSFP eligibility.

**Population Served**
Mesa and Maricopa County residents needing food assistance, including veterans, seniors, people experiencing homelessness, families and group-home residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-615-2799 or email resurrectionstreetministry@gmail.com. For Senior/Veterans Food Program registration, contact Valerie at 405-386-7799. Use 1119-1121 E Main St for Chosen 2 Serve pantry and 955 E University Dr for the Monday mobile pantry; enter from Miller St.

**Important Information to Know**
Use current official addresses rather than older Main Street listings. The Senior/Veterans page says a new site will be posted when available, so confirm that distribution location before sending someone.

resources.name: ARIZONA@WORK Maricopa County - Youth Workforce Services, East Valley Career Center
resources.description: ARIZONA@WORK Maricopa County Youth Workforce Services provides no-cost workforce support for eligible youth and young adults ages 14-24, including career exploration, education support, occupational training, paid work experiences and apprenticeships.
resources.address: East Valley Career Center, 1001 W Southern Ave, Suite 101, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Use the East Valley Career Center or staff appointment instructions after applying; center hours may vary by program.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost youth workforce support includes career exploration, mentoring, counselling, GED/high-school-equivalency and alternative-school support, leadership, occupational training, paid work experiences, apprenticeships, financial literacy and entrepreneurship.
