Enrolled eligible youth may receive testing fees, training assistance, gas cards or bus passes; none is automatic.

**Eligibility Requirements**
In-school applicants generally must be 14–21, low income and have a qualifying barrier; out-of-school applicants generally must be 16–24 and have a qualifying barrier. Examples include school disconnection, justice involvement, homelessness, foster care, pregnancy/parenting, disability and, where applicable, English-language learning. Staff determine the applicable criteria and documents; ask about other qualifying paths if the listed criteria appear not to fit.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County youth and young adults, including in-school and out-of-school youth, youth experiencing homelessness, foster-care involvement, pregnancy or parenting, disability, English-language learning, justice involvement or school disconnection.

**How to Best Connect**
Create an Arizona Job Connection account and submit interest through the Maricopa County Client Portal. East Valley Career Center: 602-372-9700, 1001 W Southern Avenue, Suite 101, Mesa. Tempe Youth Hub at Escalante Center, 2150 E Orange Street, is appointment-only at 480-350-5824. Staff schedule eligibility review after the portal request.

**Important Information to Know**
Prepare age/photo ID, Social Security and qualifying-barrier documents, plus Selective Service proof when applicable. Training funds, work placements and transportation help depend on enrollment, documentation, funding and availability; this is not a public walk-in gas-card programme.

resources.name: AllThrive 365 - Family Caregiver Services
resources.description: AllThrive 365 Family Caregiver Services provides education, support groups, dementia-focused discussion series, peer support, workshops, resource navigation and community connection for people caring for aging loved ones.
resources.address: 1201 E. Thomas Rd., Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Caregiver support groups, the Finding Meaning and Hope dementia-care discussion series, educational events and workshops, peer support, resource navigation, community connections and support for people adjusting after caregiving ends.

**Eligibility Requirements**
AllThrive says Family Caregiver Services are available to people caring for an aging adult, spouse, relative, friend or loved one. Individual groups and events may have registration, schedule, language or topic requirements.

**Population Served**
Unpaid family caregivers and care partners supporting aging adults, including dementia caregivers and people seeking emotional support, education or navigation.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-285-1800 ext. 232 or email caregiverservices@allthrive365.org. Check the official program page for upcoming support groups and events.

**Important Information to Know**
Duet transferred its family caregiver, homebound adult and kinship-care service lines to AllThrive 365 effective August 4, 2026. Specific group schedules, locations, language options and capacity may change.

resources.name: Wyyerd Fiber - Wyyerd Fiber Assist Program
resources.description: Wyyerd Fiber Assist offers eligible households 150 Mbps symmetrical fiber internet for $35 per month with installation and equipment included where Wyyerd service is available.
resources.hours: Online availability check and application; call Arizona support for questions.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Wyyerd Fiber Assist provides 150 Mbps symmetrical fiber internet for $35 per month, with no hidden fees, credit checks or contracts, and with free installation and equipment included.

**Eligibility Requirements**
New or existing Wyyerd customers may qualify if someone in the household participates in SNAP, National School Lunch Program, WIC or Head Start. Applicants submit an award letter or benefit statement; the account holder or qualified beneficiary name must be present, and service address may need to be present when the beneficiary is not the account holder.

**Population Served**
Households in Wyyerd Fiber service areas in Arizona, including only Mesa or Maricopa County addresses where Wyyerd confirms availability.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Wyyerd Fiber Assist page to check address availability and apply online. Wyyerd says it reviews eligibility within 2-3 business days and contacts applicants about the application. Arizona support phone is 623-455-4555.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a discounted Wyyerd service plan, not a government bill credit. It is useful only where Wyyerd Fiber can serve the address. Recertification may be required on a rolling one-year basis.

resources.name: Smart Schools · Online Adult High School Diploma
resources.description: Smart Schools is a nonprofit online middle and high school provider offering accredited, self-paced online high school diploma coursework for students of all ages, with certified instructors, tutoring, academic advisors, and college/career guidance.
resources.address: Administrative office: 1555 N. Fiesta Blvd., Gilbert, AZ 85233
resources.hours: Online self-paced program; enrollment support by phone or web form.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Accredited online high school diploma coursework, self-paced classes, certified instructors, one-on-one tutoring, personal academic advisor support, college and career guidance, credit for prior high school work, possible elective credit through work-study, and help with enrollment documents.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Smart Schools describes accepting students of all ages in online middle and high school. The Arizona Adult Workforce Diploma Program page lists a separate free adult pathway for Arizona residents age 21+ with some high school, computer and internet access, but that free program’s funding is currently depleted.

**Population Served**
Arizona and online learners, including adult learners who need a high school diploma and can complete online coursework.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Enroll link on Smart Schools’ site, call 844-467-5278, or email info@studentswin.org. Ask specifically about current tuition, scholarships, Arizona adult diploma funding, HUB support, technology requirements, and whether a Mesa-area client has an in-person support option.

**Important Information to Know**
Do not present the Arizona Adult Workforce Diploma Program as open and free without confirming funding; the official Smart Schools WDP page says funds are depleted and applications are not being accepted for that program. Other Smart Schools enrollment options may still be available and may have costs.

resources.name: Complete Vision Care - Mobile Optometry and Gift of Sight School Care
resources.description: Complete Vision Care provides clinic and mobile optometry across Arizona, including school, home, facility and underserved-community settings, and partners with Gift of Sight Children's Foundation to provide free eye exams and prescription glasses for uninsured children.
resources.address: 220 E Southern Ave, Suite C-3, Phoenix, AZ 85040
resources.hours: Phoenix and Globe offices list 8:00 AM-5:00 PM Monday-Friday; hours may vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Comprehensive eye exams, pediatric eye care, mobile optometry, diabetic eye exams, disease monitoring, frames/lenses and school-based exams/glasses through Gift of Sight for uninsured children.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Routine optometry eligibility, costs and insurance depend on the service. Gift of Sight is described for uninsured children across Arizona and is usually school-based through participating schools.

**Population Served**
Arizona children and adults needing optometry, especially students, homebound or facility-based patients, rural or underserved communities and uninsured children reached through Gift of Sight.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Phoenix office at 480-371-8167 for in-office appointments, mobile optometry questions or school care coordination. Providers can request the home-health optometry referral form; parents can use the school finder for participating school intake forms.

**Important Information to Know**
Mesa school participation is not guaranteed. Confirm whether the client's school, facility or home location is currently served and whether the child qualifies for Gift of Sight support.

resources.name: Wesley Community & Health Centers - Recker Road Prenatal Care
resources.description: Wesley Health Center at Recker Road is a Mesa community health center offering bilingual prenatal and postpartum care, pregnancy testing, breastfeeding education, newborn care, birth control, pediatrics, counseling, insurance eligibility help, AHCCCS acceptance and sliding-fee resources.
resources.address: 5845 E. Still Cir., Suite 104, Mesa, AZ 85206
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Wesley provides prenatal and postpartum care, pregnancy tests, prenatal care and delivery coordination with Banner University Medical Center - Phoenix, breastfeeding education and support, newborn care, birth control, family medicine, pediatric care, counseling, lab testing and insurance eligibility help.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Patients needing prenatal, postpartum, pediatric or family health services may call for an appointment. Wesley accepts most insurance plans, AHCCCS and Medicare; uninsured patients may qualify for discounts based on family size and income. Patients transferring prenatal care should have their first Wesley appointment no later than 34 weeks and bring ultrasound and lab records.

**Population Served**
Pregnant and postpartum patients, newborns, children and families in Mesa and the surrounding East Valley. Services are available in English and Spanish.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-257-4323 to schedule. Recker Road campus is at 5845 E. Still Cir., Suite 104, Mesa, AZ 85206.

**Important Information to Know**
Deliveries are coordinated at Banner University Medical Center - Phoenix, not at the Recker Road clinic. Wesley states it does not provide emergency services; call 911 for emergencies.

resources.name: Community Bridges, Inc. - Supportive Services for Veteran Families and Transition in Place
resources.description: Community Bridges, Inc. Veteran Programs provide housing-stability support for Veterans, including Supportive Services for Veteran Families and Transition in Place assistance with rental application fees, security deposits, and time-limited rental assistance for eligible Arizona Veterans.
resources.address: 1855 West Baseline Road, Suite 101, Mesa, AZ 85202
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
CBI Veteran Programs provide wrap-around services that connect Veterans with housing and ongoing care. Transition in Place helps eligible Veterans secure and maintain affordable, safe housing, including payment of rental application fees, security deposits, and up to six months of rental assistance. SSVF promotes housing stability for very-low-income Veteran families who reside in or are transitioning to permanent housing.

**Eligibility Requirements**
TIP and SSVF have separate rules. CBI states TIP eligibility includes Arizona as home of record or deployment from Arizona. SSVF is for very-low-income Veteran families who are in or transitioning to permanent housing. Housing status, income, service history, funding availability, and documentation all matter.

**Population Served**
Eligible Veteran families and Arizona Veterans, including Mesa and Maricopa County clients. CBI lists a Mesa location at 1855 West Baseline Road, Suite 101.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 888-224-2087 and ask for Veteran Programs, SSVF or Transition in Place; appointments also list 888-224-6593 or scheduling@cbridges.com. Confirm the Mesa household is in the current grant service area and whether a visit to 1855 W Baseline Road, Suite 101 is appropriate.

**Important Information to Know**
Rental help depends on screening, programme rules, funding and capacity. TIP and SSVF requirements differ from general CBI behavioural-health eligibility. The public veteran-programme page does not promise ID or birth-certificate replacement; ask the case manager for a referral if those documents are needed.

resources.name: Faith, Hope and Charity Arizona - Housing, Job Training and Behavioral Health Services
resources.description: Faith, Hope and Charity Arizona publicly describes housing, job training and behavioral-health services using a hotel location in Phoenix, but current public eligibility, fees, capacity and intake route are not established.
resources.address: 4727 E Thomas Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85018
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Housing, job training and behavioral-health services for individuals and families needing a new beginning. The program page says FHC provides stable housing through an accessible hotel location in Phoenix, along with group therapy and job-preparedness supports.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Public eligibility rules were not found. The submission describes a reintegration/reentry transitional-housing provider, but current referral pathway, fees, hotel locations, documentation requirements and whether Mesa residents are eligible need administrator confirmation.

**Population Served**
Individuals and families in the Phoenix area who need housing stability and related behavioral-health or job-training supports; exact target population and priority groups are not clear from the current public page.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the public website/contact route or the listed Phoenix address only after administrator confirmation. No reliable phone or application route was found in the checked official program page.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a useful unresolved lead, not a ready routine referral. The official page supports that FHC offers housing, job training and behavioral-health services, but the lack of public intake details is consequential for client access.
resources.resolutionReason: Retained as needs-resolution because an official FHC page supports housing and related services, but no practical public intake route, eligibility, fees or service-area details were found after targeted source check.

resources.name: Mesa Fire and Medical Department - Connector Incident Support
resources.description: Volunteer secondary responders help Mesa households after fires and other incidents with practical support, resource connections and limited stranded-motorist assistance.
resources.hours: Connector volunteer hours listed as Monday-Sunday 7:00 AM-10:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
After house fires, Connectors identify lodging, clothing and food needs, connect families with the American Red Cross and other resources, help contact insurance and follow up. On Mesa surface roads they may assist with a dead battery, flat tire or lack of fuel, provide a ride home after an incident, or transport a large wheelchair when its owner has gone to hospital.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Assistance is tied to incidents served by Mesa Fire and Medical and Connector availability. Disabled-vehicle help is for City of Mesa surface roads; this is not scheduled transport, a clothing closet or a general repair/fuel fund.

**Population Served**
City of Mesa residents and households affected by fires or emergency incidents where Mesa Fire and Medical crews or Connectors are involved.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 911 for an emergency. For programme questions or follow-up, call 480-644-LINK (5465) or email FDConnectorCoordinator@mesaaz.gov. The published contact is not a guaranteed non-emergency ride-dispatch service.

**Important Information to Know**
Deployment and assistance depend on the incident, Mesa public-safety response and volunteer availability. Confirm the follow-up route; do not promise a tow, item, payment or ride.

resources.name: Chicanos Por La Causa - HUD-approved Housing Counseling
resources.description: Chicanos Por La Causa provides HUD-approved housing counseling in Phoenix, including financial assessment, action planning, pre-purchase counseling, homebuyer education, affordable-housing option guidance, and help with landlord-tenant conflicts, mortgage delinquency, foreclosure risk, and fraud issues.
resources.address: 1402 S Central Ave, Building A, Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
HUD-approved housing counseling, financial assessment, individualized action planning, pre-purchase counseling, homebuyer education, affordable-housing option guidance, and help with landlord-tenant conflicts, mortgage delinquency, pending foreclosure, and housing-related fraud.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on the counseling or assistance requested. The separate CPLC Open Doors down-payment program is for first-time homebuyers in Phoenix with household income at or below 80% AMI; housing counseling itself should be screened directly with CPLC.

**Population Served**
Phoenix and Maricopa County residents seeking housing stability, homebuyer readiness, or foreclosure/landlord-tenant counseling. Services may be useful for Spanish-speaking clients through CPLC access.

**How to Best Connect**
Call CPLC Housing Counseling Services at 602-253-0838 or use the official Apply for Assistance link on the housing counseling page. Phoenix office: 1402 S Central Ave, Building A, Phoenix, AZ 85004.

**Important Information to Know**
This is counseling and navigation, not a guaranteed rental-assistance fund, shelter bed, or affordable unit. CPLC's family-assistance page separately states it does not have rental assistance funds.

resources.name: Rio Vista Center / Casa de Amor - Supplemental Food Boxes
resources.description: Casa de Amor, a Rio Vista Center / Arizona Baptist Children's Services community resource center in Mesa, distributes supplemental food boxes and clothing on weekday mornings with first-come daily box limits.
resources.address: 819 S MacDonald, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Food and clothing Monday-Wednesday 9:00-11:00 AM. Posted closure: Dec. 22-Jan. 2, normal hours resuming Monday, Jan. 5.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Supplemental food boxes and clothing through Casa de Amor, a community resource center serving Phoenix's East Valley.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official Casa de Amor page does not publish income, residence or document rules for food boxes. Food is limited to a fixed number of boxes per day and is first come, first served.

**Population Served**
People in Mesa and the East Valley needing supplemental food and basic clothing support.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to Casa de Amor at 819 S MacDonald, Mesa during food and clothing hours, Monday-Wednesday 9:00-11:00 AM. Call 480-464-2877 with questions.

**Important Information to Know**
Daily capacity limits matter. Arrive early and confirm holiday closures or documentation questions before travel.

resources.name: Phoenix Legal Action Network - Housing Legal Clinic
resources.description: Phoenix Legal Action Network's Housing Legal Clinic offers free attorney help for landlord problems, prioritizing immigrants and families in specified west Phoenix/Glendale ZIP codes while answering questions for other Phoenix metro residents who cannot afford an attorney as capacity permits.
resources.hours: PLAN says it aims to return housing legal assistance calls between 8:30 AM and 9:00 AM on the next business day; due to limited capacity, it cannot return calls about other legal issues through this line.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free help from an attorney for problems with a landlord. The clinic offers appointment scheduling or voicemail callback for housing legal assistance.

**Eligibility Requirements**
PLAN prioritizes immigrants and their families in ZIP codes 85043, 85035, 85033, 85031, and the part of 85301 south of Grand Avenue. As capacity permits, the clinic may answer questions for anyone in the Phoenix metro area who cannot afford an attorney.

**Population Served**
Primarily immigrant families in the listed west Phoenix and Glendale ZIP codes; other low-income Phoenix metro tenants, including Mesa-area tenants, may be considered only if capacity permits.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-341-5470 and leave a message with the caller's name, phone number, and a brief explanation of the housing legal problem, or use the appointment link on the clinic page. PLAN aims to return housing legal assistance calls the next business day between 8:30 AM and 9:00 AM.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a broad legal hotline and PLAN states it cannot return calls about non-housing legal issues through this clinic. It is a useful reserve option for Mesa only with a capacity warning because the clinic prioritizes other ZIP codes.

resources.name: Phoenix Children’s — outpatient psychiatry
resources.description: Pediatric psychiatric evaluation, counseling, medication management and family interventions.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Pediatric psychiatric evaluation, counseling, medication management and family interventions.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Ask the child’s primary-care provider for a referral; intake determines the appropriate program and location.

**Population Served**
Children and families with psychiatric or complex combined medical and mental-health needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-933-0990 and discuss referral, location and payer requirements.

**Important Information to Know**
The inpatient unit described by Phoenix Children’s serves children 12 and younger; that limit does not define every outpatient program. Do not assume Bridge Clinic enrollment without confirmation.

resources.name: Arizona Relationship Institute
resources.description: Individual, relationship and family counseling, including LGBTQIA+ affirming care.
resources.address: 7565 E Eagle Crest Dr, Suite 201, Mesa, AZ 85207
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Individual, relationship and family counseling, including LGBTQIA+ affirming care.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Appointment availability and clinician fit are assessed individually.

**Population Served**
Mesa-area individuals, couples and families.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-788-5069 and ask about the free 15-minute consultation or the reduced-fee associate program.

**Important Information to Know**
Session prices and coverage depend on the clinician; confirm them before booking.

resources.name: East Valley Institute of Technology - HopeTech Residential Community
resources.description: EVIT HopeTech is a residential community providing apartment-style housing and career-education linkage for eligible young adults ages 18-23 who were in foster care or classified as McKinney-Vento.
resources.address: 1601 W Main St, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Applications for the EVIT 2026-2027 school year are open according to the EVIT page; email to begin the application.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Apartment-style housing tied to EVIT enrollment, career training, high-school diploma or GED progress when needed, workplace-readiness and independent-living programming, community meetings and structured activity requirements.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must have been in foster care or classified as McKinney-Vento and be ages 18-23. Residents must enroll in an EVIT program, meet academic and attendance requirements, sign EVIT program documents and lease documents, work a part-time job and participate in required programming.

**Population Served**
Young adults ages 18-23 connected to foster care or McKinney-Vento homelessness classifications who are ready to pursue EVIT career training in Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Email dmccoy@evit.edu to begin the HopeTech application through EVIT online enrollment; hopetech@evit.edu is also listed. General EVIT phone: 480-461-4000. Prepare a non-relative adult recommendation and the relevant DCS/case manager, success coach or McKinney-Vento liaison contact when applicable.

**Important Information to Know**
The EVIT page lists 2026–2027 enrollment, maximum rent of $500 monthly and eight residents per apartment. Confirm the current application window and vacancy; school admission does not guarantee housing. This is residential education/workforce support, not emergency shelter.

resources.name: Church of the Master PC(USA) / Christian Assistance Network - C.A.N. Food Pantry and Crisis Assistance
resources.description: Christian Assistance Network at Church of the Master provides monthly food boxes, utility assistance and resource counseling for families in need, operating Monday mornings.
resources.address: 6659 E University Dr, Mesa, AZ 85205
resources.hours: Monday mornings 9:00-10:45 AM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
C.A.N., the Christian Assistance Network, provides monthly food boxes, once-annual utility assistance and counseling or connection to spiritual, financial, health and public-aid resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official church page says families in need can obtain a food box monthly. It does not state ID, income, address-radius or document requirements, so call before first use.

**Population Served**
Families and people in need near Church of the Master in Mesa; secondary referrals describe a local service radius, but the official page does not state the full geographic boundary.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to Church of the Master during C.A.N. Monday morning hours, 9:00-10:45 AM, or call the church at 480-985-1660 to confirm current intake and service-area rules.

**Important Information to Know**
Food boxes are monthly, not weekly. Utility help and counseling are separate from food box access and may have different rules.

resources.name: Chandler-Gilbert Community College — Coyote Cupboard and community produce
resources.description: CGCC offers public produce distributions and a separate student/employee pantry with food, household items, toiletries and school supplies, including at its Williams Campus in Mesa.
resources.address: Williams Campus, 7360 E Tahoe Avenue, Mesa, AZ 85212
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Coyote Cupboard provides free nonperishable food, household items, toiletries and school supplies for CGCC students and employees at the Pecos and Williams campuses. Separate community produce distributions welcome the public; their schedules and access rules differ from the daily college pantry.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Monthly produce events welcome community members; Coyote Cupboard is limited to CGCC students and employees.

**Population Served**
Community members needing produce and eligible college students or employees needing food and basic supplies.

**How to Best Connect**
Williams: call 480-988-8274. Published produce hours are first Tuesday 10 a.m.–noon, Higley Room; pantry hoursMonday–Friday 9 a.m.–5 p.m., Bridget Hall. Confirm the semester calendar and room.

**Important Information to Know**
Supplies are limited. Pecos has its own schedule and contact. A public produce event does not make the daily college pantry public.

resources.name: Child Crisis Arizona - Group Home for Boys in Foster Care
resources.description: Child Crisis Arizona provides a staffed group home for teenage boys in foster care, with support for daily living and healthy development.
resources.address: Residential location is not a public walk-up intake.
resources.hours: Residential care around the clock; call to ask about referral arrangements.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The group home provides around-the-clock care, support for daily living and opportunities for normal teenage activities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The provider identifies the programme for boys ages 11–17 in foster care. Placement suitability and availability must be arranged through the appropriate care team.

**Population Served**
Teenage boys in foster care.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the young person's foster-care caseworker about placement, or contact Child Crisis Arizona general enquiries at 480-834-9424 and ask specifically about the boys' group home.

**Important Information to Know**
This is distinct from the emergency shelter for ages 2–10 and Halle House for older youth. It is not a general youth walk-in shelter; confirm placement arrangements rather than travelling to a residence.

resources.name: AHCCCS - Children's Rehabilitative Services (CRS) Designation and Referrals
resources.description: Children's Rehabilitative Services is an AHCCCS designation and referral pathway for AHCCCS members under age 21 with qualifying complex medical conditions requiring active treatment.
resources.address: Mail only: AHCCCS CRS Unit, PO Box 6050, MD 15020, Phoenix, AZ 85002-5520
resources.hours: Call the CRS Unit for application questions; public hours were not separately established.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
CRS designation can add closer care coordination through the child's AHCCCS health plan and may connect eligible children to multispecialty interdisciplinary clinic services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The child must be an AHCCCS member, under age 21, and have a CRS-qualifying medical condition that requires active treatment. The application requires supporting medical documentation.

**Population Served**
Arizona children and youth under 21 who are AHCCCS members with qualifying complex medical conditions, including eligible Mesa and Maricopa County children.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the CRS Unit at 602-417-4545 or 855-333-7828. A family member, clinician or health-plan representative may complete an application with supporting medical records. Follow current AHCCCS form instructions; listed routes include dmpscrs@azahcccs.gov, fax 602-252-5286 and the CRS Unit mailing address.

**Important Information to Know**
CRS is a designation and care-coordination pathway, not a direct appointment guarantee. Continue using the child’s health plan while an application is pending. Foster-care, DDD and American Indian/Alaska Native plan pathways may differ; confirm the appropriate plan and current multispecialty provider rather than relying on historical clinic listings.

resources.name: AARP Foundation - Tax-Aide Free Tax Preparation
resources.description: AARP Foundation Tax-Aide provides free tax preparation and tax-filing help through IRS-certified volunteers, with a special focus on taxpayers over 50 and people with low to moderate income.
resources.address: Multiple seasonal sites; use locator for current locations
resources.hours: Seasonal, generally early February through mid-April. Site schedules, appointment requirements and walk-in availability vary by location; the locator closes outside tax season.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free tax preparation, e-filing help and tax-preparation coaching through IRS-certified volunteers. Service options can vary by site and may include in-person, drop-off, online coaching or self-preparation support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Tax-Aide provides help free of charge to eligible taxpayers, with special focus on people over 50 and taxpayers with low to moderate income. AARP membership is not required. A site's ability to prepare a return depends on tax complexity and volunteer capacity.

**Population Served**
Taxpayers needing free tax help, especially older adults and low-to-moderate income taxpayers in Arizona and nationwide.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the AARP Foundation Tax-Aide locator during tax season to find current Mesa or nearby sites and appointment options. For Tax-Aide questions, call 1-888-227-7669 or email taxaide@aarp.org.

**Important Information to Know**
Mesa-area sites are seasonal and can change each year. The locator may be closed outside tax season, so clients should check again close to filing season. Bring required tax documents, photo ID and Social Security/ITIN documents as instructed by the site.

resources.name: Family Involvement Center - Parent Assistance Center and Family Peer Support
resources.description: Family Involvement Center is a family-run Arizona organization offering free parent/family peer support, warmline help, care coordination, and navigation for emotional, physical, and behavioral healthcare, schools, DCS, juvenile justice, DDD, courts, benefits, housing, employment, and other systems.
resources.address: Phoenix office: 5333 N 7th St, Suite A-100, Phoenix, AZ 85014; statewide phone and virtual support available
resources.hours: Call or use the support form; public pages describe warmline, walk-in, email, website, and virtual self-referral access but do not list a single schedule.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free parent/family warmline and peer support, caregiver and youth support, parent education and navigation across schools/IEP/504, DDD, DCS, foster care, juvenile justice, family courts, benefits and behavioural/physical health. Adult and family services can help coordinate housing, employment, transport, relationships and substance-use-related needs; counselling and other enrolled services have their own intake.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Parent Assistance Center is described as available to Arizona parents and family members with self-referral options. Some expanded counseling, enrollment, or funded services may have separate eligibility rules.

**Population Served**
Arizona parents, families, caregivers, foster/kinship/adoptive caregivers, grandparents raising children, and families navigating child-serving or behavioral-health systems.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-288-0155 for Family Involvement Center or the Parent Assistance Center. The free family-support line 877-568-8468 does not require a referral. Ask about care-team participation, school plans and the family’s specific navigation need.

**Important Information to Know**
Peer support and systems navigation can help families prepare for appointments and advocate within agencies. It is not emergency care, detox, medication-assisted addiction treatment or residential treatment; ask about the actual counselling/referral options and any payer requirements for the requested service.

resources.name: Fresh Start Women's Foundation - Career Training, Coaching, and Employment Advising
resources.description: Fresh Start Women's Foundation offers free or fully funded career-training opportunities for women, plus education advising, resume and interview help and employer connections in fields such as healthcare, trades, IT, manufacturing, finance and entrepreneurship.
resources.address: 1130 E. McDowell Road, Phoenix, AZ 85006
resources.hours: Training cohorts and formats vary; connect online or by phone before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Hands-on career training opportunities for women, with education advisors, resume writing, interview preparation, cohort support and direct connections to hiring employers after successful training completion. Featured pathways include finance, trades exploratory, semiconductor manufacturing, clean energy/trades, OSHA 10 and flagger certification, CNA, IT, carpentry, electrical, cable harness wiring, automotive/diesel, CDL, DreamBuilder, Grow with Google and composites.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Fresh Start resources are designed for women in Arizona age 18 and older. Each training pathway may have its own cohort dates, prerequisites, funding limits, application steps or partner admission requirements.

**Population Served**
Adult women in Arizona seeking job training, career support and economic self-sufficiency, including women returning to work or changing careers.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the Fresh Start connect/get-started form from the website or call 602-252-8494. Main location: 1130 E. McDowell Road, Phoenix. Ask which cohorts are open, whether a training is online or in person, and what documents are needed.

**Important Information to Know**
The official page describes multiple trainings as free or fully funded, but cohort availability and pathway-specific requirements can change. Confirm current openings, waitlists and whether transportation or equipment is required.

resources.name: Maricopa SHIFT - Safe, Healthy Infants, and Families Thrive
resources.description: Maricopa SHIFT coordinates compassionate referrals and care connections for pregnant people, parents, babies, and families affected by substance use disorder in Maricopa County, including SUD/OUD treatment, MAT, insurance resources, mental-health services, prenatal/pediatric/postpartum care, WIC, home visiting, parent education, and NAS care.
resources.hours: Call or email for referral; no walk-in location is listed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Coordinated connections to SUD treatment, OUD treatment, medication-assisted treatment, insurance resources, mental-health services, healthcare provider networks, prenatal care, pediatric care, postpartum care, WIC, home visiting, parent education, neonatal abstinence syndrome care, and child-development education.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Pregnant individuals, parents, babies, and families affected by substance use in Maricopa County may be referred or inquire. SHIFT is a collaborative referral network, so the receiving provider determines program-specific eligibility.

**Population Served**
Pregnant people, parents, affected newborns, and families in Maricopa County affected by substance use disorder.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-526-6116 or email maricopaSHIFT@maricopa.gov for information or referral guidance. Families can inquire directly; confirm whether the selected receiving service needs a provider referral and what happens next. Ask the coordinator about language support at the receiving service.

**Important Information to Know**
SHIFT coordinates connections rather than providing treatment itself. Confirm the receiving provider, eligibility, response time and next steps; a referral is not an appointment or admission guarantee.

resources.name: Brighter Way Institute · Bob & Renee Parsons Center for Pediatric Dentistry
resources.description: Brighter Way Institute's Bob & Renee Parsons Center for Pediatric Dentistry provides dental care for underserved children and youth, including preventive, restorative, orthodontic, anesthesia and specialized pediatric dental services.
resources.address: 3140 W. Buckeye Rd., Phoenix, AZ 85009
resources.hours: Call 602-362-0744 to confirm pediatric center hours, intake and appointment availability; detailed public hours were not posted on the overview page reviewed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Preventive, restorative, orthodontic, anesthesia and specialized dental care for underserved children and youth through a pediatric dental center.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official dental-centers page identifies this as a dental home for underserved children and youth but does not publish full age, income, insurance, referral or capacity rules. Confirm intake before referral.

**Population Served**
Underserved children and youth in Maricopa County who need pediatric dental care and can travel to Phoenix.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Brighter Way Institute at 602-362-0744 and ask about the Bob & Renee Parsons Center for Pediatric Dentistry intake, eligibility, fees and appointment availability.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not located in Mesa. Public details on fees, documentation and referral mechanics are limited on the overview page, so families should call before traveling.

resources.name: Arizona Commission for the Deaf and the Hard of Hearing Deaf Services and Communication Advocacy
resources.description: The Arizona Commission for the Deaf and the Hard of Hearing provides statewide information, referral, communication-access advocacy, training, consultation, relay and equipment pathways, and is listed by Arizona courts as an approved domestic-violence legal-advocate organization serving all Arizona.
resources.address: 100 N 15th Ave, Suite 104, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.hours: Meeting requests can be made online; call or email before visiting. ACDHH is not a 24-hour crisis service.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Statewide information, referrals, communication-access advocacy, provider training and consultation for Deaf, Hard of Hearing and DeafBlind people. Services include relay and assistive-telecommunications pathways and help navigating communication access to public services, health care, shelters and courts.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Arizona residents who are Deaf, Hard of Hearing, DeafBlind, or need communication access information, and for providers trying to make services accessible. It is not a domestic-violence shelter or emergency hotline.

**Population Served**
Deaf, Hard of Hearing, and DeafBlind Arizonans statewide, including Mesa survivors who need communication access to hotlines, shelters, courts, health care, or public services.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the ACDHH website meeting request, call the main voice number 602-542-3323, use videophone 480-559-9441, or use Arizona Relay 7-1-1. For immediate domestic-violence safety, also contact a DV hotline, shelter, or 911.

**Important Information to Know**
The Arizona courts directory lists ACDHH as an approved domestic-violence legal-advocate organization, but current active advocate availability is unconfirmed. Use the established accessibility/referral service and ask specifically about any current legal-advocate appointment; do not promise legal advice, representation or crisis response.

resources.name: Patient Advocate Foundation - TotalAssist
resources.description: Patient Advocate Foundation's TotalAssist is a national charitable patient financial-assistance program with nearly 150 disease-specific and health-equity funds for eligible out-of-pocket healthcare costs.
resources.hours: TotalAssist call center listed on official transition pages: 866-512-3861. Legacy sources list 8:30 AM-5:30 PM ET; confirm current call-center hours when applying.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Charitable financial assistance grants for eligible out-of-pocket healthcare expenses. Patient Advocate Foundation states TotalAssist includes nearly 150 disease-specific and health-equity funds and can cover medication copays, coinsurance and deductibles, health insurance premiums, office visit charges on treatment day and treatment-administration charges. Some legacy PAN transportation grants remain governed by their grant rules.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility is fund-specific and depends on diagnosis, eligible expenses, income validation, open fund status and grant rules. New financial-assistance applications at Patient Advocate Foundation are through TotalAssist as of July 1, 2026.

**Population Served**
Patients nationwide with serious, chronic, rare or complex conditions, including eligible Mesa residents, who match an open TotalAssist fund.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply or manage grants through TotalAssist.org or Portal.TotalAssist.org. The official Patient Advocate Foundation transition page lists the TotalAssist call center at 866-512-3861.

**Important Information to Know**
The direct TotalAssist pages returned a 403 in this check, but official Patient Advocate Foundation transition pages confirm TotalAssist's launch and routes. Fund availability and eligible expense categories can change; approval is not guaranteed.

resources.name: Mesa Community College Title IX Support and Reporting Pathway
resources.description: Mesa Community College students and employees can use Maricopa Community Colleges' Title IX pathway to report sexual harassment, sexual assault, dating or partner violence, and stalking and to request supportive measures and referrals.
resources.address: 1833 W Southern Ave, Mesa, AZ 85202
resources.hours: Use the online Title IX complaint route or contact the regional EO/Title IX program director during college business hours; call 911 for immediate danger.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Title IX reporting and support for sexual assault, sexual harassment, dating or partner violence, and stalking involving Mesa Community College students or employees. The pathway can discuss reporting options, supportive academic or other available changes, and referrals to counseling, health, victim advocacy, legal, immigration, and law-enforcement resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Mesa Community College students and employees, and for incidents that fit Maricopa Community Colleges Title IX or discrimination/misconduct processes. Formal process availability depends on the person's relationship to the college and the facts of the incident.

**Population Served**
Mesa Community College students and employees affected by sexual misconduct, dating or partner violence, stalking, or related discrimination concerns.

**How to Best Connect**
For Mesa Community College Title IX reports, contact Beverly Traver, EO/Title IX Regional Program Director, at 480-731-8916 or use the online Title IX complaint form. For immediate danger call 911. MCC's Southern and Dobson campus main address is 1833 W Southern Ave, Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a reporting and supportive-measures pathway, not itself a counseling appointment. MCC’s separate Counseling Department offers student counseling. Ask about confidentiality, available supportive measures, and the difference between receiving support and filing a formal complaint before sharing details.

resources.name: Lutheran Social Services of the Southwest - Mesa Family Resource Centers, Pantries and Benefits Help
resources.description: Mesa family centers provide parenting and child-development support, benefits enrollment and education/resource navigation; two separately scheduled Mesa pantries provide groceries.
resources.address: West Mesa FRC/pantry: 142 N Date St, Mesa; East Mesa FRC: 612 S Ellsworth Rd, Mesa; East Mesa pantry: 5946 E University Dr, Mesa
resources.hours: FRC appointments/classes: call. West pantry: Tue/Thu 9–11:15 AM except second Tue; second Wed 5–7 PM. East pantry at Victory Lutheran: Mon/Wed 9–11:30 AM. Confirm schedules before travel.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Child-parent workshops, developmental screenings, parenting coaching/education, resource referrals and SNAP/AHCCCS enrollment help. Mesa food pantries provide groceries. Ask FRC staff about current GEDWorks, ESL or financial-literacy partner classes; their present class schedule and enrollment are not established.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Family centers support parents and families; First Things First programming focuses on children birth to five. Pantry instructions list photo ID. SNAP/AHCCCS rules are separate, and individual screenings, supply events or education partners may require appointments and additional eligibility checks.

**Population Served**
Mesa parents and caregivers seeking family/early-childhood or education navigation, and individuals and families needing food or benefits enrollment support. The young-child programme focus does not establish an age restriction on pantry or all benefits help.

**How to Best Connect**
West Mesa FRC and SNAP/AHCCCS appointments: 480-489-5772; East Mesa FRC: 480-489-5773; either center: FamilySPOTSE@lss-sw.org. An enrollment-help appointment is strongly encouraged. West FRC/pantry is at First Evangelical Lutheran, 142 N Date Street. East FRC is at Our Savior Lutheran, 612 S Ellsworth; the East food pantry is at Victory Lutheran, 5946 E University Drive. Ask about Spanish assistance and the current language and schedule of any partner classes.

**Important Information to Know**
These LSS-SW centers are separate from the City Main Library Family Resource Center. FRC, pantry and partner-class schedules differ. This is benefits/education navigation and family/food support, not confirmed direct emergency rent, utility or cash aid.

resources.name: Arizona DES - Home and Community Based Services (HCBS)
resources.description: Arizona DES Home and Community Based Services help functionally impaired older adults and adults with disabilities remain at home through services coordinated by local Area Agencies on Aging.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Home and community supports that may include adult day care, adult day health care, home-delivered meals, meals at senior centers, home health aide, housekeeping, personal care, respite care, transportation and visiting nurse.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be age 60 or older, or age 18-60 with a disability, and functionally impaired and unable to perform activities of daily living such as eating, bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting or mobility. Area Agency on Aging case managers determine eligibility.

**Population Served**
Functionally impaired older adults and adults with disabilities in Arizona, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents served through Area Agency on Aging, Region One.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact the local Area Agency on Aging. For Maricopa County, call Area Agency on Aging, Region One at 602-264-4357 and ask about Home and Community Based Services assessment.

**Important Information to Know**
Services depend on assessment, funding and provider availability. This is a public access pathway to coordinated services, not a guarantee of immediate in-home care or every listed service.

resources.name: The Solstice of Mesa - Income-Restricted 55+ Affordable Apartments
resources.description: The Solstice of Mesa is an affordable income-restricted 55+ apartment community in Mesa with 1-, 2- and 3-bedroom apartments, income limits, minimum income rules and online application/check-availability routes.
resources.address: 307 S Hawes Rd, Mesa, AZ 85208
resources.hours: Office hours Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; Saturday-Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Income-restricted affordable apartments for adults 55 and older, with one-, two- and three-bedroom apartment homes and an online Apply Now/Check Availability route.

**Eligibility Requirements**
At least one adult must meet the 55+ community requirement. Household income and student-status limitations apply. The property lists a minimum household income requirement of 2 times monthly rent and maximum income limits by household size.

**Population Served**
Adults age 55+ seeking income-restricted apartment housing in Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-569-6410, check availability on the website, or use the applicant login/application route. The leasing office is at 307 S Hawes Rd, Mesa, AZ 85208.

**Important Information to Know**
This is affordable apartment housing, not emergency shelter. Income-restricted does not necessarily mean rent is 30% of income. Verify current rents, voucher acceptance, availability and required deposits with the property.

resources.name: City of Mesa Office of Homeless Solutions - Homeless Resource Line (HOPE Line)
resources.description: The City of Mesa Office of Homeless Solutions Homeless Resource Line, also called the HOPE line, is a Mesa access point for people experiencing homelessness to ask about city homeless-response, navigation and partner-resource routing.
resources.hours: Public page lists the line and email but does not publish current response hours; urgent danger still requires emergency or crisis services.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
City access line for people experiencing homelessness in Mesa. Callers can ask for homeless-response routing, navigation resources, and connection to appropriate city or partner programs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people experiencing homelessness or seeking homeless-resource connection in Mesa. The line does not guarantee immediate shelter, transportation, outreach dispatch or program acceptance.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness in Mesa and people helping someone unsheltered in Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-644-HOPE (480-644-4673) or email hope@mesaaz.gov. Leave clear contact information, location and the type of help needed.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an access and routing line, not a shelter bed or emergency response. If someone is in immediate danger, call 911; for behavioral-health crisis, use a crisis line.

resources.name: The Refrigeration School, Inc. - Electro-Mechanical Technologies HVAC and Welding Specialist
resources.description: The Refrigeration School / Tulsa Welding School Phoenix campus offers hands-on HVAC/R, Electro-Mechanical Technologies, electrical and Welding Specialist programs with admissions, financial-aid support, career services and campus tours.
resources.address: 4210 E Washington St, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: Mon-Thu 8:00 AM-8:00 PM; Fri 8:00 AM-4:00 PM; Sat 9:00 AM-1:00 PM; Sun closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Phoenix campus offers skilled-trades training in HVAC/Refrigeration, Electro-Mechanical Technologies, Mechanical Maintenance Engineering, Electrical Technologies and Welding Specialist. The page lists hands-on labs, admissions support, Student Financial Services and Career Services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Admissions, education prerequisites, high school diploma/GED alternatives, program fit, financing and licensing requirements must be confirmed with admissions. Applicants submit an information form or schedule a tour.

**Population Served**
Adults and recent graduates seeking private skilled-trades training in the Phoenix metro area, including Mesa residents who can commute to the Phoenix campus.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 855-232-1669, request more information, get started online or schedule a tour. Ask admissions for total tuition and fees, program length, schedule, aid, accreditation/licensing, completion data and career-services support.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a private career school with costs. Financial aid, scholarships, WIOA support and job placement are not guaranteed for every applicant.

resources.name: The Renew Group — Mesa Residential Treatment
resources.description: Residential substance-use treatment in Mesa, with a stated 30-day program, therapy, recovery groups, nursing/psychiatric support and aftercare planning.
resources.address: 4840 E Jasmine St #105, Mesa, AZ 85205
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Residential substance-use treatment in Mesa, with a stated 30-day program, therapy, recovery groups, nursing/psychiatric support and aftercare planning.

**Eligibility Requirements**

For adult men and women; clinical assessment and coverage/payment arrangements determine admission. Confirm accepted plans and costs before committing.

**Population Served**

Adults seeking residential help for substance use and co-occurring behavioral-health needs.

**How to Best Connect**

Call admissions to ask about current beds, intake criteria, insurance verification and the appropriate arrival location.

**Important Information to Know**

The provider describes medication-assisted treatment and uses detox language, but the checked material does not establish a specific medically supervised withdrawal level. Ask directly about that capability; do not assume AHCCCS acceptance or guaranteed coverage.

resources.name: St. Vincent de Paul - Virginia G. Piper Medical Clinic Specialty Care
resources.description: St. Vincent de Paul's Virginia G. Piper Medical Clinic provides free primary and specialty medical care for uninsured and underserved patients, including specialty pathways that may include ophthalmology and diabetic-retinopathy-related care by referral.
resources.address: 420 W. Watkins Rd., Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.hours: Current clinic hours were not listed on the reviewed page; call before referral or travel.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free clinic care ranging from treatment of acute illness to chronic diseases such as diabetes, primary care, preventive care, ancillary care, and more than 30 specialties. Ophthalmology, diabetic eye care, labs, imaging, and specialty availability should be confirmed through referral or clinic contact.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The clinics serve uninsured and underserved patients. Referral materials indicate the clinic functions as a temporary health care home for uninsured patients who need care access.

**Population Served**
Uninsured and underserved patients in the Phoenix area and Maricopa County, including Mesa residents who can travel to Phoenix or be referred.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-261-6825 to ask about becoming a patient or specialty referral requirements. The Phoenix clinic is connected to the SVdP Watkins campus at 420 W. Watkins Rd., Phoenix, AZ 85003.

**Important Information to Know**
The official page states an East Valley Medical Clinic is coming to Mesa in Fall 2026, but current access for this candidate is the existing Phoenix medical clinic and referral pathway. Confirm current ophthalmology and diabetic retinopathy services before sending a client.

resources.name: New Freedom - 90-Day Reentry Housing and Behavioral Health Program
resources.description: New Freedom provides a no-cost 90-day peer-driven behavioral-health and reentry program with safe structured housing, therapy, peer mentorship, meals, clothing, hygiene essentials, transportation and employment support.
resources.address: Phoenix, AZ
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost 90-day reentry and behavioral-health program with safe structured housing, therapy, peer mentorship, meals, clothing, hygiene essentials, case management, employment/vocational support, transportation and family reunification opportunities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For justice-involved people returning home who meet New Freedom program criteria. The public page is designed for friends/family and does not publish full eligibility, referral-source or criminal-justice restriction details.

**Population Served**
Men and women reentering the community after incarceration or justice involvement, with men served at the Peoria facility and women at the Deer Valley facility according to the opened page.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-622-1178 or use New Freedom's Get in Touch route. Ask about eligibility, referral source, release-day pickup and current bed availability before planning around placement.

**Important Information to Know**
The page says the program is no cost to members and graduates commonly leave with housing and employment secured, but acceptance, capacity and restrictions must be confirmed by New Freedom.

resources.name: Military Assistance Mission - Basic Needs Support / Financial Assistance
resources.description: Military Assistance Mission Basic Needs Support provides financial assistance for eligible Arizona active-duty, National Guard, Reserve and certain post-9/11 Purple Heart or combat-action recipients; covered needs include utilities but not phone or internet.
resources.hours: Applications are reviewed Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-3:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
MAM's Basic Needs Program only assists with rent, mortgage, car payment, car insurance, utilities and food.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be stationed in and reside in Arizona, meet income rules, and qualify as active-duty, National Guard or Reserve E-5 or below, or as a post-9/11 Purple Heart/Combat Action Badge or equivalent recipient. Current members supply a current LES, military ID and most recent orders. Purple Heart applicants supply DD214/DD215, the certificate and a one-page VA rating; Combat Action Badge applicants supply DD214/DD215 and the badge/equivalent documentation. Submit complete bills and all required documents.

**Population Served**
Arizona-based military households meeting the program's rank/status, residency, documentation and income rules.

**How to Best Connect**
Start from the official Basic Needs Support page using a laptop or desktop; the provider says the application cannot be completed on a cellphone. Call 480-385-9600 for application questions during the posted Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM–3:00 PM business hours, or email mam@azmam.org. Follow the application’s document-format and current income requirements.

**Important Information to Know**
Only rent, mortgage, car payment, car insurance, utilities and food are covered. The programme excludes credit cards, phones, internet, car/home repairs, appliances, transportation, moving and funerals. Approval depends on income, complete documents and funds; it is not general aid for all veterans.

resources.name: Phoenix Public Library · College Depot
resources.description: Phoenix Public Library College Depot offers free college planning and re-engagement services, including one-on-one help with college applications, FAFSA, scholarships, career paths, skilled trades, and related adult re-engagement programs.
resources.address: Burton Barr Central Library, 1221 N. Central Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.hours: Appointment and event availability vary; confirm before travel.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free college planning and re-engagement services, including one-on-one help with college applications, FAFSA, scholarships, career paths, skilled trades, apprenticeship connections, GRIT, Craft a Profession, and adult re-engagement resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Official materials support free services but do not clearly state whether every appointment is open to Mesa residents. Some programs may be targeted to Phoenix residents, Phoenix-area students, or partner-school students, so confirm residency, age, school-year, virtual, and appointment limits.

**Population Served**
Students, families, and adult learners in the Phoenix/Valley area seeking college access, financial-aid help, scholarships, skilled-trade or career-path information, or re-engagement with education.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-261-8847, email college.depot@phoenix.gov, or use the College Depot appointments page. Ask whether phone, virtual, or in-person help is available for a Mesa client.

**Important Information to Know**
The main College Depot page requires JavaScript in some views, but official Phoenix and library materials continue to describe active free College Depot services. Confirm current appointment availability before referral.

resources.name: Harvest Compassion Center - Food Banking Re-Imagined / Clothing Boutique
resources.description: Harvest Compassion Center operates Phoenix-area shopping centers with food, hygiene, baby items, and clothing boutiques where guests can shop during posted open hours.
resources.address: North Phoenix: 4744 E Thunderbird Rd, Ste 9, Phoenix, AZ 85032; other sites in West Phoenix, Maryvale, and Tolleson
resources.hours: North Phoenix: Monday, Wednesday, Saturday 9:00-11:30 AM; West Phoenix: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday 9:00-11:30 AM; Maryvale: Tuesday, Friday, Saturday 9:00-11:30 AM; Tolleson: Wednesday and Friday 9:00-11:30 AM. Must be in line by 11:15 AM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Harvest Compassion Center provides a mini-mart and clothing boutique model with food, clothing, hygiene products, baby items, and other basic needs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Bring identification and confirm the intended center can serve the household before travelling from Mesa. Listings describe Arizona residents and a visit no more than once every 30 days; ask the center to confirm its current document and frequency rules.

**Population Served**
Arizona individuals and families needing food, clothing, hygiene products, and baby supplies who can travel to a Phoenix-area Harvest Compassion Center location.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the location closest to the client and arrive before the 11:15 AM cutoff. North Phoenix phone is 602-788-2444; West Phoenix is 602-841-7110; Maryvale is 623-247-0039; Tolleson is 623-349-0077.

**Important Information to Know**
There is no Mesa site. Check transport, the selected center’s schedule, visit limits and stock before promising specific clothing, food or baby items. Home delivery is not established.

resources.name: Agave Ridge Behavioral Hospital - Medical Detox and Addiction Treatment
resources.description: Agave Ridge Behavioral Hospital in Mesa offers inpatient treatment for adults and adolescents with mental-health and substance-use concerns, medical detoxification support, and intensive outpatient step-down care.
resources.address: 3322 S Ellsworth Rd, Mesa, AZ 85212
resources.hours: 24/7 phone line for calls and assessment inquiries.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Adolescent and adult inpatient behavioral-health and substance-use care, medically supervised detox when clinically appropriate, medication management, individual/group/family therapy and discharge planning.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The provider describes programs for adolescents ages 12–17 and adults. Assessment determines age/program fit, medical stability, detox suitability, admission and payment arrangements.

**Population Served**
Adolescents, adults, and seniors in Mesa and the greater Phoenix/East Valley area with addiction, detox, or co-occurring mental-health needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 833-448-1526 for 24/7 help or assessment scheduling. The hospital is at 3322 S Ellsworth Rd, Mesa, AZ 85212.

**Important Information to Know**
Detox and inpatient programs have different clinical criteria and capacity. Ask which services are currently available for the person’s age and needs. Discharge referral to outpatient care does not mean the hospital itself operates an intensive outpatient program.

resources.name: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services - Form I-912 immigration filing fee-waiver pathway
resources.description: USCIS Form I-912 is the official request pathway for a fee waiver for eligible USCIS forms and services when the applicant qualifies based on a means-tested benefit, low household income or financial hardship.
resources.hours: Online information and forms are available through USCIS; no local office hours apply.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Official USCIS fee-waiver request form and instructions for eligible immigration forms and services. It can help applicants ask USCIS to waive certain filing fees when they cannot afford the fee.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A fee waiver is only available for eligible forms or services. Current Form I-912 materials identify bases such as receiving a means-tested benefit, household income at or below the required Federal Poverty Guidelines threshold, or financial hardship, with supporting documentation.

**Population Served**
Eligible USCIS applicants nationwide, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents, whose immigration filing is fee-waiver eligible.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the official USCIS Form I-912 page, current form PDF and instructions before filing. The USCIS Contact Center number is 800-375-5283 for general USCIS contact.

**Important Information to Know**
Not every immigration form or fee is waiver-eligible. A fee-waiver approval does not approve the underlying immigration benefit. Always check the current form edition, instructions, required evidence and filing method before submitting.

resources.name: Bridging AZ Furniture Bank - Agency-Referred Furniture Services
resources.description: Bridging AZ Furniture Bank provides furniture, household goods and new beds through participating social-service agencies for qualified clients working their way out of homelessness, especially people with disabilities and veterans.
resources.address: 25 N Extension Rd, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Agency-referred; do not send walk-ins.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Basic furniture, household goods and new beds for qualified clients of participating social-service agencies. The program furnishes apartments and supports people moving out of homelessness.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Clients must be identified and qualified through participating social-service agencies and caseworkers. Bridging AZ does not function as a direct walk-in furniture store for individuals.

**Population Served**
People working their way out of homelessness in Arizona, including people with disabilities, veterans and households supported by partner agencies.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the client's housing case manager, social-service agency or veteran/homeless-services worker whether they are a Bridging AZ partner and can submit a furniture referral.

**Important Information to Know**
Inventory, delivery, pickup, partner list and any fees are not fully public. Confirm current referral capacity and logistics before promising furniture.

resources.name: Maricopa County — Ryan White dental insurance
resources.description: Provides dental-coverage enrollment for eligible people living with HIV in Maricopa or Pinal County.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides dental-coverage enrollment for eligible people living with HIV in Maricopa or Pinal County.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Ryan White Part A eligibility; Central Eligibility requests HIV diagnosis, county residency and current-income documentation.

**Population Served**
Eligible residents of Maricopa or Pinal County living with HIV/AIDS.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-506-6892 to ask about enrollment and participating Delta Dental providers.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm the current income rule, covered services, benefit limits and dentist availability; approval is not automatic.

resources.name: Veterans Furniture Center - HUD-VASH Furniture and Household Goods
resources.description: Veterans Furniture Center provides free new furniture and household goods to formerly homeless veterans moving into housing through HUD-VASH; veterans must be referred by VA/HUD-VASH caseworkers, not self-refer.
resources.phone: Referral through VA HUD-VASH caseworker; Phoenix CRRC: 602-248-6040
resources.address: Mail only: P.O. Box 1062, Sun City, AZ 85372-1062
resources.hours: Hours are not published; access is through VA caseworker referral.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free new furniture and household goods for veterans moving from homelessness into housing, including items such as beds, sofas or loveseats, table and chairs, dresser, TV, kitchen package, linens, towels, personal hygiene and cleaning kits.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Veterans must be enrolled in VA HUD-VASH and referred by a VA caseworker. The organization states veterans should not contact Veterans Furniture Center directly for assistance.

**Population Served**
Greater Phoenix and Maricopa County veterans moving from homelessness into housing through VA HUD-VASH.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the veteran's VA HUD-VASH caseworker to make the referral. If the veteran does not have a caseworker, the official site directs them to the Phoenix Community Resource Referral Center, 1500 E. Thomas Road, Phoenix, 602-248-6040.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a furnishing resource after housing placement, not emergency shelter or general furniture assistance. Current item availability, delivery timing and service area should be confirmed through the referring caseworker.

resources.name: Good Life Recovery — Mesa Sober Living
resources.description: Sober-living housing in Mesa with a recovery-focused shared-home environment.
resources.address: 508 S Mesa Dr, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Sober-living housing in Mesa with a recovery-focused shared-home environment.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Ask the operator about current house population, sobriety and participation rules, costs and admission requirements.

**Population Served**

People seeking recovery housing in the Phoenix area; the saved Mesa lead describes a men’s home, which should be confirmed for the current placement.

**How to Best Connect**

Call Good Life Recovery before visiting to discuss the Mesa home, availability and the application process.

**Important Information to Know**

Current operator contact and the Mesa location are verified. Published directory certification is not treated as a current license or assurance of vacancies; ask about the specific home before placement.

resources.name: AZEvictionHelp — tenant eviction information
resources.description: Arizona eviction-process information and links to assistance before, during and after an eviction case.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Arizona eviction-process information and links to assistance before, during and after an eviction case.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public site is available to Arizona tenants; legal-aid eligibility varies by provider.

**Population Served**
Tenants dealing with notices, eviction hearings or the consequences of eviction.

**How to Best Connect**
Open AZEvictionHelp, choose the stage of the case and contact a legal provider promptly.

**Important Information to Know**
Information does not postpone a hearing, stop a deadline or create an attorney-client relationship.

resources.name: Recovery Innovations — Peoria Crisis Receiving Center
resources.description: Around-the-clock crisis stabilization, observation, medication support and short-term crisis respite.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Around-the-clock crisis stabilization, observation, medication support and short-term crisis respite.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Walk-in crisis support requires no appointment; the team assesses the appropriate level of care.

**Population Served**
People in the region experiencing a mental-health or substance-use crisis.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-636-4356 or 602-636-4378, or use the center’s lobby. Confirm the receiving entrance before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
The provider reports no charge to guests. This is in Peoria, not Mesa; headquarters Suite 402 is not the patient receiving door.

resources.name: Goldensun Peace Ministries - Residential Habilitation, IDLA and Community Support
resources.description: Goldensun Peace Ministries is an AHCCCS/DDD-approved faith-based residential provider in Maricopa County offering supported living homes, habilitation, IDLA, transportation, outings, life-skills training and community support for adults with disabilities.
resources.address: Maricopa County, AZ; homes are in the Glendale area
resources.hours: Call or use the schedule-a-tour route; residential openings are not listed publicly.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Supported living homes, Individually Designed Living Arrangement, licensed habilitation, daily activities, weekly outings, DDD-approved transportation, community-based social programs, life-skills training and faith-based spiritual support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The provider describes AHCCCS/DDD approval and licensed habilitation/IDLA services. Placement likely depends on DDD/AHCCCS authorization, residential fit, guardian/family agreement and available openings.

**Population Served**
Adults with developmental disabilities in Maricopa County who need structured residential support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 623-234-3516 or email director@goldensunaz.org to ask about eligibility, DDD authorization, current openings and scheduling a tour.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a small residential provider, not an emergency housing program. The program is explicitly Christ-centered; families should decide whether that environment fits the person's preferences and rights.

resources.name: San Miguel Apartments - Affordable Apartments Waitlist
resources.description: San Miguel Apartments is an affordable Mesa apartment community with one-, two- and three-bedroom homes, published rent ranges, a phone number and a Join Our Waitlist contact route.
resources.address: 8915 E. Guadalupe Road, Mesa, AZ 85212
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Affordable apartment rentals in Mesa with one-, two- and three-bedroom homes, online application/availability links and a waitlist/contact form.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The opened official page does not publish detailed LIHTC income limits or screening criteria. Applicants should ask management for current income restrictions, application requirements, fees and waitlist rules.

**Population Served**
Households seeking affordable rental apartments in Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-354-1515 or use the Join Our Waitlist/Contact Us form on the official website. Visit/contact address: 8915 E. Guadalupe Road, Mesa, AZ 85212.

**Important Information to Know**
The website lists pricing from about $1,165 to $1,875 and says pricing/availability should be checked through the property. Current unit availability, waitlist timing, LIHTC eligibility and move-in costs must be verified with management.

resources.name: Pascua Yaqui Tribe Enrollment Division - Guadalupe Enrollment Annex
resources.description: Pascua Yaqui Tribe Enrollment Division's Guadalupe Enrollment Annex provides local access to Enrollment services for the Guadalupe area, including tribal ID, CDIB, enhanced tribal card and related enrollment-record services for eligible Pascua Yaqui members or applicants.
resources.address: Itom Hiapsi Building, 9405 S Avenida Del Yaqui, Guadalupe, AZ 85283
resources.hours: Call 480-768-2042 before visiting to confirm appointment rules, documents and fees.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides local access to Pascua Yaqui Enrollment Division services in Guadalupe and surrounding areas. The Enrollment Division pages route users to tribal identification card, Certificate Degree of Indian Blood, Enhanced Tribal Identification Card, delayed birth certificate and membership/enrollment services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Limited to Pascua Yaqui citizens, members and eligible enrollment or membership-record applicants. It is not a general tribal ID provider for members of other tribes.

**Population Served**
Pascua Yaqui members, citizens and eligible applicants in Guadalupe and nearby communities, including clients near Mesa and Tempe.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Guadalupe Enrollment Annex at 480-768-2042. The office is at the Itom Hiapsi Building, 9405 S Avenida Del Yaqui, Guadalupe, AZ 85283.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm required documents, appointment availability, fees and whether the specific service can be completed at the annex. Tribal credential offices serve only their own eligible members or applicants.

resources.name: Consulate General of Mexico in Phoenix - Community legal consultation days for Mexican nationals
resources.description: The Consulate General of Mexico in Phoenix is listed by Aliento as hosting free legal consultations for Mexican nationals, with monthly dates and times posted through the consulate's Facebook page.
resources.address: 320 E McDowell Rd #105, Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.hours: Dates and times vary; check the Consulado General de Mexico en Phoenix Facebook page or call before going.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free community legal consultations for Mexican nationals are listed at the Mexican Consulate in Phoenix. The public listing does not prove full immigration representation; treat this as brief consultation, screening and referral unless the consulate confirms otherwise.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The listed pathway is for Mexican nationals. The exact legal topics, appointment rules and whether a person must have consular registration are not stated in the public listing.

**Population Served**
