Mexican nationals in Arizona, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents who can travel to the Phoenix consulate or contact it for current sessions.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-242-7398 or check the Consulado General de Mexico en Phoenix Facebook page for the current month's consultation dates and times before traveling to 320 E McDowell Rd #105, Phoenix.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a consular/community consultation lead, not a confirmed ongoing attorney-client representation program. Confirm the next session, topic scope, documents to bring, language access and appointment process.

resources.name: A New Leaf - Faith House Domestic Violence and Crisis Shelter
resources.description: A New Leaf's Faith House is a 24-hour confidential crisis shelter in Maricopa County for single adult men and women and adults with children experiencing domestic violence, human trafficking, homelessness or other urgent circumstances.
resources.phone: 623-939-6798 Faith House; 480-890-3039 A New Leaf DV hotline
resources.address: Confidential West Valley shelter; obtain directions from staff
resources.hours: 24-hour emergency shelter model; call before going anywhere because the location is confidential.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Faith House provides confidential crisis shelter, three meals a day, basic living needs, resource connection, empowerment activities, personal and legal advocacy, counseling referrals and help connecting to employment, childcare and transportation resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For single adult men and women and adults with children experiencing domestic violence, human trafficking, homelessness or other urgent circumstances. Entry depends on screening, safety needs and capacity.

**Population Served**
Survivors and crisis-affected adults in Maricopa County, including single adults and adults with children.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Faith House at 623-939-6798 or A New Leaf’s DV hotline at 480-890-3039 for screening and routing. Use these public service contacts rather than individual programme staff. Do not travel to a confidential location without staff direction.

**Important Information to Know**
Faith House is in the West Valley, but may be relevant for Mesa clients who need safe placement. Meals and material support are for shelter participants, not a public pantry or clothing closet. Capacity and pet arrangements must be confirmed.

resources.name: Joining Hearts - Pregnancy Support and Resource Connections
resources.description: Free statewide pregnancy support, parenting information, adoption planning when requested and community-resource connections, with meetings at a place comfortable for the client.
resources.address: Statewide Arizona; a pregnancy specialist arranges a meeting with the client
resources.hours: Call or text for support and meeting arrangements; current response hours were not confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Pregnancy support, parenting information, ongoing emotional support and connections to housing, food benefits, clothing, medical care and other community resources. Adoption planning is available if the parent chooses it.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Anyone may call or text about pregnancy support, including family members. Support is free and may begin during pregnancy or after birth.

**Population Served**
Pregnant and recently parenting people and families throughout Arizona, including Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Call or text 888-818-4445. A specialist can arrange to meet at home or another comfortable location; ask about current response and appointment availability.

**Important Information to Know**
Joining Hearts describes its approach as life-affirming pregnancy support. It is not a medical facility and does not provide pregnancy tests, ultrasound or prenatal medical care. Resource connections do not guarantee another agency's housing, financial aid or appointments.

resources.name: Matthew House AZ - East Valley refugee and immigrant integration support
resources.description: Matthew House AZ helps refugee and immigrant families in the East Valley with housing subsidies, English and tutoring programs, cultural mentorship, employment coaching, financial-literacy support and Welcome Teams that help families navigate local systems and essential services.
resources.address: Mesa, AZ; mailing address 2820 S Alma School Rd, Suite 18-223, Chandler, AZ 85286
resources.hours: English classes and tutoring follow posted schedules during school schedules; no walk-in service hours are published, so contact before sending a client.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Housing subsidies and housing guidance, adult English language learning, K-12 tutoring, Welcome Teams, cultural mentorship, employment coaching, financial-literacy support and help navigating local systems, public benefits, education and essential services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The site describes service to refugee and immigrant families, especially in the East Valley. Public intake criteria, referral rules and funding limits are not posted.

**Population Served**
Refugee and immigrant families in Mesa and the East Valley who can connect with Matthew House AZ programming.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-809-6225 or email info@matthewhouseaz.org. Use the mailing address only for mail; confirm the location and format of any appointment before traveling. The website includes a Join a Class link for adult English classes.

**Important Information to Know**
The official site supports strong East Valley integration services but does not publish a walk-in service address or detailed client intake criteria. Confirm referral eligibility, funding availability and where any in-person appointment occurs.

resources.name: City of Mesa Electric Utility - Electric Smart Peaks Program
resources.description: Mesa Electric Smart Peaks is a voluntary demand-response program for City of Mesa electric customers with eligible internet-connected thermostats, offering first-year and annual gift-card incentives.
resources.hours: Online enrollment available; enrollment requests may take 5 business days to process.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The program rewards eligible customers for allowing brief smart-thermostat adjustments during peak electric demand periods between May 1 and September 30. Rewards are $100 in gift cards the first year and $50 after each summer season for continued participation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Participants must be commercial or residential customers in Mesa's electric service area, not SRP customers; have a qualifying internet-connected thermostat controlling central air conditioning; keep the thermostat connected; and have a Mesa utility account in good standing.

**Population Served**
City of Mesa electric customers with eligible smart thermostats and central air conditioning.

**How to Best Connect**
Enroll through the City of Mesa Electric Smart Peaks page. For thermostat connection problems or unenrollment, email electricprograms@mesaaz.gov.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an incentive and energy-management program, not utility arrears assistance. Events typically last no more than four hours, customers can opt out during an event, and the City or program host may accept or reject applications.

resources.name: Social Security Administration - Ticket to Work
resources.description: Social Security's Ticket to Work program connects eligible SSDI and SSI disability beneficiaries with authorized employment-support providers, benefits counseling and work-incentive information.
resources.hours: Ticket to Work Help Line: Monday-Friday 8 AM-8 PM Eastern Time.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Ticket to Work helps Social Security disability beneficiaries find authorized service providers who can explain how work affects benefits, provide training, assist with job search and support a path toward employment and financial independence.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is for eligible SSI or SSDI disability beneficiaries. Provider participation and ticket assignment depend on SSA rules and the selected Employment Network or state Vocational Rehabilitation agency.

**Population Served**
Eligible Social Security disability beneficiaries nationwide, including Mesa residents, who are considering work, looking for work or already working.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Ticket to Work Help Line at 866-968-7842, TTY 866-833-2967, use the Choose Work Find Help tool, or email TicketToWork@ssa.gov.

**Important Information to Know**
Work can affect cash and health benefits differently depending on SSI, SSDI, earnings and work incentives. Benefits counseling should happen before major earnings changes; an Employment Network may not accept every ticket.

resources.name: Free Charity Cars - vehicle distribution
resources.description: Free Charity Cars accepts free online vehicle applications from eligible U.S. residents and reviews applicants when a donated vehicle becomes available in their area.
resources.hours: Online application available; the organization says not to call staff to apply.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free Charity Cars distributes donated program vehicles to eligible applicants when suitable vehicles are donated. Applicants complete the online vehicle request form and may reapply because applications are deleted after 3 months.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be U.S. residents, age 18 or older, have a valid driver license, be at or below 200% of the federal poverty level, lack sustainable transportation, have computer/internet access, complete the online application, and be able to pay tag, title, emissions, insurance, maintenance and other costs if selected.

**Population Served**
The program lists domestic-violence survivors, medically needy people, disaster victims, families transitioning from public assistance to work, families in transitional living shelters, working-poor households, nonprofits and military families.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through the Vehicle Request Form after reading the FAQ. Do not call to apply; the FAQ says calls about receiving a vehicle can result in account deletion. Use the contact page only for appropriate non-application questions.

**Important Information to Know**
A vehicle is never guaranteed and the wait can be extensive because awards depend on local donations and review of the applicant's story. The program does not provide vehicle repair money or pay insurance, registration, tag, title or upkeep costs.

resources.name: Encircle Families - Refugee and Asylee Mentorship Program
resources.description: Encircle Families' Refugee and Asylee Mentorship Program provides culturally responsive disability education and mentorship for refugee and asylee families raising children with disabilities.
resources.address: 5025 East Washington Street, Suite 204, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: Call or use Encircle Families referral routes; program availability should be confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Culturally appropriate support and mentorship to help refugee and asylee families understand a child's disability, work with education and treatment professionals, and advocate for positive education and health outcomes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For refugee and asylee families raising children with disabilities. Exact current enrollment requirements and availability should be confirmed with Encircle Families.

**Population Served**
Arizona refugee and asylee families with children with disabilities, including families in Maricopa County resettlement communities.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact Encircle Families at 602-242-4366 or info@encirclefamilies.org, or use the family referral form. The Sonoran Center can also route questions about refugee disability work through ucedd@arizona.edu.

**Important Information to Know**
This is disability mentorship and family education, not legal immigration representation. Ask about language access, current program availability and whether virtual support is offered for Mesa families.

resources.name: Accessible Space, Inc. - R.J. Piltz Vista Bonita Apartments
resources.description: R.J. Piltz Vista Bonita Apartments is an Accessible Space, Inc. Mesa property with 18 accessible, HUD-subsidized one-bedroom apartments for qualifying households with disabilities. Rent is based on 30% of monthly household income and official application routes include online, mail or fax.
resources.address: 1140 E 5th Ave, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: Contact the property or ASI before applying or traveling; vacancy and waitlist timing are not guaranteed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Accessible, HUD-subsidized one-bedroom apartments with wheelchair-accessible kitchens, large accessible bathrooms, roll-in showers, controlled access, community room and laundry. Residents may arrange their own supportive services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must have a qualifying disability, meet income limits and pass criminal, credit and rental-history screening. No minimum income is required according to the official Accessible Space listing, but a security deposit is required.

**Population Served**
Qualifying people with disabilities who need accessible subsidized housing in Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the housing application and upload options on the Accessible Space page, or mail/fax the application as instructed in the application packet. Contact the property directly at 480-889-0893 or call ASI at 800-466-7722 for more information.

**Important Information to Know**
Availability and wait time are not confirmed by the public page. Application submission does not guarantee a unit, and screening applies. Approved pets are welcome under building rules.

resources.name: Southwest Behavioral & Health Services — Court liaison
resources.description: Provides court-linked behavioral-health navigation and community support through its justice-involved court liaison program.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides court-linked behavioral-health navigation and community support through its justice-involved court liaison program.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Confirm the qualifying City of Phoenix court involvement and referral authority; this is not universal Mesa eligibility.

**Population Served**
Eligible people involved in the participating Phoenix criminal court pathway.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the assigned court team about the SBH liaison, or call SBH at 602-265-8338 to identify the appropriate program.

**Important Information to Know**
Keep the court-specific program distinct from general outpatient behavioral-health services.

resources.name: ACLU of Arizona - civil-liberties legal assistance complaint intake
resources.description: The ACLU of Arizona accepts written civil-liberties complaints from people in Arizona and may select matters for no-cost legal assistance, advocacy, or impact litigation when government or institutional action affects constitutional rights.
resources.address: P.O. Box 17148, Phoenix, AZ 85011
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Written civil-liberties complaint intake for possible legal assistance, advocacy, or impact litigation in selected cases involving rights violations, often by government agencies or institutions.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The issue must involve civil liberties or civil rights in Arizona. The ACLU of Arizona is highly selective and does not provide general low-income legal aid, emergency help, legal advice by phone/email/in person, or routine private-dispute representation.

**Population Served**
People in Arizona, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents, who believe their civil liberties or civil rights have been violated. The page lists examples such as speech, religion, voting rights, equal protection, immigrants' rights, LGBTQ+ rights, and education equality. ACLU Arizona also identifies disability rights as an issue area; a request is still subject to its selective case review.

**How to Best Connect**
Submit the online complaint form or print and mail the complaint form from the ACLU of Arizona Ask For Help page. Do not call for complaint status; the page says review may take up to eight weeks or more.

**Important Information to Know**
Submitting a complaint does not mean the ACLU has agreed to help and does not create emergency protection or stop legal deadlines. Clients with court dates or filing deadlines should seek other legal help immediately.

resources.name: Solari Crisis Response Network - Central Arizona Crisis Line and Mobile Crisis Dispatch
resources.description: 24/7 crisis line and mobile crisis dispatch pathway for Mesa and Central Arizona, operated through Solari/Crisis Response Network and linked with Arizona's 988 and 1-844-534-HOPE crisis system.
resources.hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Solari/Crisis Response Network provides free, immediate and confidential crisis support by phone, 988 and Arizona's statewide crisis number. Crisis Intervention Specialists help with suicide thoughts, anxiety/depression, substance use, violence or abuse, finding safety, counseling and community-service connection. If the crisis cannot be resolved by phone, the line can dispatch a mobile team or connect the caller to a safe place.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Anyone in crisis or concerned about another person may call. For life-threatening medical, police or fire emergencies, call 911.

**Population Served**
People of all ages in Arizona. Central Arizona numbers serve Maricopa County, including Mesa, along with the regional crisis system.

**How to Best Connect**
Call or text 988, call Arizona statewide 1-844-534-HOPE (1-844-534-4673), or for Central Arizona call 602-222-9444 or 800-631-1314. TTY numbers listed by regional materials are 602-274-3360 or 800-327-9254. Mobile crisis dispatch is requested through the crisis line, not by calling a van directly.

**Important Information to Know**
This resource combines the crisis-line and mobile-dispatch submissions because mobile teams are dispatched through the crisis call system. Response time, provider team and dispatch decision vary by location and clinical assessment.

resources.name: HonorHealth - Financial Assistance Policy
resources.description: HonorHealth's Financial Assistance program helps patients apply for assistance paying for care through financial assistance policies, plain-language summaries, applications, income guidelines and provider coverage lists.
resources.address: HonorHealth locations in Maricopa County
resources.hours: Call Financial Customer Service for assistance; public page does not list call-center hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Financial assistance screening and application support for eligible HonorHealth care, with policy documents, plain-language summaries, financial assistance applications, income guidelines and provider coverage lists.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on individual financial circumstances, the financial assistance policy, income guidelines and whether the specific facility/provider is covered.

**Population Served**
Patients receiving HonorHealth care who need help paying for medical bills, including uninsured or underinsured patients in Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call HonorHealth Financial Customer Service at 623-300-9044 or review the English/Spanish financial assistance documents and applications on the official page.

**Important Information to Know**
This is bill-specific financial assistance, not cash aid or guaranteed free care. Confirm whether the particular outpatient clinic, physician or service is included under the policy before relying on it.

resources.name: Thrive AZ - Beds, Furniture, Household Items, and DCS Referral Support
resources.description: Thrive AZ provides foster-care-related client support and referral pathways for biological families with open DCS prevention or reunification cases and youth who are or have transitioned out of foster care.
resources.address: 14202 N 73rd Ave, Peoria, AZ 85381
resources.hours: Office hours: Monday-Thursday 8:30 AM-5:00 PM. Warehouse hours: Monday-Thursday 9:00 AM-3:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Material and client-center support tied to DCS prevention, family reunification and youth transitioning out of foster care; prior official evidence supports beds, bedding, furniture, household items, cleaning and hygiene items.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For biological families with open Department of Child Safety cases in prevention or reunification, and youth who are or have transitioned out of foster care. Prevention and reunification referral forms are for DCS caseworkers only; youth transition referrals can be made by AzCA or DCS workers.

**Population Served**
Arizona families involved in foster-care prevention or reunification and youth/young adults transitioning out of foster care, including Maricopa County clients when connected through the program.

**How to Best Connect**
Established clients can call 602-544-9547 or email clients@thriveaz.org. New prevention/reunification referrals should come from a DCS caseworker using the official referral form; youth transition referrals can be completed by AzCA or DCS workers.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general public furniture or household-goods bank. Assistance is tied to DCS/AzCA referral, eligibility, inventory and current program capacity.

resources.name: Solari - Eligibility and Care Services: SMI Determinations
resources.description: Solari reviews Arizona Serious Mental Illness eligibility determination applications; an SMI determination can open access to specialized behavioral-health and support services for eligible adults.
resources.hours: Questions and appeals by phone; the evaluation request generally begins through the person's AHCCCS contracted behavioral-health provider.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Statewide review of Serious Mental Illness eligibility determination applications, eligibility decisions, status/notice support, and appeal routes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Any Arizona resident can ask about an SMI assessment. The designation is for adults 18+; assessment applicants may be 17.5 or older. A qualifying diagnosis and serious functional impairment or qualifying risk of deterioration must be documented through the assessment process.

**Population Served**
Arizona adults or near-adults who may qualify for Serious Mental Illness services, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the AHCCCS-contracted behavioural-health provider to arrange and submit the assessment. If there is no current provider, contact the assigned AHCCCS plan or regional/tribal behavioural-health authority for a route. For a missing notice, call 855-832-2866; appeal help is available at that number or 602-845-3594.

**Important Information to Know**
Solari reviews assessments, not walk-in treatment requests. The decision notice explains appeal rights; current guidance allows 60 days from the decision to request an appeal. Missing records or an agreed extended evaluation may affect timing.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Economic Security - TANF Jobs Program
resources.description: Arizona DES TANF Jobs Program is the required employment and training program for work-eligible TANF Cash Assistance recipients, providing case management, work-related activities, job skills, and possible support services through Equus Workforce Services.
resources.hours: Call before visiting; DES notes many Jobs Program offices are virtual or may have changed hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The TANF Jobs Program helps work-eligible Cash Assistance recipients build job skills through work-related activities. It may also provide support services to remove barriers to employment. Equus Workforce Services provides case management and employment services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
People are referred to TANF Jobs after being approved, or in some cases pre-approved, for Cash Assistance benefits. It applies to work-eligible individuals, and participation is usually required to receive Cash Assistance.

**Population Served**
Arizona TANF Cash Assistance recipients who are work-eligible, including Mesa and Maricopa County families receiving or entering Cash Assistance.

**How to Best Connect**
Start with the DES Cash Assistance process. Once approved or pre-approved, work-eligible individuals are referred to TANF Jobs. For general information or to contact a Jobs Program worker, call 866-603-0017 and provide full name, case number, and phone number.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not an open public class or general training grant. It is tied to TANF Cash Assistance eligibility and required work activities. Education or training supports depend on the participant’s plan and approval.

resources.name: Chicanos Por La Causa - Supportive Housing Services / H2O Pre-Tenancy
resources.description: CPLC Supportive Housing Services offers resident service coordination, housing navigation, and H2O pre-tenancy/tenancy-sustaining supports for people experiencing or at risk of homelessness, including AHCCCS members with Serious Mental Illness.
resources.address: Phoenix, AZ
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Supportive housing services focused on housing stability, resident service coordination, housing navigation, and H2O pre-tenancy and tenancy-sustaining supports. Help may include locating housing resources, understanding applications, skill-building for tenancy success, home visits, safety checks and crisis-prevention strategies.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Housing navigation serves at-risk and low-income individuals. H2O serves people experiencing or at risk of homelessness, including people with Serious Mental Illness, who are AHCCCS members. Program fit and referral/funding stream should be confirmed with CPLC.

**Population Served**
People in Maricopa County and Arizona CPLC service areas who are experiencing homelessness, at risk of homelessness, or need support to remain housed, including AHCCCS members with SMI for H2O services.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Maricopa County CPLC supportive housing contact at 602-609-7556, email SHS@cplc.org, or use the Housing Service Request Form linked on the CPLC Homelessness page. For H2O questions, CPLC lists 855-814-4673.

**Important Information to Know**
CPLC states that housing navigation is supportive and informational only and does not provide rental assistance, deposits or direct housing placement. It also says resident service coordination does not provide direct financial assistance or direct payments for housing or health care.

resources.name: Formal contractor complaint and Recovery Fund process
resources.description: Official Arizona Registrar of Contractors pathway for licensed/unlicensed contractor complaints, hearings, and possible Residential Contractors' Recovery Fund claims.
resources.address: 1700 W. Washington St. Suite 105, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.hours: Customer service hours Monday-Friday 8:30 AM-4:30 PM; office hours Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM, closed weekends and state holidays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Arizona Registrar of Contractors investigates and works to resolve complaints against licensed contractors and unlicensed entities. The process can include investigation, written directives, legal department review, citations, hearings, and possible Residential Contractors' Recovery Fund claims for eligible residential property owners.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Complaint and Recovery Fund eligibility depends on the type of contractor, license status, property, deadline, and process step. Recovery Fund claims generally require an eligible residential property owner and, in the administrative route, a formal complaint leading to discipline and a bond-claim determination.

**Population Served**
Arizona homeowners, residential property owners, contractors, subcontractors, suppliers, and consumers with contractor-license or construction-work disputes, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the ROC online portal or complaint forms at roc.az.gov/file-complaint. For information, call 602-542-1525 or toll-free 877-MY AZROC (877-692-9762). The Phoenix office is at 1700 W. Washington St., Suite 105.

**Important Information to Know**
ROC does not provide private legal advice or attorney referrals. Civil litigation, bond claims, and agency complaint steps can affect one another. Recovery Fund claims have strict eligibility rules and time limits, and payment is not guaranteed.

resources.name: Maricopa County Human Services Department - Utility Assistance
resources.description: Maricopa County utility assistance helps eligible county residents outside Glendale, Mesa and Phoenix with current utility deposits or payments through the county client portal and local Community Action Program offices.
resources.hours: Appointments through CAP offices are first-come, first-served; online client portal available.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Maricopa County Human Services coordinates assistance with current utility deposits or payments through Community Action Program offices.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must live in Maricopa County outside the cities of Glendale, Mesa and Phoenix. The serving CAP screens the address, household and funding rules. Prepare identification, recent household-income documents and current utility bills; citizenship/qualified-noncitizen verification may be required by the funding source.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County households outside Glendale, Mesa and Phoenix needing utility payment or deposit help. County islands near Mesa require address-specific CAP confirmation.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through the Maricopa County Human Services Department Client Portal or contact the local CAP office for an appointment. Call 602-506-0589 for general inquiries.

**Important Information to Know**
The county page explicitly routes City of Mesa residents to Mesa utility-assistance programs. Applicants must use the CAP office serving their address; funding and appointments are not guaranteed.

resources.name: National Domestic Violence Hotline - 24/7 Confidential Hotline, Chat and Text
resources.description: The National Domestic Violence Hotline provides always-available confidential support by phone, live chat and text, including crisis intervention, education, safety planning and local referrals for people experiencing relationship abuse or supporting someone who is.
resources.hours: Live advocate phone, chat and text access is available as an always-on national route.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Hotline provides confidential phone, chat and text access to live advocates for support, crisis intervention, domestic-violence education, safety planning, community resources and referrals to local providers such as shelters, legal help, financial aid and counseling.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For anyone experiencing relationship abuse, concerned about abuse, or supporting someone experiencing abuse. It is a national remote service and does not require a Mesa address.

**Population Served**
Domestic-violence survivors and concerned friends or family nationwide, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents. The page also routes to StrongHearts for Native survivors, love is respect for young people, and The Deaf Hotline for Deaf and hard-of-hearing survivors.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 800-799-SAFE (7233), use live chat at thehotline.org, or text START to 88788. Use a safe device and clear browser history if technology monitoring is a concern. Spanish-speaking advocates are available through The Hotline.

**Important Information to Know**
The Hotline does not provide direct financial assistance such as cash, hotel vouchers or transportation vouchers, but advocates can connect callers to community resources that may help. For immediate danger, call 911.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Administration / Capitol Rideshare - Commuter Club Emergency Ride Home and Vanpool Subsidy
resources.description: Capitol Rideshare's Commuter Club provides eligible State of Arizona employees in Maricopa County with an Emergency Ride Home benefit and related commute supports when they use alternate modes to get to work.
resources.address: 100 N. 15th Ave., Suite 301, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Commuter Club Emergency Ride Home benefit provides a Lyft Pass credit of up to $50, up to twice per fiscal year, for unexpected emergencies on days an enrolled state employee used an alternate commute mode. Capitol Rideshare also describes vanpool and commute support for eligible state employees.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Commuter Club membership and services are limited to State of Arizona employees in Maricopa County; contractors are not eligible. The emergency ride home requires prior enrollment, an active Lyft account, alternate-mode commute use, and a qualifying unexpected emergency.

**Population Served**
Eligible State of Arizona employees in Maricopa County who commute by alternate modes. This is not a general public ride voucher.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Capitol Rideshare Commuter Club page to enroll before an emergency, or call Capitol Rideshare at 602-542-7433 with questions.

**Important Information to Know**
Emergency Ride Home cannot reimburse rides already paid out of pocket and is not for regular rides to work. Lyft Pass credit must be claimed through the RideAmigos Commuter Club account and used according to program terms.

resources.name: East Valley Institute of Technology - Adult HVACR Program
resources.description: EVIT's Adult HVACR Program is a 360-clock-hour hands-on heating, ventilation, air conditioning and refrigeration training pathway that counts as a pre-apprenticeship and prepares students for credentials such as OSHA 10, EPA 608 and NCCER pathway options.
resources.address: 1601 W. Main Street, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Program schedules, seats and start dates vary; use Request More Info or Apply Today before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Hands-on HVACR training in system installation, electrical systems, maintenance and repair, refrigeration technology and preparation for HVACR apprenticeship/career pathways. EVIT lists 360 clock hours, multiple certifications, OSHA 10 Construction Industry, HVAC EPA 608, NCCER pathway and a connection to the HVACR paid apprenticeship program.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adult program admission, schedule, tuition, supplies, certification eligibility and financial aid vary by EVIT program rules. EVIT states the HVACR program counts as a required pre-apprenticeship for paid apprenticeship programs.

**Population Served**
Mesa and East Valley adults seeking HVACR career training, certifications or a pre-apprenticeship route; VA education benefits are listed as a possible support.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the EVIT HVACR page's Request More Info or Apply Today links, or call EVIT at 480-461-4000. Main Campus: 1601 W. Main Street, Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
The opened page listed completion/job-placement figures and zero waitlist, but those can change. Confirm current seats, schedule, fees, supplies, financial aid and whether a client should enter the pre-apprenticeship before applying for the paid apprenticeship.

resources.name: Maricopa County Adult Probation - Mental Health Unit
resources.description: Maricopa County Adult Probation's Mental Health Unit provides therapeutic specialized probation supervision for probationers with an SMI determination and additional court-ordered mental-health conditions, coordinating probation expectations with treatment participation.
resources.address: Southeast Justice Center, 222 E. Javelina Ave., Suite 100, Mesa, AZ 85210; other probation locations countywide
resources.hours: Access is through assigned probation or court channels; public office hours vary by probation location.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Therapeutic specialized probation supervision for people with a Serious Mental Illness determination; coordination with treatment, medication compliance, Mental Health Court participation, and RBHA harm-reduction/risk-reduction supports. Adult Probation also lists reentry, treatment court, and court-ordered substance-use pathways.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Limited to adults under Maricopa County Adult Probation supervision who have an SMI determination through the Regional Behavioral Health Authority and have been ordered to comply with additional mental-health probation conditions.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County probationers with SMI-related probation conditions. Related specialized programs serve probationers reentering from custody, veterans in Veterans Court, supervised youth under 21 transferred to adult court, and people with court-ordered treatment needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Clients on probation should contact their assigned probation officer first. General Judicial Branch information is 602-506-3204. Do not send someone as a walk-in mental-health client unless probation staff directs that route.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not voluntary community counseling and does not replace a clinic. It is useful only when a client already has Maricopa County probation involvement or court-ordered mental-health/reentry needs.

resources.name: Child Crisis Arizona - Early Education Services: Early Head Start and Preschool
resources.description: Early Head Start and preschool services in Mesa and Phoenix. Mesa Early Head Start enrolls prenatal moms and children ages 0-3; preschool serves ages 3-5, with Family Support Specialists helping families connect to resources.
resources.address: Mesa sites and home-based options; obtain the assigned location from enrollment staff
resources.hours: Call enrollment for current classroom/home-based schedules.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Early Head Start, preschool, prenatal/home-based/center-based visits, licensed early education, and family support. Family Support Specialists help families navigate barriers and connect with resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Early Head Start serves pregnant women and children ages 0-3 living at or below 100% of the federal poverty level. The Mesa page lists prenatal moms and children 0-3 in Mesa and children ages 3-5 who meet program eligibility requirements. DES Child Care Subsidy and limited First Things First Quality Scholarships may help with preschool costs.

**Population Served**
Pregnant people, infants, toddlers, preschool children, caregivers, and families in Mesa and Phoenix, with the Mesa program focused on Mesa prenatal moms and young children.

**How to Best Connect**
For Mesa Early Head Start and preschool enrollment, call 480-304-9501 or use the official enrollment link. General Child Crisis Arizona inquiries are 480-834-9424. Ask which language options are available for the requested service.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm current enrollment, waitlists, the assigned classroom or home-based option and any preschool scholarship availability. The public enrollment notice does not guarantee placement. This is early education and family support, not emergency childcare.

resources.name: Valleywise Health - Phoenix specialty and hospital pathway
resources.description: Valleywise Health Medical Center and Valleywise Comprehensive Health Center Phoenix provide hospital and specialty-care pathways for Maricopa County patients, including ophthalmology, dental, ENT, cardiology, GI, surgery, orthopedics, podiatry, renal, women's services, pharmacy, social services, interpreter services, and care management.
resources.address: 2601 E. Roosevelt St., Phoenix, AZ 85008
resources.hours: Valleywise Health Medical Center: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Specialty clinic and department hours vary; appointments generally through 1-833-855-9973 or main 602-344-5011.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Hospital and specialty-care access through Valleywise Health Medical Center and Valleywise Comprehensive Health Center Phoenix. Listed services include emergency and acute care, burn care, cancer treatment, cardiology, ICU, trauma center, endoscopy, maternity, pediatric emergency/acute care, NICU, pharmacy, imaging, surgery, interpreter services, care management, social services, and specialty clinics such as gastroenterology, ENT, ophthalmology, cardiology, general surgery, orthopedics, podiatry, renal care, women's services, and dental.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Appointments and referrals depend on the specific department and payer or financial-assistance pathway. Mesa behavioral-health outpatient psychiatry is separate and does not itself provide the medical specialty services; its page points patients to the Phoenix Comprehensive Health Center for those specialties.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County patients, including Mesa patients already using Valleywise primary care or financial assistance, who need specialty, hospital, dental, ophthalmology, pharmacy, or care-management services not available at the Mesa community health center.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 1-833-855-9973 for appointments or 602-344-5011 for the main medical center and ask for the specific specialty department. If coming from Mesa care, ask the Mesa provider or Valleywise scheduler whether a referral is needed.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a Phoenix specialty and hospital route, not a walk-in routine-care recommendation for Mesa primary care. Confirm the referral process, location, insurance or financial-assistance schedule, and whether the specialty clinic is accepting new patients before sending a client.

resources.name: AMVETS National Service Foundation - Homeless Veterans Reintegration Program, Phoenix
resources.description: AMVETS Homeless Veterans Reintegration Program in Phoenix provides employment-focused reintegration help for veterans experiencing or at risk of homelessness, including job training, employment placement, housing assistance and links to counseling and VA claims help.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
AMVETS HVRP provides workforce reintegration support for homeless or at-risk veterans in Phoenix. Services include job training, employment placement, occupational skills training, apprenticeships, housing assistance, access to mental health and addiction counseling, and AMVETS Service Officer help with VA claims for veterans and family members.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Veterans must verify active-duty service and discharge other than dishonorable, homelessness or qualifying housing risk/partner-service status, and motivation to participate in workforce development, training and active employment. The page says at-risk homelessness within 15-60 days may be eligible.

**Population Served**
Veterans experiencing or at risk of homelessness, including homeless women veterans, homeless veterans with children, veterans transitioning from penal institutions and veterans leaving long-term care mental health facilities.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact Program Director Lewis Arnette at 623-309-6539 or larnette@amvets.org. The official page also has an online message form. Phoenix is listed as one of the HVRP launch locations.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an employment and reintegration program, not an emergency shelter bed. Eligibility documentation and current Phoenix intake logistics should be confirmed before travel.

resources.name: Banner Imaging East Mesa
resources.description: Banner Imaging East Mesa is a diagnostic imaging site in Mesa offering CT/CTA, MRI/MRA, PET/CT, nuclear medicine, fluoroscopy, ultrasound, breast ultrasound and X-ray, with online booking and phone scheduling.
resources.address: 6424 E Broadway Rd, Suite 101, Mesa, AZ 85206
resources.hours: Listed as 7:30 AM-5:00 PM when opened; call to confirm current hours before going.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Diagnostic imaging including CT/CT angiography, fluoroscopy, MRI-breast, MRI/MRA, nuclear medicine, PET/CT, ultrasound, breast ultrasound and X-ray.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Imaging usually requires an order or referral from a medical provider and payer/self-pay arrangements. The location page does not state a low-cost program.

**Population Served**
Mesa and East Valley patients needing diagnostic imaging services.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-610-7400 for an appointment or use the Banner Imaging online booking portal. Location: 6424 E Broadway Rd, Suite 101, Mesa, AZ 85206.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a diagnostic imaging provider, not itself a charitable program. Ask about required orders, insurance, self-pay estimates and whether Banner financial assistance can apply to the specific bill.

resources.name: Encore Senior Housing / PacifiCap Management - Encore on First
resources.description: Encore on First is an age- and income-restricted rental community for independent seniors in downtown Mesa, with one- and two-bedroom apartments and leasing contact information.
resources.address: 25 West First Avenue, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Age- and income-restricted senior rental housing in downtown Mesa. The property offers one- and two-bedroom apartments and community amenities such as access-controlled building entry, on-site management, fitness room, community room, library/computer lab, laundry areas and storage lockers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must meet age and income restrictions and any property leasing criteria. The official page says to see the leasing associate for details; current income limits, rent, waitlist and availability must be confirmed with the property.

**Population Served**
Independent seniors seeking an age- and income-restricted rental community in Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-834-4547 or email info@encoreonfirst.com for leasing information. Ask about age threshold, income limits, current rents, waitlist status, accessibility needs and application requirements.

**Important Information to Know**
This is affordable senior rental housing, not emergency shelter or a voucher program. Availability is not guaranteed, and the page does not publish live vacancy or exact income limits.

resources.name: ATSU-ASDOH Dental Clinic - Mesa Campus
resources.description: ATSU-ASDOH Dental Clinic is a Mesa dental teaching clinic providing general dentistry, pediatric dentistry, orthodontic screening, imaging, treatment planning and emergency dental evaluation during open clinic days at reduced fees.
resources.address: 5855 E. Still Circle, Mesa, AZ 85206
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-6:00 PM for the general clinic. Emergency dental needs are first-come, first-served on days the clinic is open.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
General dental care similar to a private dental office, including screenings, exams, cleanings, restorative care, fillings, root canals, crowns, bridges, implants, pediatric dental care, imaging, orthodontic screening and dental emergency evaluation during regular clinic hours.

**Eligibility Requirements**
ATSU says anyone is welcome for orthodontic services and no income qualification is required to take advantage of clinic services. Patients still need screening or an appointment, and treatment suitability depends on clinical needs and the teaching-clinic model.

**Population Served**
Children and adults in Mesa and the Phoenix area who need lower-cost dental care and can use a supervised student/resident teaching clinic.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-248-8100 to schedule an initial screening or ask about a dental emergency. The clinic is at 5855 E. Still Circle, Mesa, AZ 85206.

**Important Information to Know**
Reduced fees are not necessarily free; request an estimate before treatment. Teaching-clinic visits may take longer or require several appointments. Emergency evaluation is during open clinic days, not 24-hour emergency care. This location is separate from the Center for Advanced Oral Health at 5835 E Still Circle.

resources.name: First Presbyterian Church of Mesa - Mesa Mercy Market and Community Dinner
resources.description: First Presbyterian Church of Mesa's Mesa Mercy Market provides a food pantry and clothing closet on Friday mornings, along with a monthly community dinner.
resources.address: 161 N Mesa Dr, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Pantry/clothing: Fridays 8–9 AM. Community dinner: first Wednesday 5 PM. Church office: Mon–Thu 9 AM–3 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Food pantry, clothing closet, emotional and spiritual support through Mesa Mercy Market. The church also hosts a first-Wednesday community dinner.

**Eligibility Requirements**
No restrictions or fees are reported in the service listing; confirm any current document or visit-frequency requirements with the church.

**Population Served**
Mesa community members needing food or clothing support.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit First Presbyterian Church, 161 N Mesa Dr, Mesa, on Fridays 8:00-9:00 AM for Mesa Mercy Market. Call 480-964-8606 for current pantry questions.

**Important Information to Know**
The pantry/clothing window is one hour. Check holiday changes and availability before travelling for a specific size or item. The dinner has a separate monthly schedule.

resources.name: Xfinity / Comcast - Internet Essentials
resources.description: Xfinity Internet Essentials is a low-cost home internet program for qualifying households in Xfinity service areas, with online/phone application and document submission options.
resources.hours: Application/status by portal or phone; phone hours not established.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Internet Essentials offers service up to 75 Mbps for $14.95 per month; Internet Essentials Plus offers up to 100 Mbps for $29.95 per month. After approval, customers can obtain equipment by delivery or Xfinity store pickup and may purchase an offered computer for $149.99 plus tax. Xfinity describes application decisions in 1–3 business days and connection in 7–10 business days after approval; confirm timing.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must live where Xfinity Internet service is available, participate in an eligible assistance program or qualify by income, have not had Xfinity Internet within the last 90 days, and have no outstanding Comcast debt less than one year old. Listed proofs include Medicaid, housing assistance, SNAP, TANF, SSI, NSLP/Head Start, LIHEAP, WIC, Pell Grant, VA Pension, Tribal assistance or income documents.

**Population Served**
Qualifying households where Xfinity Internet service is available, including some Arizona and Maricopa County addresses after serviceability check.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online or call 1-855-846-8376. Documents can be uploaded through the application portal, emailed to IEApplication@comcast.com, mailed to Internet Essentials, PO Box 397, Bridgeport, NJ 08014-9735, or faxed to 1-888-294-7113. For address-recognition problems, call the same application phone number.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm the exact address, current plan terms and computer offer. Mesa availability may be limited. Applicants must not have had Xfinity Internet within 90 days and must not have Comcast debt less than a year old. This is separate from Lifeline. An ASL application option is linked from the application page.

resources.name: CancerCare - Financial Assistance Program
resources.description: CancerCare provides limited cancer financial assistance and resource referrals through oncology social workers when funds are open for a client's diagnosis and need.
resources.address: 485 Madison Ave, 10th Floor, New York, NY 10022
resources.hours: CancerCare lists Hopeline financial-assistance interview hours as Monday-Friday 10:00 AM-4:00 PM ET during summer hours; call to confirm current hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Limited financial assistance for cancer-related needs when funds are available. CancerCare's current page lists assistance categories such as transportation, home care, child care, transportation/lodging for some diagnoses, and pet assistance for people with cancer who have a cat or dog. If no fund is available, CancerCare says it will refer callers to other resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicant must have a cancer diagnosis confirmed by an oncology health-care provider, be in active treatment or have had/will have cancer-related surgery, live in the U.S. or Puerto Rico, and meet Federal Poverty Limit guidelines. Available assistance depends on open funds.

**Population Served**
People with cancer in the United States and Puerto Rico, including eligible Mesa residents, and in some funds their caregivers, children or pets.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 800-813-HOPE (4673) and speak with a CancerCare social worker for a brief interview. If eligible, CancerCare sends an individualized bar-coded application and requests income and oncology-provider documentation.

**Important Information to Know**
Funds are first-come, first-served and change by diagnosis and funding source. A client should call before gathering documents to confirm that a relevant fund is open.

resources.name: Central Arizona Shelter Services - Norton and Ramsey Social Justice Empowerment Center
resources.description: CASS Norton and Ramsey Social Justice Empowerment Center is a West Valley navigation hub serving people at risk of or experiencing homelessness with case management, coordinated services, street outreach coordination, job services, coordinated entry and partner-agency support.
resources.address: 7031 N 56th Ave, Glendale, AZ 85301
resources.hours: Public hours were not confirmed in current official evidence; call before travel.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Navigation hub support for people at risk of or experiencing homelessness, including case management, coordinated service planning, street-outreach coordination, job services, coordinated entry connection, partner-agency services and flexible support where available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Intended for Glendale/West Valley residents or people connected to that regional service system who are at risk of or experiencing homelessness. Program fit, public intake hours and current service availability must be confirmed.

**Population Served**
People at risk of or experiencing homelessness in Glendale and the West Valley, including families and older adults in the CASS regional system.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 623-207-8902 before visiting the Glendale center to confirm current hours, intake steps and whether the center can help the specific household.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a useful Maricopa County reserve/navigation option but is not Mesa-specific. The strongest public official description is an older CASS article, so current hours and walk-in access should be confirmed.

resources.name: Dress for Success Arizona - The Workforce Initiative
resources.description: Dress for Success Arizona's Workforce Initiative supports teens and young adults ages 16-24 entering the workforce and lists bus passes and gas cards among available resources.
resources.address: 3110 N. Central Ave., Building D (Diamond Building), Suite 200, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.hours: Boutique/Career Center: Monday–Thursday, 9:00 AM–4:30 PM; second/fourth Saturdays by appointment; Friday closed. Partner/mobile programme schedules vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Workforce Initiative provides job preparation, professional clothing, job coaching, hiring assistance and resources that include bus passes, gas cards, uniforms and certifications.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Workforce Initiative serves high-school students and recent graduates ages 16–24 through classroom and partner-based job-readiness support. Ask about the current school/partner referral route, registration and available resources. Its programme page does not state a women-only or income requirement.

**Population Served**
Phoenix-area teens and young adults ages 16-24 preparing for employment.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-489-7397 or email services@dressforsuccessphoenix.org and ask specifically about The Workforce Initiative. Confirm the classroom, partner or programme location before traveling. The organization’s office is at 3110 N. Central Ave., Building D, Suite 200, Phoenix; an office or boutique visit does not itself enroll someone in this youth programme.

**Important Information to Know**
Bus passes, gas cards and related help are tied to the workforce programme, not a stand-alone transit-pass desk. Availability depends on enrollment, partnerships and funding. Donation drop-off hours are not client-service hours.

resources.name: ICE Phoenix Field Office - Enforcement and Removal Operations check-in and detention inquiries
resources.description: ICE Phoenix Field Office / Enforcement and Removal Operations is a federal administrative access point for required ICE check-ins, outreach appointments, detention inquiries and related enforcement or removal operations contacts for Maricopa County and other counties in its area of coverage. It is not a support or legal-aid provider.
resources.phone: 602-766-7029; field office main phone also listed as 602-257-5900
resources.address: 2035 N Central Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.hours: Check-in appointments listed Tuesday-Thursday 8:00 AM-12:00 PM on ICE check-in location results; call or confirm online before travel
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
ICE Phoenix Field Office / Enforcement and Removal Operations is an official federal contact point for ICE check-ins, outreach appointments, detention-related inquiries, case logistics, and other ERO administrative matters.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Use this only when a person has an ICE appointment, check-in requirement, detention inquiry, bond or case-specific administrative need, or an attorney or accredited representative has advised contact. It is not a community support service.

**Population Served**
People with ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations matters in the Phoenix area of responsibility, including Maricopa County, and family members or representatives making detention-related inquiries.

**How to Best Connect**
The ICE check-in location result lists the Phoenix Field Office at 2035 N Central Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85004, phone 602-766-7029, email Phoenix.Outreach@ice.dhs.gov, with appointment times Tuesday-Thursday 8:00 AM-12:00 PM. Other official detention-facility pages list the Phoenix Field Office main phone as 602-257-5900. Confirm the appointment method and required documents before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an enforcement agency, not legal aid, case management, or a rights-protection service. People with immigration-court or removal concerns should seek qualified immigration counsel or a nonprofit legal provider before contacting ICE unless contact is required or urgent. The direct ICE field-office page could not be opened due to a 403 response, but official ICE search snippets and related ICE detention-facility pages support the contact details.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Economic Security - Disability Determination Services Administration
resources.description: Arizona DES Disability Determination Services Administration makes medical disability determinations for Social Security Disability Insurance, Supplemental Security Income and related Arizona disability-linked medical-assistance determinations.
resources.address: 4000 N. Central Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.hours: Public hours were not established; call the Phoenix DDSA phone number for claim questions routed through Social Security processes.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
DDSA adjudicates medical disability determinations for disability claims referred through Social Security offices and related Arizona medical-assistance eligibility processes. It may review medical records and decide whether disability standards are met.

**Eligibility Requirements**
DDSA is not a walk-in benefit program. A person usually reaches DDSA after applying for Social Security disability benefits or a disability-linked AHCCCS category that requires a medical disability decision.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents whose SSDI, SSI or disability-linked medical-assistance applications require a disability determination.

**How to Best Connect**
For Phoenix DDSA, call 800-352-0409. For starting a Social Security disability benefits application, use SSA's application routes; DDSA itself does not issue SSI or SSDI cash payments.

**Important Information to Know**
DDSA determines disability; it does not provide ongoing case management, medical treatment or cash benefits directly. Clients asking how to apply for SSI/SSDI may need Social Security application help in addition to this contact.

resources.name: Bey’s Blessings — documentation assistance
resources.description: Could add grassroots help obtaining identification and birth certificates for unsheltered people once its intake route is confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Could add grassroots help obtaining identification and birth certificates for unsheltered people once its intake route is confirmed.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The organization describes serving unsheltered people and families in need; detailed document-service criteria are not published.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness in the Phoenix area.

**How to Best Connect**
An administrator should confirm a working client-service contact and current document assistance before referral.

**Important Information to Know**
The program description is supported, but appointment arrangements, fee support and a dependable client intake route remain unresolved.
resources.resolutionReason: The program description is supported, but appointment arrangements, fee support and a dependable client intake route remain unresolved.

resources.name: Global Water Resources - Customer Assistance Program
resources.description: Global Water Resources offers payment plans and Customer Assistance Program funds for qualifying residential Global Water utility customers in its service areas, with assistance distributed through listed local community agencies.
resources.address: 21410 N. 19th Ave., Suite 220, Phoenix, AZ 85027
resources.hours: Call Global Water customer service or the listed local agency for current intake; hours were not established in this preparation.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Global Water Resources offers payment plans through Customer Service and a Customer Assistance Program that can help qualifying customers pay Global Water utility bills. Its published assistance categories include income assistance, deployed service member, disabled veteran, furloughed worker, and medical hardship programs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Only residential customers of Global Water Utilities may qualify. The income assistance program is for a customer's primary legal residence and requires the named account customer to meet program rules, including no utility tampering history within the stated period and household income at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level. Other program tracks require specific documentation such as deployment orders, veteran disability evidence, layoff/furlough evidence, disability benefits, hospitalization, or FMLA-related medical hardship.

**Population Served**
Residential Global Water utility customers in Global Water service areas who need bill-payment relief or a payment plan. This can include low-income households, deployed service members, disabled veterans, furloughed workers, and households facing medical hardship.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Global Water Customer Service at 866-940-1102 to ask about payment plans and confirm whether the client's exact address is served by a qualifying Global Water utility. For Customer Assistance Program screening, contact the local community action agency listed by Global Water for the customer's area.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a City of Mesa water program. Global Water's service territory is fragmented, and a Mesa-area client should be referred only after confirming Global Water is the actual water or wastewater provider. Qualifying customers can receive up to a stated $350 per year per utility service, and customers qualifying for more than one Global Water assistance program receive benefits from only one program per year.

resources.name: VoteRiders Helpline - Arizona ID document assistance
resources.description: VoteRiders provides free remote help obtaining voter ID and supporting documents, including birth certificates, name-change records, naturalization certificates, Social Security cards, proof of residence, DMV/SSA appointment setup, cost coverage and rides where available.
resources.hours: Call or text 866-432-8683, use the online form or chatbox.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides free help figuring out what documents are needed for ID, setting up appointments, covering costs, requesting and paying for documents, and helping obtain documents that show identity, birth certificates, name-change records, naturalization certificates, Social Security cards, proof of residence, rides to DMV or Social Security offices, and ID.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Voter-focused program for people who need ID to vote or need supporting records for voter ID. Arizona DES also points Arizona ID seekers to VoteRiders for no-cost help getting records needed for an Arizona ID card.

**Population Served**
People in Arizona and nationwide who need ID or supporting documents for voting, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents; Spanish-language access is available on the VoteRiders site.

**How to Best Connect**
Call or text 866-432-8683, use the online help form, or use the website chatbox. DES directs Arizona ID seekers to the VoteRiders Arizona help route.

**Important Information to Know**
The program is voter-ID focused, but the help can include foundational records often needed for state ID. Confirm at intake if the client's document need is not voting-related.

resources.name: Streets of Joy - Transitional Living, Sober Living, SSI/SSDI and Second Chance Programs
resources.description: Streets of Joy provides Mesa transitional living, sober-living housing, SSI/SSDI and recent-release second-chance programs with work, drug-testing and rent requirements.
resources.address: 451 E 4th Pl, Mesa, AZ 85203
resources.hours: Apply online or call before visiting; public office hours were not posted on the program page.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Transitional Living Program I with a 150 working-day journey, 3/4 sober-living housing for employed participants, SSI/SSDI program, Second Chance program for people recently released from jail or prison, job skills, fellowship, volunteer/work expectations and transition support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
3/4 program participants must already be employed, pass a drug test on entry, provide verifiable employment and pay weekly rent. The Second Chance program requires release from jail or prison within 30 days, proof of recent incarceration, release dates and clean drug tests. SSI/SSDI participants pay an entry fee and must be available for light-duty volunteering.

**Population Served**
People in Mesa seeking recovery-oriented transitional or sober living, including recently released individuals and people with SSI/SSDI. The public page uses male-focused language for Program I; confirm whether women are currently served.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-757-6921, email info@streetsofjoy.com, or use Apply Now on the program page. The location is 451 E 4th Pl, Mesa, AZ 85203.

**Important Information to Know**
Published costs include $175 weekly rent for the 3/4 program and a $650 entry fee for the SSI/SSDI program; confirm current charges. The SSI/SSDI program name refers to a housing track and does not establish help applying for those benefits. Ask about current openings, house rules, certification/licensure, drug testing, gender eligibility and whether the program fits the person’s recovery needs.

resources.name: Community Legal Services - civil legal help for document and benefits barriers
resources.description: Civil legal intake and access to forms, document printing/scanning and remote legal meetings through the CLS kiosk program.
resources.hours: Call 602-258-3434 or use CLS online intake. Confirm current MesaCAN satellite hours before visiting 635 E. Broadway Road, Mesa, AZ 85204.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides civil legal screening and kiosks where people can find forms, print and scan documents, and meet remotely with a lawyer or court.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Legal representation requires income, residency and case screening. Kiosk access does not guarantee a lawyer will take the case.

**Population Served**
People facing civil legal problems in the CLS service area, including Mesa residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-258-3434 for legal intake. For kiosk locations and access, email kiosk@clsaz.org or call 480-571-2811; confirm availability before traveling.

**Important Information to Know**
CLS is not a government ID issuer or an ID-fee fund. Ask whether the particular legal problem is within its current practice areas; the kiosk page does not promise notarization.

resources.name: Promise Arizona - Immigration Services and Citizenshipworks PAZ Portal
resources.description: Promise Arizona provides community-based immigration assistance focused on DACA and citizenship, including a Citizenshipworks pathway for starting naturalization applications before follow-up with PAZ.
resources.address: 410 E. Southern Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85040
resources.hours: Call before visiting; appointment capacity and immigration-service schedule are not fully posted.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free guidance for DACA and citizenship questions, community immigrant-rights support, Know Your Rights information, and a Citizenshipworks PAZ portal for beginning a citizenship application online before follow-up.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Citizenship help is for lawful permanent residents preparing for naturalization. DACA help depends on current federal program rules and individual eligibility. PAZ should confirm whether a client's issue is within its current scope.

**Population Served**
Arizona immigrant families, including Spanish-speaking clients and Maricopa County residents who need citizenship or DACA guidance.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-288-3663 or start through the PAZ Citizenshipworks portal linked from the immigration page. Confirm appointment availability before traveling to the Phoenix office.

**Important Information to Know**
The public page is brief and does not clearly show the full legal-services scope or current appointment capacity. Use it as a community-embedded citizenship and DACA assistance route, not as confirmed broad immigration representation.

resources.name: VA Community Care Network — Arizona access
resources.description: Explains access to VA-covered community providers when care outside a VA facility is appropriate.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Explains access to VA-covered community providers when care outside a VA facility is appropriate.

**Eligibility Requirements**
VA determines eligibility and authorisation. Arrange routine community care through the VA care team; urgent and emergency care have separate benefit rules.

**Population Served**
Eligible VA patients in Arizona, including Mesa. TriWest administers the regional community-provider network.

**How to Best Connect**
Start with the VA care team or Phoenix VA at 602-277-5551 and ask about community-care access. Use the official VA network page to understand the referral pathway.

**Important Information to Know**
A community provider’s participation does not by itself authorise a visit or guarantee VA payment. Confirm the referral and covered services before booking routine care.

resources.name: Mesa Community College · English Language Program
resources.description: Mesa Community College English Language Program offers credit ESL classes across four levels, free CELSA placement testing, conversation practice, ESL for Jobs, and an English Language Skills certificate eligible for financial aid.
resources.address: 1833 W. Southern Ave., Mesa, AZ 85202; Red Mountain Campus, 7110 E. McKellips Rd., Mesa, AZ 85207; MCC Online
resources.hours: Credit course and Conversation Circle schedules vary by term; confirm current times, room and campus.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
College ESL classes for students whose primary language is not English, four language levels, CELSA placement guidance, ESL for Jobs, pronunciation, grammar, reading/writing, listening/speaking, free conversation circles, and an English Language Skills certificate.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Students must follow MCC admission, placement, registration, and tuition or financial-aid rules. New ESL students can take the free CELSA test or use another approved test for level placement.

**Population Served**
Mesa Community College students and prospective students who want college-level English language instruction for academic, work, civic, or personal goals.

**How to Best Connect**
Call MCC at 480-461-7000, review the English Language Program page, and ask the ELP coordinator or International Education about placement, registration, tuition, and the certificate. Conversation Circles are listed as open to everyone.

**Important Information to Know**
College-credit courses have admission, placement, tuition and applicable financial-aid requirements. The English-language certificate is a transcript credential and financial-aid eligibility is separate from receiving an award. Conversation Circles are listed as open to everyone; confirm the current session. These offerings are distinct from free Title II ESL and MCC’s paused noncredit ELL courses.

resources.name: Avondale Police — Victim Services
resources.description: Voluntary victim advocacy, safety planning, case updates, court accompaniment, protective-order help, victim-compensation application support and Address Confidentiality Program assistance.
resources.hours: Monday–Thursday,7:00AM–5:00PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Voluntary victim advocacy, safety planning, case updates, court accompaniment, protective-order help, victim-compensation application support and Address Confidentiality Program assistance.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Contact the program about an Avondale-connected crime or case. Services cover domestic and teen dating violence, assault, elder abuse, threats and other person-to-person crimes.

**Population Served**

Individuals and families affected by crime in the Avondale service area.

**How to Best Connect**

Call or email during posted hours and ask which advocate can help with the incident or case. Confirm appointment location before travel.

**Important Information to Know**

This is police-connected victim support, not a confidential shelter or private lawyer. Shelter help is assistance finding options, not a guaranteed bed. Use911 for immediate danger.

resources.name: Maricopa Community Colleges · Nina Mason Pulliam Legacy Scholars Program
resources.description: The Nina Mason Pulliam Legacy Scholars Program provides qualifying disadvantaged students at Maricopa Community Colleges with full tuition, fees, books and supplies, living stipend, and mentor support.
resources.address: Maricopa Community Colleges districtwide; program manager at 2411 W. 14th St., Tempe, AZ 85281
resources.hours: Scholarship application windows are cyclical; contact the program manager or financial aid office for current deadlines.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Scholarship support covering full tuition, fees, books and supplies, plus a living stipend. The program also provides academic, peer, and alumni mentors to help scholars complete college.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Students must meet at least one listed criterion: adult with one or more dependents in the household; adult with a physical disability; or adult age 18-25 who has experienced foster care or disconnection from parents or primary caregiver and is responsible for their own financial support. Additional Maricopa scholarship and college enrollment requirements apply.

**Population Served**
Qualifying disadvantaged students at all Maricopa Community Colleges, including Mesa Community College students who fit one of the program's priority populations.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Apply for the Scholarship link on the Maricopa Nina Scholars page, call Maricopa financial aid at 480-731-8900, or contact the Nina Scholars Program Manager at 480-731-8460.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a selective scholarship with limited eligibility and application cycles. Confirm current deadlines, required documents, and whether the student meets one of the three eligibility populations before presenting it as a fit.

resources.name: Jose's Closet / AZAFAP - Donation-Based Boutique for Foster, Kinship, and Adoptive Families
resources.description: Jose's Closet, operated by AZAFAP, is a Mesa donation-based boutique providing free clothing, baby gear, diapers, food access, toys, and essentials to foster, kinship, adoptive, and extended-foster-care families through membership.
resources.address: 6515 E Main St, Ste 120, Mesa, AZ 85205
resources.hours: Tuesday-Saturday 11:00 AM-3:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Jose's Closet provides free access to clothing, toys, baby gear, diapers, food, and other essentials. Membership includes monthly shopping visits for a week of head-to-toe clothing and seasonal essentials for each child, baby gear and toys, monthly diaper bank access, and weekly food bank access.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Jose's Closet serves foster, kinship, adoptive families, and youth in extended foster care. Membership includes all children in the household up to age 21. Bring parent/caregiver photo ID, DCS placement paperwork or guardianship documentation, adoption paperwork if applicable, and birth certificates for biological children in the home.

**Population Served**
Foster, kinship, adoptive, and extended-foster-care families in Arizona who can use the Mesa boutique.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit Tuesday-Saturday 11:00 AM-3:00 PM at 6515 E Main St, Ste 120, Mesa, or call 480-309-1743. Email info@josescloset.org with membership questions.

**Important Information to Know**
Complete the membership application at the first visit and update it annually. Stock is donation-dependent; call about urgent placement needs, clothing sizes or large baby items before travelling. Listed donation items do not guarantee current availability.

resources.name: Dental Lifeline Network - Donated Dental Services Arizona
