resources.description: Dental Lifeline Network's Donated Dental Services in Arizona coordinates volunteer comprehensive dental treatment for people who cannot afford care and are over 65, permanently disabled or need medically necessary dental care, but Arizona counties are currently closed to most new applications due to lengthy waitlists.
resources.hours: Call or email the Arizona DDS coordinator; public office hours are not listed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Volunteer-provided comprehensive dental treatment for eligible patients through Donated Dental Services. Volunteers do not provide emergency or cosmetic treatment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must have no means to afford dental care and meet one criterion: over age 65, permanently disabled or needing medically necessary dental care. People with physician documentation that dental care blocks essential medical treatment may apply even if their county is closed. Veterans who meet the qualifications may also apply even if the county is closed.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents who cannot afford dental care and are seniors, permanently disabled, medically fragile or qualifying veterans.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Arizona DDS coordinator at 480-850-1474, fax 833-392-1849 or email mmclaren@DentalLifeline.org. Use the Arizona program page to check qualification and application options.

**Important Information to Know**
As of the official page opened on 2026-09-26, all Arizona counties were closed to new applications due to lengthy waitlists. This is still a useful reserve lead for qualifying veterans or medically necessary care exceptions, but it should not be presented as open routine dental intake.

resources.name: Phoenix Children's - Support for Pregnancy, Infant, and Child Loss
resources.description: Phoenix Children's provides grief and bereavement support contacts for families who have lost a child and perinatal palliative-care support for expectant families facing life-threatening or life-limiting fetal or newborn conditions.
resources.address: Phoenix Children's; bereavement and fetal/neonatal care contacts are phone/email based
resources.hours: Call or email for current support options; group/event schedules vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Phoenix Children's bereavement support connects families with grief and bereavement resources, support groups, planning documents, events, and contacts. Its perinatal palliative-care program supports expectant parents and families facing life-threatening or life-limiting fetal or newborn conditions through pregnancy, birth, and beyond.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Bereavement support is for families grieving a child. Perinatal palliative care is for expectant families managing serious fetal or newborn diagnoses. Specific services, groups, and referrals should be confirmed with Phoenix Children's.

**Population Served**
Families experiencing pregnancy, infant, newborn, or child loss, or families facing serious fetal/neonatal diagnoses in the Phoenix Children's service area, including Mesa and Maricopa County families.

**How to Best Connect**
For grief and bereavement support, contact Amanda Sahli at 602-933-3064 or asahli@phoenixchildrens.com. For perinatal palliative-care questions, call 602-933-4411 or email fetalcarecenter@phoenixchildrens.com.

**Important Information to Know**
An older ADHS WIC referral PDF also lists Phoenix Children's Support for Pregnancy and Infant Loss at 602-933-3064. Families should confirm current format, eligibility, and whether support is internal to Phoenix Children's patients or open to community members.

resources.name: Beloved South PHX Justice Center - Low-Cost Immigration Legal Consultation
resources.description: Beloved South PHX Justice Center, an Administer Justice location, offers $30 limited-scope attorney consultations for people of limited means, including immigration legal questions, with a next-steps plan, referrals and Spanish appointments available.
resources.address: 1902 W Roeser Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85041
resources.hours: First Saturdays 9:00 AM-12:00 PM; walk-ins welcome, appointments available.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Beloved South PHX Justice Center offers a 45-minute limited-scope attorney consultation, answers to legal questions, a next-steps plan, referrals and client-advocate support. Immigration is one of the listed legal issue areas, along with housing, debt, family law, criminal records, employment and public benefits.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The center serves people of limited means by self-certification; it does not require financial documents for eligibility. Minimum age is generally 18 unless the legal issue is emancipation. One legal issue is handled per appointment.

**Population Served**
Phoenix-area residents and neighbors of limited means, regardless of immigration status, who need brief legal advice or next-step planning. Spanish appointments are available.

**How to Best Connect**
Book an appointment through the location page or call toll-free 855-818-4554. The center is at 1902 W Roeser Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85041. Published hours are first Saturdays, 9:00 AM-12:00 PM. Walk-ins are welcome, but scheduling is recommended.

**Important Information to Know**
This is limited legal advice, not full immigration representation. The attorney will not go to court or take over the case. Cost is a one-time $30 copay per case, with possible free follow-up on the same next-steps plan. Confirm immigration-attorney availability and interpreter needs before traveling.

resources.name: Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of East Valley - Financial Assistance
resources.description: Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of East Valley in Mesa provides financial assistance resources for uninsured or underinsured patients who qualify for free or discounted emergency and other medically necessary rehabilitation hospital care.
resources.address: 5652 E. Baseline Road, Mesa, AZ 85206
resources.hours: Visiting hours listed as 8:00 AM-8:00 PM daily. Call for billing and financial assistance process details.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free or discounted emergency and other medically necessary care for qualifying uninsured or underinsured patients under the hospital's financial assistance policy.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on the Encompass Health financial assistance policy, medical necessity, insurance/underinsurance status and required application documents.

**Population Served**
Patients needing medically necessary inpatient rehabilitation hospital care in Mesa/East Valley who are uninsured or underinsured and may qualify for financial assistance.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the main hospital at 480-567-0350 or referral phone 866-312-7920 and ask for financial assistance or billing resources. Address: 5652 E. Baseline Road, Mesa, AZ 85206.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a specialty inpatient rehabilitation hospital and usually requires medical referral or medical necessity. It is not routine primary care, urgent care or outpatient physical therapy intake.

resources.name: Mesa Community College · Career and Technical Education
resources.description: Mesa Community College career and technical education pathway offering more than 200 degrees and certificates, including healthcare, advanced manufacturing, construction, beauty and wellness, entrepreneurship, information technology, and other career programs on campus, online, and in flexible formats.
resources.address: 1833 W. Southern Ave., Mesa, AZ 85202; Red Mountain Campus: 7110 E. McKellips Rd., Mesa, AZ 85207; MCC Online
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
MCC Career and Technical Education offers career training in fields such as healthcare, advanced manufacturing, construction, beauty and wellness, entrepreneurship, information technology, accounting, biomedical equipment technology, electronics, fire science, networking and security, sustainable horticulture, and other programs. MCC states students can earn degrees or certificates in two years or less, with classes offered on campus and online.

**Eligibility Requirements**
MCC states it is free to enroll and everyone is accepted, but each degree, certificate, licensure-track, clinical, or cohort program may have its own prerequisites, placement, application deadline, background check, costs, and financial-aid rules.

**Population Served**
Mesa and East Valley students seeking certificates, degrees, workforce credentials, career changes, transfer preparation, or skills for in-demand fields.

**How to Best Connect**
Start from the MCC CTE page and use Get Started, Schedule a Tour, Class Schedule, Financial Aid, or Request More Information links. MCC Southern and Dobson Campus is at 1833 W. Southern Ave., Mesa, phone 480-461-7000; Red Mountain Campus is at 7110 E. McKellips Rd., Mesa, phone 480-654-7200.

**Important Information to Know**
MCC lists tuition as low as $97 per credit hour, with financial aid and scholarships potentially reducing cost. Program accreditation, licensing outcomes, modality, start dates, supplies, and financial-aid eligibility vary by program and should be checked for the specific certificate or degree.

resources.name: Just 1 Life Services - The Get Right Program
resources.description: Just 1 Life Services' Get Right Program is an anti-recidivism and reentry support model for people with incarceration history, justice involvement, substance use, and community reintegration needs, combining counseling, case management, peer support, recovery groups, employment assistance, skills development, Lifeline phone help, emergency food, work clothing, and transportation to court, probation, interviews, and treatment-related appointments.
resources.address: 1616 E Main St, Suite 223, Mesa, AZ 85203; 6344 E Brown Rd, Suite 101, Mesa, AZ 85205
resources.hours: By appointment only at both Mesa locations; services may be by phone, Zoom, or in person.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Individual counseling for substance-use and behavioral-health concerns, case management, government-program navigation, recovery groups, behavioral-modification groups, peer support, mentoring, life and pre-employment skills, employment assistance, Lifeline phone support, emergency food, work clothing, and transportation to probation, court, interviews, and treatment appointments.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Get Right Program is designed for people coming out of incarceration or living with substance use and justice involvement. Program fit, payer eligibility, documentation, and appointment availability should be confirmed before referral.

**Population Served**
Justice-involved and reentry clients in the East Valley/Mesa area, including people with substance-use recovery needs, probation or court obligations, employment barriers, and reintegration needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-477-9199 or email info@just1.us. Ask which Mesa location, virtual option, program level, documents, payer, and appointment time apply.

**Important Information to Know**
Both Mesa locations are appointment-only. This is outpatient reentry/recovery support, not detox, residential treatment, MAT or emergency care. Transport, emergency food, work clothing and phone help are programme-linked and subject to availability; Lifeline has its own qualification rules.

resources.name: The Salvation Army Metro Phoenix - Phoenix Emergency Family Shelter
resources.description: The Salvation Army Phoenix Emergency Family Shelter provides up to 120 days of safe shelter for families, with meals, basic needs, case management, job training, legal assistance and permanent-housing help.
resources.address: 2707 E Van Buren St, Bldg 2, Phoenix, AZ 85008
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency family shelter for up to 120 days with meals, basic material needs, case management, job training, legal assistance, financial literacy, budgeting support, and help locating permanent housing.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For families facing housing insecurity. Family Housing Hub may be the required or best coordinated-entry route for shelter placement.

**Population Served**
Lower-income working families and families experiencing housing insecurity or homelessness in the Phoenix metro area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the shelter line at 602-267-4122. Families in need of emergency shelter can also contact Family Housing Hub at 602-595-8700 or 2-1-1.

**Important Information to Know**
Calling does not guarantee an available room. Mesa families may need coordinated-entry screening through Family Housing Hub.

resources.name: Catholic Charities Community Services Arizona - DIGNITY Diversion Program
resources.description: Catholic Charities' DIGNITY Diversion Program is a City of Phoenix Prosecutor partnership offering education, rehabilitation support, job placement assistance and a charge-dismissal pathway for people arrested for prostitution and identified as sex-trafficking survivors.
resources.address: 5151 N. 19th Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85015
resources.hours: Call Catholic Charities Diversion Program for current program access; public hours are not posted.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A diversion pathway with 36 hours of self-exploration and education, rehabilitation services including support, education and treatment to escape prostitution, job placement assistance and dismissal of charges after program completion.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Access is tied to a City of Phoenix Prosecutor partnership for people arrested for prostitution-related offenses and offered diversion. It is not a general walk-in sex-trafficking shelter or legal clinic.

**Population Served**
Sex-trafficking survivors in the Phoenix prosecution/diversion pathway. It may help a Mesa-area client only if their case or referral route fits the Phoenix diversion program.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-258-2785 and ask about the Catholic Charities Diversion or DIGNITY Diversion Program. If the person is in immediate danger or being trafficked now, use emergency or trafficking-hotline resources first.

**Important Information to Know**
This resource is highly limited by case posture and referral route. Do not promise eligibility outside the Phoenix prosecution pathway, and do not use it as a substitute for crisis shelter, trafficking placement or general legal aid.

resources.name: VA National Call Center for Homeless Veterans
resources.description: Provides free, confidential telephone connection to nearby VA homelessness services at any hour.
resources.hours: 24 hours daily
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides free, confidential telephone connection to nearby VA homelessness services at any hour.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Veterans who are homeless or at imminent risk of homelessness can call for help. Eligibility for housing or clinical programmes is assessed separately.

**Population Served**
Veterans nationwide, including people in Mesa who need a remote first contact.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 877-424-3838, available 24 hours daily. Ask for help connecting with the appropriate local VA homeless-services team.

**Important Information to Know**
The call starts a connection to assistance; it does not reserve a shelter bed or guarantee a housing payment.

resources.name: Glory Days - Nonprofit Social Adult Day Program
resources.description: Glory Days is a Mesa nonprofit social and recreational adult day program for seniors experiencing memory loss and other age-related concerns, giving participants structured activities and caregivers a regular break.
resources.address: Inside East Mesa Christian Church, 706 S. Greenfield Rd., Mesa, AZ 85206
resources.hours: Monday, Tuesday and Thursday 12:30 PM-4:30 PM; Friday-Sunday closed. Wednesday hours are not listed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Glory Days provides a community-based adult day program with social and recreational activities, cognitive stimulation, life-enrichment classes, music, art, dance, chair yoga, gardening, history, wellness and service projects. The program also gives family caregivers respite time.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is for seniors experiencing memory loss and other age-related concerns. The site does not clearly publish clinical staffing, transportation, pricing, subsidy options or which levels of cognitive or physical need can be safely accommodated.

**Population Served**
Seniors with memory loss or age-related concerns and their family caregivers in Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-999-0424 or email info@glory-days.org before attending. The program is located inside East Mesa Christian Church at 706 S. Greenfield Rd., Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a social adult day program, not a medical day-health program or guaranteed dementia supervision for every level of need. Confirm cost, enrollment, safety fit, transportation and current schedule before referral.

resources.name: City of Mesa Parks, Recreation and Community Facilities - Adaptive Recreation
resources.description: City of Mesa Adaptive Recreation offers adaptive sports, recreation, social programs, special interest classes, school break camps, sensory supports and inclusion links for youth and adults with developmental disabilities.
resources.address: Mesa Parks, Recreation and Community Facilities, Mesa, AZ
resources.hours: Program schedules and registration windows vary; call or use the registration links.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Adaptive sports, recreation and social programs, outdoor recreation, social clubs, special interest classes, school break camps, sensory bins, communication tools, noise-cancelling headphones, low-sensory areas or quiet rooms at some venues, inclusion services and scholarship/discount links.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Programs are offered to youth and adults with developmental disabilities. Specific activities may have age, registration, fee, resident/nonresident and behavior-code requirements.

**Population Served**
Mesa-area youth and adults with developmental disabilities and families seeking adaptive or inclusive recreation access.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-644-2863 or email adaptive@mesaaz.gov. Use the City registration links to review current programs, fees, inclusion services and scholarships.

**Important Information to Know**
Schedules, fees and registration windows change by activity. Ask about reasonable modifications, sensory needs and scholarship options before registering.

resources.name: Arizona Democracy Resource Center - Pathways to Freedom Welcome Home Supplies
resources.description: Arizona Democracy Resource Center's Pathways to Freedom program offers requestable Welcome Home supplies for people returning from incarceration, including hygiene essentials, socks, T-shirts, resource referrals and legal-clinic information.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Welcome Home starter kits with hygiene essentials, socks, T-shirts, a local resource guide for housing/employment/health care, and information about accessing ADRC's Free Legal Clinic.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people returning home from incarceration. The official page allows someone to request a Welcome Home Packet for themself or someone they know, but does not publish inventory guarantees, delivery timing or geographic limits.

**Population Served**
People returning from incarceration in Arizona, including Maricopa County residents, who need basic supplies and reentry information.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Request a Packet button on the Pathways to Freedom page. If helping a client, submit the request with accurate contact information and ask about timing, pickup or delivery.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general clothing closet. The public page does not list a phone or address for packet pickup and does not guarantee specific sizes or items.

resources.name: East Valley Al-Anon
resources.description: East Valley Al-Anon information center and meeting access for families and loved ones affected by another person's drinking or substance use.
resources.address: 1855 E Southern Ave, Suite 211, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
East Valley Al-Anon connects families and loved ones to Al-Anon/Alateen peer-support meetings and local information. Meeting lists include in-person and Zoom options, and Arizona Al-Anon lists the East Valley Information Center in Mesa.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Al-Anon is for people affected by another person’s drinking. Alateen provides related peer support for young people. Meeting formats and participation rules vary; use the current meeting list and ask about Spanish-language options.

**Population Served**
Family members, friends and loved ones in Mesa and the East Valley seeking mutual support around another person’s drinking.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the 24-hour phone line at 480-969-6144 or use al-anoneastvalley.org for current meeting information. The East Valley Information Center address is 1855 E Southern Ave, Suite 211, Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
Al-Anon is peer mutual support, not clinical treatment, detox, crisis response, or professional counseling. Meeting schedules can change, so confirm before travel.

resources.name: Mission of Mercy Arizona - Mesa Free Mobile Medical Clinic, Vision Care at Select Clinics
resources.description: Mission of Mercy Arizona operates a scheduled free Mesa clinic at Christ the King Community Center for primary medical care, diagnostic testing, prescription medication, health education and selected vision or specialty care.
resources.address: Christ the King Community Center, 1616 E. Broadway Rd., Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: Mesa clinic is Thursdays, generally 8:00 AM-2:00 PM on the calendar reviewed; Mesa/Phoenix appointment line is Mondays and Thursdays 1:00 PM-6:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free primary medical care, diagnostic testing, prescription medication, health education and selected vision and specialty care. Mission of Mercy Arizona states it does not offer dental services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The clinic serves people needing free medical care, especially uninsured and underserved patients. Appointments are strongly recommended; walk-ins are seen only as availability allows.

**Population Served**
Mesa and Phoenix-area patients who need no-cost basic medical care and can attend scheduled clinic days.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the bilingual Mesa/Phoenix appointment line at 602-486-7798 on Mondays or Thursdays between 1:00 PM and 6:00 PM. The Mesa clinic is Thursdays at Christ the King Community Center, 1616 E. Broadway Rd.

**Important Information to Know**
Clinic dates can change and specialty or vision services are only at selected clinics. Confirm the next Mesa clinic date and whether vision care is available before sending a patient.

resources.name: City of Tempe — Utility payment assistance inquiries
resources.description: Provides a city billing contact for Tempe utility payment arrangements.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides a city billing contact for Tempe utility payment arrangements.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Have a City of Tempe utility account. The city determines available arrangements based on the account and its current rules.

**Population Served**
Tempe utility customers who need help managing a bill.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Utility Services with the account information and explain the payment problem. The city’s low-income residential resources page also points to local assistance and water-saving programmes.

**Important Information to Know**
A payment arrangement is not a grant or debt cancellation. Home plumbing repairs and TCAA assistance have separate applications; confirm the correct route before visiting.

resources.name: DES — legal representation referrals for unemployment appeals
resources.description: DES identifies organizations that may help represent claimants in first-level appeals of a Deputy determination or overpayment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
DES identifies organizations that may help represent claimants in first-level appeals of a Deputy determination or overpayment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The appeal stage, location, case fit and the receiving provider’s rules determine eligibility.

**Population Served**
Arizona unemployment claimants, including Maricopa County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the DES list. For Maricopa County, it names ASU Civil Litigation Clinic and Community Legal Services; CLS intake is 602-258-3434.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a referral list, not a DES-provided attorney or a guarantee of acceptance. Contact a provider promptly and continue observing the appeal deadline.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Economic Security · Vocational Rehabilitation (VR)
resources.description: Arizona DES Vocational Rehabilitation helps eligible people with disabilities prepare for, find, keep, or return to work; individualized VR plans may include education or job training supports when needed for an employment goal.
resources.hours: Call or contact a VR office for appointment options; statewide toll-free information and referral help is available at 1-800-563-1221.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Vocational Rehabilitation helps eligible people with physical or mental disabilities prepare for, find, keep, or return to work. Services are individualized and can include assessment, employment planning, education or job training supports, job placement help, assistive technology, transportation help, and workplace supports when needed for a job goal.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A person may qualify if they have a physical or mental disability, the disability makes it hard to get or keep a job, they need VR services for work, and VR services can help them reach an employment goal. Services are not automatic and depend on eligibility and an approved plan.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents whose disabilities create employment barriers, including Mesa residents, students and transition-age youth. DES lists VR specialty support for blind/visually impaired and Deaf/Hard-of-hearing clients. Services remain tied to the individual employment plan.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact a local VR office by phone or in person, or send the DES referral form by email as directed on the official VR page. English, Spanish and large-print forms are available. For referral guidance, call RSA at 1-800-563-1221; ask about the appropriate office and any sensory or communication accommodation.

**Important Information to Know**
A referral does not guarantee eligibility, funding or a particular service. Education, training, assistive technology and transport must support the approved employment goal; transportation must be authorized before use, and comparable-benefit or financial-participation rules may apply. This is not a general tuition grant or on-demand ride service. Decisions can be challenged through informal review, mediation or fair hearing.

resources.name: Ascend Staffing - Mesa Branch
resources.description: Ascend Staffing’s Mesa Branch is a local staffing office with Quick Apply, job search, phone, text, email, and public office hours for job seekers seeking immediate temporary, temp-to-hire, or staffing placements.
resources.address: 1110 W Southern Avenue, Suite 11, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; Saturday 9:00 AM-3:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Ascend Staffing’s Mesa Branch helps job seekers connect with available staffing assignments. The branch page provides Search Jobs, Quick Apply, candidate portal access, phone/text/email contact, and a local office for people seeking work through the staffing company.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Specific job requirements depend on the open position and employer. Applicants should be prepared for standard staffing requirements such as identity/work authorization, background or drug screening if required by a placement, and schedule/transportation fit.

**Population Served**
Mesa-area job seekers looking for staffing assignments, including people seeking immediate work or temp-to-hire opportunities.

**How to Best Connect**
Use Quick Apply or Search Jobs on the Ascend page, call 480-962-3946, text 480-697-5979, email mesa@ascendstaffing.com, or visit 1110 W Southern Avenue, Suite 11, Mesa during listed hours.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a private staffing agency, not a public benefits program. Current openings and same-day availability change frequently and should be confirmed with the branch.

resources.name: Sun Sounds of Arizona - No-Cost Audio Access to Print Information
resources.description: Sun Sounds of Arizona provides no-cost audio access to newspapers, magazines, books, grocery ads and current information for people who cannot read standard print because of disability.
resources.address: 2323 W. 14th St., Tempe, AZ 85281
resources.hours: Application can be completed online or by printable form; call for help with the application or receiving methods.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Sun Sounds offers audio access to print information through SCA radio, telephone access, HD radio, online streaming, podcasts, digital television and some cable systems. Content includes newspapers, magazines, books, grocery advertisements and more.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Service is free for people who cannot read standard printed materials due to a disability. Applicants must provide the name, title and phone number of a verifying authority such as a doctor, nurse, optometrist, ophthalmologist or professional staff of a medical facility or public/private agency.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents, including Mesa residents, who cannot read or hold standard print because of disability, blindness, low vision or another qualifying print disability.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online, use the printable application, or call 480-774-8300 for help. Be ready to provide the verifying professional's contact information and ask which receiving method is currently available.

**Important Information to Know**
The service is no-cost for eligible applicants, but eligibility may be verified. Availability of receiver equipment, HD radio, phone, online, television or cable options should be confirmed for the person's home and technology access.

resources.name: Phoenix VA Health Care System Intimate Partner Violence Assistance Program
resources.description: Phoenix VA Health Care System offers intimate partner violence support for eligible veterans, including care coordination, links to advocacy and legal services, shelter connections, coordination with VA treatment providers, and services for homeless veterans.
resources.address: 650 E Indian School Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.hours: VA facility service hours apply; the national IPVAP coordinator directory lists the Phoenix coordinator contact. Referral may be required through the VA primary-care provider.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Intimate partner violence support through VA Phoenix Health Care, including IPV care coordinators, links to community support groups, advocacy and legal services, referrals and coordination with VA treatment providers, connection to domestic violence shelters, services for homeless veterans, and interventions for veterans who use violence in intimate relationships.

**Eligibility Requirements**
VA health-care eligibility and enrollment generally apply. The Phoenix VA facility page says a referral is required and directs patients to a primary-care provider when a referral is needed.

**Population Served**
Eligible veterans in the Phoenix VA Health Care System service area, including veterans in Mesa and Maricopa County. Support for partners, family members, or caregivers who are not VA-eligible should be confirmed with VA.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Phoenix VA Health Care at 602-277-5551 and ask for the Intimate Partner Violence Assistance Program coordinator at extension 2680. If already connected with VA care, ask the primary-care provider or social worker for referral. For immediate danger call 911; for the Veterans Crisis Line call 988 then press 1.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a VA health-system pathway, not a community shelter hotline. Confirm VA eligibility, referral requirements, confidentiality, and whether services can directly assist a non-veteran partner or only coordinate community referrals.

resources.name: Arizona Deafblind Project - Registry, Family Support, Technical Assistance and Loan Library
resources.description: Arizona Deafblind Project is an ASDB-administered statewide project that provides technical assistance, training, family support, Deafblind Registry support and loan-library materials for children and youth with combined vision and hearing loss.
resources.hours: Use the website inquiry/referral route or contact staff; response times were not stated on the official page.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The project helps determine whether a child has combined vision and hearing loss, provides classroom/program and home consultation, demonstrates strategies, attends IEP/IFSP and transition meetings, offers training, family engagement and parent events, and lends materials from its loan library.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are offered statewide to children and youth birth through 21 on the Deafblind Registry. The FAQ says any child or youth birth through 22 who is at risk for or has combined vision and hearing loss is eligible for the registry, and referral can be made even while evaluation is ongoing.

**Population Served**
Arizona children and youth with combined vision and hearing loss or risk of combined loss, plus their families, educators and service providers.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 520-770-3268 or submit the website inquiry/referral form. For Phoenix/Maricopa County, the listed Deafblind Specialist is Pat Jung at 602-771-5237 or patrice.jung@asdb.az.gov.

**Important Information to Know**
Project services are technical assistance and family/school support, not medical diagnosis or a direct cash benefit. Project staff follow up with the referring source and the child's family to confirm eligibility.

resources.name: SAGE Counseling, Inc. - City of Mesa Diversion Treatment Program
resources.description: SAGE Counseling's City of Mesa program offers diversion treatment, counseling, substance-abuse treatment, intensive outpatient tracks, case management, peer support, AHCCCS screening help, and Spanish/language assistance.
resources.address: 1830 S Alma School Rd, Suite 104, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:30 AM-5:30 PM; weekends by appointment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
City of Mesa diversion treatment, comprehensive assessment, individualized treatment planning, counseling groups, individual counseling, case management, peer support, domestic violence counseling, DUI treatment and education, substance-abuse treatment, early intervention, relapse prevention, and standard/intensive outpatient programs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Clients are scheduled for assessment and treatment planning at first contact. SAGE is contracted with AHCCCS health plans and accepts the American Indian Health Program; staff can assist with AHCCCS application screening when income and household size appear eligible. Diversion or court documentation may be required for some tracks.

**Population Served**
Mesa diversion clients and adults needing counseling or substance-abuse treatment, including AHCCCS, AIHP, and self-pay clients.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-649-3352, use Schedule an Appointment, or have a referring agency submit a referral. The Mesa office is at 1830 S Alma School Rd, Suite 104.

**Important Information to Know**
Fees apply to self-pay services; ask about the requested track, current charges, AHCCCS/AIHP coverage and required court paperwork. Spanish-speaking staff and language assistance are listed. Confirm fit for non-court mental-health needs and the purpose of any domestic-violence counselling track; this is not a survivor shelter or crisis hotline.

resources.name: AllThrive 365 — Hospital-to-home transitional support
resources.description: Provides post-hospital advocacy, home visits, appointment and prescription help, and access to available medical equipment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides post-hospital advocacy, home visits, appointment and prescription help, and access to available medical equipment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Designed for underinsured or uninsured patients treated at a participating Dignity Health hospital within the past 90 days; AZ General Hospital Mesa is included.

**Population Served**
Eligible recently discharged patients needing help following their care plan at home.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-406-2374 or use the program’s inquiry form to ask about enrollment and equipment availability.

**Important Information to Know**
This support does not replace a physician’s medical care. Hospital eligibility and available equipment must be confirmed.

resources.name: City of Mesa Municipal Court - Veterans Treatment Court
resources.description: Mesa Municipal Court Veterans Treatment Court is a problem-solving court for Veterans or service members with Mesa court involvement, coordinating treatment plans for issues such as PTSD, TBI, substance use, domestic violence, anger management, and mental-health disorders.
resources.address: 250 East 1st Avenue, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: General Mesa Municipal Court hours: Mon–Thu 7 AM–6 PM except holidays; confirm case-specific appearance instructions.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Mesa Veterans Treatment Court identifies behavioral-health issues and criminogenic factors that contributed to a Veteran or service member entering the criminal-justice system, then orders a case treatment plan. It addresses issues such as PTSD, traumatic brain injury, substance abuse, domestic violence, anger management, and mental-health disorders through coordination with VA, state, community providers, volunteer Veteran mentors, and family-support organizations.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Access depends on involvement in Mesa Municipal Court and court approval. The City page says Veterans are eligible in the court context, but it is not a walk-in treatment program for Veterans without a qualifying court case.

**Population Served**
Veterans and service members with Mesa Municipal Court cases who are appropriate for Veterans Treatment Court.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact Mesa Municipal Court at 480-644-2255 or ask the defense attorney, prosecutor, probation/court staff, or judge about Veterans Treatment Court eligibility. The court is at 250 East 1st Avenue, Mesa, AZ 85210.

**Important Information to Know**
Participation requires a qualifying Mesa Municipal Court case and court approval. Treatment plans carry legal accountability. Any domestic-violence component addresses the participant’s harmful behavior; it is not a survivor shelter, safety hotline or confidential survivor advocacy route.

resources.name: Terros Health / Lifewell Housing Solutions - HUD Housing and Permanent Supportive Housing
resources.description: Lifewell Housing Solutions at Terros Health provides affordable permanent supportive housing connected with behavioral-health services for AHCCCS members with a serious mental illness determination in greater Phoenix housing settings.
resources.address: 3003 N Central Ave, Suite 400, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Affordable permanent supportive housing in collaboration with behavioral-health services, property management and housing specialists who connect tenants to supportive resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page says the service partners with the AHCCCS Housing Program for AHCCCS members with a serious mental illness determination. Referral and unit availability are not public.

**Population Served**
AHCCCS members with SMI determinations needing supportive housing in greater Phoenix housing settings.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Terros Health appointments at 602-685-6000 or email info@terroshealth.org and ask about Lifewell HUD Housing/AHCCCS Housing Program referral requirements.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a public walk-in apartment application. Access likely depends on AHCCCS Housing Program eligibility, behavioral-health referral and available units.

resources.name: Child Crisis Arizona - Safe Place / Emergency Youth Crisis Shelter Access

resources.address: 424 W. Rio Salado Parkway, Mesa, AZ 85201

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Historical Child Crisis Arizona Safe Place youth-crisis lead retained for administrator review.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Current programme operation and eligibility under Child Crisis Arizona have not been reconciled.

**Population Served**
The historical page described youth ages 12–17; that is not established as the current Child Crisis Arizona programme.

**How to Best Connect**
Administrators can ask Child Crisis Arizona at 480-834-9424 about the status of the former programme. Current Lifeology and TXT4HELP access is listed separately.

**Important Information to Know**

resources.name: State of Arizona - Baby Safe Haven Pathway
resources.description: Arizona's Baby Safe Haven law provides a crisis safety pathway for a parent or parent's agent to voluntarily and anonymously surrender an unharmed newborn age 30 days or younger to a qualifying safe-haven provider.
resources.address: Arizona statewide; use a posted Baby Safe Haven provider such as an on-duty fire station, EMT, qualifying hospital staff member, or posted licensed child welfare/adoption agency or church
resources.hours: Emergency pathway depends on qualifying provider availability. Use a posted safe-haven location, hospital, on-duty firefighter/EMT, or emergency services in an urgent situation.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Arizona law allows a parent or parent's agent to leave an unharmed newborn with a safe-haven provider. The provider must take custody when statutory conditions are met and report the receipt of the newborn to the Department of Child Safety.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The infant must be a newborn age 30 days or younger. The parent or agent must voluntarily deliver the newborn to a qualifying safe-haven provider and not express intent to return. The statute does not cover acts outside the safe-haven surrender.

**Population Served**
Arizona parents or parent agents in crisis with an unharmed newborn age 30 days or younger, including Mesa families.

**How to Best Connect**
Use a posted Baby Safe Haven provider: an on-duty firefighter, on-duty EMT, a general or rural general hospital staff member, or a posted licensed child welfare agency, adoption agency, or church that meets the statute. For immediate danger, call 911.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a legal emergency-safety option, not ongoing parenting assistance. The parent or agent may remain anonymous and cannot be required to answer questions, but legal protection is limited to the statutory situation.

resources.name: The Tadini House · Community-Based Reentry Support
resources.description: The Tadini House provides community-based support for men returning from incarceration, including individualized guidance, goal-setting, community connection and a Participatory Defense Hub for families navigating the criminal legal system.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Community-based reentry support for men returning from incarceration, including individualized guidance, goal-setting, social support and community connection. It also operates a Participatory Defense Hub for families involved with the criminal legal system.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The submitted evidence says the envisioned residential sanctuary is not operating and that the organization currently has no formal staff or funding. Current ability to provide support should be confirmed before relying on the referral.

**Population Served**
Men returning from incarceration in the Metro Phoenix area and families navigating a loved one's criminal case or reentry.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 623-695-6483 or use the website contact route. No current public office hours or walk-in site are established in this record.

**Important Information to Know**
Do not refer as housing. The organization is a useful support lead, but the residential sanctuary was described as not yet operating and capacity may be informal or limited.

resources.name: Valle del Sol Community Health - East Valley Primary Care and Sliding Fee Program
resources.description: Valle del Sol Community Health provides primary care in Phoenix and Mesa, including family medicine, chronic disease care, women's health, vaccinations, hearing and vision screenings, lab work, diagnostic testing, medication management, behavioral-health coordination, telehealth, walk-ins, and a sliding fee scale.
resources.address: 334 W. 10th Pl., Suite 100, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Primary-care page does not list East Valley hours; call 602-258-6797 or use online scheduling. After-hours services are available by calling the main number.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Primary care and family medicine for all ages, annual physicals, wellness exams, diagnosis and treatment of acute and chronic illness, disease prevention, vaccinations and immunizations, hearing and vision screenings, women's health, lab work, diagnostic testing, medication management, specialist coordination, behavioral-health coordination, telehealth, and sliding-fee support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Valle del Sol accepts walk-ins, works with most insurance providers, and offers sliding-fee options. Sliding-fee eligibility is based on household income and family size; patients may bring proof of income or ask about sliding-fee assistance when scheduling.

**Population Served**
Phoenix and Mesa patients of all ages, including English- and Spanish-speaking patients, uninsured or underinsured patients, families, and people needing integrated medical and behavioral-health support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-258-6797 or schedule online. East Valley primary care is listed at 334 W. 10th Pl., Suite 100, Mesa, AZ 85201. Ask about sliding-fee assistance when scheduling or at the first visit.

**Important Information to Know**
Ask for an estimate, insurance/sliding-fee screening and the location of the needed service. A discount is not necessarily free care. Hearing/vision screening differs from specialty eye care; dental, pharmacy and specialty services may involve other locations or referral. Walk-in availability and after-hours arrangements should be confirmed through the main line.

resources.name: Job Connect Mesa — Career Exploration and Job Search
resources.description: A Mesa career platform connecting job searches with career exploration, training options and local workforce resources.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

A Mesa career platform connecting job searches with career exploration, training options and local workforce resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Access is through the online platform. Employers, training programs and assistance providers set their own requirements; an account may be needed for some features.

**Population Served**

Mesa-area job seekers exploring occupations, training and local employment opportunities.

**How to Best Connect**

Start with Jobs, Training or Guidance on Job Connect Mesa. For in-person help, use the City of Mesa Workforce Center’s current contact information.

**Important Information to Know**

Listings and events change. Confirm an opening with the employer and use the linked provider’s current intake details before traveling.

resources.name: Maricopa County Attorney's Office - Victim Services Division
resources.description: Maricopa County Attorney's Office Victim Services Division assists crime victims through the county criminal justice process with advocacy, victim-rights information, case notification, restitution information, post-conviction notification, and referrals to compensation and other supports.
resources.address: 225 W Madison St, Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Victim-rights information, advocacy and support during county criminal cases, case and post-conviction notification, restitution information/forms, compensation/resource referrals and victim-information materials in English and Spanish.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Generally for victims connected to Maricopa County criminal cases handled through the County Attorney, including current pending cases and post-conviction notification matters. Mesa misdemeanor matters may be handled through a city prosecutor or local victim-services route instead.

**Population Served**
Crime victims in Maricopa County criminal cases, including domestic-violence victims and victims of juvenile offenses whose cases are in the county system.

**How to Best Connect**
For notification about a current pending case, call Victim Services Division at 602-506-8522. The County Attorney address is 225 W Madison St, Phoenix, AZ 85003.

**Important Information to Know**
This is prosecution-connected victim advocacy, not independent confidential community advocacy or private legal representation. For immediate safety, shelter or civil protective orders, use the corresponding emergency, domestic-violence or court route.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Economic Security - Arizona Early Intervention Program Central Referral
resources.description: Arizona Early Intervention Program is the statewide IDEA Part C referral system for infants and toddlers with suspected developmental delays or disabilities, including Mesa and Maricopa County children.
resources.address: Statewide Arizona central referral; local early intervention teams are assigned by service area
resources.hours: Online, email, phone, and fax referral options are available; local evaluation schedules are determined after referral.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
AzEIP is Arizona's statewide early intervention system. It provides referral, evaluation, service coordination, and support to help families and caregivers support infants and toddlers learning and growing through everyday activities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Families or professionals can refer Arizona children from birth until the third birthday when there are concerns about development, disability or delays. Evaluation determines programme eligibility and services.

**Population Served**
Arizona infants and toddlers, including Mesa and Maricopa County children, and their families or caregivers.

**How to Best Connect**
Refer a child online through the AzEIP referral form, email azeipreferral@azdes.gov, call 888-592-0140, or fax 602-357-1978. Referral status can be checked by email or by calling 602-532-9960.

**Important Information to Know**
Referral does not guarantee a particular therapy or provider; the local team is assigned by service area and need. For children age three or older, ask the school district about Child Find/AZ Find instead.

resources.name: Newfound Hope Wellness and Detox Center
resources.description: Tempe treatment and housing provider serving Native American families with outpatient day treatment, therapy, psychiatric services, housing, parenting classes, GED support, childcare, peer support, meals and culturally based wellness activities.
resources.address: 4765 S Lakeshore Dr, Tempe, AZ 85282
resources.hours: Admissions route by phone or inquiry form; specific program hours were not established.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Newfound Hope Wellness and Detox Center states it provides treatment and housing for Native American families. Official services listed include outpatient day treatment, therapy services, psychiatric services, housing for families and single individuals, parenting classes, GED program, yoga and meditation, childcare, 24/7 peer support, meals, culturally based classes and activities, and evidence-based treatment modalities for addictions, mood regulation difficulties and related issues.

**Eligibility Requirements**

The official page specifically describes treatment and housing for Native American families. It does not establish detailed admission rules, detox level of care, insurance, medical-stability requirements, age limits, or whether non-Native clients are eligible.

**Population Served**

Native American families and individuals needing treatment, housing and recovery/wellness support in Tempe/Maricopa County. The page emphasizes family-unit support and culturally appropriate services.

**How to Best Connect**

Call admissions at 480-418-6386, email info@nfhaz.com, or use the inquiry form on the official website. Address: 4765 S Lakeshore Dr, Tempe, AZ 85282.

**Important Information to Know**

Although the organization name includes detox, the page reviewed did not describe a specific medically monitored detox level of care. Confirm current detox/withdrawal capacity, eligibility, payer rules, openings and whether the person must be a Native American family member before referral.

resources.name: Greater Phoenix Urban League - Summer Youth Employment Program / Youth Services
resources.description: Greater Phoenix Urban League Youth Services offers job readiness training, career coaching, financial literacy, career exploration, internships, college opportunities and a paid 5-week Summer Youth Employment Program for youth ages 16-21.
resources.address: 6044 S. 16th Street, Suite 180, Phoenix, AZ 85042
resources.hours: Ask about the next summer application cycle and current youth-service appointments.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Youth services include job readiness training, career coaching, financial literacy, career exploration, internships and college opportunities. The Summer Youth Employment Program offers a 5-week paid internship experience, counselor support, pay for 110 hours of work and job-readiness workshops.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Summer Youth Employment Program serves youth ages 16-21. Other youth services may have separate eligibility, documentation or timing requirements.

**Population Served**
Greater Phoenix/Maricopa County youth and young adults, including Mesa-area youth who can access the Phoenix-based program or partner worksites if accepted.

**How to Best Connect**
Email youthservices@gphxul.org to ask about current youth services or the next Summer Youth Employment Program application cycle. Use the notification route on the provider’s employment page.

**Important Information to Know**
The summer pathway serves ages 16–21 and describes five weeks with pay for 110 hours of work and job-readiness activities. The posted 2026 opening notice does not establish a current application window; confirm the next cycle, eligibility, worksite and transportation.

resources.name: Brighter Way Tooth Bus - Mobile Dental Center
resources.description: Brighter Way Tooth Bus is a mobile two-chair dental center serving Greater Phoenix by bringing dental screenings, education and access to care into the community for vulnerable children and adults.
resources.address: Based at 3140 W. Buckeye Rd., Phoenix, AZ 85009; mobile service in Greater Phoenix
resources.hours: Mobile schedule is not posted; call or email before referral.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A fully contained two-chair mobile dental center that brings screenings, education and access to dental care into community settings.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility and site access depend on Brighter Way's partner locations, event schedule and target populations. Current public information supports Greater Phoenix service but does not establish a regular Mesa stop.

**Population Served**
Vulnerable Maricopa County residents reached through mobile and community partner sites, including children, low-income adults, veterans, people experiencing homelessness and people with developmental disabilities.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-362-0744 or email info@brighterwaydental.org to ask whether the Tooth Bus has a current East Valley or Mesa partner site and what intake rules apply.

**Important Information to Know**
Use this as a reserve/mobile dental option, not a guaranteed Mesa appointment. Confirm location, eligibility and whether treatment beyond screening/education is available at the planned stop.

resources.name: UCP ArizonAbility — adult day programme and authorized transport
resources.description: A North Phoenix day programme for adults with developmental or physical disabilities, with DDD-authorized transportation for enrolled members.
resources.address: 1802 W. Parkside Ln., Building C, Phoenix, AZ 85027
resources.hours: Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–6 p.m.; confirm programme attendance and transport schedules.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Adult day treatment and training with life-skills activities, recreation, social participation and community outings. The programme can provide scheduled transportation authorized by DDD.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For adults with developmental or physical disabilities who meet the programme’s intake and funding requirements. Transportation requires DDD authorization and an appropriate service plan; it is not public paratransit.

**Population Served**
Adults attending the North Phoenix ArizonAbility programme. A Mesa pickup is not assured; ask about the exact residence and approved route.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-694-9300 or email arizonability@ucpofcentralaz.org to discuss intake or arrange a tour. Ask the DDD support coordinator about programme and transportation authorization before making travel plans.

**Important Information to Know**
Day-programme enrollment does not establish eligibility for unrestricted rides. Confirm attendance, costs or payer approval, personal-care needs, transport scheduling and whether the provider can serve the person’s address.

resources.name: Inside Out Network — Connections before and after release
resources.description: Provides an online network for connecting with reentry service providers, housing and employment opportunities.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides an online network for connecting with reentry service providers, housing and employment opportunities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Access depends on account and facility arrangements; each listed provider sets its own requirements.

**Population Served**
People preparing for release in Arizona and people returning to the community.

**How to Best Connect**
Use Inside Out Network’s official site; people in Arizona state facilities can ask about Opportunities on Edovo, which prompts connection starting eleven months before release.

**Important Information to Know**
Messaging a listed provider does not guarantee admission, a bed or a job. The platform connects people to services rather than supplying every listed service itself.

resources.name: St. Anne Friends of the Needy — Food boxes and infant supplies
resources.description: Offers food boxes in Gilbert, with diapers and possible infant food or formula when available.
resources.address: 14 N Cottonwood Drive, Gilbert, AZ 85234
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Offers food boxes in Gilbert, with diapers and possible infant food or formula when available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
One food box per seven days; government photo ID and the client’s in-person presence are required. No proxy pickup. Infant items depend on need and supplies.

**Population Served**
Individuals and families needing food; children’s supplies are available through the same distribution.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit 14 N Cottonwood Drive, Gilbert. Current hoursTuesday, Wednesday, Thursday andSaturday 8–11 a.m.; the provider recommends arriving 7 a.m. because service is first come. Use its website contact route for questions.

**Important Information to Know**
Limited delivery may be considered for Gilbert residents with access barriers, depending on volunteers and capacity. This is not a Mesa home-delivery promise.

resources.name: Legal Services for Crime Victims in Arizona - free legal and social services
resources.description: Legal Services for Crime Victims in Arizona provides free legal and social services for crime victims, with priority to domestic-violence and sexual-violence victims. Programs include victims' rights enforcement, protective-order representation/support, and domestic-violence legal document preparation.
resources.address: Mail only: PO Box 2156, Sun City, AZ 85372
resources.hours: Contact page listed 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; confirm current hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free victim-rights attorney representation in criminal cases; protective-order representation and safety-related support; and separate domestic-violence legal-document preparation, filing and hearing preparation for collateral civil matters. Social-service support and court accompaniment may also be available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must fit the selected program and pass conflict, case and capacity screening. Domestic- and sexual-violence victims receive priority.

**Population Served**
Arizona crime victims, including survivors seeking protective-order help or assistance with related legal documents.

**How to Best Connect**
Use Request Assistance on lscva.org/our-programs or call 623-471-6401. Identify the needed programme and any hearing date, and provide a safe way to contact the applicant.

**Important Information to Know**
Document preparation is not attorney representation. Acceptance into one service does not promise help in every legal matter; this is not a criminal-defense or general civil law firm.

resources.name: Solari Crisis Response Network - Central Arizona Peer Support Warm Line
resources.description: Solari's Central Arizona Warm Line is a 24/7 anonymous peer-support phone line for adults who want non-crisis support for loneliness, stress, depression, anxiety, substance use, recovery, coping, or local resources.
resources.hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Anonymous telephone peer support from trained Peer Support Specialists; callers can talk about loneliness, worries, depression, anxiety, substance use, recovery, coping strategies, local resources, and support groups before a crisis develops.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open to adults age 18 and older. A diagnosis or specific mental-health concern is not required. It is not for urgent crisis assessment.

**Population Served**
Adults in Central Arizona, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents, who want non-emergency peer support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-347-1100. Callers may connect up to three times per day for up to 20 minutes per call.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a warm line, not crisis dispatch, therapy, medication management, or emergency response. For suicidal thoughts or urgent concerns, call 988, Solari's crisis line, or 911 for immediate danger.

resources.name: The Olive Press - Safe House Program for Individuals in Abuse
resources.description: The Olive Press Safe House Program for Individuals in Abuse is described as all-gender-inclusive safe housing and advocacy for adults experiencing sexual or domestic violence, sex trafficking, homelessness, or other abuse. Programme listings note private-pay fees and a confidential Mesa-area listing.
resources.address: Confidential Mesa/Maricopa County safe-housing location not publicly listed
resources.hours: Call before referral to confirm intake, current bed availability, costs, safe contact, and location instructions.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Safe housing and advocacy for adults experiencing sexual or domestic violence, sex trafficking, homelessness, or other abuse. Available programme listings describe the program as all-gender-inclusive and connected to a confidential Mesa safe-housing listing.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For adults experiencing abuse or unsafe housing situations who can be accepted by the program. Current intake, fees, bed availability, and any screening rules must be confirmed directly.

**Population Served**
Adults of all genders experiencing sexual or domestic violence, sex trafficking, homelessness, or other abuse in the Mesa/Maricopa County area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 915-538-8673. Ask about current intake, cost, safe communication, bed availability, and whether the client should receive location information only after screening.

**Important Information to Know**
The official site evidence indicates private-pay fees and does not publish the confidential location. Do not promise free placement or send a client to an address without direct instructions from the program.

resources.name: Desert Manna Food Pantry - Saturday Grocery Box Distribution
resources.description: Desert Manna Food Pantry distributes free grocery boxes every Saturday morning in East Mesa, with a preferred neighborhood service area but willingness to help others when possible.
resources.address: 590 N 96th St, Mesa, AZ 85207, on the Calvary Free Lutheran Church campus
resources.hours: Every Saturday 7:00-10:00 AM, first come first served while supplies last.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Desert Manna distributes boxes of groceries at no cost. Boxes vary by donations but the pantry tries to include staples such as rice, beans, pasta, canned goods, frozen meat, bread and bakery items.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The pantry is equipped to serve people living between Power Road and Meridian, and between McKellips Road and Southern Avenue. People outside that area may still receive a box, but the pantry suggests using United Food Bank, St. Mary's Food Bank or Vivery to find a closer pantry.

**Population Served**
Families and individuals needing groceries in East Mesa, especially the pantry's stated neighborhood service area.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to 590 N 96th St, Mesa on Saturday between 7:00 AM and 10:00 AM. The pantry does not deliver, but a neighbor or family member may pick up for someone who cannot come.

**Important Information to Know**
Distribution is first come, first served and donation-dependent. The official site does not list a public phone number, so check the website before referral if schedule changes are a concern.

resources.name: VA Phoenix Health Care System - Military 2 VA (M2VA) Program
resources.description: Phoenix VA Military 2 VA helps returning service members and recently separated Veterans transition from active-duty or DoD care into VA health care, including care navigation, initial VA medical appointments, mental-health care, TBI/polytrauma connection, and referral help.
resources.address: 650 East Indian School Road, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Military 2 VA provides transitional care management for people moving from active duty or the DoD health care system into Phoenix VA Health Care. Help may include VA health-system navigation, initial VA medical appointments, post-deployment and readjustment-focused psychotherapy, mental-health medication evaluation and management, polytrauma/TBI care connection, primary-care connection, and referral assistance.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is for returning service members and Veterans who need help transitioning into VA care. Exact enrollment and service-history requirements should be confirmed with the program because VA health-care eligibility and M2VA transition criteria can differ by situation.

**Population Served**
Returning service members and Veterans in the Phoenix VA Health Care System service area, including Mesa and Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Email VHAPHOMTFReferral@va.gov for Phoenix VA Military 2 VA. For appointment/routing help, call VA Health Connect at 888-214-7264 or Phoenix VA main line 602-277-5551 and ask for M2VA. Confirm the actual appointment location and programme referral steps.

**Important Information to Know**
This is transition care and navigation, not an emergency service or a promise of an immediate appointment or benefit. For veteran crisis support, call 988 then press 1 or text 838255; use emergency services for immediate danger.

resources.name: Child Crisis Arizona / Southwest Behavioral & Health Services - Center for Child & Family Wellness counseling access
resources.description: Child Crisis Arizona's Center for Child & Family Wellness hosts outpatient counseling for youth in care and children and families referred from the community through Southwest Behavioral & Health Services, plus a NAMI caregiver support group at the Mesa center.
resources.address: 424 W. Rio Salado Parkway, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Center for Child & Family Wellness hosts outpatient counseling services through Southwest Behavioral & Health Services for youth in Child Crisis Arizona care and for children and families referred from the community. The center also hosts a NAMI monthly caregiver support group.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Counseling scheduling is through Southwest Behavioral & Health Services. Children and families referred from the community may be eligible, but payer rules, age range, clinical fit and appointment availability must be confirmed with SBH.

**Population Served**
Children, youth and families in Mesa, including youth in Child Crisis Arizona programs and community-referred children and families needing outpatient counseling.

**How to Best Connect**
Call SB&H Mesa Outpatient at 480-820-5422 or use the linked appointment request. Ask whether the appointment is at Child Crisis’s Center for Child & Family Wellness, 424 W Rio Salado Parkway, or SB&H’s office at 1255 W Baseline Road, Suite 138. Confirm the service, payer and location before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
Child Crisis Arizona hosts this pathway, but clinical counseling is delivered through Southwest Behavioral & Health Services. Confirm whether the client is seeking counseling, the NAMI caregiver group or another class/service at the center.

resources.name: The Salvation Army Metro Phoenix - Project H.O.P.E. Homeless Outreach to Place and Empower
resources.description: The Salvation Army Metro Phoenix Project H.O.P.E. is mobile outreach for families experiencing homelessness, providing basic-needs items, transportation help, identification-document help, referrals, barrier-resolution support and connection to coordinated entry, Family Housing Hub and other services.
resources.address: Call to arrange outreach; Phoenix programme office: 2707 E Van Buren St, Building 2
resources.hours: Project H.O.P.E. outreach: call for availability. Family Housing Hub screening via 211/877-211-8661 is listed daily 9 AM–7 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Mobile outreach to families experiencing homelessness. Help can include food, hygiene and other basic-needs items, transportation, help obtaining identifying documents, referrals and information, barrier-resolution support, help accessing medical, mental-health or substance-use treatment, and connections to legal, vocational, family advocacy and case-management services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For families experiencing homelessness who can be connected through Project H.O.P.E., Maricopa County Coordinated Entry or the Family Housing Hub. Exact Mesa outreach availability and fit for a specific family should be confirmed by phone.

**Population Served**
Families experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County, including families who may be connected through Family Housing Hub or coordinated-entry collaboration.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Project H.O.P.E. at 602-267-4179 and explain the family’s Mesa location and outreach needs. For current family-shelter screening, call 211 or 877-211-8661 and ask for Family Housing Hub.

**Important Information to Know**
Outreach, document and transport support are tied to homeless-family service access, not a public ride programme or guaranteed shelter bed. Confirm whether the team can currently serve the family at its Mesa location; do not travel to the office for a promised placement.

resources.name: Red Mountain United Methodist Church — Power Road and Velda Rose pantries
resources.description: Red Mountain UMC operates two Mesa food pantries; the Velda Rose choice pantry also supplies household essentials when available.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Power Road location provides emergency food bags. The Velda Rose location partners with United Food Bank to provide nonperishable food, household essentials and additional items when available, with recipients selecting quantities according to household size.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Power Road limits emergency food bags to once monthly per household; Velda Rose requires Arizona ID and sizes selections to household size.

**Population Served**
People seeking food in northeast and east Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-981-3833. Power Road church office, 2936 N. Power Road: Monday–Thursday 10 a.m.–1:30 p.m. Velda Rose, 5540 E. Main Street: Monday and Thursday 9:30–11:30 a.m.; confirm holiday changes before travelling.

**Important Information to Know**
Current provider text reports both locations serving clients during 2026, resolving the old redevelopment uncertainty. Confirm holiday changes and supplies; do not transfer one location’s rules to the other.

resources.name: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints - Employment Services Mesa Center
resources.description: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints Employment Services Mesa Center is a local employment-services access point with job coaching, job-search support and center-based contact for Mesa-area job seekers.
resources.address: 235 S El Dorado Cir, Mesa, AZ 85202
resources.hours: Call before visiting to confirm current hours and whether an appointment is needed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Mesa Employment Services center is a local face-to-face employment resource. Services may include individual job coaching, job-search support, resume and interview help, access to job-search tools and employer connections through Church Employment Services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The broader Church Employment Services program states employment help is available to anyone, including nonmembers. The local listing does not publish a full eligibility checklist.

**Population Served**
Mesa and East Valley job seekers who can contact or visit the Mesa Employment Services center.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-829-8999 or visit 235 S El Dorado Cir, Mesa, AZ 85202 after confirming hours and appointment expectations.

**Important Information to Know**
The official local page confirms the center address and phone but gives limited service detail. Call first so a client does not arrive when the center is closed or when an appointment is required.

resources.name: Access from AT&T
resources.description: Access from AT&T provides low-cost home internet pricing for eligible households where AT&T Fiber or AT&T Internet Air is available, with eligibility based on income under 200% of federal poverty guidelines or qualifying government programs.
resources.hours: Phone support: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-8:00 PM CT; Saturday 9:00 AM-7:00 PM CT; Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Access from AT&T provides low-cost home internet service for eligible households. Internet options and pricing depend on address availability and may include AT&T Fiber or AT&T Internet Air. Existing AT&T home internet customers may apply for a lower rate.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A household may qualify if someone participates in a qualifying government assistance program or if household income is below 200% of the federal poverty guideline. Examples on the official page include LIHEAP, Medicaid, SNAP, SSI, TANF, WIC, Veterans and Survivors Pension, Pell Grant, Head Start, school meal programs, and housing assistance. Address availability is required.

**Population Served**
Eligible low-income households in AT&T home internet service areas, including Mesa addresses only where AT&T service is available.

**How to Best Connect**
Enter the home address on the AT&T Access page to see available service and application links. Existing customers can apply through the partner verification link and then call 855-220-5211 after approval. Spanish support is listed at 855-220-5225.

**Important Information to Know**
Availability varies by address. Application links lead to a third-party verification site. Monthly price and speed depend on what AT&T service is available at the address, so do not promise a specific plan before the address check.

resources.name: Mercy Care ACC-RBHA Behavioral-Health Access
resources.description: Mercy Care ACC-RBHA provides physical and behavioral-health coverage, including general mental-health and substance-use concerns, for eligible AHCCCS members in Maricopa, Pinal, and Gila counties.
resources.hours: Member Services Monday-Friday 7:00 AM-6:00 PM. ACC-RBHA with SMI line is listed 24/7.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Health-plan access to physical and behavioral-health coverage for AHCCCS members, including general mental-health and substance-use concerns, provider connection, plan materials, language assistance, crisis-line information, and OIFA help navigating care concerns.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people who qualify for AHCCCS and are enrolled in or choosing Mercy Care ACC-RBHA in its service area. Eligibility and provider network access depend on AHCCCS enrollment, county, plan choice, and benefit status.

**Population Served**
Eligible AHCCCS members in Maricopa, Pinal, and Gila counties, including Mesa residents. Tribal members may choose a Mercy Care plan or American Indian Health Program/ITU options depending on their circumstances.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Member Services at 602-263-3000 or 1-800-624-3879 (TTY 711), Monday-Friday 7:00 AM-6:00 PM. For ACC-RBHA with SMI, Mercy Care lists 602-586-1841 or 1-800-564-5465, 24/7.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an insurance/plan access route, not a walk-in clinic. People not enrolled with Mercy Care may need to apply for AHCCCS, use their assigned plan, or seek another publicly funded pathway. In crisis, Mercy Care lists the Arizona behavioral health crisis line at 1-844-534-4673 or text HOPE to 44673.

resources.name: PCs for Refugees - Free Preloaded Home Computers for Refugee Families
resources.description: PCs for Refugees is a volunteer Arizona nonprofit providing free preloaded home computers, training and support to refugee families, especially in the Phoenix area.
resources.address: 1711 W. University Dr., #158, Tempe, AZ 85281
resources.hours: Office: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Saturday, 8:00–11:00 AM. Recipient pickup must be arranged.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
