The equipment inventory is available for loan to personnel from public education agencies, including districts, charter schools, and other public schools recognized by the Arizona Department of Education. Families and non-school borrowers are directed to AzTAP's general consumer loan program instead.

**Population Served**
Arizona students with disabilities in public education settings, including Mesa students, through school personnel who borrow equipment for evaluation, trial, classroom use, or temporary access.

**How to Best Connect**
School personnel should use https://adeatloan.org/ to search inventory and follow the request steps. ADE lists statewide assistive technology specialists at 602-542-4013. AzTAP contact information on the loan-library site lists 602-728-9534 or 800-477-9921.

**Important Information to Know**
Parents generally cannot borrow directly from this school library. If a family needs a household or consumer device trial, use the separate AzTAP consumer device-loan route instead. Device availability and loan duration depend on inventory and ADE/AzTAP procedures.

resources.name: AirTalk Wireless — Arizona Lifeline service
resources.description: Offers Lifeline mobile service for eligible households in its service area.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Offers Lifeline mobile service for eligible households in its service area.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Qualify for Lifeline through household income or a qualifying assistance programme, and live where AirTalk offers service. Only one Lifeline benefit is allowed per household.

**Population Served**
Eligible Arizona households needing affordable mobile service.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Arizona page to check the address and start enrollment, or call customer service. Have identity and eligibility documents ready.

**Important Information to Know**
Plan allowances and device offers vary by location and eligibility. Check the actual monthly price, device cost and coverage before enrolling; a promotional free device is not guaranteed.

resources.name: Assure Health Care Group of Arizona - All Abilities Learning Center / Day Programs
resources.description: Assure Health Care Group of Arizona operates a Mesa adult day program for adults with disabilities, offering independent living skills, vocational activities, music therapy, community outings and limited transportation for eligible DDD/ALTCS or private-pay participants.
resources.address: 7233 E. Baseline Rd., Ste. 107 & 110, Mesa, AZ 85209
resources.hours: Day program hours are Monday-Friday 8:30 AM-4:30 PM. Employment program groups are listed as 8:30 AM-12:30 PM and 12:30 PM-4:30 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Mesa day program offers structured activities such as line dancing, Zumba, culinary activities, community outings, music and music therapy, game room, animal-assisted therapy, volunteer opportunities, crafts, fitness classes and independent living skill activities. Related employment programming offers job-readiness, group supported employment and individual supported employment supports.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The day program lists eligibility as adults age 18+ who qualify for DDD services, have a qualifying diagnosis such as autism, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy or cognitive delay, have graduated or transitioned from high school, have DDD/ALTCS, and can participate in a group setting without 1:1 support. The FAQ also mentions private pay should be discussed with the program.

**Population Served**
Adults with developmental disabilities in Mesa and other Arizona Assure service areas who meet program and funding requirements.

**How to Best Connect**
For Mesa day programs, call 480-828-1858 or submit the New Member Interest Form on the day-program page to schedule a tour. For employment programming, the Mesa Director of Employment Programs is listed at 480-670-4196.

**Important Information to Know**
Transportation for the day program is limited to about 10 miles from the site and current route availability; employment program transportation is not available unless DTA is also selected. The program states 1:1 support is not available at this time.

resources.name: Area Agency on Aging, Region One - Home-Delivered Meals / Senior Nutrition Intake
resources.description: Area Agency on Aging, Region One connects older adults and adults with disabilities in Maricopa County to home-delivered meals through SAIL and the 24-hour Senior HELP LINE.
resources.address: 1366 E Thomas Rd, Suite 108, Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.hours: 24-hour Senior HELP LINE available by phone; program assessment and provider schedules vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Senior Adult Independent Living program includes case management and in-home supports such as home-delivered meals for people who qualify. The Senior HELP LINE helps callers find the right program or provider in Maricopa County.

**Eligibility Requirements**
SAIL serves older adults and adults with disabilities who live in the community and need help with activities of daily living. Meal service generally requires assessment and may be delivered through local contractors.

**Population Served**
Older adults, adults with disabilities and caregivers in Maricopa County, including Mesa residents seeking in-home meal support or meal-program routing.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the 24-hour Senior HELP LINE at 602-264-HELP (602-264-4357). Toll-free number is 888-783-7500. Ask for home-delivered meals or SAIL intake for the Mesa area.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a navigation and intake route for meal services, not a single meal delivery kitchen. Eligibility, assessment, delivery area, provider assignment, cost contribution and wait times can vary.

resources.name: U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Arizona - Bankruptcy Court Pro Bono Attorney Panel
resources.description: The U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Arizona's Pro Bono Attorney Panel can provide consultation and representation to income-qualified self-represented debtors or creditors in discrete adversary proceedings and contested bankruptcy matters when identified through the court.
resources.address: 230 N. 1st Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Consultation and possible representation by volunteer pro bono attorneys for discrete adversary proceedings and contested bankruptcy matters where litigation skills are needed.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is for pro se debtors or creditors in District of Arizona bankruptcy cases, generally with income at or below 250% of the poverty level. Bankruptcy judges identify matters that appear to qualify, and an advisory committee screens applications. Volunteer attorneys may decline cases.

**Population Served**
Income-qualified self-represented parties in District of Arizona bankruptcy cases, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents with qualifying matters before the bankruptcy court.

**How to Best Connect**
This is not open general intake. Ask the bankruptcy judge, courtroom staff, or Self-Help Center about whether a contested matter or adversary proceeding may be eligible. For more information, the court page lists Tami Johnson, Pro Se Law Clerk, at 602-682-4010 or tami_johnson@azb.uscourts.gov.

**Important Information to Know**
The panel is narrow and court-identified. It does not replace the Bankruptcy Self-Help Center and is not for routine bankruptcy filing help or general debt advice.

resources.name: Connections Health Solutions - Connections Phoenix Crisis Response Center
resources.description: Connections Phoenix is a 24/7/365 behavioral-health crisis center in Phoenix offering walk-in urgent mental-health care, 23-hour stabilization, crisis stabilization, and post-acute services for people in crisis.
resources.address: 1201 S 7th Ave, Suite 150, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.hours: Center operates 24 hours; walk-in lobby is open 7 a.m.–7 p.m.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Walk-in mental-health urgent care, 23-hour stabilization, crisis stabilization, and post-acute services for people experiencing a psychiatric or behavioral-health crisis.

**Eligibility Requirements**
People experiencing a mental-health crisis may walk in or call. Clinical assessment determines the appropriate level of care.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County and Valley residents who can access the Phoenix center, including Mesa residents when Phoenix is the appropriate crisis receiving site.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-416-7600 for current receiving instructions at 1201 S 7th Ave, Suite 150, Phoenix. The center operates 24 hours; the walk-in lobby is open 7 a.m.–7 p.m. For urgent guidance outside lobby hours, call first or contact 988.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a Phoenix crisis receiving center. The team assesses the needed level of care; outpatient treatment, transport and bed availability are not guaranteed.

resources.name: Scottsdale MAT Clinic / SMC · Proposed Maricopa Reentry Center health and MAT pathway
resources.description: County-planned pop-up health and medication-assisted treatment access for people leaving incarceration; current operation and intake need confirmation.
resources.hours: Pop-up access and schedule are arranged through reentry staff; confirm before attending.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The county FY25–26 action plan proposes a pop-up health and medication-assisted treatment clinic at Maricopa Reentry Center, with support for recovery and community reintegration. Current operation has not been confirmed.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The proposed pathway targets uninsured or underinsured people leaving incarceration. Reentry staff and the provider need to confirm whether it is operating, who can enter and the current referral process.

**Population Served**
People served through the Maricopa Re-Entry Center pathway.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask assigned reentry staff about the current clinic and referral process. SMC's public inquiry number is 480-998-4673; identify the Maricopa Re-Entry Center pathway when calling. Confirm the actual service location and appointment arrangements before traveling.

**Important Information to Know**
An action-plan entry does not establish an open clinic. An operating schedule and intake route must be confirmed before referral.
resources.resolutionReason: The only programme-specific official evidence is an action-plan strategy to establish the clinic. Current SMC pages and bounded follow-up did not confirm operation, schedule or intake. This material availability question requires administrator resolution; it is not a claim the provider closed.

resources.name: Spero House - Women's sober living homes
resources.description: Spero House is a Mesa sober living community for women, stating it is licensed by the City of Mesa and the Arizona State Department of Health and providing direct phone/contact-form access.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Women's sober living community in Mesa for people in recovery who need structured sober housing.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public page does not list full admission criteria, rates, sobriety requirements or house rules. Call or use the contact form to confirm fit before referral.

**Population Served**
Women seeking sober living in Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-287-7821 or use the website contact form to ask about admission, cost, current openings and required recovery participation.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not free emergency shelter. The site states it is licensed by the City of Mesa and the Arizona State Department of Health and is affiliated with AzRHA; confirm current license and fees during intake.

resources.name: Native American Connections - Permanent Supportive Housing Communities
resources.description: Native American Connections manages Permanent Supportive Housing communities in Maricopa County for adults experiencing chronic homelessness and/or serious mental illness or disability, combining furnished apartments with onsite supportive services for relapse, income loss, physical and mental health, and daily living stability.
resources.address: 3216 N 3rd Street, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Permanent supportive housing in furnished apartments with onsite supportive services, housing stability support, help through relapse or loss of income, support for serious physical health and mental health issues, and daily living skills support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be 18 or older, chronically homeless, and have a HUD-applicable disability. NAC's FAQ says single adults over 18 in Maricopa County experiencing chronic homelessness and/or serious mental illness are eligible to receive a housing assessment through a Coordinated Entry Access Point.

**Population Served**
Adults experiencing chronic homelessness and/or serious mental illness or other disabilities in Maricopa County, including veterans in some communities.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete a housing assessment through the Maricopa County Coordinated Entry System. NAC states a referral from the Human Services Campus is required for placement at a permanent supportive housing site. Use NAC's Find a Coordinated Entry Point link for access-point options.

**Important Information to Know**
Applicants cannot apply directly to an individual PSH property. Placement depends on Coordinated Entry assessment, referral priority, eligibility documentation, and unit availability.

resources.name: The Salvation Army Metro Phoenix - Emergency Disaster Services
resources.description: The Salvation Army Metro Phoenix Emergency Disaster Services responds to natural and human-made disasters with immediate needs support including food, shelter, clothing, disaster social services, donations management and recovery services.
resources.address: 2707 E Van Buren St, Phoenix, AZ 85008
resources.hours: Metro Phoenix office: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Disaster response for immediate needs after emergencies, including food, shelter, clothing, disaster social services, emotional/spiritual care, donations management and recovery supports.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people affected by a disaster or emergency. Assistance is situation-specific and may be coordinated through first responders, emergency management, Red Cross or Salvation Army disaster teams.

**Population Served**
Metro Phoenix and Southwest Division residents affected by fires, floods, heat emergencies or other disasters, including Mesa residents when a disaster-response pathway is activated.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Metro Phoenix office at 602-267-4100 during office hours. In an active emergency, work through 911, first responders, emergency management, Red Cross or the responding Salvation Army disaster team.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a routine clothing closet. It is most appropriate after a disaster or displacement event, and client intake may depend on the responding agency and disaster circumstances.

resources.name: Aid to Women Center - Prenatal Care and Pregnancy Support
resources.description: Chandler pregnancy center offering pregnancy tests, limited first-trimester ultrasound and a paid prenatal/postpartum care program that explicitly serves Mesa families.
resources.address: 3029 N. Alma School Rd., Suite 130, Chandler, AZ 85224
resources.hours: Chandler: Monday and Wednesday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM; Tuesday 9 AM-5 PM. Call for prenatal appointments.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Pregnancy testing, limited first-trimester ultrasound, prenatal appointments and standard obstetric labs, education and postpartum exams.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Call to discuss pregnancy stage, medical needs, insurance and the appropriate service. The provider describes its prenatal package as an option for people without insurance; suitability and additional testing are determined at intake.

**Population Served**
Pregnant and postpartum patients in Chandler and surrounding East Valley communities, explicitly including Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-966-1902. Pregnancy-test walk-ins are welcomed; other services require appointments. The Chandler center is at 3029 N. Alma School Rd., Suite 130.

**Important Information to Know**
The provider lists a $385 prenatal package with installment payments. Hospital labor/delivery, the standard diagnostic ultrasound and some additional tests or treatment are excluded; ask for the current full cost and delivery referral. Limited free ultrasound is not comprehensive prenatal imaging. Confirm service scope rather than treating general pregnancy-options information as an offer of every reproductive-health service.

resources.name: Arizona Kosher Food Pantry - Kosher Food Pantry
resources.description: Arizona Kosher Food Pantry is a dedicated kosher pantry in Phoenix and a Feeding America network member, offering culturally and religiously appropriate kosher food during weekday pantry hours.
resources.address: 7118 N 7th Street, Phoenix, AZ 85020
resources.hours: Monday, Wednesday, Friday 9:00 AM-1:00 PM; Tuesday 11:00 AM-1:00 PM; Thursday 9:00 AM-1:30 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Arizona Kosher Food Pantry provides kosher pantry food and related food access support. It describes itself as the only dedicated kosher pantry in the Southwest and a Feeding America network member.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official contact page lists pantry hours and contact information but does not fully state income, document, religious affiliation or service-area requirements. Call before sending a client from Mesa if documentation or travel is a barrier.

**Population Served**
People who need kosher or culturally/religiously appropriate food in the Phoenix/Maricopa County area, including Mesa clients who can travel and are accepted by the pantry.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit the pantry during posted hours at 7118 N 7th Street in Phoenix, call 602-492-4989, or email info@azkosherpantry.org to confirm current access rules.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a Phoenix pantry and travel from Mesa may be significant. The official page gives hours but not full eligibility rules, so confirm before a long trip.

resources.name: City of Phoenix - Phoenix Community Court vital-document support
resources.description: Phoenix Community Court is a court-linked program for unhoused people with eligible Phoenix matters. City program materials describe individualized plans with the Office of Homeless Solutions, Prosecutor, Public Defender and Community Bridges, and identify vital-document completion as a participant outcome.
resources.hours: Phoenix Municipal Court telephone service Monday-Friday, 8:00 AM-5:00 PM, excluding City holidays. Community Court access is case and referral dependent.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides coordinated court case planning and links to stabilization services for eligible unsheltered defendants, including help addressing vital-document barriers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The person must have an eligible Phoenix court matter and meet the program criteria. This is not a general ID clinic; a Mesa address alone does not establish eligibility.

**Population Served**
Unsheltered people with eligible Phoenix Municipal Court cases.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Phoenix Municipal Court at 602-262-6421 during weekday business hours and ask about Community Court eligibility or work through the assigned court team. Follow the hearing or referral instructions for location.

**Important Information to Know**
General court staff can route an inquiry but cannot promise program acceptance or document funding. Mesa Community Court is a separate program for qualifying Mesa matters.

resources.name: Arizona DES Rehabilitation Services Administration - Independent Living Older Blind Program
resources.description: Arizona DES Rehabilitation Services Administration's Independent Living Older Blind program helps adults age 55 and older with significant vision loss learn daily living, mobility, assistive technology and adjustment skills to remain independent.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Daily living skills, orientation and mobility training, assistive technology, support adjusting to vision loss, and independent-living instruction intended to help participants live independently at home and in the community.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be age 55 or older, have significant vision loss, have vision loss that limits independence, need program services to stay or become independent, and be willing to participate.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents age 55+ who are blind or have low vision that limits independence, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call toll-free 1-888-282-9857 or Phoenix area 602-266-9286 to learn more or start an application. Email rsailb@azdes.gov for program contact. TTY/TDD is available through 711.

**Important Information to Know**
Intake determines the training location, home/community/remote options, contracted provider and wait time. Request auxiliary aids or alternate formats. This is vision-related independent-living support, not eye treatment, routine exams, glasses vouchers, cash aid or the separate VR employment programme.

resources.name: One Step Beyond, Inc. - Life Skills, Employment, Culinary Training, Recreation, Respite and Intake/Enrollment
resources.description: One Step Beyond provides DDD-contracted programs for people with intellectual disabilities, including life skills, employment, culinary training, recreation, socialization, respite and intake/enrollment.
resources.address: Arizona campuses include Phoenix and Scottsdale; no Mesa campus found on official site
resources.hours: Contact intake for program schedules and location fit; campus-specific hours were not established.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Programs for individuals with intellectual disabilities and their families, including employment opportunities, life skills training, culinary employment and training, recreation, fine arts, music, dance, health and fitness, socialization, respite programs, and intake/enrollment support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official site says One Step Beyond is contracted with Arizona DES Division of Developmental Disabilities. Participants generally need program fit and DDD or other approved funding; exact eligibility, openings and campus placement must be confirmed through intake.

**Population Served**
People with intellectual disabilities and their families in Arizona, including Maricopa County residents able to access an OSBI campus or service arrangement.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 623-215-2449 or use the Intake and Enrollment page/contact forms on osbi.org. Ask which Arizona campus is realistic for a Mesa resident and whether DDD authorization is required for the desired program.

**Important Information to Know**
No Mesa campus was found on the official site. This may still be useful for Mesa clients who can travel or have funded transportation, but campus location, openings and DDD/private-pay requirements should be confirmed before referral.

resources.name: Semiconductor Technician Quick Start
resources.description: Maricopa Community Colleges' Semiconductor Technician Quick Start is a 10-day, 40-hour in-person training that prepares learners for semiconductor and advanced-manufacturing technician roles, with current Mesa-area and future Mesa cohort routes.
resources.address: Chandler-Gilbert Community College Williams Campus, 7360 E. Tahoe Ave., Mesa, AZ 85212; future Mesa Community College cohorts at 1833 W. Southern Ave., Mesa, AZ 85202
resources.hours: Cohort dates vary; the page lists future Spring 2027 Mesa Community College dates to be posted later.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
In-person semiconductor technician quick-start training, 10 days at 4 hours per day, with hands-on semiconductor/advanced manufacturing content. Successful completion can provide an industry-relevant certification for a resume and three college credits.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Enrollment depends on completing the program's interest/assessment and campus steps. Stipend eligibility requires successfully completing the class and passing the NIMS Technician Certification test; students who do not meet those requirements are responsible for tuition and fees.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County learners seeking semiconductor or advanced-manufacturing technician training, including Mesa residents able to attend CGCC Williams Campus or future MCC cohorts.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the official page's interest/enrollment route. For Chandler-Gilbert Williams Campus, email azami@cgc.edu. For future Mesa Community College cohorts, email azami@mesacc.edu.

**Important Information to Know**
The page lists Mesa Community College Spring 2027 dates as forthcoming. The stipend covers Arizona resident tuition only after successful completion and NIMS test passage, so confirm costs, schedule, and requirements before referral.

resources.name: AZCEND · Housing Stability legal advocate / rent and utility assistance navigation
resources.description: AZCEND housing-stability lead connecting eligible households to rent/utility assistance and listed by Arizona courts as an approved Housing Stability Certified Community Legal Advocate organization in Chandler/Maricopa County.
resources.address: 132 W Bruce Ave, Gilbert, AZ 85233
resources.hours: Gilbert CAP hours: Monday 7:30 AM-6:00 PM; Tuesday-Thursday 7:30 AM-5:00 PM; Friday 8:30 AM-noon.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
AZCEND's Community Action Program helps with rent, utilities, water, gas, electric, and mortgage assistance for eligible households in listed service areas. The Arizona courts' legal-advocates directory lists AZCEND as an approved Housing Stability organization with a certified legal advocate in Chandler/Maricopa County.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The opened rent/utility page is specifically for Gilbert residents. The AOC directory lists AZCEND's legal-advocate service area as Chandler / Maricopa County. Assistance depends on program geography, financial hardship, documentation, funding, and legal-advocate availability.

**Population Served**
Low-income households facing rent, utility, housing-stability, or homelessness risk in AZCEND service areas. Mesa eligibility for AZCEND's legal-advocate service should be confirmed because public rent/utility pages are city-specific.

**How to Best Connect**
For the Gilbert CAP page, call 480-892-5331 ext. 200 or email cap@azcend.org. The AOC directory lists AZCEND CCLA contact Ariel Ackerman at 480-963-1423. The Maricopa County Housing Stability Rental and Utility Assistance portal is linked from AZCEND's page.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a useful reserve housing-stability legal-advocate lead, not clearly a Mesa-specific rent/utility program. Applying does not guarantee funding or legal help. Confirm current geography and whether the certified legal advocate can assist the specific Mesa household before referral.

resources.name: Verizon - Verizon Forward Home Internet Discount
resources.description: Verizon Forward provides an up to $30 monthly discount on compatible Verizon or Frontier home internet plans for eligible households, subject to address and plan availability.
resources.hours: Online availability check and application; phone hours not established.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Reduced-cost home internet through a variable Verizon Forward discount of up to $30 per month on eligible Verizon 5G Home, LTE Home, Verizon Home Internet Lite, Fios and Frontier Fiber plans. Verizon states final cost is $20 per month or higher depending on plan and other discounts.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A customer may qualify through programs or criteria such as Lifeline, SNAP, Medicaid, WIC, income at or below 200% of Federal Poverty Guidelines, Pell Grant, SSI, Section 8, Veterans and Survivors Pension, BIA General Assistance, FDPIR, Tribal TANF or qualifying Tribal Head Start. The selected plan must be compatible and service must be available at the address.

**Population Served**
Eligible home internet customers where Verizon or Frontier qualifying plans are available, including possible Mesa/Maricopa addresses after serviceability check.

**How to Best Connect**
Use Verizon Forward's Check Availability or sign in as an existing customer, complete the application and upload required eligibility documents if requested. New customers must complete the final step to apply the discount after qualification.

**Important Information to Know**
Not all Mesa addresses have eligible Verizon or Frontier home internet. Limited to one Verizon Forward discount per account, older plans may not qualify, and the discount may appear after 1-2 bill cycles once eligibility and service are complete.

resources.name: Phoenix Indian Medical Center Behavioral Health Clinic
resources.description: Phoenix Indian Medical Center Behavioral Health Clinic provides psychiatric, psychological, social-service, substance-use, psychotherapy, medication-treatment, family/group therapy, crisis-intervention, and benefits-coordination services for eligible IHS patients.
resources.address: 4212 N. 16th St., Phoenix, AZ 85016
resources.hours: Clinic hours Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM; walk-in nurse screening Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-3:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Psychiatric, psychological, social-service, and substance-use consultation services; psychosocial assessments; psychotherapy; medication treatment; group work; family therapy; crisis intervention; substance-use counseling; and benefits coordination.

**Eligibility Requirements**
IHS eligibility applies. IHS states members of federally recognized American Indian and Alaska Native Tribes and their descendants are eligible for IHS services, and patient registration should confirm documentation and appointment requirements.

**Population Served**
Eligible American Indian and Alaska Native patients in the Phoenix Area, including Mesa residents who can access Phoenix Indian Medical Center.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-263-1518. The Behavioral Health Clinic is at 4212 N. 16th St., Phoenix, AZ 85016. Walk-in nurse screening is listed Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-3:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
IHS is not health insurance, and eligibility, registration, and available services should be confirmed before travel. For non-IHS eligible urban Native clients, an urban Indian health program may be a better fit.

resources.name: Chicanos Por La Causa - CPLC Family Immigration Services, Phoenix
resources.description: Chicanos Por La Causa Family Immigration Services provides DOJ-accredited low- and no-cost immigration services through a Phoenix contact route, including consultations, citizenship, DACA renewals, green-card renewals, work permits, family petitions, consular processing, adjustment, U visas and VAWA.
resources.address: 1402 S Central Ave, Bldg. A, Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.hours: Use the online Request Service form or call/text the Phoenix immigration contact for appointment availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Low- and no-cost consultations and immigration assistance for citizenship/naturalization, DACA renewals, green-card renewal including Form I-90, work-permit renewal, family petitions, consular processing, adjustment, U visas and VAWA matters within accredited scope.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Clients must have a case type within CPLC’s current immigration-services scope. The official page says CPLC currently does not offer representation for immigration-court cases, so people facing deportation or other court matters need an attorney or another removal-defense referral.

**Population Served**
Immigrants and mixed-status families in Arizona, including Phoenix/Central Arizona and Mesa-area residents able to use the Phoenix office or online request route.

**How to Best Connect**
Submit the Request Service form on the immigration page or call/text the Phoenix immigration line at 602-837-2129. Email Phoenix.immigration@cplc.org. The Phoenix contact address is 1402 S Central Ave, Bldg. A, Phoenix, AZ 85004.

**Important Information to Know**
The page lists a Phoenix contact but its service-area prose also names southern-Arizona cities. Confirm Mesa case acceptance, fees, appointment location and the exact document/case scope through Phoenix intake. CPLC does not currently offer immigration-court representation; removal cases need a different legal route.

resources.name: Arizona College - Mesa Medical Billing and Coding and Medical Assistant with Phlebotomy
resources.description: Arizona College's Mesa campus offers short healthcare career programs, including Medical Assistant with Phlebotomy and Medical Billing and Coding, with hybrid options, career services, admissions contact, and financial-aid/scholarship screening.
resources.address: 163 N. Dobson Rd., Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Mesa campus listed hours: Monday-Thursday 9 AM-6 PM, Friday 9 AM-5 PM, Saturday-Sunday closed; additional hours available upon request.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Arizona College Mesa offers allied health career programs including Medical Assistant with Phlebotomy, Medical Billing and Coding, Pharmacy Technician, and Dental Assistant. The candidate programs are listed as a 31-week Medical Assistant with Phlebotomy undergraduate diploma and a 30-week Medical Billing and Coding undergraduate diploma, with hybrid online/in-person options. Career Services offers resume, cover letter, job application, interview, networking, and on-the-job success support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Program admissions are handled by Arizona College. The Mesa page says no high school diploma or GED is required for diploma program enrollment, except Pharmacy Technician; applicants should confirm admission requirements for the exact program.

**Population Served**
People seeking healthcare career training at the Mesa/East Valley campus, including Mesa, Gilbert, Chandler, Tempe, Scottsdale, and Apache Junction area students.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 855-706-8382 or submit the request-information form to speak with Admissions and Financial Aid. Visit the Mesa campus at 163 N. Dobson Rd. during posted hours.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a private career school. Tuition is not listed on the landing page; financial aid and scholarships depend on eligibility. Verify total cost, aid, transferability, schedule, ARIZONA@WORK approval, and job-placement expectations before referral.

resources.name: Dignity Health — Children’s dental clinic at Gilbert Heritage Center
resources.description: Provides a contact for children’s dental-care appointments at Gilbert Heritage Center.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides a contact for children’s dental-care appointments at Gilbert Heritage Center.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Confirm current age, insurance, income and service-area requirements directly; a different Chandler clinic’s residency rule must not be assumed here.

**Population Served**
Children who qualify for the Gilbert outreach dental program and can travel there.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-292-8728 to confirm the current Gilbert Heritage Center clinic, available services and appointment requirements.

**Important Information to Know**
The published 2026 calendar identifies this separate clinic, but the timetable and fees must be checked before travel.

resources.name: Prisma Community Care - gender-affirming social support and identity-document navigation
resources.description: Prisma Community Care provides no-cost patient social support for gender-expansive people, including help applying for legal name and gender-marker changes and navigating related agency services and referrals.
resources.address: 1101 N Central Ave, Suite 200, Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Prisma's gender-affirming care program includes social support for navigating social transitions, including name and gender marker changes, housing assistance, agency services, local gender-affirming resources and referrals at no cost to patients.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Support is described for Prisma patients receiving gender-affirming care or related support. Hormone therapy is described for people age 19 and older, but identity-document navigation may be part of broader support services; confirm appointment eligibility.

**Population Served**
Transgender, non-binary and gender-expansive people in the Phoenix/Maricopa County region who can become Prisma patients or access Prisma support services.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Prisma Community Care at 602-307-5330 to schedule an appointment or ask about gender-affirming support and name or gender-marker change navigation. The clinic is at 1101 N Central Ave, Suite 200, Phoenix.

**Important Information to Know**
This is navigation and support, not legal representation and not a guarantee of payment for government filing or document fees. It is a strong referral when the client is seeking gender-affirming care or patient support along with identity-document changes.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Education - SUN Bucks / Summer EBT 2026
resources.description: Arizona SUN Bucks provides seasonal Summer EBT grocery benefits for eligible school-aged children; 2026 applications closed August 3, 2026 but hotline help remains available for pending applications, missing benefits and card issues.
resources.hours: Hotline availability not stated on the page; call 1-833-648-4406 for SUN Bucks questions or 1-888-997-9333 for EBT card service.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
SUN Bucks, also called Summer EBT, provides grocery-buying benefits to eligible low-income families with school-aged children when school meals are not available during summer. The 2026 benefit is listed as a one-time $120 per eligible child.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Some children are automatically eligible through school meal, SNAP, TANF, FDPIR, eligible Medicaid, foster care, homelessness, migrant education or Head Start-related status. Other children at NSLP/SBP schools may need to apply during the application window.

**Population Served**
Arizona families with eligible school-aged children, including Mesa and Maricopa County families.

**How to Best Connect**
For SUN Bucks questions, missing benefits, address updates, eligibility or appeals, call the SUN Bucks hotline at 1-833-648-4406. For EBT card activation, balance, PIN, lost/stolen/damaged cards or replacement cards, call 1-888-997-9333.

**Important Information to Know**
The ADE page states that 2026 SUN Bucks applications closed August 3, 2026 and late applications will be denied. This remains useful for pending timely applications, benefit questions, appeals, card replacement and future-year monitoring.

resources.name: Arizona SHIP - Medicare Counseling and Senior Medicare Patrol
resources.description: Free, objective Medicare counseling and Senior Medicare Patrol help for Medicare-eligible people, beneficiaries, families and caregivers in Maricopa County.
resources.hours: Counselor appointment availability varies; call for current options.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
SHIP provides free, unbiased help understanding Medicare, comparing plan options, applying for Medicare cost-saving programs, and troubleshooting Medicare coverage questions. Senior Medicare Patrol helps prevent, detect and report Medicare fraud, errors and abuse.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Medicare beneficiaries, people approaching Medicare eligibility, and their family members or caregivers. Cost-saving programs have separate income and resource rules.

**Population Served**
Arizona Medicare beneficiaries and Medicare-eligible individuals, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Arizona SHIP at 800-432-4040 or use the official site to find county counseling. Ask about Medicare options, cost-assistance screening, coverage problems or suspected Medicare fraud. Appointment availability varies.

**Important Information to Know**
SHIP counselors explain options and provide objective counseling; they do not sell insurance plans and cannot guarantee plan acceptance, provider network participation or approval for financial assistance.

resources.name: Archwood Community Resource & Empowerment Strategies · Justice Reinvestment Initiative
resources.description: Archwood Community Resource & Empowerment Strategies was identified in a 2025 ADHS Justice Reinvestment award summary for a justice-impacted entrepreneurship, mentorship, financial-literacy, legal, wellness, rights-restoration and resource-connection initiative in Maricopa County.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The grant summary describes business training, peer mentorship by justice-involved facilitators, financial literacy, legal and wellness support, rights restoration clinics and resource connection for justice-impacted people.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Current program name, grant implementation status, intake route, Mesa-area access and eligibility criteria are unresolved.

**Population Served**
Justice-impacted individuals in Maricopa County, according to the submitted ADHS award-summary evidence.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Archwood website to look for current contact or program announcements. No reliable phone, address or intake route was established in this record.

**Important Information to Know**
Do not treat this as a ready referral until an administrator confirms the program is operating and how clients enroll. It remains a useful lead because the service concept directly matches reentry barriers.
resources.resolutionReason: Needs administrator resolution: current program identity, operating status, intake route and Mesa/Maricopa access could not be established from the assigned evidence.

resources.name: Disabled American Veterans - National Service Office at Phoenix VA Regional Office
resources.description: Disabled American Veterans Department of Arizona National Service Officers are accredited representatives who help veterans and families prepare, present and prosecute claims for VA compensation, pension and other benefits.
resources.address: 3333 N Central Ave, Suite 1053, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Accredited DAV National Service Officer representation for veterans and families pursuing VA compensation, pension and other benefits. NSOs prepare, present and prosecute claims before VA and other government entities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Veterans and eligible family members pursuing VA benefits may contact DAV. Specific representation depends on the claim, documentation and DAV/VA procedures.

**Population Served**
Arizona veterans and their families, including Mesa and Maricopa County veterans needing accredited VA claims representation.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Phoenix DAV NSO office at 602-627-3286 or email DAV.VBAPHO@VA.GOV. The submitted Phoenix VA Regional Office address is 3333 N Central Ave, Suite 1053; confirm appointment and entry instructions before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
This is the accredited NSO route, distinct from local DAV Chapter 8 walk-in/appointment help. It is not general civil legal aid or court representation.

resources.name: Mountain Park Health Center - Pregnancy and Women’s Health Care
resources.description: Federally qualified community health center network offering women's health and pregnancy care, including prenatal care, high-risk pregnancy team support, behavioral health, dietitian and pharmacist support, pediatrics/newborn planning, postpartum information, tele-visits, AHCCCS access, and clinic locations across Phoenix metro including Tempe.
resources.address: East Valley option: Tempe Clinic, 1840 E Broadway Rd, Tempe, AZ 85282; confirm the required service location
resources.hours: Hours vary by clinic; locations page says clinics are open Monday-Friday and some Saturdays/evenings.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Pregnancy and women's health care with a care team that can include a doctor or nurse practitioner, pharmacist, behavioral health consultant, and dietitian. Services include prenatal care, high-risk pregnancy support, pregnancy education, pediatric/newborn planning, postpartum guidance, tele-visits, and help coordinating delivery.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Patients needing pregnancy, postpartum, women’s health or pediatric care may call to schedule. Sliding-fee discounts depend on household income and size and can help uninsured/underinsured people or those with limited coverage. Eligibility staff can assist with AHCCCS; confirm plan acceptance and screening documents.

**Population Served**
Pregnant people, postpartum patients, newborns, children, and families in the Phoenix metro area, including Mesa clients who can travel to Tempe or another Mountain Park clinic.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Mountain Park Health 24/7 at 602-243-7277 to schedule or ask about the closest pregnancy-care site. The closest listed East Valley clinic is Tempe Clinic, 1840 E. Broadway Rd., Tempe, AZ 85282. Hours vary by clinic. Request Spanish interpretation when scheduling.

**Important Information to Know**
No Mesa clinic is established in the reviewed location list. Tempe is an East Valley option, but confirm it offers the needed prenatal/specialty service, delivery arrangements, appointment availability and tele-visit options. A sliding-fee discount is not a guarantee of free care.

resources.name: AZCEND - Interfaith Homeless Emergency Lodging Program (I-HELP)
resources.description: AZCEND I-HELP provides nightly shelter, meals, showers, case management, job help, medical referrals, bus passes, benefits connection and housing assistance for adults experiencing homelessness in Chandler and the East Valley.
resources.address: 345 S California St, Chandler, AZ 85225
resources.hours: Call for I-HELP bed availability and an interview appointment. New guests must complete an interview before entering I-HELP.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Safe nightly shelter, hot meals, warm showers, one-on-one personal assistance, job placement, medical referrals, bus passes, SNAP/AHCCCS benefits connection, housing assistance and case management.

**Eligibility Requirements**
I-HELP is for adults experiencing homelessness. All new guests must complete an interview before entering and should call for bed availability and to schedule an appointment.

**Population Served**
Adults experiencing homelessness in Chandler and the East Valley. Mesa residents should ask AZCEND directly whether they can be served or should use a Mesa access point instead.

**How to Best Connect**
Call AZCEND at 480-963-1423 ext. 112 for I-HELP availability and an interview. The main office is 345 S California Street, Chandler; obtain instructions before travelling to the office or any rotating overnight site.

**Important Information to Know**
This is Chandler-based emergency lodging, not a Mesa walk-in shelter or motel voucher. Confirm Mesa access and transport; an interview is not a bed guarantee. Participant meals, bus passes and other supports do not establish public walk-in aid or Mesa eligibility for AZCEND’s separate CAP funds.

resources.name: Maricopa County Assessor's Office - Disabled Veteran and Surviving Spouse Property Tax Personal Exemptions
resources.description: The Maricopa County Assessor administers disabled veteran and surviving-spouse property-tax personal exemptions, including disability-percentage exemptions and 100% service-connected veteran primary-residence exemptions when requirements are met.
resources.address: 301 West Jefferson Street, 2nd Floor, Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.hours: Public Assistance Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Personal exemption applications for disabled veterans and qualifying surviving spouses. Current Assessor guidance describes exemptions based on veteran disability percentage and a full primary-residence exemption for veterans rated 100% service-connected when requirements are met.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Use the rules for the tax year being claimed. For 2026, personal exemptions retain income and residency requirements; the listed household limits are $39,865 without children under 18 and $47,826 with children under 18 or qualifying disabled children, with stated income exclusions. The Assessor announces removal of income limits for disabled-veteran/surviving-spouse exemptions beginning tax year 2027, plus expanded 100%-disability/TDIU and surviving-spouse provisions. Ownership, residence, VA documentation and approval still matter.

**Population Served**
Qualifying disabled veterans and surviving spouses who own property in Maricopa County, including Mesa homeowners.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Assessor Valuation Relief page and current Personal Exemption application. Call 602-506-3406, or visit 301 W. Jefferson St., 2nd Floor, Phoenix during public-assistance hours.

**Important Information to Know**
Do not apply 2027 provisions to a 2026 claim. The general current-year deadline is February 28, or September 1 with an approved deadline waiver; those 2026 dates have passed. Ask about the appropriate 2027 application or any remaining legal option. A qualifying full primary-residence exemption requires Assessor approval; other exemption and senior-freeze programmes have different rules.

resources.name: Tempe Community Action Agency - I-HELP Emergency Shelter
resources.description: Tempe Community Action Agency's I-HELP provides emergency overnight shelter for adults experiencing homelessness, plus evening meals, showers, laundry, intensive case management, resource navigation, and daytime access to computers, phones, employment help, food bags and hydration.
resources.address: 2146 E Apache Blvd, Tempe, AZ 85281
resources.hours: Intakes Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-10:00 AM at 2146 E Apache Blvd. Call the services-site front desk for current instructions and capacity.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency overnight sleeping space, evening meals, showers, laundry, intensive case management and resource navigation. During daytime operating hours, I-HELP participants and the extended community may use computers and phones, employment assistance through TCAA's Financial Success Center, emergency to-go food bags and hydration.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adults experiencing homelessness may seek intake. Public information does not guarantee admission, and Mesa clients should confirm fit, capacity and any residency or referral expectations at intake or by phone.

**Population Served**
Adults experiencing homelessness in Tempe and the East Valley, including Mesa adults when current program rules and capacity allow.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to the TCAA services site at 2146 E Apache Blvd in Tempe for intake Monday-Friday from 8:00 AM to 10:00 AM, or call 480-422-8922 ext. 5882 before travel. Ask what to bring and whether beds or daytime services are available.

**Important Information to Know**
This is TCAA’s Tempe programme, separate from other cities’ I-HELP services. Call before travelling from Mesa to confirm geographic fit, required documents and capacity. Daytime community resources do not guarantee overnight admission or a bed.

resources.name: Mi Familia Vota - Arizona - Citizenship application assistance and Know Your Rights training
resources.description: Mi Familia en Accion / Mi Familia Vota provides citizenship information and support for eligible lawful permanent residents, plus Know Your Rights education for immigrant communities; public pages should be checked for current sessions before referral.
resources.address: 3030 N Central Ave, Suite 900, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.hours: No ongoing office hours for citizenship help are posted; current sessions and clinics should be confirmed online or by phone.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Citizenship information sessions, naturalization support, connection to pro bono legal consultation and N-400 review through trusted legal professionals, and Know Your Rights education for immigrant community members.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Citizenship support is aimed at eligible lawful permanent residents, particularly people of Latin American origin. Know Your Rights materials are educational and not legal advice.

**Population Served**
Arizona immigrant and Latino communities, including Phoenix and Maricopa County residents who can attend current sessions or use online resources.

**How to Best Connect**
Check the Mi Familia en Accion citizenship and Know Your Rights pages for current sessions and resources, and call the Arizona office number, 602-263-2030, to confirm appointment availability and scope before sending a client.

**Important Information to Know**
The current public Know Your Rights page states that Mi Familia en Accion and Mi Familia Vota are not legal experts and community members should contact a lawyer for legal advice. A current search result showed no upcoming citizenship events at the time checked, so confirm before referral.

resources.name: Lifeology AZ - Safe Place, Emergency Youth Shelter and Transitional Housing
resources.description: Lifeology AZ is the National Safe Place lead agency for Maricopa County and operates youth crisis response, Safe Place connection, a Basic Center Program emergency youth shelter, shared transitional housing and workforce supports. Youth can use Safe Place sites, text support, the national hotline, or Lifeology's phone.
resources.hours: Safe Place help is described as 24/7. Emergency shelter and program intake should be confirmed by phone at 602-349-8708 or through Safe Place access.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Safe Place crisis connection, emergency youth shelter, meals, basic needs, counseling, family support, case management, crisis intervention, life-skills support, family reunification when appropriate, shared transitional housing for young adults, workforce readiness and connection to education/employment resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Lifeology describes Safe Place immediate help for youth ages 14-22. Its Basic Center Program emergency shelter provides up to 21 days of shelter and supportive services for youth ages 14-17 experiencing homelessness, family conflict, or unsafe living situations. Shared transitional housing is for young adults ages 18-23.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County youth in crisis, runaway youth, youth experiencing homelessness, and young adults needing a path toward housing stability.

**How to Best Connect**
For Safe Place help, text SAFE and the youth’s location to 44357, use a site displaying the Safe Place sign, or call 888-290-7233. For Lifeology programme intake call 602-349-8708 or email info@lifeologyaz.org. Call 911 for immediate danger; obtain placement and travel instructions from staff.

**Important Information to Know**
Safe Place is listed for ages 14–22, Basic Center shelter for ages 14–17 with stays up to 21 days, and shared transitional housing for ages 18–23. Consent, referral and capacity differ by programme. Contact starts screening, not a guaranteed bed or unscreened walk-in placement.

resources.name: Maricopa County Department of Public Health and Cartwheel - Countywide School-Based Telemental Health Initiative
resources.description: Maricopa County Department of Public Health is contracting with Cartwheel for a countywide 2026-2027 school-based telemental-health initiative so participating K-12 schools can refer students to therapy, family support, parent coaching, and psychiatric care.
resources.hours: Access depends on participating schools and school referral. Cartwheel describes school referral followed by care-coordinator outreach, then virtual appointments.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
School-based telehealth pathway for evidence-based therapy, family support, parent coaching, psychiatric care, care coordination, medication management when appropriate, and parent guidance for students referred by participating K-12 schools.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Access is through participating Maricopa County K-12 schools, voluntary participation, and parental consent. Cartwheel bills family insurance; the county announcement says county funds supplement remaining costs so families are not denied due to inability to pay.

**Population Served**
Students and families at participating K-12 schools in Maricopa County, with a focus on medically underserved areas and communities facing long waits or transportation barriers.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the student’s school counselor or support team whether the school participates in the 2026–27 county Cartwheel partnership and how to request a referral. Parent or guardian consent is required.

**Important Information to Know**
The program is school-referred, not a general public self-referral service. Confirm current school participation, insurance and how the county-funded portion applies. Media contacts do not schedule care.

resources.name: Casa de Amor Community Resource Center - Clothing Assistance
resources.description: Casa de Amor Community Resource Center in Mesa provides direct clothing assistance during Monday-Wednesday morning hours, along with counseling, pregnancy and family resources, SNAP services and supplemental food boxes.
resources.address: 819 S. MacDonald, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Monday-Wednesday 9:00 AM-11:00 AM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Direct clothing assistance, counseling, pregnancy and family resources, SNAP services and supplemental food boxes at a Mesa Community Resource Center.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page does not list detailed clothing eligibility, documents, quantity limits or visit frequency. Call or visit during service hours to ask what identification or household information is needed.

**Population Served**
Mesa and nearby East Valley households seeking clothing, food boxes, pregnancy resources or family resource-center help.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-464-2877 or visit 819 S. MacDonald during Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday 9:00 AM-11:00 AM service hours. Arrive early because the service window is short.

**Important Information to Know**
Goods depend on current stock. The official page supports clothing as a direct service but does not guarantee sizes, quantities or same-day availability.

resources.name: HRSA — Find a Health Center
resources.description: Find community health centers and their locations through the federal HRSA directory.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Find community health centers and their locations through the federal HRSA directory.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The locator is public; each health center confirms services, appointments and fee-discount documentation.

**Population Served**
People seeking a community health center near a U.S. address or ZIP code, including Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Search the official locator, then contact the chosen health-center site directly.

**Important Information to Know**
Not every location offers dental, pharmacy or behavioral care; a locator result is not an appointment or guarantee of free treatment.

resources.name: Maricopa Community Colleges · Scholarship Manager Portal and One-to-One Scholarship Advising
resources.description: Maricopa Community Colleges Scholarship Manager Portal is the districtwide application portal for current and prospective Maricopa students to apply for scholarships, with one-on-one scholarship coordinator sessions for application and essay help.
resources.hours: Online portal; scholarship coordinator appointments are scheduled online.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
District and foundation scholarship application access, financial support opportunities for academic goals, student login for applications, donor scholarship information, and one-on-one sessions with scholarship coordinators for help with the online application, scholarship essay tips, and scholarship questions.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Current and prospective Maricopa Community College students are encouraged to apply. Eligibility, deadlines, award amounts, and required materials vary by scholarship.

**Population Served**
Current and prospective students at Maricopa Community Colleges, including Mesa Community College students who need help paying for education.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Scholarship Manager Portal student login to apply. If help is needed, schedule a one-on-one session with a scholarship coordinator through the link on the portal.

**Important Information to Know**
The portal states 2026-2027 scholarship applications are open. Scholarships are gifts that do not need to be repaid, but awards are competitive or eligibility-specific and not guaranteed.

resources.name: House of Refuge - Donation Center Food Bank
resources.description: House of Refuge operates a certified Arizona food bank at its East Mesa Donation Center with essentials available without questions or forms.
resources.address: 6858 E Ursula Ave, Mesa, AZ 85212
resources.hours: Food page lists Monday and Friday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m., closed weekends. Donation page lists Monday–Friday; call to confirm Tuesday–Thursday food pickup.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Certified food bank providing food essentials through the House of Refuge Donation Center.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page says the food bank is open to everyone, with no questions asked and no forms to fill out.

**Population Served**
Community members and families needing food in East Mesa; the page does not limit food-bank access to House of Refuge housing residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit 6858 E. Ursula Ave., Mesa, during confirmed food-bank hours. The food-page contact is 480-988-9395; the donation page also lists 623-244-4018. Administration: 480-988-9242.

**Important Information to Know**
Public food access is separate from resident-only furniture/clothing shopping and housing screening. Current pages agree weekends are closed but describe weekdays differently; confirm the intended pickup day, holidays and stock before travel.

resources.name: Jewish Family & Children's Service - Helping Hands Jewish Emergency Financial Assistance
resources.description: Jewish Family & Children's Service Helping Hands provides short-term emergency financial relief to Jewish individuals and families in Maricopa County after job loss, illness, personal loss or other unforeseen hardship.
resources.address: 4747 N 7th St, Suite 100, Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Helping Hands is an emergency assistance fund that provides short-term financial relief to Jewish individuals and families in Maricopa County who are struggling to meet basic needs after unexpected hardship.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public page identifies the service for Jewish individuals and families in Maricopa County facing hardships such as job loss, illness, personal loss or other unforeseen financial challenges. JFCS does not publish detailed bill types, document rules, payment method or fund limits on the page.

**Population Served**
Jewish individuals and families in Maricopa County who need short-term help with basic needs after a financial hardship.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-762-7319 for more information. The listed office address is 4747 North 7th Street, Suite 100, Phoenix, AZ 85014.

**Important Information to Know**
Assistance depends on program review and available funds. The public page does not specify whether payment is made to vendors or clients, which expenses are covered, or what documents are required; callers should ask before relying on it for an urgent deadline.

resources.name: Brain Injury Alliance of Arizona - Survivor Resource Referral and Support Groups
resources.description: Brain Injury Alliance of Arizona provides a statewide helpline, survivor resource referral, support groups, education and assistance requests for people affected by brain injury and their caregivers.
resources.address: 5025 E. Washington St., Suite 108, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: Call or text for current support group schedules and response times.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Statewide helpline, brain-injury resource facilitation/referral, survivor and caregiver support groups, education and peer connections. Ask about transportation-assistance requests and other specific supports; criteria and availability are programme-specific.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services focus on brain injury survivors, families, caregivers and professionals. Specific assistance requests, groups or events may have separate registration and availability limits.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents affected by brain injury, including Mesa and Maricopa County survivors, caregivers and family members.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the helpline at 888-500-9165, call the office at 602-508-8024, text 520-310-3301 or email info@biaaz.org. The Phoenix survivor/caregiver group listed on the official page meets at Ability360, 5025 E. Washington Street.

**Important Information to Know**
This is navigation, education and community/peer support, not emergency medical treatment. Confirm the exact group date, site, registration and any transport-assistance criteria; the Ability360 group location does not imply walk-in clinical care.

resources.name: VA Phoenix Beneficiary Travel Self Service System and Travel Reimbursement
resources.description: VA Phoenix beneficiary travel pathway lets eligible veterans and caregivers submit and track reimbursement claims for travel to VA-approved care using BTSSS or paper VA Form 10-3542.
resources.hours: BTSSS online access is available anytime; telephone assistance is on weekdays. Confirm current call-center hours and time zone.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Beneficiary Travel Self Service System lets eligible veterans and caregivers submit and track travel reimbursement claims for VA-approved care. Paper VA Form 10-3542 remains available for people who do not use the online system.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Possible eligibility includes a service-connected rating of 30% or more, travel for a service-connected condition, VA pension or low income, travel for a compensation/pension exam, or specified disabilities such as vision impairment, spinal cord injury/disorder, double or multiple amputation, or enrollment in VA Rehab Programs.

**Population Served**
Eligible veterans and caregivers using VA-approved care through VA Phoenix or other VA facilities.

**How to Best Connect**
Use BTSSS through AccessVA with ID.me or Login.gov, or paper VA Form 10-3542. Phoenix travel assistance: 602-277-5551 ext. 7650; national beneficiary-travel help: 855-574-7292. Confirm current call hours/time zone.

**Important Information to Know**
Submit a claim for each appointment within 30 days; late claims are usually denied, though exceptions may apply. Set up travel direct deposit separately and keep the claim profile current. Deductibles and prior approval for special transportation modes may apply. Eligibility and reimbursement depend on the trip; this does not arrange or fund an upfront ride automatically.

resources.name: Soberman's Estate
resources.description: State-licensed residential treatment center in Cave Creek providing individualized substance-use and co-occurring disorder treatment for adult men, with nursing coverage and family/alumni support.
resources.address: 3010 E Cloud Rd, Cave Creek, AZ 85331
resources.hours: Residential program; call admissions for consultation and availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Soberman's Estate is a residential behavioral-health and addiction treatment center for adult men, providing substance-use and co-occurring disorder treatment, individual therapy, nursing support, family support, alumni support, and recovery/wellness programming.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is gender-specific for adult men. Admission requires consultation and clinical/payment screening for residential treatment fit.

**Population Served**
Adult men experiencing alcoholism, substance-use disorders, process addictions, trauma, anxiety, stress, depression, or other co-occurring issues.

**How to Best Connect**
Call admissions at 480-351-6749 for a confidential consultation. The estate address is 3010 E Cloud Rd, Cave Creek, AZ 85331; mailing address is 100 Easy St. #5167, Carefree, AZ 85377.

**Important Information to Know**
The provider describes a private, small residential setting and The Joint Commission lists residential and outpatient levels of care. Confirm cost, insurance/payment, bed availability, and exact level of care before referral.

resources.name: AZ ABLE - Disability Savings Accounts
resources.description: AZ ABLE provides tax-advantaged disability savings and investment accounts for eligible Arizona residents so money can be saved for qualified disability expenses while protecting certain needs-based benefits.
resources.hours: Customer service phone is listed Monday-Friday 7 AM-6 PM Mountain Time; website chat may be available.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
AZ ABLE provides STABLE accounts for qualified disability expenses, including living expenses, education, housing, transportation, employment supports, assistive technology, health and wellness, legal fees, and related disability needs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The beneficiary must be an Arizona resident with a qualifying disability that began before the program's current age-of-onset limit, and must meet SSI/SSDI disability or physician-certification rules.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents with qualifying disabilities and authorized legal representatives or family members helping manage savings for a person with a disability.

**How to Best Connect**
Start at az-able.com, use the eligibility information and enrollment tools, or call 1-800-439-1653 for help. For AZ ABLE presentations, email az-able@azdes.gov.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a savings and investment account, not a grant or emergency cash program. Non-qualified withdrawals, contribution limits, investment risk, fees, and SSI rules should be reviewed before opening an account.

resources.name: Thomas Suites Campus of Care - Transitional Living for People Reentering Society
resources.description: Thomas Suites Campus of Care is a reentry transitional-living lead whose official site describes temporary supportive housing for men and women reentering society from incarceration, but current operation and safe referral status need administrator resolution because public evidence conflicts.
resources.address: 2333 E Thomas Road, Phoenix, AZ 85016
resources.hours: Official site lists a 24/7 reception desk, but current operating status and admissions hours must be confirmed before referral.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The official Thomas Suites site describes transitional living and supportive temporary housing for men and women reentering society from incarceration, with suites, meals, laundry, Wi-Fi, recreational amenities, 24/7 reception, and an environment focused on sobriety, personal growth, community, and reintegration.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official site does not publish admissions criteria, referral requirements, supervision requirements, costs, length of stay, background restrictions, or whether residents must be referred by corrections, parole, probation, or another agency.

**Population Served**
The official site describes serving men and women reentering society from incarceration. Mesa or Maricopa County eligibility is not specifically stated, but the facility address is in Phoenix.

**How to Best Connect**
Do not send a client directly until current operation is resolved. The official site lists 2333 E Thomas Road, Phoenix, AZ 85016 and 602-957-1910. If administrators decide to pursue the lead, first confirm whether Thomas Suites is operating, accepting residents, and legally able to provide the represented service.

**Important Information to Know**
There is a consequential conflict: the official website describes an active reentry transitional-living facility, but a 2025 FOX 10 report said AZDHS indicated Thomas Suites had shut down and that a Motel 6 appeared to be taking its place after concerns about an unlicensed health-care operation. The official site footer also states it was recovered by the free version of Wayback Downloader. Current identity, operation, licensing/service scope, and admissions access are not reliable enough for referral without administrator confirmation.
resources.resolutionReason: Needs resolution: targeted checks found an official site with address and phone describing reentry transitional living, but current-status evidence materially conflicts, including a news report attributing closure information to AZDHS and the official site's Wayback-recovered footer. This prevents responsible referral until current operation, legal service scope, and admissions route are confirmed.

resources.name: Arizona Recreation Center for the Handicapped (ARCH) - Day Treatment, Drop-In, ARCHKids and Respite Recreation
resources.description: ARCH offers Phoenix-based adaptive recreation, adult day treatment, private-pay adult drop-in, ARCHKids programming and respite-supported outings for people with disabilities.
resources.address: 1550 W. Colter Street, Phoenix, AZ 85015
resources.hours: Call for program schedules, tour availability and intake; exact program hours vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
ARCH provides Day Treatment for Adults, adult Drop-In recreation, ARCHKids programming, Adventure Club/respite-supported recreation and facility-based adaptive recreation opportunities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
DTA participants must no longer be attending high school, have a DDD Coordinator and be state-funded for a day program. Drop-In participants must not require direct 1:1 supervision and must pay the listed fee. ARCHKids may be state funded or private pay. Adventure Club participants needing 1:1 support must provide an attendant or use available respite hours.

**Population Served**
Children, youth and adults with developmental or other disabilities who can practically access ARCH's Phoenix campus from Mesa or elsewhere in the Valley.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-230-2226, email info@archaz.org, complete the online Participant Information Form, or contact ARCH to arrange a tour and discuss needs.

**Important Information to Know**
This is Phoenix-based, so transportation and schedule fit should be confirmed. Drop-In fees were listed as $40 per month or $2 per day on the page reviewed. DDD authorization, private pay, supervision needs and capacity affect access.

resources.name: City of Scottsdale - Scottsdale Family Advocacy Center
resources.description: Scottsdale Family Advocacy Center co-locates professionals for sensitive cases including child abuse, domestic violence and sexual assault, with crisis intervention, forensic nurses, child safety, police investigation and victim support resources.
resources.address: 10225 E Via Linda, Scottsdale, AZ 85258
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 7:00 AM-7:00 PM; closed Saturday, Sunday and city holidays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Family advocacy center services for sensitive cases, including domestic violence and sexual assault, with co-located forensic nurses, child safety investigators, crisis intervention specialists, police investigators, interview rooms, victim-support spaces, resource guidance and referrals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The center serves Scottsdale, Fountain Hills, Paradise Valley, Cave Creek, Carefree, Tempe and county jurisdictions in the northeast Valley. Mesa clients should use this mainly when the case or safest access point is in those jurisdictions.

**Population Served**
Domestic-violence, sexual-assault, child-abuse and other sensitive-case victims in Scottsdale and listed northeast Valley/county jurisdictions.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Family Advocacy Center at 480-312-6300. For emergencies call 911; for Scottsdale Police non-emergency call 480-312-5000; for Police Crisis Intervention Specialists call 480-312-5055.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not Mesa-specific. Use it as a reserve option for northeast Valley or Scottsdale-connected incidents and confirm fit before sending a client in person.

resources.name: Sojourner Center Emergency Shelter, Transitional Housing and Community Outreach
resources.description: Sojourner Center provides emergency shelter, transitional support, community outreach, case management, safety planning, child and youth services, pet companion services, resource referrals, and lay legal support for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and human trafficking.
resources.address: Mail only: PO Box 20156, Phoenix, AZ 85036; shelter location is confidential
resources.hours: 24-hour shelter hotline: 602-244-0089. Community Outreach direct line is listed during business hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency shelter with stays described up to 120 days, 24-hour staff, meals, case management, child/youth support, resource items, groups, pet companion services and lay legal support. Transitional housing offers support for up to two years subject to screening. Community Outreach provides mobile case management, safety planning, groups, referrals and protective-order/court support for survivors who do not need shelter.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people impacted by domestic violence, sexual assault, or human trafficking. Shelter, transitional supports, and outreach depend on safety needs, screening, and availability.

**Population Served**
Survivors and families in Greater Phoenix and Maricopa County, including Mesa referrals, people still living with an abuser, survivors not seeking shelter, and survivors with children or pets.

**How to Best Connect**
For immediate shelter or safety help, call the 24-hour hotline at 602-244-0089. For non-emergency general contact, call 602-244-0997. For Community Outreach, call 602-244-0089 during business hours or email sojocommunityoutreach@jfcsaz.onmicrosoft.com.

**Important Information to Know**
Use hotline/programme directions, not a street address or the mailing box. Confirm Mesa outreach coverage, current beds, transitional placement and pet arrangements; a companion shelter does not mean every pet stays in the survivor’s room. Lengths of stay are programme limits, not guaranteed placements.

resources.name: Community Legal Services - Low Income Taxpayer Clinic
resources.description: Community Legal Services' Low Income Taxpayer Clinic helps eligible taxpayers with IRS-related controversies, taxpayer rights education, economic-hardship requests and related tax debt issues; it does not prepare tax returns.
resources.address: 305 S. 2nd Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.hours: CLS intake calls are generally completed Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-2:00 PM; call to confirm tax-program availability.
