resources.description: Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community Health & Human Services has evidence of a Behavioral Health Re-Entry Counselor / STEP IOP re-entry service role providing counseling, group therapy, intake assessment and transition planning for people reentering the community. Public client eligibility and intake route for this specific component remain unresolved.
resources.address: 10005 E. Osborn Rd., Scottsdale, AZ
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The official job posting describes individual counseling for behavioral health, trauma, substance use and reentry readiness; STEP IOP re-entry group therapy; intake assessments; treatment planning; comprehensive reentry plans covering housing, employment, medical/behavioral-health continuity, cultural/community resources and probation requirements; release-planning coordination; coping skills; decision-making strategies; prosocial behaviors and relapse-prevention tools.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Unresolved for clients. The service appears connected to SRPMIC Health & Human Services Adult and Family Services and may be limited to SRPMIC community members, eligible Native/tribal patients or specific outpatient/corrections referrals.

**Population Served**
Potentially SRPMIC community members or eligible Native/tribal clients reentering the community from incarceration or outpatient counseling systems near Scottsdale/Tempe/Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Administrators should confirm through SRPMIC Health & Human Services Behavioral Health Services before referral. Prior official SRPMIC behavioral-health evidence lists outpatient mental-health/substance-use services at 480-278-7742 ext. 4201 and residential substance-abuse services at 480-362-5640.

**Important Information to Know**
This is retained as a useful unresolved lead because the evidence is from an official current job posting rather than a client-facing intake page. The remaining obstacle is public eligibility and access route, not whether the role exists.
resources.resolutionReason: Official SRPMIC job posting confirms the reentry counselor/STEP IOP service functions, location and department. Client-facing eligibility and intake for this specific reentry component remain unresolved, so administrator confirmation is needed.

resources.name: UMOM New Day Centers / Helping Hands Housing Services - Permanent Affordable Housing Communities
resources.description: UMOM's Helping Hands Housing Services develops permanent affordable housing communities in Maricopa County; properties are managed by Biltmore Properties and UMOM program participants do not receive tenancy preference.
resources.address: 3333 E Van Buren St, Phoenix, AZ 85008
resources.hours: Use property-specific leasing contacts through Biltmore Properties; UMOM does not list a single common application or vacancy line.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Permanent affordable housing communities developed by UMOM's subsidiary Helping Hands Housing Services, including family, senior, veteran-priority and supportive affordable communities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility and application requirements are property-specific. UMOM states program participants may apply for tenancy at UMOM-built properties but receive no preferential treatment, and UMOM cannot financially subsidize tenancy in those properties.

**Population Served**
Low-income renters seeking affordable housing in Phoenix and Maricopa County, including some communities for seniors, veterans or supportive-housing needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Review the UMOM affordable housing portfolio and follow the property-specific leasing route through Biltmore Properties, Inc. Call UMOM at 602-275-7852 for general direction if the property route is unclear.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not an emergency shelter, coordinated-entry intake or single vacancy list. Vacancies, rents, waitlists and application steps must be checked with each property manager.

resources.name: A New Leaf - East Valley Men's Center
resources.description: A New Leaf East Valley Men's Center is a 104-bed Mesa shelter for men experiencing homelessness, offering a bed, storage, housing planning, employment assistance, transportation assistance and substance-use support-group referrals.
resources.address: 2345 N Country Club Dr, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Pre-screen required online. Phone intakes are not being taken because of staff limitations and community need.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency shelter for men, a bed and personal storage during the stay, permanent-housing planning, onsite workforce help with resumes, references and interviews, transportation assistance and referrals to substance-use support groups.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For men experiencing homelessness in Arizona/East Valley who complete the required pre-screen and meet program fit. Children under 18 are not allowed on site.

**Population Served**
Men experiencing homelessness, especially those able to access the Mesa shelter and participate in housing and employment planning.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the pre-screen linked on the East Valley Men's Center page. The page says phone intakes are not being taken; individuals may call 877-211-8661 for shelter placement guidance, but the pre-screen is the first step for this program.

**Important Information to Know**
Complete the prescreen before seeking placement; phone intakes are not being taken and a bed is not guaranteed. Workforce and transportation help are shelter-connected. Recovery help is referral to support groups, not detox, medication treatment or residential addiction treatment.

resources.name: PCs for People — Affordable computers and mobile internet
resources.description: PCs for People offers eligibility-based low-cost prepaid 4G/5G internet and hotspot options, with no contracts or credit checks, for customers who meet income or public-benefit rules and have coverage.
resources.hours: Order online or by phone; confirm support hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
PCs for People offers affordable computers and prepaid mobile internet/hotspot options. Equipment can be ordered remotely for shipping; an Arizona storefront is not required. Internet plans are advertised without credit checks or contracts, with an upfront device cost.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Households qualify through an accepted income-based government benefit, income below 200% of federal poverty guidelines, or income at or below 60% of area median income. Photo identification and current income/benefit documentation are required; citizenship proof is not required. Organizations should ask about their separate purchasing eligibility.

**Population Served**
Income-eligible households that need low-cost internet service at home or on the go, including people in Mesa or Maricopa County where cellular coverage is adequate.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the PCs for People website to review computer options, shipping and internet coverage, or call 877-450-8585. Have ID and eligibility documentation ready. Email support@pcsforpeople.org with documentation questions.

**Important Information to Know**
Check cellular coverage at the actual use location and confirm equipment, shipping and prepaid service costs. Devices may not be resold or redistributed to unqualified recipients. The former Affordable Connectivity Program is not an available benefit.

resources.name: A New Leaf / Homeward Bound - Current Family Shelter or Thunderbird Apartments Status Unresolved
resources.description: Homeward Bound was acquired by A New Leaf, and recent A New Leaf materials describe the former Homeward Bound property as renamed Thunderbird Apartments. Earlier materials describe family shelter and wraparound supports, but current routine shelter intake and housing model need administrator resolution.
resources.address: 2302 W Colter St, Phoenix, AZ 85015
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Historically, Homeward Bound provided apartment-like shelter and wraparound services for families experiencing homelessness, including employment, child care, food/basic-needs and youth supports. A New Leaf acquired Homeward Bound and recent A New Leaf materials say the property long known as Homeward Bound is now renamed Thunderbird Apartments.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Current eligibility is unresolved. Earlier materials focused on families facing homelessness, but current A New Leaf materials suggest a transition toward apartments/affordable housing, so shelter eligibility and referral path should not be assumed.

**Population Served**
Useful unresolved lead for families experiencing homelessness or housing instability in the Phoenix metro area; current population served at the former Homeward Bound property needs confirmation.

**How to Best Connect**
Do not rely on the old Homeward Bound website, which redirects to A New Leaf. Contact A New Leaf or 2-1-1 Arizona for current Homeward Bound/Thunderbird Apartments status and whether any family shelter, transitional housing or affordable-housing application route remains available.

**Important Information to Know**
This record is needs-resolution because current identity and access conflict with older shelter descriptions. The official Homeward Bound domain now redirects to A New Leaf, and A New Leaf announced a 2026 name change to Thunderbird Apartments. Administrators should confirm whether the old family shelter program still operates, has changed, or has been replaced.
resources.resolutionReason: Retained as needs-resolution because official A New Leaf evidence confirms acquisition and later renaming of the former Homeward Bound property, creating a consequential conflict with the submitted family shelter/wraparound description and no clear current intake route.

resources.name: West Valley Veteran Success Center
resources.description: West Valley Veteran Success Center is a Be Connected/City of Surprise partnered walk-in access hub where service members, veterans and family members can connect with navigators, AmeriCorps support, ADVS benefits counselor appointments and referrals for multiple needs.
resources.address: 12425 W. Bell Road, Suite 124, Surprise, AZ 85378
resources.hours: Walk-in during business hours; VBC sessions are by appointment only.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The center offers walk-in access to resources and support, a part-time Be Connected navigator, a full-time AmeriCorps member, benefits/service navigation, ADVS Veteran Benefits Counselor appointments, and connections to career navigation, education programs, family support, financial support referrals, food security, healthcare resources, housing solutions, rent assistance and utility assistance.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page describes services for service members, veterans and family members. ADVS Veteran Benefits Counselor sessions are by appointment only and cannot serve walk-ins.

**Population Served**
Service members, veterans and family members in the West Valley and Maricopa County; statewide phone support remains available through Be Connected.

**How to Best Connect**
Walk in during business hours at 12425 W. Bell Road, Suite 124, Surprise, AZ 85378, call 623-222-1600, or call Be Connected at 866-4AZ-VETS (866-429-8387). To schedule the onsite VBC, call the VBC call center at 602-535-1215.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a partnered access hub, so some services are onsite and others are referral-only. The location is in Surprise, not Mesa; for Mesa clients, consider whether distance makes a phone-based Be Connected route more practical.

resources.name: NAMI Valley of the Sun - Peer and Family Mental-Health Support Groups and Education
resources.description: NAMI Valley of the Sun offers non-clinical peer and family mental-health support, education, advocacy, and programs for adults living with mental-health conditions and for family members, caregivers, and supporters in Maricopa County, with virtual and in-person event options.
resources.address: 5025 E Washington St, Suite 112, Phoenix, AZ 85034; events may be virtual or at community locations
resources.hours: Meeting times vary by group and event calendar. Check the NAMI directory or affiliate calendar before attending.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free or low-cost peer-led mental-health support and education programs such as NAMI Connection, NAMI Family Support Group, Family-to-Family, Peer-to-Peer, In Our Own Voice, and related education/advocacy programs. Events may be virtual or in person.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Program audience varies. NAMI Connection is for adults who have experienced symptoms of a mental-health condition. Family Support Groups are for adult family members, significant others, and friends of people with mental-health conditions. Registration rules vary by event.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County residents affected by mental illness, including peers living with mental-health conditions and family members, caregivers, partners, and supporters.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-244-8166, email info@namivos.org, or use the NAMI Valley of the Sun affiliate listing and calendar to find current programs. The office is at 5025 E Washington St, Suite 112, Phoenix, AZ 85034.

**Important Information to Know**
NAMI support and education are not clinical treatment, medication management, emergency dispatch, or clinician referral. For imminent danger or crisis, call or text 988 or use local crisis services.

resources.name: Child Crisis Arizona - Safe Kids Maricopa County Car Seat Safety
resources.description: Child Crisis Arizona leads Safe Kids Maricopa County, offering no-cost virtual car-seat safety classes, no-cost car-seat or booster-seat checks and child injury-prevention education for parents and caregivers.
resources.address: Maricopa County; Child Crisis Arizona lead organization at 424 W. Rio Salado Pkwy, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Class and check schedules vary; view the current schedule or email safekidsmaricopa@childcrisisaz.org for assistance.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Safe Kids Maricopa County offers no-cost virtual car-seat safety classes, no-cost car-seat and booster-seat checks, child injury-prevention education and water-safety education. Families are encouraged to attend a class before scheduling a car-seat or booster-seat check.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Public information does not list income or residency restrictions for classes and checks, but services are focused on Maricopa County families and caregivers. Availability depends on current class and check schedules.

**Population Served**
Parents, caregivers and families with children who need help selecting, installing or using car seats and booster seats safely.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Child Crisis Arizona Safe Kids page to view upcoming classes and car-seat check resources. Email safekidsmaricopa@childcrisisaz.org if no scheduled class works. General Child Crisis Arizona inquiries can go to 480-834-9424. Ask which language options are available for the requested service.

**Important Information to Know**
The official page supports free classes and checks, but does not guarantee free car-seat supply for every family. If a family specifically needs a free or replacement seat, confirm current inventory, eligibility and event details before referral.

resources.name: Mesa Alano Club
resources.description: Mesa recovery community center providing a physical location for recovery meetings and fellowship, with scheduled AA, CA, HA, FA, CoDA and other peer-support meetings.
resources.address: 145 E 1st Ave, Mesa, AZ
resources.hours: Meeting schedule varies by day; posted meetings include early morning, noon, afternoon and evening options.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Alano Club of Mesa provides an environment and physical location for recovery meetings and fellowship. Its posted meeting schedule includes Alcoholics Anonymous, Cocaine Anonymous, Heroin Anonymous, Fentanyl Anonymous, CoDA and other meetings, with open and closed formats.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Meeting-specific eligibility varies. Some meetings are open, some are closed, and some are fellowship-specific. Club membership is optional for supporting the club and is listed separately from meeting attendance.

**Population Served**
People in Mesa seeking recovery meetings, sober fellowship and peer support. The schedule includes a Mesa veterans meeting, men's meeting and GLBT-friendly meeting, but each group controls its own format.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the official meeting schedule before travel. The saved address is 145 E 1st Ave, Mesa, AZ. Confirm meeting time, fellowship, room and whether the meeting is open or closed.

**Important Information to Know**
This is peer/community support, not medical detox, MAT, licensed outpatient treatment, crisis response or housing. The club states it is not affiliated with Alcoholics Anonymous, even though AA and other fellowships meet there.

resources.name: Dental Hearts - Nonprofit Dental Implant Program
resources.description: Dental Hearts is a nonprofit implant dental center in Phoenix offering discounted implant-related treatment, including no-fee sinus lifts and implant surgery, with patients paying discounted costs for prosthetic components placed on implants.
resources.address: 12320 N 32nd St, Suite 2, Phoenix, AZ 85032
resources.hours: Call to schedule and confirm consultation availability; public hours are not listed on the opened page.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Affordable implant dentistry, including implant surgery, sinus lifts, implant overdenture work, extractions and bone grafting services tied to implant treatment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Patients must qualify after a 3D CT scan and consultation and may be treated through a training program. The program is for people who want affordable implant dentistry, including veterans and underserved patients.

**Population Served**
Phoenix and Maricopa County patients who may benefit from dental implants but cannot afford conventional private-practice fees, including veterans and underserved adults.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 623-471-6400 to schedule or ask about consultation, qualification, pricing and current services. Address: 12320 N 32nd St, Suite 2, Phoenix, AZ 85032.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a limited-scope implant program, not routine low-cost dental care. The site states patients pay for what goes on top of implants at discounted rates. It also states no-fee extractions and bone grafting will be offered in September 2026, so current availability should be confirmed.

resources.name: SMC Arizona - MAT Services Clinic and Counseling Services
resources.description: SMC Arizona outpatient opioid treatment program and counseling clinic providing MAT with methadone, Suboxone/buprenorphine, Vivitrol/naltrexone and Brixadi, plus individual, group and family counseling, case management and peer support.
resources.address: 10207 N Scottsdale Rd, Scottsdale, AZ 85258
resources.hours: Appointments available Monday-Friday; exact dosing/intake hours were not listed in the page reviewed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
SMC Arizona is an opiate treatment program with outpatient substance-abuse counseling services. Official services include medication-assisted treatment, group counseling, family groups, individual therapy, counseling, case management, peer support, methadone, Vivitrol, Brixadi and Suboxone services, buprenorphine and naltrexone. The page lists telehealth intake availability and Valley Metro Reduced Fare availability.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are provided to adults 18 and up. SMC says clients must meet ASAM criteria for opioid treatment and that priority admission status is given to pregnant clients. Maintenance services are stated to be accessible regardless of ethnic group identification, physical or mental disability, race, color, national origin, religion, gender, sexual orientation or political affiliation. Insurance providers are listed by logos on the site, but exact accepted plans and self-pay costs must be confirmed.

**Population Served**
Adults age 18 and older with opioid-treatment needs who can use the Scottsdale clinic. Pregnant clients meeting treatment criteria receive priority admission.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-998-HOPE (480-998-4673) or use the Get Help Now route on the official SMC site. Medical and clinical services are provided at 10207 N Scottsdale Rd, Scottsdale, AZ 85258. Ask about telehealth intake, dosing schedule, insurance, pregnant-client priority, and transportation/reduced fare options.

**Important Information to Know**
This entry is for the Scottsdale clinic. Ask about available medication, dosing/intake hours, telehealth, costs, accepted insurance and reduced-fare transport arrangements. It does not establish an active Maricopa Re-Entry Center pop-up.

resources.name: Community Legal Services Volunteer Lawyers Program - HIV/AIDS Law Project
resources.description: Community Legal Services Volunteer Lawyers Program identifies the HIV/AIDS Law Project as a distinct civil legal service offering advice, estate-planning documents, and referrals for Maricopa County residents living with HIV or AIDS.
resources.address: 305 S 2nd Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides legal advice, estate-planning document assistance, and referrals for people living with HIV or AIDS through Community Legal Services' Volunteer Lawyers Program.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Maricopa County residents living with HIV or AIDS who meet CLS financial, geographic, subject-matter, conflict, and capacity screening requirements.

**Population Served**
People living with HIV or AIDS in Maricopa County, including Mesa residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Community Legal Services at 602-258-3434 and ask about the Volunteer Lawyers Program HIV/AIDS Law Project or related intake.

**Important Information to Know**
Help depends on eligibility, legal issue, conflicts, and volunteer-attorney availability. Clients with immediate court or benefits deadlines should say so during intake.

resources.name: The Worker AZ / St. Joseph the Worker - Workforce Villages Housing Program
resources.description: The Worker/St. Joseph the Worker Workforce Villages Housing Program provides 90-day shared transitional housing and financial coaching for people working full-time but unable to save for independent housing.
resources.address: Mesa office: 1833 W Main St #128, Mesa, AZ 85201; Phoenix office: 382 E Palm Ln #150, Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Ninety-day transitional housing in a shared one-bedroom apartment, weekly one-on-one support meetings, life-skills and financial workshops, savings requirements, and one year of follow-up support after moving to independent housing.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Participants must have a W2 direct-hire full-time job, earn at least $18 per hour, have been on the job 30-45 days or have two pay stubs, save 80% of net earnings, attend meetings/workshops, and pass review; some felonies are accepted subject to review.

**Population Served**
People working full-time in the Phoenix/Mesa area who face housing challenges and need a structured bridge to independent housing.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through the Workforce Housing application link on the website or call 602-755-JOBS (602-755-5627). Mesa office: 1833 W Main St #128, Mesa, AZ 85201.

**Important Information to Know**
The page states the current wait time for new applicants is two to three months. This is not crisis shelter and requires full-time direct-hire employment.

resources.name: Fort McDowell Yavapai Nation - Enrollment Department
resources.description: Fort McDowell Yavapai Nation's Enrollment Department is the tribal contact for enrollment-related records. For ID recovery, it is useful for members or applicants who need tribal enrollment verification or tribal documentation that can support state ID, benefits, voting or service access.
resources.address: 17661 E. Yavapai Road, Fort McDowell, AZ 85264
resources.hours: Call 480-789-7114 to confirm Enrollment Department hours, requirements, fees and whether appointments are needed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Tribal enrollment contact and enrollment-document support through the Fort McDowell Yavapai Nation Enrollment Department. Public directory information identifies an Enrollment Coordinator and contact route.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For Fort McDowell Yavapai Nation members, applicants or people with a legitimate enrollment-record need. The Nation determines enrollment and document rules.

**Population Served**
Fort McDowell Yavapai Nation members and eligible applicants in the Fort McDowell/Fountain Hills area and surrounding Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-789-7114 or email genos@fmyn.org before visiting 17661 E. Yavapai Road, Fort McDowell, AZ 85264. Ask what proof is needed for enrollment verification, tribal ID or replacement records.

**Important Information to Know**
The public department page verifies the Enrollment Department contact but does not list current tribal ID replacement fees, forms or processing times. Those details must be confirmed directly with the department.

resources.name: Arizona Sunshine Angels — Independent Living Support
resources.description: Help with work clothing, transportation and first-home essentials for older youth in or leaving foster care.
resources.hours: Contact Monday–Friday, 9 AM–5 PM; arrange programme services first.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Independent Living help for older foster youth can include work clothing, a bicycle or bus-pass costs to reach employment, identification-card costs and first-dorm or apartment furnishings.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For older teens in foster care and young people transitioning out of care. Ask whether a participating group home, caregiver or caseworker must request help, and confirm geography, documentation, funding limits and current availability.

**Population Served**
Older youth in foster care and young people leaving care in the Phoenix metropolitan area.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the contact form or call to ask about the Independent Living program. Explain the needed item and current foster-care or transition status; confirm the request process before purchasing or traveling.

**Important Information to Know**
Award limits, timing and available items are not published. Support depends on the program’s assessment and resources; it is not an unrestricted furniture store.

resources.name: VA Survivors Pension and Dependency and Indemnity Compensation
resources.description: VA survivor-benefits pathway for Dependency and Indemnity Compensation, Survivors Pension, and related family/caregiver benefits for qualifying surviving spouses, children, and parents.
resources.hours: VA benefits hotline generally Mon-Fri 8:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m. ET.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
VA provides application information for survivor compensation and pension benefits, including Dependency and Indemnity Compensation, Survivors Pension, Aid and Attendance-related pension support, education/career benefits, health benefits, burial-related benefits, and home-loan benefits where eligible.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Rules depend on the benefit. Relationship to the veteran, service history, cause of death, income/net worth, age, disability, remarriage, and dependent status may matter.

**Population Served**
Eligible surviving spouses, dependent children, and parents of veterans nationwide, including Mesa and Maricopa County households.

**How to Best Connect**
Start with the VA survivor compensation page and call 800-827-1000 for VA benefits help. Accredited representatives or local VA benefits offices can help prepare applications.

**Important Information to Know**
DIC and Survivors Pension have different rules and evidence requirements. Income-tested pension and service-connected death compensation should not be treated as interchangeable; application help is advisable.

resources.name: ARIZONA@WORK Maricopa County - WIOA Supportive Services and Career Center Navigation
resources.description: ARIZONA@WORK Maricopa County provides no-cost workforce services in Mesa and may provide WIOA supportive services, such as transportation, work clothing, tools, testing, childcare, limited utility help and training-related costs, when needed for approved workforce participation.
resources.phone: East Valley Career Center 602-372-9700; Workforce Development 602-506-0589
resources.address: 1001 W. Southern Ave., Suite 101, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
For approved WIOA participants, support can include transportation, bus passes, gas cards, basic auto repairs, work clothing/tools, testing or licensing, child care, limited utility help and training-related costs when necessary for the service plan and not available elsewhere.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Supportive services are for eligible WIOA Adult, Dislocated Worker, or Youth participants and must be documented in the person's service plan. Priority for adult individualized career and training services includes public-assistance recipients, low-income individuals, people who are basic-skills deficient, and eligible veterans/spouses. Supportive services are not an entitlement and depend on eligibility, documented need, approval, and available funds.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County job seekers outside the City of Phoenix, including Mesa-area adults, dislocated workers and youth who need help becoming self-supporting through employment or training.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the County East Valley Career Center at 602-372-9700, Workforce Development at 602-506-0589, or use the County Client Portal. Ask an advisor to assess enrollment and document support in the approved plan. The County centre is at 1001 W. Southern Ave., Suite 101, Mesa. Unemployment insurance is handled separately by Arizona DES.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not general emergency cash or an entitlement. Support depends on documented need, programme approval and available funds, with vendor payments rather than direct participant cash. Automobile purchases, insurance, registration, fines and late fees are not allowed under the reviewed transport policy.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Economic Security - Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program Career Advancement Network (SNAP CAN)
resources.description: SNAP Career Advancement Network (SNAP CAN) is a voluntary employment and training network for eligible Nutrition Assistance recipients, offering education, job readiness, supervised job search, vocational training, retention support, virtual services, and employment-related support payments through providers.
resources.address: Statewide; choose an approved SNAP CAN provider serving the participant's county
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
SNAP CAN helps eligible SNAP recipients build skills, get training, gain work experience, find jobs, keep jobs, and use virtual services. Provider services can include adult basic education, English language learning, GED, career planning, resume preparation, supervised job search, job fairs, job retention, and vocational training.

**Eligibility Requirements**
To qualify, a person must be age 16 or older, receive Nutrition Assistance/SNAP, and not receive TANF Cash Assistance.

**Population Served**
Arizona SNAP recipients who need employment and training help, including Mesa and Maricopa County participants who choose an approved SNAP CAN provider.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact a SNAP CAN provider directly and say the participant wants to join the voluntary SNAP CAN program. If unsure where to start, complete the DES SNAP CAN Provider webform and a SNAP CAN Specialist will help find a provider.

**Important Information to Know**
Support services are at no cost for participants and may help with child care, training materials, interview clothing, uniforms, job equipment, cell phone or internet bills, laptop or hotspot, and related needs, but supports vary by provider. SNAP CAN cannot assist with SNAP benefit questions; call 1-855-432-7587 for Nutrition Assistance questions.

resources.name: Billy’s Way Home — street outreach and Community Table
resources.description: Provides volunteer street outreach, meals and hygiene supplies, with a contact for bicycle-support inquiries.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides volunteer street outreach, meals and hygiene supplies, with a contact for bicycle-support inquiries.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Outreach availability and the current service area must be confirmed with the team.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness in the Phoenix area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 6026280674 or email billyswayhome@gmail.com to ask where and when the team can provide help.

**Important Information to Know**
Do not travel to its administrative address expecting a distribution. The tiny-home village is a vision, not an operating housing programme.

resources.name: Step One Halfway House - Transitional Housing Program
resources.description: Step One Halfway House provides safe, drug-free, supportive transitional housing for men working toward employment, education, independence and stable community living.
resources.address: 2932 N 14th St, Suite B, Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Supportive transitional housing in shared furnished homes with two-man rooms, utilities, bus-route access, house guidelines, curfew, staff presence, resident leadership, and a pathway toward employment and independent housing.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The site describes housing for men in transition and a safe, drug-free model. Call to confirm admission requirements, sobriety rules, background considerations and openings.

**Population Served**
Men seeking affordable supportive housing while rebuilding stability.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-749-5434 or email info@steponehalfwayhouse.org. The current official contact address is 2932 N 14th St, Suite B, Phoenix, AZ 85014.

**Important Information to Know**
The site says no one is turned away for lack of funds and describes a housing scholarship program, but fees and scholarship availability should be confirmed. The current website address differs from the submitted 9636 N 11th Ave address.

resources.name: City of Mesa Municipal Court - Mesa Community Court and SMI Treatment Court docket
resources.description: Mesa Community Court is a problem-solving court for unhoused people with eligible Mesa Municipal Court cases, providing legal intervention paired with social-service referrals such as shelter, physical and mental-health providers, substance-use treatment, benefits, IDs, workforce support, youth and elder care and education; a separate SMI Treatment Court docket serves eligible people with SMI designation connected to an assigned clinic.
resources.address: 250 E. 1st Ave., Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Mesa Municipal Court: Monday–Thursday 7 AM–6 PM except holidays; confirm the specific docket and referral schedule.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Mesa Community Court helps unhoused people resolve eligible pending cases while connecting them to social services. Services can include referrals for shelter, physical and mental-health providers, substance-use treatment, workforce support, outreach, identifying documents, eligible benefits, youth and elder care, and education opportunities. A separate SMI Treatment Court docket coordinates with assigned clinics for people with SMI designation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
This is court-connected and eligibility-limited. Community Court is for unhoused individuals with eligible pending Mesa Municipal Court cases. The SMI Treatment Court docket is for individuals with a serious mental illness designation who are connected with their assigned clinic.

**Population Served**
Unhoused Mesa Municipal Court participants with eligible cases, and a separate group of court-involved people with SMI designation connected to assigned behavioral-health clinics.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Mesa Municipal Court at 480-644-2255 or ask court staff about Community Court or the SMI Treatment Court docket. The court is at 250 E. 1st Ave., Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
These are court-connected pathways, not open community counselling, a walk-in ID clinic or ordinary civil legal representation. Court approval controls participation and case handling; referrals do not guarantee treatment, shelter, benefits or dismissal. People without a qualifying matter should use direct community-service intake.

resources.name: Phoenix VA Health Care System - Health Care for Re-entry Veterans and Veterans Justice Outreach
resources.description: VA Health Care for Re-entry Veterans (HCRV) and Veterans Justice Programs help incarcerated and justice-involved veterans with outreach, pre-release assessments, referrals to VA/community medical, mental-health, social, employment and housing services, and short-term case management after release.
resources.address: 650 E Indian School Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.hours: National Call Center for Homeless Veterans is free, confidential and available 24/7 at 877-424-3838.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
HCRV provides outreach and pre-release assessment for veterans in prison, referrals and linkages to medical, mental-health and social services, employment services on release and short-term case-management assistance after release. Veterans Justice Outreach and Phoenix VA homeless programs can help connect justice-involved or homeless veterans to the nearest VA resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For veterans who are incarcerated, leaving jail or prison, justice-involved, homeless or at imminent risk of homelessness. VA cannot provide medical services that correctional institutions are required to provide while the veteran is still incarcerated.

**Population Served**
Veterans in or returning to the Phoenix VA service area, including Maricopa County and Mesa veterans leaving incarceration or facing justice-system and homelessness barriers.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the National Call Center for Homeless Veterans at 877-424-3838, available 24/7, and ask to be connected to the nearest VA homeless/justice program. For local Phoenix VA justice-program contact, use vhaphovjohcrv@va.gov when appropriate. The Phoenix VA medical center is at 650 E Indian School Rd, Phoenix.

**Important Information to Know**
This is veteran-specific and works through VA eligibility and local VA program capacity. It is not an emergency shelter guarantee or a court attorney service, but it is a key reentry route for veterans before and after release.

resources.name: Furniture Bank, Inc. - Agency-Referred Furniture and Home Furnishings
resources.description: Furniture Bank, Inc. / Furniture Bank of Phoenix provides furniture and essential home furnishings for greater Phoenix households emerging from homelessness through agency-only requests, with client or agency financial participation required.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Furniture, beds, linens, household items, food/groceries, toiletries and related essentials so homes are move-in ready for people emerging from homelessness and participating in self-sufficiency programs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Agency-only application page; individuals cannot apply directly. The official request page states this is not a free furniture program and the agency or client may need to contribute at least $500.

**Population Served**
Children, families, veterans, people with disabilities and individuals in the greater Phoenix area who are emerging from homelessness and connected with a participating agency or helping organization.

**How to Best Connect**
A case manager from a helping agency or faith-based organization should email info@FurnitureBank.us and use the agency request page. The provider communicates by email, not phone, and does not accept direct individual applications or walk-ins.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not free furniture: the agency or client must generally contribute at least $500. The programme furnishes homes rather than single beds/items. The page retains an old notice that new applications were paused until March 2025; the case manager must establish current acceptance, costs, delivery and capacity before promising help. The agency describes a 24-hour response/payment step when a waitlisted client’s turn arrives.

resources.name: St. Joseph's Hospital and Medical Center - MOMobile Maternity Outreach Mobile Unit
resources.description: St. Joseph’s MOMobile offers prenatal care, pregnancy tests, referrals and maternity education through a mobile unit. CARE Campus in Mesa lists a Tuesday stop; appointments and suitability should be confirmed.
resources.address: CARE Campus stop: 466 S. Bellview St., Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: CARE Campus lists Tuesdays 9 AM–2 PM; call to confirm the date and appointment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
MOMobile is described by St. Joseph's Foundation as a fully equipped maternity care center on wheels offering early and continuous prenatal care, pregnancy tests, referrals, education, exam rooms, ultrasound, fetal monitoring and laboratory capability.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Historical and public partner materials describe MOMobile for low-income, uninsured or women-in-need in Arizona/Maricopa County communities who may otherwise lack prenatal care. Current clinical eligibility, insurance rules and appointment requirements must be confirmed by phone.

**Population Served**
Pregnant people in Maricopa County communities with barriers to prenatal care, especially low-income or uninsured patients. A current Mesa stop was not confirmed.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-406-4006 for an appointment, eligibility, insurance/cost, documents and the current schedule. CARE Campus lists MOMobile on Tuesdays 9 AM–2 PM at 466 S. Bellview St., Mesa. Confirm the specific date before travelling.

**Important Information to Know**
The CARE Campus host currently lists the Mesa stop. Mobile schedules and clinical suitability can change; ask about high-risk pregnancy referrals. Mobile prenatal care is not emergency care and does not guarantee delivery arrangements.

resources.name: Simply Serene Detox & Recovery Center
resources.description: Mesa behavioral-health inpatient detox facility offering 24/7 medical detox, stabilization, medication-assisted treatment support, dual-diagnosis care, therapeutic support, and aftercare coordination.
resources.address: 947 E Impala Ave, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: 24/7 medical detox and recovery support; admissions contact available through phone and online admit form.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Simply Serene Detox and Recovery Center provides medically supervised detox in Mesa with 24/7 physician-led monitoring, withdrawal stabilization, medication-assisted treatment support, dual-diagnosis care, counseling or therapeutic support, case management, and aftercare coordination.

**Eligibility Requirements**
People seeking medical detox or recovery stabilization should contact admissions for a clinical and insurance/payment screening. The official admit form asks whether the person has health insurance, but insurance status alone is not enough to determine eligibility.

**Population Served**
People with substance-use withdrawal or early recovery needs in Mesa and surrounding areas; the site also describes support for co-occurring mental-health conditions.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-905-3335, email admissions@simplyserene-detox.com, or submit the official admit form. The facility address is 947 E Impala Ave, Mesa, AZ 85204.

**Important Information to Know**
Arizona Department of Health Services lists Simply Serene Detox and Recovery Center, LLC at 947 East Impala Avenue in Mesa as a Behavioral Health Inpatient Facility. Confirm accepted insurance, cost, bed availability, and whether medical detox is clinically appropriate before travel.

resources.name: Maricopa County Justice Courts - Southeast Veterans Treatment Court
resources.description: Maricopa County Justice Courts Veterans Treatment Court is a problem-solving court track for eligible veterans with misdemeanor Justice Court cases, including Mesa-area justice courts assigned to the Southeast region.
resources.address: Southeast Veterans Treatment Court, Ocotillo Regional Court Center, 201 E Chicago St, Chandler, AZ 85225
resources.hours: Court appearance schedules and video options depend on the assigned VTC region. The court page says email replies may take up to 3 days.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Veterans Treatment Court develops specialized action plans for veterans with qualifying Justice Court misdemeanor criminal cases. The court coordinates judges, staff, volunteers, veteran mentors, community partners, VA-related forms, treatment planning, and resource connection for needs such as jobs, housing, bus passes, and groceries.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Justice Courts page states that anyone with proof of U.S. military service and criminal misdemeanor charges may qualify. Misdemeanor criminal charges in any Maricopa County Justice Court may be handled in VTC. Civil cases such as evictions, small claims, and civil suits are not accepted.

**Population Served**
Veterans with misdemeanor criminal cases in Maricopa County Justice Courts, including cases from East Mesa, North Mesa, West Mesa, Highland, San Marcos, San Tan, and University Lakes courts routed to the Southeast region.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the court currently handling the case to request transfer to Veterans Treatment Court. Southeast VTC is at the Ocotillo Regional Court Center, 201 E Chicago St, Chandler. Call 602-372-3400 or email VeteransCourt-SE@jbazmc.maricopa.gov for Southeast VTC questions.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not civil legal aid and does not handle eviction, small-claims, or civil suits. Forms must be returned on time, and missing court dates can remove a participant from VTC. This Justice Court pathway is distinct from Superior Court veterans programs.

resources.name: Surprise Prosecutor — Victim Services
resources.description: Case updates and victim-rights support through the Surprise City Prosecutor’s Victim Services Program.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Case updates and victim-rights support through the Surprise City Prosecutor’s Victim Services Program.

**Eligibility Requirements**

For victims connected to criminal cases handled by the Surprise City Prosecutor. Confirm the case and any referral requirements when contacting the program.

**Population Served**

Surprise crime victims, including domestic-violence survivors with a municipal case.

**How to Best Connect**

Call623-222-1177 or emailvsp@surpriseaz.gov. The published program correspondence address is16081N.CivicCenterPlaza,Suite104,Surprise,AZ85374; confirm an appointment before travel.

**Important Information to Know**

The city’s victim-contact form says those contact details are confidential. Do not extend that promise to all statements or case documents. This is case support, not a shelter or independent lawyer.

resources.name: One Small Step / Clothes Cabin - Homeless Assistance Services
resources.description: One Small Step / Clothes Cabin offers practical homeless assistance in Gilbert for currently unsheltered clients, including showers, weekly laundry, mailboxes, storage lockers, clothing, hygiene goods and referrals to outside services. It is a nearby East Valley option for Mesa clients who can travel.
resources.address: 710 N Cooper Rd, Gilbert, AZ 85233
resources.hours: Tuesday-Wednesday 9:00 AM-3:00 PM; Thursday 4:00 PM-7:00 PM. Arrive at least 1.5 hours before closing to complete laundry.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Showers, one free load of laundry per week, mailboxes, storage lockers, clothing, hygiene goods through Clothes Cabin and referrals to outside services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For clients who are currently homeless or unsheltered. Mailbox and locker availability may depend on capacity.

**Population Served**
Currently homeless individuals in Gilbert and the surrounding East Valley, including Mesa residents when travel is practical.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to 710 N Cooper Rd, Gilbert during posted homeless-assistance hours, call 480-285-4111, or email info@onesmallstepaz.org. Arrive at least 1.5 hours before closing for laundry.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not in Mesa, but it fills nearby gaps for showers, laundry, mail and storage. Confirm locker and mailbox availability at intake.

resources.name: Phoenix Children’s — Financial counseling and assistance
resources.description: Provides a hospital and specialist-bill assistance route for families using Phoenix Children’s care.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides a hospital and specialist-bill assistance route for families using Phoenix Children’s care.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Application, income and insurance documentation apply; eligibility also depends on the facility, provider and medically necessary service.

**Population Served**
Children and families receiving eligible Phoenix Children’s services.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Financial Counseling at 602-933-2000; the page lists weekday phone hours 7 a.m.–6:30 p.m. Arizona time. Ask about application documents and coverage enrollment.

**Important Information to Know**
Assistance does not automatically cover every independent clinician or ancillary charge. Obtain the current policy and provider list; this is not unrestricted cash aid.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Economic Security - Child Care Assistance
resources.description: DES Child Care Assistance helps eligible Arizona families pay DES-approved child care providers, with a current waitlist for most applicant families because funding is limited.
resources.hours: Online applications and renewals are available; phone support is through DES Child Care Assistance.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
DES Child Care Assistance helps families pay for child care in DES-contracted center-based or home settings. Benefits are sent directly to the child care provider and depend on care hours and provider rates; the benefit may not cover all child care costs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
General eligibility includes Arizona residency, children birth through age 12, income at or below 165% of the Federal Poverty Level for many families, a qualifying eligible activity, documentation, and selection of a DES-contracted child care provider. Categories include teen parents in school, families in homeless or domestic violence shelters, caregivers unable or unavailable to provide care, and certain grandparents or guardians. DCS, Tribal child welfare, and TANF Jobs referrals have different rules.

**Population Served**
Arizona families who need child care for work, school, qualifying activities, or safety/stability reasons, including eligible Mesa and Maricopa County families.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply or renew online through the A-to-Z Arizona portal, or submit a paper application by email to CCA@azdes.gov, fax, mail, or in person at a DES office. For questions, call 1-833-947-6396 to speak with a Child Care Eligibility Specialist.

**Important Information to Know**
DES has a waiting list for most families because funding is limited; Cash Assistance, DCS and other qualifying referral pathways may have different rules. Ask about the family’s route and current status. Applications can take up to 30 days to process. Do not submit both online and paper applications for the same request. Benefits may not cover all provider costs.

resources.name: Operation Homefront - Critical Financial Assistance Program
resources.description: Operation Homefront's Critical Financial Assistance Program provides short-term financial help for eligible military families experiencing hardship, including overdue bills, home repairs and other critical needs.
resources.hours: Online portal application; call toll-free with questions.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Critical Financial Assistance can help eligible military families with overdue bills, home repairs and other urgent family needs. Applications are reviewed by Operation Homefront caseworkers through an online portal.

**Eligibility Requirements**
One route is for post-9/11 line-of-duty wounds, illness or injury; discharged applicants need Honorable or General Under Honorable Conditions status and must be within ten years of separation. Certain deployed E-1–E-6 members with legal dependents qualify under detailed deployment rules. The general active-duty E-1–E-6 dependent-household route covers only food and dependent vision care. Read the category-specific criteria and supply military, discharge, deployment or injury documents as applicable.

**Population Served**
Eligible active-duty military and veteran families experiencing financial hardship, including Arizona families who meet national program criteria.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through My Operation Homefront from the 1st through the 10th of the month; the published cutoff is 11:59 PM Central time on the 10th. Review the service-category criteria and submit required documents. Call 877-264-3968 with eligibility questions.

**Important Information to Know**
Review occurs after the application window closes. Covered needs depend on service category and caseworker approval; a general active-duty applicant should not assume eligibility for rent, utility or vehicle assistance. Funding and approval are not guaranteed.

resources.name: Aid to Women Center - Parenting Prep Material Support
resources.description: Aid to Women Center offers free baby and maternity material support through weekly Parenting Prep classes, including diapers, wipes, baby clothes, blankets, maternity clothes, car seats, strollers, Pack 'n Plays and other baby items.
resources.address: 3029 N Alma School Rd #130, Chandler, AZ 85224; 7625 S 24th St, Phoenix, AZ 85042
resources.hours: Chandler Center: Monday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM, Tuesday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM, Wednesday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM. South Phoenix Center: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM on the current material-support page.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free material support for baby needs through weekly Parenting Prep classes. Items listed include diapers, wipes, baby clothes, baby blankets, pacifiers, maternity clothes, car seats, strollers, Pack 'n Plays, bassinets, high chairs and bouncers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Clients sign up for weekly Parenting Prep classes and earn items through participation. Large items and sizes depend on need, availability and current inventory.

**Population Served**
Pregnant and postpartum women and parents in South Phoenix, Tempe, Chandler, Mesa, Gilbert, Scottsdale and the East Valley who need pregnancy, postpartum or baby support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-966-1902 or email support@aidtowomencenter.org. The Chandler Center is at 3029 N Alma School Rd #130, and the South Phoenix Center is at 7625 S 24th St.

**Important Information to Know**
Material support is tied to Parenting Prep participation, not a walk-in baby supply closet. Availability of larger items such as car seats, strollers, bassinets and Pack 'n Plays may vary.

resources.name: Military Assistance Mission - Baby Bundle Bash
resources.description: Military Assistance Mission's Baby Bundle Bash selects eligible expecting Arizona military families for a group baby shower with essentials for an upcoming child.
resources.address: 19225 N Cave Creek Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85024
resources.hours: Event-based program; the official page lists the next Baby Bundle Bash cycle and application link when available.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Baby Bundle Bash provides selected expecting military families with baby-shower essentials for an upcoming child. The program is event-based rather than a walk-in closet.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Official eligibility is Arizona active-duty, National Guard and Reserve military E-5 and below, plus post-9/11 recipients of a Purple Heart Certificate, Combat Action Badge or equivalent. It is one-time assistance per family, for a first or second child, and the expecting parent must be at least 16 weeks pregnant at the shower or the baby must have been born within one month of the shower. A spouse who is expecting must be verified in DEERS.

**Population Served**
Expecting Arizona military service members and military spouses who meet the program rules, including eligible Mesa and Maricopa County households.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Apply Today link on the Baby Bundle Bash page when applications are open. For questions, call Military Assistance Mission at 602-246-6429 or contact Bryan Glasco at 480-200-6063 or bryan@azmam.org.

**Important Information to Know**
Selection and event timing are not guaranteed. The page inspected on 2026-09-26 still referenced applications for a February 2026 event, so clients should confirm the next available cycle before relying on this option.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Revenue - Property Tax Credit and Increased Excise Tax Credit
resources.description: Arizona Department of Revenue administers the refundable property tax credit for qualifying very-low-income older adults or SSI recipients and the income-based increased excise tax credit, including a claim form for some people who otherwise do not need to file an Arizona return.
resources.address: 1600 W Monroe St, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
State tax-credit pathways that may reduce tax liability or provide a refundable credit: the property tax credit for qualifying older adults or SSI recipients with very low household income, and the increased excise tax credit for qualified low-income taxpayers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Property tax credit rules include full-year Arizona residency, paying property tax or rent on a main Arizona home, being age 65 or older by December 31 of the tax year or receiving Title 16 SSI, and meeting very low household-income limits. Increased excise tax credit eligibility depends on income, household/exemption rules, dependency status, and other tax-year instructions.

**Population Served**
Eligible full-year Arizona residents, including Mesa and Maricopa County homeowners or renters with low income, older adults, and SSI recipients.

**How to Best Connect**
Use Arizona Department of Revenue tax-credit instructions and the appropriate form, such as Form 140PTC for property tax credit and increased excise tax credit, or Form 140ET for some taxpayers not required to file an Arizona return. For general ADOR questions, use the Department of Revenue contact routes.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not immediate emergency aid. Claims require the correct tax-year form and filing deadline, and the property tax credit income limits are very low. Tax advice may be needed if the household is unsure how to file.

resources.name: Excellence Recovery
resources.description: Buckeye residential addiction and mental-health treatment provider serving adults from Mesa, Tempe, Chandler, Gilbert, Phoenix and the East Valley.
resources.address: 21248 W Almeria Rd, Buckeye, AZ 85396
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Excellence Recovery provides residential addiction treatment serving East Valley and Phoenix-area adults. Care may address opioids, fentanyl, heroin, cocaine, methamphetamine, benzodiazepines, prescription drugs, alcohol, mental-health concerns and dual diagnosis, with continuing-care planning.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adults seeking residential addiction or mental-health treatment may call for a confidential conversation, insurance review, clinical assessment and admission planning. Exact medical exclusions, payer rules and openings must be confirmed.

**Population Served**
Adults from Mesa, Tempe, Chandler, Gilbert, Phoenix and surrounding Arizona communities who can receive care at the Buckeye residential location.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 623-248-7092, email hello@excellencerecovery.org, or use the insurance verification/contact form. Confirm transportation, insurance/self-pay cost and whether residential treatment is the appropriate level of care.

**Important Information to Know**
The official page describes Excellence Recovery as located in Buckeye and serving the East Valley, not physically located in Mesa/Tempe. It is not an emergency access point or methadone clinic.

resources.name: Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community - Office of Membership Services tribal ID cards and CDIB records
resources.description: Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community Office of Membership Services provides SRPMIC tribal photo ID cards, membership and enrollment records, CDIB-related service routing and enrollment applications for eligible Community members and applicants.
resources.address: 10005 E Osborn Rd, Scottsdale, AZ 85256
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Membership Office facilitates and assists with SRPMIC enrollment and membership records, processes name and address changes, provides tribal photo ID cards to Community Members, and maintains voter registration records. The phone directory also lists Membership Services for identification cards, CDIBs and enrollment applications.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Limited to enrolled SRPMIC Community Members and eligible SRPMIC enrollment or membership-record applicants. Members of other tribes must contact their own tribal enrollment office.

**Population Served**
Enrolled Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community members and people with SRPMIC enrollment or membership-record matters in Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Membership Services at 480-362-7330 or 480-362-7600 to confirm the process, documents, location and any fees before travel. The public SRPMIC address is 10005 E Osborn Rd, Scottsdale.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a tribal membership and credential office, not a general Arizona ID office. Public pages confirm tribal photo ID services, but replacement-card details, remote options and fees should be confirmed directly.

resources.name: Housing Authority of Maricopa County - Rental Assistance Programs and Wait List
resources.description: Housing Authority of Maricopa County provides county-level rental assistance and affordable property programs, including HCV, PBV, FUP, HUD-VASH, Mainstream and HAMC-owned affordable properties, for households in HAMC jurisdiction.
resources.address: 8910 N. 78th Avenue, Building D, Peoria, AZ 85345
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Housing Choice Vouchers, project-based vouchers, HAMC-owned affordable properties and special-purpose pathways such as Family Unification, Mainstream disability vouchers and HUD-VASH when available. The applicant portal supports waitlist status and contact updates.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on the selected HAMC program, household income, referral requirements and whether the location falls within HAMC jurisdiction. FUP, HUD-VASH and Mainstream vouchers have separate referral and population rules.

**Population Served**
Low-income households and special populations in participating HAMC areas of Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call HAMC at 602-744-4500, email info@maricopahousing.org, or use the HAMC applicant portal to check waitlist status and update information. Office: 8910 N. 78th Avenue, Building D, Peoria, AZ 85345.

**Important Information to Know**
HAMC’s jurisdiction differs from the City of Mesa Housing Authority. Incorporated Mesa is generally served by Mesa’s authority; county islands or other covered locations may have a HAMC route. Confirm the actual target address and programme before applying. Waitlists and application windows change; neither listing nor application guarantees assistance.

resources.name: Central Christian Church ACTS Homeless Ministry - Mesa Campus
resources.description: ACTS Homeless Ministry at Central Christian Church's Mesa campus is a recurring first-and-third-Saturday outreach that picks up guests by van and provides breakfast, showers, clean clothing, haircuts and other support resources.
resources.address: 933 N Lindsay Rd, Mesa, AZ 85213
resources.hours: 1st and 3rd Saturday of each month; contact localoutreach@centralaz.com for current pickup points, timing and capacity.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
ACTS Homeless Ministry picks up guests with vans and brings them to the Mesa campus for breakfast, showers, clean clothing, haircuts and other resources for people who are homeless or working poor.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people experiencing homelessness or working poverty who can access the scheduled van pickup. Pickup points, space and service details are not fully published and should be confirmed.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness and working poor guests in the Mesa area who can attend the scheduled outreach day.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact localoutreach@centralaz.com before the first or third Saturday to ask about current pickup locations, arrival time, capacity and available services. The Mesa campus is 933 N Lindsay Rd., Mesa, AZ 85213.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a limited twice-monthly outreach, not a daily drop-in center. The public page confirms the recurring schedule and services but does not publish pickup points or capacity.

resources.name: ADCRR — Release preparation courses
resources.description: Offers in-custody release-preparation curricula covering practical planning, employment and community transition, including Merging Two Worlds.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Offers in-custody release-preparation curricula covering practical planning, employment and community transition, including Merging Two Worlds.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Enrollment depends on facility offerings, release timing and the individual’s program plan.

**Population Served**
People in Arizona correctional facilities preparing to return to the community.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the assigned case manager, correctional officer or facility education staff about Preparation for Release, Reentry Preparation and Merging Two Worlds in the current program catalog.

**Important Information to Know**
A listed curriculum does not establish a place in the next class or guarantee work or housing after release.

resources.name: Banner - University Medicine · Comprehensive Pain and Addiction Clinic
resources.description: Phoenix outpatient addiction medicine clinic offering treatment for substance and alcohol use, MOUD, outpatient alcohol withdrawal and medication management, harm reduction, pregnancy-related SUD care, infectious-disease services, and co-occurring mental-health treatment.
resources.address: 1300 N 12th St, Suites 320 & 608, Phoenix, AZ 85006
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; closed Saturday-Sunday.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Banner - University Medicine Comprehensive Pain and Addiction Clinic provides outpatient addiction medicine for substance and alcohol use. Official services include outpatient addiction medicine, inpatient consultation at Banner University Medical Center Phoenix, care for substance use in pregnancy at any gestational age, community referrals, STI/blood-borne infection prevention and testing, contraception, neonatal opioid withdrawal outpatient weaning, medication for opioid use disorder, outpatient alcohol withdrawal medication management, contingency management for stimulant use disorder, co-occurring mental-health treatment, naloxone/harm reduction, and medications such as buprenorphine, extended-release buprenorphine, naltrexone, and alcohol maintenance medications.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Patients needing outpatient medical care for substance or alcohol use; most major insurance is accepted, but patients should check their own plan. Same-day emergency issues, severe withdrawal, or pregnancy emergencies may require ER/911 rather than clinic care.

**Population Served**
Adults and pregnant patients in Phoenix/Maricopa County needing addiction medicine, MOUD, alcohol-use treatment, harm reduction, or substance-use care connected to pregnancy or chronic pain.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-839-0220 for the clinic or use Banner's provider scheduling where available. Location hours are Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
This is outpatient medical addiction care, not residential treatment. Banner states it no longer accepts cash or personal checks at this location; confirm payment method and insurance before the visit.

resources.name: SAMHSA — FindTreatment.gov and National Helpline
resources.description: A national treatment locator and telephone referral service for mental-health and substance-use care.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

A national treatment locator and telephone referral service for mental-health and substance-use care.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Public search and referral assistance are available; the selected facility determines clinical eligibility, coverage and charges.

**Population Served**

People seeking care anywhere in the United States or its territories, including clients willing to travel beyond the local area.

**How to Best Connect**

Search by city, ZIP, facility name or distance and narrow the results using the site’s filters. The National Helpline provides treatment information and referrals24/7.

**Important Information to Know**

Facility information comes from provider reports and may change. Call a facility before visiting to confirm needed services, accepted payment and current access.

resources.name: Area Agency on Aging, Region One - Family Caregiver Support Program
resources.description: The National Family Caregiver Support Program, delivered locally through Area Agency on Aging, Region One, offers caregiver information, access assistance, support groups, training, respite and limited supplemental services for eligible family caregivers.
resources.address: 1366 E. Thomas Rd., Suite 108, Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.hours: Access through the 24-Hour Senior HELP LINE.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Caregiver information, assistance accessing supportive services, counseling, support groups, caregiver training, respite care and limited supplemental services. Local options can include in-home respite, consumer-directed reimbursement, adult day health respite and caregiver education.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligible caregivers include adults caring for an older adult or a person with Alzheimer's disease or a related neurological disorder, and certain relatives age 55+ raising children or adults with disabilities. Respite and supplemental services have additional assessment criteria and depend on funding.

**Population Served**
Family caregivers in Maricopa County, including caregivers of older adults, dementia caregivers and some older relative caregivers raising children or adults with disabilities.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Area Agency on Aging 24-Hour Senior HELP LINE at 602-264-HELP (4357) or toll-free 888-783-7500 and ask for Family Caregiver Support.

**Important Information to Know**
This program does not automatically pay someone to care for a family member. Respite and supplemental help depend on assessment, risk level, eligibility, funding and provider availability.

resources.name: City of Tempe CARE 7 - Veteran Services and Support
resources.description: Tempe CARE 7 Veteran Services provides no-cost service coordination and navigation for people who have served in the U.S. military, regardless of discharge status or VA eligibility, with help connecting to housing, employment, education, benefits, mental health, substance-use and personal support resources.
resources.hours: CARE & HOPE line available 24 hours a day at 480-350-8004.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
CARE 7 Veteran Services provides 24-hour service coordination and navigation at no cost, including housing assistance connections, employment and education guidance, health and wellness coordination for mental health, substance abuse and counseling, benefits navigation and personal support. CARE 7 can bridge veterans to Phoenix VA, ADVS, East Valley Regional Veterans Court, VA CRRC, Family Housing Hub, CASS, Tempe I-HELP, Community Bridges and other partners.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Former U.S. military service members may inquire regardless of discharge status or VA eligibility. Ongoing local help may depend on Tempe residency; Mesa residents should confirm the service area and ask about an appropriate referral.

**Population Served**
Veterans and former service members, especially Tempe/East Valley residents needing resource navigation, crisis-to-recovery support or benefits/social-service guidance.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the CARE & HOPE line at 480-350-8004, available 24 hours daily, and ask for veteran-service navigation. The listed veteran contacts are Michael Garrison at michael_garrison@tempe.gov and Sean Green at sean_green@tempe.gov. Arrange any in-person meeting before traveling.

**Important Information to Know**
This is navigation and coordination, not guaranteed direct financial assistance, housing placement or treatment. It may prioritize Tempe residents; Mesa clients should confirm eligibility for ongoing services and use the phone route first.

resources.name: Valley Metro Commute Solutions — ShareTheRide and commute options
resources.description: Valley Metro Commute Solutions offers ShareTheRide commuter matching and information about carpool, vanpool, transit, bike and employer commute alternatives.
resources.hours: Online platform access varies; call Valley Metro Commute Solutions for help.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
ShareTheRide helps commuters find potential carpool, vanpool, bike or bus connections. Commute Solutions also provides information on employer commute planning, telework/work-schedule options and alternatives to driving alone.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Best fit is a recurring commute with a stable route or schedule. A listing or match does not guarantee a safe, accessible, affordable or reliable ride.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County commuters, including people living or working in Mesa, and employers planning recurring commute options.

**How to Best Connect**
Use https://www.sharetheride.com/ or call Valley Metro Commute Solutions at 602-262-7433 for commute-program questions. Participants should evaluate schedules, safety, cost-sharing, insurance, accessibility and backup options before relying on a match.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a matching platform, not a vetted ride provider, taxi service or emergency transportation program. It may be useful when fixed-route transit does not solve a stable work commute by itself.

resources.name: Valle del Sol — WIC nutrition services
resources.description: Provides a WIC application route through Valle del Sol’s listed Phoenix sites.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides a WIC application route through Valle del Sol’s listed Phoenix sites.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Income and WIC pregnancy/postpartum/infant/young-child criteria apply; insurance is not required.

**Population Served**
Eligible families in the Phoenix/Mesa service region who can reach the currently operating WIC locations.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the WIC team 602-848-4470, or main 602-258-6797. The provider lists Central Phoenix at 7thStreet/Indian School and Maryvale at 84thAvenue/Thomas, Monday–Friday 8: 30 a.m.–5 p.m.; confirm an appointment and address.

**Important Information to Know**
Do not use the old 430 N Dobson Mesa WIC address without fresh confirmation. The general page title mentions Mesa, but its actual WIC access section names Phoenix sites.

resources.name: Gompers - Employment Services Continuum
resources.description: Gompers' Employment Services Continuum offers disability employment opportunities, individual supported employment, transition-to-employment soft-skills instruction, group supported employment, center-based employment and VR/RSA-connected supports.
resources.address: Phoenix metro area; contact Gompers for current program site
resources.hours: Call or use the contact form for current intake, funding, transportation and program schedules.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Gompers Employment Services Continuum includes Individual Supported Employment with one-on-one job coaching, Transition to Employment instruction in soft skills for securing and maintaining employment, community job exploration and public-transportation practice, Group Supported Employment, Center Based Employment and partnerships with Vocational Rehabilitation/RSA for qualifying individuals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Gompers employment services are designed for people with disabilities. Exact eligibility, DDD/RSA or other funding requirements, age, transportation and current capacity are not fully stated on the employment-services page and should be confirmed through Gompers.

**Population Served**
People with disabilities in the Phoenix metro area who need supported employment, transition-to-employment training, group employment, center-based employment or job-coaching support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Gompers at 602-336-0061 or use its contact form and select Employment Services. Ask about the appropriate employment program, referral or funding requirements, current openings and Mesa access.

**Important Information to Know**
Supported employment and work training depend on program fit, authorization, available staff and transportation arrangements. Ask which program and site can meet the person’s needs before traveling.

resources.name: Friendly House - Immigration and Legal Services Department
resources.description: Friendly House provides affordable immigration legal representation, advocacy, and community education with in-person and virtual consultations. Services include DACA, VAWA, U/T visas, family petitions, green-card renewals, adjustment, removal-related work, naturalization, work authorization, FOIA/FBI requests, travel documents, and waivers.
resources.address: 802 S. 1st Ave., Suite #1, Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.hours: In-person and virtual consultations by appointment; call or email to schedule.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Friendly House Immigration and Legal Services offers immigration consultations and representation. Listed services include DACA, VAWA, U visas, T visas, affidavits of support, fiance visas, green-card renewals, family-based petitions, adjustment of status, cancellation of removal in deportation proceedings, consular processing, naturalization/citizenship, employment authorization, FOIA/FBI requests, travel documents, mock interviews, and I-601/I-601A waivers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
