Eligibility depends on the immigration case type and the department's consultation and representation screening. The official page describes the service as affordable, not free legal aid.

**Population Served**
Immigrants and immigrant families who can access Phoenix or virtual services, including Mesa residents, domestic-violence/crime/trafficking survivors and people needing immigration documents or citizenship/family services.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-416-7200 or email immigration@friendlyhouse.org to schedule an immigration consultation. Friendly House states that the 802 S. 1st Ave. office has in-person and virtual services available.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm consultation fees, exact case or court scope, representation capacity, language needs and deadlines. This is not general civil legal aid, a state ID/birth-certificate issuer, a DV crisis line or shelter. Survivors can ask about safe virtual/in-person consultation and use a separate advocate for immediate safety planning. Use the immigration office in Suite 1 rather than a general-directory suite.

resources.name: Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community - Food Bank / Food Distribution Center
resources.description: Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community Social Services Food Bank / Food Distribution Center offering food distribution, bread distribution, emergency food boxes and child/infant boxes for the SRPMIC community.
resources.address: Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community; older public notice listed 1952 E Longmore Rd, Scottsdale, AZ for food-box pickup
resources.hours: Current public hours are not confirmed. Older SRPMIC Food Distribution Center notices listed Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM and Tuesday 10:00 AM-3:00 PM, with midday closure in one notice; call before referral.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
SRPMIC Social Services lists Food Bank / Helping Hands services including a food distribution program, bread distribution, emergency food boxes, child and infant boxes and donated items. The SRPMIC phone directory lists a Food Distribution Center.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official Social Services page describes culturally sensitive community-based services for the Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community. Public pages do not fully state whether food-bank access is limited to enrolled members, residents, community families or other eligible tribal-service participants; screen eligibility by phone first.

**Population Served**
Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community families and community members near Mesa/Scottsdale who need food support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the SRPMIC Food Distribution Center at 480-362-7277 or SRPMIC Social Services at 480-362-5645. The Social Services page also lists LEARN/Food Bank/Helping Hands contact Winterelk.Valencia@SRPMIC-nsn.gov.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general public Mesa pantry. Eligibility, current pickup address and current hours should be confirmed before referral. Older SRPMIC public notices listed 1952 E Longmore Rd and weekday pickup hours, but current official directory/contact pages are the safer route for screening.

resources.name: Choice Recovery Centers - Choice IOP
resources.description: Choice Recovery Centers / Choice IOP provides adult intensive outpatient substance-use treatment in Mesa, with intake screening, drug and alcohol recovery support, online or in-person options, and flexible day/evening/weekend programming.
resources.address: 303 N Centennial Way, Suite 200, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Morning, evening, weekend, and telehealth IOP options are advertised; call for current schedule.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Adult intensive outpatient treatment for drug and alcohol recovery, individualized programming after intake screening, in-person or online IOP, and flexible morning, evening, and weekend options.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adults seeking outpatient substance-use treatment may contact intake. Screening determines clinical fit and whether a higher level of care is needed. Ask about current age criteria, accepted insurance plans, authorization and out-of-pocket costs.

**Population Served**
Adults in Mesa and Maricopa County seeking outpatient drug or alcohol treatment, including clients needing telehealth or nontraditional group times.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-527-0337 or email admin@choiceiop.com. The Mesa address is 303 N Centennial Way, Suite 200, Mesa, AZ 85201.

**Important Information to Know**
This is outpatient/IOP, not detox or residential treatment. Provider branding may appear as Choice Recovery, Choice IOP, or Choice Health Integrated; confirm the current legal and payer details during intake.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Corrections, Rehabilitation & Reentry - Sex Offender Education and Treatment Program
resources.description: ADCRR in-custody counseling and treatment pathway for people with sex-offense histories, using education and treatment programming within the correctional system.
resources.address: ADCRR facilities statewide; public contact: 701 E Jefferson St, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
ADCRR Counseling and Treatment Services includes the Sex Offender Education and Treatment Program. Official program materials describe sex-offense education and treatment as part of ADCRR behavioral-health and reentry-related programming.

**Eligibility Requirements**
This is an ADCRR program for eligible incarcerated people or people otherwise assigned through the corrections system. It is not a general community counseling intake for anyone with a past sex offense.

**Population Served**
People in ADCRR custody or ADCRR-controlled programming who are assessed or assigned for sex-offense education and treatment.

**How to Best Connect**
People in custody should ask facility case management, counseling/treatment staff, or their assigned ADCRR contact about eligibility. Public questions can go through ADCRR at 602-542-0023 as submitted or the main ADCRR contact 602-542-5497.

**Important Information to Know**
This resource is important because many reentry programs exclude people with sex-offense histories, but this ADCRR program is correctional-system based. Community treatment referral partners and post-release continuity are not clearly posted on the public page and should be confirmed for the specific client.

resources.name: WEDCO Employment Center - Occupational Rehabilitation and Supported Employment Services
resources.description: WEDCO Employment Center provides occupational rehabilitation and supported-employment services for individuals with disabilities in the greater Phoenix and Tucson metro regions and parts of Pinal County, including resume help, job development and placement, interviewing skills, benefits counseling, career exploration, retention support, work adjustment training, classroom training and RSA-funded services.
resources.address: 7600 N. 16th St., Suite E155, Phoenix, AZ 85020
resources.hours: Public site does not list office hours; call before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
WEDCO provides occupational rehabilitation and employment services for individuals with disabilities. Services include classroom computer and office-skills training, face-to-face or phone engagement, onsite job coaching, resume creation, job development and placement, interviewing skills, benefits counseling, career exploration, retention supports, work adjustment training, job training, supported education and RSA rehabilitation instructional services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on the funding/referral route. WEDCO describes services through Mercy Care for adult SMI participants in Maricopa County, General Mental Health contracts with Banner, Molina, Mercy Care and Arizona Complete Health for adult GMH Title participants valleywide, and RSA-contracted services funded through Arizona DES. Confirm the client's plan, VR/RSA referral or behavioral-health status before referral.

**Population Served**
Individuals with disabilities preparing to enter, re-enter or retain employment in the greater Phoenix and Tucson metropolitan regions and parts of Pinal County. Services are available in Spanish.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Phoenix office at 602-274-2605. The contact page lists 7600 N. 16th St., Suite E155, Phoenix, AZ 85020. Ask which service route applies for a Mesa client and whether a referral from Mercy Care, RSA, Vocational Rehabilitation or a health plan is required.

**Important Information to Know**
WEDCO is not a general walk-in job center. It is a disability and behavioral-health/vocational rehabilitation provider with funder-specific eligibility and referral requirements. Public pages do not list office hours, so call before travel.

resources.name: Arizona Immigrant and Refugee Services - Immigration Specialist and Refugee Resettlement
resources.description: Arizona Immigrant and Refugee Services provides refugee resettlement and immigrant support services, including an Immigration Specialist for family petitions, citizenship, permanent residency, immigration-document replacement, TPS/DED, family reunification, consultations, work permits and refugee-related applications.
resources.address: 10240 N 31st Ave, Suite 112, Phoenix, AZ 85051
resources.hours: General office Monday–Friday 9 a.m.–4:30 p.m.; immigration specialist walk-ins Wednesday and Friday 11 a.m.–2 p.m.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Refugee resettlement/case coordination, Preferred Communities, Matching Grant, temporary housing, food/clothing and other client essentials, English-language instruction, translation/referrals, job training/employment services, walk-in SIV services and State RRP benefits. Immigration support includes family petitions/reunification, citizenship, permanent residency, lost/stolen immigration-document replacement, TPS/DED, green-card/work-permit processing, I-730 refugee and I-131 re-parole applications.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Programme eligibility depends on immigration/ORR-qualifying status, Arizona residence, arrival/status dates, funding and case type. Material help is for eligible AIRS participants and depends on stock; ask about Mesa access and intake. People outside refugee/eligible-newcomer categories should confirm which immigration services can assist.

**Population Served**
Refugees, SIV holders, asylees, parolees, ORR-eligible immigrants and other immigrants in Arizona or Maricopa County whose needs fit AIRS programs.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit or contact AIRS at 10240 N 31st Ave, Suite 112, Phoenix, AZ 85051. Call 602-944-1821 or email info@airsaz.org. Immigration Specialist walk-in hours are Wednesday and Friday 11:00 AM-2:00 PM; call to make an appointment outside walk-in hours.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a public clothing closet or a state ID/birth-certificate issuer. Immigration support is principally case/form assistance; full removal-court defence is not established. Confirm exact service, documents, fees, material availability and appointment or pickup arrangements before travelling.

resources.name: Resilient Health - First Episode Psychosis
resources.description: Resilient Health's First Episode Psychosis program provides early intervention and relapse-prevention services for people ages 15-30 experiencing psychosis within less than two years since first episode.
resources.address: 1415 N 1st St, Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.hours: Call or email for referral and appointment information; public page does not post clinic hours for FEP.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Early intervention and relapse-prevention services for psychosis, focused on helping participants build tools for recovery and resilience.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Ages 15–30 with a recent first episode of psychosis; the program assesses diagnosis, illness duration and fit. The provider excludes substance- or trauma-induced psychosis, autism spectrum disorder and traumatic brain injury from this FEP program.

**Population Served**
Adolescents, young adults, and adults ages 15-30 in the Phoenix/Maricopa area who meet FEP clinical criteria.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 877-779-2470 or email fepreferrals@rhaz.org. The program is at 1415 N 1st St, Phoenix. Families and professionals can ask about referral.

**Important Information to Know**
Clinical screening determines fit. If this program is unsuitable, ask the referring clinician about an alternative; this program’s exclusions do not mean treatment is unavailable elsewhere.

resources.name: Educate–Empower–Succeed — Student Employment Transition
resources.description: Pre-employment transition workshops covering job exploration, work readiness, further education, self-advocacy and work-based learning, coordinated with schools.
resources.address: 1921 S. Alma School Rd., Suite 208, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Pre-employment transition workshops covering job exploration, work readiness, further education, self-advocacy and work-based learning, coordinated with schools.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Arizona Pre-ETS serves eligible students with disabilities ages 14–22 who are enrolled in education. Confirm the required request, documentation and local workshop arrangements.

**Population Served**

Students with disabilities in Mesa and the provider’s contracted service areas.

**How to Best Connect**

Contact Sonya Beck by phone or email and ask about Pre-ETS. The state contractor directory lists the Mesa office and request route.

**Important Information to Know**

These workshops prepare students for work; they do not guarantee a job. Other adult vocational or tutoring services have separate eligibility and payment arrangements.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Economic Security - ARIZONA@WORK Employment Service
resources.description: Arizona DES Employment Service is a no-cost public employment service open to all job seekers, offering resume help, interview preparation, job searching, career assessments, goal setting, job referrals, placement, and reemployment services.
resources.address: Statewide; Mesa access through ARIZONA@WORK East Valley Career Center, 1001 W. Southern Ave., Suite 101, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: DES workforce specialists can meet in person at an ARIZONA@WORK office, by phone, or online by appointment. East Valley Career Center hours are Monday-Thursday 8 AM-7 PM and Friday 8 AM-5 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Employment Service provides no-cost help with resumes, interview preparation, job searching, career assessments, goal setting, job referrals and placement, reemployment services for people receiving unemployment benefits, and access to ARIZONA@WORK resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Employment Service is open to all job seekers and employers. Specialized programs such as veterans, Vocational Rehabilitation, SNAP CAN, TANF Jobs, youth, SCSEP, and reentry have separate eligibility rules.

**Population Served**
Arizona job seekers and employers, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents who need general workforce help. Veterans, people with disabilities, older workers, youth, reentry clients, and benefit-linked participants may be routed to specialized services.

**How to Best Connect**
Get help in person at an ARIZONA@WORK office, by phone at 1-833-762-8196, or online through a Google Meet appointment from the DES Job Seekers page. Mesa clients can use the East Valley Career Center at 1001 W. Southern Ave., Suite 101.

**Important Information to Know**
Workforce specialists cannot resolve unemployment claim questions; DES lists 1-877-600-2722 for unemployment claim help. Training funds or specialized services require separate eligibility screening.

resources.name: Maricopa County Department of Public Health - STI & HIV Clinic, Mesa, with Same-Day PrEP Navigation
resources.description: Maricopa County's Mesa STI/HIV clinic offers appointment and walk-in STI and HIV services, including STI testing/treatment, HIV and hepatitis C testing as available, and PrEP/nPEP navigation with same-day PrEP starter prescriptions for eligible STI clinic patients.
resources.address: 1950 S. Country Club Dr., Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 8:00 AM-12:00 PM and 1:00 PM-5:00 PM; Wednesday 9:00 AM-12:00 PM and 1:00 PM-5:00 PM. Clinics close daily 12:00 PM-1:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
STI testing and treatment for chlamydia, gonorrhea and syphilis; HIV and hepatitis C testing as available; online result access; and PrEP/nPEP education, navigation and linkage to community providers. County award-program information states eligible STI clinic patients may receive a 28-day same-day PrEP starter prescription while being linked to ongoing care.

**Eligibility Requirements**
County STI/HIV clinics welcome appointments and walk-ins. The same-day PrEP pathway is for eligible patients attending MCDPH STI clinics who would benefit from PrEP. Public pages do not list a county residency requirement.

**Population Served**
People seeking STI/HIV testing, treatment or HIV prevention support in Mesa and Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-506-7218 or schedule online from the county STI/HIV page. Mesa clinic: 1950 S. Country Club Dr., Mesa, AZ 85210. For walk-ins, arrive before 11:00 AM or before 3:00 PM to improve the chance of same-day care.

**Important Information to Know**
There is a $20 STI clinic visit fee, and patients are seen regardless of insurance status or ability to use insurance. This is focused STI/HIV/HCV and PrEP/PEP prevention care, not a full primary-care clinic. Walk-ins are accepted but same-day care is not guaranteed.

resources.name: Maricopa County Human Services Department - Early Head Start and Head Start
resources.description: Maricopa County Early Head Start and Head Start are no-cost family-centered early education and school-readiness programs for qualifying families with children from six weeks through age five, including Mesa and East Valley locations.
resources.address: 1001 W. Southern Ave., Suite 106, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Apply online, by phone, or at the Mesa office; classroom schedules and openings vary by site.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost Early Head Start and Head Start early education, school readiness, screenings, family support, health/well-being and parent engagement. Disability/special-health-care coordination includes work with school districts and AzEIP, with disability enrollment slots and plan-based services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For the 2026–2027 school year, families must live or work in the service area and meet the programme’s child-age rules, generally 6 weeks through age 5 before kindergarten eligibility. Public assistance, foster care, homelessness, income up to 130% of federal poverty guidelines or an excessive-housing-cost adjustment may establish eligibility. Ask about Early Head Start options during pregnancy and the specific disability-service plan.

**Population Served**
Mesa and East Valley families with infants, toddlers, and preschool-age children, including low-income families, foster children, children experiencing homelessness, children with special needs, teen parents, and grandparents or kin raising children.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through the county page, visit the Mesa office at 1001 W. Southern Ave., Suite 106, or call 602-372-3700 to complete an application with a Family Support Specialist.

**Important Information to Know**
Application does not guarantee placement. Ask about site, age group, waitlist, accommodations and documents; the county currently notes Lattie Coor’s full waitlist. Disability services may involve AzEIP, the school district, classroom or home, according to the child’s plan.

resources.name: Arizona Association for Foster and Adoptive Parents / Jose's Closet - Emma's Eats Food Bank
resources.description: Jose's Closet in Mesa includes Emma's Eats, a food bank serving foster, kinship and adoptive families through a foster-family resource center.
resources.address: 6515 East Main Street Ste 120, Mesa, AZ 85205
resources.hours: Tuesday-Saturday 11:00 AM-3:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emma's Eats is a food bank inside Jose's Closet. Jose's Closet also provides free access to donated clothing, toys, baby gear and other essentials for foster, kinship and adoptive families.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The page identifies Jose's Closet as a resource for foster, kinship and adoptive families. It does not fully state documentation rules for Emma's Eats, so families should ask whether proof of foster, kinship, guardianship or adoptive placement is required.

**Population Served**
Foster, kinship and adoptive families in Mesa and Arizona who need food and essential items for children in their care.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit during posted hours, call 480-309-1743, email info@josescloset.org, or use the contact form on the Jose's Closet page. The Mesa location is 6515 East Main Street Ste 120.

**Important Information to Know**
Emma's Eats is population-specific and may not be a general public pantry. Confirm membership or documentation expectations before sending a family for food.

resources.name: Resurrection Street Ministry - Veterans Transportation
resources.description: Resurrection Street Ministry Veteran Ride Service provides free, appointment-based non-emergency transportation for East Valley Veterans to VA medical appointments and Veteran service organizations, including the Gilbert VA clinic, Phoenix VA hospital, Mesa Vet Center, DAV, and other registered Veteran service offices.
resources.address: 1135 East Main Street, Mesa, AZ 85203
resources.hours: By appointment only.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
RSM Veteran Ride Service provides non-emergency transportation for Veterans in the East Valley to medical appointments and Veteran service organizations. Public listings identify rides to the Gilbert VA Clinic, Phoenix VA Hospital, Mesa Vet Center, DAV Chapter 8, and other registered Veteran service offices.

**Eligibility Requirements**
RSM’s page identifies the service for local Veterans in need in Fountain Hills, Chandler, Mesa, Tempe, Gilbert, and Apache Junction. City of Mesa and 2-1-1 listings specify homeless, low-income, or disabled East Valley Veterans, and 2-1-1 lists VA card or DD-214 with photo ID requirements and possible income proof for more than one ride every six months.

**Population Served**
East Valley Veterans, including Mesa Veterans, especially those who are homeless, low income, or disabled and need non-emergency transportation to VA or Veteran service appointments.

**How to Best Connect**
Request a ride through the provider’s appointment number, 405-386-7799, or ResurrectionStreetMinistry@gmail.com. General RSM information is 480-615-2799. Call well ahead; 2-1-1 lists at least 72 hours notice. Confirm pickup/destination and documents rather than travelling to the organization’s 1135 E. Main St. site for a ride.

**Important Information to Know**
Rides are free and by appointment, subject to drivers and trip approval; drivers do not accept tips. This is non-emergency transport, not cash assistance. Ask about vehicle accessibility, mobility equipment and repeat-ride documentation. RSM food services are a separate programme.

resources.name: Pacific Developmental Abilities LLC - Habilitation and Community Based Services
resources.description: Pacific Developmental Abilities LLC offers Mesa-area HCBS for children and adults with developmental disabilities, including attendant care, habilitation, respite, IDLA and DDD-authorized transportation to employment.
resources.hours: Call or schedule an appointment through the website; public office hours were not listed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Home and community-based services for children and adults with developmental disabilities, including attendant care for daily living and safety, habilitation for independent-living skills, respite care for caregivers, individually designed living arrangement habilitation, and transportation to employment when approved by DES DDD.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are for children and adults with developmental disabilities. Transportation-related services are described for members approved by Arizona DES Division of Developmental Disabilities; other services may also require DDD authorization or another payer.

**Population Served**
Children and adults with developmental disabilities and their caregivers in the Mesa area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-226-7458, email info@pacificdevelopmental.com or puhegwu@cox.net, or use the website appointment/contact link. Ask about DDD authorization, available direct-care workers, location coverage and current openings.

**Important Information to Know**
The official page does not show a street address in the accessible text. Confirm service radius, funding source, staffing availability and whether the specific service can be provided at the client's Mesa address.

resources.name: AHCCCS — Medical Assistance applications and community assistors
resources.description: AHCCCS Medical Assistance can be applied for online through Health-e-Arizona Plus, by printed application, by phone and through community assistors; the official page also lists processing periods and more than 150 community-partner assistors using HEAplus.
resources.hours: HEAplus/DES phone help is commonly listed as Monday-Friday business hours; use the website for online application access. Community-assistor hours vary by partner.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Online, paper, telephone and community-assistor routes for AHCCCS Medical Assistance, KidsCare and related categories. Health-e-Arizona Plus also handles Nutrition and Cash Assistance applications. AHCCCS lists regional behavioural-health/substance-use contacts for people awaiting a decision or not eligible for medical coverage; ALTCS registration is a separate long-term-care process.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on Arizona residency, income/resources, household category, age, pregnancy, disability, immigration/citizenship status and program-specific rules. AHCCCS lists different processing periods by program and circumstances.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents, who may qualify for Medicaid/AHCCCS medical coverage, KidsCare, Medicare Savings Programs or related medical-assistance categories.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through Health-e-Arizona Plus or call 855-432-7587; use the community-assistor finder for partner help. AHCCCS general information is 602-417-4000 or 800-654-8713. For Maricopa/Central Arizona RBHA-funded behavioural-health access, ask 800-564-5465 about the applicable pathway.

**Important Information to Know**
Applications do not guarantee approval or immediate coverage. Keep proof requests and renewal letters current. Each benefit and RBHA service has its own eligibility; this is not a veterans-only programme. HEAplus supports English and Spanish; ALTCS requires separate financial and medical screening.

resources.name: Narcotics Anonymous - East Valley Area Meetings and Helpline
resources.description: Arizona Region of Narcotics Anonymous East Valley Area provides meeting information, a local helpline, service-area contact information, meeting map access, and peer support for people seeking recovery from drug addiction.
resources.address: PO Box 5264, Mesa, AZ 85211
resources.hours: Meeting times vary by group; helpline availability should be confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Peer-led Narcotics Anonymous recovery meetings, East Valley Area meeting information, local helpline, statewide phone-line links, meeting map, virtual meeting links, and NA recovery fellowship.

**Eligibility Requirements**
NA is for people who want recovery from drug addiction. Meeting formats vary by group; check whether a meeting is open, closed, virtual, or in person before attending.

**Population Served**
People seeking drug-addiction peer recovery support in Mesa, the East Valley, Maricopa County, and statewide Arizona communities.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the East Valley helpline at 480-897-4636 or use the Arizona NA East Valley Area page and meeting links. The East Valley service mailing address is PO Box 5264, Mesa, AZ 85211. Use the Arizona NA website’s Reuniones en español link to find Spanish meetings and confirm the current listing.

**Important Information to Know**
NA is peer support, not licensed treatment, detox, medication treatment, or emergency care. People with dangerous withdrawal, overdose risk, or acute crisis need medical or crisis help in addition to meetings.

resources.name: Gila River Health Care · Substance Use Services
resources.description: Gila River Health Care substance-use services through Behavioral Health, including addiction medicine, outpatient treatment, IOP, Matrix stimulant-use treatment, continuing care, Thwajik Ki residential treatment and transitional living for eligible Native American clients.
resources.address: 3850 N 16th St, Laveen, AZ 85339
resources.hours: OASIS outpatient services: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; youth evening hours may vary by client need.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Gila River Health Care Behavioral Health provides substance-use services including addiction medicine, assessment and treatment for alcohol and other drug addiction, medication-assisted treatment for alcohol, opioid and tobacco addiction, OASIS outpatient services, intensive outpatient programming, Matrix stimulant-use treatment, continuing care, Thwajik Ki residential treatment and a transitional living program after residential completion.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Thwajik Ki states that any Native American from a federally recognized tribe is eligible. Individuals do not need AHCCCS for admission, although AHCCCS is preferable. Residential clients must present sober and free of withdrawal symptoms; impaired individuals are referred to detox first. Admission with a sexual-offense history is reviewed individually.

**Population Served**
Eligible Native American clients, including people from federally recognized tribes. This should not be presented as public addiction treatment for all Mesa residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Thwajik Ki Residential Treatment Center at 520-796-3860 for residential questions. OASIS outpatient services operate Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM. Ask which Gila River Health Care campus or outpatient clinic is appropriate, and confirm referral, transportation and detox requirements before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
Gila River Health Care is highly relevant for eligible Native American clients in the Mesa/Maricopa area but eligibility is tied to tribal/Native American status. Residential treatment is a minimum of 16 weeks and may be extended; transitional living requires a separate application after residential completion.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Education — Secondary Transition Support
resources.description: State guidance, planning tools and a support-request route for IEP transition from school to employment, further education and independent living.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

State guidance, planning tools and a support-request route for IEP transition from school to employment, further education and independent living.

**Eligibility Requirements**

For Arizona students with disabilities, families and education teams working on secondary transition. The local IEP team arranges the student’s actual services.

**Population Served**

Students with IEPs and their families or school teams across Arizona.

**How to Best Connect**

Use the Secondary Transition Support Request or team email link on the ADE page. Explain the planning or school-system question.

**Important Information to Know**

This is information and technical support, not an adult-service placement, benefit award or legal representative. Keep the student’s goals central to the IEP discussion.

resources.name: Maricopa County Superior Court - Protective Order offices and Domestic Violence Advocates
resources.description: Maricopa County Superior Court Protective Order offices help people use AZPOINT and court processes for orders of protection and injunctions, with domestic violence advocates available at court locations and remote or onsite hearing options.
resources.address: 222 E Javelina Ave, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: LLRC locations generally Monday-Friday 8:00 am-5:00 pm.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Protective-order office help for Orders of Protection, Injunctions Against Harassment and Injunctions Against Workplace Harassment. AZPOINT helps prepare petitions, and court staff can process remote or onsite hearing requests. Domestic violence lay legal advocates are linked from the protective-order page.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people seeking protection from domestic or family violence, harassment or workplace harassment. A petition must be filed with a court and heard by a judge. Relationship and incident requirements depend on the type of order requested.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County residents and other Arizona protective-order petitioners, including domestic violence survivors using the Southeast Justice Center in Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete AZPOINT until it is court-ready and gives a confirmation number. For a remote hearing, call 602-506-7353 with the confirmation number. For onsite filing, bring the confirmation number to a Superior Court location such as Southeast Justice Center, 222 E Javelina Ave, Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
If in immediate danger, call 911. Protective orders do not guarantee safety and cannot resolve landlord-tenant disputes or change custody/visitation orders. Orders become enforceable only after service, and service rules differ by order type.

resources.name: AZLawHelp — statewide legal-aid screening
resources.description: Online and telephone screening for free or reduced-fee legal assistance, with a provider directory.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Online and telephone screening for free or reduced-fee legal assistance, with a provider directory.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Provider eligibility depends on income, location, case type, conflicts and capacity.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents seeking civil legal assistance.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 866-637-5341 or use Apply Online on AZLawHelp. Follow any instructions to complete intake with the receiving provider.

**Important Information to Know**
Screening is not acceptance or legal representation. The site is being rebuilt; some legal-information content is not currently available.

resources.name: Terros Health - Transitional Aged Youth Housing / DCS Transitional Housing Program
resources.description: Terros Health Transitional Aged Youth Housing is a DCS-partnered housing support for young adults ages 18-21 transitioning out of foster care, with furnished apartment-style housing and supportive services.
resources.address: 3003 N Central Ave, Suite 400, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Small, furnished apartment-style housing with supportive services for independent adulthood, including help connected to education, vocational training, transportation, financial literacy, nutrition and healthcare resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Official Terros information says the program serves individuals ages 18-21 transitioning out of the foster care system through a partnership with the Arizona Department of Child Safety. Referral is likely through DCS or Terros screening.

**Population Served**
Transition-age youth ages 18-21 leaving foster care in Arizona.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Terros Health at 602-685-6000 or email info@terroshealth.org and ask about Transitional Aged Youth Housing. Youth with a DCS caseworker should also ask the caseworker about referral eligibility.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm current referral requirements, service area and openings with Terros or DCS before arranging a referral.

resources.name: Maricopa County Bar — Lawyer Referral Service
resources.description: Provides a paid consultation route when nonprofit immigration legal services do not fit.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides a paid consultation route when nonprofit immigration legal services do not fit.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Ask for an attorney in the relevant practice area; the ordinary referral consultation costs $50 for 30 minutes.

**Population Served**
People able to use a limited paid legal consultation.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-257-4434 and request an immigration-law referral.

**Important Information to Know**
Further work and fees are agreed separately with the attorney; this is not free representation.

resources.name: Executive Office for Immigration Review - Phoenix Immigration Court
resources.description: The EOIR Phoenix Immigration Court is the official non-detained immigration court access point for people with Phoenix court hearings. It provides court address, filing-window hours, general inquiry contact, asylum EAD clock contact, and links to EOIR self-help and court-procedure resources.
resources.address: 250 N 7th Ave, Suite 300, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.hours: Public hours Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM; window filing hours 8:00 AM-4:00 PM, except federal holidays and emergency closures
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Phoenix Immigration Court handles immigration court proceedings under the Executive Office for Immigration Review. The official page provides the court address, public and filing hours, general inquiry email and phone, asylum EAD clock request email, court procedures, observation rules, and links to self-help and EOIR resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
This is for people with matters before the Phoenix Immigration Court or people needing court-specific information. A client should follow the address and instructions on their own hearing notice, because hearing location and case status control where they must appear.

**Population Served**
People in immigration proceedings assigned to the Phoenix Immigration Court, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents whose notices list this court.

**How to Best Connect**
For general court inquiries, email Phoenix.Immigration.Court@usdoj.gov or call 602-640-2747. The court is at 250 N 7th Ave, Suite 300, Phoenix, AZ 85007. Public hours are Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM and window filing hours are 8:00 AM-4:00 PM, except federal holidays and unexpected closures.

**Important Information to Know**
The court is not a legal-aid provider and cannot act as the client's attorney. Confirm the hearing notice, case status, and address before travel. Security screening is required, and unauthorized electronic submissions are discarded unless specifically requested by court staff or an immigration judge.

resources.name: Mesa Community College · Learning Enhancement Center Tutoring
resources.description: Mesa Community College Learning Enhancement Center offers free in-person, virtual, and online tutoring and learning support for current MCC students in courses where they are currently enrolled.
resources.address: 1833 W. Southern Ave., Mesa, AZ 85202; Red Mountain Campus: 7110 E. McKellips Rd., Mesa, AZ 85207; MCC Online
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
MCC's Learning Enhancement Center offers free in-person, virtual, and online tutoring across many academic subjects. The center also offers personalized learning support, embedded tutoring, bootcamp workshops, and subject-specific tutoring locations across campus.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Tutoring is available to current MCC students and only for courses in which the student is currently enrolled at MCC. Most tutoring does not require an appointment, but Japanese tutoring requires scheduling in advance.

**Population Served**
Current Mesa Community College students who need help with coursework, study skills, writing, reading, math, science, nursing, computer science, ESL-related coursework, or other supported subjects.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the MCC Tutoring page to find subject-specific tutoring locations and online or virtual options. For campus contact, call Southern and Dobson at 480-461-7000 or Red Mountain at 480-654-7200.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not public tutoring for nonstudents. Students who need disability accommodations should coordinate with MCC Disability Resources and Services as needed.

resources.name: Phoenix Indian Center / Urban Indian Coalition of Arizona - Prevention Services and Suicide Prevention Trainings
resources.description: Phoenix Indian Center and the Urban Indian Coalition of Arizona provide culturally responsive prevention services, including suicide-prevention trainings, substance-misuse prevention, youth and family programming, and coalition meetings.
resources.address: 4041 N Central Ave, Building B, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.hours: Program schedules vary; coalition and training dates are posted on the Prevention Services page and calendar.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Suicide prevention awareness, safeTALK, QPR, ASIST, substance-misuse prevention, Living in 2 Worlds youth programming, Parenting in 2 Worlds, Gathering of Native Americans, virtual webinars, and Urban Indian Coalition of Arizona meetings.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Program-specific requirements apply. The page identifies some trainings and gatherings as open to ages 15 and older, American Indian middle/high school students, parents or guardians of American Indian youth, or trained/workforce suicide-prevention participants.

**Population Served**
Urban American Indian youth, families, parents, caregivers, community members, and prevention partners in the Phoenix area, with some virtual options.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-264-6768 or email UICAZ@phxindcenter.org for prevention trainings and coalition information. Use the event registration links for specific workshops.

**Important Information to Know**
This is prevention, education, and community support, not individual therapy, psychiatric care, or crisis response. Use 988 or emergency services for immediate suicide or safety concerns.

resources.name: Compudopt - Mesa Computer Giveaway and Compudopt Connect Internet
resources.description: Compudopt offers a Mesa computer giveaway registration and low-cost 5G internet options through Compudopt Connect, with address checks and eligibility based on qualifying programs or income.
resources.hours: Online registration; support by phone or email. Giveaway dates and internet fulfillment depend on program availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Compudopt offers digital-skills learning, English/Spanish online computer tutorials and periodic local classes, including adult learning options. A separate Mesa computer giveaway serves qualifying households, and Compudopt Connect offers low-cost 5G internet subject to address coverage.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Class requirements vary; do not apply the giveaway’s K–12 rule to all learning. The household computer giveaway requires a child in K–12 education and no working family-owned computer; a school-owned loaner does not count. Connect internet uses separate qualifying-benefit or income-below-200%-FPL criteria and a service-address check.

**Population Served**
Under-resourced youth, families and communities needing computers or internet access, including Mesa households for the listed giveaway.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Mesa programme page for classes, online lessons and the separate Mesa Giveaway registration. For internet, use the Connect address-check and ordering process. Call 855-532-5060 or email info@compudopt.org for help; confirm the actual event/pickup location.

**Important Information to Know**
Registration does not guarantee a computer; selection depends on stock. A past class’s laptop award is not a promise for future classes. Internet may require router, monthly or prepaid charges and can have a waitlist. No Houston-headquarters pickup is implied for Mesa applicants.

resources.name: Remote Area Medical — Free clinic event finder
resources.description: Find scheduled free medical, dental and vision clinic events and check whether a location is accessible.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Find scheduled free medical, dental and vision clinic events and check whether a location is accessible.

**Eligibility Requirements**
RAM says its events welcome everyone without ID, income proof or insurance; services are first-come, first-served and event-specific.

**Population Served**
People able to attend a scheduled RAM clinic, including uninsured patients.

**How to Best Connect**
Check the live clinic schedule and the selected event’s patient instructions before arranging travel.

**Important Information to Know**
No current Mesa or Maricopa event is confirmed here. This is a reserve event-finding route, not an available local appointment.

resources.name: Valleywise Health - Women's Refugee Services / Refugee Women's Health Clinic
resources.description: Valleywise Women's Refugee Services provides culturally and linguistically responsive women's health, maternity, prenatal, antepartum, postpartum and gynecologic care, using Cultural Health Navigators to help refugee women and children access care.
resources.address: Valleywise Comprehensive Health Center - Phoenix, 2525 E. Roosevelt St., Phoenix, AZ 85008; West Maryvale clinic also listed
resources.hours: Phoenix Comprehensive Health Center clinic hours vary by individual clinic; West Maryvale is listed Monday-Friday 7:00 AM-6:00 PM. Call scheduling for current refugee clinic appointments.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Women's Refugee Services provides gynecological services, full maternity care, antepartum and postpartum care, health navigation, interpretation support through Cultural Health Navigators, monthly educational classes for childbirth and newborn care, physical activity and nutrition classes, sexual health education, reproductive life planning and outreach/health education activities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is designed for refugee women and their children needing culturally responsive women's health or maternity care. Standard Valleywise scheduling, coverage and financial-assistance processes may apply.

**Population Served**
Refugee women, soon-to-be mothers and children in the Phoenix/Maricopa County Valleywise service area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Valleywise scheduling at 1-833-855-9973 and ask for Women's Refugee Services or the Refugee Women's Health Clinic. The listed locations are Valleywise Comprehensive Health Center - Phoenix, 2525 E. Roosevelt St., and Valleywise Community Health Center - West Maryvale.

**Important Information to Know**
This is women’s health/maternity care and navigation, not immigration casework. Listed service locations are Phoenix and West Maryvale, not a confirmed Mesa clinic. Call to confirm the exact appointment site, insurance/fees, transport and availability before travelling.

resources.name: Maricopa County Department of Public Health - East Valley / Mesa Children's Immunization Clinic
resources.description: Maricopa County Department of Public Health East/Mesa immunization clinic providing routine vaccines for children from birth through age 18, with appointments primarily scheduled online or by phone and no out-of-pocket cost for uninsured children per county clinic flyer.
resources.address: 1950 S. Country Club Dr., Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday 8 AM-4:30 PM; Wednesday 9 AM-4:30 PM; closed Saturday/Sunday and county holidays; lunch closure may apply.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Routine child immunizations for children from birth through age 18 at the county East/Mesa clinic.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The county immunization page says clinics serve children from birth through age 18. Bring the child needing vaccines, immunization record, and insurance card if insured. County flyer evidence says uninsured children can be seen with no out-of-pocket cost.

**Population Served**
Children and families in Maricopa County, including Mesa-area children needing school, child care, or routine vaccinations.

**How to Best Connect**
Schedule online through Maricopa County or call the CARES Team at 602-506-6767. The Mesa clinic is at 1950 S. Country Club Dr., Mesa, AZ 85210. Appointments are primary; walk-ins may be limited.

**Important Information to Know**
Call or schedule before going to confirm vaccine availability, current clinic hours, holiday or special closures, lunch closure and required documents.

resources.name: Phoenix Computer Academy High-Impact IT, Project Management, and Systems Support Training
resources.description: Phoenix Computer Academy offers IT, project management, office administration, web design, and certification-oriented training from Phoenix and Gilbert campuses, including an East Campus near Mesa.
resources.address: East Campus: 725 W. Elliot Rd., Suite 112, Gilbert, AZ; Phoenix Campus: 1215 E. Elm St., Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Training programs aligned to industry jobs, including computer networking, cybersecurity, cloud computing, Linux certifications, database administration and data analytics, computer hardware/software support, IT project management, PMP, Agile certifications, human resources certifications, Microsoft Office, QuickBooks, and web design.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official programs page does not publish a single eligibility checklist. Applicants should confirm admissions requirements, course prerequisites, schedule, costs, certification exam fees, WIOA or grant funding availability, and whether the chosen program is offered at the Gilbert East Campus.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County learners seeking IT, project management, systems support, office, or web-related training, including Mesa-area clients able to attend the Gilbert East Campus.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-321-3023 and ask about current program dates, East Campus availability, total cost, funding, and employment assistance. East Campus: 725 W. Elliot Rd., Suite 112, Gilbert, AZ 85232.

**Important Information to Know**
The official site confirms programs and campuses but is limited on costs, current cohorts, funding, and job-placement detail. Verify all program-specific terms before referral.

resources.name: City of Mesa - @Mesa Public WiFi
resources.description: Free municipal Wi-Fi in downtown Mesa and at listed City parks, aquatics facilities, and many City buildings.
resources.hours: Varies by access-point location; some sites have restricted hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
City of Mesa provides free public Wi-Fi under the @mesa network in downtown Mesa and at multiple parks, aquatics facilities, and inside or around most City buildings.

**Eligibility Requirements**
No income or residency requirement is stated. Users need their own Wi-Fi-capable device and must be at or near a covered location.

**Population Served**
People in Mesa who need no-cost internet access while near a City public Wi-Fi location.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the City's Wi-Fi location map to find a nearby access point. For questions, call 480-644-4442 or email wifi@mesaaz.gov.

**Important Information to Know**
Coverage is location-specific, and some sites have restricted hours. This is public access Wi-Fi, not home internet service or device assistance.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Child Safety - Youth Driver Education Program
resources.description: Arizona Department of Child Safety's Youth Driver Education Program helps eligible foster youth learn about driving and car ownership, including permit preparation, ADOT-required training, behind-the-wheel instruction, and support toward a driver's license.
resources.address: 3003 N. Central Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Youth Driver Education Program teaches youth in foster care about driving and car ownership. Public DCS information describes classroom preparation for the permit test, behind-the-wheel instruction, ADOT-required training, and support toward a state-issued driver's license.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is for youth in foster care who are eligible to obtain a learner's permit. Related DCS youth transition information says the DCS Specialist and adults involved with the youth provide information and support for youth interested in permits or licenses.

**Population Served**
Arizona foster youth, including Maricopa County youth in care, who are old enough and otherwise eligible to pursue a learner's permit or driver's license.

**How to Best Connect**
The youth or caregiver should ask the youth's DCS Specialist or case team about the current Youth Driver Education referral pathway, required approvals, caregiver sign-off, and available driving-school slots.

**Important Information to Know**
Public evidence is primarily DCS program information and news. Do not send a youth directly to a general office for enrollment; the responsible route is through the assigned DCS team.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Economic Security - The Emergency Food Assistance Program (TEFAP)
resources.description: Arizona TEFAP provides emergency food through local congregate meal and food package distribution sites; clients use partner sites rather than applying directly to DES.
resources.hours: Distribution schedules vary by site.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Emergency Food Assistance Program provides emergency food through local distribution sites, including prepared congregate meals at some sites and food packages at others.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For congregate meals, DES describes no formal application; a person goes to a site and states need. TEFAP food packages require application at a distribution site and household gross income at or below 185% of the federal poverty level; confirm current documentation requirements with the site.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents seeking emergency food, including Mesa and Maricopa County households using participating food banks, pantries or meal sites.

**How to Best Connect**
Use a current local food finder such as AZ Food Help or United Food Bank to identify the nearest participating TEFAP distribution site, then contact or visit that site according to its posted schedule.

**Important Information to Know**
TEFAP is a funding and food-supply pathway, not one single public pickup location. Eligibility, documents and hours depend on the local partner site. Homebound clients should ask the local site about alternate application or delivery options.

resources.name: State Bar of Arizona — free clinics and phone banks
resources.description: Event-based brief legal consultations and legal-topic phone banks organized by the Public Service Center and partners.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Event-based brief legal consultations and legal-topic phone banks organized by the Public Service Center and partners.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Registration, topics, locations and capacity differ by event.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents seeking brief help with a topic offered at a current event.

**How to Best Connect**
Check the current event page. A Glendale clinic is listed for October 13, 2026; registration is through PSC@staff.azbar.org or 602-340-7293.

**Important Information to Know**
Events do not provide continuous intake or promise ongoing representation. The October 21 veterans-benefits phone bank publishes its call number during the broadcast; the registration number is not that phone-bank line.

resources.name: Keys to Change - Keys to Freedom reentry and homelessness navigation lead
resources.description: Keys to Change is a Maricopa County homelessness-services nonprofit. The assigned Keys to Freedom reentry lead appears tied to homelessness and legal-history barriers, while current public intake is through Keys to Change's low-barrier Key Campus and Get Help/contact routes rather than a clearly published Keys to Freedom application.
resources.address: 204 S. 12th Avenue, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.hours: Keys to Change states its staff and volunteers are open 24/7 to provide low-barrier services; confirm the specific Keys to Freedom availability before promising program entry.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Keys to Change provides low-barrier homelessness services, client-centered programs, partner navigation, housing-focused intervention and countywide collaborations. The Keys to Freedom lead describes reentry navigation, peer support, legal advocacy, housing, employment and legal-barrier resolution for recently released people experiencing homelessness, but a current public program page for that specific grant track was not found.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Current official Keys to Change pages state the organization serves single adults experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County. Keys to Freedom-specific eligibility, referral priority and opening status should be confirmed with Keys to Change before referral.

**Population Served**
Single adults experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County, including people returning from jail or prison who also need homelessness navigation and stabilization.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Get Help route on the Keys to Change website or call 602-282-0853. The Key Campus address is 204 S. 12th Avenue, Phoenix, AZ 85007. Ask specifically whether Keys to Freedom or another reentry navigator is available for the client's release status and Mesa/Maricopa County connection.

**Important Information to Know**
Do not present this as guaranteed housing, legal representation or employment placement. The supported current public route is Keys to Change homelessness navigation; the named Keys to Freedom grant program needs confirmation for current intake and capacity.
resources.resolutionReason: Confirm the current named Keys to Freedom programme and referral route; general Keys to Change navigation remains independently usable.

resources.name: Labor Temps Mesa Industrial and General Staffing
resources.description: Labor Temps, Inc. is a Mesa staffing service specializing in industrial, skilled, semi-skilled, and general labor positions, with an online application route and stated fast-pay process.
resources.address: 525 S. Gilbert Rd., Suite A-4, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Temporary skilled, semi-skilled, industrial, warehouse, construction, assembly, driving, office, housekeeping, janitorial, and general labor staffing. The site links to an online application and says paychecks are available within 24 hours of completed jobs, except Friday work.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The site does not list a complete worker eligibility checklist. Applicants should confirm active openings, required identification and work authorization, any screening, transportation expectations, and whether a specific assignment requires tools, safety gear, or prior experience.

**Population Served**
Mesa and East Valley job seekers pursuing industrial, warehouse, construction, housekeeping, janitorial, driving, office, or general labor work.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the online application link on the official website, call 480-969-7009, email labortemps@labortempsaz.com, or contact the office at 525 S. Gilbert Rd., Suite A-4, Mesa, AZ 85204.

**Important Information to Know**
The site is sparse on application hours, fees, pay timing details, transportation, and current assignments. Call before visiting if the client needs same-day work or has limited transportation.

resources.name: Mom's Pantry
resources.description: Mom's Pantry is a Phoenix community food bank open on weekends; useful as a Maricopa County reserve option for clients who can travel.
resources.address: 13440 N Cave Creek Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85022
resources.hours: Saturday 10:00 AM-2:00 PM; Sunday 10:00 AM-1:00 PM. Check Get Help page for holiday hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Mom's Pantry is a community food bank providing food to families experiencing hardship.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The opened official page does not state Mesa-specific eligibility, documentation or service-area restrictions. Confirm details before referral.

**Population Served**
People and families facing food insecurity who can access the north Phoenix pantry.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit 13440 N Cave Creek Rd, Phoenix during weekend pantry hours, call 602-992-0083 or email info@momspantryphoenix.org.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a Phoenix-based reserve option, not a Mesa-local pantry. Transportation from Mesa may be significant, and holiday hours may differ.

resources.name: Seniors Personal Assistance Corporation - No-Cost Senior Benefits and Prescription Assistance Consultation
resources.description: Seniors Personal Assistance Corporation is a Mesa nonprofit that provides no-cost senior consultation and information about benefit programs, including prescription-drug assistance, food stamps, food boxes, utility assistance, free cell phone programs, Medicare cost sharing and Medicare plan referrals.
resources.address: 1255 W. Baseline Road #D186, Mesa, AZ 85202
resources.hours: Official page does not post service hours. Call before visiting or referring.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost senior consultation and resource information for benefit programs, including prescription-drug financial assistance, drug discount cards, Food Stamps, food boxes, electric utility assistance, free cell phone programs, estate planning forms and resources, vital-document reviews, State Health Insurance and Medicare cost sharing, and Medicare plan assistance or referrals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page describes services for seniors struggling to manage bills, prescriptions and medical costs, but does not publish income, document, residence, insurance or appointment rules.

**Population Served**
Seniors in the Mesa area seeking benefit-program information, food assistance referrals, prescription affordability help or Medicare-related assistance.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-278-9194 before visiting or referring. Ask what services are currently offered directly, whether an appointment is required, and what documents are needed.

**Important Information to Know**
Consultation is described as no cost. Ask which services are provided directly versus referred, including food boxes, and confirm appointments, documents and current benefit terms. The listing does not establish a walk-in pantry or guaranteed free phone. Use Arizona SHIP for independent Medicare-plan counselling and clarify any plan-related referral.

resources.name: Phoenix Children's - Ophthalmology plus Financial Assistance
resources.description: Phoenix Children's Ophthalmology provides pediatric ophthalmology and optometry services for common, complex and rare eye conditions, including Mesa location access, adult strabismus care and financial assistance for eligible medically necessary care.
resources.address: Mesa ophthalmology location: 2045 S. Vineyard, Suite 137, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Clinic hours vary by location and appointment; call for scheduling. Financial Counseling phone hours are Monday-Friday 7:00 AM-6:30 PM Arizona time.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Eye testing and treatment for common, complex and rare eye conditions; pediatric ophthalmology and optometry; emergency eye-care coordination through Phoenix Children's emergency departments; laser pediatric refractive surgery; corneal collagen cross-linking; and care for children and adults with strabismus. Financial counselors can help families understand insurance, AHCCCS/coverage options and Phoenix Children's financial assistance.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Appointments and referrals may be required depending on the condition and payer. Phoenix Children's financial assistance is for eligible emergency or medically necessary care and is based in part on family income; families must complete an application and provide documentation.

**Population Served**
Children with eye conditions and adults with strabismus, including East Valley families who can use the Mesa ophthalmology location.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Ophthalmology at 602-933-3937. For financial assistance questions, call Phoenix Children's Financial Counseling at 602-933-2000. Mesa location: 2045 S. Vineyard, Suite 137, Mesa, AZ 85210.

**Important Information to Know**
Financial assistance applies to eligible medically necessary care, not necessarily routine glasses. Insurance authorization and referrals may be needed. The policy states emergency medical conditions are treated regardless of ability to pay.

resources.name: Unhooked Recovery - Mesa Detox, Residential, and Outpatient Services
resources.description: Unhooked Recovery provides Mesa residential substance-use treatment, outpatient services, detox services, assessment, counseling, family services, trauma therapy, case management and recovery supports.
resources.address: Residential/detox: 215 S Power Rd, Mesa, AZ 85206; outpatient: 5801 E Main St, Mesa, AZ 85205
resources.hours: Hours are not listed on the page reviewed; call the relevant service number for admissions and current availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Residential alcohol and substance-use treatment, outpatient services, detox services, assessment, counseling, family services, trauma therapy, case management, sober-living/recovery supports and medically assisted treatment approach.

**Eligibility Requirements**
People seeking substance-use treatment may inquire. Admission depends on clinical assessment, level of care, payer or grant funding and current capacity.

**Population Served**
Men and women with substance-use disorders in Mesa and the East Valley. The official page states the organization does not discriminate by ancestry, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, disability, familial status or national origin.

**How to Best Connect**
Call residential services at 602-368-4471, outpatient services at 602-368-3114, or detox services at 480-309-1635. Use the online information request form if phone contact is not possible.

**Important Information to Know**
Detox, residential and outpatient services use different locations and phone numbers. Confirm the right level of care, transportation, payment or Substance Use Block Grant availability and current opening before referral.

resources.name: ASU Law Post-Conviction Clinic
resources.description: ASU Law Post-Conviction Clinic investigates and litigates Arizona wrongful-conviction and manifest-injustice cases, but does not accept direct outside referrals; potential clients must contact Arizona Justice Project.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The ASU Law Post-Conviction Clinic investigates claims of wrongful conviction and manifest injustice from prisoners convicted of crimes in Arizona. Students may work on post-conviction relief, habeas, forensic testing, parole, and clemency matters, and may represent clients in court or before the Arizona Board of Executive Clemency.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The matter must be an Arizona post-conviction claim fitting the clinic's work and accepted through the Arizona Justice Project referral route. The clinic does not accept direct outside referrals or direct service inquiries.

**Population Served**
People unable to afford legal representation who have Arizona post-conviction wrongful-conviction or manifest-injustice claims and are referred through Arizona Justice Project.

**How to Best Connect**
Do not contact the clinic directly for service. Contact Arizona Justice Project at 602-496-0286 or by email as directed on the ASU page for referral to this clinic or another clinic that can assist.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general criminal defense clinic and is not a direct public intake option. The practical referral route is Arizona Justice Project; if timing is urgent, this clinic is unlikely to be a fast legal remedy.

resources.name: The Centers for Habilitation - Transportation Services
resources.description: The Centers for Habilitation operates accessible vehicles for supported individuals, including trips between TCH group homes and day programs, medical appointments, job sites, events, recreation and social-enterprise volunteering.
resources.address: 215 Lodge Drive, Tempe, AZ 85282
resources.hours: Call TCH for intake and program-specific transportation schedules.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
TCH Transportation operates accessible vehicles for people already supported by TCH programs. Trips include transportation between group homes and the main-campus day program, medical appointments, job sites, events, recreational activities and social-enterprise volunteering.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official transportation page describes rides on behalf of TCH supported individuals. This should be treated as transportation attached to TCH disability services, not an open ride request line for the general public.

**Population Served**
People with developmental or physical disabilities supported by TCH programs in the Tempe/Phoenix metro service context, including Mesa residents when they are eligible for and connected to TCH services.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the TCH main number at 480-838-8111 or use the contact form on the TCH website. Explain the person's disability-support needs, current TCH or DDD/VR connection, pickup location, destination and whether transportation is needed for day program, work, medical or residential support.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not public paratransit, same-day taxi service or general non-emergency medical transportation. Confirm funding, enrollment in TCH services, pickup boundaries, vehicle accessibility and schedule capacity before relying on it.

resources.name: Arizona South Asians for Safe Families — Current Service Confirmation Needed
resources.description: Historical survivor-service listings describe culturally specific safety, practical and legal-support assistance for South Asian communities in Arizona. Current operation and intake remain unresolved.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Historical survivor-service listings describe culturally specific safety, practical and legal-support assistance for South Asian communities in Arizona. Current operation and intake remain unresolved.

**Eligibility Requirements**

An administrator must establish current operation, reachable intake, service area and eligibility before any client referral.

**Population Served**

Historically, South Asian survivors and families in Arizona. Current scope is unconfirmed.

**How to Best Connect**

Administrators can investigate the historically published helpline and seek confirmation through Arizona survivor-service partners. Do not send a client to an old website or mailing address.

**Important Information to Know**

The former organization website now redirects to unrelated gambling content. That does not prove the provider closed, but the site must not be used for referral. The saved directory evidence is older and needs reconciliation.
resources.resolutionReason: The former organization website now redirects to unrelated gambling content. That does not prove the provider closed, but the site must not be used for referral. The saved directory evidence is older and needs reconciliation.

resources.name: AZ HUGS — family crisis housing and outreach
resources.description: Family crisis-housing inquiries and outreach connections to shelter, treatment and other practical help. HUGS HOUSE is a short-term shelter programme for one family at a time.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Family crisis-housing inquiries and outreach connections to shelter, treatment and other practical help. HUGS HOUSE is a short-term shelter programme for one family at a time.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The HUGS HOUSE programme serves a family with minor children experiencing homelessness. Staff must determine fit and capacity.

**Population Served**
Families with children experiencing homelessness in the Valley.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-688-3180 to ask about the current family-housing programme and outreach options.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a very small programme. Do not plan around a guaranteed bed, motel payment or immediate placement; availability and other help depend on current resources.

resources.name: Mercy House - Senior Bridge
resources.description: Mercy House Senior Bridge is a 40-unit bridge shelter in Phoenix for adults 55+ who are actively engaged in a housing plan and awaiting permanent affordable housing placement.
resources.address: Phoenix, AZ
resources.hours: Not a walk-up facility.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Senior Bridge provides temporary housing and support while participants move toward a permanent affordable home.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The programme serves adults age 55+ who are actively pursuing permanent housing. Phoenix describes referrals through participating City-owned shelters.

**Population Served**
Eligible older adults already connected with participating Phoenix shelter and housing teams.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the current shelter caseworker whether a Senior Bridge referral is appropriate. The official Mercy House regional page provides a provider-contact route for programme enquiries.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a public walk-up shelter or a guarantee that a Mesa resident can enroll directly. Its 40-unit size is capacity, not current vacancies. Keep its referral rules separate from Mercy House rapid rehousing.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Health Services — Low-cost medical and dental clinic finders
resources.description: Provides state directories for locating sliding-fee primary care and reduced-fee dental clinics.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides state directories for locating sliding-fee primary care and reduced-fee dental clinics.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The directories are public; each clinic sets its own income, insurance, age and appointment rules.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents seeking affordable medical or dental care, including Mesa and Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the state clinic locator and reduced-fee dental list, then contact the selected clinic directly.

**Important Information to Know**
Directory information and PDF lists can lag provider changes; confirm actual services, fees and intake.

resources.name: U.S.VETS Prescott — Veteran housing and supportive services
resources.description: VA FY2025-2026 Grant and Per Diem Special Need awards list U.S.VETS special-needs beds in Arizona, including women-veteran beds associated with Phoenix VA station 644 and frail-elderly beds associated with Northern Arizona HCS station 649.
resources.address: 1040 Whipple St., Prescott, AZ 86305
resources.hours: Call the Prescott housing contact for current screening and appointment arrangements.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
U.S.VETS Prescott offers veteran housing and supportive-service pathways. The housing team can explain emergency, transitional, long-term supportive, permanent and Transition In Place options and associated case management.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Veteran status, housing need and the particular programme’s screening and documentation requirements apply. Ask whether relocation from Mesa is appropriate and whether any available programme fits the household.

**Population Served**
Veterans needing housing support in Northern Arizona, including Mesa veterans considering a longer-distance option when eligible.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact Prescott housing representative Justin Price at 928-379-1763 and confirm intake at 1040 Whipple St., Prescott. Ask which housing pathway is currently accepting referrals.

**Important Information to Know**
Prescott is a longer-distance Northern Arizona option. Do not assume a vacancy from a grant award or future Fort Whipple development. Phoenix women-veteran housing has a separate location and intake; it is not located in Prescott.

resources.name: DES Division of Developmental Disabilities — eligibility and member supports
resources.description: DES DDD determines developmental-disability eligibility and coordinates authorized supports, employment services, targeted coordination for some non-ALTCS members and communication/language access.
resources.address: Mesa-area eligibility office: 125 E. Elliot Road, Chandler, AZ 85225
resources.hours: DDD Customer Service Center: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM Arizona time; eligibility specialists are listed Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
DDD eligibility and support coordination, person-centered planning, authorized day/home/community supports, respite, habilitation, attendant care, therapies and transport. Employment pathways include individual/group supported employment, employment support aides, Pathways to Employment, center-based employment and coordination with VR. Targeted Support Coordination connects qualifying non-ALTCS members to community resources and acute care. Free communication/language access can include sign-language/oral interpreters, large print, audio and accessible formats.

**Eligibility Requirements**
DDD eligibility depends on qualifying developmental disability or under-6 at-risk criteria, Arizona residence, records and functional/programme requirements. Many funded supports require ALTCS, medical necessity and plan authorization. Targeted Support Coordination instead requires DDD eligibility, AHCCCS medical coverage and no ALTCS eligibility. Employment supports require DDD membership and authorized planning; high-school members may have after-school/break options. Communication assistance is for access to DDD services by members, applicants and families.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents with qualifying developmental disabilities and their families, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call DDD Customer Service at 844-770-9500 option 1, relay 711; eligibility specialists are at 602-771-0272. Ask the assigned support coordinator about services or an Employment Services Specialist. Ask staff for language/access accommodations early; contact Customer Service if staff cannot arrange them. Confirm the appropriate office before submitting documents in person.

**Important Information to Know**
Diagnosis does not guarantee DDD eligibility or every service. Authorizations, funding, provider availability and the person’s plan govern access. Targeted coordination is not ALTCS long-term-care coverage. Employment can affect benefits; request benefits counselling before changing work or pay. Communication assistance is an accommodation, not a separate cash benefit.
