resources.name: M.I.K.I.D. - Family Support and Behavioral Health Navigation
resources.description: M.I.K.I.D. is a family-run behavioral-health organization serving Arizona children, youth, and families through prevention, counseling, youth programs, family support, lived-experience navigation, health and wellness support, and ParentSupport Now reunification supports.
resources.hours: Call or use the referral form for current program availability; service settings and schedules vary by program.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Family-centered behavioral-health supports for children and youth, including family support partners, parent support, counseling, youth services, prevention and education, health and wellness support, ParentSupport Now reunification support, and navigation of behavioral-health, school, court, health, and community-resource systems.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official referral form includes self-referral, underinsured/uninsured referral, and Parent Support Now referral options. Specific services may require behavioral-health home involvement, AHCCCS/Medicaid information, guardian information, service-plan documents, or program-specific screening.

**Population Served**
Children, youth, young adults, and families in Arizona, including parents, grandparents, foster parents, kinship caregivers, and families navigating child-serving behavioral-health systems.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 1-844-805-2080. For referral questions or submissions, email referrals@mikid.org or use the M.I.K.I.D. referral form. General email is info@mikid.org.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a family-run peer and behavioral-health support organization, not a crisis line. Ask which services are available in Maricopa County and whether telehealth, in-home, clinic-based, or community support is available for the family.

resources.name: AzTAP Assistive Technology Services and AzLAT Loans
resources.description: AzTAP helps Arizona residents with disabilities, families, providers, employers, and the public identify, try, borrow, reuse, and finance assistive technology, including communication and computer-access technology.
resources.address: 300 W Clarendon Ave, Suite 475, Phoenix, AZ 85013
resources.hours: Call to arrange services. Closed Friday, October 2, 2026; reopening Monday, October 5, 2026.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
AzTAP offers assistive-technology consultations, demonstrations, short-term device trials, adaptive gaming, device and durable-medical-equipment reuse resources, refurbished-computer discounts, training and technical assistance. AzLAT offers affordable loans for assistive-technology purchases. Tools can address communication, computer access, hearing, vision, mobility or smart-home needs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
AzTAP assists people with disabilities of all types and ages, family members, service providers, employers, and the general public. Specific loan or device programs may have separate requirements.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents with disabilities and people supporting them, including family members, caregivers, providers, employers, and organizations.

**How to Best Connect**
Call AzTAP at 602-728-9534 or 800-477-9921, or email AskAzTAP@nau.edu. The office remains 300 W. Clarendon Ave., Suite 475, Phoenix. For AzLAT, call 602-728-9507 or email AskAzLAT@nau.edu about the online application and review timing. AzTAP announces an October 2, 2026 closure and October 5 reopening.

**Important Information to Know**
Device trials do not usually transfer ownership; availability, loan duration, shipping and reuse stock vary. AzLAT is repayable financing subject to application and credit review, not a grant. Reviewed typical terms are $100–$20,000, fixed 4.5% interest and 6–60 months; confirm current terms. This is not a general utility or internet-bill subsidy.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Corrections, Rehabilitation & Reentry - Community Reentry Bureau
resources.description: ADCRR bureau responsible for release, transition, and community supervision for people released from Arizona prisons, including specialized caseloads such as Veterans, AARS, special needs, electronic monitoring, and absconder reduction functions.
resources.address: 701 E. Jefferson St, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
ADCRR Community Reentry oversees release, transition, community supervision, specialized caseloads, and contracted or evidence-based supervision services for people released to the community. Official material describes Veterans Caseload support in Maricopa County and parts of Pinal County, AARS for lower-risk reporting, special-needs supervision, and other supervision supports.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services depend on ADCRR release status, supervision status, risk/need assessment, specialized caseload assignment, and internal eligibility criteria. This is not a public drop-in social-service program for people outside ADCRR supervision.

**Population Served**
People released from Arizona prisons to ADCRR community supervision, including eligible veterans, people with special mental-health or medical needs, and people assigned to specialized caseloads.

**How to Best Connect**
Call ADCRR general contact at 602-542-5497 or the Education, Programs, and Community Reentry contact at 602-771-5500. People already supervised should work through their assigned community reentry officer or local community reentry office.

**Important Information to Know**
This resource can be important for reentry coordination, but it is also a supervision authority. Specific benefit to a client depends on their ADCRR status and officer assignment. It should not be described as independent housing, cash aid, or walk-in case management for the general public.

resources.name: Mesa Community College · AZ Teacher Registered Apprenticeship Program Partner Pathway
resources.description: Mesa Community College is a partner with Mesa Public Schools in the Arizona Teacher Registered Apprenticeship Program (AZTRAP), a paid teacher-apprenticeship pathway where apprentices work in a local education agency while completing educator-preparation coursework and required FAFSA/acknowledgement steps.
resources.address: 1833 W Southern Ave, Mesa, AZ 85202; 7110 E McKellips Road, Mesa, AZ 85207; MCC Online
resources.hours: Contact MPS Pathways for teacher-apprenticeship position timing; MCC enrollment follows college schedules.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
AZTRAP prepares future educators through paid classroom experience under mentor teachers while apprentices complete educator-preparation coursework. MCC supports eligible academic pathways, including a Bachelor of Arts in Early Childhood Education - Dual Language and transfer pathways for elementary, special and secondary education.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The MCC page is for people who are already teacher apprentices or seeking teacher-apprenticeship positions through Mesa Public Schools. Eligible students must have an academic goal leading to Arizona teacher certification, be enrolled in applicable classes, complete FAFSA, and for MPS apprentices submit the student acknowledgement form. Hiring/enrollment into apprenticeship positions is handled by the participating local education agency.

**Population Served**
People pursuing Arizona teacher certification through a paid teacher-apprenticeship relationship with Mesa Public Schools or another eligible LEA, and MCC students in eligible educator-preparation pathways.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact the MPS Pathways Department at teach@mpsaz.org to ask about teacher-apprenticeship positions. If already an apprentice, follow MCC's AZTRAP page steps for academic goal/enrollment, FAFSA and acknowledgement. MCC main phone is 480-461-7000.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not open general job placement. A client generally needs to be hired as a teacher apprentice by an eligible LEA before the MCC scholarship/coursework steps apply. Earlier spring 2026 application information is superseded by the current MCC AZTRAP page.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Economic Security - Federal Bonding Program
resources.description: DES Federal Bonding Program provides free fidelity bond insurance for employers hiring eligible workers who face barriers such as criminal records, recovery history, public assistance, poor credit, little work history, or dishonorable military discharge.
resources.address: Statewide employer-requested program through DES
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Federal Bonding Program helps employers hire job seekers who may face barriers by providing free fidelity bond insurance for the first bond. DES states the bond covers up to $5,000 for six months and has no deductible.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Workers must meet Arizona’s legal working age rules, have federal taxes automatically deducted from pay, and obtain permanent part-time or full-time employment. Self-employment is not covered. The employer requests the bond after offering a job and the worker accepting it.

**Population Served**
Job seekers with employment barriers, including people with criminal records or parole/probation status, people recovering from alcohol or drug use, people receiving public assistance, people with poor credit or bankruptcy history, youth or adults with little work history, and people dishonorably discharged from the military.

**How to Best Connect**
Use this when an employer hesitates to hire because of bonding risk. After the employer offers a job, an authorized employer representative submits the DES Federal Bonding Request web form.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not job placement by itself; it is an employer-requested hiring incentive tied to a real job offer. The bond covers intentional theft-related losses, not poor work, mistakes, accidents, or injuries.

resources.name: Social Security Administration - SSI/SSDI Disability Income Application Pathway
resources.description: Social Security Administration is the direct application and claim-management pathway for SSI and SSDI disability income. SSI can provide monthly payments for eligible people with disabilities or blindness and adults age 65 or older with limited income/resources; SSDI can provide monthly payments and Medicare for workers whose disability limits work and who have enough work history.
resources.hours: SSA national phone service and local office appointment hours vary; SSA advises arranging an appointment for local office help when possible.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
SSI and SSDI disability benefit application routes through SSA. SSI provides monthly payments for eligible people with disabilities or blindness and adults age 65 or older with limited income and resources. SSDI provides monthly payments and possible Medicare for people whose disability or blindness stops or limits work and who have enough work history.

**Eligibility Requirements**
SSI generally requires limited income/resources and disability, blindness, or age 65 or older. SSDI generally requires disability or blindness and enough work history. SSA makes the final medical and non-medical eligibility decisions.

**Population Served**
Mesa and Maricopa County residents seeking federal disability or SSI income benefits, including adults, children, blind applicants, workers whose disability limits work, and low-income older adults.

**How to Best Connect**
Start with SSA's SSI or disability application pages, call 800-772-1213, use TTY 800-325-0778, or use SSA's office locator to find the appropriate local office and appointment route. Apply or call as soon as possible because SSI benefits generally cannot be paid for periods before the application effective date.

**Important Information to Know**
Applying is free; approval is not guaranteed. Medical evidence, work history and income/resource records may be required, and appeal deadlines matter. SSI and SSDI have different financial/work-history rules; Medicare has separate timing and eligibility. Report required changes in income, resources and living arrangements after approval. These are not immediate rent or utility grants.

resources.name: Veterans Medical Leadership Council - Returning Warrior Veteran Crisis Financial Assistance
resources.description: Veterans Medical Leadership Council provides emergency financial safety-net support for Arizona and Maricopa County veterans in crisis, especially veterans connected with Phoenix VA Health Care System social workers. Support may address basic needs such as housing, utilities, emergency home or auto repair, transportation-related needs, and treatment-related gaps that fall outside federal or state funding guidelines.
resources.address: P.O. Box 12289, Glendale, AZ 85318
resources.hours: No public walk-in hours are posted. VMLC says veterans cannot approach directly for assistance and must be engaged with a VA social worker to be vetted.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency financial safety-net support for veterans in crisis, including the Returning Warrior Program for veterans transitioning back into civilian life and having difficulty meeting basic needs. Official VMLC pages describe help for needs such as shelter, emergency home or auto repair, utility bills, and treatment for post-traumatic stress and traumatic brain injuries; public testimonials describe assistance with rent, utilities, phone bills, car payments, and housing stability.

**Eligibility Requirements**
VMLC states veterans cannot approach directly and must be engaged with a VA social worker to be vetted. Its Returning Warrior fund works primarily with Phoenix VA Medical Center social workers and focuses on Maricopa County veterans in need. Support is for verified needs that fall outside federal and state funding guidelines and is paid directly to the landlord or organization owed, not directly to the veteran.

**Population Served**
Arizona veterans in crisis, with a primary focus on Maricopa County veterans connected to the Phoenix VA Health Care System or Arizona State Veteran Home. Mesa veterans may be relevant when they are working with VA social work and have a verified need.

**How to Best Connect**
If the veteran already has a VA social worker, ask the social worker whether a VMLC referral is appropriate. If the veteran is homeless or at risk and not connected to VA social work, start with VA Phoenix CRRC at 602-248-6040 or another Phoenix VA access point and ask about social-worker assessment and VMLC/Returning Warrior options.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not direct public intake, a guaranteed grant, or cash paid to the client. VMLC's FAQ says approved checks are sent within a few days directly to the landlord or organization where the debt is due. Lack of a public application phone is an access limitation, but the VA social-worker route is explicit.

resources.name: Choices Pregnancy Centers of Greater Phoenix - Mesa Center
resources.description: Mesa faith-based pregnancy center offering emergency baby supplies by phone inquiry, free pregnancy tests, free ultrasound, LifePath classes, and pregnancy-related support. The official page states Choices does not perform or refer to abortion clinics.
resources.address: 3155 E. Southern Ave., 2nd Floor, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: Monday 9 AM-5 PM; Tuesday 9 AM-7 PM; Wednesday-Friday 9 AM-5 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency baby supplies when available, a Baby Boutique with diapers, wipes, infant clothing, strollers, car seats, bottles and hygiene items, LifePath education, pregnancy support, free pregnancy testing and ultrasound subject to scheduling/clinical suitability.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Boutique purchases use Baby Bucks earned through LifePath classes/lessons. Families needing emergency supplies should call to ask about help outside that route. Confirm current stock, classes, documentation and medical-scope eligibility; no universal income rule is published.

**Population Served**
Pregnant people, parents, babies, and families in Mesa and the East Valley. Choices lists English and Spanish site options.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Mesa center at 480-733-2740, text/call/schedule online, or walk in during listed hours. Mesa hours are Monday 9 AM-5 PM, Tuesday 9 AM-7 PM, Wednesday-Friday 9 AM-5 PM. The center is at 3155 E. Southern Ave., 2nd Floor, Mesa, AZ 85204.

**Important Information to Know**
Choices is faith-based and states it does not perform or refer for abortion. It is not a substitute for prenatal medical or emergency care. Confirm medical credentials, ultrasound scope/availability, counselling limits, appointments and the specific supplies needed before referral.

resources.name: Maricopa County Department of Public Health - East Valley Immunization Clinic
resources.description: Maricopa County's East Valley immunization clinic in Mesa provides free routine vaccines for children and adults, with insurance billed when available but not required.
resources.address: 1950 S. Country Club Dr., Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; Wednesday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; closed daily 12:00 PM-1:00 PM and county-observed holidays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Routine childhood vaccines and listed adult vaccines through the county public-health immunization clinic system.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Child vaccines are for children from birth through age 18. Adult vaccine eligibility depends on insurance status, age recommendations and vaccine availability. Vaccines are free whether insured, uninsured or underinsured; insurance is billed when available.

**Population Served**
Children, adults and families in Maricopa County, including Mesa residents needing routine immunizations or school-required vaccines.

**How to Best Connect**
Book online from the county immunization page or call the CARES Team at 602-506-6767. Mesa clinic: 1950 S. Country Club Dr., Mesa, AZ 85210.

**Important Information to Know**
Foreign travel vaccines are not provided. Bring immunization records, insurance card if insured and parent/guardian identification when available. Adult vaccine availability can change.

resources.name: Southwest Autism Research & Resource Center - Family, Child, Teen, Adult, Vocational, and Autism Services
resources.description: Southwest Autism Research & Resource Center provides autism-specific services across the lifespan, including diagnostic, children's, teen/adult, family, community, employment, and research-related programs.
resources.address: 300 N. 18th St., Phoenix, AZ 85006; multiple Valley locations
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; use Request Services or call before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
SARRC offers autism-specific diagnostic services, children's services, teen and adult services, family services, community services, research participation, preschool/community-school services, relationship and connection education, and employment-related supports for autistic people.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are autism-specific. Age, diagnosis, assessment needs, payer/insurance, location, program fit, waitlists, and fees vary by service.

**Population Served**
Autistic children, teens, adults, and families in the Phoenix metro area, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents who can access SARRC locations or approved remote/community services.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-340-8717 or use SARRC's Request Services link. Ask which service fits the person's age and need, whether Mesa-area access or telehealth/community options are available, and what payer, assessment, or waitlist rules apply.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an autism-specific resource, not a cross-disability provider. Confirm costs, insurance, DDD or private-pay fit, current openings, and exact program location before referral.

resources.name: Arizona Self Help — Benefits screening
resources.description: Provides a free screening tool for potential eligibility across health and human-service benefits.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides a free screening tool for potential eligibility across health and human-service benefits.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The screening tool is open to the public. Each benefit programme makes its own eligibility decision.

**Population Served**
Arizona individuals and families looking for benefit programmes that may fit their circumstances.

**How to Best Connect**
Answer the screening questions on Arizona Self Help, review the suggested programmes and follow each programme’s application instructions.

**Important Information to Know**
A screening result is not an application, approval or promise of funding. Confirm current programme rules and intake with the responsible agency.

resources.name: Fresh Start Women's Foundation - Justice-Involved Women
resources.description: Fresh Start Women's Foundation supports justice-involved women with individualized support, goal planning, second-chance career advising, career training, community partner connections, resource referrals, and transportation support such as Lyft codes when available.
resources.address: 1130 E McDowell Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85006
resources.hours: Use the program page to connect; public page does not list walk-in hours for this initiative.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Individualized support for justice-involved women, including one-on-one coaching, needs assessment, goal and action planning, second-chance career advising, career training opportunities, community partner collaborations, resource/referral services, and transportation support such as Lyft codes when available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is for women with justice involvement who are navigating reintegration after incarceration. Current intake rules, county requirements, and whether services begin before or after release should be confirmed with Fresh Start.

**Population Served**
Justice-involved women in the Phoenix and Maricopa County area rebuilding employment, education, transportation, and community stability after incarceration.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the justice-involved women page to connect with Fresh Start and ask about enrollment. Fresh Start's public phone contact is 602-252-8494.

**Important Information to Know**
Fresh Start is not a shelter or a general Lyft voucher programme. Direct cash, training enrollment or rides are not guaranteed; support depends on programme fit, participation, staff assessment and funding.

resources.name: Area Agency on Aging, Region One - MOSAIC Native American Senior Center
resources.description: Area Agency on Aging, Region One's MOSAIC Native American Senior Center offers Native American elders age 60 and older a place for information, education, activities, social connection and congregate meals in Maricopa County.
resources.address: 1430 E. Indian School Rd., Suite 110, Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Information, education, activities, social connection and congregate meals for Native American elders. The program page also references an event calendar and a center-based setting.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Spanish-language official page describes the center for Native Americans over age 60 in Maricopa County. Confirm transportation, operating days, meal registration and participation requirements before traveling from Mesa.

**Population Served**
Native American adults age 60 and older in Maricopa County; the official page states multiple tribes are represented.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Katie Stevens at 602-241-4739 for more information, or call the Senior HELP LINE at 602-264-HELP (4357). The center is listed at 1430 E. Indian School Rd., Suite 110, Phoenix.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a Phoenix-based population-specific senior center, not tribal government aging administration. Mesa elders should confirm transportation and schedule before going.

resources.name: Puente Human Rights Movement - Donation-based Immigration Legal Clinic
resources.description: Puente Human Rights Movement operates a donation-based immigration legal clinic for community members and families, helping with options, paperwork when possible and next steps by appointment.
resources.address: 1937 W Adams St, Phoenix, AZ 85009
resources.hours: Appointments based on availability; call to schedule and leave a message if no one answers.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Donation-based immigration legal support for community members and families. Listed services include DACA renewals, asylum support, case work, lawful permanent resident renewals, citizenship, work permits and notary services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Appointments are based on availability. The page does not publish formal geographic, income or case-acceptance rules.

**Population Served**
Immigrant and working-class communities in the Phoenix metropolitan area, including Mesa residents who can contact the Phoenix clinic.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-252-1283 to schedule an appointment. If no one answers, leave a message for a return call. The organization address is 1937 W Adams St, Phoenix, AZ 85009.

**Important Information to Know**
Services use a suggested-donation model. The page describes support, paperwork and next steps; it does not guarantee attorney representation or acceptance of every asylum or court matter.

resources.name: Syracuse University IVMF — Onward to Opportunity
resources.description: Provides online career training and preparation for industry certifications.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides online career training and preparation for industry certifications.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Veterans generally need 180 days of service and an Honorable discharge. Transitioning active-duty members, eligible part-time Guard/Reserve members and military spouses have separate eligibility rules.

**Population Served**
Eligible military-connected adults nationwide who can commit to structured online study.

**How to Best Connect**
Submit the online interest form with a personal email and select the distance-learning option if no installation is nearby. Questions:315-443-6898 or IVMFeducation@syr.edu.

**Important Information to Know**
Participation is normally once, with coursework planned within 90 days and reliable computer/internet access needed. Training is free; employed participants normally pay their exam fee. One exam may be covered for eligible unemployed participants or those in their final six months of active service after meeting course and exam requirements.

resources.name: Mesa Arts Center - Creative Aging Lifelong Learning
resources.description: Mesa Arts Center offers free professionally led Lifelong Learning arts experiences for adults 55 and older, including in-person and virtual creative classes and social engagement.
resources.address: 1 E. Main St., Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Class schedules vary; Box Office hours Tuesday-Saturday 12:00 PM-5:00 PM, Sunday-Monday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Mesa Arts Center Lifelong Learning provides free professionally led arts experiences for adults ages 55 and older, with creative expression, movement, story, dance, artmaking, community and social engagement. The page lists in-person and virtual classes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For adults age 55 and older. Individual classes have changing dates, registration windows, capacity and any materials or accessibility details.

**Population Served**
Adults age 55 and older in Mesa and nearby communities who want creative activity, skill building and social connection.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Creative Aging/Lifelong Learning page to view available classes or call Mesa Arts Center Box Office and Registration at 480-644-6500. The center is at 1 E. Main St., Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
The official page describes the program as free, but schedules change throughout the year. This is enrichment and social connection, not clinical or custodial care.

resources.name: Focus Employment Services - Supported Employment
resources.description: Focus Employment Services provides supported employment, job development, work adjustment, vocational counseling and rehabilitation instruction, with Phoenix-area offices by appointment.
resources.address: Phoenix, Tempe, Metro Phoenix and Chandler offices; nearest to Mesa is Tempe or Chandler by appointment
resources.hours: Offices list Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM by appointment only.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Supported employment that connects clients with employers, targets jobs based on interests and needs, offers career advice and placement services, and provides follow-along mentoring and coaching through networking, applications and interviews. The site also lists job development, work adjustment, vocational counseling and rehabilitation instructional services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Public pages do not fully spell out payer eligibility. Access appears commonly tied to qualifying behavioral-health benefits, rehabilitation needs or participating clinics; clients should confirm referral source, insurance/benefit eligibility and current capacity.

**Population Served**
People in the Phoenix metro area who need supported employment tied to behavioral-health or rehabilitation needs, including clients able to meet by appointment at Phoenix, Tempe, Metro or Chandler locations.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-312-1045 or email info@focusemployment.com to schedule an appointment. Offices are by appointment only and include Tempe at 922 S. Mill Avenue and Chandler at 955 W. Chandler Boulevard #5.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm the referral route, clinic or health-plan connection, cost and whether the Tempe or Chandler office is best for a Mesa client before sending them.

resources.name: UMOM New Day Centers - Client Essential Items / Move-In Support
resources.description: UMOM provides essential items to UMOM clients during shelter stays and as they move into stable housing, including blankets, pillows, hygiene items, diapers, casual clothing, socks, underwear and footwear.
resources.address: 3333 East Van Buren Street, Phoenix, AZ 85008; donation warehouse 2107 E Magnolia Street, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: Warehouse donation hours Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-3:00 PM; client access is through UMOM programs and shelter/housing pathways, not public walk-in shopping.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Essential items for UMOM clients during shelter stays and move-in to stable housing. Items include blankets, pillows, shampoo, conditioner, menstrual products, toilet paper, diapers, underwear, socks, casual footwear and casual clothing for infants through adults.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people enrolled in or connected to UMOM shelter, rapid rehousing, permanent affordable housing or related homelessness programs. Public material-assistance shopping is not posted.

**Population Served**
Families with children, single women, veterans' families and other people experiencing homelessness or housing instability in Maricopa County who are served through UMOM or coordinated shelter routes.

**How to Best Connect**
Use UMOM's Find Help page for the right shelter route. Families with children are directed to Family Housing Hub and 2-1-1; single women can call Halle Women's Center at 602-362-5833. For general UMOM contact, call 602-275-7852.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a client-only essential-items resource, not a public clothing closet or furniture bank. UMOM says it does not accept home furniture or used household appliances/kitchen tools, so move-in goods are limited to current program supplies and partner resources.

resources.name: Bridging AZ Furniture Bank - Veterans Furniture Project
resources.description: Bridging AZ Veterans Furniture Project is a veteran-focused woodworking and furniture-repair social enterprise connected to Bridging AZ Furniture Bank; it helps disabled, unemployed, and formerly homeless Veterans build skills while Bridging AZ supplies beds and furniture through participating agencies and caseworkers.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Veterans Furniture Project teaches disabled, unemployed, and formerly homeless Veterans basic to advanced woodworking, metal fabrication, furniture repair, and furniture-building skills. Bridging AZ Furniture Bank also provides beds, furniture, and household goods through participating social-service agencies and caseworker referrals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Training/workshop participation is veteran-focused and appears intended for Veterans who are disabled, unemployed, or formerly homeless. Furniture assistance is not offered directly to individuals; Veterans needing furniture should work through a caseworker at a participating agency.

**Population Served**
Arizona Veterans connected to the Veterans Furniture Project and households, including Veterans, transitioning out of homelessness through agency/caseworker referral.

**How to Best Connect**
For furniture, ask a caseworker at a participating agency to arrange help; Bridging AZ does not directly serve individual requests. For project information, call 480-375-5454 or email Jim@BridgingAZ.org. Confirm current training enrollment and the workshop/warehouse location before travelling.

**Important Information to Know**
Furniture is by participating-agency referral, not a walk-in giveaway. Confirm whether training is currently recruiting and what participation involves. Do not assume a paid apprenticeship, AmeriCorps placement or immediate furniture availability.

resources.name: Shot in the Dark - Mesa Harm-Reduction Site
resources.description: Shot in the Dark provides free harm-reduction supplies, naloxone, safer injection and smoking supplies, wound-care supplies, testing events, referrals and support at a Mesa weekly site.
resources.address: Mesa site location is disclosed by text; public page lists the Mesa site but not a street address
resources.hours: Mesa site listed Wednesday 7:30 PM-9:00 PM; text before travel to confirm location and schedule.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free naloxone and training, sterile syringes and safer injection supplies, safer smoking supplies, wound-care supplies, safer sex supplies, rapid HIV/Hepatitis C testing events, referrals, a participant ID card and nonjudgmental support. Site-dependent basic-needs supplies include food, snacks, water, clothing, menstrual products and daily hygiene products; inventory varies.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page says supplies and support are free, no ID is required and there are no hoops to jump through. Text the support line for current site details.

**Population Served**
People in Mesa, the East Valley and Maricopa County who use drugs or need overdose-prevention and safer-use supplies.

**How to Best Connect**
Text or call the East Valley line at 602-456-9811 for the current Mesa location and schedule. The public page lists Mesa on Wednesday 7:30 PM-9:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
The Mesa street address is intentionally not public. This is harm reduction and referral support, not detox or clinical treatment.

resources.name: Bridges Reentry — Magdalene residential and mentoring programs
resources.description: Provides women-focused residential support and mentoring around release from incarceration.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides women-focused residential support and mentoring around release from incarceration.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Ask about the two-year residential program’s admission rules, current openings and costs; mentoring in Perryville is a separate pathway.

**Population Served**
Women returning from incarceration who qualify for the Phoenix West Valley program.

**How to Best Connect**
Email Admin@bridgesreentry.org or use the provider’s program contact route to discuss the appropriate pathway before arranging travel.

**Important Information to Know**
The current site describes two homes with twelve resident places; that is total capacity, not availability. Do not assume immediate placement or free housing.

resources.name: Florence Crittenton Services of Arizona / CPLC - Girls Ranch Young Mothers Lead
resources.description: Arizona Florence Crittenton/CPLC lead for vulnerable girls and young women, including a Girls Ranch group-home program described by CPLC as serving young mothers with parenting-skills support.
resources.address: Florence Crittenton / CPLC, Phoenix and Scottsdale area; public program address not established for Girls Ranch
resources.hours: Call the organization before referral; current public intake hours and admission process were not established.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Arizona Florence Crittenton, now associated with Chicanos Por La Causa, is described by CPLC as helping young women escaping abuse, sex trafficking, poverty, homelessness, drug addiction or neglect. A 2024 CPLC story describes Girls Ranch in Scottsdale as a group home for young mothers where a teen mother received parenting-skills support, support groups, communication skills and help refocusing on school and her child.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Current public admission criteria, referral source requirements, age limits, custody/placement rules and whether pregnant or parenting teens can self-refer were not clearly established from current program pages. Do not assume the Colorado Florence Crittenton Student and Family Support or early-childhood programs apply in Arizona.

**Population Served**
Vulnerable girls and young women in Arizona; available public Arizona evidence specifically mentions young mothers and girls facing abuse, sex trafficking, poverty, homelessness, teen pregnancy, drug abuse or neglect.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Arizona Florence Crittenton/CPLC public website and call the Florence Crittenton main number found on the Arizona site, 602-274-7318, to ask whether Girls Ranch or another current Arizona program can accept a referral for a pregnant or parenting teen or young mother.

**Important Information to Know**
The submitted Student and Family Support Program and Early Childhood Education details appear to come from a separate Colorado affiliate and should not be used for Arizona referrals. Treat this as a cautious lead for administrators or caseworkers until current intake, eligibility and capacity are confirmed.

resources.name: GLO Phoenix - Bus Pass Program
resources.description: GLO Phoenix lists a Bus Pass Program offering weekly or monthly bus passes and state driver license or ID fee support for people released from jail or prison within the past 12 months, but official pages conflict about whether the organization serves Arizona/Phoenix or Pittsburgh.
resources.hours: Contact program for meeting and referral details.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The official program page describes a reentry transportation initiative offering weekly bus passes, monthly bus passes and state driver license or identification card fee support for people facing transportation barriers after incarceration.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program page says individuals must have been released from jail or prison within the past 12 months and undergo referral/review of parole status, employment situation and mobility challenges. Support is currently limited to one-time help per person.

**Population Served**
Justice-impacted people recently released from jail or prison. The intended geography is unresolved because official pages mention Valley Metro passes but also describe the organization as serving Pittsburgh, PA.

**How to Best Connect**
Email info@glophoenix.org or call the listed office number 412-368-0004. Referrals are reviewed before recipients are invited to a one-on-one meeting.

**Important Information to Know**
Administrator resolution is needed before routine Mesa referral. The official site contains conflicting geography: some pages describe Valley Metro bus passes and a Phoenix reentry program, while the home/about pages describe Pittsburgh service. Do not promise Arizona availability until confirmed.
resources.resolutionReason: Official pages conflict about Arizona/Phoenix versus Pittsburgh service. Confirm Arizona availability before making this resource available for Mesa referrals.

resources.name: Episcopal Diocese of Arizona Prison Ministry - Bridges Reentry Release-Day Pickup
resources.description: Episcopal Diocese of Arizona Prison Ministry / Bridges Reentry provides release-day pickup support for women released from Perryville prison, including donated clothing, shoes, hygiene gift packs and transportation to approved housing or reentry destinations.
resources.address: 114 W. Roosevelt St., Phoenix, AZ 85003-1406
resources.hours: Release-day coordination; call the Diocese or use the official page contact pathway for current process.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Release-day pickup support for women leaving Perryville prison, including donated clothing to wear at release, shoes, simple hygiene items or gift packs, and transportation to housing, parole-related destinations, bus stations, halfway houses or reentry residences when needed.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official prison-ministry page describes service for women being released from Perryville prison. Current referral, volunteer-team availability and client coordination steps must be confirmed with Bridges Reentry or the diocesan prison ministry contact.

**Population Served**
Women leaving Perryville prison who need first-day reentry support and transportation to an approved destination in Arizona.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the official prison ministry page to contact the listed Bridges/diocesan reentry contact, or call the Episcopal Diocese of Arizona at 602-254-0976 and ask for Prison Ministry / Bridges Reentry release-day pickup information.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a coordinated reentry ministry, not a public clothing closet. The page is oriented partly to volunteers; confirm the actual client referral pathway and release-date coordination before relying on it.

resources.name: Dogs Day Out AZ - Support for People Experiencing Homelessness with Dogs
resources.description: Dogs Day Out AZ provides free dog food, water, toys, shoes, clothing, bedding, strollers and wagons to dog owners experiencing homelessness in the Phoenix area and surrounding cities. The practical public access route is by phone, email, or the listed web presence.
resources.address: Confidential Location, Tempe, AZ 85281
resources.hours: 2-1-1 lists 24-hour phone access; distribution timing and location are not public and should be confirmed by phone.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free dog supplies for unhoused dog owners, including pet food, water, toys, dog shoes, dog clothing, bedding, strollers and wagons.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For dog owners experiencing homelessness in the Phoenix area and surrounding cities. Required documents vary by service according to the directory listing.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness who have dogs, including Mesa-area clients when Dogs Day Out can serve their location.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-249-5676 to ask how to receive supplies and where distribution or outreach is happening. The public location is confidential; do not send clients to an address without phone confirmation.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a pet-support resource, not human shelter. The best current public evidence is a 2-1-1 listing last assured March 1, 2026; the primary web presence appears to be social media, so distribution process and coverage should be confirmed directly.

resources.name: Wesley Health Center at Recker Road — Mesa clinic and refugee-care access
resources.description: Wesley Health Center at Recker Road is a Mesa health center offering family medicine, pediatric care, prenatal care, sexual health and contraceptive care, comprehensive HIV services, diabetes education, lab testing, preventive screening, refugee care clinics, counseling, insurance eligibility, and no-cost breast/cervical cancer screening for those who qualify.
resources.phone: Recker clinic602-257-4323; Refugee Patient Appointment Line602-368-9605
resources.address: 5845 E. Still Cir., Suite 104, Mesa, AZ 85206
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM. Wesley states it does not provide emergency services or care.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Family medicine, pediatric care, prenatal care, sexual health and contraceptive care, comprehensive HIV services, diabetes self-management education, lab testing, preventive screening, refugee care clinics, counseling, insurance eligibility support, and no-cost breast and cervical cancer screening for those who qualify.

**Eligibility Requirements**
General health-center eligibility is not narrowly limited on the official page. Wesley links to insurance and sliding-fee resources; uninsured patients should ask about discount eligibility and required documents. Specialized services such as refugee care, HIV services, prenatal care, and Well Woman screening have program-specific rules.

**Population Served**
Mesa and East Valley patients, including children, adults, families, pregnant patients, uninsured/underinsured patients and people needing chronic-disease or HIV support. The refugee-care track serves refugees, asylees, immigrants, temporary-visa holders and people with limited English proficiency.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-257-4323 for the Recker clinic at 5845 E. Still Circle, Suite 104, Mesa. Refugee-care appointments use 602-368-9605; Wesley describes voicemail callbacks within 24 hours. Confirm the correct site, requested service, fees/discounts and documents; specialized refugee services may be at another campus.

**Important Information to Know**
Wesley does not provide emergency care; use 911 for emergencies. Dental services are not listed for Recker. Health navigation is not immigration legal representation. Screening, refugee care and other specialist programmes have their own rules.

resources.name: The Veterans Consortium — Veterans benefits court appeals
resources.description: Provides free legal screening and possible representation for an appeal to the Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims.
resources.address: 2101 L Street NW, Suite 225, Washington, DC 20037
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides free legal screening and possible representation for an appeal to the Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A veteran or qualifying family member must have a Board of Veterans’ Appeals denial, no current attorney for the case, and at least one arguable issue accepted by the programme.

**Population Served**
Eligible veterans and family members nationwide, including Arizona.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the programme’s online intake and Court forms, supplying the Board decision, or email intake@vetsprobono.org.

**Important Information to Know**
The usual appeal deadline is 120 days from the final Board decision’s mailing date. Seek help promptly and do not assume that asking for representation pauses the deadline. This is a court-appeal programme, not ordinary initial claims assistance.

resources.name: Community Medical Services — Mesa on Arbor
resources.description: Outpatient opioid-use treatment with medication, counseling and recovery support.
resources.address: 6116 E Arbor Avenue, Building 1, Mesa, AZ 85206
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Outpatient opioid-use treatment with medication, counseling and recovery support.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Clinical intake determines the appropriate treatment. Call to confirm age eligibility, accepted coverage and any self-pay costs; the location page specifically lists Cigna.

**Population Served**

People seeking help with opioid use, including heroin or fentanyl, in Mesa and the East Valley.

**How to Best Connect**

Call the Arbor clinic to arrange intake and ask what to bring. Posted hours are Monday–Friday 4:30–11:30 a.m. and Saturday 6–9 a.m.; Sunday is closed.

**Important Information to Know**

This is a separate access point from CMS Mesa on Main. Ask about new-patient arrival times and dosing requirements; published opening hours do not guarantee immediate admission.

resources.name: Carrington College Mesa Dental Hygiene Clinic
resources.description: Carrington College Mesa Dental Hygiene Clinic offers complimentary teaching-clinic dental hygiene appointments, including cleanings, fluoride, home-care instruction, dental screening, sealants and X-rays with dental hygiene services.
resources.address: 1300 S. Country Club Dr., Suite 2, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 7:30 AM-4:00 PM; appointment times may vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Complimentary dental cleanings, fluoride application, home-care instruction and dental screening. Other services include dental sealants and X-rays with dental hygiene services only.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official clinic page does not state an income requirement. Patients must schedule with the clinic and participate in a teaching-clinic appointment where a student provides care under instructor and clinic dentist sign-off.

**Population Served**
Community members seeking no-cost preventive dental hygiene services in Mesa, especially uninsured or underinsured people who need a cleaning or screening.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-717-3510 to schedule, confirm appointment times or cancel. Address: 1300 S. Country Club Dr., Suite 2, Mesa, AZ 85210.

**Important Information to Know**
This clinic provides hygiene and preventive services, not fillings, extractions, dentures or emergency dental treatment. Appointments take longer than a typical dental office because it is a teaching clinic.

resources.name: Beia's Families - Behavioral Health, Peer Support, and Supportive Services
resources.description: Beia's Families provides culturally competent behavioral-health, peer-support and supportive services, including daily peer support groups, case management, psychoeducation, skills training, employment resources, empowerment housing and Healthy Families Arizona home visiting for eligible expectant and new parents.
resources.address: 515 W. Buckeye Rd., Suite 207, Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 9:30 a.m.-2:30 p.m.; after-hours appointments by request.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Beia's Families offers behavioral-health support, peer support groups, supportive services, individualized and intensive case management, community-resource navigation such as SNAP, psychoeducational groups, skills training, employment and career development resources, empowerment housing and Healthy Families Arizona home visiting for eligible families.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Peer and supportive-service eligibility should be confirmed directly. Healthy Families Arizona families are screened by criteria and participate voluntarily; services may continue as needed until the child turns five.

**Population Served**
Underserved and underrepresented individuals and families in the Phoenix/Maricopa County area, including expectant and new parents for Healthy Families Arizona and people needing peer support or behavioral-health support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-313-2049 or email info@beiasfamilies.org. The office is at 515 W. Buckeye Rd., Suite 207, Phoenix. Hours are Monday through Friday 9:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m.; after-hours appointments are available by request.

**Important Information to Know**
The website describes behavioral-health help, peer support and supportive services but does not fully state licensure scope or accepted health plans. Confirm whether the client needs clinical counseling, peer support, case management, housing support or Healthy Families home visiting before referral.

resources.name: Copper Springs · Avondale Substance Use Treatment
resources.description: Avondale behavioral-health hospital offering detox, inpatient substance-use treatment, PHP, IOP, telehealth outpatient care, and Help for Heroes specialty programming.
resources.address: 10550 W McDowell Road, Avondale, AZ 85392
resources.hours: Open 24 hours; walk-ins accepted 24/7.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Copper Springs offers substance-use detox, inpatient addiction treatment, outpatient substance-use PHP and IOP, medication management and wellness training, with telehealth available for outpatient programs. The Avondale location also lists specialized Help for Heroes programming.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Avondale location serves adolescents and adults, but age eligibility differs by program and level of care. Treatment begins with an assessment by phone, chat, video or in person. Confirm medical stability, the suitable program, insurance and costs before admission.

**Population Served**
Adolescents and adults in the Phoenix metro area, including Mesa residents able to travel to Avondale. The site specifically names active-duty military, veterans, first responders and other high-risk frontline professionals as specialty populations.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-565-3035 24/7, use online chat/scheduling, or walk in at 10550 W McDowell Road in Avondale. Confirm whether Avondale or Gilbert/Copper Springs East is the best location.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a regional hospital-based option outside Mesa. Outpatient telehealth may reduce travel for some clients, but inpatient and detox services require placement and assessment.

resources.name: Cloud Covered Streets - Mobile Shower, Laundry, Haircut and Clothing Trailer
resources.description: Cloud Covered Streets operates a rotating mobile trailer that provides showers, laundry, haircuts, clean clothing and other essentials to people experiencing homelessness, with location-specific schedules posted online.
resources.address: Rotating locations in the Phoenix metro area; check current schedule before travel
resources.hours: Posted trailer hours are typically 9:00 AM-1:00 PM, or earlier if no guests; locations and dates rotate.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Mobile showers, laundry, haircuts, clean clothing and other essentials from a rotating trailer, plus posted links to other shelter and crisis resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For guests experiencing homelessness who can attend a posted trailer location during operating hours. Services depend on the day's location, time, capacity and supplies.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness in the Phoenix metro area. Some schedules may include Mesa or East Valley stops, but the current calendar must be checked.

**How to Best Connect**
Check the Cloud Covered Streets Phoenix Resources page for the next trailer date and location, or call 480-695-0004 if the schedule is unclear. Do not rely on an older Mesa stop without checking the current calendar.

**Important Information to Know**
The schedule is date-specific and rotates. On September 26, 2026, the page showed recent September locations and stated services may end early if no guests are present, so missionaries should confirm before sending a client.

resources.name: Arizona Commission for the Deaf and the Hard of Hearing - Statewide Support Service Provider Program
resources.description: ACDHH's Statewide Support Service Provider Program provides limited SSP service hours for eligible DeafBlind and combined vision-hearing loss adults to support independence and community access.
resources.hours: Use the SSP Services Application link on the official page; current enrollment timing and availability should be confirmed with ACDHH.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Statewide SSP Program provides support service provider hours for self-determined DeafBlind and combined vision-hearing loss consumers. SSP support is intended to promote independence, quality of life and access to community environments.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Program guidelines include being an Arizona resident, over age 18, able to direct SSP service activities, able to document U.S. citizenship, and willing to follow SSP program rules and orientation. Vision and hearing guidelines and barriers to accessing environments are used to determine participation.

**Population Served**
Arizona adults who are DeafBlind or have combined vision and hearing loss and meet ACDHH SSP participation guidelines.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Statewide SSP Program page and its SSP Services Application link. Because the page describes a limited 18-month process serving approximately 35 consumers, ask ACDHH whether applications or waitlist spots are currently open.

**Important Information to Know**
The page states participants are responsible for incidental activity expenses such as parking, bus fare, entrance fees or event tickets. SSPs are not emergency interpreters, and capacity appears limited.

resources.name: VetPhoenix - Justice-Impacted Veteran Peer-Led Support and Reentry Navigation
resources.description: VetPhoenix is a veteran-led nonprofit describing peer-led support, housing support, reentry help, justice-system navigation, research, and policy work for justice-impacted veterans. Official pages provide an email, phone number, and Get Help route, but current public pages do not confirm Mesa, Maricopa County, or Arizona service coverage.
resources.address: Mail only: P.O. Box 11373, Whittier, CA 90603
resources.hours: No public office hours are listed. VetPhoenix says messages are not monitored continuously and aims to respond within two business days.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
VetPhoenix describes peer-led support for justice-impacted veterans, including housing support, reentry support, justice-system navigation, family support, advocacy, research, and policy work. Its Get Help page says the intake route connects people with peer-led programs, housing support, and justice-system navigation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Public pages identify the intended client as a justice-impacted or justice-involved veteran. Exact eligibility, documentation, program availability, and whether support is direct service or referral depend on current staff, partner commitments, and approved program scope.

**Population Served**
Justice-impacted veterans and, in some materials, their families. Official pages show a Whittier, California mailing address and a Los Angeles County jail agreement; they do not clearly establish service to Mesa, Maricopa County, or Arizona veterans.

**How to Best Connect**
Use VetPhoenix's Get Help page, email info@vetphoenix.org, or call 909-978-7216. VetPhoenix says it aims to respond within two business days and that messages are not monitored continuously. In a crisis, use the Veterans Crisis Line by calling 988 and pressing 1 or texting 838255.

**Important Information to Know**
This record needs administrator resolution before routine Mesa referral. Official pages confirm VetPhoenix exists and has a contact route, but the public evidence currently found does not confirm Arizona coverage, Mesa/Maricopa partnerships, or the submitted smart-glasses service for blind veterans. A separate public smart-glasses program appears to exist through another organization, so do not promise VetPhoenix smart-glasses help without confirmation from VetPhoenix.
resources.resolutionReason: Needs resolution: official VetPhoenix pages support organization identity, contact information, peer-led support, housing/reentry/navigation language, and a Los Angeles County Sheriff agreement, but they do not establish Mesa/Maricopa or Arizona service coverage. Targeted searches did not confirm the submitted smart-glasses-for-blind-veterans service as a VetPhoenix program.

resources.name: AHCCCS - Substance Use Prevention, Treatment and Recovery Services Block Grant Pathway
resources.description: AHCCCS Substance Use Prevention, Treatment and Recovery Services Block Grant is a statewide public funding pathway that supports SUD treatment and recovery services for uninsured and underinsured people through regional behavioral-health systems.
resources.address: 150 N 18th Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.hours: Use AHCCCS/RBHA contact routes; provider hours vary by assigned provider.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Public funding and access pathway for substance-use prevention, treatment, recovery, early intervention, and support services. Services are implemented through ACC-RBHAs and TRBHAs and participating providers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
AHCCCS states SUBG funds support uninsured and underinsured individuals. Priority populations include pregnant women/teenagers who use drugs by injection, pregnant women/teenagers who use substances, people who inject drugs, women/teenagers with dependent children and their families, and other people with SUD as funding is available.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents, who need SUD treatment or recovery services and lack adequate coverage.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the AHCCCS SUBG page and behavioral-health system map to identify the regional behavioral-health authority or contracted provider. Mesa clients are generally routed through the Central Arizona RBHA/provider network rather than AHCCCS directly providing treatment.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a funding and access pathway, not a clinic. Funding, provider capacity, and waitlists vary; callers may be routed to a contracted provider.

resources.name: Valleywise Health - Financial Assistance and Uninsured Discount Program
resources.description: Valleywise Health's Financial Assistance and Uninsured Discount Program helps eligible uninsured or underinsured patients reduce costs for Valleywise hospital and FQHC services, including separate schedules for FQHC and non-FQHC care.
resources.hours: Financial assistance questions by phone; Valleywise appointment line 1-833-855-9973; billing/financial assistance phone 602-344-8181.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Financial assistance and uninsured discount schedules for Valleywise Health services, including separate schedules for Valleywise services other than FQHC services and for Valleywise Federally Qualified Health Center services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Discounts and financial assistance are based on household income and eligibility requirements. Valleywise staff can help patients understand bills and determine whether they qualify.

**Population Served**
Uninsured and underinsured Valleywise Health patients in Maricopa County, including Mesa patients using Valleywise community health centers, specialty clinics, hospital care, pharmacy, or other Valleywise services.

**How to Best Connect**
For questions about a bill or financial assistance, call 602-344-8181. For appointments, call 1-833-855-9973 and ask about the correct financial assistance or FQHC discount schedule for the planned service.

**Important Information to Know**
FQHC and hospital/non-FQHC schedules differ; identify the actual service/site and have billing staff assess eligibility. This is help with Valleywise medical costs, not general cash. A discount does not guarantee no-cost care, service approval or an appointment.

resources.name: HousingSearch.AZ.gov — free rental-housing search
resources.description: A free Arizona rental finder covering market-rate and affordable homes, accessible units and other housing options.
resources.hours: Search-help line Monday–Friday 7:00 AM–6:00 PM MST.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A free Arizona rental finder covering market-rate and affordable homes, accessible units and other housing options.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Anyone may use the search. Each landlord or housing programme determines its own income, screening and rental requirements.

**Population Served**
People looking for Arizona rental housing that fits their location, budget or access needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Search the website or call 877-428-8844, Monday–Friday 7 a.m.–6 p.m.MST, for search help. TTY users may dial 711.

**Important Information to Know**
Listings are not guaranteed vacancies, approvals or subsidies. Confirm price, application requirements and availability directly with the property. Call 211 for a housing crisis.

resources.name: Arizona Relay Service 711 and customer profiles
resources.description: Arizona Relay Service 7-1-1 is a statewide relay service that makes telephone communication accessible for people who are Deaf, hard of hearing, DeafBlind, or have speech-related communication needs.
resources.hours: Relay access is available by dialing 7-1-1; emergency calls should go directly to 9-1-1.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-charge relay communication connects hearing/voice callers and people who are Deaf, hard of hearing, DeafBlind or have speech-related communication needs. Relay options include TTY, voice/hearing carry-over, TeleBraille and speech-to-speech. A free customer profile can save call preferences, greeting and speed-dial information.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The service is for people who need relay access because of hearing, speech, DeafBlind or related communication needs. A person must have a usable phone, TTY or compatible relay method for the type of call.

**Population Served**
People in Arizona who are Deaf, hard of hearing, DeafBlind or have difficulty speaking, and people calling them.

**How to Best Connect**
Dial 711 for relay access. Arizona Relay Customer Service lists 800-347-1695 or 866-259-1768, voice/TTY, for questions or customer profiles. For an emergency contact 911 directly rather than 711.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a no-cost communication access service, not a phone bill subsidy, device grant or internet service. Some phone systems may need configuration to dial 7-1-1 correctly.

resources.name: New Hope Community Center - Food Box and Client-Choice Pantry
resources.description: New Hope Community Center provides food boxes, client-choice food shopping, clothing, family aid and job-search support for specified East Mesa ZIP codes.
resources.address: 6915 E University Dr, Mesa, AZ 85207
resources.hours: Monday-Wednesday 9:00 AM-12:00 PM. Registration 9:00-11:45 AM. Pick up food 9:00 AM-12:00 PM; select-your-own food 9:00-11:00 AM; resources, bus passes and clothing 9:00-11:30 AM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Food boxes, client-choice food shopping, clothing, financial assistance through Family Aid, job-search/job-fair support, resources and bus-pass help. Family Aid is listed once every 365 days; ask which expenses and funding are currently available. 211 Arizona additionally lists bicycles when available for working people experiencing homelessness; confirm that limited pathway with the centre.

**Eligibility Requirements**
New Hope assists ZIP codes 85205, 85206, 85207, 85208 and 85209. Family aid is listed as once every 365 days. The page does not clearly state food-box frequency or required documents.

**Population Served**
Households in the listed East Mesa ZIP codes needing food and related basic-needs support.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to New Hope Community Center, 6915 E University Dr, Mesa, during Monday-Wednesday service hours. Registration is open until 11:45 AM. Call the message phone at 480-807-1668 with questions.

**Important Information to Know**
ZIP eligibility, documentation and current supply must be checked. Food choice closes at 11 AM; clothing/resources/bus passes at 11:30 AM; registration at 11:45 AM. Family aid is once per 365 days, not a stated food-box frequency. Bicycle details come from 211 rather than the provider’s own service rules and must be confirmed before promising one.

resources.name: Southwest Lending Closet - Durable Medical Equipment Loan Program
resources.description: Southwest Lending Closet loans durable medical equipment at no fee for up to 90 days to people in Arizona who can travel to its Avondale pickup site.
resources.address: 218 N Central Ave, Avondale, AZ 85323
resources.hours: 2-1-1 lists hours as Monday, Wednesday, Friday, and Saturday 9:00 AM-noon; Tuesday and Thursday noon-3:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Loans durable medical equipment such as wheelchairs, transport chairs, walkers, shower chairs, elevated toilet seats, and bath transfer benches for short-term use.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The programme serves Arizona residents needing temporary equipment.211 lists state-issued photo ID or driver’s license; the Arizona AT/DME Reuse Coalition specifies a US driver’s license and two different phone numbers. Call to confirm accepted identification and contact requirements before pickup.

**Population Served**
People anywhere in Arizona who need temporary durable medical equipment and can travel to the Avondale location or send someone to pick up equipment.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 623-932-1016 before traveling to confirm current inventory and documents. Visit 218 N Central Ave, Avondale, AZ 85323 during listed pickup hours.

**Important Information to Know**
Loans are reported as no fee and up to 90 days; confirm the current term and return arrangements. Stock changes, powered wheelchairs are not offered, and no Mesa delivery is established. Arrange transport or an authorized person to collect equipment in Avondale.

resources.name: Catholic Charities Arizona — Refugee Services and intensive case management
resources.description: Catholic Charities supports eligible refugees already living in Arizona through case coordination, housing/medical/safety and employment services, with intensive case management and limited assistance when eligible.
resources.address: 5151 N 19th Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85015
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Refugee case coordination for housing instability/eviction risk, health, safety and employment; eligible rent help may cover up to one month. Preferred Communities intensive support can include medical transport, medication help, SSI/SSDI applications and housing stabilization. Employment services include skills assessment, job matching/referrals, resumes/interviews, vocational/workplace vocabulary, interpretation, interview transport and public-transit training. Ask case management about needed clothing/household essentials; this is not a public goods closet.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Catholic Charities states Refugee Services serves ORR-eligible refugees for up to five years after arrival. Specific rent or stabilization help depends on eligibility, need, and available program resources.

**Population Served**
ORR-eligible refugees already living in Arizona, including high-need refugees with chronic medical conditions or disabilities and refugee families facing housing instability.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 855-316-2229 for Refugee Services intake. Refugee employment inquiries are listed at 602-749-4455; ask for client intake rather than employer services. Confirm the appointment location, qualifying status/arrival date and Mesa service access.

**Important Information to Know**
New refugee arrivals are described as paused, but support continues for eligible refugees already in Arizona. Assistance depends on assessment, eligibility and resources; do not promise rent, household goods, transport or a job. This is not an open public English class or unrestricted cash fund.

resources.name: Veterans Crisis Line
resources.description: Free confidential 24/7 crisis support by phone, text, or chat for veterans, service members, National Guard and Reserve members, and people supporting them; VA enrollment is not required.
resources.hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Veterans Crisis Line provides free, confidential crisis support. Responders listen, help with immediate distress, and connect callers, texters, or chat users with resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
No VA enrollment is required. The line serves veterans, service members, National Guard and Reserve members, and people who support them.

**Population Served**
Veterans, service members, National Guard and Reserve members, family, friends, and supporters nationwide, including Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Dial 988 and press 1, text 838255, or use live chat at the website. For immediate life-threatening emergencies, call 911 or go to an emergency department.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a crisis access and routing service, not ongoing therapy. It can help connect the person to next-step resources after the crisis contact.

resources.name: Arizona Association of Manufactured Home Owners - Housing Stability Certified Community Legal Advocate
resources.description: Arizona Association of Manufactured Home Owners is an Arizona-approved Housing Stability Certified Community Legal Advocate organization for mobile, manufactured, park-model, and RV home owners living on leased land.
resources.address: 2753 E. Broadway Rd., 101-443, Mesa, AZ 85204 (mailing address)
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Manufactured-home owner advocacy and housing-stability assistance through a court-listed certified community legal advocate.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For owners of mobile, manufactured, park-model or RV homes on leased land in Arizona. Confirm membership, fees, issue scope and current advocate availability.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents facing rights or tenancy issues involving a home they own on leased land.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-966-9566 or email info@aamho.org. Ask about legal-advocate assistance for the specific problem; the Broadway address is a mailing address.

**Important Information to Know**
A community legal advocate has limited authority and does not provide unrestricted attorney representation. Ownership of the home does not remove the need to address the lease or park’s legal rules.

resources.name: Dignity Foundation - Dignity Home
resources.description: Dignity Home is a Dignity Foundation referral-partner program where referred individuals and families shop for essential household items such as cookware, small appliances, dishes, bedding, towels and cleaning supplies for a new home.
resources.address: 6501 E Greenway Pkwy, Suite 103-502, Scottsdale, AZ 85254
resources.hours: Referral-only; call or use the referral-partner process for current appointment timing.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A one-on-one shopping experience for referred individuals and families to choose household essentials for a new home, including cookware, small appliances, dishes, bedding, towels and cleaning supplies.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Participants must be referred by trusted community organizations or referral partners. The foundation focuses on people transitioning to independent, self-sufficient living situations.

**Population Served**
Referred individuals and families rebuilding stability, including people moving from transitional housing into a home.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the client's caseworker or nonprofit agency whether they are a Dignity Foundation referral partner and can submit a referral. For questions, call 602-848-2422 or email ktrapp@dignityfoundation.org.

**Important Information to Know**
This is referral-only and not a walk-in household-goods pantry. Confirm whether a Mesa agency can refer, current appointment location, item availability and transportation assistance before promising help.

resources.name: Parent Support Arizona - Special Education, DDD and Behavioral Health Advocacy
resources.description: Parent Support Arizona helps families of children with unique needs navigate behavioral health, Arizona DDD and education systems and connects them with advocates.
resources.address: 625 W. Southern Ave., Suite E-173, Mesa, AZ 85210; virtual and by appointment only
resources.hours: Office hours are virtual and by appointment only.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Parent Support Arizona offers complex care management, advocacy connection and system-navigation help for families managing a child's behavioral health, developmental disability, special education, 504/IEP or related school-support concerns.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public page does not list formal income, insurance or diagnosis eligibility. Families should contact the organization to explain the child's needs and ask whether Parent Support Arizona or an independent advocate referral is appropriate.

**Population Served**
Arizona parents and caregivers of children with emotional, behavioral, psychiatric, developmental-disability or education-support needs, including Mesa families.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Get Help Now/contact route on the website or call 480-382-4020. The mailing address is 625 W. Southern Ave., Suite E-173, Mesa, and office hours are virtual and by appointment only.

**Important Information to Know**
Parent Support Arizona states it connects families to independent advocates and does not provide legal services or legal advice. Public information does not state fees, insurance, or whether advocacy referrals are free, so families should ask about costs before engaging services.

resources.name: St. Stephen's Episcopal Church - Food Pantry Lead
resources.description: Eastern Phoenix church-operated pantry lead submitted for Maricopa County reserve use; call before referral to confirm current pantry hours and Mesa-resident access.
resources.address: 2310 N 56th St, Phoenix, AZ 85008
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
St. Stephen's Episcopal Church was submitted as an eastern Phoenix church-operated food pantry. The available official site confirms the church identity and contact route, but current pantry schedule and rules were not established in this bounded check.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Current eligibility, documentation rules and whether Mesa residents may use the pantry should be confirmed directly before referral.

**Population Served**
People seeking food pantry assistance in the eastern Phoenix/Maricopa County area, subject to current church pantry rules.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-840-0437 or use the church website to confirm whether the food pantry is currently operating, its hours and whether the household can be served before traveling to 2310 N 56th St, Phoenix, AZ 85008.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a reserve lead outside Mesa. Do not send a client without confirming current pantry operation and eligibility because the official homepage is not enough by itself to establish current food-pantry hours.

resources.name: Society of St. Vincent de Paul - Mesa Dining Room
resources.description: Society of St. Vincent de Paul's Mesa Dining Room provides daily lunch and seasonal heat relief in Mesa, with cold water, air conditioning and temporary shelter during heat season. The official page notes partner services at the site; Homeless ID Project also uses the location on scheduled Tuesdays.
resources.address: 49 W Broadway Rd, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Lunch daily 9:30 AM-11:30 AM. Heat relief June 1-September 30 daily 12:00 PM-4:30 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
