Daily lunch, summer heat relief, cold water, air conditioning, temporary daytime shelter during heat season, and access to community partner services at the Mesa Dining Room.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open to people needing meals or heat relief. Specific partner services, including showers or document-help events, may have their own schedules and rules.

**Population Served**
Mesa and East Valley neighbors experiencing homelessness, heat risk or food insecurity.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to 49 W Broadway Rd during lunch or heat-relief hours. Call 602-619-9411 for site questions. Parking is available inside the gate; check with the security guard to open the gate when you arrive.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a prepared-meal and seasonal daytime heat-relief site, not a food-box pantry or overnight shelter. The posted heat-relief season is June 1–September 30; confirm dates and partner shower/document-help schedules separately. The current provider address is 49 W. Broadway Road.

resources.name: AHCCCS Noncitizen Medical Assistance / Federal Emergency Services Program eligibility
resources.description: Official eligibility and application guidance for noncitizen AHCCCS medical coverage and emergency-only services.
resources.hours: Online benefit applications are available through Health-e-Arizona Plus; phone support is through 855-432-7587.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
AHCCCS medical-coverage screening and the Federal Emergency Services pathway for eligible noncitizens.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Immigration status and other program requirements determine coverage. AHCCCS announces narrower noncitizen eligibility beginning October 2026; some refugees, asylees and humanitarian groups may lose full coverage unless another qualifying status applies.

**Population Served**
Noncitizens seeking Arizona medical coverage or help understanding a coverage notice.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through Health-e-Arizona Plus or call 855-432-7587. Ask AHCCCS or a benefits assister to review current status, effective dates and any notice.

**Important Information to Know**
Emergency-only coverage is not full insurance and still requires eligibility. DES Refugee Medical Assistance is a separate program; do not assume the same status or duration rules.

resources.name: Salt River Project (SRP) - M-Power Customer Assistance
resources.description: SRP M-Power customers can access account advances, Extreme Heat Warning disconnection protections, income-qualified discount enrollment and resource counselor referrals when they are having trouble keeping prepaid power on.
resources.hours: SRP customer service is available 24/7 by phone for M-Power assistance.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
SRP offers M-Power customer support including temporary account advances, no disconnection during National Weather Service Extreme Heat Warnings, access to the SRP Income-Qualified Discount, and resource counselor connections to Community Action Agencies for utility and other critical needs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The customer must be an SRP M-Power prepaid electric customer. Advance eligibility is account-specific. SRP states accounts with a medical designation are not eligible for M-Power. Income-qualified discounts require meeting SRP discount requirements.

**Population Served**
SRP M-Power prepaid electric customers, including Mesa residents served by SRP, who are having difficulty making energy purchases.

**How to Best Connect**
Call SRP at 602-236-8888 anytime. Customers can also check the SRP M-Power mobile app to see if they qualify for an advance and can sign up for the Income-Qualified Discount online or by phone.

**Important Information to Know**
An advance is repayable: 35% of future energy purchases goes toward repayment. It is not a cash grant. Accounts needing a medical designation cannot use M-Power; ask SRP about a billed plan. Protection during National Weather Service Extreme Heat Warnings is not a year-round disconnection ban.

resources.name: Banner Health - Arizona Financial Assistance Program for Discounted and Charity Care
resources.description: Banner Health's Arizona Financial Assistance Program offers charity care or sliding-scale discounts for eligible Banner hospital, physician, home care, imaging, rehabilitation and surgery-center bills.
resources.hours: Billing assistance phone hours listed by Banner: Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-7:00 PM, Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM, Saturday 8:00 AM-12:00 PM MST.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Discounted and charity care for eligible Banner bills. Banner states assistance is based on household income and household size at or below 400% of the Federal Poverty Level, or medical expenses exceeding 50% of household income, with assistance approved on a sliding scale.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicant must have an eligible Banner-related bill and meet the income or medical-expense criteria. Banner requires the correct application form, all required information and supporting documents; forms differ by hospital, physician, home care, imaging, rehabilitation or surgery-center bill type.

**Population Served**
Patients with Banner Health bills in Arizona, including Banner facilities serving Mesa and Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Choose the correct Arizona application form on Banner's financial-assistance page, complete it with supporting documents, and send it by mail or email as directed on the form. Call 888-264-2127 for questions or payment arrangements.

**Important Information to Know**
This is help with qualifying Banner bills, not unrestricted cash or guaranteed free care before treatment. Some non-Banner professional charges may be excluded. Spanish and other translations are available. Use the form for the actual billing entity; approval and discount depend on documents and policy.

resources.name: International Rescue Committee in Phoenix — newcomer case support and employment
resources.description: IRC Phoenix connects eligible refugees, asylees and other newcomers with case coordination, employment/economic support, housing and food pathways, and resettlement goods. The client office is in Glendale; services have programme-specific eligibility.
resources.address: 4425 W Olive Avenue, #400, Glendale, AZ 85302
resources.hours: Client Rescue page lists Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; call or email before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Newcomer case coordination for emergency needs, housing stability and self-sufficiency; humanitarian support for eligible asylum-seeking families released from custody; Refugee Cash Assistance and Refugee Support Services when eligible. Employment support includes job placement, vocational coaching, workplace culture, on-the-job learning, financial education and economic-empowerment connections. Food access can include casework, New Roots and client distributions. Clothing/household essentials may come through welcome kits, apartment setup and the Resettlement Shop.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Each pathway has its own humanitarian/immigration status, arrival-date, documentation, case-need and funding rules. IRC serves refugees, asylees, asylum seekers, trafficking/torture survivors and other eligible newcomers, but belonging to one group does not qualify a person for every programme. Goods and basic-needs supports are tied to accepted IRC clients.

**Population Served**
Phoenix-area refugees, asylees, trafficking survivors, survivors of torture and other immigrant/newcomer clients, including eligible Maricopa County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-433-2440 or email Phoenix@rescue.org. The Phoenix-area office is 4425 W. Olive Ave., Suite 400, Glendale. Ask about the specific employment, housing, food, cash-assistance or resettlement need, Mesa access and remote appointments. Existing clients should use their caseworker.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general public job centre, rent fund, pantry, clothing closet or walk-in shelter. Current programme acceptance and stock/capacity control help. Donor drop-off hours do not establish client distribution times; confirm appointments and the service location.

resources.name: A Guiding Light Services — Home and Community-Based Services
resources.description: Respite, habilitation and attendant care for children and adults with developmental disabilities.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Respite, habilitation and attendant care for children and adults with developmental disabilities.

**Eligibility Requirements**

The provider describes Arizona DDD-linked services. Confirm the member’s authorization, service area, support needs and available staffing.

**Population Served**

Arizona children and adults with developmental disabilities and family caregivers.

**How to Best Connect**

Use the provider’s Inquire form to request the relevant service. It asks about the person’s age, city and schedule and says to allow up to three business days for a response.

**Important Information to Know**

A request does not guarantee a worker or start date. Confirm funding and the exact service address before arranging care; no unconfirmed office address is supplied.

resources.name: ARIZONA@WORK Maricopa County - East Valley Career Center / DES Veterans Services
resources.description: ARIZONA@WORK Maricopa County East Valley Career Center is the Mesa workforce-system access point for job search, training and DES Veterans Services, including veterans priority of service and specialized help for eligible veterans with employment barriers.
resources.address: 1001 West Southern Avenue, Suite 101, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 8 AM-7 PM; Friday 8 AM-5 PM; closed Saturday-Sunday.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The County East Valley Career Center provides employment and training access, job-search support and workforce referrals. Eligible veterans receive priority for covered employment/training services, and DES Veterans Services are available at the center.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligible veterans receive priority of service. DVOP-style intensive help is generally for eligible veterans with significant employment barriers, so the office should screen the veteran's situation before promising a specific specialist.

**Population Served**
Veterans and eligible spouses in Mesa, the East Valley and Maricopa County who need workforce help.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-372-9700 or visit 1001 W Southern Ave, Suite 101, Mesa during posted office hours. Ask specifically for DES Veterans Services or veterans priority employment services.

**Important Information to Know**
Ask staff to screen for the right service. Veteran priority does not automatically establish eligibility for a DVOP specialist or every funded training/support benefit. This County location is distinct from the City workforce office at Broadway.

resources.name: T-Mobile - Project 10Million
resources.description: T-Mobile Project 10Million provides eligible K-12 student households one free hotspot and 200GB of internet per year for five years, subject to coverage and program terms.
resources.hours: Online application; no public phone hours identified for the program page.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free student mobile internet through one hotspot per household and 200GB of data per year for five years. T-Mobile ships the device for free if the application is accepted.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A K-12 student can qualify through National School Lunch Program eligibility or proof of participation in listed programs such as SNAP/EBT, FDPIR, Community Eligibility Provision or Medicaid. Proof must be uploaded with the online application.

**Population Served**
Eligible K-12 student households in the United States, including Arizona households where T-Mobile coverage is available.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through the Project 10Million page. The application process asks the parent or guardian to fill out the form, upload proof of eligibility, sign the service agreement and receive the device by shipment if approved.

**Important Information to Know**
This is intended for student mobile connectivity. Coverage is not available everywhere, roaming is not available, annual data ends at 200GB or 365 days, video is limited to standard-definition speeds and service may be slowed or restricted under network-management rules.

resources.name: Maricopa County Department of Public Health - Domestic Medical Examination / Refugee Medical Screening
resources.description: Maricopa County Department of Public Health is listed by Arizona DES as the Maricopa provider for domestic medical examinations/refugee medical screening for eligible newly arrived refugees and other ORR-eligible beneficiaries.
resources.address: 1645 E Roosevelt St, Phoenix, AZ 85006
resources.hours: Call to confirm appointment timing and referral process; DES lists the service provider phone as 928-258-9984.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Domestic medical examination/refugee medical screening for newly arrived eligible refugees and other Office of Refugee Resettlement-eligible beneficiaries. The screening is intended to identify communicable diseases and other health conditions and connect clients to follow-up care.

**Eligibility Requirements**
DES states refugees and other eligible beneficiaries are eligible for the domestic medical examination up to 90 days after arrival or grant of qualifying status. This is not open general primary care.

**Population Served**
Newly arrived ORR-eligible beneficiaries in Maricopa County, including refugees, asylees, Cuban/Haitian entrants, SIV holders, trafficking survivors and other qualifying humanitarian immigrants when eligible.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the DES-listed Maricopa provider number, 928-258-9984, and ask about refugee medical screening at 1645 E Roosevelt St, Phoenix. A resettlement agency or DES refugee program may also route eligible clients.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a health-screening and healthcare-linkage pathway, not immigration legal representation. Confirm eligibility, timing after arrival/status grant, required documents and referral route before sending a client.

resources.name: Operation Homefront — Critical Financial Assistance
resources.description: Financial help for qualifying military households, with covered needs determined by the applicant’s service category.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Financial help for qualifying military households, with covered needs determined by the applicant’s service category.

**Eligibility Requirements**
One route covers post-9/11 line-of-duty wounds, illness or injury; discharged applicants need Honorable or General Under Honorable Conditions status and must be within 10 years of separation. Certain deployed E-1–E-6 members with legal dependents qualify under detailed deployment rules. The general active-duty E-1–E-6 dependent-household route covers only food and dependent vision care.

**Population Served**
Military households that meet one of the stated service categories, including eligible Mesa families.

**How to Best Connect**
Read the category-specific criteria and apply through My Operation Homefront from the 1st through the 10th of a month. The published cutoff is 11:59 p.m. Central time on the 10th. Submit all required documents.

**Important Information to Know**
Review occurs after the window closes. Assistance and covered expenses are not guaranteed; a general active-duty applicant should not assume eligibility for rent or vehicle help.

resources.name: CommonSpirit Health / Dignity Health Arizona - Arizona General Hospital Mesa Financial Assistance
resources.description: CommonSpirit/Dignity Health Arizona financial assistance provides charity care and discounted hospital-care assistance for eligible uninsured and underinsured patients, including Arizona General Hospital Mesa bills.
resources.address: Arizona General Hospital Mesa, 9130 E. Elliot Rd., Mesa, AZ 85212
resources.hours: Call the hospital billing or patient-services route on the application for current assistance hours; no separate call-center schedule was posted on the opened page.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Financial assistance for eligible hospital services, including 100% charity care and discounted care under the CommonSpirit financial assistance policy.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Uninsured or underinsured patients with family income up to 200% of Federal Poverty Level may be eligible for a 100% discount for eligible hospital services. Patients from 201% through 400% FPL may be eligible for discounted care at Amount Generally Billed.

**Population Served**
Patients with eligible Dignity Health/CommonSpirit Arizona hospital bills, including Arizona General Hospital Mesa patients.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Arizona General Hospital Mesa financial assistance application linked on the official page, or contact the hospital billing/patient-services route listed on the application.

**Important Information to Know**
This is hospital bill assistance, not routine-care access or cash aid. Physician charges or other provider bills may be excluded unless listed as covered by the policy. Multiple language versions are available.

resources.name: Southwest Human Development - Fussy Baby Program
resources.description: Southwest Human Development's Fussy Baby Program helps caregivers of infants in the first year with excessive crying, soothing, feeding, sleeping, development concerns and caregiver stress, with Maricopa County home visits and statewide phone/video support.
resources.address: Maricopa County in-home service; statewide phone or virtual consultation
resources.hours: Access is through the Birth to Five Helpline; early childhood specialists are available Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-8:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Fussy Baby Program provides telephone, home-visiting and virtual video support for families with hard-to-soothe infants, excessive crying, sleeping problems, feeding difficulties and caregiver stress during the baby's first year.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program supports parents and caregivers concerned about a baby's development or fussiness during the first year of life. In-home services are for families residing in Maricopa County; telephone and virtual video consultation are available statewide.

**Population Served**
Parents and caregivers of infants birth to 12 months, including families in Maricopa County and families elsewhere in Arizona needing phone or virtual support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Birth to Five Helpline at 877-705-5437 and ask about the free Fussy Baby Program. The online sign-up form can also be used. The intake helpline offers English and Spanish; confirm the language available for any home or video visit.

**Important Information to Know**
This is parent/caregiver support and developmental consultation, not a substitute for pediatric care. Families should contact a pediatrician or emergency care for medical red flags such as fever, breathing concerns, dehydration or injury.

resources.name: Arizona Complete Health-Complete Care Plan - AHCCCS Member Transportation
resources.description: Arizona Complete Health-Complete Care Plan members use Member Services to access covered AHCCCS transportation benefits for eligible medical and behavioral-health appointments; Care1st members were moved into this plan effective October 1, 2024.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Arizona Complete Health-Complete Care Plan is an AHCCCS Medicaid plan. Members who need non-emergency medical transportation should use the plan's Member Services route for covered ride arrangements under AHCCCS NEMT rules.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The client must be enrolled in Arizona Complete Health-Complete Care Plan or have been transitioned from Care1st into this plan, and the trip must be to an AHCCCS-covered service when the member cannot arrange other transportation. Plan-specific authorization, notice, and trip rules apply.

**Population Served**
Arizona Complete Health-Complete Care Plan members in its service area, including enrolled Mesa and Maricopa County AHCCCS members.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Medicaid Member Services at 1-888-788-4408 or use the number on the member ID card. Have the appointment date and time, provider address, pickup address, AHCCCS ID, mobility device, escort, and accessibility needs ready.

**Important Information to Know**
This is only for enrolled plan members and covered health-related trips. Care1st's official page says all Care1st members joined Arizona Complete Health-Complete Care Plan on October 1, 2024; use Arizona Complete Health for current Care1st-related NEMT questions.

resources.name: Father Matters - Family Law Assistance / Men at Work wraparound legal assistance
resources.description: Father Matters provides family-stabilization and reentry-oriented wraparound services, including help understanding family court, child support/modification, legal-assistance linkage and family-law matters for men and women.
resources.address: 3146 E. Wier Ave., Suite 26, Phoenix, AZ 85040
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Family Law Assistance and Men at Work wraparound services, including help understanding family court, child support or modification issues, linkage to legal assistance and family-law matter navigation. Father Matters also provides parenting, reentry, job, resource referral, supervised parenting and support services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For families and parents seeking Father Matters support. The page does not clearly state that Father Matters provides attorney representation; clients should treat this as navigation, referral or legal-assistance linkage unless intake confirms otherwise.

**Population Served**
Arizona families, parents, fathers, mothers and returning citizens connected to Phoenix/Maricopa County services.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-774-3298, email info@fathermatters.org or use the Schedule a Call link on the Father Matters website. Main Phoenix location is 3146 E. Wier Ave., Suite 26.

**Important Information to Know**
The legal-help scope is not fully defined on the public page. It is useful for family-court and child-support navigation or referrals, but urgent court deadlines or contested legal matters may also require a legal-aid provider or attorney.

resources.name: Phoenix Rescue Mission — historical walk-in/drop-in centre
resources.description: Could add a useful drop-in route if its current existence and public access can be established.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Could add a useful drop-in route if its current existence and public access can be established.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Current standalone drop-in eligibility and operation remain unresolved.

**Population Served**
Administrators checking an older homeless-services lead.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask Phoenix Rescue Mission at 6022333000 whether a public drop-in centre currently operates separately from residential intake.

**Important Information to Know**
The detailed 24-hour and meal/shower schedule comes from a much older government guide and has not been confirmed on current provider pages. Do not send a client to 1801 S 35 th Avenue based on those old hours.
resources.resolutionReason: The detailed24-hour and meal/shower schedule comes from a much older government guide and has not been confirmed on current provider pages. Do not send a client to1801S35th Avenue based on those old hours.

resources.name: Christ the King Catholic Church - H.O.P.E. Outreach Food Pantry
resources.description: Christ the King H.O.P.E. Outreach distributes TEFAP pre-packed food boxes and bags to households in a defined Mesa service boundary.
resources.address: 1616 E Broadway Rd, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: Tuesday 10:30 AM-12:00 PM and Thursday 4:45-6:15 PM; closed Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, Friday and Saturday. Posted special closures include Nov. 19, Dec. 24 and Dec. 31, 2026.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
TEFAP food distribution with pre-packed boxes or bags that may include shelf-stable food, meat, fruits, vegetables and toiletries or hygiene products when available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Clients must live in the listed service area, bring proof of identification, and may visit once every two weeks. Service is limited by the posted capacity of 125 clients per day.

**Population Served**
Mesa households north of Baseline Road, south of Brown Road, east of Horne and west of Val Vista who need emergency groceries.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the H.O.P.E. distribution listing for 1616 E. Broadway Road and current pantry hours. Call 480-964-1719 or email CTK@CTKMesa.org to confirm before travel, especially near holidays. The parish office at 1551 E. Dana Avenue is a separate address.

**Important Information to Know**
The service boundary and capacity limit matter. English and Spanish are listed; clients outside the boundary should be routed to another pantry.

resources.name: Maricopa County Adult Probation Department - Sex Offender Program
resources.description: Maricopa County Adult Probation's Sex Offender Program is a probation supervision and treatment pathway for people with sex-offense convictions, providing enhanced supervision, surveillance, intensive treatment for sexual deviancy, accountability, relapse-prevention-oriented controls, and family/victim involvement when appropriate.
resources.address: Central Court Building, 201 W. Jefferson Street, Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.hours: Access depends on court/probation assignment and the assigned probation officer.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Enhanced community supervision, surveillance, and intensive treatment addressing sexual deviancy, accountability, intrinsic controls to prevent hands-on offenses, and family or victim involvement when possible and appropriate.

**Eligibility Requirements**
This pathway is for convicted sex offenders under Maricopa County Adult Probation supervision. It is not open community reentry housing or a self-referral counseling program.

**Population Served**
People with sex-offense convictions who are under Maricopa County probation authority and assigned to this supervision/treatment pathway.

**How to Best Connect**
Work through the assigned probation officer or Adult Probation Department. For general questions, call the Information Center at 602-506-3204.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a court/probation control and treatment pathway. Community housing, legal rights, and treatment-provider questions for a Mesa-area client should be coordinated through probation and qualified legal/treatment providers.

resources.name: Wesley Community & Health Centers - Well Woman HealthCheck Program
resources.description: Wesley Community & Health Centers provides Well Woman HealthCheck Program breast and cervical cancer screening at Wesley health center locations, including the Mesa Recker Campus, for low-income, uninsured, and/or underinsured women who qualify.
resources.address: 5845 E Still Cir, Suite 104, Mesa, AZ 85206
resources.hours: Program-specific hours were not listed; Recker Campus health center hours are Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free breast and cervical cancer screening for people who qualify through Wesley's Well Woman HealthCheck Program contractor services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Wesley states the program is for women who are low-income, uninsured and/or underinsured. Contact Wesley's program contact to confirm age, income, insurance, documentation, and screening rules.

**Population Served**
Women needing breast and cervical cancer screening at Wesley health center locations, including Mesa Recker Campus patients.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Nancy Vasquez at 602-368-9617 or email nvasquez@wccphx.net to ask about eligibility and appointments. Mesa Recker Campus is at 5845 E Still Cir, Suite 104, Mesa, AZ 85206.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a screening program, not emergency cancer treatment. Eligibility and appointment availability should be confirmed directly before referral.

resources.name: Arizona State University Sandra Day O'Connor College of Law - Immigration Clinic
resources.description: ASU Law’s Immigration Clinic trains law students through supervised immigration-law practice for immigrant and community-advocate clients, but public intake and outside referral rules are not clearly published.
resources.address: 111 E Taylor St, Phoenix, AZ 85004
resources.hours: Client intake and referral availability require administrator confirmation.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A supervised law-school immigration clinic with casework described on ASU Law’s clinic page.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Current client case-selection and referral rules remain unresolved.

**Population Served**
Potential immigration-clinic clients; enrolled law students are the service providers, not the target client group.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the official clinic page to establish the current client referral route before making a referral.

**Important Information to Know**
Do not rely on classroom schedules or conflicting old telephone numbers as public intake. Keep this proposal administrator-only until access is resolved.
resources.resolutionReason: Needs administrator resolution because ASU’s official page confirms real immigration clinic client work but does not provide a public intake route or case-selection process sufficient for responsible direct referral.

resources.name: New Hope Behavioral Health Center — OTP/SUD Treatment Clinic
resources.description: New Hope Behavioral Health Center is a Mesa OTP/SUD treatment clinic offering opioid-use-disorder medications, counseling, naloxone, behavioral-health supports and related health testing.
resources.address: 215 S. Power Rd., Suite 114, Mesa, AZ 85206
resources.hours: Monday–Friday 4:30 AM–2:30 PM, closed Wednesday 11:30 AM–12:30 PM; Saturday 6:30–8:30 AM; closed Sunday and federal holidays.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Outpatient opioid-use treatment with methadone, buprenorphine/Suboxone, Sublocade, Brixadi, Vivitrol, naloxone, counselling and behavioural therapy, plus related Hepatitis C/HIV services and telehealth by arrangement.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Methadone candidacy and medication choice depend on assessment. New Hope describes services for adults and lists pregnant patients, veterans and LGBTQ+ clients among populations served; confirm any minor or young adult eligibility directly. Payment options include AHCCCS/ACC plans, Medicare/Medicaid dual eligible, SUBG when available, TriWest, self-pay and FSA/HSA.

**Population Served**
Mesa and East Valley people seeking opioid-use disorder treatment, including men, women, pregnant patients, veterans and LGBTQ+ clients.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-981-1022 or 877-508-9490, or email information@nhbhc.net, for the Arizona OTP/SUD clinic in Suite 114. Outreach is 480-993-5919. Existing OTP/SUD after-hours medical contact is 480-826-2646, including text. Use the separate Integrated Behavioral Health Clinic entry for Suite 216 appointments.

**Important Information to Know**
Doors close promptly at posted closing times. Confirm pregnancy pathway, guest dosing, take-home dosing, adolescent eligibility, current funding and whether a payer requires a different assigned provider before referral.

resources.name: Native American Connections - West Valley Housing Assistance Center
resources.description: Native American Connections operates the West Valley Housing Assistance Center in Surprise as a community hub for people facing homelessness or housing instability. It is currently open for heat relief, hydration and cooling, with housing assistance and partner services being phased in through fall 2026.
resources.address: 12779 W Grand Ave, Surprise, AZ 85374
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM for heat relief, hydration and cooling.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Heat relief, hydration, cooling space and phased-in housing-assistance services. The center is designed as a hub for warm referrals, coordinated support and partner services for people facing homelessness or housing instability.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open for heat relief and hydration during posted hours. Housing assistance and shelter-unit services have separate eligibility and intake routes; official page says shelter eligibility and intake are managed by Phoenix Rescue Mission, not on site.

**Population Served**
West Valley individuals and families facing homelessness or housing instability. Mesa clients would generally use this only if they are in or can reasonably reach the West Valley.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit 12779 W Grand Ave, Surprise Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM for cooling/hydration. For general WVHAC questions, email WVHAC@nativeconnections.org. Families can call Family Housing Hub at 877-211-8661; single adults can use Brian Garcia Welcome Center; youth can call 602-263-5531; Native American adults and youth can call 602-648-9739.

**Important Information to Know**
This is far from Mesa and should be treated as a reserve option. On-site partner services are expected to begin in October 2026, and not all planned housing services may be active yet.

resources.name: Midwestern University Clinics - Eye Institute and Therapy Institute Low Vision Rehabilitation
resources.description: Midwestern University Eye Institute and Therapy Institute provide comprehensive eye exams, glasses and contacts, disease screening, pediatric eye care, low-vision rehabilitation, vision therapy and related rehabilitative services in Glendale.
resources.address: 5865 W. Utopia Rd., Glendale, AZ 85308; Therapy Institute 5815 W. Utopia Rd., Glendale, AZ 85308
resources.hours: Eye Institute clinic hours Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM. Optical hours vary. Therapy Institute listed Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Comprehensive eye exams, glasses and contact lenses, disease screening, primary eye care, pediatric eye care, low-vision and rehabilitative vision services, sports vision, vision therapy and related therapy services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Patients should schedule by phone and bring photo ID, payment, insurance card if applicable and medication information. Insurance acceptance and financial-hardship options should be confirmed before travel.

**Population Served**
Children and adults needing eye or vision care, including people with low vision or rehabilitative vision needs who can travel to Glendale.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 623-537-6000 to schedule and ask which institute is appropriate. Eye Institute address is 5865 W. Utopia Rd.; Therapy Institute is 5815 W. Utopia Rd., Glendale, AZ 85308.

**Important Information to Know**
This is university clinic care, not guaranteed free care. Payment is generally due at service and optical orders when placed. Ask patient accounts at 623-537-6000 about MWU Cares financial-hardship options, accepted insurance, referral/prior-authorization needs and the correct institute. Mesa clients need Glendale transport planning.

resources.name: AHCCCS - SSI Medical Assistance Only / Aged, Blind or Disabled Medical Assistance
resources.description: AHCCCS SSI Medical Assistance Only / aged-blind-disabled medical assistance is a Medicaid eligibility pathway for Arizona residents who are age 65 or older, blind or disabled and meet program rules without receiving SSI cash Medicaid automatically.
resources.hours: Use Health-e-Arizona Plus or AHCCCS/DES application assistance; phone support is generally weekday business hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
SSI MAO / aged-blind-disabled medical assistance can provide AHCCCS Medical Assistance coverage for qualifying people who meet age, blindness or disability criteria and financial/nonfinancial rules.

**Eligibility Requirements**
AHCCCS policy lists requirements including a valid application, age 65 or older, blindness or disability, Arizona residency, Social Security number, U.S. citizenship or qualified noncitizen status, assignment of medical-benefit rights and income at or below the applicable limit. AHCCCS also describes health insurance for individuals who are blind or have a disability, with no monthly premiums for those who qualify.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents who are aged, blind or disabled and may need AHCCCS medical coverage, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents not receiving SSI cash benefits.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply through Health-e-Arizona Plus or call 1-855-432-7587 for application help. Ask specifically about the aged, blind or disabled / SSI MAO category if disability or blindness is part of eligibility.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a Medicaid eligibility category, not Social Security cash benefits. Disability determination, income calculation, documentation and other AHCCCS rules may affect approval. Current eligibility should be confirmed during application.

resources.name: Mesa Fire and Medical Department - Home Safety Education
resources.description: Free Mesa Fire and Medical Department in-home safety education program that helps City of Mesa residents reduce fall and fire risks and can include smoke-alarm checks or installation and grab-bar installation where possible.
resources.hours: Scheduling is by email contact; appointment wait times are not posted.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Home Safety Education Program sends a trained Mesa Fire and Medical volunteer to identify possible hazards in the home, suggest and make immediate changes where possible, provide fall-prevention and fire-risk education, help with home escape planning, check or install smoke alarms including alarms for deaf and hard-of-hearing residents, and install grab bars where possible. Group presentations are also available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page states the program is free and available to all City of Mesa residents. It is not limited to seniors.

**Population Served**
City of Mesa residents, including older adults, people with fall risks and residents who need fire-safety or smoke-alarm support.

**How to Best Connect**
Email FDHomeSafety@mesaaz.gov to schedule an in-home appointment or group presentation. For urgent fire, medical or safety emergencies, call 911.

**Important Information to Know**
The page does not guarantee appointment timing or that every recommended modification can be supplied. The program is education and immediate low-level safety support, not full home repair.

resources.name: Honora Healthcare Services - Transportation (TRA/TRE) for Day Program and Employment Services
resources.description: Honora Healthcare Services provides non-emergency ground transportation using TRA/TRE service codes for members receiving its day-treatment/day-program or group supported employment services.
resources.address: 3930 E. University Drive, Mesa, AZ 85205; 1805 E Elliot Road, Suite 114, Tempe, AZ 85284
resources.hours: Program transportation hours are not fully published; confirm with the specific Honora program site.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Honora Healthcare Services provides non-emergency ground transportation for members using TRA/TRE services tied to day program services and employment-related group supported employment services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The transportation page describes service for members receiving day program services such as DTA, DTT and DTS, or employment-related GSE services. Payer authorization and referral requirements should be confirmed with Honora.

**Population Served**
Members enrolled in or being referred to qualifying Honora day-treatment, after-school/summer day-treatment or group supported employment services, including people with developmental or other support needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the DeRonke Center in Mesa at 480-807-0018 or the after-hours number 602-330-3472. For Tempe DTA/GSE call 480-656-5473; for DTT/DTS call 480-809-6779.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not open public transportation. It is restricted to Honora members and specific program services. Confirm authorization, service codes, pickup area, schedule, cost or payer coverage before relying on it.

resources.name: Maricopa Community Colleges - Reduced-Price Transit and Bus Passes
resources.description: Maricopa Community Colleges offers reduced-price Valley Metro 31-day and semester transit passes for eligible students and employees, with Mesa Community College contacts listed for local access.
resources.address: Mesa Community College: 1833 W Southern Ave, Mesa, AZ 85202; Red Mountain Campus: 7110 E McKellips Rd, Mesa, AZ 85207
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Reduced-price Valley Metro bus/light rail passes for Maricopa Community Colleges students and employees. The district page lists semester passes, regular 31-day passes, and reduced-fare 31-day passes with subsidized out-of-pocket costs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Students must be registered for 6 or more credit hours and commute to campus by transit at least two days per week. Employees must work 25 or more hours per week and commute to a Maricopa work site by bus or light rail at least two days per week. Student workers may use the student subsidy if otherwise eligible.

**Population Served**
Maricopa Community Colleges students and employees, including Mesa Community College students and staff.

**How to Best Connect**
Start with MCC Student Life and Leadership to request an eligible subsidized-pass voucher, then pay at the Bookstore. Local contacts listed by the district are Beth Ann Wright at 480-461-7277 and Erica Horihan at 480-654-7758. Ask which campus office and pass option to use.

**Important Information to Know**
The reviewed district prices are $115 for a semester pass and $32 for a regular 31-day student or employee pass. Approved reduced-fare 31-day passes are $7 for students and $12 for employees. Confirm current prices and reduced-fare eligibility. Subsidized vouchers are limited and first come, first served; a full-price purchase may be available if the subsidy is exhausted.

resources.name: Arizona Farmers Market Nutrition Program - Senior FMNP and WIC FMNP Coupons
resources.description: Arizona Farmers Market Nutrition Program provides once-yearly $50 coupon benefits for eligible seniors and active WIC participants to buy fresh Arizona-grown produce at participating markets and farm stands.
resources.hours: 2026 applications are posted to close September 30, 2026, subject to available funding; coupons may be spent through November 15, 2026.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Senior FMNP and WIC FMNP provide seasonal coupon booklets for fresh Arizona-grown fruits and vegetables at approved farmers markets and farm stands.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Senior FMNP applicants must be at least 60 and meet income eligibility at or below 185 percent of the Federal Poverty Level. WIC FMNP applicants must have at least one active WIC benefit recipient in the household on the application date; eligible WIC categories include infants 6 months or older, children ages 1-5, and WIC-designated pregnant, postpartum or breastfeeding participants.

**Population Served**
Eligible Arizona seniors and WIC households, including Maricopa County residents who can use participating markets or farm stands.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through the AZFMNP application page or request a paper application by emailing info@azfmnp.org or calling 833-836-8253 ext. 4. Use the official market finder to identify participating locations.

**Important Information to Know**
Benefits are first come, first served and depend on funding. The page states 2026 applications close September 30, 2026 and coupons must be spent by November 15, 2026.

resources.name: Mesa Community College - Care Team Emergency Financial Assistance and Student Life Basic Needs Supports
resources.description: Mesa Community College lists Care Team emergency financial assistance and Student Life basic-needs supports for MCC students, including help or referrals for school needs, housing, rent, utilities, transportation, childcare, food, DES/SNAP, medical, dental and veterans emergency funds.
resources.phone: Care Team 480-461-7288; Student Life Southern/Dobson 480-461-7285; Student Life Red Mountain 480-654-7759; Veteran Services 480-461-7425 or 480-654-7752
resources.address: 1833 West Southern Ave, Mesa, AZ 85202; Red Mountain Campus 7110 East McKellips Road, Mesa, AZ 85207
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
MCC's Care Team lists referrals and emergency financial assistance for school needs, housing, rent and utilities, plus help with transportation, child care, mental/behavioral health, legal services, food, DES/SNAP, medical resources and dental resources. Student Life also lists free bus passes, discounted bus vouchers, Mesa Market food, hygiene and clothing, and Veteran Services lists emergency funds for veterans.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The public page is for Mesa Community College students and MCC resources. Specific fund availability, application steps and award rules are not published on the page and must be confirmed with the Care Team, Student Life or Veteran Services.

**Population Served**
Mesa Community College students at Southern and Dobson, Red Mountain and MCC Online who need emergency or basic-needs support.

**How to Best Connect**
For Care Team support, call 480-461-7288 or visit Southern and Dobson Student Success Building 36N. Student Life contacts are Southern and Dobson 480-461-7285 and Red Mountain 480-654-7759. Veteran Services contacts are Southern/Dobson 480-461-7425 and Red Mountain 480-654-7752.

**Important Information to Know**
This is student-specific assistance, not general public aid. Emergency financial assistance may depend on current fund availability and documentation. Ask whether aid is paid to the student, the school or a vendor before relying on it for a deadline.

resources.name: Efficiency Arizona Home Energy Rebates
resources.description: Efficiency Arizona is a statewide rebate program for qualified households to install efficient appliances, HVAC, insulation, air sealing, wiring, and panel upgrades, with rebates based on income and eligible products.
resources.address: 1700 W Washington St, Ste 500, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Efficiency Arizona offers rebates for qualified home energy upgrades, including heat pumps for heating/cooling, heat pump water heaters, electric cooking appliances, heat pump clothes dryers, insulation, air sealing, ventilation, wiring, and electric load service center/panel upgrades. Rebates can cover a percentage of project costs up to $14,000 per household depending on income and project type.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility depends on household income, product type, property/project rules, and program guidelines. Applicants must apply and be approved before using the contractor or retail pathway. Current documentation is required and expired documents are not accepted.

**Population Served**
Qualified Arizona households, especially income-qualified homeowners or households able to complete eligible energy upgrade projects.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply by creating an account and completing the online application linked from EfficiencyArizona.com. The official page estimates the application takes 10-15 minutes if documentation is ready. Use the eligibility checker before beginning.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a rebate pathway, not emergency utility-bill, arrears, or shutoff assistance. The rebate may not cover the full project cost; the applicant is responsible for any balance, taxes, and installation fees. The page warns that applications are still being accepted but must meet new federal-guideline changes.

resources.name: Disabled American Veterans Chapter 8 - Veteran Financial Assistance Grant
resources.description: Disabled American Veterans Chapter 8 in Mesa offers one-time grants up to $300 for veterans in need, including rental, utility, and transportation assistance paid directly to landlords or utility companies.
resources.address: 655 N Gilbert Rd, Mesa, AZ 85203
resources.hours: Mesa office Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-noon, with one Saturday monthly. Chapter claims visits have separate appointment/walk-in rules.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Short-term veteran financial assistance with one-time grants up to $300 for rental assistance, utility assistance, and transportation. Payments are made directly to landlords or utility companies.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open to veterans in need. For balances over $300, the applicant must show they can cover the remainder. Documentation listed on the Veteran Assistance Application is required.

**Population Served**
Mesa/East Valley veterans in need of short-term rent, utility, or transportation assistance.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to the Mesa office at 655 N Gilbert Rd to start, or call 480-890-2424. Bring documentation listed on the application form.

**Important Information to Know**
The grant is limited in amount and depends on available resources and documentation. It is not ongoing monthly assistance.

resources.name: Community 43 - Community 43 Clubhouse
resources.description: Community 43 Clubhouse is a membership-based mental-health recovery community in Phoenix offering a clubhouse model with daily structure, peer connection, meaningful work, life skills, community activities, purpose-building, transitional employment opportunities and scholarship support for mental-health services.
resources.address: 4343 N. 16th St., Phoenix, AZ 85016
resources.hours: Monday-Tuesday 7:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m.; Wednesday-Friday 7:30 a.m.-7 p.m.; Saturday-Sunday 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Community 43 offers a Clubhouse model for mental-health recovery, including daily activities, meaningful social connection, life skills, work-ordered day participation, shared decision-making, supportive relationships, inclusive community activities, transitional employment opportunities and scholarships for mental-health services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Prospective members should complete the membership application, email it to referralsC43@community43.org and arrange a tour. The public page does not list diagnosis documentation, cost or insurance requirements; confirm membership fit directly.

**Population Served**
People living with mental illness or needing mental-health recovery support, especially those facing isolation or low-income barriers in the Phoenix/Maricopa County area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-274-4343, email ReferralsC43@Community43.org, complete the Become a Member form and arrange a tour. The clubhouse is at 4343 N. 16th St., Phoenix. Hours are Monday-Tuesday 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Wednesday-Friday 7:30 a.m. to 7 p.m., and Saturday-Sunday 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

**Important Information to Know**
Community 43 is non-clinical clubhouse recovery support, not outpatient therapy or crisis care. It may be a good reserve option for social connection, daily structure, purpose and recovery community.

resources.name: Oakwood Creative Care - The Hub Mesa / Mesa Memory Cafe
resources.description: Oakwood Creative Care's Hub Mesa hosts the free Mesa Memory Cafe and other dementia-focused caregiver supports for people with memory impairment and their care partners.
resources.address: 6915 E. Main St., Mesa, AZ 85207
resources.hours: Memory Cafe listed Tuesdays 1:00 PM-2:30 PM and Wednesdays 9:30 AM-11:00 AM; call or email before attending because calendars can change.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Mesa Memory Cafe is a free social and supportive program where a person living with memory impairment attends with a family member or care partner. Participants can share coffee and a pastry, join engagement activities, and connect with caregiver support and dementia resources at The Hub Mesa.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A person with memory impairment should attend with a care partner. The public page does not list income, insurance or diagnosis documentation requirements for Memory Cafe attendance.

**Population Served**
People living with memory impairment, dementia or aging-related memory challenges, and their family caregivers or care partners in Mesa and nearby East Valley communities.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact dementiafriendlymesa@oakwoodcreativecare.org or call The Hub Mesa at 480-625-3867. The program is at The Dementia Hub, 6915 E. Main St., Mesa, AZ 85207. The listed Memory Cafe times are Tuesdays 1:00 PM-2:30 PM and Wednesdays 9:30 AM-11:00 AM.

**Important Information to Know**
This is supportive education, social connection and caregiver support, not medical diagnosis, unattended respite or personal care. Some Oakwood Hub offerings may be free, while GUIDE membership or other Oakwood services can have separate eligibility or payment rules.

resources.name: City of Mesa - Abandoned Bicycle Program
resources.description: The City of Mesa Abandoned Bicycle Program lets qualifying community organizations request free recovered bicycles for distribution to clients who need transportation to work, school or similar destinations.
resources.address: City of Mesa Police Department Evidence Section / Neighborhood Outreach process, Mesa, AZ
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 7:30 AM-5:30 PM
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The program donates available abandoned bicycles from Mesa Police to eligible organizations. Organizations may distribute the bikes to clients in need for transportation to work, school and similar destinations.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Requests must come from government agencies, charitable nonprofits or community-benefit groups. Organizations must use bikes for clients, not employees or directors, may not sell them, and must use the official request form.

**Population Served**
Clients of approved community organizations in Mesa who can use a bicycle for transportation.

**How to Best Connect**
An eligible organization should submit the Abandoned Bicycle Request form with at least 30 business days of notice. Contact 480-644-5432 or volunteer@mesaaz.gov with questions. If approved, police property staff arrange pickup.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not direct individual walk-in intake. Bicycles are subject to availability, condition varies and some may require refurbishing. Organizations may request no more than 30 bicycles per calendar year.

resources.name: Mesa Public Schools - Parent University
resources.description: Mesa Public Schools Parent University offers free in-person and virtual parenting, school-readiness and family-skill classes for adults; Mesa residency is not required.
resources.address: 155 N. Center St., Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Community Education office hours: Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM; Friday 8:00 AM-4:15 PM. Class dates vary.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Parent University offers free in-person and virtual classes on parenting skills, reading, kindergarten preparation, social-emotional learning, suicide awareness and other rotating family topics. Some classes are offered in Spanish, and Spanish interpretation can be requested on the registration form.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Classes are open to adults; Mesa residency is not required. Participants must meet the requirements for the specific in-person or online class.

**Population Served**
Parents, caregivers, school staff and community adults who want parenting, school-readiness or child-development skills for children and families.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Parent University registration form on the Mesa Public Schools page, email parent-u@mpsaz.org, or call 480-472-0233 with class questions. Community Education is located at 155 N. Center St., Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
Classes are free, but topics and schedules rotate. Childcare is not provided, and children are not allowed in classes unless a class specifically invites students.

resources.name: Child & Family Resources - Housing Stability Certified Community Legal Advocate sponsor
resources.description: Child & Family Resources is listed by Arizona Courts as an approved Housing Stability Certified Community Legal Advocate organization for Phoenix/Maricopa County; its Phoenix office can be contacted to ask about housing-stability legal advocate availability and referral steps.
resources.address: 1951 W Camelback Road, Suite 370, Phoenix, AZ 85015
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Potential limited-scope housing-stability legal advocate help through Certified Community Legal Advocates, such as eviction-process guidance or housing-related civil legal advice within the CCLA scope.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Arizona Courts lists approved organizations as resource hubs serving low-income people with housing instability or domestic violence needs. Child & Family Resources' public Phoenix page does not describe a public legal intake, so callers should confirm current eligibility and referral requirements.

**Population Served**
Phoenix/Maricopa County families and community members connected to Child & Family Resources, especially those with housing-stability legal needs.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Phoenix office at 602-234-3941 or contact Child & Family Resources through its Phoenix location page. Ask specifically for Housing Stability Certified Community Legal Advocate services or referral instructions.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a clearly advertised walk-in legal aid clinic. The strongest public support is the Arizona Courts CCLA directory, while the provider's own Phoenix page lists family and youth programs. Confirm availability, issue fit and whether Mesa residents can be served before relying on it for urgent eviction deadlines.

resources.name: Chicanos Por La Causa - Parenting Arizona / Guadalupe Family Resource Center
resources.description: Chicanos Por La Causa Parenting Arizona offers free parenting classes and family resource center programming in Maricopa County, including the Guadalupe Family Resource Center near Mesa and Tempe.
resources.address: 5840 E. Calle Santos Bravo, Guadalupe, AZ 85283
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
CPLC Parenting Arizona provides and connects at-risk families to parent education, life-skills training, community resources, free parenting classes, family resource center activities, weekly classes, social events, and community connection. Curricula include Active Parenting and Fatherhood/Motherhood is Sacred.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Free parenting classes are offered to parents and caregivers of children in Maricopa and Coconino counties. Home visitation with Parents as Teachers is listed for other Arizona areas, not Maricopa, so Mesa families should use the Guadalupe/Maricopa class and FRC route unless CPLC confirms otherwise.

**Population Served**
Parents and caregivers in Maricopa County, including families near Mesa, Tempe, and Guadalupe who need parenting education, family-resource-center connection, or culturally grounded parent support.

**How to Best Connect**
For Maricopa County parenting classes, email ParentingAZworkshops@cplc.org or call 480-491-2301. The Guadalupe Family Resource Center is at 5840 E. Calle Santos Bravo, Guadalupe, AZ 85283; the CPLC page also links a registration form. Ask which language options are available for the requested service.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a parenting education and family resource center option, not direct child care, medical care, or emergency financial assistance. Confirm whether a Mesa family can enroll in the desired Guadalupe FRC activity and whether sessions are virtual or in person.

resources.name: Arizona Masonry Council - Central Arizona Masonry and Block Machine Operator Apprenticeships
resources.description: Arizona Masonry Council operates masonry workforce-development programs, including registered masonry apprenticeship and a block/masonry machine-operator apprenticeship; current public pages conflict about which track is accepting applications, so call before referral.
resources.address: 3133 W. Frye Rd., Suite 101, Chandler, AZ 85226
resources.hours: Masonry classes have been described as Saturday mornings January-November; current schedule and track availability must be confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Arizona Masonry Council workforce development includes masonry apprenticeship, tender training, and a block/machine-operator apprenticeship. The machine-operator program is described as a three-year earn-while-you-learn registered apprenticeship combining on-the-job learning, classroom instruction, and hands-on skill development in hydraulic, pneumatic, mechanical, electrical, and masonry technology systems.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Requirements vary by track and employer. Public materials include an application for Central Arizona apprenticeship service in the greater Phoenix metropolitan area with classes/lab at EVIT in Mesa; the application asks about reliable transportation and ability to perform masonry job duties.

**Population Served**
Central Arizona and Phoenix metro job seekers interested in masonry or block machine-operator trades, including Mesa/East Valley applicants who can access EVIT or participating employer locations.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-262-0510 or email support@azmasonry.org. Ask whether Central Arizona masonry apprenticeship, machine-operator apprenticeship, or tender training is currently accepting applications, and confirm the next interview night, employer requirements, fees, and class location.

**Important Information to Know**
The masonry apprenticeship page says not accepting applications/check back, while the machine-operator page offers registration. Preserve this conflict and verify the desired track before sending a client.

resources.name: Mesa Arts Center - Arts in Service
resources.description: Mesa Arts Center Arts in Service provides studio-arts experiences and creative pathways for veterans and service members seeking supportive community, stress relief, wellness, or art-making career exploration.
resources.address: 1 E. Main St., Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Classes follow the current Arts in Service schedule. Box office/registration: Tuesday–Saturday, noon–5:00 PM; Sunday–Monday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Studio-arts classes and creative pathways for veterans and service members focused on supportive community, stress relief, overall health and wellness, and possible art-making career interests.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The page describes Arts in Service as a veteran and service-member program. Current class availability, registration rules, and any service-verification steps should be checked during registration.

**Population Served**
Veterans and service members in Mesa and the surrounding area.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Arts in Service page to explore classes and register, or contact Mesa Arts Center Box Office & Registration at 480-644-6500 / boxoffice@mesaartscenter.com. Location: 1 E. Main St., Mesa, AZ 85201.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a wellness/community arts program, not clinical mental-health treatment or emergency assistance. Schedules and class seats can change, so check current offerings before sending a client.

resources.name: Arizona DES — Registered Apprenticeship Search
resources.description: A public route to Arizona’s registered apprenticeship information and active program sponsors across trades and occupations.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

A public route to Arizona’s registered apprenticeship information and active program sponsors across trades and occupations.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Each sponsor sets entry, screening, employment, training and application-window requirements. A listing does not establish that applications or jobs are currently available.

**Population Served**

Arizona job seekers comparing paid work-and-learning pathways.

**How to Best Connect**

Use the Arizona DES apprenticeship page to find sponsors, then contact the selected program directly. Ask a workforce center about individual funding or support eligibility.

**Important Information to Know**

Registration confirms the program’s apprenticeship framework, not an immediate vacancy, free training or a guarantee of employment. Confirm location, costs and travel before applying.

resources.name: City of Phoenix — HOPWA Housing and Utility Assistance
resources.description: Housing-stability help for eligible households with a member living with HIV or AIDS in Maricopa or Pinal County, including Mesa.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
HOPWA offers short-term rent, mortgage and utility assistance to prevent loss of current housing. A separate placement route may help with deposits, first or last month's rent and approved move-in fees.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The City's linked program guidance requires a household member diagnosed with HIV or AIDS, income at or below 80% of area median income, and current residence in Maricopa or Pinal County. For the short-term assistance route, the household must not already receive housing or utility help from another housing program.

**Population Served**
Eligible households living with HIV or AIDS in the two listed counties, including Mesa residents. This program has a broader service area than Phoenix's general city-resident crisis assistance.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-534-2433 and specifically ask for HOPWA assistance, or apply through the City's linked Community Services Program portal. Ask what current supporting documents and appointments are required.

**Important Information to Know**
Funding, documentation and individual program rules affect assistance. The currently linked eligibility flyer is dated February2024; confirm its requirements during intake. A request is not a guarantee of housing or payment.

resources.name: Society of St. Vincent de Paul Phoenix - Shelter, transitional housing and weather relief
resources.description: Society of St. Vincent de Paul offers adult emergency shelter by referral, transitional housing for eligible adults, seasonal heat relief, and walk-in overnight shelter inquiry at the Phoenix Dining Room.
resources.address: Washington Street Shelter: 2739 E Washington St, Phoenix, AZ 85034; transitional housing at Watkins campus, Phoenix; Mesa Dining Room heat relief: 49 W Broadway Rd, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Transitional housing intake phone: 8:00 AM-3:00 PM; emergency shelter is referral-only and staffed/security 24/7; heat relief runs seasonally; call for open overnight beds.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Adult emergency shelter by community-partner referral, transitional housing with case management, seasonal heat relief at dining rooms, and overnight shelter inquiry at the Phoenix Dining Room.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Transitional housing eligibility includes adults 55+, adults 18+ living with a disability, adults 18+ working or looking for work, and select veteran beds at Ozanam Manor. Washington Street emergency shelter requires referral from community partners and prioritizes nearby residents. Phoenix Dining Room overnight shelter is adults 18+ and walk-in inquiry is allowed.

**Population Served**
Adults experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County, including seniors, adults with disabilities, working/job-seeking adults and some veterans.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-850-6900 between 8:00 AM and 3:00 PM for transitional housing eligibility screening. Emergency shelter is referral-only with no walk-up access. Call 602-478-8172 to ask about open overnight beds at the Phoenix Dining Room.

**Important Information to Know**
Transitional housing has no cost for residents with no income; otherwise cost is 30% of income. Same-day bed availability is not guaranteed. Mesa heat relief is available at the Mesa Dining Room seasonally but overnight shelter is listed only at the Phoenix Dining Room.

resources.name: Maricopa County Department of Public Health - Tuberculosis Control and Prevention Clinic
resources.description: Maricopa County Tuberculosis Control and Prevention Clinic provides TB diagnostic, treatment and case-management services for Maricopa County residents and visitors with latent TB infection, active TB disease, TB exposure or TB clearance needs.
resources.address: 1645 E. Roosevelt St., Phoenix, AZ 85006
resources.hours: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 8:00 AM-11:30 AM and 1:00 PM-4:30 PM; Wednesday 9:00 AM-11:30 AM and 1:00 PM-4:30 PM. Closed daily 12:00 PM-1:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
TB diagnostic services, TB blood and skin testing, symptom evaluation, chest X-rays for clinic patients, sputum and other specimen testing, nurse case management, treatment for active TB and latent TB infection, directly observed therapy, anti-TB medications, lab monitoring, referrals for other medical problems, and TB clearance screenings when capacity permits.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are for Maricopa County residents and visitors diagnosed with, suspected of having, exposed to or at high risk for TB. TB clearance screenings are for non-symptomatic community members by appointment only when clinic capacity permits.

**Population Served**
Maricopa County residents and visitors with TB disease, latent TB infection, TB exposure or required TB clearance screening.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-372-1407 or use the county appointment website for TB clearance availability. The clinic is at 1645 E. Roosevelt St., Phoenix, AZ 85006.

**Important Information to Know**
TB clearance screening has a one-time $65 fee; cash, credit and debit are accepted, checks and insurance are not. For latent TB evaluation/treatment and other services, call the clinic for cost details. This is not a general primary-care clinic.

resources.name: Agua Fria Food & Clothing Bank - Clothing Bank / Backpacks & More
resources.description: Agua Fria Food and Clothing Bank offers a clothing bank, showers, baby care supplies and Backpacks & More school-uniform support for West Valley households; Mesa eligibility should not be assumed.
resources.address: 405 E Harrison Dr, Avondale, AZ 85323
resources.hours: Business hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-noon; Saturday and Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Monthly gently used clothing at no cost for individuals and families in need, showers and shower kits for people without shower facilities, baby formula/food/diapers for a limited number of babies, senior food boxes, and a Backpacks & More school-uniform/supplies program by application.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page says clothing requires valid identification and proof of current address. Backpacks & More is for children who live in the service area and attend a school requiring uniforms, with May applications. Baby Care is based on need, availability and application. The exact public service-area boundary is not stated on the official page inspected.

**Population Served**
Primarily Southwest/West Valley residents who can access the Avondale site, including people without housing, seniors, families with babies and children needing school uniforms.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 623-932-9135 before referring a Mesa-area client, especially to confirm service-area rules and clothing-bank days. The site is at 405 E Harrison Dr, Avondale.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a useful Maricopa County reserve for West Valley clients, but not Mesa-focused. Do not assume a Mesa resident can use the clothing bank or school-uniform program without confirming address eligibility.

resources.name: Honora Healthcare Services - Group Supported Employment
resources.description: Honora Healthcare Services provides group supported employment for members in supervised community work settings with paid work and transportation tied to employment-related services.
resources.address: 3930 E. University Drive, Mesa, AZ 85205; 1805 E. Elliot Road, Suite 114, Tempe, AZ 85284
resources.hours: Call for current program schedule, intake and openings.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Honora's Group Supported Employment service provides long-term ongoing support for employed members in on-site supervised community employment settings. The service promotes community integration with other workers and provides paid work. Honora also provides non-emergency ground transportation for day program and employment-related services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The page describes services for members and does not fully state public eligibility. Group supported employment usually requires disability-service authorization; confirm DDD or other funding, service fit, transportation and current work-group availability before referral.

**Population Served**
People with disabilities in Mesa and Tempe who need supervised group supported employment and related transportation through Honora's service system.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Mesa DeRonke Center at 480-807-0018 or after-hours 602-330-3472. For the Tempe Debisi Center, call 480-656-5473 for DTA/GSE. Ask about GSE authorization, active work groups, transportation boundaries and openings.

**Important Information to Know**
The page confirms paid work in supervised community settings, but it does not list wages, employer sites, openings or detailed funding rules. Verify active placements and authorization before referral.

resources.name: The Welcome to America Project - Newcomer Welcomes and Career Bridge
resources.description: The Welcome to America Project supports newly resettled refugees and newcomers with household goods, clothing, transportation assistance, community connections, and Career Bridge employment-readiness services from its Tempe location near Mesa.
resources.address: 1711 W. University Dr., Suite 158, Tempe, AZ 85281
resources.hours: Client services are scheduled through WTAP or partners; call for referral and appointment details.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Newcomer welcome support, household essentials, clothing access, transportation assistance, community connection, and Career Bridge support such as resume/CV help, interview preparation, employer referrals, mentorship, free training access, and budget guidance.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are for newly resettled refugees and newcomers. Some employment/Career Bridge services may require ORR-designated eligible status and employment authorization; confirm eligibility and referral route with WTAP.

**Population Served**
Newly resettled refugee families and other eligible newcomer households in the Phoenix/Tempe area, including families near Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-490-0088 or email info@wtap.org to ask about newcomer support, referrals, or Career Bridge. The Tempe office is close to Mesa, but services may be scheduled or partner-mediated.

**Important Information to Know**
This is refugee integration and practical resettlement support, not immigration legal representation. Clients should not assume they can self-shop for goods without an arranged referral or appointment.

resources.name: City Hope Arizona / Christ Church - City Hope Centers Clothing
resources.description: City Hope Centers provide no-cost food and clothing at Gilbert and Phoenix centers. Guests may visit each center once per calendar month; no appointment is needed, government ID is requested, and distributions may close early at capacity. The Mesa center provides food only.
resources.address: Gilbert Center: 1120 S Gilbert Rd, Suite 101, Gilbert, AZ 85296; Phoenix Center: 1640 W Camelback Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85015; Mesa Center food-only: 655 E University Dr, Mesa, AZ 85203
resources.hours: Gilbert: Monday, Wednesday, Saturday 9:00-11:30 AM. Phoenix: Tuesday and Thursday 2:00-4:30 PM; Saturday 9:00-11:30 AM. Mesa food-only: Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday 9:00-11:30 AM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost shopping for food and clothing items at City Hope Centers. Gilbert and Phoenix centers include clothing; the Mesa center provides food only.

**Eligibility Requirements**
No appointment is necessary. Guests are allowed one visit to each center per calendar month and should bring a driver's license or government-issued ID.

**Population Served**
Households in the Valley who can access City Hope centers and need no-cost food or clothing. Mesa clients needing clothing should use the Gilbert or Phoenix center rather than the Mesa food-only center.

**How to Best Connect**
For clothing, use Gilbert or Phoenix center hours. Gilbert: 1120 S Gilbert Rd, Suite 101, 480-900-5422. Phoenix: 1640 W Camelback Rd, 480-716-4399. Mesa questions: 480-805-1031.

**Important Information to Know**
Each distribution may close early after reaching capacity. Arrive at least 15 minutes before closing and confirm the center's current clothing availability before travel.

resources.name: Phoenix Rescue Mission - Hope Coach Mobile Outreach / Street Outreach Services
resources.description: Phoenix Rescue Mission's Hope Coach mobile outreach can be requested for a person living on the street by calling with the nearest cross streets. Outreach teams provide water, seasonal basic needs and case-management connection toward shelter, housing, recovery programs and other services.
resources.address: Mobile outreach throughout Maricopa County; mailing address PO Box 6708, Phoenix, AZ 85005
resources.hours: Outreach hours and response times are not published; call and provide clear location details.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Mobile outreach for people living unsheltered, including water, hygiene/seasonal supplies, repeated engagement, peer/case management, help addressing missing IDs/documents and connections toward shelter, housing, recovery and other services. Staff may assess fit for Mission programmes such as Rescue-Assess-Place; separate admission rules apply.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people living unsheltered in the outreach team's service area. A request needs the nearest cross streets or clear location details. Coverage and response timing depend on field operations.

**Population Served**
People experiencing unsheltered homelessness in Maricopa County, including Mesa when within current outreach coverage.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-346-3361 for street outreach or 602-233-3000 for Mission help, giving the nearest cross streets and current location. Ask about Mesa coverage, response timing and the appropriate referral. This is not emergency dispatch; use 911 for immediate danger.

**Important Information to Know**
Outreach does not guarantee same-day contact, a bed or programme acceptance. This is navigation and case support, not an open rent/utility cash fund. Residential or recovery programmes have separate eligibility.

resources.name: Bank On Arizona - Certified Safe Bank and Credit-Union Accounts
