resources.description: Bank On Arizona connects people to certified low-cost, low-fee bank and credit-union accounts as an alternative to check-cashing, overdraft-heavy accounts, and payday products.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Connections to Bank On certified checking or savings accounts at participating banks and credit unions. Certified accounts are federally insured, cost $5 or less per month, allow free deposits, withdrawals, and bill payments, and do not allow overdraft or nonsufficient-funds fees.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Clients must meet the account-opening requirements of a participating financial institution. Bank On says to bring current government-issued identification; some institutions may accept other IDs or request a second form of ID.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents who need a safe, affordable bank or credit-union account, including people who are unbanked or underbanked.

**How to Best Connect**
Use Bank On Arizona's website to find a participating bank or credit union and ask about opening a Bank On Arizona account. For general questions, call 602-899-5282 or email jessica@bankonaz.org.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a cash grant or emergency bill-payment program. It is most useful when paired with paychecks, public benefits, or tax refunds that can be direct-deposited into a safer account.

resources.name: Exceptional Student Services Dispute Resolution - Due Process
resources.description: Official Arizona Department of Education due-process complaint and hearing pathway for IDEA special-education disputes involving identification, evaluation, placement, or FAPE.
resources.address: 1535 West Jefferson Street, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Arizona Department of Education Exceptional Student Services provides the official due-process complaint pathway for special-education disputes. Due process can resolve matters about identification, evaluation, placement, or the provision of a free appropriate public education.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A due-process complaint can be filed by a parent, a public education agency, or a student who has reached age 18 in Arizona. The dispute must fit the IDEA/special-education due-process scope.

**Population Served**
Arizona students with disabilities, families, adult students, and public education agencies, including Mesa schools.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the online model due-process complaint form or downloadable English/Spanish forms on the ADE due-process page. For questions, contact the ESS Reception Desk at 602-542-4013.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an administrative legal pathway, not attorney representation or advocacy. Families may still need a separate advocate or attorney for legal strategy, hearing preparation, or representation.

resources.name: Homeless ID Project - Mesa and Phoenix replacement ID services
resources.description: Homeless ID Project provides free help obtaining replacement Arizona IDs, driver licenses, birth certificates and supporting documents, with secure document storage and TeleMVD access at selected locations.
resources.address: 49 W Broadway Road, Mesa, AZ 85210; Phoenix office at 1125 W Jackson St, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.hours: Mesa SVDP Dining Room: 2nd and 4th Tuesdays, 1:00 PM-3:30 PM, first come, first served. Phoenix Keys to Change/Lodestar office: Monday-Friday, 8:00 AM-1:00 PM, closed every 2nd Wednesday and 3rd Monday of the month, first come, first served.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost help seeking replacement Arizona IDs/driver licenses, birth certificates from all 50 states and supporting records, with application help, eligible fees, TeleMVD at selected locations and secure document storage. Veteran guidance explains the Arizona no-cost veteran ID/license pathway.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people experiencing homelessness or housing instability who need documents. Staff assess available identity evidence, including when everything is lost; government rules still apply. The veteran no-cost pathway may require recent documentation of homelessness from a provider/VA within 60 days and veteran-status evidence such as DD214 or VA records.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness in the Phoenix and Tucson metro areas, including Mesa and Maricopa County clients who can use the Mesa SVDP site or the Phoenix Keys to Change office. Veteran-specific help is also linked from the program.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to the Mesa shared-space site at SVDP Mesa Dining Room, 49 W Broadway Road, on the 2nd and 4th Tuesdays from 1:00 PM to 3:30 PM, first come, first served, or call 602-223-3427. The Phoenix office is inside the Lodestar Day Resource Center at Keys to Change, 1125 W Jackson St, and is listed Monday through Friday from 8:00 AM to 1:00 PM, first come, first served. Confirm holiday and closure dates before sending a client.

**Important Information to Know**
The project helps and funds the process; it does not itself issue records, override MVD/vital-record rules or guarantee timing. IDs may take 7–10 business days after processing, with temporary paper ID when applicable. License testing, reinstatement or other requirements may remain. Mesa is a twice-monthly shared site; SVdP is the host, not the daily document agency.

resources.name: VA Phoenix Minority Veteran Care
resources.description: VA Phoenix Minority Veteran Care works to increase local awareness of minority-veteran issues, identify access barriers, and help veterans find VA benefits, services and programs.
resources.address: 650 E. Indian School Road, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.hours: Coordinator hours are not published; call VA Phoenix main line for routing.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Care coordination and facilitation to help minority veterans understand and access VA benefits, services and programs; identify barriers; and improve access within VA Phoenix Health Care.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are for veterans using or seeking VA Phoenix care and benefit information. The program acts as a mediator and facilitator and does not process claims, equal-employment complaints or employee-related issues.

**Population Served**
All veterans, with focus on minority veterans including Black, Asian American, Hispanic, Native American, Alaska Native, Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander veterans.

**How to Best Connect**
Call VA Phoenix Health Care at 602-277-5551 and ask for Minority Veteran care or the Minority Veterans Program care coordinator.

**Important Information to Know**
This is navigation and facilitation inside VA, not a claims-processing office. For claims filing, use VA benefits counselors or an accredited representative.

resources.name: Double Up Food Bucks Arizona - SNAP Produce Match
resources.description: Double Up Food Bucks Arizona matches SNAP/EBT spending dollar-for-dollar for fruits, vegetables, dried beans and edible plants/seeds at participating Arizona locations.
resources.hours: Use only during participating market, farm stand, CSA, mobile market, corner store or grocery store hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Double Up Food Bucks Arizona gives a dollar-for-dollar produce match when a person spends active SNAP/EBT benefits at a participating location. The match can be used for fruits, vegetables, dried beans, and edible plants and seeds.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A person must have a SNAP/EBT card with an active balance and shop at a participating Double Up location.

**Population Served**
Arizona SNAP participants, including Mesa and Maricopa County households, who can shop at participating markets, farm stands, CSAs, mobile markets, corner stores or grocery stores.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Double Up Arizona website to learn how it works and find participating locations. At a participating site, use the SNAP/EBT card and ask staff how the Double Up match is issued there.

**Important Information to Know**
There is no separate application. The official page lists no daily limit at farmers markets, mobile markets, CSAs and farm stands, and a $20 per day limit at corner/grocery stores. Participating locations and hours change, so check the map before travel.

resources.name: Maricopa County Public Defender Outreach - Veterans StandDown legal aid and restoration-of-rights resources
resources.description: Maricopa County Public Defender outreach, with Office of Public Defense Services partners, documents free legal aid at Veterans StandDown events for veterans engaged in the criminal justice process and provides a public inquiry route for restoration of rights, set-asides, and sealing forms.
resources.address: 301 W Jefferson St, Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.hours: Check current outreach events; record-relief process questions may be emailed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Public Defender outreach offers legal help at veterans StandDown events and provides a contact for questions about restoration of rights, set-asides and sealing forms.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Event assistance has its own eligibility and schedule. Record-related remedies depend on the case and law.

**Population Served**
Veterans with criminal-justice legal needs and people seeking county record-relief process information.

**How to Best Connect**
Email pdinfo@maricopa.gov about the process or future events. The outreach page links to the county criminal-court forms.

**Important Information to Know**
The published March 12–13, 2026, StandDown has passed. Do not travel to a past event or assume this inquiry contact creates representation; confirm the next applicable service.

resources.name: Maricopa County Adult Probation Department · Drug Court, Reach Out Program, and court-ordered SUD treatment
resources.description: Maricopa County Adult Probation provides limited-access justice-system pathways including Drug Court, DUI Court, Reach Out residential substance-use treatment in lieu of custody, contracted treatment referrals and reentry supports for people under court/probation jurisdiction.
resources.address: 222 E Javelina Ave, Suite 100, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: Access depends on court/probation status and assigned officer or court team.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Drug Court clinical assessment, substance-use disorder treatment, random testing and monthly team check-ins; DUI Court; Reach Out residential treatment opportunity in lieu of remaining in custody; contracted treatment referrals; supervision services; and reentry/custody reintegration supports.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Limited to people under Maricopa County court/probation jurisdiction who are assigned or approved for a specialized service. Drug Court, DUI Court and Reach Out have court/probation criteria and are not public walk-in treatment programs.

**Population Served**
Adults with substance-use needs who are participating in eligible Maricopa County probation, Drug Court, Reach Out or related court-controlled treatment pathways. The assigned court or probation team determines the appropriate program.

**How to Best Connect**
Contact the assigned probation officer, defense attorney, court team or Adult Probation main line at 602-506-3204. Mesa-area probation offices include the Southeast Justice Center area at Javelina Avenue.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a court/probation pathway, not a general treatment provider. Participation can affect legal obligations and must be coordinated with the court/probation team.

resources.name: Arizona Behavioral Health Corporation / HOM — Mainstream rental vouchers
resources.description: Rental vouchers for very-low-income households with a disabled member, administered by HOM for Arizona Behavioral Health Corporation.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Rental vouchers for very-low-income households with a disabled member, administered by HOM for Arizona Behavioral Health Corporation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The programme serves disabled households without a preference for a particular disability. Homelessness is not required. Income, household and voucher rules apply.

**Population Served**
Eligible households with disabilities seeking rental assistance.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask HOM about the Mainstream waiting list and application requirements. ABC programme questions can also go to 602-712-9200.

**Important Information to Know**
ABC reports that all 125 vouchers are leased and HOM maintains the waiting list. An inquiry does not establish that new applications are open or that a voucher is available.

resources.name: NATIVE HEALTH - Maternal, Infant, and Early Childhood Home Visiting Program
resources.description: NATIVE HEALTH Maternal, Infant, and Early Childhood Home Visiting strengthens pregnant families and families with children birth to five through parent education, home visits, health and wellness support, child safety, school readiness and resource connection.
resources.address: 777 W. Southern Ave., Building C, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.hours: NATIVE HEALTH Mesa is listed Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-7:00 PM, with telehealth/virtual services until 7:00 PM; home visits are scheduled with enrolled families.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Home Visiting Program provides parent educator visits weekly, every other week or monthly depending on family need. Services focus on family health and wellness, parent-child health, child safety, school readiness, family income/benefits/education, parenting skills, stress, depression, domestic violence risk and substance-use risk.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is designed for pregnant families and families with children birth to five. NATIVE HEALTH lists eligible family members as pregnant mothers, teen parents, fathers and grandparents serving as caregivers. The Mesa location describes the program for pregnant Native American women or families with children through age five.

**Population Served**
Pregnant families, teen parents, fathers, grandparents and caregivers of children ages 0-5. The Mesa location specifically identifies pregnant Native American women or caregivers with children through age five.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-654-1378 ext. 13003 or email dnieto@nachci.com for referrals. Families can also start through NATIVE HEALTH Mesa at 777 W. Southern Ave., Building C, Mesa, AZ 85210.

**Important Information to Know**
Public pages support the home-visiting service and referral route. Eligibility language differs slightly between the general program page and the Mesa location page; non-Native families should call to confirm eligibility or ask for referral to the right home-visiting provider.

resources.name: Chicanos Por La Causa Parenting Arizona - Drug Abuse Prevention for Teens
resources.description: Chicanos Por La Causa Parenting Arizona offers free teen drug-abuse prevention education using the Safety First curriculum, with six virtual sessions for ages 11-18 and parent/caregiver resource connections.
resources.address: Phoenix: 6850 W Indian School Rd, Suite 4, Phoenix, AZ 85033; Guadalupe: 5840 E Calle Santos Bravo, Guadalupe, AZ 85283
resources.hours: Call or register online for current session schedules.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Drug-abuse prevention education for teens using the Safety First curriculum, covering teenage drug use and dependency, risk/effects of drug use, safe decision-making skills, and resources that can help if needed. Parenting Arizona also offers parent/caregiver support and community resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Children/teens ages 11-18 may participate in the six virtual prevention sessions. Confirm registration, language availability, and whether Mesa residents are eligible for the current class cycle.

**Population Served**
Teens ages 11-18 and families in Maricopa County communities served by CPLC Parenting Arizona, including virtual access when available.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-834-2933 or use the program's online registration/contact link from the Parenting Education page. Local Parenting Arizona offices include Phoenix and Guadalupe.

**Important Information to Know**
This is prevention education, not treatment, detox, counseling, or MAT. Youth already struggling with addiction may need a treatment provider in addition to this program.

resources.name: Family Housing Hub - Coordinated Entry for Families Experiencing Homelessness
resources.description: Family Housing Hub is Maricopa County's coordinated access point for families with children under 18 who need homeless services, including shelter assessment, problem-solving, housing planning, waitlist access and referral to participating family shelters or housing resources when eligibility and openings align.
resources.address: MesaCAN satellite, when directed:635 E. Broadway Rd., Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: 2-1-1 phone support is available 7 days a week from 9:00 AM-7:00 PM. MesaCAN satellite hours are Tuesday 9:00 AM-3:00 PM for Mesa residents directed to coordinated entry.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Family coordinated entry, problem-solving/diversion, shelter screening/waitlist access, housing plans and connection to income/housing resources. Matched programmes may offer move-in/rental help when eligible; the Hub itself is not a direct cash fund.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For families in Maricopa County with children under 18 who are facing a housing or homeless crisis and need homeless services. All adults in the household seeking shelter must participate in screening. There is no cost to be added to the waitlist.

**Population Served**
Families with minor children in Maricopa County, including Mesa families who can call 2-1-1 or use the MesaCAN satellite if directed to coordinated entry.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 2-1-1, visit 211arizona.org, or dial 877-211-8661 first. If directed to a physical location and the family is a Mesa resident, visit Family Housing Hub at MesaCAN, 635 E Broadway Rd, Tuesday 9:00 AM-3:00 PM. Arrive by posted closing time to be seen that day. UMOM also lists Family Housing Hub phone access through 602-595-8700.

**Important Information to Know**
Screening does not guarantee an immediate bed, housing or financial help. Matching follows need, safety, programme eligibility and openings, not simply arrival order. All access locations use the same system; use one route rather than visiting multiple offices. Keep a phone reachable, including unfamiliar incoming numbers, and visit a physical office only if directed or unable to use phone access.

resources.name: AHCCCS — school behavioral-health access
resources.description: School-linked referrals and information about behavioral-health coverage.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
School-linked referrals and information about behavioral-health coverage.

**Eligibility Requirements**
A parent or guardian normally consents to referral. An IEP is not required.

**Population Served**
Arizona students and families, including uninsured or underinsured students.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the school nurse or principal. Medicaid members can call their plan; others may ask the regional behavioral-health plan. Questions: bhinschools@azahcccs.gov.

**Important Information to Know**
On-campus services and grant-funded eligibility vary; a referral does not guarantee a funded appointment.

resources.name: Laborers Training School Arizona Apprenticeship
resources.description: The Laborers Training School at the Jon P. Preciado Training Center provides construction laborer apprenticeship and training in Phoenix, with an online application that places applicants on a waiting list for an Apprenticeship Entry Assessment.
resources.address: 1202 N. 57th Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85043
resources.hours: Office hours: Monday-Friday 6:00 AM-3:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Construction laborer apprenticeship and training, including on-the-job training with competitive pay and more than 50 construction-related classes for apprentices and journeyworkers. Applicants can apply online and be placed on the waiting list for an Apprenticeship Entry Assessment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The site states the school has an open application process for men and women age 18 or older interested in working in the construction trade. Placement depends on waiting-list movement, assessment, employer demand, and apprenticeship requirements.

**Population Served**
Arizona job seekers pursuing construction laborer apprenticeship or training, including Mesa/Maricopa County applicants who can travel to the Phoenix training center or assigned job sites.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online from arizonalts.com, then wait to be contacted for the Apprenticeship Entry Assessment. Call the office at 602-314-5072 for questions. Training center: 1202 N. 57th Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85043.

**Important Information to Know**
Application does not guarantee immediate entry or job dispatch. Confirm current cohort timing, assessment steps, union or employer requirements, transportation, tools, and whether any BuildItAZ-funded supports are available to the applicant.

resources.name: Arizona State Schools for the Deaf and the Blind - Early Learning Program
resources.description: Arizona State Schools for the Deaf and the Blind Early Learning Program provides early learning and early-intervention expertise for young children who are Deaf, hard of hearing, blind, visually impaired or DeafBlind.
resources.address: Phoenix regional contact for Maricopa County services; ASDB main administration is outside Mesa
resources.hours: Referral and service schedules depend on AzEIP, ASDB Early Learning Program and preschool or school-district assignment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
ASDB Early Learning Program supports young children with hearing or vision disabilities through early-intervention coordination, family coaching, sensory-disability specialists, ASL or listening-and-spoken-language support, orientation and mobility, and preschool/early learning pathways.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Birth-to-three children generally enter through AzEIP. Children with hearing or vision concerns who are already in AzEIP may be referred to ASDB Early Learning; preschool services have separate eligibility and school-district/designated-representative rules.

**Population Served**
Arizona children from birth to age five who are Deaf, hard of hearing, blind, visually impaired or DeafBlind, including Mesa and Maricopa County children.

**How to Best Connect**
For children under 3, start with AzEIP referral. For ASDB Early Learning referral questions, email elp.referral-info@asdb.az.gov or call the Phoenix regional contact at 602-771-5204.

**Important Information to Know**
ASDB is a specialty sensory-disability pathway, not the only early-intervention entry point. Services depend on evaluated sensory needs, IFSP or preschool eligibility, and local assignment.

resources.name: A New Leaf - La Mesita Family Homeless Shelter Lead
resources.description: La Mesita is named by Family Housing Hub as an A New Leaf participating family shelter, but current public A New Leaf pages primarily describe La Mesita Apartments rather than a direct family homeless-shelter page. Family shelter access should be handled through Family Housing Hub while administrators confirm the current La Mesita shelter identity and referral details.
resources.hours: No direct public shelter intake hours confirmed; use Family Housing Hub or 2-1-1 for family shelter screening.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Potential family shelter or family homeless-services placement connected to A New Leaf and the Family Housing Hub system. Family Housing Hub lists A New Leaf: La Mesita among participating shelters.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Likely for families with children who complete Family Housing Hub screening and are matched when a shelter opening fits the household. Direct public eligibility and walk-up rules for La Mesita itself were not confirmed.

**Population Served**
Families with children experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County, including Mesa/East Valley families if matched through coordinated entry.

**How to Best Connect**
Do not send a family directly to the reported La Mesita address. Call 2-1-1, visit 211arizona.org, dial 877-211-8661 or call Family Housing Hub/UMOM at 602-595-8700 for coordinated family shelter screening.

**Important Information to Know**
There is a consequential public-source conflict: Family Housing Hub names A New Leaf: La Mesita as a participating shelter, while current A New Leaf housing pages emphasize La Mesita Apartments as long-term affordable housing. This needs administrator confirmation before listing as a direct shelter.
resources.resolutionReason: Family Housing Hub lists La Mesita shelter but current provider material describes long-term apartments; reconcile the shelter identity and placement route before routine referral.

resources.name: GoTEN - Refugee English classes, citizenship coaching, sewing ministry and kids support
resources.description: GoTEN is a faith-based nonprofit serving refugee neighbors in Phoenix through free services, English learning, citizenship-related coaching, sewing ministry, kids support, employment readiness and volunteer friendship/community connection.
resources.address: Mail only:PO Box 36343, Phoenix, AZ 85067
resources.hours: Class and program schedules are not fully posted for students; contact GoTEN for current openings.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free services and relationship-based support for refugee neighbors, including English learning, citizenship coaching or preparation, sewing classes, kids programs, employment readiness and friendship/community connection.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page frames services around refugee neighbors in Phoenix. Public student eligibility, registration steps, class openings, childcare and whether services are limited to specific neighborhoods or referral partners are not fully stated.

**Population Served**
Refugee families and refugee neighbors in the Phoenix area, including adults seeking English/citizenship learning or employment readiness and families needing community connection.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-462-7000 or email info@goten.org. Ask how a refugee student or family can register for English, citizenship, sewing, employment services or kids programming and whether Mesa-area refugee households can participate.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a faith-based ministry and not immigration legal representation. It is a useful refugee-integration reserve option, but confirm class location, schedule, openings and transportation before referral.

resources.name: SafeLink Wireless — Lifeline mobile service
resources.description: Offers Lifeline mobile service for eligible households in its service area.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Offers Lifeline mobile service for eligible households in its service area.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Qualify for Lifeline and live at an address where SafeLink offers service. Only one Lifeline benefit is allowed per household.

**Population Served**
Income-eligible households and people qualifying through an eligible public benefit.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the SafeLink website to check the ZIP code and start enrollment, or call the published support number. Confirm device compatibility and service coverage.

**Important Information to Know**
Plan allowances, device availability and offers vary. Do not assume a free new phone or a particular data allotment. Survivors needing to separate a shared phone plan can also ask Lifeline about its separate temporary survivor benefit.

resources.name: A New Leaf Financial Wellness / Operation HOPE - Financial Coaching, Credit Building, and Workshops
resources.description: A New Leaf Financial Wellness offers free online and in-person financial coaching, credit-building education, and workshops across Valley program sites including MesaCAN, with an Operation HOPE partnership.
resources.address: 868 E University Dr, Mesa, AZ 85203
resources.hours: Call or email for current coaching and workshop availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Financial Wellness provides financial coaching, credit-building support, education, and workshops. Coaches help households understand budgets, saving, debt payoff, credit, and financial goals. Operation HOPE partners with A New Leaf to provide free financial coaching services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page describes free resources for households across the Valley; any appointment capacity, workshop schedule, or program-specific enrollment rules should be confirmed when contacting staff.

**Population Served**
Households across the Valley seeking financial stability, including people connected with A New Leaf sites such as MesaCAN, workforce services, shelters, and other community offices.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-636-6813 or email financialcoaching@turnanewleaf.org. For the Operation HOPE partnership, the A New Leaf page lists Ruth McKinney as a contact at 622-229-5385 and Ruth.McKinney@operationhope.org.

**Important Information to Know**
This is coaching, education, and planning support, not emergency bill payment. Ask about current workshop dates, coaching availability, language access, and whether meetings are online or in person.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Corrections, Rehabilitation & Reentry - Women's Services Bureau
resources.description: ADCRR Women's Services Bureau provides gender-responsive programming and care for incarcerated women, including parenting, wellness, career development, workforce and specialty partner programming such as Televerde Foundation and Arouet Foundation.
resources.address: 701 E Jefferson St, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
ADCRR Women's Services Bureau provides gender-responsive care and programming for incarcerated women. Public information lists parenting and family connection programs, health and wellness supports, career development, CTE/apprenticeships, and specialty programs offered with Televerde Foundation and Arouet Foundation.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are for incarcerated women in ADCRR custody and depend on facility placement, program availability, and ADCRR criteria. Community access after release should be confirmed through ADCRR, Arouet, Televerde, or the assigned reentry contact.

**Population Served**
Women incarcerated in Arizona ADCRR facilities, including women preparing for return to Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call ADCRR at 602-542-5497 or use the Women's Services page as the public entry point. Incarcerated clients should ask facility staff or case management about Women's Services and partner program eligibility.

**Important Information to Know**
This is primarily an institutional/pre-release resource, not a Mesa walk-in program. The public page supports partner programming but does not give a detailed post-release continuity route for every woman; confirm the current handoff before relying on it.

resources.name: A New Leaf - Tenant Based Rental Assistance
resources.description: A New Leaf Tenant Based Rental Assistance provides temporary rental subsidy, utility and security deposits, utility allowance and housing case management for people who are currently homeless, with eligibility set by participating cities and HOME funding rules.
resources.hours: Coordinated entry required; A New Leaf directs all families and single clients to call 2-1-1 for assistance.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Temporary rental subsidy, utility and security deposits, utility allowance, housing case management, connections to local resources, workforce assistance and referrals. Rental subsidy can be provided for up to 24 months when approved.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people who are currently homeless. Eligibility is determined by individual cities and HOME funding requirements. Participants pay $25 per month or 30% of adjusted gross household income toward rent, whichever is higher.

**Population Served**
Currently homeless households in participating Valley jurisdictions, including Mesa when funding and local program rules apply.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 211 for coordinated-entry assistance. For programme questions, email Housing@turnanewleaf.org or call A New Leaf general information at 480-969-4024. Staff meet participants in the community; do not use the administrative office as a walk-in TBRA intake.

**Important Information to Know**
TBRA is not guaranteed and is not a direct walk-in rent fund. Current Mesa funding, local eligibility, referral route, documentation and openings should be confirmed through coordinated entry or A New Leaf.

resources.name: Onward Hope - Healthy Families Arizona
resources.description: Onward Hope Healthy Families Arizona is a free voluntary home-visitation program in Maricopa County for pregnant women and families of newborns, offering parenting support, developmental assessments and links to health care, child care, housing, education and employment resources.
resources.address: 1408 W. Camelback Road, Phoenix, AZ 85013
resources.hours: Onward Hope office hours are listed Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; Saturday-Sunday by appointment only. Home visits are scheduled with enrolled families.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Healthy Families Arizona provides free voluntary home visitation, emotional support, parent-child interaction and discipline guidance, periodic developmental assessments, referrals when delays are identified, and links to community services, health care, child care, housing, education and employment.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The infant must be under three months old at enrollment, or the family must be pregnant or caring for a newborn. Families should have life stressors or risk factors that could affect child outcomes, such as poverty, unemployment, lack of health insurance, lack of prenatal care, low birth weight, single or teen parenthood, special needs, substance abuse, domestic violence or mental health concerns.

**Population Served**
Pregnant women, caregivers and families of newborns in Maricopa County. Onward Hope is one of the listed Healthy Families Arizona providers for Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Onward Hope at 602-441-2723 or email info@onwardhope.org. Families and referring workers can ask for the Healthy Families Arizona program.

**Important Information to Know**
The program is free and voluntary. Services may continue as needed until the child turns five. Enrollment depends on age, risk factors, geography and program capacity.

resources.name: Maricopa County Clerk — Mesa passport application acceptance
resources.description: Provides a Mesa appointment location for submitting an eligible passport application after the required identity and citizenship evidence is assembled.
resources.address: 222 E Javelina, Mesa, AZ 85210
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides a Mesa appointment location for submitting an eligible passport application after the required identity and citizenship evidence is assembled.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must meet US passport eligibility and supply the required forms, proof, photo and fees for their situation.

**Population Served**
Eligible passport applicants who can attend the Southeast Regional Court appointment.

**How to Best Connect**
Book through the Clerk appointment page; passport service is 8:00 AM-4:00 PM Monday-Friday by appointment, at 222 E Javelina in Mesa. Call 602-372-5375 for office questions.

**Important Information to Know**
Appointments are limited and cannot be booked more than 60 days ahead. The Clerk accepts applications but does not issue passports or replace missing supporting evidence.

resources.name: Arizona Commodity Senior Food Program (CSFP / Food Plus)
resources.description: Arizona Commodity Senior Food Program, also called Food Plus, provides a monthly USDA food package at no cost for income-qualified Arizona residents age 60+ through local distribution sites.
resources.hours: Distribution schedules depend on the local CSFP site.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Monthly Commodity Senior Food Program food package at no cost. Packages can include shelf-stable milk, juice, cereal, grains, peanut butter, beans, canned meat or fish, fruits and vegetables and other USDA foods.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Participants must live in Arizona, be at least 60 years old and have household income at or below 130% of the federal poverty level. Photo identification is required, and additional proof of age may be needed if the ID does not show age.

**Population Served**
Low-income Arizona residents age 60+, including Mesa and Maricopa County seniors who can use a local distribution site.

**How to Best Connect**
Find a local CSFP package distribution site through the DES locations table; Maricopa County sites are routed through the AZ Food Help partner network. Applications are usually completed at the distribution site. Homebound applicants should contact the local site for alternate application or delivery options.

**Important Information to Know**
Monthly packages supplement a diet and are not immediate emergency food. Capacity is limited and a waitlist may apply. Confirm the current Mesa-area distribution site and schedule; homebound applicants can ask about alternate application, pickup or possible delivery arrangements.

resources.name: Desert Voices — Hear for Kids
resources.description: Hearing-related assistance including diagnostic testing, hearing aids or repairs, cochlear-implant repairs or programming, medical clearance and loaner hearing aids.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Hearing-related assistance including diagnostic testing, hearing aids or repairs, cochlear-implant repairs or programming, medical clearance and loaner hearing aids.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Published criteria are household income at or below 250% of federal poverty level, birth through age 18 or through 21 if enrolled in school, and no AHCCCS coverage or eligibility. Special circumstances can be discussed. Covered services must be performed in Maricopa County.

**Population Served**

Financially eligible Arizona children and students needing hearing care.

**How to Best Connect**

Contact Desert Voices at 602-224-0598 or hearforkids@desert-voices.org for application and participating-provider instructions before arranging care.

**Important Information to Know**

Confirm approval and the covered service before a visit. Participating providers accept the program’s voucher payment for covered services. This program was previously administered by the EAR Foundation of Arizona.

resources.name: Qwick - Phoenix-area hospitality shift platform
resources.description: Qwick is an app-based hospitality work platform where verified professionals can pick up shifts at restaurants, hotels and venues, including roles such as bartender, line cook, event server, prep cook, dishwasher, host and housekeeping.
resources.hours: App-based access; verification typically takes 2-3 business days after profile, background check and ID verification.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Qwick lets hospitality professionals download an app, complete verification, browse and accept shifts, work shifts and receive same-day direct-deposit pay. Roles include bartender, barback, line cook, prep cook, event chef, server, dishwasher, host, busser, banquet server and housekeeping.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Professionals must download the app, complete a profile, pass a background check and verify ID. Shift availability depends on the market, skills, ratings, location and employer requirements.

**Population Served**
Hospitality workers and job seekers in Arizona markets, including Phoenix-area and Mesa-area workers when app shifts are available nearby.

**How to Best Connect**
Download the Qwick Pro app from the official Qwick professional page, complete verification and browse shifts in the local market.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a gig/flexible-shift platform, not a social-service agency. Mesa-specific shifts were not publicly confirmed; availability, pay, transportation and schedule depend on current app postings.

resources.name: Catholic Charities Community Services - Unaccompanied Refugee Minors Program
resources.description: Arizona DES identifies Catholic Charities as the current coordinator for the Unaccompanied Refugee Minors Program, a federally coordinated foster-care placement and services pathway for refugee children from birth to age 18 who are without a parent or guardian and eligible for U.S. resettlement.
resources.hours: Call Catholic Charities at 602-997-6105 to confirm the correct URM referral route.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The Unaccompanied Refugee Minors Program provides safe and nurturing foster-care placement along with related services and benefits for eligible unaccompanied refugee children. Arizona DES states the program is currently coordinated through Catholic Charities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is for refugee children from birth to age 18 who are without a parent or guardian and are eligible for resettlement in the United States, as identified by the U.S. Department of State and U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. This is not a general walk-in youth immigration service.

**Population Served**
Eligible unaccompanied refugee minors placed in Arizona through federal and state refugee-resettlement systems.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Catholic Charities at 602-997-6105 and ask for the Unaccompanied Refugee Minors Program or the correct referral pathway. Use the DES Refugee Resettlement page to confirm current program contacts before giving the number to a family.

**Important Information to Know**
Eligibility and placement are determined through federal and state systems. This resource is useful for administrators and referral partners handling a qualifying URM case; it should not be described as ordinary immigration legal help or a public foster-care application for any immigrant youth.

resources.name: Arizona Justice Project — actual innocence and manifest-injustice case review
resources.description: Pro bono case-review and representation organization for actual innocence or manifest injustice claims from Arizona convictions or federal convictions stemming from Arizona incidents.
resources.address: 4001 N 3rd Street, Suite 401, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.hours: No walk-ins; written communication and application submission required.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Arizona Justice Project reviews cases involving actual innocence or manifest injustice and may accept qualifying cases pro bono for post-conviction relief, forensic testing, clemency, parole, or related litigation. It uses a pre-screen application, full intake, investigation, and acceptance process.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The person must be serving time on an Arizona conviction or a federal conviction stemming from an Arizona incident, have a claim of actual innocence or manifest injustice, and not currently be represented by an attorney or entitled to an attorney at public expense.

**Population Served**
Indigent or otherwise unrepresented people with Arizona-linked convictions who may have actual innocence or manifest-injustice claims, plus family or friends helping start review.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the pre-screen application and return it by email to info@azjusticeproject.org or by mail to AZ Justice Project, 4001 N 3rd St. #401, Phoenix, AZ 85012. The organization says communications should be in writing and it does not take walk-ins.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not general criminal defense, direct appeal counsel, or civil legal aid. Case review can take months, and accepted litigation can take years. Applying does not mean the case will be accepted.

resources.name: Per Scholas Phoenix · Tuition-Free Technology Training
resources.description: Per Scholas Phoenix provides no-cost, career-focused technology training for eligible Phoenix metro and Maricopa County learners, with certifications, learner support, career coaching, and employer connections.
resources.address: 3838 N. Central Ave., Suite 250, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.hours: Course schedules vary; many courses are full-time Monday-Friday for 12-16 weeks.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost IT and technology training, industry-recognized certifications, hands-on skills, learner support, financial coaching, resume and interview preparation, career coaching, and employer-partner connections. Current Phoenix examples include data center technician, healthcare IT technician, and low-voltage/fiber technician options.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Per Scholas Phoenix says training is open to applicants who meet income requirements, want IT skills, and are residents of the Phoenix metro area. Individual courses may require technical experience, Maricopa County residence, schedule availability, and course-specific prerequisites.

**Population Served**
Phoenix metro and Maricopa County adults seeking entry or advancement in technology careers, including Mesa residents able to meet course format and commute requirements.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Phoenix location page to find current courses and submit the eligibility form. Email phoenix@perscholas.org for general questions or kbegay@perscholas.org for admissions questions; the national phone is 718-991-8400.

**Important Information to Know**
Course seats, deadlines, prerequisites, format and start dates change; admission and a job are not guaranteed. Training is no cost for accepted learners, but many courses require full-time participation and do not generally pay attendance. Any case-by-case assistance or separate personal-expense loan needs its own review and terms.

resources.name: New Life Center - Hope's Closet for Emergency Shelter Residents
resources.description: Hope's Closet is New Life Center's thrift store; New Life Center emergency shelter residents can receive clothing and furnishings from the store at no charge during shelter and when exiting.
resources.address: 415 N Litchfield Rd, Goodyear, AZ 85338
resources.hours: Hope's Closet public store hours listed in prior official evidence: Tuesday-Saturday 9:30 AM-5:00 PM; closed Sunday and Monday. Shelter access is through New Life Center crisis intake.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free clothing and furnishings for adults and children who are New Life Center emergency-shelter residents, plus low-cost public thrift shopping for clothing, furniture and household items.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Free goods are restricted to New Life Center emergency-shelter participants. Public shoppers may buy thrift items, but the official page does not describe a general free-shopping or hardship-voucher program for non-residents.

**Population Served**
Domestic and sexual violence survivors and their children connected to New Life Center shelter services, plus public thrift shoppers who can travel to Goodyear.

**How to Best Connect**
For safety or shelter help, use New Life Center's get-help pathway rather than treating the store as the first point of crisis intake. For store questions, call 623-925-0965 or email manager@newlifectr.org.

**Important Information to Know**
This is far from Mesa and is most useful for Mesa clients if they are already connected to New Life Center shelter or can use the thrift store at public prices. Do not promise free furniture or clothing to the general public.

resources.name: Fix It Foundation - Free Vehicle Maintenance and Basic Repairs
resources.description: Fix It Foundation is a Mesa nonprofit that provides selected people in need with free vehicle maintenance and basic services so they can keep safe, reliable transportation.
resources.address: Mesa, AZ
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Fix It Foundation provides free vehicle maintenance and basic automotive services for selected candidates, helping people keep existing vehicles safe and reliable.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The foundation says it helps first responders, veterans, educators, elderly people and others in need. A referral form is used to nominate someone, and the foundation selects candidates who are the best fit. The referred person must agree to be contacted.

**Population Served**
People in need of automotive service in the Mesa area, including first responders, veterans, educators, seniors and low-income or hardship-affected drivers.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the official Refer form to nominate someone needing essential automotive services. Include the person's city/location, vehicle details, known issues, reason for referral and consent to be contacted.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a walk-in repair shop and not guaranteed emergency repair funding. The website supports free maintenance and basic services, but does not publish a full repair menu, wait time or capacity. Major repairs may be outside scope unless the foundation accepts the case.

resources.name: Valor on Eighth — Veteran-family affordable housing inquiry
resources.description: Provides an affordable-housing community designed around veterans and families, with supportive services through Save the Family.
resources.address: 1001 East 8 th Street, Tempe, AZ 85281
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides an affordable-housing community designed around veterans and families, with supportive services through Save the Family.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Income, household composition, leasing rules and availability determine access. Ask about current application and veteran-family criteria.

**Population Served**
Veterans and families, including women veterans, who can live in Tempe.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Save the Family at 480-898-0228 for the current Valor on Eighth housing and support contact. The property is at 1001 East 8 th Street, not the agency’s Mesa office.

**Important Information to Know**
Save the Family is the support/referral contact; this number is not represented as the leasing desk. Do not assume an opening or that historical SSVF funding and services remain unchanged.

resources.name: AHCCCS · Pre-Release Health Services for Justice-Involved Youth
resources.description: AHCCCS Justice Initiatives include CAA 2023 pre-release Medicaid/CHIP services for eligible justice-involved youth, using health-plan Justice Liaisons to coordinate providers and post-release contact.
resources.address: 150 N 18th Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Medicaid/CHIP pre-release services and care coordination for eligible justice-involved youth, with health-plan Justice Liaisons coordinating providers and post-release contact.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The current pathway is for eligible youth and participating facilities; the submitted evidence says it currently includes eligible youth released from ADJC, with statewide expansion planned. Adult reentry clients are not the target population.

**Population Served**
Eligible justice-involved youth in Arizona secure or correctional settings, including youth who may return to Mesa or Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the AHCCCS Justice Initiatives page or call AHCCCS at 602-417-4000 for routing. Families should also ask the youth's facility, health plan or Justice Liaison about eligibility and pre-release coordination.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a public-system health-care coordination pathway, not a community walk-in program. Service expansion status, participating facilities and youth-specific eligibility should be confirmed.

resources.name: Chicanos Por La Causa - CPLC Healthy Aging / Senior Services
resources.description: Chicanos Por La Causa Healthy Aging provides senior housing-connected advocacy, case management, center meals and home-delivered meals from Casa de Primavera in Phoenix, with culturally responsive Spanish-language access.
resources.address: Casa de Primavera, 1617 N. 45th Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85035
resources.hours: Call CPLC Healthy Aging for current meal, case-management and resident eligibility details.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
CPLC Healthy Aging provides senior advocacy, case management, support services, congregate meals and home-delivered meals. The CPLC page also identifies related home health care contact information.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The home-delivered meal description identifies adults age 60+ who can no longer prepare meals for themselves or leave home to eat congregate meals. Other CPLC Healthy Aging services appear tied to Casa de Primavera senior housing and should be confirmed before referral.

**Population Served**
Older adults connected to the Casa de Primavera senior community in Phoenix and eligible older adults using CPLC senior meal services.

**How to Best Connect**
Call CPLC Healthy Aging at 602-269-6245. The program is located at Casa de Primavera, 1617 N. 45th Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85035.

**Important Information to Know**
Mesa service is not established on the official page. Treat this as a culturally responsive Phoenix reserve option, not a primary Mesa senior-meal referral unless CPLC confirms service fit.

resources.name: Phoenix Police Department - U Visa Certification for Immigrant Crime Victims
resources.description: Phoenix Police Department provides the local law-enforcement certification process for eligible immigrant crime victims seeking U nonimmigrant status when Phoenix Police is the proper certifying agency.
resources.address: Phoenix Police Department, Violent Crimes Bureau (U-visa), 100 W. Washington St., Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.hours: Certification is process-based rather than walk-in social services; use the official page and forms and contact the listed Phoenix Police U-visa/Violent Crimes Bureau route before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Law-enforcement certification for eligible immigrant crime victims pursuing U nonimmigrant status. This is the certification step only, not completion of the full U visa application.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The qualifying crime must be connected to the City of Phoenix/Phoenix Police as the certifying law-enforcement agency. Other jurisdictions require certification from the appropriate agency.

**Population Served**
Immigrant crime victims who need Phoenix Police certification for a U visa-related request.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the official Phoenix Police U visa certification page for instructions and forms. Clients with legal deadlines should also work with an immigration attorney or accredited representative.

**Important Information to Know**
The certification is no-cost government paperwork but does not guarantee U visa approval and does not replace immigration legal advice. Mesa crimes generally need the certifying agency for the jurisdiction where the crime was investigated.

resources.name: Arizona Department of Public Safety - Fingerprint Clearance Card replacement
resources.description: Arizona Department of Public Safety Clearance Card Section accepts online and paper replacement requests when an Arizona fingerprint clearance card is lost, stolen or affected by a name change.
resources.address: 2222 W Encanto Blvd, Phoenix, AZ 85009; mailing address: Arizona DPS Clearance Card Section, PO Box 18390, Phoenix, AZ 85005-8390
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Processes fingerprint clearance card applications, replacement requests and status checks. A replacement card can be requested online through the Public Services Portal or by paper form if the card is lost, stolen or the person's name changes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Relevant only for people who have, had or need an Arizona fingerprint clearance card for a job, license, certification, school or sponsoring agency requirement. DPS cannot pre-screen eligibility before receiving and reviewing required records.

**Population Served**
Arizona fingerprint-clearance-card holders or applicants, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents whose work or licensing requires the card.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the DPS Public Services Portal for card applications, replacement requests and status checks. Call the Clearance Card Section at 602-223-2279 for program questions. Technical PSP support is 602-223-2999 option 8.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general state ID card. A paper replacement request must include the listed $5 fee by approved payment type. DPS does not provide public fingerprinting for this purpose; applicants must use approved fingerprinting options.

resources.name: Terros Health - University Health Center
resources.description: Mesa Terros Health community health center offering substance-use treatment, individual and group counseling, psychiatry, medication services, care coordination, social-services enrollment, peer-support training/certification, supported education, and employment supports.
resources.address: 262 E University Dr, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Clinic and telehealth Monday-Friday 8am-5pm; weekends closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
University Health Center provides substance-use treatment, individual counseling, group counseling, psychiatry, medication services, care coordination, social-services enrollment, supported education/GED, culinary skills, basic computer skills, peer-support training and certification, employment support, and telehealth.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Terros states community health centers provide care regardless of ability to pay. Clients should call for appointment, clinical screening, and insurance/payment review.

**Population Served**
Mesa/East Valley clients needing substance-use, behavioral-health, psychiatric, recovery-support, education, and employment-related supports.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-685-6000 for new and existing patients. The center is at 262 E University Dr, Mesa, AZ 85201.

**Important Information to Know**
University Health Center may be especially useful when a client needs recovery support plus skills, education, or employment services. Confirm current group schedules, peer-support training availability, and payer requirements before referral.

resources.name: Crime Victim Compensation — Maricopa County claims
resources.description: Arizona's Crime Victim Compensation Program may help eligible crime victims and claimants with financial losses directly resulting from victimization. ACJC administers the program statewide, while claims are processed at the county level; Maricopa County handles Maricopa County claims.
resources.address: Statewide program; Maricopa County Victim Compensation Bureau, 225 W Madison St, Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.hours: Call the county compensation program for current application and board-review timing.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Possible payment of qualifying crime-related medical/mental-health costs, funeral expenses, crime-scene cleanup and wage loss, through county claim review under Arizona rules. Online and paper application routes include English and Spanish.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For eligible crime victims/claimants with covered losses. Use the county where the crime occurred. An offender need not be arrested or convicted; reporting, cooperation, filing and loss rules still apply. Supply the application, police reports and bills/invoices. Other available recovery sources must be used first.

**Population Served**
Arizona crime victims and claimants, including Mesa and Maricopa County victims with qualifying losses from crimes that occurred in Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through the ACJC victim compensation application or call the Crime Victim Compensation Program for the county where the crime occurred. For Maricopa County, call the Victim Compensation Bureau at 602-506-4955 or mail to 225 W Madison St, Phoenix, AZ 85003.

**Important Information to Know**
Awards depend on county coordination, independent-board review, programme rules and funding; this is not immediate cash. The county excludes property damage/loss, pain and suffering, collisions deemed accidents, relocation, rent, mortgage and utility expenses. Ask the coordinator about deadlines and the specific expense.

resources.name: Phoenix Prosecutor — Crime Victim Services
resources.description: Victim information and support for misdemeanor cases handled by the Phoenix Prosecutor, including criminal-process and victim-rights guidance.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Victim information and support for misdemeanor cases handled by the Phoenix Prosecutor, including criminal-process and victim-rights guidance.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Most useful for a Phoenix municipal criminal case. County felony cases use the Maricopa County Attorney’s victim-services route.

**Population Served**

Victims of Phoenix misdemeanor crimes, including domestic-violence survivors.

**How to Best Connect**

Call602-261-8192 and explain the case connection. Ask about the assigned advocate, current process and appropriate support. Confirm any office visit first.

**Important Information to Know**

This is prosecution-connected assistance, not private legal representation or confidential community counseling. It is separate from Phoenix Family Advocacy Center and the county felony service.

resources.name: Aster Aging — Neighbors volunteer support
resources.description: Aster Aging's Neighbors Program provides volunteer-supported essential transportation to doctors, pharmacies and grocery stores for seniors in Mesa, Chandler and Gilbert, along with companionship and other independence supports.
resources.hours: Arrange rides/visits through the coordinator; volunteer capacity varies.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Volunteers help with essential trips to medical appointments, pharmacies and grocery stores, as well as companionship, telephone support, supplemental pet food and assistance with visual tasks at home.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For older adults in the program’s Mesa, Chandler and Gilbert service area. Enrollment, the requested task and volunteer availability determine what can be arranged.

**Population Served**
Older adults who need support to remain independent at home, including people with low vision or blindness who need help with visual tasks.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Neighbors coordinator at 480-629-5502, email awurth@asteraz.org, or use the interest form on Aster’s Neighbors page. Describe the home address, trip or task, appointment time and mobility needs.

**Important Information to Know**
Arrange help in advance and confirm ZIP coverage, waiting time, ride frequency, accessibility and companion needs. This is not emergency transport, medical treatment, personal attendant care or guaranteed recurring service. Aster Home Care is a separate programme.

resources.name: City of Mesa Office of Homeless Solutions - Mesa Homeless Resource Line
resources.description: Mesa Homeless Resource Line is the City of Mesa's non-emergency access line for people experiencing homelessness and community members seeking routing to homeless outreach, shelter, housing and partner resources.
resources.hours: City materials describe a non-emergency route; not a 24/7 emergency shelter intake.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
City access line for homeless-response routing, resource navigation, shelter connection, housing assistance information, and questions about helping or referring someone experiencing homelessness in Mesa.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For people experiencing homelessness or housing insecurity in Mesa, or people helping someone unsheltered in Mesa. The line does not guarantee immediate shelter, transportation, outreach dispatch, or program acceptance.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness or housing insecurity in Mesa and Mesa community members or helpers seeking non-emergency homeless-services guidance.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-644-HOPE (4673) or email hope@mesaaz.gov. Leave clear contact information, the person's location, household details, safety concerns, and the type of help needed.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an access and routing line, not a shelter bed. If someone is in immediate danger, call 911. For behavioral-health crisis, use a crisis line or 988.

resources.name: Salt River Project (SRP) - Residential Electric Assistance Programs
resources.description: SRP assistance pathways for residential electric customers include payment plans or extensions, the Income-Qualified Discount, Project SHARE referral, Safety Net third-party alerts, Medical Preparedness outage notification, Home Energy Assessment, and weatherization support through local agencies.
resources.hours: SRP customer service is available 24/7; resource counselors for some programs are listed Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
SRP offers several distinct support pathways for residential electric customers: payment plans or bill extensions, a $10 or $35 monthly Income-Qualified Discount for eligible households, Customer Resource Counselor referrals to community assistance, Project SHARE bill assistance through Salvation Army referral, Safety Net alerts to a chosen third party when a bill is past due, Medical Preparedness planned-outage notification for approved life-support equipment, free Home Energy Assessment products and advice, and weatherization funding routed through local agencies.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Most options require an SRP account or SRP service address. The Income-Qualified Discount requires the SRP account to be in the customer's name, the customer to live at the permanent residence where the discount is received, household income at or below SRP's current federal poverty guideline thresholds, and annual reapplication. Medical Preparedness requires approved electric-dependent FDA Class III medical equipment at home, a billed residential price plan, and physician verification. Weatherization uses income guidelines and local agency screening. Project SHARE and community bill assistance depend on agency rules and funding.

**Population Served**
SRP residential electric customers in Mesa and the SRP service territory, especially income-qualified households, customers with past-due bills, and households with medically necessary electric equipment.

**How to Best Connect**
For urgent bill trouble, call SRP at 602-236-8888 as soon as possible; customer service is listed as available 24/7. For the Income-Qualified Discount, apply online, call 602-236-8888, or download and return the application. For Medical Preparedness enrollment, call 602-236-3000 Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM or call 602-236-8888 after hours for an application. For Project SHARE, call SRP Customer Resource Counselors at 602-236-3000. For weatherization, Mesa residents are routed to Mesa Community Action Network at 480-833-9200, and Maricopa County outside Phoenix/Mesa is routed to 480-808-0429.

**Important Information to Know**
SRP assistance options are separate and have different rules. Medical Preparedness is an outage preparation and notification program, not a guarantee of uninterrupted power or payment protection. Safety Net alerts a third party but does not make that person responsible for payment. Weatherization and Project SHARE depend on local agencies and available funds. Confirm that the service address is in SRP territory before referral.

resources.name: Child & Family Support Services
resources.description: Community-based child and family counseling, psychiatric services, behavioral support and skills training.
resources.address: 10439 S 51 st St, Suite 100, Phoenix, AZ 85044
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Community-based child and family counseling, psychiatric services, behavioral support and skills training.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Intake determines program, age and payer fit.

**Population Served**
Children, youth, young adults and their families.

**How to Best Connect**
Use Seeking Services on the provider’s services page to request intake and ask about Mesa-area delivery.

**Important Information to Know**
Services are arranged in homes and communities; the administrative address is not a walk-in crisis site.

resources.name: Arizona Optometric Association - VISION USA / Community Outreach
resources.description: Arizona Optometric Association VISION USA / Community Outreach uses community screeners and volunteer optometrists to provide complete eye exams and low-cost glasses for eligible Arizonans without insurance who cannot afford an eye doctor.
resources.address: 8350 E. Raintree Dr., Suite 240, Scottsdale, AZ 85260
resources.hours: Public page does not list patient service hours; call or use a referring agency before applying.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Volunteer optometrists donate complete eye examinations. Glasses may be available when needed at a low cost, listed on the official page as $20, through support from labs and frame manufacturers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
People needing an eye exam who do not have insurance and cannot afford an eye doctor should work with a social worker, case worker, charitable organization, agency, school nurse, Salvation Army, Lions Club or similar screener to submit an application on their behalf.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents with vision care cost barriers, including Mesa residents, when a referring screener and volunteer optometrist are available.

**How to Best Connect**
Do not send a client as a simple walk-in. Contact AZOA at 602-279-0055 or azoa@azoa.org, or ask the client's social worker, agency, school nurse, Lions Club or similar screener to pursue a VISION USA referral.

**Important Information to Know**
The page gives an AZOA contact and referral instructions but not a public patient self-referral form. Confirm current program operation and referral partners before promising an appointment.

resources.name: Arizona Corporation Commission - Utilities Consumer Services
resources.description: Arizona Corporation Commission Utilities Consumer Services investigates disputes involving regulated utilities after the customer first contacts the utility, including rates, deposits, disconnections, service refusal and utility policies.
resources.address: 1200 W. Washington St., Phoenix, AZ 85007
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Consumer Services staff can investigate disputes about regulated utilities, including rates, installations, disconnections, bill responsibility, deposits, refusal of service, utility service quality, and utility policies and procedures.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The complaint must involve a utility regulated by the Arizona Corporation Commission, and the customer should first try to resolve the issue directly with the utility. The Commission cannot file the complaint on behalf of the accountholder.

**Population Served**
Arizona customers of regulated private or investor-owned utilities, including eligible Maricopa County accounts.

**How to Best Connect**
Submit the online informal complaint form, or contact the Utilities Division by phone at 602-542-4251, in-state toll-free at 800-222-7000, email UtilitiesDiv@azcc.gov, mail, or in person at 1200 W. Washington St., Phoenix.

**Important Information to Know**
The Commission does not regulate SRP or municipal utility rates/service, including City of Mesa utilities. It also does not handle landlord utility billing, bottled propane/oil, cable or satellite TV, or internet-provider complaints. Contact the provider first and check the appropriate complaint authority.

resources.name: Arizona State University Employee Assistance Office Counseling
resources.description: ASU Employee Assistance Office offers free, voluntary and confidential short-term counseling, behavioral-health assessment, consultation and referral for eligible ASU employees and their spouse, dependents or household members, including a Polytechnic campus location in Mesa.
resources.address: Polytechnic campus: 6027 S. Sagewood, Room 101, Mesa, AZ 85212
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free, voluntary and confidential behavioral-health counseling, assessment, brief interventions, organizational consultation and referrals for personal and work-related issues. The brief model generally provides one to five sessions and refers to insurance or community care when ongoing treatment is needed.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Benefits-eligible ASU employees, spouses, dependents and household members may contact the Employee Assistance Office. Parental consent is required for children under age 18.

**Population Served**
ASU faculty and staff and eligible household members, including employees connected to the Polytechnic campus in Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-965-2271 for counseling appointments and non-emergencies. After scheduling, complete the EAO intake forms. Polytechnic location: 6027 S. Sagewood, Room 101, Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
This is short-term employee assistance, not continuing specialty care for the general public. For life-threatening emergency, call 911; ASU's page also directs people to call or text 988 for crisis support.

resources.name: Accord Healthcare Institute - Certified Nursing Assistant/Aide (CNA/LNA)
resources.description: Accord Healthcare Institute is a Phoenix private healthcare training school offering Certified Nursing Assistant training that prepares students for the Arizona Board of Nursing CNA exam and possible LNA application.
resources.address: 4141 N S Herrera Way, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Accord's CNA course teaches the knowledge and skills needed to become a Certified Nursing Assistant, including lecture, safety and infection control, body systems, resident care, skills lab practice, and clinical experience with patients. The school also lists phlebotomy and EKG programs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The CNA page lists admission requirements of being at least 16 years old and passing an entrance exam. It lists 120 clock hours, approximately 6-8 weeks, with advanced placement of 32 hours or more available for those who qualify.

**Population Served**
People who can travel to Phoenix for short-term healthcare career training, including Mesa and Maricopa County job seekers considering CNA/LNA work.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-714-3439 or email tspence@accordhealthcareinstitute.com. Ask about current start dates, total tuition and fees, books, uniforms, clinical schedule, exam fees, payment plans, WIOA/ETPL status, and commute requirements.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a private career school. The official pages checked do not publish total tuition, current seats, clinical placement details, pass rates, or funding approval. Do not promise WIOA funding or employment; verify cost and approval before referral.

resources.name: City of Mesa Transportation Department - Transit Services / Public Transit
resources.description: City of Mesa Transit Services is the official city access point for Mesa public transit information, including bus, express service, BUZZ circulators, light rail, fares, ADA paratransit, RideChoice and ADA Platinum Pass links.
resources.hours: Transit schedules vary by route and program; check Valley Metro schedules before travel.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
City of Mesa Transit Services provides public transportation information through Mesa's agreement with Valley Metro. The page links riders to local bus, express bus, Mesa Downtown BUZZ, Mesa Fiesta BUZZ, light rail, fare options, ADA paratransit eligibility, East Valley Paratransit, East Valley RideChoice and ADA Platinum Pass information.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Public routes are generally open to riders who can use the route and pay any applicable fare. ADA Paratransit, RideChoice and Platinum Pass programs have separate eligibility rules.

**Population Served**
Mesa residents, workers and visitors using regional transit, including riders with disabilities who need accessible transit information.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the City of Mesa Public Transit page as a starting point, email transportation.info@mesaaz.gov, or call City of Mesa Transit Services at 480-644-2160. For trip planning and current schedules, use Valley Metro or call 602-253-5000.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an information and navigation access point, not a guarantee of fare assistance or a ride. Specific programs such as ADA paratransit and RideChoice require eligibility confirmation.

resources.name: Phoenix VA suicide-prevention coordination and Veterans Crisis Line
resources.description: Phoenix VA suicide-prevention coordinators help veterans and concerned supporters connect to crisis response, ongoing counseling, case management, gun-safety resources and behavioral-health follow-up.
resources.phone: Crisis988 then press 1; text 838255; Phoenix VA602-277-5551
resources.address: 650 East Indian School Road, Phoenix, AZ 85012
resources.hours: Suicide-prevention coordinators are available during regular business hours; 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline is available 24/7.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
VA Phoenix suicide-prevention coordinators can help veterans get ongoing support such as counseling and other services. VA Phoenix also provides suicide-prevention care coordinators, suicide-prevention case managers, gun-safety locks and connection to behavioral-health care.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The Phoenix VA page is for veterans in crisis or people concerned about a veteran. VA states a veteran can go directly to the nearest VA medical center in an emergency regardless of discharge status or VA health-care enrollment; routine ongoing services may require VA eligibility or care coordination.

**Population Served**
Veterans served by Phoenix VA Health Care, including veterans in Mesa and the East Valley, and people concerned about a veteran in crisis.

**How to Best Connect**
For crisis support anytime, call 988 then press 1, text 838255 or use VeteransCrisisLine.net chat. For ongoing Phoenix VA suicide-prevention coordination during business hours, email VHASPCAZ-644PHOSuicidePreventionTeam@va.gov or call 602-277-5551 and ask for the team.

**Important Information to Know**
Email and routine coordination are not urgent response. For immediate life-threatening danger, call 911 or go to the nearest emergency department. VA says a veteran can go directly to the nearest VA medical centre in a crisis regardless of discharge status or VA-health enrollment; routine ongoing care has separate eligibility.

resources.name: PeopleReady Phoenix JobStack Flexible Work
resources.description: PeopleReady Phoenix connects workers to temporary and flexible work through its Phoenix branch and JobStack app in industries such as construction, manufacturing, retail, hospitality and events.
resources.address: 2901 West Thomas Road, Suite 2, Phoenix, AZ 85017
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 5:30 AM-6:00 PM; Saturday-Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
