PeopleReady offers temporary and flexible staffing work, branch support and JobStack app access. Job seekers can register, complete onboarding, view available jobs and accept shifts that fit their schedule.

**Eligibility Requirements**
PeopleReady states job seekers complete onboarding and need required identification for Form I-9. No resume is required for onboarding. Work availability, assignment requirements and background or skill requirements vary by job.

**Population Served**
Job seekers in the Phoenix metro area, including Mesa-area clients who can travel to Phoenix or use the JobStack app for local shifts.

**How to Best Connect**
Download JobStack or view jobs from the PeopleReady Phoenix branch page. The Phoenix branch phone is 602-353-9330 and is open weekdays 5:30 AM-6:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
The verified branch is in Phoenix, not Mesa. Mesa shift availability depends on app postings, transportation and job requirements. PeopleReady is a staffing company, not a social-service program.

resources.name: Maricopa County Sheriff's Office - MOSAIC Program
resources.description: MOSAIC is a Maricopa County Sheriff's Office in-custody substance-use program for qualified people in MCSO custody. County materials describe it as an intensive seven-week program focused on trauma, substance-use coping skills, possible early release and skill-building before return to the community.
resources.hours: Available only to qualified people in MCSO custody; ask jail/program staff about screening and eligibility.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
MOSAIC is an intensive seven-week substance-abuse treatment program in MCSO custody. It teaches participants skills to address past trauma and replace substance use, and county materials say it may offer possible early release and help participants gain skills before returning to life outside custody.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Only for qualified people who are incarcerated in Maricopa County Sheriff's Office custody. Eligibility, capacity and classification requirements are controlled by MCSO/jail program staff.

**Population Served**
People in Maricopa County jail custody with substance-use and reentry needs who meet MCSO program criteria.

**How to Best Connect**
A person in custody should ask MCSO jail programs, classification or jail health/reentry staff about MOSAIC eligibility. Families can review county jail resources and use approved jail communication channels; the county main line is 602-506-3011.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a community treatment referral and cannot be accessed after release as a walk-in service. Use it as a custody-based option to ask about when a client is currently in the Maricopa County jail system.

resources.name: Worthy of Wheels - Transportation Assistance / Vehicle Repair Application
resources.description: Worthy of Wheels reviews online applications from Arizona residents for transportation assistance that may include vehicle repair, replacement or other transportation solutions when the applicant's owned and insured vehicle is needed for essential activities and funding is available.
resources.hours: Apply online; review timing depends on the request and available resources.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Worthy of Wheels provides application-based transportation assistance. Approved assistance may include vehicle repair, replacement or other transportation solutions, and approved repair assistance is paid directly to repair providers when applicable rather than given as cash.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must currently reside in Arizona, own and insure the vehicle, have a valid driver's license, need the vehicle for work, school, medical care or essential family needs, and be experiencing financial hardship that prevents them from completing the repair independently. Required documents include proof of income, vehicle registration or ownership, current insurance, driver's license photos and vehicle photos; a repair estimate is helpful if available.

**Population Served**
Arizona individuals and families with transportation barriers, including Mesa-area residents who meet the vehicle, documentation and hardship criteria.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the online Assistance Application at https://www.worthyofwheels.com/application and gather the income, ownership, insurance, license and vehicle-photo documents before starting. A repair diagnosis or estimate is helpful but not required. Send questions through the contact form or to info@worthyofwheels.com.

**Important Information to Know**
Assistance is not guaranteed and depends on available resources, need, urgency, safety, impact and program guidelines. Incomplete or missing documentation can delay or deny review, and Worthy of Wheels decides the type and extent of assistance offered.

resources.name: AZCEND - Showers and Laundry
resources.description: AZCEND provides free on-site showers and laundry in Chandler, including towels, shampoo, soap, detergent and fabric softener. Laundry is limited to one load per person per day.
resources.address: 345 S California St, Chandler, AZ 85225
resources.hours: Showers: Sunday-Friday 9:15 AM-11:45 AM last call. Laundry: Sunday-Friday 9:30 AM-4:30 PM last call.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free hot showers and free on-site laundry. AZCEND provides towels, shampoo, soap, detergent and fabric softener; laundry is limited to one load per person per day.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page describes first-come, first-served access and does not list income, residency or document requirements for showers/laundry. No bags are allowed for showers.

**Population Served**
People who can reach the Chandler AZCEND site and need hygiene or clean-clothing access, including people experiencing homelessness or housing instability.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to 345 S California St, Chandler during posted service hours or call 480-963-1423 to confirm current access before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
This does not advertise a clothing closet. It is still useful when the practical clothing need is clean clothing, laundry supplies or shower access. Services are first come, first served and may fill.

resources.name: Maricopa County Law Library Resource Center - Southeast Justice Center
resources.description: The Maricopa County Law Library Resource Center provides court forms, procedural information, research help, resource guides, workshops, webinars, brief form review, legal-service provider lists, and online resources for self-represented litigants, including at the Southeast Justice Center in Mesa.
resources.address: Southeast Justice Center, 222 E. Javelina Ave., Mesa, AZ 85210; East Court Building, 101 W. Jefferson St., Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; confirm any clinic or appointment schedule before travel.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Court forms, procedural information, legal research guidance, resource guides, workshops/webinars, brief in-person/remote form-completeness review and legal-service referrals. Subjects include civil, family, probate, juvenile, criminal-record and protective-order processes, including name changes and birth-certificate or marriage-license corrections.

**Eligibility Requirements**
People must use the correct forms and procedures for their court and case type. LLRC staff may provide legal information and form assistance, but they cannot provide individualized legal advice or attorney representation.

**Population Served**
Self-represented Maricopa County court users, including Mesa residents using the Southeast Justice Center or remote LLRC resources.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-506-7353 or email services@jbazmc.maricopa.gov. Visit the Southeast Justice Center at 222 E. Javelina Ave. in Mesa or use the LLRC online resources. Confirm clinic schedules and appointment availability before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
This is court self-help, not attorney representation. Use current forms and correct case/court rules. Printing, copying, filing and certified copies may carry fees; fee waiver/deferral forms are available. A court order does not automatically update records: certified copies may then need submission to Vital Records, SSA, MVD or other agencies.

resources.name: Angel Flight West - Free Medical Flights and Earth Angels Ground Transportation
resources.description: Angel Flight West arranges free volunteer-pilot flights for medically stable people who need long-distance non-emergency medical transportation and have financial need or another compelling reason they cannot use commercial transportation.
resources.address: 3163 Donald Douglas Loop South, Santa Monica, CA 90405
resources.hours: Requests generally need at least 5 business days' advance notice; shorter requests may sometimes be considered.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Angel Flight West arranges free non-emergency flights with volunteer pilots, usually to help a patient reach medical treatment. Passengers may request companions, repeat trips, and help connecting to ground transportation providers when needed.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The passenger must have financial need or another compelling reason they cannot travel commercially, have a firm appointment before pilots are sought, obtain a physician medical release, be medically stable, be able to sit upright in a small aircraft without in-flight medical care, and fit the service territory and aircraft limits.

**Population Served**
People in need who require long-distance non-emergency medical transportation, including Arizona patients whose trip can be served by Angel Flight West or referred to an appropriate partner.

**How to Best Connect**
Submit the flight request online or call 310-390-2958. Existing passengers can request repeat flights at 888-4-AN-ANGEL. Have appointment timing, home ZIP code, destination city, companion needs, and medical-release information ready.

**Important Information to Know**
Flights depend on volunteer pilots, weather, aircraft capacity, medical release, and trip fit. It is not an air ambulance; passengers needing medical care during flight or who cannot sit upright should ask about charitable air ambulance options.

resources.name: National Kidney Foundation of Arizona — Car Payment, Repair and Fuel Assistance
resources.description: National Kidney Foundation of Arizona offers one-time car payment or repair assistance up to $500 for eligible kidney patients who use their own car for dialysis and other medical appointments.
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; Friday 8:00 AM-12:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
NKF AZ offers one-time help of up to $500 for either a car payment or a car repair when a kidney patient needs their vehicle for dialysis and medical appointments. A separate fuel programme provides gas cards for a three-month period according to round-trip mileage.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Meet NKF AZ general patient-aid requirements, household income at or below 400% of the federal poverty level, and liquid assets no greater than $2,000. For car payment/repair help, wait at least 12 months after receiving rent or utility assistance. Fuel assistance is unavailable when insurance provides non-emergency medical transportation.

**Population Served**
Arizona kidney patients who rely on their own vehicle for dialysis and medical appointments.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the appropriate car payment/repair or transportation-fuel application linked on the NKF AZ patient-assistance pages. First-time applicants also complete New Applicant Registration. Call 602-840-1644 for questions.

**Important Information to Know**
Car aid does not cover insurance, emissions testing, registration or reimbursement for repairs already completed; car-payment applicants must explain how future payments will be sustained. Three-month fuel tiers are $120 for round trips of 15 miles or less, $240 for more than 15 but less than 100 miles, and $480 for 100 miles or more, potentially limited to $160 per month. Report mileage accurately and confirm the applicable tier and disbursement rules.

resources.name: Refugees and Immigrants Community for Empowerment - Citizenship, ESL, GED, Employment Readiness and Navigation
resources.description: Refugees and Immigrants Community for Empowerment provides citizenship support, ESL, GED, employment readiness, elderly empowerment, and community navigation for refugee and immigrant communities in Phoenix and Maricopa County.
resources.address: 1717 W. Northern Ave., Suite 212, Phoenix, AZ 85021
resources.hours: Citizenship support page lists Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-4:00 PM; call to confirm current class and appointment availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Citizenship application guidance, document help, citizenship classes, mock interviews, workshops, ESL, GED support, employment readiness, elderly empowerment, and community navigation for refugee and immigrant households.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Services are directed to refugees, immigrants, and asylum seekers. Citizenship assistance is for people pursuing naturalization; exact class openings, language levels, and documentation requirements should be confirmed with RICE.

**Population Served**
Refugee and immigrant community members in Phoenix and Maricopa County, including adults and families who need citizenship-prep, English, education, employment, or navigation support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-666-0857 or email rice@riceaz.org. The office is at 1717 W. Northern Ave., Suite 212, Phoenix; confirm appointments or class enrollment before traveling.

**Important Information to Know**
RICE is strongest as a community education, citizenship-prep, and navigation resource. Direct immigration legal representation or DOJ-accredited legal scope was not confirmed in the public materials used here.

resources.name: Grace United Methodist Church — Adult Learning Center
resources.description: Adult learning classes hosted in Mesa, including English learning described in the program’s literacy-directory listing. The church currently lists adult learning events.
resources.address: 2024 E. University Dr., Building 300, Mesa, AZ 85213
resources.hours: Church office: Monday–Thursday, 9 AM–noon. Class schedule differs; confirm with the Adult Learning Center.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Adult learning classes hosted in Mesa, including English learning described in the program’s literacy-directory listing. The church currently lists adult learning events.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Ask the Adult Learning Center about the appropriate level, current registration, fees, materials and any attendance requirements.

**Population Served**

Adults seeking community-based English learning in Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**

Contact the church office and ask for the Adult Learning Center. Classes are held in Building 300; confirm the class date and room before attending.

**Important Information to Know**

Older listings also describe GED, citizenship and computer classes, but their present availability and fees need confirmation. Do not assume every older course is currently offered.

resources.name: Maricopa County Recorder's Office - Military Discharge Recordation and Certified DD-214 Copies
resources.description: Maricopa County Recorder's Office can record military discharge documents at no recording fee and process requests for copies of recorded DD-214 military discharge records, including certified copies when appropriate.
resources.address: 301 W Jefferson St., Second Floor, Suite 200, Phoenix, AZ 85003
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Records military discharge documents without a recording fee and supplies copies of DD-214s already recorded with the County. Certified copies and related record searches are free when requested for a qualifying federal benefit claim under A.R.S. 39-122.

**Eligibility Requirements**
This helps when a DD-214 has been recorded with the Maricopa County Recorder or when a veteran wants to record an original or certified military discharge document. Request forms and privacy restrictions apply; if the applicant is not the claimant, additional documentation may be required.

**Population Served**
Veterans and authorized requesters with DD-214/military discharge records connected to Maricopa County recording services.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-506-3535 Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM or visit the Recorder's main downtown office at 301 W Jefferson St., Second Floor, Suite 200, Phoenix. Use the public records/request forms page for the Military Discharge DD-214 form.

**Important Information to Know**
Explain the federal pension, allowance, compensation, insurance or other benefit purpose when requesting the free search or certified copy. Ordinary copies for other purposes may carry the listed $1-per-page and $3 certification fees. Privacy and authorized-requester rules still apply. Use the National Archives or VA route for a military record that was never recorded here.

resources.name: AZCEND - Senior Nutrition Program
resources.description: AZCEND provides East Valley senior nutrition through congregate meals at Chandler and Gilbert senior centers, home-delivered meal routing through the Senior Helpline, wellness checks and activities.
resources.address: Chandler Senior Center, 202 E. Boston St., Chandler, AZ 85225; Gilbert Senior Center, 130 N. Oak St., Gilbert, AZ 85233
resources.hours: Chandler and Gilbert on-site meals are served Monday-Friday; Gilbert lunch listed 11:30 AM-12:30 PM. Call each site for reservations and current schedule.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
AZCEND senior services include on-site meals, home-delivered meals, wellness checks and senior-center activities such as exercise, bingo, outings and health screenings.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The centers suggest a $4.50 meal contribution for people 60 and older or people under 60 with disabilities; other diners pay $6.00. Funded home-delivered meals require separate screening. Complete the annual participant form and arrange reservations with the chosen center.

**Population Served**
Older adults and adults with disabilities using Chandler and Gilbert senior-center meal programs, plus eligible homebound older or disabled adults through the home-delivered meal pathway.

**How to Best Connect**
For Chandler meals, call 480-782-2721. For Gilbert meals, call 480-503-6061. For program-funded home-delivered meal screening, call the Senior Helpline at 602-264-4357; for private-pay meal information, call 480-503-6058.

**Important Information to Know**
Mesa service is not explicit for congregate meals; this is best treated as an East Valley reserve option near Mesa. Annual participant forms and reservations may be required.

resources.name: PDS Foundation Dentists for Special Needs - Special Needs Dentistry Clinic
resources.description: PDS Foundation Dentists for Special Needs is a sensory-integrated Phoenix dental office for patients with special needs, offering comprehensive dental care, emergency dentistry, sedation options and Spanish-language access.
resources.address: 4550 E. Bell Rd., Building 1, Suite 106, Phoenix, AZ 85032
resources.hours: Monday 8:00 AM-3:00 PM; Tuesday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; Wednesday 7:00 AM-2:00 PM; Thursday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; Friday 7:00 AM-2:00 PM; Saturday-Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Special-needs dentistry, routine exams, preventive and restorative dental care, emergency dentistry, crowns, dentures and other dental services. The clinic uses sensory supports such as a sensory room, weighted blankets and adapted operatories, and offers nitrous oxide, oral conscious sedation and general anesthesia for children only.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The clinic focuses on people with special needs and dental access barriers. It accepts many major dental insurance plans and offers financing/payment-plan options; uninsured affordability should be confirmed before scheduling.

**Population Served**
People of all ages with intellectual or developmental disabilities, mobility limitations, autism, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, extreme dental anxiety and related needs who can travel to north Phoenix.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-344-9530 or use the online appointment request. The office is at 4550 E. Bell Rd., Building 1, Suite 106, Phoenix, AZ 85032.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a specialized dental office, not a free clinic. General anesthesia is described for children only, and costs/insurance should be confirmed before referral.

resources.name: Arizona Summer Meals — Seasonal site finder
resources.description: Locates free summer meals for children and teens while school is out.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Locates free summer meals for children and teens while school is out.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Open-site meals are for ages 18 and under without an income application; children normally attend, with different arrangements at designated rural to-go sites.

**Population Served**
Arizona children and teens needing food during summer breaks.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the official Arizona Summer Meals finder or call 602-528-3434. The current page says the 2026 season has ended and expects resumption in late May 2027; verify the next site calendar before travel.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a seasonal reserve option, not an available September meal. Sites appear only during their operating dates. SUN Bucks grocery benefits are a different program.

resources.name: Terros Health - Stapley Health Center
resources.description: Terros Health Stapley Health Center is a Mesa community health center offering integrated primary medical care, psychiatric care, behavioral health, substance-use treatment, MAT, children's services, telehealth, Medicaid/social-services enrollment, care coordination, and Genoa pharmacy access.
resources.address: 1111 S. Stapley Dr., Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: Clinic and telehealth: Monday-Thursday 7:30 a.m.-8:00 p.m.; Friday-Saturday 7:30 a.m.-5:00 p.m.; Sunday closed. Genoa pharmacy: Monday-Friday 8:30 a.m.-5:00 p.m., closed noon-1:00 p.m.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Stapley provides primary/psychiatric medical care, individual/group/couples/family and specialty counselling including EMDR/DBT, substance-use treatment and MAT, medication services, children’s services, Arizona Families FIRST, justice services, care coordination, telehealth, Medicaid/social-service enrollment support and Genoa pharmacy access.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Terros community health centers provide care regardless of ability to pay and offer a discount/sliding fee schedule based on qualifications such as family income, size, and situation. Insurance, AHCCCS/Medicaid, Medicare, and self-pay options should be confirmed with intake.

**Population Served**
Mesa children, adults, families, uninsured or underinsured patients, people needing integrated medical and behavioral health care, and justice-involved clients needing supported whole-health care.

**How to Best Connect**
New patients call 602-685-6000; existing patients call 602-302-7900. The centre is 1111 S. Stapley Dr., Mesa. Online appointment requests and walk-in access are described, but call about the exact clinician, service, documentation and timing.

**Important Information to Know**
Dental/routine vision are not core onsite services; ask staff about referrals. Services, clinical fit, fees/insurance, appointment capacity and in-person/telehealth options vary. Use 988 or the crisis line for immediate mental-health crisis rather than wait for routine intake.

resources.name: The Mesa House Inc. - Safe, clean re-entry program for men
resources.description: The Mesa House is a nonprofit Mesa reentry and sober living program for men, including veterans and civilians, providing safe, clean housing and 12-step-based structure.
resources.address: 28 S Olive, Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; Saturday 9:00 AM-12:00 PM; Sunday closed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Men’s sober/transitional and reentry housing with 12-step structure, community-service expectations and resident supports including food/clothing, employment/service referrals and work-related bus passes when available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For men, including veterans/civilians and accepted probation/parole participants, who meet programme admission rules. Ask about sobriety/testing, work readiness, any 90-day commitment, medication policy, supervision/offense restrictions, documents, fees and beds. Transportation support is tied to residency/admission, not public access.

**Population Served**
Men in Mesa, including veterans and civilians, who need sober reentry housing.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-844-2968 or email TheMesaHouse@gmail.com. The listed address is 28 S Olive, Mesa, AZ 85204.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not emergency shelter or a public bus-pass programme. Confirm admission and current availability before travel; do not assume every criminal history, clinical need or medication is accepted. Recovery housing is not detox or clinical treatment.

resources.name: Immigration Equality — LGBTQ and HIV-related immigration legal help
resources.description: Provides specialized free immigration legal help for LGBTQ and HIV-positive asylum seekers, including detention support.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Provides specialized free immigration legal help for LGBTQ and HIV-positive asylum seekers, including detention support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Population, case type and capacity govern acceptance; an inquiry does not guarantee representation.

**Population Served**
LGBTQ or HIV-positive immigrants and asylum seekers.

**How to Best Connect**
Use Legal Help on the organization’s website. People in detention may call 917-654-9696 during its posted hotline hours.

**Important Information to Know**
The detention line does not accept calls from people outside detention. This is a national pathway, not a Phoenix walk-in office.

resources.name: Banner Behavioral Health Hospital - Inpatient and outpatient behavioral health
resources.description: Regional Banner Health psychiatric hospital in Scottsdale offering inpatient behavioral-health care and outpatient/step-down services for adults and adolescents, including assessments, medication, DBT, detoxification and other psychiatric supports.
resources.address: 7575 E Earll Dr, Scottsdale, AZ 85251
resources.hours: Assessment/intake and inpatient care may be available around the clock; call before travel. Outpatient program hours vary by service.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Inpatient psychiatric stabilization and outpatient behavioral-health programs for adults and adolescents, including assessment, individual/family/group therapy, DBT, medication management, chemical-dependency treatment, detoxification, IOP and ECT when clinically appropriate.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Clinical assessment determines the safest level of care. Inpatient services are for people whose symptoms or safety needs require hospital care; outpatient services require fit with program and payer rules.

**Population Served**
Adults and adolescents in Arizona, including Mesa and East Valley residents who can access Scottsdale or another Banner behavioral-health location.

**How to Best Connect**
For inpatient assessment, call the Phoenix Valley Help Line at 480-448-7511 or Banner Behavioral Health Hospital at 480-448-7500. For outpatient assessment, Banner lists 602-254-4357, and the Scottsdale outpatient clinic lists 480-827-5320.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a regional hospital-based option, not a Mesa community counseling walk-in. If there is immediate danger, call 911 or go to the nearest emergency department; for crisis counseling, call or text 988.

resources.name: Catholic Charities Community Services Arizona - Pathways Domestic Violence Counseling and Victim Advocacy
resources.description: Catholic Charities Pathways provides community-based domestic-violence counseling intake and victim advocacy for survivors who may need nonresidential support, mobile advocacy, safety planning and resource connection.
resources.hours: Call for current appointments and location instructions; public walk-in hours were not confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Domestic-violence counseling intake, victim advocacy, mobile advocacy, safety planning, case management, support groups, employment help and housing/resource referrals for survivors outside or after shelter.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For domestic-violence survivors seeking counseling or advocacy support. Eligibility, appointment location and current capacity must be confirmed by phone.

**Population Served**
East Valley and Maricopa County domestic-violence survivors who need nonresidential counseling, advocacy, safety planning or resource connection.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Pathways counselling intake at 602-749-4405, or victim advocacy at 602-819-0082 or 480-267-5761. Ask for the current appointment location and requested service before travelling. Ask about Spanish support groups and current availability.

**Important Information to Know**
This is community counselling/advocacy, separate from the confidential My Sisters’ Place shelter. It does not establish current licensed legal representation or an individual legal-advocate licence. Ask staff about the specific legal/court need and any referral.

resources.name: Mercy Care Developmental Disabilities Health Plan
resources.description: Mercy Care Developmental Disabilities is an AHCCCS/DDD health plan serving Arizona DDD and ALTCS members with physical and behavioral health coverage and limited long-term services and supports.
resources.hours: Member Services: Monday-Friday 7 AM-6 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Managed health-plan coverage for assigned Mercy Care Developmental Disabilities members, including physical health, behavioral health and limited long-term services and supports, plus member services, provider directory help and materials in alternate languages/formats.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Access is for people eligible through Arizona DDD/AHCCCS/ALTCS who choose or are assigned to Mercy Care Developmental Disabilities. People seeking DDD eligibility generally apply through DES DDD, not directly by walking into Mercy Care.

**Population Served**
Arizona members of the Division of Developmental Disabilities and ALTCS who are enrolled in Mercy Care Developmental Disabilities, including Maricopa County members when assigned.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Member Services at 602-263-3000 or 1-800-624-3879, TTY 711. For DDD eligibility help, Mercy Care points applicants to DDD Apply by email and DES DDD Customer Service at 1-844-770-9500.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a health plan, not a general disability service agency. Eligibility, providers, prior authorization and care coordination depend on DDD/AHCCCS enrollment and plan assignment.

resources.name: La Mesa Ministries — Resource Center and housing/document support
resources.description: La Mesa Ministries offers forms, appointments, mail, identity-document and benefit assistance, housing navigation, financial-management classes and conditional move-in/household support, with limited transportation help.
resources.address: 805 N Country Club Dr, Mesa, AZ 85201
resources.hours: Resource Center: Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday 10:00 AM-4:00 PM, appointments suggested. Mesa gathering: Tuesdays, campus opens 4:30 PM, meal 6:00 PM, worship 6:30 PM. Tempe gathering: Thursdays on the same schedule.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Resource-centre forms/appointments, official mail, caseworker housing navigation, help obtaining IDs, driver licenses, birth certificates and Social Security cards, and federal-benefit applications. A four-week financial-management class may lead to qualifying move-in assistance and furniture/household help. Outreach gatherings offer basic supplies and daily bus passes when available; staff/volunteers may help arrange interview or medical-appointment rides.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Resource-centre eligibility is assessed by need, programme fit and staffing. Housing/move-in goods may require completing the financial-management class and qualifying for assistance; not every graduate receives help. Transit passes, rides and supplies depend on availability.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness or poverty in Mesa and Tempe who need meals, basic supplies, document help, resource connection or transportation support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-590-4622 or use the contact/Need Help links. Mesa Resource Center at 805 N. Country Club Drive lists Tuesday–Thursday 10 AM–4 PM, appointments suggested. Financial-management classes start the first Tuesday monthly at 5:30 PM for four weeks. Mesa Tuesday gatherings open 4:30 PM, meal 6 PM, worship 6:30 PM; Tempe Thursday gatherings have a separate location to confirm.

**Important Information to Know**
La Mesa is a faith-based ministry with Christian elements. It is not an ID issuer, staffing agency, public furniture bank or guaranteed ride programme. Confirm document fees, current schedules, classes, appointment location and the requested assistance before relying on it.

resources.name: Disability Rights Arizona — Client Assistance Program for Vocational Rehabilitation
resources.description: Disability Rights Arizona's Client Assistance Program helps people with disabilities understand and enforce rights as Arizona Vocational Rehabilitation applicants or clients, including disputes about eligibility, services, goals, delays, reductions, closures, and appeals.
resources.address: 5025 E. Washington St., Suite 202, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: Temporary DRAZ intake notice: no new intakes September 21-28, 2026; intake reopens Monday, September 28, 2026 at 8:00 AM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
CAP helps Vocational Rehabilitation applicants and clients understand and exercise rights. Help can include information and referral, self-advocacy materials, advocacy assistance to resolve problems with VR staff or providers, and representation in selected meetings or appeals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The person must be a person with a disability with a rights issue involving Vocational Rehabilitation or related Rehabilitation Act-funded services, such as denial of the right to apply, ineligibility, disagreement over employment goals, delayed or denied services, case closure, or ADA employment-protection questions.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents with disabilities who are applying for or receiving Vocational Rehabilitation services, including transition-age students and adults in Mesa and Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-274-6287 or 800-927-2260, or submit an online request for services through DRAZ's Apply for Assistance page. CAP services are free and confidential. The DRAZ intake page had a temporary new-intake closure from September 21 through September 28, 2026.

**Important Information to Know**
CAP is free and confidential, but representation is selective and its scope is VR/related rehabilitation rights. General disability-rights and PABSS services have separate pathways. DRAZ announced a temporary new-intake pause with reopening September 28, 2026 at 8 AM; check current intake before submitting. Existing public self-advocacy information remains available.

resources.name: Aster Aging — senior-center meals and Meals on Wheels
resources.description: Two Mesa senior centers offer meals and activities; home-delivered meal programs add nutrition and wellness checks.
resources.address: Downtown: 247 N. Macdonald, Mesa, AZ 85201; Red Mountain: 7550 E. Adobe St., Mesa, AZ 85207
resources.hours: Senior centers: Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–4 p.m. Meal reservations and delivery schedules are arranged separately.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Two Mesa senior centres offer weekday lunch, cafes, social activities, exercise, arts, education and wellness. Meals on Wheels offers hot weekday or weekly frozen deliveries and wellness checks. Aster also lists CSFP food boxes, SNAP application assistance and outreach/social support; ask intake about the appropriate programme.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Senior-center meals and home-delivery programs have different rules. Center meals for adults 60 and older have a suggested donation; ask about arrangements for other diners. Center membership contributions are optional. The Meals For You delivery track serves City of Mesa residents who are 60 or older or have a documented developmental disability. Other funded delivery tracks require their own assessment.

**Population Served**
Mesa and East Valley older adults, homebound adults, adults with disabilities and senior center participants who need meals, social connection or benefits/outreach support.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Downtown at 480-962-5612 or Red Mountain at 480-218-2221 for center registration and lunch reservations. For meal delivery, call Aster Outreach at 480-962-5612. For Meals For You, call 480-634-1659 or email rcocova@asteraz.org. The administrative office is 45 W. University Drive, SuiteA; it is not either senior-center dining room.

**Important Information to Know**
The center membership contribution of $24 or more is optional, not a required admission charge. Prior reviewed meal guidance lists a $4 suggested senior lunch donation. Aster lists Meals For You at $6.60 per meal, up to five lunches weekly for qualifying participants. Confirm meal reservations, dietary options, delivery boundaries, current costs and capacity.

resources.name: City of Phoenix Human Services Department - Project Assist
resources.description: City of Phoenix Project Assist helps eligible Phoenix City Services customers with water, sewer, and trash bills.
resources.hours: Appointments may be requested by phone starting 7:00 AM Monday; appointments are limited.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Project Assist helps eligible Phoenix customers request assistance with payment of their Phoenix City Services Bill, including water, sewer, and trash services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must reside in Phoenix, have a Phoenix City Services Bill, and be at or below 200% of the federal poverty income level.

**Population Served**
Income-qualified City of Phoenix residents or customers with Phoenix City Services bills. This does not serve Mesa water or trash accounts.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Phoenix Human Services Department at 602-534-2433 to schedule an appointment, or apply online through the City of Phoenix Family Services Centers portal. Phone appointments are limited and callers may begin calling at 7:00 AM on Mondays.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a Phoenix-only utility bill program and should be used for Mesa clients only if they have a qualifying Phoenix City Services account. Assistance depends on appointment availability and eligibility review.

resources.name: Sojourner Center - On-Site Resource Center for Domestic Violence Survivors
resources.description: Sojourner Center's on-site resource center provides essential items at no cost to survivors participating in its programs, with donated items including bedding, towels, hygiene, baby items, children's clothing and case-by-case furniture.
resources.address: Confidential participant setting; public mailing address P.O. Box 20156, Phoenix, AZ 85036
resources.hours: 24-hour hotline for shelter help: 602-244-0089. Resource center access is through Sojourner programs, not public walk-in hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost essential items through Sojourner's on-site resource center for survivors rebuilding after domestic violence. Needed/accepted items include bedding, towels, hygiene items, baby items, children's clothing, and some furniture such as bed frames or couches when needed and accepted.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Material items are for Sojourner Center participants and survivors connected to its services. The resource center is not open to the public.

**Population Served**
Survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault or human trafficking and their children who are connected to Sojourner Center programs.

**How to Best Connect**
For immediate domestic violence shelter or safety help, call Sojourner Center's 24-hour hotline at 602-244-0089. For non-emergency questions, call 602-244-0997 or email info@sojournercenter.org.

**Important Information to Know**
Do not send clients to a public shopping location or disclose confidential shelter settings. Furniture and household items depend on participant need and resource center inventory.

resources.name: Phoenix Rescue Mission - Housing Assistance Program document help
resources.description: Phoenix Rescue Mission Housing Assistance Program helps people experiencing homelessness work toward permanent housing through outreach case management, housing applications and help securing IDs, Social Security cards, birth certificates and other documents needed for housing.
resources.hours: Call 602-233-3000 to request street outreach or ask about the housing pathway; outreach and screening are case-by-case.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Case-managed housing screening, applications, voucher navigation, property search and help obtaining IDs/driver licenses, Social Security cards, birth certificates and other necessary documents. Approved support can include limited security-deposit/basic-expense help, furniture/household necessities and continuing case management to reduce future eviction risk.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Clients typically enter through Phoenix Rescue Mission outreach, referrals from social workers or other Mission programs. Housing assistance and voucher support are case-by-case and depend on program approval and funding.

**Population Served**
People experiencing homelessness in Phoenix and the Valley, including outreach-accessible Maricopa County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-233-3000. People on the streets can call with nearest cross streets to request contact from a street outreach case manager; the housing page also has an inquiry form.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a stand-alone document replacement office and does not guarantee a voucher, apartment or document fee payment. ID help is embedded in an approved housing pathway and usually follows outreach or referral screening.

resources.name: A New Leaf · MesaCAN Economic Development Program
resources.description: A New Leaf MesaCAN Economic Development Program provides free in-person small-business workshops, technical assistance, and business-startup support for current and aspiring business owners, with a focus on low- to moderate-income employment and entrepreneurship.
resources.address: 635 E. Broadway Rd., Mesa, AZ 85204
resources.hours: By appointment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
MesaCAN Economic Development provides free in-person small-business workshops in collaboration with community partners, including SCORE, MesaCAN T.I.M.E., and Beyond the Chair. The program supports current and aspiring business owners and connects participants to education, counseling, technical assistance, and business-development resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page emphasizes current and aspiring business owners across the Valley, with a focus on employing low- to moderate-income individuals. Workshop registration is recommended; participant eligibility and matched-savings connections should be confirmed with staff.

**Population Served**
Mesa and Valley residents pursuing entrepreneurship, self-employment, or small-business education, especially low- to moderate-income entrepreneurs.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-258-6927 or email mcedp@turnanewleaf.org. The program is at 635 E. Broadway Rd., Mesa, and is listed as by appointment.

**Important Information to Know**
This is entrepreneurship education and business technical assistance, not a general job-training school. Workshop calendars change; confirm current dates, registration, language options, and any eligibility rules.

resources.name: Open Arms Care Center — Gilbert Clothing and Food Assistance
resources.description: Historical Gilbert assistance program whose current intake and location need administrator verification.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Historical listings describe clothing and food assistance for Gilbert households.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Older sources describe Gilbert residency and community-assistance-card rules; current eligibility is unresolved.

**Population Served**

Historically Gilbert residents experiencing material hardship.

**How to Best Connect**

Administrator review is required before referral. Do not use the former website, which currently redirects to unrelated content.

**Important Information to Know**

Current location, hours and operating contact remain unresolved. This uncertainty is not evidence that the organization has closed.
resources.resolutionReason: Historical Gilbert material identifies the food pantry, but current location, intake, food or clothing services and safe operating contact remain unresolved; the former provider website must not be used for referral.

resources.name: City of Tempe - Supporting Next Steps
resources.description: Supporting Next Steps is a City of Tempe program for returning citizens and caregivers referred by Maricopa County Sheriff's Office Correctional Health Services when the family and children live in Tempe, offering tailored case management and connection to employment, stable housing, basic needs, education, counseling resources, and parenting workshops.
resources.address: City Hall, 31 E. 5th St., Tempe, AZ 85281
resources.hours: Contact the program by email or city phone; public page does not list walk-in hours for this program.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Tailored case management and support for family reunification and reintegration, including help connecting to employment, stable housing, basic needs, education, counseling resources, parenting workshops, employment workshops, and education workshops.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page says Supporting Next Steps receives referrals from Maricopa County Sheriff's Office Correctional Health Services for returning citizens who have children and families living in Tempe. It is not a general Mesa reentry program.

**Population Served**
Returning citizens and caregivers/children in Tempe-connected families affected by incarceration.

**How to Best Connect**
Email nextsteps@tempe.gov or call the City of Tempe at 480-350-4311 to ask about the referral process and whether the family fits the Tempe residency requirement.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a useful reserve option only for Tempe families. Mesa residents without a Tempe-connected family should use Maricopa County or Mesa-area reentry services instead.

resources.name: City of Phoenix Office of Public Health · Free Naloxone Overdose Reversal Kits
resources.description: City of Phoenix provides free naloxone overdose reversal kits at Phoenix Public Library locations and other city sites, with no questions asked. The page also links to other community and mail-order naloxone sources.
resources.address: Phoenix Public Library locations and other City of Phoenix sites
resources.hours: Distribution hours vary by library or city site; check the City of Phoenix map or the specific site before travel.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Free naloxone overdose reversal kits intended to reverse opioid overdose. Kits include two doses of naloxone, gloves, instructions, and substance-use resource information.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The City of Phoenix page states kits are available free and no questions asked at participating city locations. Mesa clients must be able to access a Phoenix distribution site or use a linked community/mail-order source.

**Population Served**
Community members who may witness or experience opioid overdose, including people with opioid use disorder, people using substances, friends, family members, and other helpers.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the City of Phoenix naloxone page and map to find a current distribution site, or call the City of Phoenix main line at 602-262-3111 for city-site questions. For Mesa-area alternatives, the page links to Sonoran Prevention Works, SUCLA, NaloxoneAZ, and pharmacies.

**Important Information to Know**
Naloxone is overdose safety support, not addiction treatment. In an overdose, call emergency services and administer naloxone when indicated. Pharmacy naloxone may have a cost even though city kits are free.

resources.name: Maricopa County Department of Public Health - Home Visitation Services (NFP and MECSH)
resources.description: Maricopa County nurse home-visiting services for pregnant and parenting families through Nurse-Family Partnership and MECSH, with pregnancy/parenting support, child development guidance, screenings and referrals.
resources.hours: Visits scheduled after intake; submit the referral or call for availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Maricopa County Home Visitation Services offers two evidence-based nurse home-visiting programs: Nurse-Family Partnership and Maternal Early Childhood Sustained Home-Visiting. Visits may cover healthy pregnancy, parenting, breastfeeding/feeding, infant and child development, developmental screenings, school readiness, parent-child relationships, stress management, referrals for healthcare, child care, job training and other community supports.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Nurse-Family Partnership begins before the 28th week of pregnancy for families who live in NFP service areas and meet income requirements; it focuses on first-time mothers and can continue until the child turns two. MECSH serves pregnant and parenting clients, does not require first-time motherhood, allows enrollment during pregnancy through eight weeks postpartum, can continue until the child's third birthday, and has no income eligibility requirement. Enrollment is free and voluntary.

**Population Served**
Pregnant and parenting families in Maricopa County, including Mesa families when their address and timing fit the NFP or MECSH pathway.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the referral form linked from the county Home Visitation Services page; pregnant or parenting families can refer themselves, and providers or community partners can also refer. Call 602-316-0180 for questions.

**Important Information to Know**
NFP has service-area and income rules, so not every Mesa ZIP code or family will qualify for NFP. MECSH has different rules and may be a fit for non-first-time parents. Completing the referral does not guarantee enrollment or immediate availability.

resources.name: Mesa Community College · TRIO Student Support Services
resources.description: Mesa Community College TRIO Student Support Services provides no-cost academic support to accepted or enrolled MCC students with academic need who are first-generation, meet federal low-income guidelines, or have a documented disability.
resources.address: 1833 W. Southern Ave., Mesa, AZ 85202; Red Mountain Campus, 7110 E. McKellips Rd., Mesa, AZ 85207; MCC Online
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
No-cost academic and persistence support for accepted TRIO participants. Services may include tutoring, advising, educational planning, transfer preparation, study support, workshops, and connection to campus resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must be currently enrolled or accepted for enrollment at MCC, be a U.S. citizen or national or meet federal student-aid residency requirements, demonstrate academic need, and meet at least one TRIO criterion: first-generation college student, financial need under federal guidelines, or documented disability with MCC DRS.

**Population Served**
Eligible Mesa Community College students who need extra academic support, including first-generation students, low-income students, and students with documented disabilities.

**How to Best Connect**
Start from the MCC TRIO page and ask the TRIO office about the current application, capacity, and documentation needed. General campus contact is 480-461-7000, and the submitted TRIO phone is 480-461-7553.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a general pre-enrollment college-access program. A client must be accepted or enrolled at MCC and admitted to TRIO before receiving services; capacity may be limited.

resources.name: Horizon Health and Wellness · Supported Employment Services
resources.description: Horizon Health and Wellness offers supported employment services for adults with intellectual/developmental disabilities in Arizona, including employment counseling, assessment, vocational evaluation, resume and interview preparation, job coaching, job search help and support for entering or retaining work.
resources.hours: Call for program intake and appointment details.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Supported employment services help adults with intellectual/developmental disabilities prepare for, enter, and retain employment. Services include employment counseling, individual needs assessment, vocational evaluation, employment preparation, resume writing, interviewing techniques, personal and social adjustment training, job coaching, job search, community-resource referral and support services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page describes the service for adults with intellectual/developmental disabilities and says Horizon works with people already connected with systems of care such as Rehabilitation Services Administration and DES. Referral or authorization requirements should be confirmed by phone.

**Population Served**
Adults with intellectual/developmental disabilities in Arizona who need support to reach employment goals.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Horizon Health and Wellness at 833-431-4449 and ask for Supported Employment Services, RSA/DES referral requirements, and whether the program can serve a Mesa or Maricopa County client.

**Important Information to Know**
The page states statewide Arizona service but does not list a Mesa office for this program. Confirm service location, remote options, payer/authorization rules and current availability before relying on it for a referral.

resources.name: HIV Care Directions - Housing Information Services / HOPWA-related Housing and Supportive Services
resources.description: HIV Care Directions, a program of Area Agency on Aging Region One, provides case management and HIV-related support for adults 18+ with HIV in Maricopa and Pinal Counties. Housing-related help includes assistance finding and maintaining subsidized or affordable housing and connection to HOPWA housing information and provider matching.
resources.address: 1366 E Thomas Rd, Suite 200, Phoenix, AZ 85014
resources.hours: 2-1-1 lists Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; call for current intake.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
HIV medical and non-medical case management, Ryan White eligibility support, transportation help for HIV-related medical care, health-insurance premium and medical-cost assistance for eligible clients, help finding and maintaining subsidized or affordable housing, and HOPWA housing information/referral matching.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For adults age 18 and older with HIV in Maricopa or Pinal County. Directory evidence says intake may require proof of HIV/AIDS status and photo ID; call if documents are missing or unsafe to carry.

**Population Served**
Adults living with HIV/AIDS in Maricopa and Pinal Counties, including Mesa residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-264-2273 for intake or HOPWA housing information. Ask what documents are needed, whether an appointment is required, and whether any barrier accommodation is available if a client lacks ID.

**Important Information to Know**
Phoenix administers HOPWA for Maricopa and Pinal Counties; eligible Mesa households can inquire through Care Directions. Housing matching does not guarantee a subsidy or vacancy. HOPWA, Ryan White and other supports have separate income, documentation, eligibility and capacity rules.

resources.name: Arizona Career Development Center · Justice-Impacted Workforce Readiness Project
resources.description: Arizona Career Development Center was identified in a 2025 ADHS Justice Reinvestment award summary for workforce readiness, rapid employment entry and reintegration support for justice-impacted individuals in Maricopa County.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The grant summary describes workforce readiness, rapid employment entry, reintegration support after incarceration and wraparound collaboration for housing, financial literacy, trauma-informed care, single parents and vulnerable populations.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Current intake, eligibility, program start/status and whether Mesa residents are actively served are unresolved.

**Population Served**
Justice-impacted individuals in Maricopa County, with submitted evidence also mentioning single parents and vulnerable populations.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Arizona Career Development Center website to seek current contact information. No reliable public phone, address or intake route was established in this record.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not ready for ordinary referral until current access is confirmed. Retain as an administrator lead because the described workforce and wraparound services match reentry needs.
resources.resolutionReason: Needs administrator resolution: current intake, eligibility, active service status and Mesa-area access are not established by the assigned evidence.

resources.name: Journey of Hope Healing Center - Re-Entry and Supportive Housing Program
resources.description: Journey of Hope Healing Center offers a Mesa 90-day Re-Entry and Supportive Housing Program with transitional housing, life-skills training, group therapy, case management, ID help, housing coordination, recovery coaching, peer support, and long-term housing/employment transition help for people after incarceration with mental-health or substance-use needs.
resources.address: 6335 E Main St. Ste D, Mesa, AZ 85205
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM for the Mesa clinic.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A 90-day transitional reentry program with supportive housing, life-skills training, group therapy, case management, ID coordination, housing support, recovery coaching, peer support, and assistance with long-term housing and employment after completion.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is for people navigating mental-health or substance-use challenges after incarceration. Funding, bed availability, clinical fit, waitlist, and any criminal-history exclusions should be confirmed at referral.

**Population Served**
People after incarceration in Mesa who need structured reentry support, behavioral-health care, substance-use recovery support, and housing stability.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-932-4430, email referrals@journeyofhopehealingcenter.com for referrals, or use the website contact form. The clinic is at 6335 E Main St, Suite D, Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
This appears to be a private/clinical provider; confirm payer, insurance, sliding-scale availability, housing location, bed count, and current capacity before referral.

resources.name: Refugee Education and Clinic Team (REACT) - Clinical Branch
resources.description: REACT, the Refugee Education and Clinic Team, provides refugee and asylum seeker medical support, health education, community engagement and resources in Maricopa County through student/community clinical and education branches.
resources.hours: No regular clinic hours are posted; call or email to ask about current clinical events, workshops and referral options.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Medical support, health education, community workshops, direct community engagement, health needs assessment, resources and clinical-branch support for refugees and asylum seekers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program focuses on refugees and asylum seekers in Maricopa County and the greater Phoenix area. Public pages do not post a standard walk-in clinic eligibility or schedule.

**Population Served**
Refugees and asylum seekers in Maricopa County and the Greater Phoenix area facing geographic, linguistic and cultural barriers to health care.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-543-4390 or email reactarizona@gmail.com to ask about current clinical events, education workshops, referral options and whether the client can be connected to care.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a community clinical-support and education team, not a confirmed ongoing primary-care medical home. Use it as a specialized support and navigation lead for refugee/asylum-seeker clients while also connecting the client to a regular clinic when ongoing care is needed.

resources.name: IRC Phoenix — Immigration, Civics and English/Education Services
resources.description: IRC Phoenix provides affordable immigration legal/civics services, English and citizenship preparation, youth education/school advocacy and community-integration support. Broader community access and case-specific rules should be checked through the Glendale office.
resources.address: 4425 W Olive Ave, Suite 400, Glendale, AZ 85302
resources.hours: Call or email IRC Phoenix for current intake and appointments.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Immigration legal/civics help with green cards, citizenship, family reunification, DACA and other immigration benefits through DOJ-accredited guidance. Related community-integration support includes English-language development, naturalization-test preparation, youth education/school advocacy, cultural orientation and language-access connections. Ask about the specific immigration-document, travel-document, work-authorization or fee-waiver issue before assuming local service availability.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Immigration/civics and English/citizenship services are described as supporting the wider Maricopa County community as well as refugees/asylees and other newcomers. Each case/class, fee, capacity and document requirement needs screening. Population-specific resettlement or refugee benefits have separate rules and should not be imposed automatically on these classes/legal services.

**Population Served**
Refugees, asylees, other eligible newcomers and community members across Maricopa County, including Mesa-area clients who can contact the Glendale/Phoenix office.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-433-2440 or email Phoenix@rescue.org and ask specifically for Immigration and Civics Instruction, English/citizenship or youth education support. Office:4425 W. Olive Ave., Suite 400, Glendale. Describe the needed service, deadline, language and Mesa access needs.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not an established general free removal-defence clinic. Confirm representation scope, fees, documents, current classes and local document-replacement services. IRC resettlement, employment, health and Safety/Wellness supports have separate intake pathways.

resources.name: Maricopa Community Colleges - Incarcerated and Community Re-entry Education Programs
resources.description: Maricopa Community Colleges and Rio Salado College provide incarcerated and community re-entry education pathways, including reentry-focused coursework and Workforce Development and Community Re-Entry certificate/degree options covering employability, family reunification, personal development, substance-use education, and community transition skills.
resources.hours: Course access varies by term, facility and programme; contact admissions before enrollment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Maricopa Community Colleges offers incarcerated and community re-entry education programs for students seeking education, workforce development, and transition support. Rio Salado College has partnered with the Arizona Department of Corrections on occupational, educational, and workforce-development programs. The Workforce Development and Community Re-Entry CCL/AAS pathway includes job readiness, job preparation, job retention, family reunification, personal and social skill development, and substance-use education.

**Eligibility Requirements**
College enrollment rules, placement, tuition/financial aid, and department or division permission can apply. The AAS page states department or division permission is required for admission to the Workforce Development and Community Re-Entry program. Some offerings may be tied to correctional partnerships or distance learning rather than open community self-enrollment.

**Population Served**
People who are incarcerated, recently incarcerated, or returning to the community and seeking education, credentials, workforce preparation, or transition support through Maricopa Community Colleges.

**How to Best Connect**
Start with the Maricopa Community Colleges incarcerated re-entry page, the Workforce Development and Community Re-Entry degree page, or the linked Rio Salado program offerings/enrollment route. Maricopa Community Colleges' main number is 480-731-8000.

**Important Information to Know**
This is education/workforce preparation, not emergency reentry housing, clinical substance-use treatment or case management. Course availability depends on campus, correctional partner, term, format and required department approval. Released students should ask about community enrollment/continuation, costs and financial aid.

resources.name: EPCOR Arizona - Water and Wastewater Low-Income Assistance Program
resources.description: EPCOR Arizona low-income program offering up to $10 per month off eligible water or wastewater bills.
resources.hours: Customer Care is available 24/7 by phone.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
EPCOR's Low Income Program offers up to $10 off the monthly bill for eligible water and wastewater customers when space is available.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The applicant must be in an EPCOR Arizona territory, be a residential customer or live in an HOA, apartment complex, or mobile home park served by EPCOR, and have annual income at or below 200% of the U.S. Federal Poverty Guidelines for water and wastewater.

**Population Served**
Low-income households with qualifying EPCOR Arizona water or wastewater service, including some residents billed through HOAs, apartments, or mobile-home parks.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete EPCOR's application form and submit it to mywater@epcor.com or mail it to 5350 W. Bell Road, Suite 122, Glendale, AZ 85308. Call 1-800-383-0834 with questions.

**Important Information to Know**
This does not serve City of Mesa water accounts. EPCOR states the credit depends on meeting guidelines and space in the program.

resources.name: Maricopa County Department of Public Health - Refugee Clinic Domestic Medical Examination
resources.description: Maricopa County Refugee Health / Refugee Clinic conducts domestic medical examinations and screening for eligible new arrivals, with lab screening for public-health conditions and linkage to follow-up care.
resources.address: 1645 E. Roosevelt St., Phoenix, AZ 85006
resources.hours: Public Health Administration offices are Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM excluding observed holidays; Refugee Clinic service hours and appointments must be confirmed by phone.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Domestic medical examinations for eligible new arrivals, lab screening for conditions such as tuberculosis, HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B, age/history-based additional screening, mental-health screening for new arrivals age 14 and older, and linkage to follow-up care.

**Eligibility Requirements**
This pathway is for eligible refugees and other qualifying newcomers/new arrivals, often coordinated with resettlement agencies. It is not open general primary care.

**Population Served**
Eligible refugees, humanitarian parolees, special immigrant visa recipients and other qualifying newcomers in Maricopa County who need domestic medical screening and connection into local healthcare systems.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Maricopa County Refugee Health at 602-506-6650. The county report identifies the Refugee Clinic within Community Health and Records Services at 1645 E. Roosevelt St., Phoenix, AZ 85006.

**Important Information to Know**
Use this for qualifying newcomer/refugee screening situations. Public client-facing intake details are limited, so confirm eligibility, timing after arrival, referral route and required documents before sending a client.

resources.name: Agnes' Centers for Domestic Solutions Domestic Violence Intervention, Counseling, Support Groups, and Legal Advocacy
resources.description: Agnes' Centers for Domestic Solutions is a Tempe lead for domestic-violence-related counseling, support groups, education, and advocacy, but current official program confirmation could not be established.
resources.address: 455 S 48th St, Suite 106, Tempe, AZ 85281
resources.hours: Unknown; do not refer without direct administrator confirmation.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Older government resource materials describe services for people affected by domestic or sexual abuse, including education, counseling, support groups, and legal advocacy. A current NPI listing supports an active community/behavioral health organization at the submitted Tempe address and phone, but a current official program page was not found.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Unresolved. Older funding material tied one program to low-income men affected by domestic violence and required proof of income, proof of identity, and court documents if court-mandated; current eligibility for survivor services could not be confirmed.

**Population Served**
Potentially people affected by domestic or sexual abuse in Tempe/Maricopa County; exact current population, gender scope, and survivor versus offender-service scope require confirmation.

**How to Best Connect**
Administrator should call 480-664-6554 before any referral and verify current operation, service scope, fees, eligibility, appointment process, and whether survivors can safely contact the program.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a useful unresolved lead, not a ready referral. The former website agnescenters.com was not confirmed as a current official source, and public evidence is split between older domestic-violence resource listings and a current NPI identity listing. Do not send a survivor there until the office verifies current services.
resources.resolutionReason: Current NPI evidence supports organization identity, address, and phone, and government resource materials support historical domestic-violence service scope. The remaining obstacle is consequential: no current official program page or direct current service-scope evidence was found, so routine referral would risk sending a survivor to an unconfirmed program.

resources.name: VA.gov / National Archives - Military Service Records and DD214 Request
resources.description: VA.gov's military-service-records pathway explains how veterans and eligible requesters can request DD214s and other service records from the National Archives online, by mail, or by fax, including records needed for VA health, housing, education, claims and burial-benefit eligibility.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Official VA.gov guidance for requesting DD214s and other military service records from the National Archives. Records can show character of discharge, duty stations, awards, qualifications, licenses, certificates, and medical or health records.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Veterans can request their own records; eligible next of kin of deceased veterans and authorized representatives need required proof/authorization. Public access and fees change when records become archival 62 years after separation. Identity verification may be needed for online access.

**Population Served**
Veterans, next of kin, and other eligible requesters nationwide, including Mesa and Maricopa County clients needing records for benefits or referrals.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the VA records page to reach National Archives eVetRecs, which requires an identity-verified ID.me account. Alternatively, complete and sign SF-180 and follow its destination instructions for the branch, service dates and record type. For records held at NPRC, the fax is 314-801-9195 and status phone is 314-801-0800. VA can request your DD214 as part of a benefits application.

**Important Information to Know**
Check the SF180 destination for the branch, service dates and record type; do not send every request to NPRC. Most qualifying non-archival requests are free; archival copies may have fees. Do not send original supporting documents. Records can be incomplete. VA can request a DD214 for a benefits application, and an accredited service officer can help with identity-verification barriers.

resources.name: Disability Rights Arizona - protection and advocacy legal services
resources.description: Disability Rights Arizona is Arizona's federally mandated protection-and-advocacy agency. It provides free disability-rights legal advocacy and possible representation for issues such as abuse, neglect, discrimination, education, employment, housing, accessibility, health care, mental health, assistive technology, voting, and rights of incarcerated people.
resources.address: 5025 E. Washington St., Suite 202, Phoenix, AZ 85034
resources.hours: Temporary notice on the intake page: no new intakes September 21-28, 2026; intake reopens Monday, September 28, 2026 at 8:00 AM.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Disability Rights Arizona provides free disability-rights legal help, advocacy, information, and possible representation. Areas include special education, vocational services, employment, housing, public accommodations, abuse and neglect, health care, assistive technology, mental health, voting rights, representative payee issues, and rights of incarcerated people with disabilities.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The disability-related rights issue must fit DRAZ authority/priorities, case merit, deadlines, available staff/resources and whether another adequate attorney or agency can resolve it. DRAZ may provide resources/referrals when it cannot represent the person.

**Population Served**
Children and adults with disabilities in Arizona, including Mesa and Maricopa County residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Apply for Assistance page, including Spanish intake access, or call 602-274-6287 or 800-927-2260. The posted temporary intake pause is scheduled to end September 28, 2026 at 8 AM; check the page before submitting. Phoenix office:5025 E. Washington St., Suite 202.

**Important Information to Know**
Services are free but not every case is accepted. Intake or website information does not create an attorney-client relationship or stop legal deadlines. Public self-advocacy resources remain available during the temporary new-intake pause.

resources.name: RefurbIT Discount Program
resources.description: AzTAP partners with Achieve Human Services and RefurbIT to provide low-cost refurbished computers and iOS devices statewide, with an additional 25% discount for Arizonans with disabilities who receive qualifying public benefits.
resources.address: 300 W Clarendon Ave, Suite 475, Phoenix, AZ 85013
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
The RefurbIT program sells low-cost refurbished computers and iOS devices. A disability-specific discount provides an additional 25% off RefurbIT's already discounted price after approval. Example starting prices listed by AzTAP include monitors around $29.99, desktops around $79, and laptops around $189, with Windows 11 and a 12-month warranty for PC/laptop purchases.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The general public may purchase available RefurbIT items. For the extra 25% discount, an Arizona household member must have a disability and currently receive a qualifying public benefit such as AHCCCS/Medicaid, Section 8, LIHEAP, free lunch, SSDI, SSI, KidsCare/SCHIP, SNAP, TANF, or VA benefits.

**Population Served**
Arizona residents seeking low-cost refurbished computers or iOS devices, with an added discount for Arizonans with disabilities who receive qualifying public assistance.

**How to Best Connect**
Complete the Online RefurbIT Discount Application on the AzTAP page. AskRefurbIT@nau.edu, 602-776-4670 or 800-477-9921 can help with the application. For actual product stock or purchase arrangements, contact Achieve/RefurbIT at 928-341-4141 or aesinformation@achievehs.org. Confirm pickup or shipping; the AzTAP address is not a guaranteed inventory counter.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a purchase programme, not a free giveaway. Confirm current prices, stock, device features, warranty and extra software charges. AzTAP announces closure on October 2, 2026 and reopening October 5.

resources.name: Ayuda Smiles - Smiles for Veterans
resources.description: Smiles for Veterans, operated by Ayuda Smiles, helps Arizona veterans who do not qualify for VA dental care access dental resources and critical dental care at little to no cost through provider collaborations.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Smiles for Veterans advocates for dental health care for Arizona veterans in need and facilitates dental resources and critical dental care at little to no cost through collaborations with dental providers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The official page focuses on veterans who do not qualify under current VA dental guidelines. The application process may have additional eligibility, documentation, service-area, provider availability and waitlist requirements.

**Population Served**
Arizona veterans in need of dental care, especially veterans without VA dental eligibility.

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Application for Assistance link on the Smiles for Veterans website, call 520-245-2997, or email smilesforveterans@gmail.com.

**Important Information to Know**
The programme reports a waiting list. Dental help depends on participating providers, funding, required verification and case fit; application does not guarantee immediate treatment. Check VA dental eligibility separately and ask which care costs are covered.

resources.name: American Bar Association Commission on Immigration - Detention Information Hotline
resources.description: The American Bar Association Commission on Immigration Detention Information Hotline lets people in immigration detention without attorneys call from detention-facility phones for immigration information and referrals to local nonprofit organizations and immigration attorneys.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
